# Octopush — Feature Map

> **This file is the single source of truth for everything Octopush can do and how it does it.**
>
> **Maintenance mandate (binding):** Any change that adds, removes, or meaningfully alters a user-facing feature **must** update this document in the same change. A PR that ships a feature without updating `docs/FEATURES.md` is incomplete. Keep it exhaustive — down to the smallest context-menu item, toggle, keyboard shortcut, and empty state. When you add a new surface, add its features here; when you delete one, delete its entry. This rule is also recorded in `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`.
>
> _Conventions:_ each feature is one bullet — **Name** — what it does (user-facing). _Support:_ the files / Tauri commands / Zustand stores / mechanism that implement it. _Entry:_ how the user reaches or triggers it. File paths are relative to the repo root; symbol names are durable, occasional line numbers are approximate hints only.

**Octopush** is "The IDE for Agentic Developers — eight arms, zero wasted tokens." It is a Tauri 2 desktop app (macOS-first) with a React 19 + TypeScript frontend and a Rust backend. Workspaces are git worktrees. Its visual identity is **Atelier in Onyx & Brass** (see `docs/design-system.md`).

---

## Architecture at a glance

- **Frontend** (`src/`) — React 19 + TypeScript, Tailwind v4 (`@theme` tokens in `src/styles.css`), state in **Zustand** stores (`src/stores/`), all IPC funneled through `src/lib/ipc.ts` (`invoke` from `@tauri-apps/api/core`). CodeMirror 6 editor, xterm.js terminals, React Flow pipeline builder, Recharts usage charts.
- **Backend** (`src-tauri/src/`) — Rust. Tauri commands in `commands.rs` (registered in `lib.rs`'s invoke handler, ~190 commands), state in `state.rs`, SQLite data layer in `db.rs`, errors via `error.rs` (`Result<T, AppError>`). Domain modules: `chat_engine`, `orchestrator/*` (Direct mode), `git_ops`/`git_lock`/`github`, `providers/*`/`provider_router`, `token_engine`, `issue_tracker/*` (Jira), `mcp/*` + `mcp_setup`, `pty_*`/`talk_shell`, `theme`, `settings`, `perf`, `skills`, `context_guard`.
- **Two bundled sidecar binaries** (same crate, separate `[[bin]]`):
  - **`octopush-pty-server`** — an out-of-process PTY daemon that owns all pseudo-terminals so shells survive app restarts/updates (`src-tauri/src/bin/octopush-pty-server/*`).
  - **`octopush-mcp`** — a read-and-author MCP server that exposes Octopush's pipelines/roles/projects/workspaces/runs to external CLIs over stdio (`src-tauri/src/bin/octopush-mcp/*`).
- **Three primary modes** per workspace — **Talk** (AI chat), **Run** (terminals) / **Direct** (multi-agent pipeline orchestration), **Review** (diff, editor, AI review). A right-hand **Companion** panel adapts to the mode; a left **Workspace Rail** lists projects → workspaces.
- **Data locations** — SQLite at `~/Library/Application Support/octopush/octopush.db`; settings/keys/themes/providers under `~/.octopush/` (`settings.json`, `providers.json`, `theme.json`); PTY daemon socket/pid/logs and scrollback under `~/.octopush/`. **Local-first, no telemetry** — outbound traffic only to configured AI providers and to integrations the user enables (Jira, GitHub); the Rust core's own requests go through one hardened HTTP client (`src-tauri/src/tls.rs`: OS trust store + the eMudhra compromised-CA denylist, see section 10).

## 1. Application Shell, Modes & Navigation

### App shell layout & structure
- **Vertical app frame** — The shell stacks `AppTopBar` (28px chrome) → main row (Rail · main · Companion) → `PerfMonitorBar` (footer), all `h-screen w-screen bg-octo-bg`. _Support:_ `src/App.tsx`. _Entry:_ always present once a project is open.
- **Three-column shell** — `<main>` holds the middle column only: a `ContextHeader` band (workspace identity) over the canvas column. The `WorkspaceRail` (left) and the `Companion` (right) are its SIBLINGS — both full height between the top bar and the status bar, both flush to their window edge, each carrying one hairline (`border-r` / `border-l`) toward the canvas. `<main>` is inset `--shell-gutter` (8px) from both. _Support:_ `src/App.tsx`, `Companion.tsx`, `WorkspaceRail.tsx`. _Entry:_ structural.
- **Shell spacing** — Three layout tokens set the air between the standing surfaces, the same in every mode and with the rail or the Companion folded: `--shell-gutter` (8px) is `<main>`'s inset from the rail and from the Companion; `--shell-stack` (8px) sits above the `ContextHeader`, between it and the mode band, and between the mode band and the canvas; `--shell-foot` (8px) is the canvas column's bottom padding above the status bar. The `ContextHeader` card pads 12px inline and 6px block. (Before 2026-11-18 these were 16 / 16 / 12 / 16px, and the header padded 16 / 8px.) _Support:_ `src/styles.css` (`--shell-*`), `src/lib/tokens.ts` (`shell`), `src/App.tsx`, `src/components/ContextHeader.tsx`, `src/components/ModeBand.tsx`; `src/lib/shellSpacing.test.ts`; spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-run-mode-and-rail-groups-design.md` (Part 5). _Entry:_ structural.
- **Always-mounted canvas (PTY survival)** — The left canvas column is never gated on `activeWorkspace`; empty-project/creator layers overlay it instead, so running terminals across projects keep their PTYs and xterm scrollback. _Support:_ `src/App.tsx`; `allTerminalRefs` flattens every `(workspace, terminal)` pair so all `TerminalPane`s mount simultaneously. _Entry:_ structural.
- **Error boundaries (crash containment)** — A render or effect error no longer blanks the window. **Root:** `main.tsx` wraps the whole tree (the app and Quick View) in a `root` boundary. It shows a full-window recovery screen ("Octopush hit an unexpected error.", **Reload Octopush** reloads the WebView, **Copy error details**). **Per surface:** each mode canvas (Talk, Run, Review, Direct), the empty-project layer and the Companion has a `panel` boundary. A crash there shows an inline "This panel hit an error." card with **Try again**, which remounts only that surface, and **Copy error details**. Talk, Review, Direct and the Companion also clear on a workspace switch (`resetKey`). The collapsed Companion shows a single rouge icon button instead (`compact`). Every palette, dialog, context menu, sheet and room opened from `App.tsx` (⌘K, search, session switcher, PR composer, Settings, the new-mission and Add project sheets, confirm dialogs, Jira modals, What's new, Upgrade, Run history, Mission Control, Logbook) has an `overlay` boundary. The same card shows in a `ModalShell` and adds **Close** (and Escape), which dismisses the surface. Errors are logged to the WebView console as `[octopush] <surface> hit a render error:` with the component stack. Nothing goes over the network, and the cards never show the raw error text. The details reach the clipboard only on **Copy error details** and are never put into a chat or run. _Support:_ `src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx` (the app's one class component, because React has no hook boundary), `src/lib/errorReport.ts`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/App.tsx`. _Entry:_ automatic.
- **macOS traffic-light reservation + window drag** — Top bar reserves 78px for overlaid traffic lights and is a `data-tauri-drag-region`, so the window drags from any empty area. _Support:_ `src/components/AppTopBar.tsx`. _Entry:_ the top chrome bar.

### Three-mode (four-mode) workspace system
- **Mode model** — Four modes exist: `talk | run | review | direct`; display order is `["run","talk","review","direct"]`. Labels: Talk/Run/Review/Direct. Shortcuts are numbered in display order: Run `⌘⇧1`, Talk `⌘⇧2`, Review `⌘⇧3`; Direct is `⌘⇧D` because macOS takes `⌘⇧4` (screenshot) before the webview. _Support:_ `src/lib/modes.ts` (`WorkspaceMode`, `MODES`, `MODE_LABELS`, `MODE_SHORTCUTS`). _Entry:_ ModeSwitcher / shortcuts.
- **Per-workspace mode memory** — Each workspace remembers its own active mode (`modePerWorkspace`), defaulting to `talk`. Switching workspaces restores that workspace's last mode. _Support:_ `src/App.tsx`. _Entry:_ automatic.
- **Talk mode** — Conversational agent chat for the active workspace (`ChatView`); can open files in the editor and hand a command to Run; one of Run's sessions can sit beside the conversation (see "A terminal beside the conversation (Talk's seat)"). _Support:_ `src/App.tsx`, `components/chat/TalkSeat.tsx`. _Entry:_ Talk tab / ⌘⇧2.
- **Run mode** — Terminal surface; all PTYs mounted, only the active workspace's active terminal is visible (or up to four side by side — see "Sessions side by side (up to four)"); every pane sits under its caption, and the mode band's right track holds the **session line** (see Run · session navigation); shows a "Start a new terminal." empty state when the workspace has zero terminals ("…You can keep several sessions open, switch between them from the line above, or open them side by side."). _Support:_ `src/App.tsx` `RunEmptyState`, `components/run/SessionLine.tsx`, `components/run/RunPanes.tsx`. _Entry:_ Run tab / ⌘⇧1.
- **Review mode** — Three-pane review: `ReviewSidebar` (Changes+Files navigator) · `ReviewCanvas` (Diff/Editor toggle, hosts `EditorTabs`+`EditorPane`). Re-fetches git status/diff after commit/push/hunk actions, applied only if the workspace they were read for is still active, so a quick switch never paints the previous workspace's status (`lib/workspaceRefetch.ts`, #908). _Support:_ `src/App.tsx`. _Entry:_ Review tab / ⌘⇧3.
- **Direct mode** — Autonomous pipeline/run canvas (`DirectCanvas`), keyed by workspace id, seeded from `workspace.task` and `linkedIssueKey`. _Support:_ `src/App.tsx`. _Entry:_ Direct tab / ⌘⇧D.
- **References in the brief (`@file` · `/skill`)** — The Direct launcher's brief takes the two references TALK's composer has, over the same catalogs (`list_workspace_files`, `list_skills` — project ∪ user): `@` ranks worktree files, `/` lists skills, with the skipped skill files below them as in Talk (`list_skipped_skills`; the menu opens on a query that matches only a skipped file, Escape dismisses it, and Enter/Tab select only skills). Unlike TALK a slash may start a reference **anywhere** in the prose, not just at position 0 (a brief is prose, not a command line). ↑/↓ move · Enter/Tab insert · Esc dismisses; ⌘⏎ begins the run only when no list is open. Both references stay in the text as written — a `@path` is a pointer the agents resolve with their own read tools, a `/slug` is resolved backend-side at stage start. Recomputes when a catalog lands so a list opened before the read finished still fills. _Support:_ `src/components/direct/RichPromptTextarea.tsx` (reuses `lib/mentions`, `chat/MentionPopover`, `chat/SlashMenu`). _Entry:_ Direct launcher brief.
- **A named skill reaches the role that runs it** — A reference survives as text in the brief and is resolved **when the stage starts**, the same way a TALK message's `/skill` tokens are resolved when its turn runs: `skills::referenced_skills` matches standalone `/slug` tokens against the worktree's known skills (project ∪ user), so a path segment (`src/code-review.ts`), a longer slug (`/code-review-notes`), an unknown name, or a token inside a fenced code block resolve to nothing. Resolution reads the **brief + that stage's role prompt + its instructions**, so a role can carry a skill into every run it joins. Both substrates get the same instructions appended to the stage's system prompt in the one shared shape (`# Skill: <name>`, `skill_prompt_section`) — the API runner and the CLI runner compose that prompt through the same function. A skill added or edited after the run was created is picked up. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/skills/mod.rs` (`referenced_skills`, `skill_prompt_section`), `orchestrator/mod.rs` (`StageContext.skills`), `orchestrator/runner.rs`, `orchestrator/cli_runner.rs`. _Entry:_ automatic per stage.
- **Mode band** — The switcher's own line, directly above the canvas and spanning the canvas column only (not the Companion); the pill is centred on the canvas via a `minmax(0,1fr)/auto/minmax(0,1fr)` grid, so the status tail in the right track can never shift or overlap it — the tail cell stretches across its track and right-aligns with flex (`min-w-0 justify-end`, never `justify-self-end`, which sizes a cell to its content), so a long tail truncates in place on a narrow window. The band is also a **demotion ladder** of its own (`.octo-modeband`, a container): at 720px and under, in every mode, the switcher's **inactive** modes shed their labels (one rung for all modes, so the switcher never changes width when the mode changes) and keep their icon, tooltip and accessible name, while the active mode keeps its label (each label's collapse tweens from a cap near its own width, `calc(7 * (1ch + 0.2em))`, so it starts at once instead of from the generic 40ch). When the tail is a control the right track has a **floor** (`tailMin`, the session line's `LINE_FLOOR_PX` = 119px; the grid's third track is `minmax(tailMin,1fr)`): the empty left track gives up its room first and the switcher slides off centre rather than the control losing a button. At 334px and under that floor no longer fits beside the switcher, so the track keeps only the control's **last rung** (`tailLastMin`, the session line's `LINE_LAST_PX` = 26px: its `⌘⌥K` list button) and the control sheds down to it; nothing is clipped and no hidden track is reserved. The container (`.octo-modeband`) wraps the grid (`.octo-modeband-grid`), because a container query can only change what is inside it. A read-out tail (Talk, Review, Direct) has no floor and truncates as before, with more room once the labels shed. Rendered only when a workspace is active. Holds the `ModeSwitcher` plus the active mode's status tail. _Support:_ `src/components/ModeBand.tsx` (`tailMin`, `tailLastMin`), `styles.css` (`.octo-modeband`, `.octo-modeband-grid`, `.octo-demote-mode-label`); slotted in `src/App.tsx` above `CanvasSplit`. _Entry:_ always visible in a workspace.
- **ModeSwitcher (segmented pill)** — Four segments in a `border-strong` pill on onyx, each a **lucide icon + mono/caps label** (`SquareTerminal` Run · `MessageSquare` Talk · `GitCompare` Review · `Waypoints` Direct), with a gliding+resizing brass-ghost indicator measured live from button geometry (ResizeObserver + window resize), 280ms ease. The icons exist because the words carry culture — "Run" reads as *execute something* to one developer and *where my shells are* to another — and they go on all four segments, since iconising only Run would read as a special case rather than a mode; the labels stay because mode navigation is where a wrong guess costs the most. On a narrow band the **inactive** modes shed their labels (the band's ladder, see **Mode band**): each label is a rung (`.octo-demote-mode-label`) that collapses with the standard glide, the active mode always keeps its own, every segment has an explicit accessible name and its `title` (`Review (⌘⇧3)`), and the indicator re-measures as the segments resize (it observes each segment, since two modes can trade labels of the same width). _Support:_ `src/components/ModeSwitcher.tsx` (`MODE_ICON`). _Entry:_ the mode band.
- **Mode status tail** — The band's right end reports what the active mode's room holds: Talk "34k / 200k context" (hidden before the first assistant turn; the counts go through the shared `formatContextTokens`, so a 1M window reads "1M", exactly as in the Companion's context meter, never "1000k") · Review "N files changed · +A −B" (diff stat parsed from the diff on screen: the working diff, or in the **Since base** view the committed one, counting its files)/"Nothing to review" — on an E2 demotion ladder (`ReviewTail`): as the track narrows it sheds whole atoms, "changed" first, then "· +A −B", down to the floor "N files", so it always ends on a complete value and never on "· …"; the rungs are shed by state from their measured widths against the track's (`rungsToShed`), and the full reading stays in the `title` · Direct "Crew running"/"Crew waiting on you"/"Crew idle"/"No runs yet". In **Run** the slot is a control rather than a read-out — the **session line** (see Run · session navigation) — falling back to the plain "No terminals" when the workspace has none. Crossfades with the mode (`FadeSwap`); derived from state App already holds, so it costs no extra IPC. `ModeBand`'s `meta` prop takes a `ReactNode`: a string renders as the canonical mono status line, a node renders as-is. _Support:_ `src/lib/modeMeta.ts` (`modeMetaLabel`, `reviewTailParts`, `diffStat`, `runTailState`), `lib/cost.ts` (`formatContextTokens`); `ModeBand.tsx`; `ReviewTail.tsx`; `run/SessionLine.tsx`. _Entry:_ automatic per mode.
- **Mode-tab attention pulse** — A Run/Talk segment pulses brass (`animate-attention-pulse`) when that workspace has a matching attention flag and the user is in a different mode; tooltip switches to "… needs your attention". _Support:_ `ModeSwitcher.tsx`; `attentionStore`. _Entry:_ automatic on background completions.
- **Mode-overlay crossfade** — Each mode canvas is an absolutely-positioned, opacity/visibility/pointer-events-gated overlay (200ms) so switching modes never unmounts the others. _Support:_ `src/components/ModeOverlay.tsx`. _Entry:_ structural.
- **Cross-mode "Run in terminal" hand-off** — From a Talk tool card, take a shell command to Run mode: switches mode and copies the command to the clipboard (deliberately not auto-executed). _Support:_ `src/App.tsx` `handleRunInTerminal`; toast "Command copied — paste into the terminal to run". _Entry:_ Talk chat tool action.

### ContextHeader (top header band)
- **Eyebrow & name — one grammar in both states** — The band is a mono **eyebrow** (all meta) over a serif **name** line (the one thing you are looking at). The eyebrow carries, in order: mission intent glyph + label (or "Workspace" when no mission and no ticket), the sandbox toggle (see "Header sandbox toggle"), the grandparent/parent ticket chain (clickable, opens in Jira), the active ticket key (type-tinted), the status, the branch chip, and — at the eyebrow's right end — `from <base>` and the workspace's port range (see "Workspace ports"). The name line is the ticket summary when a ticket resolves (manual link wins, else branch-detected gated on project key + tracker configured), otherwise the workspace name — animated on change, titled, and **it owns the full width in both states**, so a long branch can no longer squeeze it out. The `◈` brass diamond is retired: the type-tinted key already marks the ticket. _Support:_ `src/components/ContextHeader.tsx`; `useActiveIssue`, `parentIssuesStore`, `INTENT_ICON`. _Entry:_ automatic header.
- **Header sandbox toggle (#1230)** — With a mission, the eyebrow's sandbox glyph is a toggle for the mission's Execution axis, `none` ↔ `sandbox` (`HeaderSandbox`, `data-tour="header-sandbox"`, `aria-pressed`). `Shield` shows whenever the sandbox is in effect: the mission's `exec_isolation` is `sandbox`, or its Git axis is `readonly` (review, probe, perf), which forces the sandbox on. `ShieldOff` shows otherwise. **Turning it on** is one click: `update_mission`'s `exec_isolation` (`missionsStore.setExecIsolation`), with a toast that says what "Share with new missions" took back (`sandboxOnBody`). **Turning it off** asks first, in a `ModalShell` dialog shared with the launcher foot's toggle (`SandboxOffDialog`, `data-tour="header-sandbox-confirm"`; no click-outside, and Enter never confirms; Esc and **Keep the sandbox**, which takes the focus, cancel). The dialog belongs to the mission it was opened on: a switch to another workspace, or a sandbox that went off meanwhile, closes it, and confirming acts on that mission only. It shows "Turn off the sandbox?", says that the mission's agents will be able to write outside the workspace, and ends with the upright-serif CTA **Let its agents write outside the workspace**. **A read-only mission** shows `Shield`, can't be turned off (`aria-disabled`), and its title says "Read-only mission: its agents read the code and never change it. The sandbox is always on." **Timing:** a Talk turn resolves the sandbox once as it starts and a stage as it starts, so a change applies from the next turn or stage, never in the middle of a command; the titles, the dialog and the toasts say so. In Talk, a read-only mission forces Plan only, and its refusals name the mission (`permissions::plan_refusal`); a command its sandbox stopped ends with "(This command ran under the read-only sandbox because this workspace's mission is read-only: …)" (`chat_engine::name_forced_mission`, `READ_ONLY_MISSION_NOTE`; the director's commands). _Support:_ `src/components/HeaderSandbox.tsx` via `ContextHeader.tsx` (`missionId`, `missionExecIsolation`, `missionGitIsolation` from `App.tsx`), `missionsStore.setExecIsolation`, `commands::update_mission`. _Entry:_ the header, with a mission.
- **Branch chip — middle-truncated, never clipped** — The branch renders through `<MidTruncate>` (`src/components/primitives/MidTruncate.tsx`, CSS `.octo-midtrunc`): the head ellipsizes into whatever room is left and the last 12 characters stay pinned, so `…-per-shard-copy` and `…-per-shard-guard` remain distinguishable. Always titled with the full string. The chip's wrappers (`.octo-prov` and the branch button) are `flex-1 min-w-0`, so the MidTruncate box elides into the definite width the eyebrow leaves, the same shape as the rail; sized from its own text, WebKit hard-cut the branch with room to spare. The chip shares one measuring pass with every other MidTruncate on screen (the rail's rows above all), and a row in that pass that can't be measured never leaves the branch held at `clip` (#865, #870): it is still cut on its own ellipsis. The grown wrappers are `pointer-events-none` and draw nothing: the `GitBranch` glyph (MidTruncate's optional `lead`), the brass hover wash, the hover colour and the focus ring all sit on the text-sized MidTruncate box (`pointer-events-auto`), so hovering blank space beside the name does nothing. No percentage `max-width` anywhere in that chain (a test enforces it). _Support:_ `ContextHeader.tsx`, `MidTruncate`, `.octo-prov` / `.octo-midtrunc*` in `src/styles.css`. _Entry:_ automatic.
- **Branch provenance popover** — Hover **or Tab** to the branch chip to get exactly what the ladder sheds: the full branch (selectable, with a copy button → toast "Branch name copied"), the base branch and the workspace's **Ports** range. It deliberately does not restate the changed-file count the tail already shows. Anchored to the header (not the chip) so it can never reach past the canvas, painted above it (`.octo-header` owns `z-index: 20`), and kept mounted and faded (`.octo-prov-pop`, `focus-within`) rather than conditionally mounted. _Support:_ `ContextHeader.tsx`; `copyToClipboard`. _Entry:_ hover/focus the branch chip.
- **Workspace ports (#1219)** — Each workspace owns a block of 10 local ports, so each workspace's dev server can read its own port from `OCTOPUSH_PORT` instead of two workspaces fighting over `localhost:3000` (nothing rebinds a port a server hard-codes). **Allocation:** the lowest free block from 40000–48999 (below macOS's ephemeral ports), taken the first time the workspace needs one — a Run terminal, the Talk shell, or the header asking — and stored in `workspaces.port_base` (nullable, additive migration; a partial unique index keeps two rows off the same block). A block whose base fails a `127.0.0.1` bind test is skipped. Every row holds its block, so archiving and restoring keep it; deleting the workspace (or its project) frees it for the next one. **Exports:** every Run terminal of the workspace (`spawn_terminal_session`, the setup terminal included, and `create_session`/`restore_active_sessions` through `ContextGuard::set_ports` for a root that is a workspace's worktree) and each Talk thread's shell, for `$` commands and the agent's `run_command` (`TalkShell::set_spawn_env` from `ChatEngine::set_shell_ports`), start with `OCTOPUSH_PORT` (the base), `OCTOPUSH_PORT_COUNT` (10) and `CONDUCTOR_PORT` (the base again, the name setup scripts imported from a Conductor repo read). A value the caller already set wins; a shell already running when the workspace got its block keeps the env it started with. Direct API tools, CLI stages and Routines don't get the variables yet. **Header:** the eyebrow ends with an `EthernetPort` glyph and `40020–40029` (`data-tour="header-ports"`, `.octo-fade-in`, never demoted), titled "Ports 40020–40029 for this workspace · terminals and the Talk shell get OCTOPUSH_PORT=40020 and OCTOPUSH_PORT_COUNT=10"; the provenance popover repeats it as **Ports**. Nothing shows when no block could be given. _Support:_ `workspace_ports.rs` (`pick_base`, `base_is_free`, `ensure`, `ensure_for_root`, `PortBlock`), `db::ensure_workspace_port_base`, `commands::workspace_ports`, `ipc.workspacePorts`, `hooks/useWorkspacePorts.ts`, `ContextHeader.tsx`, `talk_shell.rs`, `context_guard.rs`. _Entry:_ automatic.
- **The demotion ladder** — As the header narrows (it is its own `@container`), meta is shed in a fixed order, each step animating its own width instead of unmounting: **≤900px** `from <base>` folds (stays in the popover and tooltip), **≤780px** the parent ticket chain folds (still one click away in Jira), **≤640px** the status **name** becomes the category dot it already implies (name moves to the tooltip). A shed rung also leaves the tab order, so a keyboard user never lands on a control they cannot see. The active ticket key and the name line never demote — they are the floor. _Support:_ `.octo-header` / `.octo-demote*` / `.octo-status-*` in `src/styles.css`; `ContextHeader.tsx`. _Entry:_ automatic on canvas resize.
- **Working-tree indicator** — Right side shows a verdigris dot (titled "Working tree clean" / "N files changed…") and "N unstaged" when changes exist. _Support:_ `ContextHeader.tsx`. _Entry:_ automatic.
- **PR chip** — Per-state pull-request chip (open ●/draft ◐/merged ✓/closed ✕) with `PR · #<number>` and ↗; click opens the PR URL in the system browser. A hover-revealed copy button copies the PR URL to the clipboard (toast: "PR URL copied") without opening the browser. _Support:_ `ContextHeader.tsx` `PR_STATE_STYLE`; `openPrByWs` cache fed by `findPrForBranch` polled every 60s; copy via `copyToClipboard`. _Entry:_ click the chip; hover for the copy icon.
- **PR chip CI checks** — On an open or draft PR the chip carries a checks glyph for the head commit's CI: sage `CircleCheck` passing, amber `CircleDashed` pending, rouge `CircleX` failing; its tooltip says "Checks passing" / "Checks running" / "Checks failing: test, lint" (the failing checks by name). Failing also shows a `Wrench` "Fix failing checks…" button: it reads the tail of the failed Actions runs' logs (`gh run view <id> --log-failed`, at most 3 runs, 8k chars in total, the budget split evenly), then opens the Direct launcher on the same workspace with a brief naming the PR, the failed checks and that log tail. Everything in the brief that comes from GitHub is framed as data: the PR title and check names are kept on one line (newlines and control characters become spaces, backticks single quotes), the log sits in a fence one backtick longer than the longest backtick run inside it (so the log can't close it), and the brief states that the title, check names and log are untrusted and that the crew must not follow instructions inside them. If the launcher's brief already holds text, the fix-checks brief is added below it after a blank line instead of replacing it (asking for the same brief twice adds it once). The launcher keeps its usual crew selection; nothing starts until the user presses Start. While the logs load the wrench is disabled (`aria-busy`, tooltip "Reading the failed logs…") and ignores further clicks. If the logs can't be read, or no failing check is an Actions run, the brief still names the failed checks, just without the log section. With no `gh` and no token there is no glyph and nothing errors; cancelled, skipped and neutral checks count as passing. Through the REST fallback the check runs are read page by page (100 a page, up to 10 pages), so a failing check past the first 100 still counts. On the `gh` path, a `statusCheckRollup` that comes back with 100 or more entries (gh's cap) is re-read with `gh api --paginate repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{headRefOid}/check-runs` and rolled up with the rollup's commit statuses; if that read fails, the rollup's answer stands. _Support:_ `ContextHeader.tsx` `CHECKS_STYLE`; `lib/prChecks.ts` (`checksTitle`, `failedRunIds`, `fixChecksBrief`, `fenceFor`, `inlineSafe`); `App.tsx` `handleFixChecks` → `lib/fixChecks.ts` `prefillFixChecks` → `runsStore.setLauncherPrefill` (empty `pipelineId`, `append: true`; `PipelineSetup` applies it through `prefilledTask`) + `selectRun(ws, null)`; Rust `github.rs` `checks_from_gh_rollup` / `checks_from_rest_check_runs` / `more_check_run_pages` / `gh_rollup_may_be_capped` / `gh_check_runs_command` / `check_runs_from_gh_pages` / `checks_from_gh_rollup_and_runs` / `join_failed_logs`, `commands.rs` `rest_check_runs` / `gh_check_runs` / `pr_failed_check_logs`. _Entry:_ hover the glyph; click the wrench.

### AppTopBar
- **Active project name** — The parent project of the active workspace rides with the wordmark (`Octopush · ATLAS-API`), separated by a mute `·`: mono/caps/sage so the brand keeps the voice and the project reads as state, at most 180px so a long name can never push the centred mark off centre, `title="Project · <name>"`. A name that fits renders whole; a longer one (counted in mono characters, `projectNameFits`) is middle-truncated (`<MidTruncate>`, 12 characters pinned, design-system E1) in a fixed 180px box, so projects sharing an org prefix stay apart. Omitted entirely (divider included) until a project resolves. _Support:_ `src/components/AppTopBar.tsx` (`projectName` prop, fed from `App.tsx`'s `activeProject`). _Entry:_ always visible with a project open.
- **Live mascot (The Octo) + wordmark** — Centered in the top bar: a 20px `OctoMark` next to the `Octopush` wordmark (`.brand-wordmark`, Fraunces), whose body language mirrors global app state via `useMascotState` (`src/hooks/useMascotState.ts`), priority **blocked > working > idle** — any workspace flagged in `attentionStore` **or any Direct run `paused`** (checkpoint gate / budget park — waiting on the director, matching Mission Control's needs-you triage) → `blocked` (frozen, eyes half-mast: stillness is the signal); else any chat streaming (`chatStore.streamingByWs`) or Direct run `running` (`runsStore`) → `working` (paddling at double tempo, eyes scanning); else `idle` (slow float, staggered paddle, blinks). Tooltip/aria reports the exact state ("Octopush — 2 agents working"). Decorative-plus-informative; no click behavior. _Support:_ `src/components/AppTopBar.tsx`; `icons/OctoMark.tsx`; `hooks/useMascotState.ts`. _Entry:_ top bar, centered.
- **Fleet chip (runs tray)** — Global top-bar chip (left side), the entry to Mission Control. Attention-split priority chain (the same `needsYou` predicate Mission Control's Needs-you band uses; a run waiting for its Claude plan with an automatic resume scheduled, and no sibling halt, gate or question beside it, counts in flight, not needs-you): any run waiting on the director → brass `{n} needs you`, pulsing (`octo-stage-pulse`) — the chip's only pulse trigger, per Law 2's fleet scope; else any run running with nobody waiting → quiet hairline `{n} in flight` (sage, no pulse); else runs **settled this session or while the app was closed** (undismissed — see Mission Control's "While you were away") → verdigris `✓ {n} done` (Lucide `Check`, not a literal glyph) counting **completed runs only** — an aborted or failed run is never "done" (#845); its tooltip adds `, {m} ended` when some ended otherwise; with nothing completed but runs that aborted or failed, a muted `■ {n} ended` (Lucide `Square`, filled like the aborted `■`, tooltip "{n} runs ended without completing") — the entry no longer vanishes the moment background work finishes, and overnight crews are waiting there on launch. **No cost figure in this chip** — the combined live-cost figure lives only in the Mission Control header. Hidden only when the board is truly empty. Clicking opens the **Mission Control room** (which replaced the old A2 `MenuSurface` popover — one canonical surface for the fleet). Hydrated on launch via `list_active_runs` (and `list_runs_settled_since` for the settled count); kept live by `run://*` events. The needs-you count also shows on the Dock icon (§10 "Dock badge") and beside the menu bar Octo (§10 "Menu bar Octo"). `data-tour="fleet-chip"` on every variant. _Support:_ `src/components/RunsTray.tsx`; `lib/runStatus.ts` (`needsYou`, `fleetCounts`, `settledCounts` — front-end only; the Dock badge counts needs-you alone, so it has no Rust twin); `runsStore` (`settledAt`). _Entry:_ top bar, left side.
- **Mission Control (the missions cockpit)** — A full-screen **room** (`OverlayRoom`, Settings precedent) showing the whole fleet that needs the director: **every Direct run across every workspace** as a live crew card **plus mission-attention items** — a Talk conversation that finished streaming, **a Talk approval card waiting on you**, or a terminal that rang its bell (from `attentionStore.flagsByWs`, mapped to their mission) rendered as needs-you **`AttentionCard`s** (`MessageSquare`/`Terminal` glyph + "waiting in Talk"/"terminal bell" + mission title; an approval reads "approval in Talk" with "Approve or deny: git push --force" as its brief, stays until the card is answered, and its click opens the conversation the oldest card waits in (`chatStore.showPendingApproval`); a terminal flag whose `reason` came from Claude Code's hooks reads "waiting on permission" / "waiting on your input" with "Claude Code is waiting on …" as its brief, via `attentionCopy`; clicking jumps to that mission's Talk/Run surface). The board is a **discriminated union** (`{kind:"run"} | {kind:"attention"}`) so runs and attention share one FIFO needs-you band under the single-beacon law. Three triage bands with Law 1 ink grading, each opened by its mono caps eyebrow with 32px above it and 12px to its first card row (so the label sits with its own cards and the bands read as separate groups): **Needs you** (`paused` — gate / halted stage / budget park; full ink, brass border, FIFO by `statusSince`), **In flight** (`running`, plus a run **waiting for its Claude plan to reset** with an automatic resume scheduled and nothing else in it waiting for the director — `isPlanWaiting` (`planWait.resumeAt` set and `planWait.otherHold` false), no decision required, so it never takes the beacon; a sibling stage's real halt, gate or question beside the plan limit keeps the run in Needs you: glyph: a sage lucide `Hourglass` (tooltip *"Waiting for your Claude plan's window to reset"*) + `waiting`, sage live line `plan limit · resumes 19:40` (`data-tour="mission-control-plan-wait"`), hover actions **Resume now** (`Play`, `data-tour="mission-control-plan-resume-now"`; resumes the run's plan-limited stage by id, `planWait.planLimitedStage` over the run's detail, read first when the card has none, so a gate held beside it is never the one resolved; with no plan-limited stage left it resolves nothing) and **Don't resume automatically** (`TimerOff`) beside abort; once it waits for the director it is back in Needs you; `opacity-75`), **Settled** (runs that reached `completed`/`aborted` **this session — or while the app was closed** — they linger until dismissed, so nothing that finishes in the background silently vanishes; session-local `runsStore.settledAt`; `opacity-45` rising to `0.85` on hover/focus). **While you were away:** on launch `runsStore.loadSettledWhileAway` (once per session, so a dismissed card never comes back) calls the read-only `list_runs_settled_since` (default `since` = the `last_quit_at` marker in `app_meta`, stamped on `RunEvent::Exit`; 24 h ago when it's missing or unreadable; strictly after the marker; newest finish first, capped at 50) and seeds those runs onto the Settled band as ordinary cards stamped with their real finish time (no completion sweep replay), tracked in `runsStore.awayRunIds`. While any are still on the board the header shows one quiet line under the title row — `While you were away · {n} settled · saved $X` (mono, sage, `.octo-rise-in`; `data-tour="mission-control-away"`); runs with no baseline stay out of the saving, and when none can be priced it reads `unpriced`, never `$0.00`. Dismissing a card or clearing the band takes it off the line; so does re-running it (a re-run keeps the run id, so once the tracker sees it go live it leaves `awayRunIds` and its next settle is an ordinary session settle). Seeded cards sort on the band by their real finish time. Nothing shows while loading or when nothing settled. Each card: a mono meta row — status glyph/word (an in-flight card's `●` running dot is verdigris, matching the "in flight" count; brass stays with needs-you) · the **workspace name** (mute, truncates first; `data-tour="mission-control-card-workspace"`, omitted when the workspace isn't loaded), read as **`group · workspace`** when the mission sits in a mission group: the group's name in the same mute mono before it (`data-testid="mission-control-card-group"`, titled `Group: <name>`, `shrink-[100]`, so the group gives way before the workspace name does), and nothing for a loose mission or a group that is gone or belongs to another project (`missionGroupNameOf` in `lib/railGroups.ts`, the rail's `ownGroupId` rule); no filter chips, no new band, triage stays fleet-wide · on an in-flight or needs-you card (never a settled one), the **collision segment** (#732) when another live workspace of the project changes the same files — an amber (overlap) or rouge (confirmed conflict) `GitCompareArrows` + mute *"overlaps auth-flow · 2 files"* (*"conflicts with … · N files"*; *"· +N more"* when several collide), truncating before the status word, with every collision and its files on its tooltip; it is not a needs-you item and never takes the beacon (`data-tour="mission-control-card-collision"`; opening the room rescans the projects its crews work in) · a fixed-width **time-in-state** slot (`mm:ss` rolling to `Hh MMm`, tabular — not a "WAITING N MIN" eyebrow) · the **title: the run's task in serif** (intent glyph + task, truncated with the full task on its `title` tooltip; `data-tour="mission-control-card-task"`) — the task, not the workspace, is the title because many crews share one workspace and the task is what tells them apart · **`StageDots`** micro-track (replaces the retired roman-numeral track; one dot per stage, colored by status) · a **fixed-slot live line** (sage state text in both bands — on a needs-you card brass stays with the border and glyph; running → the stage's live activity ticker via `lib/liveLine.lastActivity`; gate → "{stage} holds the gate · loop n/m"; **`ask_director` block → a distinct `?` glyph + "{stage} asked you · waiting on your answer"** (not the gate wording — an answer form is waiting, not an approval) — the `?` card also carries an **inline answer**: a disclosure (`{n} questions · recommended answers`, `ChevronRight`, `data-tour="mission-control-ask-toggle"`) that expands on the grid-rows `Reveal` to each question with the crew's recommended answer, then **Accept recommended** (`data-tour="mission-control-ask-accept"`; sends every default through `answer_blocker` with `source: "mission_control"`, which writes the journal notice "✓ Director accepted the recommended defaults (from Mission Control)"; reads "Sending…" and ignores further clicks while in flight; when the send fails the card shows a rouge inline line, "Couldn't send the answers · open the run to answer"; hidden when any question has a blank default, since there's nothing to accept) and **Answer…** (jumps to the full answer form on the Direct canvas; hidden when the workspace isn't loaded). Clicks inside never trigger the card's jump, and nothing is ever accepted without the click; halt → first error line, amber `⟳ stalled` for transient; settled → savings epitaph) · ledger foot (spent mute, `data-tour="mission-control-card-spent"`; saved verdigris) with hover actions — **abort** (two-step confirm) or **dismiss** (settled). **Diff size (settled and needs-you cards):** after the spent figure the foot shows a quiet mono slot, `· +120 −40 · 6 files` (mute, tabular, `.octo-pop-in`, no brass, no pulse; `data-tour="mission-control-card-size"`), with a tooltip saying what was measured ("Against main: 6 files changed, +120 −40 lines"). It is the workspace's diff from its merge base with the workspace's base branch to the working tree — commits, staged and unstaged edits and untracked files together, what a reviewer of the crew's branch reads (`commands::workspace_diff_size` → `git_ops::diff_size`, git2 diff stats, no diff text; 5 s timeout). The base and merge base resolve exactly like the collision radar's: `fromBranch`, else the project's default branch (`collisions::workspace_base`), and the newest of the merge bases with `origin/<base>` and `<base>` (`collisions::resolve_merge_base`), so a stale local base never inflates the size. Renames are detected (a moved file counts only its edits). Untracked content is bounded like the radar's: an untracked directory with more than `MAX_UNTRACKED_DIR_FILES` (20) files counts as one file and is never read, and untracked files are line-counted only within 200 files / 4 MiB in total (binary files count no lines, like git); entries past those caps count as files, and the tooltip adds "(N large untracked entries not line-counted)". With no base, or one that no longer resolves, it is the uncommitted changes against HEAD, and the tooltip says "Uncommitted changes (no base branch)". A crew that changed nothing reads `· no changes`. It is measured **once per run state** (`stores/diffSizeStore.ts`, keyed `<runId>:<status>:<statusSince>`, so a paused card that later completes, or resumes and pauses again, is measured again, but re-renders, room re-opens and stage events never re-diff), only while the workspace is loaded; at most 2 measurements run at once (the rest queue), and the sizes of runs that leave the board are evicted (`prune`). Nothing shows while it is unknown, for an unloaded workspace, or when the worktree is gone or the diff fails — never a made-up zero. In-flight cards get no size. Runs in one workspace share its size. **Settled order:** the Settled band header carries a quiet toggle (`ArrowDownUp` + `Oldest first` / `Smallest first`, `data-tour="mission-control-settled-order"`; default Oldest first, today's order; session-local). Smallest first sorts by lines added + removed, and runs with nothing to show keep their oldest-first order after the measured ones (`orderSettled`); while any visible card's size is still loading the band stays in oldest-first order and sorts once when the last size lands, so the grid never jumps card by card. Nothing is ever merged or reviewed automatically. Law 2's fleet scope: only the **longest-waiting** needs-you card pulses (`octo-stage-pulse`, FIFO index 0); every other needs-you card keeps a static brass border. Card click **jumps** to the run's workspace + Direct surface (no checkpoint resolution on-card — judging a gate needs the artifact/diff, so deeper intents resolve to the jump; the one exception is accepting an `ask_director` block's recommended defaults, above). Header: band counts + a combined live-cost figure over **active** runs only (`saved $X · Y% under all-premium · spent $Z`, saved verdigris and spent ivory, not brass — this figure is Mission-Control-only; the `RunsTray` chip dropped it) + quiet `Plus` **"Send out a crew"** (→ Direct mode) + `ESC · CLOSE`. A crew completing gets the one sanctioned ceremony: a single solid `.octo-sweep` line (no gradient) across its ledger foot as it settles. Empty state: *"The floor is quiet."* + the dispatch CTA. Free users see their single run; starting a 2nd hits the existing `runs.parallel` gate → upgrade sheet. _Support:_ `src/components/MissionControl.tsx`, `src/stores/diffSizeStore.ts`, `commands::workspace_diff_size` + `git_ops::diff_size`, `src/components/direct/StageDots.tsx`, `primitives/OverlayRoom.tsx` (shared with Settings), `runsStore` (`settledAt`/`statusSince`/`dismissSettled`/`clearSettled`/`loadSettledWhileAway`/`awayRunIds`), `commands::list_runs_settled_since` + `db::{list_runs_settled_since, away_since, mark_quit}`, `lib/liveLine.ts` (ticker vocabulary shared with `RunFlow`); design record `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-09-mission-control-design.md`. _Entry:_ fleet chip click · `⌘⇧M`.
- **Cross-machine run History (Pro-real Part B / B1+B2)** — A `History` button (top bar, right side) opens a global **History sheet** (`ModalShell`) listing the signed-in **Pro** user's terminal Direct runs **from every machine they've signed in on** — task, status glyph/word, cost, machine name, and relative time — read-only, with a **Refresh** control. Rows carry the depth-of-field row optic (`opacity-45`, rising to `0.85` on hover/focus). For **Free / signed-out** users the button instead opens the **upgrade sheet** (`feature: "history.sync"`), an upsell. **Opt-in, off by default** (Settings → Account → Sync → "Sync run history across your Macs"; `settings.json` `historySyncEnabled`, absent ⇒ `false`, so existing Pro users stay off until they choose). **Per account, not per Mac:** the opt-in is bound to the Clerk user id that granted it (`syncOwner`) — any other signed-in user (or nobody) reads it as OFF, so a second person signing in on the same Mac can never backfill the first person's runs into their account — and **sign-out clears both opt-ins and the owner**. `set_sync_pref` is the **only writer**: `save_settings` (the panes' whole-file read-modify-write) carries the opt-ins and owner over from disk, so a stale save can't flip them. With it off, **nothing is sent or fetched**: the orchestrator push, launch backfill, pull and drill-in all short-circuit, every network fn in `sync.rs` re-checks the opt-in itself (`PushOutcome::Disabled` / "History sync is off" error), and the sheet shows a **"History sync is off."** state pointing to Settings › Account (Refresh disabled). Turning it on runs the one-shot backfill + pull (single-flight per kind — a rapid on/off/on shares one run — via `lib/syncBackfill.ts`), and **that first backfill's outcome is toasted** ("Run history is syncing · N runs from this Mac uploaded." / "Couldn't sync your run history · Sync stays on and retries at the next launch."; `history_sync_push_all` now errors when the metadata push itself fails); launch backfills stay silent. Turning it off stops future uploads; already-synced data **stays on the server** (no delete endpoint yet) and the UI says so. _Mechanism:_ when a run reaches a terminal state (`completed`/`aborted`) and sync is on, the orchestrator **fire-and-forgets** a push of that run's **metadata** (task/status/cost/summed tokens/per-stage role+model+status/timestamps/machine name) to the Octopush **sync API** (`octopush-api.vercel.app/api/sync-runs`, same Vercel project as billing), authenticated with the Clerk **access token** (refreshed if expired) and Pro-re-checked **server-side**; the server (Turso/libSQL) owns each row by the authenticated Clerk `sub` (never trusts the client) and upserts by run id (terminal runs are immutable → append-only, no conflicts). On launch (Pro + opted in) and the moment the user turns sync on, the app **backfills** this machine's terminal runs in one capped batch, then **pulls** the full history into a **local read-only `synced_runs` mirror** (kept separate from the FK-constrained `runs` table — pulled runs have no local workspace). **The pull pages (#799):** `sync::pull_runs` sends its first `GET /api/sync-runs` with no query (as before), then follows the service's `next_cursor` (`?cursor=` only) through every page (newest run first by the run's own `created_at`, octopush-api#27), and only a complete set reaches `replace_synced_runs`: any failed or unreadable page, a repeated cursor, more than `MAX_RUN_PULL_PAGES` (50) pages, or the toggle going off mid-pull fails the whole pull, and `history_sync_pull` then keeps and lists the existing mirror. A run seen on two pages is kept once. An older service that answers `{ runs }` with no cursor is one page. The run pull never sends `since` (it replaces the mirror, so it is always a full pull). **Run size cap (#799):** `push_runs` passes every run through `sync::cap_run_payload`, which keeps each run's JSON at most `MAX_RUN_PAYLOAD_BYTES` (250,000; the service refuses the whole batch with 413 when one run is over 256 KiB): a run under it is untouched; otherwise the machine/workspace names (1,024 bytes) and the status and stage role/model/status (256 bytes) are capped, then the `task` is cut to fit (but not below 4,096 bytes while stages remain), each cut field ending in "… (truncated)" (char-boundary safe); if that is not enough, trailing stage summaries are replaced by **one summary stage in the existing shape** — role `… (N stages truncated)`, status `truncated`, no model, the dropped stages' summed cost (so the stage costs still add up) — and only then is the task cut further; ids and timestamps never change. The one field that may be added is the summary stage's `includes_unpriced: true` (#978), sent only when a folded stage had no cost and a model this Mac can't price (`token_engine::prices_in` against the catalog, History's own rule), so a run that isn't cut, and every other stage, goes out byte for byte as before; an older payload reads it as false, and the service stores the run blob verbatim. The task keeps at least `TASK_FLOOR_BYTES` (4,096) while stages can still be folded (tested at, just above and well above the floor). **Drill-in (B2):** clicking a row fetches that run's **full story lazily** — per-stage **journals** (LiveEntry-shaped, rendered as inert mono lines with `iconForTool`), **artifact texts**, and **diff snapshots** (`DiffViewer`) — pushed once at terminal time (journals capped 200 entries/48KB per stage newest-win, artifacts 16KB, diffs 96KB head+tail; server backstop 1.5MB/blob, 2k rows/owner in `synced_run_details`) and fetched on demand (`history_run_detail` → `/api/sync-run-detail`; session-cached incl. the "none" answer). Only a `404` whose body is `{"error":"no_detail"}` (octopush-api#27) reads as "none" (`sync::is_no_detail_body`); any other 404 (a moved route, a proxy page) is a fetch error the sheet can retry. The detail view is a `FadeSwap` list↔detail drill-in with `StageDots`, role icons, and honest states (loading / retryable fetch error / "synced before journals were kept"). Synced stages carry no price flag, so the sheet asks `unpriced_models` once per distinct model set: a stage whose model this Mac can't price and whose cost is `$0` reads mute "unpriced" (tooltip `unpricedTitle`) instead of `$0.00`, and a run total with any such stage — list row and detail header — gets a mute " + unpriced" (a stage with a cost, priced on its origin Mac, never counts); when every such stage is unpriced and the total is `$0`, the total itself reads mute "unpriced", never "$0.00 + unpriced". A run whose trailing stages were folded into one summary stage to fit the sync size limit keeps the flag (#978): the summary stage's `includes_unpriced` (see "Run size cap") counts as an unpriced stage in the list row and the detail header, and the tooltip says stages were folded into one summary to fit the sync limit, since their models didn't travel (after `unpricedTitle` when other unpriced models can be named). Synced values render as **inert text** (never HTML). Gated end-to-end by the **opt-in AND** `history.sync` (`sync::sync_active(SyncKind::History)` — opt-in read first, so with it off the keychain-backed entitlement isn't even consulted; `AppError::UpgradeRequired` for Free, then "History sync is off" on pull/detail; no-op push otherwise; server 403). _Support:_ `src/components/HistorySheet.tsx`, `historyStore`, `syncPrefsStore`, `AppTopBar` History button, `App` launch sync (fires on entitled ∧ opted-in); `src-tauri/src/sync.rs` (`SyncKind`, `sync_active`/`opted_in`, `SyncRun`, `build_run_payload`, `cap_run_payload`, `push_runs`/`pull_runs`, `is_no_detail_body`); contract tests against copies of the API's fixtures in `src-tauri/tests/fixtures/sync-api/` (`tests.rs` `sync_contract_tests`), `settings.rs` (`historySyncEnabled`, `sync_opted_in`), `auth::current_access_token`, `orchestrator::sync_run_history` (3 terminal sites + bridge), `db` (`app_meta` + `machine_id`, `synced_runs` mirror, `list_terminal_runs`); commands `history_list`/`history_sync_pull`/`history_sync_push_all`/`get_sync_prefs`/`set_sync_pref`. _Entry:_ top bar → History. See [`docs/premium/pro-real-part-b-history-sync.md`](premium/pro-real-part-b-history-sync.md).
- **Library sync (Pro, opt-in)** — A signed-in Pro user who turns on **"Sync custom pipelines & roles"** (Settings → Account → Sync; `settings.json` `librarySyncEnabled`, **off by default** incl. for existing users) has their **custom pipelines and roles follow them across machines**. With it off no save/delete hook, launch heal-push or pull touches the network (call sites gate on `sync::sync_active(SyncKind::Library)`; `push_library_items`/`pull_library` re-check the opt-in themselves); turning it on runs the heal-push + pull at once; turning it off stops future uploads (the heal-push re-checks the opt-in between chunks) and leaves already-synced items on the server. Same per-account binding, sign-out reset, `set_sync_pref`-only writer, single-flight backfill and first-backfill toast ("Library is syncing" / "Couldn't sync your library"; `library_sync_push_all` errors when a chunk fails) as run-history sync. Mutable templates ⇒ **per-item last-writer-wins** on an `updated_at` stamp (new column on `pipelines`/`roles`, bumped by every save; RFC3339 — lexicographic = chronological), **enforced in SQL on the server** so racing machines never regress a newer edit. Deletions travel as **tombstones** (delete on machine A propagates; an edit made *after* the delete revives the item — newest intent wins; a role still in use locally survives a tombstone). **Push:** fire-and-forget after every `save_pipeline`/`delete_pipeline`/`save_role`/`delete_role` + a whole-library heal-push on launch. **Refused items stay unsent and are named (#799):** before sending, `push_library_items` refuses locally any item whose `data` JSON is over `MAX_LIBRARY_ITEM_BYTES` (64,000 bytes, the service's limit, measured by `library_item_bytes` so it never undercounts), with the service's own reason `oversize`; it never leaves the Mac. It reads the service's additive `rejected: [{id, kind, reason}]` (octopush-api#27; `kind` matched when present, since a pipeline and a role can share an id), and keeps every refused item in an unsent list (`SyncStatus.libraryRejected`: kind, id and reason code only, at most 50, in memory and in `settings.json` `lastSyncAttempt.libraryRejected`) until a later push of that item is stored; a failed chunk leaves its items as they were. The library's "Last sent · N items" now counts the items the service stored; a failed attempt still counts the items attempted. A pre-#27 service answering `{ ok, count }` reads as "all stored"; an unreadable 2xx answer (not a JSON object, or `rejected` not a list; `read_library_push_answer`) counts as a failed attempt: none of that chunk's items is taken as stored and earlier refusals stay listed. The list is dropped with the toggle (off, on again, another account) and on sign-out. **Pull:** on launch (once entitled) — **roles first** (pipelines validate against them), pipelines re-validated on apply (invalid/unparseable items are skipped, never written), then the pipeline/roles stores reload. **Incremental pull (#823):** each `GET /api/sync-library` answer's `next_since` is stored per account (`settings.json` `libraryPullSince { owner, nextSince }`, `owner` = the `syncOwner` it was stored for; owned by `sync::library_since`, carried over whole-file saves) once the items are applied (`commit_library_pull`, only while library sync is still on **and still owned by the account the pull began under** — `LibraryPull.owner`, re-checked under the settings write lock by `set_library_since_for` — so a pull racing an account switch stores nothing for the new account), and sent as `?since=` on the next pull, which then returns only the items and tombstones the service received since. It is a full pull (no `since`) when nothing is stored (first pull, sign-in), after an account switch, turning library sync off or on again, or sign-out (all drop the stored value), when the stored value is older than 90 days (tombstones older than that are pruned server-side) or unreadable (`library_since_usable`), and after `400 {"error":"bad_since"}` (the value is dropped and the pull retried once without it; any other 400 is an error and keeps it). **No `next_since` is kept — the stored one is dropped, so the next pull is full — when anything could have been missed** (`library_since_to_keep`): an item this build couldn't apply for a parse, validation or DB error (`apply_pulled_library` returns `LibraryApply { applied, skipped }`; LWW losses, id mismatches, builtin ids and in-use roles don't count), an envelope it couldn't read, or one of a kind it doesn't know (`LibraryPull.unreadable`; `sync::read_library_items` keeps only `LIBRARY_KINDS`, `pipeline` and `role`, #978), or an answer at the service's per-GET cap of 2,000 items (`LIBRARY_PULL_MAX_ITEMS`; the library GET has no paging yet). So an item saved by a newer build comes back once this Mac can read it. Items are applied exactly as before (`commands::apply_pulled_library`, per-item LWW): an item missing from an incremental pull is unchanged, never deleted — only a tombstone deletes. An older service that ignores `since` returns the whole library and no `next_since`, which applies the same way and makes the next pull a full one. No new field is sent. Builtins **never travel** in either direction (a pulled item claiming a builtin id/key is refused). Server: `/api/sync-library` (Turso `synced_library_items`, byte cap 64,000 bytes/item — an oversized item is refused and listed in `rejected`, never vetoes the batch; quota = 1000 **net** rows/owner counting inserts only — edits always land; tombstones pruned after 90 days; stamps validated: unparseable or >24h-future are skipped). Client pushes are **chunked** (≤200/POST) so a large library's heal never 413s wholesale. A role tombstone refused because the role is in use locally **bumps the local stamp**, so the next push genuinely revives the item cloud-side. **Known limitation:** authoring or deleting via `octopush-mcp` (a pipeline or, now, a role) bypasses the push hook (the MCP process can't push) — an MCP-deleted item resurrects on the next pull, and an MCP-authored one won't propagate; touch it once in-app to make it stick. Gated by the opt-in AND `library.sync` (Pro; `UpgradeRequired` on pull for Free, then "Library sync is off"). _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/sync.rs` (`SyncKind`, `SyncPipeline`, `SyncLibraryItem`, tombstones, `LibraryRejection`, `apply_library_rejections`, `LibraryPull`, `library_since`, `commit_library_pull`), `settings.rs` (`LibraryPullSince`, `library_since_for_owner`, `set_library_since`), `db` (`list_custom_*_for_sync`, `upsert_*_from_sync`, `pipeline_stage_drafts`, LWW stamps), commands `library_sync_push_all`/`library_sync_pull` (`apply_pulled_library`) + mutation hooks, `get_sync_prefs`/`set_sync_pref`; `syncPrefsStore`; `App` launch effect (fires on entitled ∧ opted-in). _Entry:_ Settings → Account → Sync (Pro).
- **Scratchpad toggle** — `NotebookPen` button toggles the scratchpad split. _Support:_ `AppTopBar.tsx`; `scratchpadStore.toggleOpen`. _Entry:_ top bar, right side.
- **Settings button** — `Settings` icon opens Settings on the General tab. _Support:_ `AppTopBar.tsx`. _Entry:_ top bar, right side.

### CanvasSplit (scratchpad split)
- **Resizable canvas/scratchpad split** — When the scratchpad is open, splits the canvas with a draggable divider (20–80% clamp); both columns stay in the DOM (display/width/visibility toggled, never conditionally unmounted) to avoid remounting terminals/duplicating input. 200ms width transition. _Support:_ `src/components/CanvasSplit.tsx`; `ScratchpadEditor`. _Entry:_ scratchpad toggle in top bar.

### Companion (right panel)
- **Always-mounted, resizable Companion** — Right panel persists width in `localStorage` (default 312, clamp 280–600); drag the 4px left-edge handle to resize, double-click to reset. _Support:_ `src/App.tsx`; `src/components/Companion.tsx`. _Entry:_ left-edge drag handle.
- **Collapse to slim strip** — Collapses to a 56px strip carrying only the expand control, persisted; expand/collapse buttons. Mode switching is unaffected by the collapse — the mode band above the canvas is always on screen. _Support:_ `App.tsx`; `Companion.tsx`. _Entry:_ collapse button / expand button on the strip.
- **Panel header** — "Companion" eyebrow (mono caps) + the collapse control. _Support:_ `Companion.tsx`. _Entry:_ top of the expanded panel.
- **Mode-specific content crossfade** — Below the shared header/Jira block, mode content crossfades via `FadeSwap` keyed on mode. _Support:_ `Companion.tsx`; `src/components/primitives/FadeSwap.tsx`. _Entry:_ mode switch.
- **Talk Companion** — Two sections on one chrome, or one room: **Chats** (`CompanionHistory`) + **Conversation** (`CompanionContext`: context meter, ledger cost, the mission's logbook line, capabilities, budgets); while a sub-agent is focused the panel is that sub-agent's room (`CompanionCrewJournal`) and nothing else. Every Talk and Run section hangs on `CompanionSection` — a 36px mono eyebrow that folds its body (grid-rows `Reveal`, remembered in `localStorage` under `octo.companion.section.<key>`), an optional `meta` at the eyebrow's right (mute, its own case, the part that truncates), one hairline between sections, no framed cards inside the panel. **Run** — `CompanionRun`: Context · Changes · Mission, on the same `CompanionSection` chrome (see "Companion · Run"; navigation lives on the mode band's session line). **Review** — `CompanionReview`. **Direct** — `CompanionRuns` + `LogbookCard`. _Support:_ `Companion.tsx`. _Entry:_ per mode.

### Companion · Chats (CompanionHistory)
- **Collapsible section** — `Chats · N` eyebrow (`CompanionSection`, key `chats`) folds the list; the `+` sits on the eyebrow bar. _Support:_ `CompanionHistory.tsx`, `CompanionSection.tsx`.
- **Conversation thread list** — Lists persisted chat threads for the workspace; only the open thread is boxed (panel-2 fill, brass-dim border, `aria-current`, `data-active`) — every other row gets a hover-only brass wash, so a hovered row never reads as a second selection; the border is reserved on every row so nothing shifts; the title fills the row and wraps to two lines (`line-clamp-2`), with the full title as the row's `title` tooltip; the title crossfades in when it changes (`.octo-fade-in`, keyed by the title: a generated, regenerated or renamed title, #1137); the row actions (pin · rename · regenerate title · export · delete; a tour pointing at one shows them, as a hover would) overlay the row's right end on a panel fade (`.octo-row-actions-fade`: the row's own fill — panel, panel-2 on the open row, plus the brass-ghost wash on a hovered row) and are revealed by opacity on hover or keyboard focus (`focus-within`, 220ms, `--ease-octo`, inset focus rings; the hover wash fades with them on the row's own timing, via the registered `--row-wash`), so they reserve no space beside the title and revealing them never rewraps it; the overlay itself is `pointer-events-none` (only its buttons catch the pointer), so a click on the end of the title under its fade still opens the chat; meta is the last activity time — the clock time today (`14:32`), then `YESTERDAY`, `3D AGO`, a date (ticks each minute). List carries `data-tour="companion-chats-list"`. _Support:_ `src/components/CompanionHistory.tsx`; threads from `chatStore`. _Entry:_ Talk mode panel.
- **New / select / delete conversation** — `+` starts a new thread; row click switches active thread; hover/focus-revealed `X` deletes a thread. _Support:_ `CompanionHistory.tsx`; `chatStore.newThread/selectThread`, `App.handleDeleteChat`. _Entry:_ Chats eyebrow / rows.
- **Empty state** — "No active chats." when none. _Support:_ `CompanionHistory.tsx`.

### Companion · Conversation (CompanionContext)
- **Context meter** — "context X / limit" plus a brass progress bar (warning past 80%, rouge past 95%); numerator is the last assistant turn's **`contextTokens`** — the size of the turn's LAST prompt, uncached + cached + written (rows from before it was recorded fall back to their uncached `inputTokens`), denominator the active model's `maxContext` (default 200k). Both counts use the one shared context formatter, `formatContextTokens` (`4k`, `200k`, `1M`, `1.5M`; rounding never yields `1000k`), which the Talk header tail, the model pickers (`ModelPicker`, `ModelSwitcher`) and Settings › Models' `ctx` meta use too, so context reads the same everywhere. The meter is the shared `ContextMeter` (`contextTone`), which Run's Context section draws too. _Support:_ `src/components/CompanionContext.tsx`, `src/components/ContextMeter.tsx`, `lib/cost.ts` (`formatContextTokens`), `App.tsx` (`lastTurnInputTokens`); `ipc.listModels`. _Entry:_ Talk Companion.
- **Conversation cost — from the ledger** — `spent` (brass; tooltip: model calls and the share of prompt tokens served from the cache), `of which sub-agents`, and `saved vs all-strong · $ · %` (verdigris) — all read from `get_thread_cost(thread_id)` (`db::thread_cost` over `spend_events.thread_id`/`origin`), so the figure is the same one Settings › Usage shows: the director's rounds **and** every sub-agent attempt, cache-aware. `saved` is the same tokens priced on the strong tier's model (`settings.model_tiers.strong` → `prices_for`), shown only when that tier is priced and the saving is real. Calls on an **unpriced** model are in neither figure: an `unpriced` line names the model(s), and when every call is unpriced `spent` reads "unpriced" rather than "$0.00". Re-read when a turn settles or a sub-agent continuation ends (`useThreadCost`) — never per row. Replaces the message-row `SavingsLedger` (which priced turns as uncached input and could not see the ledger). _Support:_ `CompanionContext.tsx` (`costLines`, `usd`), `commands::get_thread_cost`, `db::thread_cost`, `ThreadCost`. _Entry:_ Talk Companion, after the first billed call.
- **Unstaged & tool-call counters** — "unstaged" = changed-file count (click → Review); "tool calls" = live count of `role:"tool"` messages in the active chat (ticks in real time). _Support:_ `CompanionContext.tsx`. _Entry:_ Talk Companion.
- **Mission line** — `mission · 2h 10m · $4.20 · saved $1.10` (the free per-mission Logbook slice, `useMissionLogbook`; "no work yet" until something is recorded), click → the Logbook Room (`Maximize2` glyph). Direct mode keeps the standalone `LogbookCard` on the same hook, which re-reads when a TALK turn settles, a run changes status, or a transcript ingest pass changes the ledger (`octo://spend-ingested`). _Support:_ `hooks/useMissionLogbook.ts`, `CompanionContext.tsx`, `LogbookCard.tsx`. _Entry:_ Talk Companion (with a mission).
- **Instructions row — which files this conversation follows** — `follows` + one mono name per instruction file Talk and its sub-agents carry (the worktree's CLAUDE.md chain, or its AGENTS.md; see Talk "The project's instructions"), in the order they're sent, rendered only when there is one (`data-tour="companion-follows"`), above the `can use` row. The row's tooltip says what the files are and gives one line per file: `CLAUDE.md · 3k tokens`, `· trimmed to fit` when it was capped, "left out, the instructions were already at their limit", or `skipped: outside the project` / `skipped: over 4 MiB` for a file that was named but never read. A name that wasn't sent (left out or skipped) is struck through in mute. Past 20 skipped files, the rest are counted: the row ends with `+N more` and the tooltip with `+N more skipped`. Read with `list_project_instructions(workspacePath)` (`project_instructions::InstructionList { files: [{ label, path, tokens, trimmed, skipped }], moreSkipped }`, no file content) on a worktree change and when a turn starts or settles, so an edited file shows; a late answer for another worktree is dropped. _Support:_ `src/components/CompanionInstructions.tsx` (`instructionsTitle`), `commands.rs` (`list_project_instructions`), `project_instructions.rs`. _Entry:_ Talk Companion › Conversation.
- **Capabilities row — which MCP servers this conversation can use** — `can use` + one chip per MCP server configured for the workspace (user ∪ project `.claude/mcp.json`, reachable or not), rendered only when there is one (`data-tour="companion-can-use"`; the label's tooltip says the servers come from Settings › Integrations and the project's `.claude/mcp.json`). **Default: every server is on in every conversation.** Each chip is a toggle (`aria-pressed`): a click turns that server **off for this conversation only**, a second click turns it back on. The off list is stored per thread (`chat_threads.mcp_disabled`, a JSON array; NULL, as on every row from before the column, = all on), read with `get_thread_mcp_disabled` and changed one server at a time with `set_thread_mcp_server(thread, server, off)`, which reads and writes the list under the DB lock and returns it, so two toggles never lose each other. In the Companion (`mcpScopeStore.toggle`) the chip changes at once; a thread's writes go out one at a time in click order and the last answer is the list shown; a failed write re-reads the stored list; clicks are ignored (`aria-disabled`) until the open thread's own list has loaded, so a click right after a thread switch never acts on the previous thread's state; a load that started before a click never overwrites it. A fork keeps its conversation's off list. Renaming a server in Settings carries it over: every conversation that had the old name off has the new one off (`Db::rename_thread_mcp_servers`, all rows in one transaction, after `mcp.json` is written; `mcp::real_renames` keeps only renames the save really made), except in a conversation whose project's own `.claude/mcp.json` still defines the old name (`project_config`), where it still means that server. A failure there is logged, never fails the save: the file is written, so the servers are reset and the change event goes out regardless. **Live status per chip** from `list_mcp_server_status(worktree)` (`McpRegistry::status`, `mcp/scope.rs`), which reads the registry and spawns nothing: the `Server` icon is verdigris when connected, rouge when its last start failed, mute when not started yet or off (never brass); the name is ivory, or mute and struck through when off. The chip's `title` says it in words: "docs-server · connected · 12 tools · click to turn off in this conversation", "· not started yet · it starts on first use", "· failed: <first line of the reason>", or "· off in this conversation · click to turn it back on". **Trust (#1243):** a server the user trusts, or one with tools always allowed, shows a mute `ShieldCheck` after its name (`.octo-pop-in`; not while off), and its title adds "· runs every tool without asking in Edit freely; one it marks destructive still asks (Settings › Integrations revokes it)", or names the tools (`trustTitle`, `trustFor`); read with `list_mcp_trust(worktree)` alongside the status and on `mcp://trust-changed`, so a server the project's `.claude/mcp.json` defines shows none. With no conversation yet the chips show their status but don't toggle. **Refresh:** the row re-reads the status on a workspace or thread change, when a turn starts or settles, and on `mcp://config-changed` (Settings saved the MCP config) or `mcp://status-changed` (Reconnect, or a turn's discovery started or failed to start servers) via `ipc.onMcpChanged`; the last reading stays while a reload runs. The row also shows when there is no server but there are skills or sub-agent types (below). _Support:_ `CompanionMcpScope.tsx` (`chipTitle`, `chipTone`), `stores/mcpScopeStore.ts`, `CompanionContext.tsx`, `mcp/scope.rs` (`McpServerStatus`, `status`, `list_tools_except`), `db::{thread_mcp_disabled, set_thread_mcp_disabled, set_thread_mcp_server_off}`; tests `CompanionMcpScope.test.tsx`, `talk_mcp_scope_tests`; demo scenario `talk-mcp`. _Entry:_ Talk Companion.
- **Capabilities row — the skills and sub-agent types this conversation can use** — after the MCP chips, two quiet mono counts in mute: `skills · N` (`data-tour="companion-can-use-skills"`) and `agents · N` (`data-tour="companion-can-use-agents"`); a count is left out at zero (built-in agents mean `agents` is almost always there). Each opens a menu below it (`MenuSurface`, `.octo-menu-enter`; Escape or a press outside closes it, a second press on the count too). **Skills:** one row per skill with `/name`, its one-line description and where it comes from (`project`, `user`); a click adds `/name ` to the Talk draft (`chatStore.queueDraftInsert`, the hand-off "Ask Talk about this" uses) and closes the menu — the skill runs with that message, as when typed. **Agents:** one row per sub-agent type Talk's `Agent` tool can run under, with its description, its source (`built-in`, `project`, `user`) and a line with its tier or model and its tools: `fast tier` for a tier or a `haiku`/`sonnet`/`opus` alias, the model id as written, or `Talk's model` when the definition sets none (or `inherit`); the tools listed, `every tool` when the definition doesn't restrict them, or `no tools`. Read-only: an agent row changes nothing. Read with `list_skills` and `list_subagent_types` (`skills::agents::scan_agent_definitions`, project ∪ user ∪ built-in) on a worktree change and when a turn starts or settles; the last reading stays while a reload runs and when a re-read fails (a failed first read for a worktree leaves that count out), and a late answer for another worktree is dropped. _Support:_ `CompanionCatalog.tsx` (`useTalkCatalog`, `CompanionCatalogCounts`, `sourceLabel`, `agentModelLabel`, `agentToolsLabel`), `CompanionMcpScope.tsx`; tests `CompanionCatalog.test.tsx`. _Entry:_ Talk Companion › Conversation.
- **Budget rows** — `budget · today` / `budget · this month`: spend vs budget with a bar that turns warning/rouge at 80%/100%; workspace budget preferred over global; rendered only when a matching budget exists; click → Settings › Usage. _Support:_ `CompanionContext.tsx`; `budgetsStore`. _Entry:_ Talk Companion (when budgets set).

### Run · session navigation (line · captions · switcher)

Terminal navigation lives in the **mode band**, not in the Companion: collapsing the Companion must never remove the only way to change session. The **session line** there replaced the 44px rail on the canvas's left and the band's one-session anchor (2026-11-18), and each session's name, state and actions now have one home: its pane's caption. Design record of the vocabulary that carried over (session roles, the ⌥ peek, the bell marker): [`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-15-run-terminal-navigation-design.md`](superpowers/plans/2026-08-15-run-terminal-navigation-design.md).

- **Session line (the mode band's right track)** — One 24px cell per open session, in session order, then `+` (*Open a new session*; it opens in the focused pane), a hairline, and the **layout button**. A cell shows the session's **role icon** and gives each fact one channel: the icon's **ink is presence** (ivory in a pane, mute off screen; never brass, also while busy); a reserved 2px underline whose **colour is focus** (brass on the focused pane's session, the line's only brass besides attention) and whose **motion is work** (`.rail-bar-running-x`, the workspace rail's marching idiom laid horizontally: sage, or brass on the focused session; a solid bar with reduced motion). **Click** (or `Enter`/`Space`) focuses the session's pane when it is on screen, else shows it in the focused pane; **⌥-click** (or `⌥Enter`) opens it beside: the empty seat, else a new pane up to four, else the focused pane. The whole line is **one tab stop** (`role="toolbar"`, on the focused session's cell): `←`/`→`/`Home`/`End` move focus across the cells, `+N`, `+` and the layout button without switching. The cells are a `tablist`: `aria-selected` on the focused pane's session, `aria-current` on every session on screen. Cells enter with `.octo-fade-in`. Rendered only when the workspace has ≥1 session (otherwise the band reads "No terminals"). Dragging a cell reorders the sessions (see "Drag to reorder sessions" below). _Support:_ `src/components/run/SessionLine.tsx`; `terminalsStore` (`setActive`, `openBeside`, `createTerminal`), `terminalLayoutStore`, `attentionStore`; `styles.css` (`.rail-bar-running-x`). _Entry:_ Run mode band.
- **Drag to reorder sessions** — Drag a session line cell along the line and drop it on another cell to move the session there; the cells it passes make room with a horizontal-only translation on the house curve (`dur.quick`, `ease.octo`), and the dragged cell lifts onto the panel ground. A press that travels under 5px stays a click, and the click that ends a drag is swallowed, so a drag never switches the pane's session. The new order is the session order everywhere: the cells, `⌘⌥1`–`⌘⌥9` (and their instant label, ⌥ peek and pane-caption hints), `⌘⌥←/→` and the ⌘⌥K switcher. It applies at once and is saved through `reorder_terminals`; a failed save puts the old order back with a "Couldn't reorder sessions" toast (also when a live change such as a busy tick landed meanwhile; only a newer reorder or a session opened or closed since is left as it is). Panes keep their sessions. The drop's place is taken in the full session order, so with the line capped at eight cells, a cell dropped on a focused session that sits past the others lands at that session's place and can go into `+N`. Pointer only, and not on a folded line (one cell). _Support:_ `run/SessionLine.tsx` (`SortableCell`, dnd-kit `PointerSensor` with a 5px distance), `terminalsStore.reorderTerminals` (`orderSessions`, `moveSession`), `commands::reorder_terminals` → `Db::set_terminal_order` (renumbers `terminals.position` in one transaction; ids of other workspaces or unknown ids are ignored, and sessions left out keep their order after the listed ones).
- **Number peek (⌥ hold)** — Holding **⌥** flips every cell of the session line from its icon to its `⌘⌥N` jump number (the first nine), so the shortcut is taught exactly when the hand is already on the modifier; window blur resets it. ⌥ only, never a bare ⌘ — otherwise every ⌘C/⌘S would flash the line. Nothing lives only behind the gesture: the number is in the instant label, on the pane caption and in the switcher. _Support:_ `hooks/useModifierPeek.ts`, `SessionLine.tsx`.
- **Instant label** — Hover a cell, or focus it from the keyboard, and a label opens under it at once: the session's name in sans, then in mono what it is doing (the live command while busy, else the role phrase; *waiting on permission* / *waiting on your input* first; a setup run until it succeeds; `starting` or `didn't start`; `· rang` after it when the session's bell rang — a busy session with no resolvable command reads "running", never "shell at the prompt") and its `⌘⌥N`. Text only, no actions: those live on the pane caption.
