It enters with `.octo-fade-in` and leaves with `.octo-fade-out` after an 80ms grace, so crossing from one cell to the next moves the label instead of blinking it. Portalled and `fixed` under the measured cell, right-aligned to it, so nothing clips it. `aria-hidden`: the cell's accessible name is the same text (`<name> — <doing> · ⌘⌥N`), and the cell has no native `title`. It also goes on any click, and whenever the line may have moved under it: the panes changed, the band resized, another session took the focus, or a session opened or closed and the cells shifted. A cell focused by a press, on its way to a click, opens no label; one the keyboard opened stays until focus leaves. _Support:_ `SessionLine.tsx` (`useInstantLabel`), `lib/sessionDoing.ts`.
- **Per-session bell marker** — A 5px brass dot on the session line cell of the session that rang while hidden (`attentionStore` flags now carry a `terminalId`). Static, not pulsing — the mode switcher's pulse already owns the cross-mode signal and Law 2 allows one pulsing element per scope. It clears only when the user actually focuses **that** session, not merely on entering Run mode (`lib/attentionFocus.ts` — a pure, tested rule; flags with no terminal id, e.g. chat pings, still clear on the mode alone), and **closing the session clears it too**, so a marker can never outlive the thing it points at and strand the workspace in Mission Control's needs-you band. Bell and idle pings keep **one flag per workspace** — a newer ping replaces the older. **Claude Code's hook waits are per session** (`attentionStore.waitsByTerminal`): when several off-screen sessions wait on permission or input, every one of their cells carries the dot (its title reads *Claude Code is waiting on you in this session*), and the instant label (and the cell's accessible name) reads *waiting on permission* / *waiting on your input*. Each wait clears on its own — focusing that session, typing into it, `pty://settled`, or closing it — without touching another session's (`lib/attentionFocus.ts` `clearsWait`; the workspace flag goes with it only when that flag is the same hook wait). A session without a cell (past eight, or folded on a narrow band) puts its dot on the `+N` / `N sessions` button. _Support:_ `SessionLine.tsx`, `lib/attentionFocus.ts`, `attentionStore.ping/clearForTerminal/clearWait`, `TerminalPane.tsx`, `terminalsStore.deleteTerminal`, `App.tsx` focus effect.
- **Session switcher (⌘⌥K)** — In Run (in Talk, ⌘⌥K opens the conversation switcher on the same frame, `run/SwitcherFrame.tsx`). A `ModalShell align="top"` palette scoped to terminals: search across label, role and running command; `↑`/`↓` move; `⏎` switches; `⌥⏎` opens the selected session **beside** instead (checked before plain `⏎`; with no room left and no empty seat it replaces the focused pane's session, and the footer hint reads `⌥⏎ · Replace` instead of `⌥⏎ · Beside`); `⌫` (empty query only) closes a session, guarded against a double-press deleting the same id twice, and asks first when the session is busy or waits on the user (the same confirm as a pane caption's **Close session…**; Escape answers the confirm and leaves the switcher open); a final **"Open a new session"** row creates one — so the palette answers an empty workspace too; the current session is marked `here`. **Waiting sessions list first**, oldest wait first (off-screen hook waits by when they started, then on-screen panes whose caption says waiting, then the rest in session order — `orderWaitingFirst`), so the selected first row and `⏎` go to the prompt that has waited longest; their state line carries the pane caption's suffix *· waiting on permission* / *· waiting on your input* (mute mono, one static brass dot). Rows keep their `⌘⌥N` number, and searching keeps the same order. Keyboard focus is in its query input on open, however it was opened (the icon, `⌘⌥K`, `⌘D` from a terminal; `ModalShell` `initialFocus`). `⌘⌥K` toggles it and refuses to open under another dialog; it also closes on workspace/mode change. **Pairing mode** (Open beside: `⌘D`, *Open beside…* in a pane caption's menu, a click on an empty seat): the serif placeholder reads *Which session sits beside this one?*, the list leaves out the sessions already on screen (rows keep their `⌘⌥N` number), `⏎` puts the pick beside the panes, and the last row reads **"Open a new session beside"** (it opens the session straight into the empty seat or the new pane, never into the focused one; the slot is chosen once the session exists, so if the seat was filled meanwhile the new session stays off screen rather than replace one that is shown). When Run has no room left and no empty seat, a header line reads *Replaces the session in the focused pane* and a pick does exactly that. `⌫` still closes the selected session. _Support:_ `src/components/run/SessionSwitcher.tsx` (`pairing`). _Entry:_ `⌘⌥K` · the session line's `+N` / `N sessions` button · `⌘D`.
- **Layout button** — The last control of the session line. Its glyph is the layout on screen (`PaneLayoutIcon`: a frame and the dividers inside it) and its tooltip reads `Layout · N panes`. It opens a `.octo-menu-enter` menu (`MenuSurface`): **One pane · Two, side by side** (hinted `⌘D`) **· Two, stacked · Three · Four**, radio rows with a `Check` on the current one. A **larger** layout fills an empty seat and then each new pane with the next sessions not on screen, in session order, and keeps focus where it was; when the sessions run out it leaves one empty seat (a layout holds at most one), so a layout that needs more panes than the workspace has sessions plus that seat is disabled (*Open another session to fill this layout*). A **smaller** layout takes an empty seat and then the trailing panes off screen — never the focused session's pane — and closes no session. The two-pane rows set the workspace's orientation override; with two or three panes the menu adds **Automatic orientation** (a checkbox row: *Side by side while every pane keeps 72 columns, stacked below that*), checked until the user picks an orientation, and unchecking it pins the one on screen. Three panes follow the orientation in force. A note under the rows reads *Fills new panes with the next sessions not on screen.* Arrow keys move through radio and checkbox rows as well as plain ones (`useMenuChrome`). The button **toggles**: a press on it while its menu is open closes the menu and does not open it again; and when the menu closes (Escape, a press elsewhere, a pick) keyboard focus returns to the button (`useAnchoredMenu`). A closing press dragged off the button before release never swallows a later keyboard activation (`Enter`/`Space`, a click with `detail` 0). _Support:_ `SessionLine.tsx`, `terminalLayoutStore` (`choosePaneLayout`, `setPaneCount`, `maxPaneCount`, `paneLayoutOf`, `splitOrientation`, `splitByWs`), `icons/PaneLayoutIcon.tsx`, `RunPanes.tsx` (measures the canvas and publishes the orientation), `lib/useMenuChrome.ts`, `lib/useAnchoredMenu.ts`. _Entry:_ session line › layout button.
- **More sessions than room** — Past **eight** sessions the last cell reads `+N` and opens the `⌘⌥K` switcher: the first seven keep a cell, and the focused session takes the seventh when it sits further down, so the line always shows where the focus is. On a **narrow band** the line is a demotion ladder (`planLine`, from the track's width, measured with a `ResizeObserver`; the track is sized by the band's grid, never by this content): the cells fold from the left into one **`N sessions`** button that opens `⌘⌥K`, while the focused session's cell, `+` and the layout button stay. Narrower still, that button becomes a `List` icon (*All N sessions · ⌘⌥K*). That is the **floor**: the fold button, the focused session's cell, `+` and the layout button. The mode band keeps the line's track at least that wide (`LINE_FLOOR_PX`, 119px) and sheds the switcher's inactive labels to make room (see **Mode band**). When the band is too narrow for even that (334px and under, e.g. a 600px Companion in a 960px window), the track keeps only `LINE_LAST_PX` (26px) and the line takes its **last rung**: the `List` button alone, which opens `⌘⌥K` (switch, open, close) and carries a waiting session's brass dot; the cells, `+` and the layout button go (an open layout menu closes with its button). It stays in the tab order, since nothing is clipped. _Support:_ `SessionLine.tsx` (`visibleSessions`, `planLine`, `lineWidth`, `LINE_FLOOR_PX`, `LINE_LAST_PX`), `ModeBand.tsx`, `App.tsx`.
- **Pane caption (the session's one home)** — Every pane sits under a 32px caption (`.octo-rise-in`, panel ground), a lone pane too. Left to right: the role icon (its `title` is the role phrase); the **name** (double-click it, press `F2` on it, or pick the menu's *Rename*, and it becomes an input in place: `Enter` commits, `Escape` abandons, losing focus commits, an empty or unchanged name changes nothing; a press on the name, or anywhere on the caption, focuses the pane); **what the session is doing**, in mono (the command in sage while it runs, else the role phrase in mute; `starting`; `didn't start` in rouge; a setup run until it succeeds); *· waiting on permission* / *· waiting on your input* while Claude Code's hooks say so (see **Attention surfacing**); a verdigris **Restored** badge (*Reattached from the previous Octopush run*) for the ~5s the store keeps it; the session's `⌘⌥N` (on the focused pane, or under the pointer); a `⋯` **Session actions** menu; and, in a split view only, a **minus** (*Leave the view · the session keeps running*). The focused pane's caption has an ivory name and icon, and in a split view a `border-strong` line under it (alone, there is no other pane to tell it from, so it keeps the plain hairline); the others a sage name and a mute icon. **A pane has no `×`**: leaving keeps the session running, so it is a minus, and closing is by name, in the menu. Menu: **Rename** · **Open beside…** (`⌘D`; offered while Open beside can do something; with four panes and no empty seat it reads **Replace in this pane…**, focuses this pane, and the pick replaces its session) · **Swap with…** and the other panes' sessions (split only) · **Leave the view** (split only) · **Close session** (sage; rouge on hover and on keyboard focus). An **idle** session closes at once. A **busy** one (an agent or a command running in it) reads **Close session…** and opens a confirm first, built like Direct's Abort confirm on `ModalShell`: the serif question *Close this session while it works?*, a line naming the command and the session and saying it can't be reopened, **Keep the session** (focused) and an upright-serif rouge **Close the session**; Escape keeps it. A session Claude Code's hooks say **waits on the user** (on screen or off, `waitingByTerminal` / `waitsByTerminal`) asks too, even when it prints nothing, as an agent parked on a permission prompt does: *Close this session while it waits on you?* and *claude is waiting on permission in …*. The question goes, unanswered, if the pane moves on to another session. There is no undo, because a closed session's shell and scrollback are gone. The `⋯` button toggles its menu and gets the focus back when the menu closes, as the layout button does. An empty seat's caption reads *Empty seat* and keeps only the minus. _Support:_ `src/components/run/RunPanes.tsx` (`PaneCaption`), `run/PaneWaiting.tsx`, `lib/sessionDoing.ts`, `lib/menuStyles.ts` (`MENU_ITEM_ROUGE`), `run/useCloseSession.tsx` (`useCloseSession`, `closeAsksFirst`), `lib/useAnchoredMenu.ts`, `terminalsStore.renameTerminal/deleteTerminal`. _Entry:_ Run canvas.
- **Session roles (the icon vocabulary)** — What a session is *doing*, derived from the daemon's foreground command: shell `ChevronRight` · dev server `Globe` · building `Hammer` · test run `FlaskConical` · installing packages `Package` · git `GitBranch` · agent CLI `Sparkles` · editor/TUI `PenLine` · unclassified `Terminal`. Classification is a pure function over the argv summary (package-manager subcommands, `npm run <script>` names, delegators like `npx`/`sudo`/`env` looked through, paths and `.exe` stripped); genuinely ambiguous commands (a bare `node`) stay **unknown** rather than guessing. Roles are **sticky** — only a placeable command replaces one, so a dev server keeps its identity between rebuilds — and survive a workspace reload (live state, not DB state). _Support:_ `src/lib/sessionRole.ts` (`roleForCommand`, `ROLE_WORD`), `src/lib/roleIcons.ts` (`iconForSessionRole`), `terminalsStore` (`role`, `command`).
- **Starting shell line** — Until a session's PTY has drawn anything (spawn-or-attach in flight, or attached but no prompt yet), the pane shows a quiet mono line in the prompt's slot (top-left, on the canvas background): a 14px working Octo and *Starting shell in ‹workspace›…* (the workspace name, else the folder name). The first `pty://data` chunk for the session (the prompt, or replayed scrollback after a reattach) — or `pty://exit` — fades it out over the prompt; a rejected spawn replaces it with the error state below. The store reads the same moment: the session is `starting` in `terminalsStore` (set on create and on first load) until the pane's `onFirstOutput` calls `markStarted`. _Support:_ `TerminalPane.tsx` (`StartingShell`, `hasOutput`, `onFirstOutput`), `terminalsStore` (`starting`, `markStarted`), `App.tsx` (`workspaceName`). _Entry:_ Run canvas.
- **Session didn't start (spawn failure)** — When `spawn_or_attach_terminal` is rejected (no shell, sandbox denial, daemon down), the pane covers its canvas with a designed error state instead of writing the raw error into the terminal: a rouge mono eyebrow *Session didn't start*, one sans line naming the likely cause (permission · terminal service not responding · shell or folder not found · generic; the error arrives over IPC as `other: …`, and one the daemon itself reported (`other: daemon error: …`) is described by its actual cause, never as the service being down — except `daemon connection closed`, which the app's own reader synthesises on socket EOF), the raw error behind a **Technical detail** disclosure (grid-rows `Reveal`), and a ghost serif **Try the shell again** that re-runs spawn-or-attach in the same xterm. The session is marked `failed` in `terminalsStore` (never running; the Companion's Context section is not drawn for it); a successful retry clears it. Success and rejection are handled side by side, so a bug after a successful spawn can't masquerade as a failure. _Support:_ `TerminalPane.tsx` (`SpawnFailed`, `onSpawnError`), `src/lib/spawnFailure.ts` (`describeSpawnFailure`, `spawnErrorDetail`), `terminalsStore.markFailed`, `App.tsx`. _Entry:_ Run canvas.
- **Cycle sessions (⌘⌥← / ⌘⌥→)** — Previous/next session in the focused pane, wrapping; sessions shown in another pane are skipped; no-op with fewer than two to cycle. _Support:_ `hooks/useGlobalShortcuts.ts` (`session-step`).
- **Sessions side by side (up to four)** — Run can show two, three or four sessions at once (spec: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-run-session-pair-design.md`](superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-run-session-pair-design.md)). **Open beside** (`⌘D`, or *Open beside…* in a pane caption's menu) opens the switcher in pairing mode; **⌥-click** on a session line cell opens that session beside directly, and the line's **layout button** picks a pane count (see Run · session navigation); the pick goes in the first empty seat, else in a new pane appended at the end, and is focused. **Positions** are fixed per count, in reading order (slot index, also the order of `⌘[`/`⌘]`): two are left · right (stacked: top · bottom); three are a large slot 0 on the left with top-right and bottom-right beside it (stacked: a large top with bottom-left and bottom-right); four are a 2×2 grid (top-left · top-right · bottom-left · bottom-right). Slot 0 keeps whatever session it held when the third pane opened; focus never moves sessions, only *Swap with…* does; leaving a pane shifts the ones after it down and lays them out again for the new count. **Orientation** (two and three panes): *Automatic* by default — decided from the canvas width at **even** splits for the current count: side by side when every pane of an even side-by-side layout would get at least 72 terminal columns (counted at the terminal's default 13px size; at even splits the narrowest of two or three panes is half the canvas), else stacked. The dividers never enter into it, so dragging or evening one (side by side or stacked) never changes the orientation; only the window or canvas width and the pane count do. The layout button's *Two, side by side* / *Two, stacked* set an override per workspace that holds for two and three panes until its *Automatic orientation* is checked again; four panes are always the 2×2 grid and the 72-column rule doesn't apply. With four panes and no empty seat, a caption menu's item reads **Replace in this pane…** and the pick replaces that pane's session. **Empty seat:** when every session is already on screen, Open beside adds one empty pane instead (at most one at a time): the eyebrow `BESIDE`, the serif line *Bring a session alongside.* and a ghost serif **Open a new session here**, which opens a new session straight into it; a click elsewhere on the seat focuses it and opens the pairing switcher. The item is offered while a session is on screen and Open beside can do something. **Deleting a session that is on screen** removes its pane exactly as leaving does (focus moves to the next pane in reading order); when no pane is left showing a session, the view returns to one pane holding the neighbour (the one after, else the one before) — never a session already on screen. The panes are split by 1px `--color-octo-border` dividers (`aria-label` "Resize the panes", `title` "Drag to resize · Double-click to even"), one fraction each: two panes `[split]`; three `[mainSplit, sideSplit]` (the main divider between the large pane and the pair, the side one between the pair); four `[colSplit, rowSplit]`, one **shared cross** whose lines run the full width and height. Drag to resize (panes refit on animation frames; the PTY is told its size only on pointer-up), a focused divider moves 5% per arrow key (`←`/`→` for a vertical line, `↑`/`↓` for a horizontal one; 1% with `⇧`), double-click evens it; the dividers and their ±3px grips sit above the `TerminalHost` frames (`z-10`), so the pointer reaches them; every fraction is clamped to 20–80% and evens when the count changes. Every count sits in one 2×2 CSS grid (`paneGrid`): two `fr` tracks per axis, the unused one at `0fr`, so a change of count or orientation glides the tracks over `--dur-standard` with `--ease-octo` — the grid-rows `0fr↔1fr` idiom — and the dividers glide with them (instant during a drag and with reduced motion). A `TerminalSlot` also re-measures on frames while an ancestor transitions, so a pane that only moves (same size) is followed, and at every commit of the layout around it, so a divider step or a change of count lands its rect before paint and its ResizeObserver then finds nothing new to publish (no ResizeObserver loop). Each pane has its **caption** (see **Pane caption** under Run · session navigation), whose menu holds *Swap with…* and *Leave the view* and whose minus leaves the view (*Leave the view · the session keeps running*); every pane keeps full ink. Leaving never closes a session; with one pane left the view returns to one captioned pane. A pane is focused by a click (its caption or the terminal itself) or `⌘[`/`⌘]`; the focused pane is the "active" session that the session line's brass underline, `⌘⌥1..9`, `⌘⌥←/→`, `⌘⌥K` and the Companion follow. **One pane per session:** picking a session that is already on screen (session line, `⌘⌥N`, switcher) only focuses its pane. On the session line every session on screen has an ivory icon and `aria-current="true"`; `aria-selected` and the brass underline stay on the focused one. While two or more panes are shown the **Companion folds** to its 56px strip (tooltip *Folded to make room for the panes · ⌘\\*); `⌘\` or the strip's control brings it back **over** the panes without resizing them until the next fold, and returning to one pane restores the user's latest explicit choice (a toggle while paired wins). Panes that come on screen fade in (`.octo-fade-in`). **Persistence:** Run's layout (slots, orientation, dividers, focused pane) and Talk's seat persist per workspace in `localStorage` (`octopush.terminalLayouts`), written through on every change and read back at launch, keeping only well-formed layouts (a session in two slots, more than one empty seat or a bad count is dropped; dividers and focus are clamped). A session that no longer exists is pruned on load (`loadTerminals`) and on delete; deleting a workspace forgets its layouts and its most-recently-used list. _Support:_ `src/components/run/RunPanes.tsx`, `terminalLayoutStore` (`focus`/`swap`/`leave`/`setRatios`/`setOrientation`/`resolveOrientation`/`paneGrid`/`openBeside`/`besideAction`/`besideSlot`/`besideReplaces`/`readLayouts`/`forgetWorkspace`), `workspaceStore.remove`, `lib/xtermTheme.ts` (`terminalCellWidth`), `TerminalSlot.tsx`, `terminalsStore.besideAction/besideReplaces/openBeside/createBeside/deleteTerminal`, `TerminalHost` (`onPaneFocus`), `hooks/useCompanionFold.ts`, `SessionLine.tsx`, `SessionSwitcher.tsx`, `App.tsx` (`openBeside`). _Entry:_ `⌘D` · pane caption › `⋯` › Open beside… · ⌥-click a session line cell · the layout button · `⌥⏎` in `⌘⌥K`; tour surface `run/open-beside` (opens the pairing switcher only when Open beside would pair; it never leaves an empty seat behind).
- **A terminal beside the conversation (Talk's seat)** — A `SquareTerminal` icon at the top right of the Talk canvas, in its own 32px row above the conversation (level with the seat's caption, so it never sits over the first message; the composer keeps its place) (tooltip *Open a terminal beside the conversation · ⌘D*; `aria-pressed` while open) or `⌘D` in Talk toggles one seat beside the chat column. It holds one of Run's sessions — the same PTY, drawn by `TerminalHost` over a `TerminalSlot` in mode `talk`; the per-thread `$` shell stays separate. Opening reshows the seat's last session if it still exists, else the seat opens empty (`BESIDE` · *Bring a session alongside.* · **Open a new session here**; tooltip *Choose a session for this seat*) with the pairing switcher (*Which session sits beside this one?*), which lists every session but the seat's own — including ones Run shows, since only one mode is visible — and whose last row, *Open a new session beside*, opens a new session straight into the seat (Run leaves it unseated unless Run shows nothing yet). The seat has a caption (role icon and label; a click picks another session; a minus (lucide `Minus`, as on a Run pane) *Leave the view · the session keeps running* closes the seat, never the session) and a 1px divider on its left (`aria-label` "Resize the panes", `title` "Drag to resize · Double-click to even"; drag, `←`/`→` 5%, 1% with `⇧`, double-click evens; 20–80% of the canvas). **The seat never covers the composer:** its width is capped so the conversation keeps `--talk-chat-min` (44rem, the composer's control bar on one line at its natural width), on drag and as the window narrows; when the canvas is too narrow for that and a 40-column terminal (`--talk-seat-min`, 21rem), the seat keeps 21rem and the conversation narrows, never below `--talk-chat-floor` (18rem), the composer's estimate and Send wrapping together onto a second line. A drag past the cap keeps the width it showed, so the next drag or arrow key moves the seat at once. The seat's width glides over `--dur-standard` (instant while dragging); on close its caption, divider and terminal stay through the glide and go at its end (at once with reduced motion). At launch a restored seat stays blank until the workspace's sessions are listed, so its session never flashes as an empty seat. While a dialog is open, the toggle does nothing. **Focus in the seat is Talk's own, per workspace** (`talkFocusedByWs`): clicking into the terminal or picking its session gives it keyboard focus and OSC 52; focusing the conversation or closing the seat takes it back; it never changes `activeByWs` or Run's focused pane. A session in both Run's grid and the seat is resized once, to the visible pane, on a mode change: a switch that glides the Companion to or from its strip (Run with one pane ↔ Talk with the seat open, Review ↔ Run with panes) holds every PTY's size until that glide ends and the slots have then kept their rects for three frames (`useFoldSettle` sets `terminalLayoutStore.settling`, the same suspension as a divider drag: panes refit on frames, the PTY hears the settled size once), so each visible PTY gets one `resize_session`, or none when its size didn't change. Reduced motion holds the same way (its near-instant transition still lands the new width a frame or more after the switch): the three still frames only count once the Companion's measured width matches its target, since the glide's end or the fallback timer can come before that width publishes the slots' new rects; a width that never lands lets go after 30 frames. While the seat is open the **Companion folds** as it does for Run's panes; `⌘\` brings it (and its context meter) back over the canvas. The seat persists per workspace with Run's layout. _Support:_ `src/components/chat/TalkSeat.tsx`, `terminalLayoutStore` (`TalkSeat`, `toggleTalk`/`seatTalk`/`setTalkWidth`/`pruneTalk`, `talkByWs`, `seatTalkSession`, `talkFocusedByWs`), `terminalsStore` (`createInTalkSeat`, `toggleTalkSeat`), `SessionSwitcher.tsx` (`talk`), `RunPanes.tsx` (`EmptySeat`), `App.tsx` (`TerminalHost` mode `talk` while the seat's slot is mounted), `hooks/useFoldSettle.ts`, `styles.css` (`--talk-chat-min`/`--talk-seat-min`/`--talk-chat-floor`). _Entry:_ Talk › the `SquareTerminal` icon · `⌘D` in Talk.
- **Run-scoped session shortcuts** — `⌘⌥1..9`, `⌘⌥←/→`, `⌘[`/`⌘]` and `⌘⌥K` act only in **Run** mode (elsewhere they would silently reshuffle a surface the user isn't looking at). `⌘D` (physical `KeyD`) is one global entry that branches on the mode: Open beside in Run, the terminal seat in Talk, and it leaves the key alone elsewhere; a focused code editor or scratchpad keeps `⌘D` (next occurrence), because CodeMirror handles it first. `⌘⌥N` matches the **physical key** (`e.code`), because macOS rewrites the printed character under Option even with Cmd held — and `⌘1..9`/`⌘K` now exclude `altKey` so they can't swallow the session chords. _Support:_ `App.tsx` key handler; `lib/focus.ts` for the active mode.

### Companion · Run (CompanionRun)

What the terminals can't show. The Companion never repeats the canvas, it follows the focus, and a section with nothing to say is not drawn: a session's name, state and controls live on its pane, not here. Three `CompanionSection`s, top to bottom, each folding from its eyebrow and remembered under `octo.companion.section.run-context` / `run-changes` / `run-mission`; one hairline between them, no framed cards. Brass appears twice only: the context meter's fill and the serif link.

- **Context (the focused pane's Claude Code session)** — Follows the focused pane (`terminalsStore.getActiveId`). It is asked for only when that pane's session has the agent role and the CLI that gave it the role is `claude` (`TerminalState.agentCli`, recorded with the role by `agentCliForCommand` and replaced with it, since Codex, aider and the rest share the agent role), and drawn only when `get_session_usage` answers. The eyebrow names the session it describes at its right (mute, its own case, truncating), since a split view shows several. Body: the **context meter**, the same `ContextMeter` Talk's Conversation section uses (`148k / 1M` through `formatContextTokens`, a thin bar whose width is the percentage, never also printed; brass, the warning tone from 80%, rouge from 95%; here the figure stays ivory and only the bar takes the tone); then mono rows **Spent** (the session's priced spend in the ledger; `$1.50 · partly unpriced` when some of its calls ran on a model with no price, `unpriced` rather than `$0.00` when all did; tooltip: the call counts), **Cached** (`94% of prompt tokens`: the share of the session's prompt tokens read from the cache; omitted when the cache was never reported) and **Model**; from 80%, one mono line in the warning tone, *Past 80% · /compact soon* (grid-rows `Reveal`). When the model's window isn't in the catalog the prompt's size stands alone with no bar; when the context size isn't known (see below) the meter is left out and the rows stay. Otherwise the whole section folds away (grid-rows `Reveal`, keeping what it showed until it has left). **When Context does not appear:** the focused pane is a shell, a dev server, a log tail, Codex or another agent CLI, or its PTY has stopped; the pane's Claude Code session has ended (`/exit`, a closed process) or was just cleared and has no reply yet; the hooks setting (Settings › General, "Let Claude Code say what it's waiting on") is off; the workspace is not a worktree Octopush created (the project's own checkout, an adopted checkout: no hooks are installed there); Claude Code is older than the tested floor or its version is unknown; a session that was already running when the session hooks were installed, before its next `Stop`; and whenever the backend can't tell the figures are that terminal's current session's (next entry). A focus change, an empty answer and a failed read all clear the figures (`useSessionUsage` keeps nothing from an earlier read of another pane). Re-read on the edges that can change it, never on a timer: the focused pane changing, `pty://claude-session` and `pty://settled` in any Run terminal, and `octo://spend-ingested`. _Support:_ `src/components/CompanionRun.tsx` (`ContextSection`, `spentLabel`), `src/components/ContextMeter.tsx` (`contextTone`), `src/hooks/useSessionUsage.ts`, `src/lib/sessionRole.ts` (`agentCliForCommand`), `terminalsStore` (`agentCli`), `ipc.getSessionUsage` / `ipc.onClaudeSessionChanged` / `ipc.onPtySettled`. _Entry:_ Run Companion, a Claude Code pane focused.
- **Session usage (`get_session_usage`) — whose numbers these are** — Read-only command behind Context: `get_session_usage(terminal_id)` → `SessionUsage { contextTokens?, maxContext?, spentUsd, calls, unpricedCalls, cacheHitPct?, model, asOf }` or `null`. **The link:** the ledger keys a transcript's rows by Claude Code's own session id (`source_id = cc:<session id>`), and the only place a Run terminal and that id meet is a Claude Code hook: its environment carries `OCTOPUSH_TERMINAL_ID`, its payload `session_id`. The hook poller keeps **one current session per terminal** in `terminal_claude_session(terminal_id PK, session_id, linked_at)` while the hooks setting is on (`claude_hooks::remember_sessions`, applied in queue order, also for rows too old to deliver): `SessionStart` (startup, `/clear`, `/resume`, `--resume`, `--continue`, a fork, a compaction) makes the payload's session the terminal's at once; `SessionEnd` (`/exit`, `/clear`, `/resume` to another, logout, a signalled process) removes the row and records the session in `ended_claude_sessions(session_id PK, ended_at)`, so a late `Stop` of its own can't bring it back. Only its `SessionStart` (a resume) can, and only one that fired after that end: `SessionStart` is asynchronous and `SessionEnd` is not, so the start of a session that ended at once can be written after its end, and a start that is not newer than the recorded end links nothing (`db::link_terminal_claude_session`, comparing the rows' own stamps). `ended_claude_sessions` gets one row per finished conversation and is pruned in `Db::migrate`, so as the app starts and as each `octopush-mcp` server starts: rows older than 30 days go (`db::prune_ended_claude_sessions`, `ENDED_SESSION_DAYS`). Nothing else prunes it; any other signal (`Stop`, a `Notification`) names its session too, which is the whole link for a session whose hooks predate the session events, and how a terminal returns to its own session. A session is current in one terminal only: named by another terminal it leaves the first, which then has none (never an older one). Closing a terminal removes its row; turning the setting off forgets them all. Recorded on Claude Code 2.1.327: `/clear` fires `SessionEnd` (reason `clear`, the old id) and then `SessionStart` (source `clear`, a new id), so there is no window in which the cleared conversation's figures stay. **Spend, cache share:** `db::run_session_ledger("cc:<id>")` over `spend_events` (unpriced rows counted and left out of the spend, as in `thread_cost`; cache share by `cache_hit_pct`), so a sub-agent's calls count toward its session. **Context size:** `transcripts::last_prompt` reads the end of the session's own transcript (`<projects>/<cwd, sanitized>/<session id>.jsonl`, resolved like the ingestor's directories; 256 KiB, then 8 MiB, never the whole file) for the last `assistant` line with usage that is not a sub-agent's (`isSidechain`): input + cache read + cache write, with its model and time. A sub-agent's newer, smaller prompt is its own context, so the newest ledger row would not do. Unknown (no meter) when the transcript is gone or the conversation was compacted with no message since (a `compact_boundary` line after the last message). **Window:** the model's `max_context` from the provider catalog (`token_engine::catalog` → `find_model`, the catalog `list_models` serves Talk's meter from), `null` for a model it doesn't list. **Withheld (`null`)**, so nothing is shown rather than a guess: the terminal has no current session; the ledger has no row for the session yet (a conversation with no reply ingested, or rows keyed by a legacy RUN session on the same root); or the session has a **rival** (`db::run_session_has_rival`): another Claude Code session was metered in the workspace after both this pair's last hook and this session's last message, and it is neither over nor another terminal's current session. With the session hooks an interactive session in an Octopush terminal is one or the other, and a print-mode or SDK session there (a `claude -p` the agent runs) is recorded as ended when it starts and again when it ends, so it is never a rival either. The exception is a print-mode run that reuses the id of a session some terminal runs now (`claude -p --continue`, or `--resume` of its own id, from the agent's own terminal): its start and end are not queued at all (`db::claude_session_is_linked`, checked in `record_hook_at`), so the live session keeps its terminal and its Context; its other signals are queued without the session id, as for any print-mode run. The rival check therefore only catches what the hooks can't: a session whose hooks predate them (there `/clear`, a resume or a restart is silent until the next `Stop`, and the previous figures stay until an ingest pass meters the newcomer, up to about a minute after its first reply) and a session started in the worktree outside Octopush's terminals. **Known limits:** a `claude -p` an agent runs on a Claude Code that doesn't set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` in the hook's environment would take the terminal over for as long as it runs and unlink it when it ends; the parent's next hook (`Stop`, a `Notification`) links the terminal back. A Claude Code process killed with `SIGKILL` fires no `SessionEnd`, so its last figures stay for that terminal until another session starts there or the pane's CLI changes. The window is the catalog's, which can be larger than the one the user's plan gives that model. The transcript ingestor and how it attributes spend are unchanged. _Support:_ `commands::get_session_usage`, `transcripts::{terminal_usage, session_usage, last_prompt, SessionUsage}`, `db::{run_session_ledger, link_terminal_claude_session, end_terminal_claude_session, terminal_claude_session, run_session_has_rival, prune_ended_claude_sessions, claude_session_is_linked}`, `claude_hooks::{remember_sessions, sessions_known, record_hook_at}`, `agent_adapter::{session_hook_command, interactive_entrypoint}`; contract tests `transcript_tail_gives_the_sessions_last_main_thread_prompt`, `session_hook_payloads_move_the_terminal_between_sessions`.
- **Changes (uncommitted files, live)** — Eyebrow meta `3 files · +84 −12` (the line total over the listed files; left out when the working diff holds no lines for them, such as staged-only or binary changes, or when the 1 MiB cap cut the diff). One row per file, up to 8, then `+N more`: the status letter Review's Changes list uses (`N` `M` `D` `R` `?`, `!` in rouge for a conflict; tooltip: the word), the path with its file name pinned (`MidTruncate`, tail = the name and its slash, 8 to 20 characters; full path in the tooltip) and `+added −removed` in verdigris and rouge when the working diff has lines for it. A row opens Review at that file (the existing diff jump; from another mode it waits up to 2 s for Review's diff to land instead of toasting *Not in the current diff* at once, and the wait is dropped, with no toast, by a newer jump, leaving Review or switching workspace: `revealDiffTargetWhenReady` with an `AbortSignal`). Rows rise in, and `+N more`, the clean line and the link fade in (`.octo-rise-in` / `.octo-fade-in`). The upright-serif phrase **Read the diff** switches to Review. Clean tree: one mute line, *The working tree is clean.*, and, while the workspace has commits since its base, the Review Companion's *3 commits ahead of main* line (then Read the diff stays, for the Since base view). Before the first status arrives the section claims nothing. **Data, no second poller:** App's own 3 s git poll (the one Review uses) feeds it. While this panel is open in Run (not folded for the panes) the poll also reads the working diff when the tree is dirty and keeps only its per-file counts (`changeStats` → `runChangeStats`), and reads `get_committed_diff` once per clean state, keeping only the count, its base and merge base (`runAhead`): when the tree becomes clean, and again if the status signature moves while it stays clean (`runChangesReader`, `runChangesTick`). The signature (`gitStatusSig`) holds the branch, ahead/behind, HEAD's commit (`GitStatus.head`, from `git_ops::status_files`) and the changed files, so a commit, `reset --hard`, merge or cherry-pick moves it even on a workspace branch with no upstream, and even when no dirty tick saw it: the agent edited and committed while the window was hidden (the poll skips those ticks; the focus refresh then reads the new HEAD) or within one 3 s tick. Any dirty tick also voids the count. Neither diff text is stored from Run and `reviewSourceStore` is written from Review alone, so the Review canvas (mounted but hidden outside Review) never renders a diff on Run's account. One refresh runs at a time (a slow read skips the ticks behind it), and `get_git_diff` builds the diff on a blocking thread, off the async runtime. Review's own refresh is unchanged. _Support:_ `CompanionRun.tsx` (`ChangesSection`), `src/lib/runChanges.ts` (`changeStats`, `changesMeta`, `gitStatusSig`, `runChangesReader`, `runChangesTick`, `STATUS_LETTER`, `pathTail`), `App.tsx` (the git poll, `navigateToFile`), `lib/diffJump.ts`. _Entry:_ Run Companion.
- **Mission** — The mission's Logbook line on the section chrome: **Worked** · **Spent** · **Saved** (the figures Talk's mission line and Direct's Logbook card show, from `useMissionLogbook` over the mission's life; Saved only when there is a saving; *No work recorded yet.* until something is). A `Maximize2` control on the eyebrow opens the Logbook Room. Not drawn for a workspace with no mission. _Support:_ `CompanionRun.tsx` (`MissionSection`), `hooks/useMissionLogbook.ts`. _Entry:_ Run Companion (with a mission).

### Companion · Review cockpit (CompanionReview)
- **Readiness verdict** — One-line AI-free verdict from working-tree state: clean / "Resolve N conflicts first" (rouge) / "N staged · the secret guard will ask first" (rouge; when the guard's scan of the staged diff found a possible secret or couldn't read it all — see the next entry) / "N staged · ready to commit" / "N files to review" (the unit is files, matching the diff). No count line under it: the file count and +/− stat live once, in the mode band's tail (`ReviewTail`). _Support:_ `src/components/CompanionReview.tsx`. _Entry:_ Review Companion.
- **Secret guard verdict line (#835)** — With something staged and no conflicts, the Companion asks the secret guard what Commit would find (`secret_scan_staged`: the same staged-diff scan, read-only, run on a blocking thread, redone on every new git status — including one where the staged files look the same, such as a hunk accepted into an already-staged file — and every 5 s while something is staged and the window is visible (`SECRET_RESCAN_MS`; skipped while a scan is still running), so an agent's edit + re-add between two polls is caught too; a result a newer scan has overtaken is dropped). When Commit would stop, one sans line under the verdict, behind a rouge `ShieldAlert`, names it *"possible secret · GitHub token in src/a.ts:3"* (+ "and N more"; a partial scan adds "scanned the first 16 MB; the rest wasn't checked"), followed by an upright-serif **Show it** link that jumps to the first finding in the diff. Its text carries the tooltip *"Secret guard: Commit will ask before recording this"*. It unfolds on `<Reveal>` and folds away once the staged change is clean. It blocks nothing and carries no fingerprint, so it can't stand in for the confirm: Commit still rescans and opens the guard's dialog. Quiet with the guard off, with nothing staged or when the scan can't run. `data-tour="review-companion-secret"`. _Support:_ `SecretVerdict` / `useStagedSecretPreview` in `CompanionReview.tsx`, `lib/secretGuard.ts` (`SecretPreview`, `previewSummary`), `secret_scan::preview` / `ScanPreview`. _Entry:_ Review Companion.
- **Scan this branch's commits (#820)** — Branch & publish, under "N commits ahead of main": an on-demand, read-only secret scan of every commit since the base, listing kind · file:line · masked preview. See "Secret guard › Scan this branch's commits". _Support:_ `BranchSecretScan` in `CompanionReview.tsx`. _Entry:_ Review Companion.
- **Collision verdict line (collision radar, #732)** — Under the verdict, one sans line when another live workspace of the project changes the same files: *"Will conflict with refund-webhooks in 1 file."* (rouge `GitCompareArrows`, an in-memory merge confirmed it) or *"Overlaps refund-webhooks in 2 files."* (amber), followed by an upright-serif **Open refund-webhooks** link that selects that workspace (same project, so `workspaceStore.select`). The tooltip lists every collision and its files. It unfolds on `<Reveal>` and folds away when the overlap clears; it never changes the verdict above or blocks a commit. Mounting it rescans the workspace's project (throttled). `data-tour="review-companion-collision"`. _Support:_ `CollisionVerdict` in `CompanionReview.tsx`, `collisionStore`, `lib/collisions.ts`. _Entry:_ Review Companion.
- **Provenance ("How this change was built")** — Traces which agent turns shaped the changed files: "Shaped by N agent turns across M files"; each turn expandable to show its model + truncated message; file chips jump into the diff. States: tracing/loading, "likely hand-written", or the turn list. _Support:_ `CompanionReview.tsx`; `ipc.listFileEdits`, `ipc.getMessage`. _Entry:_ Review Companion.
- **Branch & publish** — Sync line: "Not published yet" / "Up to date with origin" / "↑ahead · ↓behind", or a mute "—" (tooltip "Ahead/behind unknown…") when git couldn't count the commits in time (`aheadBehindKnown` false); plus last commit short-SHA + subject. Under the sync line, while the workspace has commits since its base, a mono *"3 commits ahead of main"* line (`GitCompare`; tooltip names the merge base; `data-tour="review-companion-ahead"`), read from `reviewSourceStore` — the committed view's own fetch, so no extra IPC (#851). _Support:_ `CompanionReview.tsx`; `ipc.getLastCommit`, `reviewSourceStore`. _Entry:_ Review Companion.

### Companion · Runs (CompanionRuns / CompanionCurrentRun)
- **Run list** — Lists Direct runs for the workspace with status glyph+word (running `●` in verdigris, like the run-track's running stage — brass is kept for the viewed row's left edge and paused (needs-you) runs, whose `◆ paused` glyph and word stay brass; the current-run summary's status tag uses the same colours, and its cost is ivory, never brass), cost, optional linked issue key; active/viewed run highlighted at full ink, past rows at the depth-of-field row optic (`opacity-45`, rising to `0.85` on hover/focus, 180ms — same convention as Mission Control's settled band and HistorySheet); stale-while-revalidate cache. _Support:_ `src/components/CompanionRuns.tsx`; `runsStore`, `runStatusMeta`. _Entry:_ Direct Companion.
- **Begin a new run** — `+` clears the viewed run to start fresh. _Support:_ `CompanionRuns.tsx`. _Entry:_ Runs eyebrow `+`.
- **Savings ledger line** — "saved $X across N runs" (only when ≥ $0.005). _Support:_ `CompanionRuns.tsx`; `aggregateSavings`. _Entry:_ Direct Companion.
- **Current-run summary** — For the viewed run: brass "current run" eyebrow + status, the `StageDots` universal micro-track, the current stage's title in a fixed-height truncating slot (S1 — a static label, not an activity ticker; the canvas `RunFlow` alone owns the live activity stream), cost + ↑in/↓out tokens. _Support:_ `src/components/CompanionCurrentRun.tsx`, `src/components/direct/StageDots.tsx`. _Entry:_ Direct Companion (run selected).
- **Claude plan line** — Under the run's cost, for a run with a Claude Code (CLI, non-Codex) stage and once a Claude-plan stage has reported: a mono-meta line `Claude plan · 5h 62% · resets 19:40 · week 31%` plus its age (`as of 12 min ago`; never shown without it) — the age of the *oldest* figure on the line, so a fresh 5-hour reading never makes an older weekly one look current. Sage; amber when a window is at ≥ 80% or `allowed_warning`; rouge when `rejected`. Near or at a limit one calm sentence follows in the same tone (warning amber, rouge when used up) (*"Your Claude plan's 5-hour window is at 94% — it resets at 19:40."*). Another window (e.g. weekly Opus) joins the line only when it is the one near its limit; a window whose reset time has passed reads `reset since` instead of a stale figure. The `overage` window reads `extra usage` (`unavailable` when rejected without a figure, with *"Extra usage on your Claude plan isn't available right now."* — it may only be turned off — never "used up"). A window seen more than 7 days ago whose reset has passed (or that gave no reset time) is dropped (`currentWindows`), so the line disappears after a move to an API key. Re-read on `plan://updated` and whenever the run's cost moves (detached runs). Hidden for API-key users. _Support:_ `ClaudePlanLine.tsx`, `lib/claudePlan.ts`, `stores/claudePlanStore.ts`; `get_claude_plan`. _Entry:_ Direct Companion (`data-tour="companion-claude-plan"`).
- **Empty state** — "No runs yet — direct your first." _Support:_ `CompanionRuns.tsx`.
