Its session rollouts, state DBs (`state_5`, `logs_2`, `goals_1`, `memories_1`, `queue_1`, `thread_history_1`), `history.jsonl`, `session_index.jsonl`, `shell_snapshots/`, `tmp/` arg0 helpers and `log/` stay writable: they are shared only by the Codex stages of the same workspace and access mode. **Sign-in preflight (unsandboxed, fails closed, `sandbox::codex_auth_plan`):** when `CODEX_API_KEY` reaches the stage (login shell or app env) nothing is read or copied; an API-key sign-in in `auth.json` goes to the stage as `CODEX_API_KEY`, never into a file; a ChatGPT sign-in last refreshed more than 7 days ago (or not at all), or whose access token expires within a day, fails the stage with "Open Codex once to refresh sign-in" before anything is made; a fresh one is copied read-only as `auth.json` with its refresh token blanked, so Codex in the stage can never perform its rotating refresh (a refresh that can't be saved signs the user out everywhere). Reads aren't confined, so a process in the stage can still read the user's own `auth.json`. No saved sign-in copies nothing (and removes an old copy). Any other sign-in (external tokens, agent identity, personal access tokens, Bedrock) and an unreadable `auth.json` fail the stage with a readable message. Secrets never reach a log line (`CodexAuthPlan` and `CodexHome` redact them). **A read-only Codex stage is refused in a sandboxed mission** (a readonly mission included, since it forces the sandbox on): Codex runs each command of a `--sandbox read-only` stage under its own `sandbox-exec`, and inside the mission profile applying that nested profile fails with `sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`. Such a stage fails before anything is set up with "A read-only Codex stage can't run in a sandboxed mission yet. Give this stage a Claude model." (`cli_runner::codex_read_only_refusal`), and the Direct launcher says so before the run begins. **The shared `~/.cache` is not writable:** `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `PRE_COMMIT_HOME` and `UV_CACHE_DIR` point into the stage's own build-cache root instead (`sandbox_cache_env`), so those caches start cold once per workspace. `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR` is left alone: Puppeteer looks up its browser there at run time and would miss the one already installed in `~/.cache/puppeteer`, which stays readable. **Hard links stay inside the write roots:** `file-link` isn't part of `file-write*`, so the profile also has a global `(deny file-link)` before the allows and re-allows `file-link` only under the same subtree roots (never for the `~/.claude.json` literal). Seatbelt checks a hard link's source as well as the new name, so a stage can link only a file that is already inside its write roots, to a name inside them: git's object links and repacks, pnpm's store links in the build cache and cargo's `target/` links keep working, while a link to a file outside the roots is refused and nothing outside can be changed through one. Symlinks are ordinary writes and are unaffected. An empty root list renders no allow at all, since an SBPL allow without filters matches every path. **The system write roots can't be replaced:** each system root dir (`/dev`, `/private/tmp`, `$TMPDIR`, each `~/.claude` state dir) and its realpath is denied as a path (`file-write*` and `file-link`, after the allows), so a stage writes inside it but can't remove or rename the dir itself or put a symlink in its place. Before each launch `sandbox::assemble_write_roots` checks every system root and leaves out (fail closed) one that resolves to `/`, `/Users`, `$HOME` or an ancestor of `$HOME`, holds the build-cache, stage temp or Codex home base (`~/Library/Caches/octopush/build-cache`, `…/tmp`, `…/codex-home`), resolves under `~/.config`, `~/.ssh` or `~/Library` outside `~/Library/Caches`, doesn't resolve, isn't a directory, or (for the `~/.claude` state dirs) isn't owned by the user, and a state dir that is, holds or sits inside `~/.claude` itself or one of its config entries (as given or resolved: a `projects` linked to `~/.claude`, say); `~/.claude.json` stays writable but is left out when it isn't a single-link regular file of the user's or is a symlink to anything outside `~/.claude/` (a path-component prefix, so `~/.claude-old` is outside). Each one left out is named, with its reason, on the stage's launch line (`… · left out of the sandbox: ~/.claude/projects resolves under ~/.config`) as well as in the app log, so a dropped root never breaks a stage quietly. A missing `~/.claude` (or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) and each missing state dir are created outside the sandbox first, owner-only (0700, `sandbox::ensure_home_roots`, never through a link, and only on macOS); the state dirs go in `~/.claude`'s realpath, and only when it passes the same checks as a system root. The profile is passed inline (`sandbox-exec -p`), so no profile file exists: a profile written to `$TMPDIR` (itself a write root) could be overwritten by another sandboxed stage between the write and the spawn, launching the victim stage unconfined. **Git hooks and config are off-limits:** a planted hook script, a `core.hooksPath` / `core.fsmonitor` setting or a redirected `.git` pointer would run code on the host, outside the sandbox, on the user's next `git commit` or `git status` — so a sandboxed agent **cannot write the hooks dir git runs, the repo's git config, or any `.git` pointer that decides where git looks for them**. `sandbox::resolve_git_layout` asks `git rev-parse --git-dir --git-common-dir --git-path hooks` (realpaths; the last answer is the *effective* hooks dir, so a configured `core.hooksPath` such as husky v9's gitignored `.husky/_` is covered). It **fails closed**: when git can't answer (e.g. a sandboxed command corrupted a linked worktree's `HEAD`) or the layout isn't one git would create (a `.git` file pointed at `$HOME`), the stage fails with a readable error instead of running without the git rules. `git_write_rules` re-allows the per-worktree git dir plus the shared `objects/`, `refs/`, `logs/`, `reftable/` and `packed-refs`, so `git add`/`git commit` work in a **linked worktree** whose index and refs live outside its own subtree. A trailing `(deny file-write* …)` block (SBPL: the last matching rule wins) then blocks the effective hooks dir (plus its parent dirs inside the workspace or any other writable root — a `core.hooksPath` pointing into `$TMPDIR`, `/private/tmp` or a `~/.claude` state dir — so it can't be swapped for a symlink), `<common>/hooks`, `<common>/info`, the legacy `<common>/remotes` and `<common>/branches` (a planted remote definition there would redirect a later `git fetch`), `config` / `config.worktree` (and their `.lock` files), **every** worktree's `commondir` / `gitdir` / `config.worktree` under `<common>/worktrees/*` (an escaped SBPL `regex`, so a main checkout can't repoint a sibling worktree), submodule git dirs under every `modules/` (shared, the workspace's own and each sibling worktree's `<common>/worktrees/*/modules`), `<common>/worktrees` and each `<common>/worktrees/<name>` dir as paths (seatbelt checks a rename only against its source and destination, so neither can be renamed away and replaced by a planted dir; writes *inside* the linked worktree's own git dir stay allowed), the workspace's own `.git` entry and writes to any nested `.git` path inside the workspace — for main checkouts and linked worktrees alike. A matching trailing `(deny file-link …)` block covers the same paths and wins over the root `file-link` allow, so a stage can't hardlink `.git/config` or a hook into the writable tree and write through the link. As intended, a sandboxed stage can't run `git config`, `git branch --set-upstream-to`, `git worktree add`/`remove`/`prune`, `git submodule add`/`update`, `git init` in a subfolder, or commit inside a submodule. Readonly missions stay temp-only (no git rules). **Build-capable without widening the boundary:** a sandboxed `npm install`/`cargo build` needs a writable package-manager cache, but the real `~/.cargo`/`~/.gradle`/… are **config/executable dirs** — a sandboxed agent could plant a `~/.cargo/config.toml` `rustc-wrapper` or a `~/.gradle/init.d/*.gradle` that runs OUTSIDE the sandbox on the next build. So those global dirs stay **read-only**; instead `sandbox::sandbox_cache_env` redirects the toolchains' write caches (`CARGO_HOME`, `npm_config_cache`, `GOPATH`/`GOCACHE`, `GRADLE_USER_HOME`, `DENO_DIR`, `PIP_CACHE_DIR`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, …) into a **cache root per workspace, access mode and tenant**, `~/Library/Caches/octopush/build-cache/<workspace>/<mode>` (0700; `<workspace>` hashes the workspace path and `<mode>` the mission's write roots plus the launch's tenant, `sandbox::CacheTenant`: a CLI stage's exec choice and read guard, an in-process `run_command`, or a Codex writer in its own sandbox. So a readonly mission doesn't share a writer's cache, an exec-`none` readonly review doesn't share a read-confined one's, and no Codex stage or `run_command` shares a read-confined Claude stage's, while launches with the same workspace, access mode and tenant, such as two read-confined readonly reviews of one workspace, share one). **Cleanup:** deleting a workspace removes its whole `<workspace>` dir (every access mode and its Codex root), its stages' temp dirs and its sandboxed Codex homes (kept while another workspace row still sits at that path, `sandbox::remove_workspace_build_caches` from `delete_workspace`), and on launch `sandbox::prune_build_caches` removes every cache root, stage temp dir and sandboxed Codex home unused for 30 days (`BUILD_CACHE_MAX_AGE`; each use refreshes the root's and the temp dir's mtime) and then any workspace dir left empty, removing links without following them; it prunes nothing when `build-cache` (or `tmp`) or `~/Library/Caches/octopush` is a symlink or not owned by the user. `sandbox::prepare` creates it and adds only that subtree to the profile; the shared base sits outside every write root, so a stage can't plant a `CARGO_HOME/config.toml` in the cache of another workspace or access mode (as it could while every cache sat in the shared, writable `$TMPDIR`). The root dir itself is denied as a path (`file-write*` and `file-link`), so a stage can't remove it and put a symlink in its place, and `prepare` **fails closed** if the root, its workspace dir or the base is a symlink or isn't a directory the user owns: it checks and chmods through one `O_NOFOLLOW` handle, and puts the root in the profile as `<realpath of base>/<workspace>/<mode>`, never re-resolved — so a swapped root can neither get the app to chmod the link's target nor make that target writable to the next stage. A Claude stage's temp dir gets the same checks and the same path deny (`sandbox::ensure_stage_tmp`). It sits beside `build-cache`, not inside the cache root, to keep the path short: macOS caps a Unix socket path at 104 bytes, and `<cache root>/tmp` (about 89 bytes for an 8-letter user name, against 60 for `tmp/<key>` and 49 for the default `/var/folders/…/T/`) leaves too little room for a socket a test or tool binds in a temp dir of its own. Builds work, `~/.cargo` et al. are never writable, and read-only missions can still write nothing in the checkout. The active mission's sandbox state shows as a mute **`Shield`** glyph in the ContextHeader intent eyebrow. **Read-only missions** (review/probe, `git_isolation = "readonly"`) reuse the exact same machinery to become **read-only-by-construction**: `sandbox::sandbox_write_roots` folds both axes into one decision — a readonly mission forces the sandbox ON with **empty** write roots (temp-only), so its agents read the checkout but can write nothing to it, regardless of the mission's own `exec_isolation`. Enforced at both surfaces (the run-stage resolution in `run_stage_once` and the TALK tool resolution in `send_agentic` both call `sandbox_write_roots`). **Out of scope (documented):** reads are not a kernel boundary: the Seatbelt profile denies writes only, so a program that opens a file itself, out of sight of Claude Code's checker, can still read it; MCP tool calls run in the user's own configured MCP server processes and aren't wrapped; hook scripts the repo keeps in its own tracked files (e.g. husky's `.husky/pre-commit`, which `.husky/_` calls) and files the repo's config already `include`s from inside the workspace stay writable — such edits show in the diff for review; files git ignores, such as `node_modules`, stay writable and don't show in the diff, yet the user's next unsandboxed build or test runs them; the workspace's `.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored) stays writable, and hooks or MCP servers it defines run unsandboxed in the user's later Claude Code sessions there; `~/.claude.json` stays writable (the CLI needs it) and can hold MCP servers that run unsandboxed; the `~/.claude` (or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) state dirs stay writable and are shared with the user's other Claude Code sessions, so a stage can change another session's transcript (read back on `--resume`), shell snapshot or session env, and can move a dir it prepared into `projects/` as another project's dir, with an auto memory in it (only writes under `projects/*/memory` are denied); a tool that ignores `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and writes `~/.cache` directly now fails there (as one writing `~/Library/Caches` already did), and the user's own `~/.cache` (pre-commit environments, a Hugging Face token under it) isn't seen through `XDG_CACHE_HOME`; `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is followed only as set for the stage at launch (a value the CLI picks up some other way isn't seen); an existing `.credentials.json` stays writable, so a stage can replace the stored login with another one; the shared refs stay writable (a linked worktree commits through them), so a stage can move or delete any branch or tag, not only its own; an agent can start a rebase or cherry-pick itself, and its todo (`.git/rebase-merge/git-rebase-todo`, `.git/sequencer/todo`), like one already in progress, stays writable — its `exec` lines would run on the host if the user later runs `git rebase --continue`; a sandboxed Codex stage's home is shared by the Codex stages of the same workspace and access mode, so one can change another's session rollout (read back on `codex exec resume`), state DBs (goals, memories jobs, thread history), arg0 helpers or shell snapshots; it doesn't load the user's global Codex `AGENTS.md`, skills, rules, prompts, plugins or memories (they stay in `~/.codex`), nor a `managed_config.toml` there (`/etc/codex` still applies); its denied names are matched by ASCII case and the two single-letter folds, not every Unicode folding a volume may apply (a name the profile missed is still removed before the next launch); a ChatGPT sign-in copy keeps a valid access token (no refresh token) in the stage's home until the next launch replaces or removes it; and a directory that already holds its own `.git` can still be moved into the workspace (e.g. a staged repo renamed into place of a submodule's checkout, or a new submodule-like dir), whose config git would honour when it recurses into a submodule — the nested-`.git` rule blocks writing a `.git` path, not moving in a parent that contains one. **Gating: FREE** — a free tier safer than the competition is the point; a product that charges for security reads as extortion. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/orchestrator/sandbox.rs` (profile builder + inline-profile argv wrapper + per-workspace build cache + per-workspace Codex home and sign-in preflight, `prepare_codex_home` / `codex_auth_plan` + `prepare` + `is_write_allowed`), the fail-closed match in `orchestrator/cli_runner.rs`, the sandbox-aware `chat_engine::execute_tool` + `sandboxed_write` (threaded from `send_agentic` via `active_mission_for_workspace` and from `run_agentic_loop`/`ApiRunner` via `StageContext`), `exec_isolation` + `exec_choice` + `allowed_write_roots` on `StageContext` (derived by `sandbox::stage_isolation`), `db::update_mission_exec_isolation`, `mission::validate_exec`; frontend `MissionCreator` Execution `Listbox`, `ContextHeader` `Shield` (`missionExecIsolation`). _Entry:_ wizard Step 2 → Execution → *Local sandbox*; Shield glyph in the header. (Container/cloud tiers arrive with later movements.)
- **Mission Logbook (worked time · cost · savings)** — Every mission accrues a ledger of what it actually *cost* to run: **worked hours** (real activity time, not wall-clock), **spend**, and **savings vs an all-premium baseline**. Two data spines feed it: (1) **spend attribution** — `spend_events` carries a nullable `mission_id`, stamped at write time from the active mission of the row's workspace (TALK/DIRECT/REVIEW; RUN-legacy and ad-hoc have no workspace so stay unattributed), with a one-shot backfill (`spend_events_mission_backfill_v1`); (2) **activity spans** — a `work_spans` table records *when* a mission was actively worked, written by `record_activity(workspace, surface, source)` which **coalesces** repeated pings into one open span while work stays within a 10-minute idle window (so worked time is span-union seconds, never double-counted across overlapping surfaces). Hooks fire on real work across all four surfaces: a completed **TALK** turn (`chat_engine`), each **DIRECT** stage spend (`record_direct_spend`), **terminal** PTY output (the `spawn_or_attach_terminal` output hook, throttled to ≤1 beat/min per terminal so a live session's span grows without per-chunk cost), and **review** AI calls (`ai_complete` on a workspace). `logbook_summary(scope, from, to)` rolls it up: per-mission worked-second union (merged intervals) + cost + `savings = Σ max(baseline−cost, 0)` + run/message counts + a per-surface breakdown. **Monetization:** the **per-mission** scope is **free** (you always see what your own mission cost); the cross-mission **project/global** scopes are **Pro** (`entitlement::feature::LOGBOOK_REPORTS`, gated by `require_logbook_reports`) — the aggregate "where did my month go" view is the premium surface. The first visible slice is the **Logbook card** in the Talk & Direct Companion (`LogbookCard`): a collapsible micro-panel showing the active mission's worked time (sage, tabular), spend (ivory, tabular — a cost is data, never brass), and savings (verdigris), reserved-geometry + `octo-fade-in` so figures resolve without layout shift; empty state *"No work recorded yet."* _Support:_ `db.rs` (`work_spans`, `record_activity`, `mission_spans_summary`/`mission_run_stats`/`mission_message_count`, `logbook_summary`, `LogbookMissionRow`/`LogbookSurfaceSecs`; `spend_events.mission_id` + `mission_spend`), activity hooks in `chat_engine.rs` (talk), `record_direct_spend` (direct), `commands::spawn_or_attach_terminal` + `db::workspace_for_terminal` (terminal, throttled) and `commands::ai_complete` (review), `commands::logbook_summary` + `require_logbook_reports`, `entitlement::feature::LOGBOOK_REPORTS`; frontend `src/components/LogbookCard.tsx`, `ipc.logbookSummary`, `LogbookMissionRow` type. _Entry:_ Talk/Direct Companion, below the savings ledger.
- **Logbook Room (cross-mission rollup — Pro) — `⌘⇧L`** — A full-screen `OverlayRoom` (Mission Control precedent) that aggregates the Logbook across missions: a **scope switch** (the current project · all missions; a project name too long for its 160px option is middle-truncated — `<MidTruncate>`, 10 characters pinned, design-system E1 — with the full name as its title) × a **period switch** (7 days · 30 days · all time) — each switch's active option is a brass-ghost fill with ivory text, not brass text, so the LOGBOOK eyebrow is the header's only brass ink — a totals ledger in the header (worked time sage · **saved** verdigris, savings-first · spent ivory), and a per-mission table (intent glyph + title · worked · spent in sage, like worked time, not brass · saved · runs · messages, sorted by spend, `octo-rise-in` stagger). **Monetization boundary:** per-mission stays free (the Companion card); the cross-mission Room is **Pro** (`logbook.reports`). A free user still opens the Room but meets a **proactive upsell** (never a failed fetch; a mute lock, and a ceremonial brass-ghost serif CTA "Open the full logbook with Pro", `data-tour="logbook-upsell-cta"` — not a solid-brass button, which stays reserved for the beaconed decision) — the client checks `hasFeature("logbook.reports")` before calling, and the gated `logbook_summary` (project/global scopes) is the backend backstop; either path surfaces the `UpgradeSheet` (which gained a `logbook.reports` copy branch). **Export:** "Copy as Markdown" (`logbookToMarkdown` → `copyToClipboard`) — a shareable report table. The free Companion card carries a **Maximize** affordance that opens the Room, so the free surface is the Room's teaser (free→Pro funnel). _Support:_ `src/components/LogbookRoom.tsx`, shared `src/lib/logbook.ts` (`fmtHours`/`periodRange`/`logbookTotals`/`logbookToMarkdown`), `entitlementStore.hasFeature` + `upgradeStore` + `UpgradeSheet` `logbook.reports` branch, `App.tsx` `⌘⇧L` handler + `logbookOpen` state, `Companion`→`LogbookCard` `onOpenRoom`. _Entry:_ `⌘⇧L` · the Companion Logbook card's Maximize icon.

### Project lifecycle — create
- **New-project wizard (2-step, 4 types)** — Upright-serif "A new project" flow with arabic steps (`STEP 1 OF 2` / `STEP 2 OF 2`; Roman numerals retired app-wide by the Direct beauty redesign). Type cards: **Empty** (∅), **Clone** (⎘), **Open** (⌖), **From a prompt** (`Sparkles` — genesis; replaced the dead "Template · Coming soon" card). Picking "From a prompt" opens the genesis step ("What do you want to build?") — the shared `GenesisPrompt` block + a Location field (default `~/Octopush`); "Set a crew on it" runs the same `handleGenesis` the Welcome uses (a project is born + a crew is staged). So genesis is reachable from **both** entries — a brand-new user (Welcome) and one with projects open (Rail → Add project). _Support:_ `src/components/NewProjectFlow.tsx`, `GenesisPrompt.tsx` (shared with the Welcome), `App.handleGenesis` (`onGenesis` prop, location-aware). _Entry:_ Rail footer "Add project" → full-screen overlay.
- **Create empty project** — Scaffolds a folder under a location (default `~/.octopush/projects`), `git init`, baseline commit, auto-creates the "main" workspace. `create_project` takes an optional `task` (used by prompt genesis to seed the main workspace + mission title) and never `git init`s over a non-empty dir (`resolve_free_project_dir`). _Support:_ `projectStore.create` → `create_project` → `db.insert_project` + `git_ops::init_repo`/`ensure_initial_commit` + `ensure_main_workspace`. _Entry:_ Step 2 "Name your new study".
- **Open existing folder** — Native folder picker; the chosen folder shows as a preview row (`Folder` icon + basename + full path) before opening; registers the folder as a project, `git init`s it if not a repo, heals empty initial commits. _Support:_ `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog`, `ipc.openProject` → `open_project`. _Entry:_ Step 2 "Open a folder.".
- **Clone from remote URL** — Paste git URL → auto-detect repo name + host badge (lucide `Globe` icon + host text, retired `§ host`); editable name + location; streams live progress bar (phase · current/total · %) that follows git's `\r` redraws within a phase. _Support:_ `clone_project` → `clone_via_shell` shells `git clone --progress` through the user's **login shell** (inherits SSH agent/keychain/gitconfig); emits `clone://progress`. URL parsed by `src/lib/parseGitUrl.ts` (mirror of Rust `git_url::parse_git_url`): HTTPS/SCP/`ssh://` on any host, GitLab groups, and Azure DevOps shapes (`org@dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo`, `ssh.dev.azure.com:v3/…`, legacy `*.visualstudio.com`) — the `_git` marker is skipped and percent-encoded names decode to a readable folder name (`My%20Repo` → `My Repo`; a terminal `git clone` would create `My%20Repo`). _Entry:_ Step 2 "Clone a repository."
- **Clone auth fallback (HTTPS PAT)** — On `AuthRequired`, shows a private-repo panel: username + Personal Access Token, "Remember for {host}"; retries via a temp `GIT_ASKPASS` script (`commands::ASKPASS_SCRIPT`, answers git's Username/Password prompts from env vars; token placeholder is `ghp_…` on github.com, neutral elsewhere). The retry runs `git -c credential.helper=` so the typed credentials win over whatever the keychain still holds for that host, and clones from the URL with the typed `username@` embedded when the URL names no user (`url_with_user`) so the origin remote records the account and later lookups are exact even with several accounts for one host. "Remember for {host}" drives both stores: Octopush's settings and, via `git credential approve` through the login shell (only if git actually asked the askpass for the password, and under the URL's user), the keychain — so the new project can fetch and push like a terminal clone; unchecked, nothing is persisted and later remote operations on that project will need credentials. The retry is a real clone: primary button and fields disabled, progress streamed, panel kept (with what was typed) if the token is rejected; editing the URL dismisses the panel and clears its fields; the username prefills from saved credentials, else from the URL's `user@`. Works for any HTTPS host that prompts (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, self-hosted); failures are classified by `classify_clone_failure` under `LC_ALL=C` so the panel appears whatever the user's locale. _Support:_ `AppError::AuthRequired`, `credential_approve_payload`, `ipc.saveGitCredentials`. _Entry:_ inline panel.
- **Clone SSH-key-missing fallback** — On `SshKeyMissing`, suggests `ssh-add …` with "Try again" and "Switch to HTTPS" (rewrites SSH→HTTPS for any user@host, including Azure DevOps `ssh.dev.azure.com:v3/…` → `dev.azure.com/…/_git/…` and legacy `vs-ssh.visualstudio.com:v3/…` → `org.visualstudio.com/…/_git/…`; an unrecognised path on those Azure SSH hosts is left unchanged rather than rewritten onto a host that serves no HTTPS; a custom `ssh://host:port` drops the port). _Support:_ `AppError::SshKeyMissing`, `sshToHttps`. _Entry:_ inline panel.

### Project lifecycle — open / pin / reorder / customize / close / reopen / delete
- **Open project** — Idempotent: un-closes, bumps `last_opened`, heals missing main workspace, preserves Jira key/pin/tint; persists `lastOpenedProjectPath` (restored next launch). _Support:_ `projectStore.open`, `open_project`, `db.reopen_project`.
- **Recent projects list** — Backend-ordered `pinned DESC, sort_order, created_at ASC`, excludes closed. _Support:_ `projectStore.loadRecent` → `list_recent_projects` → `db.list_projects`.
- **Pin / unpin project** — Toggles `pinned`; pinned sort first. A pinned project **stays in its project group**: it leads the group, and because a group stands where its first project stands, the group comes up into the pinned run with it (see "Project groups" under the Workspace Rail). _Support:_ `set_project_pinned`. _Entry:_ Project context menu.
- **Reorder projects (drag + menu)** — Drag-handle reorders the rail (persists `sort_order`); conditional "Move up"/"Move down" menu items, which step the way the rail is drawn (`stepInRail`): a project in a project group moves among that group's projects and has no step past its ends; a loose project steps over a whole group. A step is offered only when it would show: not past the rail's ends, and not where the pinned-first listing would undo it (an unpinned project has no step above a pinned one, a pinned one none below an unpinned one), so the menu never writes an order that changes nothing. Every reorder persists the full order as the rail shows it, so a group's projects are one run in `sort_order` too. The new order shows at once (pinned first, as the backend lists it) and is then written; a refused write puts the old order back and toasts `Couldn't reorder the projects` / `Your rail is back as it was.`. _Support:_ `@dnd-kit`, `projectStore.setOrder` → `set_project_order`, `src/lib/railGroups.ts` (`stepInRail`, `resolveTopDrop`). _Entry:_ header grip / context menu.
- **Move a project to a group** — Project context menu **Move to group ›** (first row of the pin / move block). In a project's menu the group action is about **project groups**: the submenu lists them (the current one checked), then **New group…**, which makes a group that **already holds this project** and opens its name in edit (a group made from an item never starts empty), and **Remove from group** for a project that is in one. Joining a group from the menu makes the project its last one (the order is persisted); leaving keeps the project's own place. See "Project groups" under the Workspace Rail. _Support:_ `MoveToGroupItem.tsx`, `src/lib/groupActions.ts` (`createProjectGroup`, `moveProjectToGroup`). _Entry:_ Project context menu (right-click, or `⇧F10` / the context-menu key on the project line).
- **Customize project (name + tint)** — `ProjectCustomizeMenu`: name input + 7-swatch tint grid; persists to **both** localStorage and DB. _Support:_ `ProjectCustomizeMenu.tsx`, `update_project_customization`. _Entry:_ "Change tint" / "Rename project".
- **Set Jira project key** — Optional menu item; stored per-project for branch→issue auto-detection. _Support:_ `update_project_jira_key`. _Entry:_ "Set Jira project key…".
- **Close project (soft)** — Sets `closed_at`, preserves workspaces/terminals/chats; restorable from Recently closed. _Support:_ `close_project`. _Entry:_ context menu danger row.
- **Reopen project** — Clears `closed_at`, bumps `last_opened`. _Support:_ `reopen_project`. _Entry:_ Recently-closed drawer "Restore".
- **Delete project (from disk, permanent)** — Deletes all workspaces+worktrees, then `rm -rf` project dir, then DB row; guarded by a **type-the-name** confirm. _Support:_ `delete_project`; `ConfirmDialog requireInput`. _Entry:_ context menu danger row.
- **Project utility actions** — Reveal in Finder, Copy path, Open in editor, Open in terminal. _Support:_ `reveal_in_finder`/`open_in_editor`/`open_in_terminal`. _Entry:_ context menu.

### Workspace lifecycle — create
- **New-mission wizard (3-step, intent-first)** — "A new mission" flow (arabic step index `1 Intent` · `2 Task & branch` · `3 Setup script`). **Step 1 — Intent:** a card grid — **Build** (`Hammer`) / **Fix** (`Wrench`) write code; **Review** (`Eye` "Review the work") / **Probe** (`FlaskConical` "Probe a question") / **Perf** (`Gauge` "Chase a regression" — a specialized read-only investigation that stages the **Perf probe** crew, see §4) are **non-code, read-only** intents, and **Test a ticket** (`ClipboardCheck`, "Build it, run it, ship nothing.", card 6, `data-tour="mission-intent-test"`) builds and runs a ticket locally (keyboard `1`–`6`, ←/→/↑/↓ to move, Enter to continue) — you begin a mission, and the worktree follows. Review/probe/perf force **`readonly`** git isolation: the Isolation disclosure shows a fixed *"Read-only — its agents read the code and never modify it, enforced by the sandbox rather than asked of the agent"* note (the writer Git-state/Execution Listboxes are hidden for these intents). **Test a ticket** always sends **`ephemeral`**, also when a PR is picked (whose head still becomes the base); its Isolation disclosure shows *"Runs locally, ships nothing. This workspace is thrown away when the mission is done. Talk's agents can build, run and edit config here. A push, pull request or publish they ask for is refused by Octopush, not asked of them. Crews don't run in this mission."* in place of the Git-state Listbox (Execution stays). With a ticket linked, the base defaults to the ticket's own branch (`lib/ticketBranch.ts` `ticketBranch`: the first local branch whose detected key is exactly the ticket's, then the first remote one, never an earlier `test/` branch; otherwise the repo default) and the branch to `test/<KEY>` (through `uniqueBranch`), so the ticket's branch never moves; a base the user picks is kept. Once created, the mission's Talk composer is seeded (`chatStore.seedComposer`) with `lib/testBrief.ts` `testBrief(issue)` from `get_issue`: the key, summary and URL, the description, and the ask (build it, bring it up, follow or derive the test plan, record each command and what it showed, end with a verdict of Works, Doesn't work or Couldn't test, then the evidence, the steps to reproduce a failure and what couldn't be checked). A ticket that can't be read still gives its key and summary and says the description couldn't be read. Nothing is sent until the user sends it. The `initialIntent` prop opens the wizard on an intent. **Step 2 — Task & branch:** task → a **short branch** (`lib/branchName.ts` `branchFromTask`: the ticket key first when the mission is created from one, else — only when the project has a Jira key — that project's first key found in the task (a bare `UTF-8` is never a ticket); the key's text is removed before words are picked so it never repeats, glued to punctuation or not; then up to four significant words of the task, filler dropped (`genesis.pickWords`, the same rule as project names); never over 60 characters, cut on a word boundary and never inside the key — `GUIDE-3753-add-gitlab-group-preview` from a 25-word summary; a name an existing branch already has gets `-2`, `-3` (`uniqueBranch`), so two tasks sharing their first words never share a workspace; editable override, verbatim on blur, the typed field capped at 60), live "BRANCH … from {base}" preview whose worktree path shows the directory as the backend will cap it, deep paths included (`worktreeSlugMax`), optional PR base (PrPicker), and a collapsed **Isolation** disclosure (`Reveal`) with **two labelled `Listbox`es** — **Git state** (*Own worktree* / *Ephemeral*; picking a PR sets `pr` and shows an info panel instead) and **Execution** (*None* / *Local sandbox* — the mission's `exec_isolation` axis; sandbox confines the agent's writes to the workspace, **free**). **Step 3 — Setup:** setup-script textarea (remembered per-project; prefilled from a Conductor repo's `.conductor/settings.toml` when the project has no template — see below); CTA "Begin the mission". The chosen **intent**, **git isolation**, and **execution isolation** are recorded on the auto-paired mission (`create_workspace` forwards intent/git to `mission::ensure_for_workspace`, then applies `exec_isolation` in place via `update_mission_exec_isolation` when it differs). _Support:_ `src/components/MissionCreator.tsx`, `workspaceStore.create` → `create_workspace(…, intent, gitIsolation, execIsolation)` → `workspace::create` + `mission::ensure_for_workspace` + `mission::validate_exec`, `primitives/Reveal` + `controls/Listbox`, `companionPrefsStore`. _Entry:_ per-project "+" on header.
- **Ensure-or-adopt creation (always gives you a place to work)** — `create_workspace` runs through the shared `workspace::create` (also used by `octopush-mcp`) and *ensures* a workspace for the branch exists, returning a `CreateOutcome` (`created` | `adopted` | `existed` | `restored`). It never fails just because the branch is in use: (1) a workspace already tracking the branch is returned (un-archived + worktree rebuilt if it was archived); (2) if the branch is already checked out somewhere — the main worktree or one made outside Octopush — that checkout is **adopted** (a workspace row is registered over it; no second worktree, since git allows a branch in only one worktree); (3) otherwise a fresh worktree is created under `.octopus-worktrees/`. Idempotent on `(project, branch)` and on the checkout path, so it never duplicates a rail row (the store also upserts by id). _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/workspace.rs` (`create`, `provision_worktree`, `reuse_or_restore`, `workspace_at_path`), `git_ops::create_worktree`/`live_worktree_on_branch`, `db::find_workspace_by_branch`/`set_workspace_worktree_path`.
- **Managed vs adopted worktrees** — Each workspace row carries a **`managed`** flag (`workspaces.managed`, default 1): worktrees Octopush *created* are managed; an *adopted* checkout (a branch already checked out that we registered a workspace over) is set `managed=0`. Only managed worktrees are ever `rm -rf`'d (and their branch deleted) on delete/archive; adopted checkouts — and the main workspace (project root) — just drop/flip the DB row. Octopush never destroys a directory or branch it didn't create. _Support:_ `db::set_workspace_managed`/`is_workspace_managed`; `commands::owns_worktree_on_disk` (`managed && !is_project_root`), used by `delete_workspace`/`archive_workspace`; adoption sets the flag in `workspace::create`.
- **Branch name override** — Editable branch field (at most 60 characters); the suggestion comes from `branchFromTask`; warns "Branch exists — the workspace will reuse it" on collision (creation then reuses that branch). _Support:_ `MissionCreator.tsx`, `lib/branchName.ts`, `listBranches`.
- **Short worktree directories** — The worktree lives at `.octopus-worktrees/<branch slug ≤ 60>-<id8>`: the branch part is cut on a word boundary (`workspace::shorten_slug`, `DIR_SLUG_MAX`), and under a deep project path it gives way further so the whole path, sanitized the way Claude Code names its transcript directory, stays within Claude Code's 200-character cap (`CLAUDE_DIR_NAME_CAP`, `worktree_dir_name_under`, never under eight characters of slug). Why: Claude Code's transcripts for a session are keyed by that path, and a path past the cap is one the ledger could not follow. A symlinked parent counts at its resolved length, since Claude Code records the physical cwd. The MCP's `create_workspace` derives the same short branch from a task (`workspace::branch_from_task`, a mirror of the frontend's — `src/lib/branchName.fixtures.json` pins both to the same cases and a test pins the Rust stopword list to `genesis.ts`), with the project's Jira key for detection and `unique_branch` against the repo's branches and the project's workspaces. _Support:_ `workspace.rs` (`branch_from_task`, `pick_words`, `unique_branch`, `shorten_slug`, `worktree_dir_name`, `worktree_dir_name_under`), `octopush-mcp/tools.rs`.
- **Base branch picker** — Inline `BaseBranchPicker` lists local branches (repo default first) + a "REMOTE" section (`origin/…`); filter above 8 branches. _Support:_ `BaseBranchPicker.tsx`, `list_branches`; base resolved by `git_ops::resolve_base`. _Entry:_ creator branch-preview row.
- **Start workspace from a PR** — `PrPicker` chip retargets base to a PR's head ref (`ensurePrBranch` fetches it), prefills task with PR title. _Support:_ `MissionCreator.handlePickPr`, `ipc.ensurePrBranch`. _Entry:_ creator branch row.
- **Setup script** — Commands that run in a visible `setup` Run terminal when the mission's worktree is created; the mission opens either way. Only a freshly created worktree runs it (`CreateOutcome::Created`): a reused, restored or adopted workspace never re-runs it, and step 3 says so for an existing branch. Shows the honest worktree path; remembered on success as the project template (prefill in `companionPrefsStore`, and `projects.setup_script` via `set_project_setup_script` so Routines' fresh worktrees run it too). Step 3 says so ("Saved as this project's setup script…", `data-tour="mission-setup-template"`); when the template changes an info toast confirms it (**Setup script saved for this project** / **…cleared…**), and a failed write raises **Couldn't save the project's setup script** (the mission is still created; Routines keep the previous script). A workspace created over `octopush-mcp` stores its script but never runs it. _Support:_ `create_workspace` (returns `setupTerminalId` / `setupError`), `workspace_setup.rs`, `MissionCreator.tsx` (`data-tour="mission-setup-script"`).
- **Setup script from `.conductor/settings.toml`** — A repo set up for Conductor already declares its setup: when the project has no setup template (`projects.setup_script` and the `companionPrefsStore` prefill both empty), step 3 asks `conductor_setup_script(projectId)` (the backend reads the repo from the project's row in the DB, never from a path the frontend sends) and, if the repo has one, prefills the field with `[scripts].setup` from `.conductor/settings.toml`, with `.conductor/settings.local.toml` on top (its `setup`, when it has one, wins; an empty one clears it). A quiet mono line under the field says **From .conductor/settings.toml · edit before it runs** (`data-tour="mission-setup-conductor"`, `.octo-rise-in`), plus **· N lines** when the script is taller than the six-line field and **· long line** when any line is over 200 characters (so a line below the fold, or one hidden by wrapping, can't pass unseen), and **· non-ASCII characters** when the script has any (a homoglyph letter is worth a closer look); a script that reads `CONDUCTOR_PORT` gets no note, since the setup terminal starts with the workspace's port block (see "Workspace ports"). The line shows only while the field holds exactly what was read, and hides after any edit. Nothing runs until the user begins the mission, a value the user already typed is never overwritten, and the save-as-template behaviour is unchanged (the script, edited or not, becomes the project's template on create). The reader returns nothing when `settings.toml` is missing (a local file alone isn't enough), either file isn't valid TOML or `setup` isn't a string, the script is blank, a file resolves outside the repo (a symlinked file or `.conductor` directory — canonical-prefix containment, like `contained_path`), isn't a regular file (a FIFO or device is refused without blocking: the resolved path is opened `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` and checked on the open handle), or is over 64 KiB, and when the script contains anything but ordinary characters (`workspace_setup::hides_characters`, an allowlist that fails closed): printable ASCII, space, tab, newline, CR only within CRLF, non-ASCII letters and digits, and the Latin combining accents U+0300–036F except the grapheme joiner U+034F — and a non-ASCII character never starts a word: it can't come first, or right after ASCII whitespace, a shell operator or a quote (`; & | ( ) < > ' " \ = $` and the backtick), because combining marks are letters by property and one laid on a space makes ` <mark>#` read as a comment while bash runs what follows. So "café" (NFC or NFD) and `mkdir -p src/設定` pass, while `cd 設定` is refused (rare). Never accepted: whitespace look-alikes (NBSP, U+2028, …, which bash doesn't split words on, so a `# ;` that looks like a comment would run), controls (C0, DEL, C1), format, bidi, zero-width, tag or variation-selector characters, or blank fillers (U+115F–1160, U+17B4–17B5, U+3164, U+FFA0) — whether written literally or as TOML escapes. A failed lookup leaves the field empty. Run and archive scripts aren't read. _Support:_ `workspace_setup::conductor_setup_script` (the `toml` crate), `commands::conductor_setup_script`, `ipc.conductorSetupScript`, `lib/conductorSetup.ts` (`wantsConductorPrefill`, `conductorSourceLine`), `MissionCreator.tsx`.
- **Conductor variables for setup scripts** — Every setup script (a mission's setup terminal and a Routine's headless setup) gets Conductor's `CONDUCTOR_ROOT_PATH` (the project's main checkout), `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_PATH` (the new worktree) and `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME` (the workspace name), so a script imported from a Conductor repo runs unchanged — but only where the variable isn't already set. **Setup terminal:** the values reach the runner as `OCTOPUSH_CONDUCTOR_*` (`workspace_setup::runner_env`), which unsets them and exports Conductor's names for the script only (not the shell left open afterwards), skipping any the user exports; the script runs under `$SHELL -l -c`, so a value set in the user's login profile also wins. **Routine:** only the app's own environment is checked — a variable in it is kept, otherwise Octopush's value is added to the `bash -c` env (`workspace_setup::conductor_env`, `routines::run_setup`); the user's shell profiles aren't read, so a value set only there doesn't apply. `CONDUCTOR_PORT` isn't the runner's: the setup terminal, like every Run terminal of the workspace, starts with the workspace's port block (see "Workspace ports") and the runner passes it to the script untouched; a Routine's headless setup gets no port yet. Other terminals and agents never see the three path and name variables. _Support:_ `workspace_setup.rs` (`RUNNER`, `runner_env`, `conductor_env`), `commands.rs::start_setup_terminal`, `routines.rs`.
- **Share with new missions (link dependency folders, copy env files)** — Opt-in, per project: step 3 of the new-mission wizard lists, under the setup script, what the project's main checkout has and git ignores — dependency folders to **link** (`node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`; build outputs such as `target`, `dist` or `build` are never offered) and top-level `.env` / `.env.*` regular files to **copy** (a symlinked one isn't offered) — each with a `Link` / `Copy` `TogglePill`, all off until the user turns one on (`data-tour="mission-share"`; the section shows only when there is something to list). Each row says what it is: a link is "the main checkout's own folder, linked"; a copy is "copied into the worktree, readable by the mission's agents". The copy under the list says it plainly: applied to a new worktree before its setup script and saved for the project; **a linked folder is the main checkout's own folder, not a copy**, so an install or a clean run inside a mission changes it for the main checkout and for every other mission; **a copied env file is a plain file in the mission's worktree, so agents in the mission can read it**; copies stay git-ignored so they never stage; to keep a link out of commits Octopush adds its name to the repo's local `.git/info/exclude`, where it stays; and Routines and workspaces created over MCP don't share. **Install warning:** while a dependency folder is switched on to link and the setup script in the field above contains an install or clean command (`npm ci`, `npm install`/`npm i`, `pnpm install`/`pnpm i`, bare `yarn` or `yarn install`, `bun install`, `pip install`, `uv sync`/`uv pip install`, `poetry install`, or an `rm -r…` of `node_modules`/`.venv`/`venv`; comment lines ignored), an amber line names the commands and the linked folders: "This setup script runs npm ci. With node_modules linked, that changes the main checkout's folder, for the main checkout and for every other mission." (`data-tour="mission-share-install"`, `lib/shareWithMissions.setupInstallWarning`; not shown for a sandboxed mission, which gets no links). The choice is saved (`set_share_with_missions`, `projects.share_with_missions` as JSON, sanitized to the allowlist) **before** `create_workspace` runs, and a failed save stops the creation with an inline error; an unchanged list isn't rewritten. `create_workspace` then applies it only to a freshly created worktree (`CreateOutcome::Created`, never the main checkout, compared by canonical path), before the setup terminal starts: an entry is applied only while the main checkout **still git-ignores it** (the list was saved earlier; otherwise it is left out as "no longer git-ignored in the main checkout"); links are absolute symlinks to the main checkout's folder, copies keep the source's permissions and never replace anything already in the worktree. Because a `.gitignore` line like `node_modules/` matches only directories and never a symlink, each linked name is added as `/<name>` under an Octopush marker to the repo's local `.git/info/exclude` (shared by every worktree, never committed); the file is replaced in one step (written beside it, then renamed). These lines are written only when a link is made and are never removed, not even when the project stops sharing. Afterwards every shared entry must be git-ignored **in the worktree** (its branch may carry another `.gitignore`), or it is removed again and reported, so a copied `.env` stays an ignored, untracked file the secret guard never sees staged, and a link never reaches a commit. What was made is **recorded** in the worktree's own git directory (`<git dir>/octopush-shared`, outside the working tree, gone with the worktree), and only recorded entries are ever removed again. **Sandboxed missions** (`exec_isolation = sandbox`) get **neither links nor env copies**: a link points outside the worktree, and Claude Code's read guard would refuse reads through it; an env file is not copied because a sandboxed stage can't read outside its working directory and a copy would put the file inside it. Both are reported under **Some entries weren't shared** ("node_modules: not linked in a sandboxed mission", ".env: not copied into a sandboxed mission"); step 3 says so in amber when anything is switched on and Execution is *Local sandbox*, and adds that turning the sandbox on later removes a mission's links and its unchanged env copies (`data-tour="mission-share-sandbox"`). The same holds when Execution changes after creation: when `update_mission` sets `exec_isolation = sandbox` (the Direct launcher's "sandbox it" toggle), and when `create_workspace` reuses an existing worktree for a sandboxed mission, `commands::unshare_for_sandbox` → `worktree_share::unshare` takes back what the record lists: a recorded link that is still a symlink to the main checkout's folder of the same name is removed (the link, never the folder), and a recorded env copy that is still byte-identical to the main checkout's file is removed; a copy that was **changed in the mission is kept** (deleting it could lose work) and named, and the mission's agents can still read it. A real folder, a link the user made (even one to the main checkout's folder), a file Octopush didn't copy and the main checkout itself (however its path is spelled) are left alone. `update_mission` returns `unlinked`, `uncopied` and `keptCopies`, and the **Sandbox enabled** toast names them ("Removed the link to the main checkout's node_modules; install inside this mission if it needs it.", "Removed the copied .env from this mission's worktree.", ".env.local was changed in this mission, so it stays: its agents can still read it.", `lib/shareWithMissions.sandboxOnBody`); a reused worktree reports them under **Some entries weren't shared**. The toggle's tooltip says folders linked and unchanged env files copied from the main checkout are removed. Turning the sandbox off again doesn't bring them back. What was shared shows on the setup terminal's first line (`· linked node_modules · copied .env`, via `OCTOPUSH_SETUP_SHARED`, unset before the script runs); with no setup script, an info toast **Shared with the new mission** says the same, and anything left out raises **Some entries weren't shared** with one reason per entry. **A Routine's fresh worktree and an `octopush-mcp` workspace don't share** (decided): both call `workspace::create` directly and never reach the sharing step, and a test pins that neither file references it. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/worktree_share.rs` (`LINK_CANDIDATES`, `candidates`, `apply`, `exclude_with`, `write_atomic`, `RECORD_FILE`, `recorded`, `unshare`, `same_dir`), `commands.rs` (`share_with_missions`, `set_share_with_missions`, `share_into_fresh_worktree`, `unshare_for_sandbox`, `unshared_sentences`, `update_mission`'s `UpdatedMission`), `db::get_project_share`/`set_project_share`, `workspace_setup::SHARED_ENV`, `lib/shareWithMissions.ts` (`setupInstallCommands`, `setupInstallWarning`, `sandboxOnBody`), `MissionCreator.tsx`, `UnattendedReadiness.tsx`, `missionsStore.setExecIsolation`, `workspaceStore.create`.
- **Setup terminal** — `create_workspace` adds a `setup` terminal record and spawns its PTY through the daemon at once (so it runs whatever the UI does, and its output survives an app restart): the daemon starts the app-written runner (`<data dir>/octopush/setup-runner.sh`) instead of a bare login shell; it runs the script (passed in `OCTOPUSH_SETUP_SCRIPT`, never interpolated, with Conductor's variables — see above) with `$SHELL -l -c` (a Routine's headless run uses `bash -c` instead — see Routines), prints `setup finished · exit 0` or `setup failed · exit N`, reports the code with a private OSC (`ESC ] 6973 ; exit=N BEL`), then stays open as a login shell. The new workspace opens with the setup terminal as its active session. The Run pane hands the OSC to `terminalsStore.reportSetupExit`, which honours it only in a setup terminal — one `trackSetup` registered (the ids persist in `localStorage` `octopush.setupTerminals` so a restart still restores them; closing the terminal forgets it); the same bytes printed in any other terminal change nothing. Its cell on the session line reads `setup · running` → `setup failed · exit N` with a static rouge dot (`data-tour="run-setup-session"`); a failure of a run seen starting raises a toast with **Open the setup terminal** (switches to that workspace's Run session, opening its project first when another project is open — the rail's cross-project path, `lib/workspaceTarget.ts`); a replayed marker after a restart restores the state silently. If the setup can't start (daemon down), the workspace is still created and a "Setup didn't start" toast says why. _Support:_ `commands.rs::start_setup_terminal`, `lib/setupRun.ts`, `TerminalPane.tsx`, `run/SessionLine.tsx`, `terminalsStore.setupByTerminal`.
- **Link Jira issue on create** — Optional `linkIssueKeyOnCreate` links the ticket after creation. _Support:_ `update_workspace_link`.
- **Existing-workspace-for-ticket guard** — Modal warns if a workspace already maps to that ticket. _Support:_ `ExistingWorkspaceAlertModal.tsx`.

### Workspace lifecycle — archive / restore / rename / delete / customize / link
- **Archive workspace** — For a **managed** worktree: removes the dir + prunes the worktree slot (by path) but **keeps the branch**; flips DB `status='archived'`. Adopted checkouts and the main worktree keep their directory (row-only flip). _Support:_ `archive_workspace`, `owns_worktree_on_disk`, `git_ops::delete_worktree`. _Entry:_ context menu (hidden for main).
- **Restore archived workspace** — Recreates the worktree from the kept branch, flips `status='active'`; lists archived rows newest-first, each with its mission group's name before the branch when it has one: restoring returns it to that group if the group still exists, and loose otherwise (see "Archive" under "Mission groups"). _Support:_ `ArchivedWorkspacesModal.tsx`, `restore_workspace`/`list_archived_workspaces`, `git_ops::create_worktree`. _Entry:_ Project context menu "Archived workspaces…".
- **Archive merged missions (#963)** — Project context menu, after "Archived workspaces…", only while one of the project's rows says "merged · archive?": **Archive merged missions…** with their count (`GitMerge`). It opens a confirm that lists them by name (the first eight, then "and N more"; a mission whose worktree holds local files reads "fix-a (has local files)") and says the worktrees go and the branches stay; with local files it adds that archiving deletes them (up to three named, then "and N more") and Undo doesn't bring them back; when one of the listed paths is under `.claude/` (Claude Code settings beyond Octopush's own hooks, see "Merged-and-clean missions") it adds "That includes Claude Code's settings in .claude/, such as its "don't ask again" choices." The button reads **Archive it** for one mission and **Archive them** for several. Confirming hands the list, with the exact local-file paths it named per mission, to `archive_merged_workspaces`, which re-checks each mission at that moment and archives only those that still pass (see "Archive merged missions (re-checked)"); a **Skipped** warning toast names each mission left in place and why ("fix-a has uncommitted changes.", the first four, then "And N more."), and the offer is read again; the success toast ("Archived 3 merged missions") offers **Undo**, which restores them all; "Archive failed" only when the whole call fails. The list is exactly the rows that offer the action (`archivableMissions`). _Support:_ `ProjectContextMenu` (`mergedCount`, `onArchiveMerged`), `archiveMergedBody`, `archiveMergedMissions`, `skippedBody`, `ConfirmDialog`.
- **Delete workspace (permanent)** — For a **managed** worktree: removes the dir, prunes the slot (by path), deletes the branch, removes the DB row; confirm dialog. Adopted checkouts and the main worktree keep their directory and branch (row-only removal). _Support:_ `delete_workspace`, `owns_worktree_on_disk`, `git_ops::delete_worktree`/`delete_branch`. _Entry:_ context menu danger (hidden for main).
- **Rename workspace** — Single-field `RenameDialog`. _Support:_ `rename_workspace`. _Entry:_ context menu.
- **Customize workspace (glyph + tint)** — `WorkspaceCustomizeMenu`: 1-char glyph + 7-swatch tint grid; persists `null` when matching defaults. The typed glyph is saved through the same `normalizeGlyph` the rail and ⌘K render with, so what is saved is what shows (an unusable glyph such as `ß` saves as the default). _Support:_ `update_workspace_customization`. _Entry:_ context menu / right-click monogram.
- **Link / change / unlink Jira ticket** — Conditional menu items by linkage state; opens a Jira ticket picker. Under a project that reads Epiku they say "Epiku story", the picker is titled "Link Epiku story" / "Change Epiku story", and its rows are that project's stories; a project whose tracker isn't the cached list's gets no rows, only the exact-key fallback, checked against its own tracker (`issueTrackerSelectors.ticketNoun`, `pickerCandidates`). _Support:_ `update_workspace_link`. _Entry:_ context menu Jira group.
- **Workspace utility actions** — Reveal in Finder, Copy path, Copy branch name, Open in editor, Open in terminal. _Support:_ same ipc helpers. _Entry:_ context menu.
- **Move a mission to a group** — Workspace context menu **Move to group ›** (after Customize…): the project's mission groups, **New group…**, **Remove from group**. Project context menu **New mission group** makes an empty one: it sits in the menu's missions block with **Archived workspaces…**, a block away from **Move to group ›**, and is never labelled plain "New group" (it was in 0.4.131; from a project, "New group" read as "a group for this project", which is what **Move to group › New group…** now does). See "Mission groups" under the Workspace Rail. _Support:_ `MoveToGroupItem.tsx`, `src/lib/groupActions.ts`. _Entry:_ context menus.

### Workspace Rail (left panel) — "the index"
- **One surface, no frames** — Projects and missions read as a typeset index, not a file explorer: no project cards, no bordered monograms, no chips. Hierarchy is carried by type and space (a 28px serif project line over 32px rows); `bg-octo-panel` with one right hairline. _Support:_ `WorkspaceRail.tsx`. _Spec:_ `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-workspace-rail-index-redesign-design.md`.
- **Project header (index line)** — `ProjectMark` hexagon in **mute** (the project's tint accent only when the user chose one via "Change tint" — never N brass hexagons) + the project name in **Spectral 13**, ivory when the project holds the active workspace and sage otherwise (ivory on hover). The name is middle-truncated (`<MidTruncate>`, `RAIL_NAME_TAIL` pinned, design-system E1) so projects sharing an org prefix stay apart, with the full name in the fold button's title (in its own while a filter is typed). The hover actions and the open project's chevron take no width until hover/focus (`max-width` + opacity, 220ms; their focus rings are inset), so the name uses the whole line meanwhile. The name is the one keyboard-reachable fold control (a button with `aria-expanded`); the "New mission in …" plus and the drag grip are revealed on hover/focus, and so is the chevron — pointer decoration (`aria-hidden`, not a second tab stop) that stays visible while folded and rotates −90°. While a filter is typed every project is held open: the name stops toggling, the chevron is not rendered, and the stored fold state is left untouched. Right-click anywhere on the line → project menu; `⇧F10` or the context-menu key on the focused name opens it at the line, and that menu gives the line the focus back when it closes; the focus is held on the line through what the menu did (`src/lib/railFocus.ts`): **Move to group** renders the project under another parent, which replaces the focused element, and the new line is focused again after the rail renders, until the next key or pointer press and for 1 s at most (`HOLD_MS`), so a later reload never pulls the focus back. In a tinted **project group** the hexagon takes the group's tint when the project has none of its own (`projectMarkColor`). While the project is **folded** over a workspace that signals attention, the line carries the signal for it (see "Attention — the single beacon"): the mark pulses for the beacon, or a static 5px brass dot joins the aggregates. _Support:_ `SortableProjectGroup`, `ProjectMark.tsx` (`color` prop).
- **Header aggregates only while folded** — `N missions · dirty count (GitCommitHorizontal) · open-PR count (GitPullRequest, verdigris)` in mono 10px mute fade in (opacity + `max-width`, so they cost the name no width while hidden) when the project is folded and are `aria-hidden` + `inert` while it is open — a count visible in the list is never repeated in its header. _Support:_ `SortableProjectGroup`.
- **Rail collapse / expand** — Two widths: 280px / **44px** (220ms, width-only transition). Collapsed = the slim-rail geometry of Review's collapsed navigator: 32px cells, a reserved 2px identity edge, one cluster per project headed by its mark (`role="img"`, named), a 20px hairline between clusters, the `+` at the top. A mission group keeps its two marks at this width (see "Mission groups"); a project group is a sub-cluster between two hairlines that span the rail (see "Project groups"). _Support:_ `WorkspaceRail`, `CollapsedRail`; toggle in the footer (`PerfMonitorBar.onToggleRail`).
- **Collapsed flyout** — Hover or focus a cell for a popover in the shared menu chrome (`MENU_CHROME` from `src/lib/menuStyles.ts`, the same string `MenuSurface` wears), portalled to `document.body` (a wheel over it never scrolls the rail out from under it), positioned `fixed` against the measured cell and clamped into the viewport after measuring: the eyebrow, outermost first (`project`; `project · mission group` for a mission in a group; with the project's own group in front when it has one: `project group · project · mission group`) · mission name (serif) · status line (`ticket · ↑N · ↓N · PR open · uncommitted changes · overlaps {workspace} · N files · working… · needs your attention (kind)`; `clean` only once a git summary has arrived and says so, nothing while it is unknown) · the `⌘N` jump. 120ms leave grace (re-entering the flyout cancels the close); a flyout the keyboard opened ignores the pointer leaving and closes on blur-out; any flyout closes on scroll. Cells carry no native `title` — the flyout is the tooltip; the accessible name is the mission name. _Support:_ `CollapsedCell`.
- **Per-project fold** — Persisted to localStorage (`railProjectCollapsed`); grid-rows 0fr↔1fr, 280ms; a live filter unfolds everything. A project unfolds by itself when one of its groups goes into rename (a group was just created from its menu). _Support:_ `WorkspaceRail`.
- **Search line** — One 36px head line (expanded rail only): borderless `Search` icon + upright-serif placeholder "Find a project or mission" (short enough to fit beside the state filter and `+` at the default rail width, elided with an ellipsis if the rail is narrower; the full "Find a project, group or mission" is the line's `title` and the input's label); the line's bottom hairline turns brass on focus. Matches project-group, project, mission-group or mission names (case-insensitive; a project-group hit keeps all of its projects with all their missions, and a group with no hit of its own keeps only the projects that have one); the hit inside a mission or group name is washed with the found-match tokens (`--octo-match` / `-ring` / `-ink`) via the shared `HighlightedLabel` + `matchRange` primitive (`src/components/primitives/HighlightedLabel.tsx`, also the file tree's), which locates the hit on the name itself with an escaped case-insensitive regex — never on a lowercased copy; a project-name hit keeps all of its missions, and a group-name hit keeps all of that group's missions (`filterRailItems`); a group with no hit of its own shows only its member hits and leaves when it has none; projects with no hit leave the rail; "Nothing matches" (serif, mute) when nothing survives; Escape clears; every drag (projects, project groups, missions, mission-group headers) is off while filtering. _Support:_ `WorkspaceRail`, `HitName`, `src/lib/railGroups.ts`.
- **State filter (#963)** — A `ListFilter` icon at the end of the search line (title "Show missions by state", `data-tour="rail-state-filter"`) opens a menu: **Every mission · Needs you · Working · Idle**, each state with its count (`menuitemradio`, a check on the current one). The state is the fleet chip's: a run that `needsYou` → Needs you; else a run in flight (running, or parked on a Claude plan with a resume scheduled) or the row's marching edge (chat, terminal) → Working; else Idle (`runsState` / `missionState` in `src/lib/railState.ts`, read through a shallow-compared selector so a run's cost tick re-renders nothing). It narrows whatever the text filter leaves (`filterRailMissions`: a group keeps its passing members and leaves with none, whatever its name; a project with none leaves), and like the text filter it holds every fold open, turns drags off and lets a selection go. While a state is picked the icon is brass and names it ("needs you"); alone, an empty result reads "No mission needs you" / "No mission is working" / "No mission is idle". Not persisted; the slim rail ignores it, and ⌘K's Go to group clears it when it hides the group. _Support:_ `RailStateFilter.tsx`, `WorkspaceRail`.
- **Merged · archive? (#963)** — A mission whose PR is merged at its worktree's HEAD with a clean worktree (`mergedPrByWs`, see "Merged-and-clean missions"), that is Idle, has no open PR on its branch again and whose latest git summary shows no changes and no commits ahead (`archivableMerge`) shows a quiet mono "merged · archive?" button at the end of its row meta (mute, brass on hover; `data-tour="rail-merged-archive"`). Its title names the PR and says what Undo restores: with local files, "Its local files go too and Undo doesn't bring them back, so they are listed first."; without, "Undo brings it back whole: it holds no local files and no saved Claude Code choices." Clicking it archives that mission through the same re-check (worktree removed, branch kept; a mission that no longer passes is skipped with the same warning toast); while that runs the button is disabled and a second click, here or from the menu, is ignored (`workspaceStore.archivingIds`) and the success toast offers **Undo**, which restores it from the kept branch and reloads the project. A mission with local files opens the single-mission confirm first ("Archive this merged mission?", **Archive it**), since Undo can't bring those back. Nothing is archived by age or by itself. _Support:_ `WorkspaceRow`, `src/lib/archiveMerged.ts`, `App` (`onArchiveMerged`).
- **Add project** — The `+` icon button (title/aria "Add project") at the right of the search line, and at the top of the collapsed rail. Icon only — no text label, no footer row. _Support:_ `WorkspaceRail.onAddProject`; `ProjectPickerModal.tsx` for the generic picker.
- **Active workspace scrolls into view** — Whenever a workspace becomes active (a rail click, a ⌘1…⌘9 jump, a ⌘K pick, a project just opened whose workspace lands below the fold), the rail scrolls its row into view: `block: "nearest"`, so a row already on screen never moves, smooth unless `prefers-reduced-motion` (then an instant jump); once per activation, so refreshes never yank the list, and an id that becomes active before its row renders is scrolled to as soon as the row appears. Both widths (expanded rows and collapsed cells). **Inside a folded mission group:** activating the mission unfolds its group first (and stores that), then the scroll is repeated once the fold has opened (at once, and again after the 280ms transition, so reduced motion and the animated case both land on the row). Only the workspace the app restores by itself at launch is not an activation (`workspaceStore.launchRestoredId`: what the load of the project the startup restore reopened made active; the restore flags it with `beginLaunchRestore` before opening the project and `cancelLaunchRestore` when it couldn't), so a group folded on purpose stays folded across a restart; an app that launched with no project to reopen has no restored workspace, so the first project the user opens unfolds as any activation does; every other first activation unfolds, also when the rail mounted with nothing active, and so does coming back to the restored workspace later. _Support:_ `src/hooks/useScrollActiveIntoView.ts` (finds the `aria-current="location"` monogram/cell), `WorkspaceRail` + `CollapsedRail`.
- **Workspace selection + persistence** — Click selects; remembers last-active workspace **per project**. _Support:_ `workspaceStore.select`/`rememberActiveForProject`.
- **Row anatomy (32px)** — reserved 2px identity edge · 20px monogram · name (sans 13, sage rising to ivory on hover, ivory when active; **middle-truncated** with `<MidTruncate tail={14}>` so names that differ only at the end — `Production deploy (octopush-api)` / `(octopush-web)` — keep both their head and their distinguishing tail, full name in the tooltip; the `…` sits flush against the tail in every row, with no stray space or gap (`seatEllipsis`, which measures with the head held at `text-overflow: clip` by its own inline style — never a stylesheet rule keyed on the box, which Safari could leave applied after the pass, #872 — so WKWebView's own ellipsis can't cap the cut, then sizes the head to its kept glyphs plus one `…`, so the `…` is the head's own `text-overflow: ellipsis` — a cut head is never left at `clip`, #864, not even when one row of the shared pass can't be measured: that row keeps the plain CSS ellipsis and the others are still cut, #865); a line or paragraph separator, form feed or vertical tab in a name renders as a space; a search hit keeps a plain truncating line with its wash) · right-aligned unboxed meta. No row ever changes height or shifts with state. _Support:_ `WorkspaceRow`.
- **Identity edge = state only** — brass on the active row; `.rail-bar-running` marching segments while the workspace works (brass on the active row / cell, sage everywhere else); transparent at rest. The workspace tint never colours the edge. _Support:_ `WorkspaceRow`, `CollapsedCell`, `styles.css` (`.rail-bar-running`, sized inline per consumer).
- **Monogram identity** — A bare Spectral glyph (custom or first letter) in the workspace's tint accent. Every surface (expanded rail, collapsed rail, ⌘K's Workspaces rows, the customize popover) resolves it through `resolveMonogram`, which runs the stored glyph through `normalizeGlyph`: the first grapheme, trimmed, in capital form via a locale-independent mapping (`m` → `M`; symbols, digits and emoji unchanged). Empty, whitespace or control input, or a lowercase letter with no single-glyph capital (`ß`, which macOS types for ⌥S, → "SS"), falls back to the name's initial, so a `main` workspace reads "M", never "ß" (#848) — no border, no fill; the one carrier of the tint. `aria-current="location"` on the active one, `aria-label` = the mission name (the name button's accessible name is its visible text, so the glyph stays the single name-labelled control); right-click → workspace menu (or the customize popover when no menu is wired). _Support:_ `src/lib/monogram.ts` (`resolveMonogram`, 7 named `TINTS`).
- **Mission posture in the tooltip** — The monogram's `title` is `"{intent} mission · read-only · sandboxed"` (qualifiers only when they apply; no tooltip when the workspace has no mission). The rail spends no glyph slot on posture; the ContextHeader carries it in full. _Support:_ `WorkspaceRow` (three `useMissionsStore` scalar subscriptions).
- **Active-workspace styling** — brass edge + `--brass-ghost` ground + ivory name. _Support:_ `WorkspaceRow`, `CollapsedCell`.
- **Attention — the single beacon** — Among the workspaces that may signal (flagged, not active, not running), exactly **one** pulses (`.animate-attention-pulse`; reduced motion → a static `--brass-dim` halo): the one waiting longest (oldest `flag.since` — the first ping of the current wait; `at` moves with every ping and would let a chatty terminal steal the beacon). Every other one carries a **static 5px brass dot** (expanded: last atom of the meta; collapsed: the cell's corner). Running suppresses attention in both rail modes — the marching edge owns the row until the run pauses or finishes, then the flag takes over. `aria-label` "{name} — needs attention"; the name tooltip names the kind. **Nearest visible ancestor:** a fold must never swallow the signal, so when the signalling row is hidden the outermost folded container around it carries it instead: the **project line** when the project is folded (its mark pulses), else the **mission-group header** when the group is folded (its chevron pulses; in the slim rail, the group's chevron). A container hiding several signals shows the strongest: the pulse for the beacon, otherwise one static dot (in the folded aggregates; at the chevron's corner in the slim rail). Folds are ignored while a filter holds everything open, and the slim rail has no project fold. A workspace counts as a member only of a group of **its own project** (`ownGroupId`, the test the layout applies), so a header never carries a signal for a row that is drawn loose. Exactly one element pulses in every case; headers that carry a signal add a visually hidden " — needs attention" to their name. _Support:_ `resolveAttention` + `resolveAttentionCarriers` (pure, exported, tested), `nearestVisibleAncestor` (`src/lib/beacon.ts`), `attentionStore`.
- **Per-workspace meta (unboxed)** — right-aligned mono 10px tabular: linked-issue key (sage) · ahead `↑N` · behind `↓N` (mute, lucide arrows) · open PR (`GitPullRequest`, verdigris) · uncommitted changes (`GitCommitHorizontal`, mute; hidden on the active row — the ContextHeader shows it) · collision mark (`GitCompareArrows`, amber/rouge; see Collision radar below) · attention dot. Every atom carries a `title`; the icon-only ones (PR, dirty, the dot) also an `img` role + label. **Demotion rung:** when a long name would lose its tail, the ahead/behind pair collapses (animated `.octo-demote.octo-demote-shed`) and its counts move into the name's tooltip (`… · 3 commits ahead · 1 commit behind`); the ticket key, PR, dirty, collision and attention marks are the floor. Decided per row by `shedsGitMeta()` from the name's length, since the rail's width is fixed. _Support:_ `workspaces_git_summary`, `open_prs_for_project`.
- **⌘N hint** — `App` maps `⌘1…⌘9` (`Ctrl+1…9` off a Mac — the chord binds `metaKey || ctrlKey`, and the hint follows the platform via `modKeyLabel()` in `src/lib/platform.ts`) to the active project's `workspaces` list (the list the key handler indexes) and hands the rail `shortcutByWs`; the name tooltip reads `"{name} (⌘N)"` and the collapsed flyout shows the key — only on rows the shortcut really reaches. _Support:_ `App.tsx` (`shortcutByWs`, memoised with `projectGroups`), `WorkspaceRail.shortcutByWs`.
- **Per-project "New mission"** — Hover/focus-revealed Plus in the header line (`New mission in {project}`). A mission group's header has its own (`New mission in this group`), which also files the new mission in the group. _Support:_ `onNewWorkspaceForProject`, `onNewWorkspaceInGroup`.
- **Reorder projects** — Hover/focus-revealed grip (drag handle) on the header line — see "Reorder projects (drag + menu)" above. _Support:_ `@dnd-kit`.
- **Right-click context menus** — Row / cell → workspace menu; header line or collapsed cluster mark → project menu (coordinates passed through; `⇧F10` / the context-menu key on the project line too, and on a mission row's monogram or name in the expanded rail, which opens the mission's menu at the row and gives the row the focus back when it closes — `holdMissionRowFocus` in `lib/railFocus.ts`, which only fills a lost focus, so a dialog an action opened keeps its own; a selected row of a multi-selection opens the selection's menu instead, see "Multi-select"); mission-group header or its slim-rail chevron, or a project group's header → group menu (owned by the rail). _Support:_ `WorkspaceRail`.
- **Mission groups (folders of one project's missions)** — A group is a named, optionally tinted, foldable folder inside a project. It holds that project's missions; a mission is in at most one group; groups do not nest; a group that loses every mission stays until it is removed. Spec: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-run-mode-and-rail-groups-design.md`](superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-run-mode-and-rail-groups-design.md), Part 1; cheatsheet: design-system §8 "Rail groups". Project groups (sections of projects) are the entry after this one.
  - **Signature (expanded rail):** a 28px header line with a `ChevronDown` that is **always visible**, centred in the monogram column and coloured with the group's tint (mute when it has none; it rotates −90° when folded), then the name in mono 11px, normal case, sage (ivory on hover). The members are the normal mission rows, indented **14px**, beside a **1px guide** in the group's tint at 50% opacity (`--color-octo-border-strong` when untinted) that starts under the chevron and stops 5px above the last member's foot, so the group's end is drawn and the next loose mission returns to the outer alignment. 2px above the group, 6px below. **Monograms are never recoloured:** a mission keeps its own glyph and tint; the group's tint lives on the chevron and the guide only. The two near-neutral tints (bone, smoke: `PALE_TINTS`) reach those marks through `--tint-mark-<name>`, which `themeStore` solves per theme (`solveMarkInk`): the tint itself where it clears 3:1 on the rail's panel (every dark theme), mixed toward the theme's text just far enough to clear it otherwise (on vellum bone sat near 1.4:1). The chevron in the slim rail and in ⌘K uses the same ink. The rows stay full width, so the brass active bar and the marching edge remain at the rail's left edge; the row's git-meta demotion rung accounts for the indent.
  - **Order:** `layoutMissions` interleaves a project's groups with its loose missions. Missions keep the rail's order (`created_at`, oldest first). A group stands where its first member stands; between groups the backend's `sortOrder` is the law, so a group is pulled up to the group that follows it instead of two groups swapping; an empty group goes right before the next group, or last. A mission whose `groupId` names no loaded group is a plain loose row.
  - **Folded aggregates:** only while folded (a count visible in the list is never repeated in a header): the member count, a verdigris `GitPullRequest` when a member has an open PR, and the static attention dot (or the pulse on the chevron, see "Attention"). An empty group reads `empty` in mute, folded or not, and draws no guide. No marching edge on a folded header: running is a row's state. **Folded over the active mission**, the group's name reads in ivory instead of sage, the cue a project's line gives for the project that holds the active workspace; open, the name stays sage, because the active row itself is in sight.
