  - **Fold:** click the header (one tab stop, `aria-expanded`); `←` folds and `→` unfolds when it has the focus; grid-rows 0fr↔1fr, 280ms. Persisted to localStorage under `railGroupCollapsed` (ids of folded groups; an open group has no entry), like project folds; the database stores none. A live filter unfolds everything and leaves the stored state alone (the header stops toggling meanwhile).
  - **Create:** mission menu **Move to group › New group…** makes a group with that mission already in it; project menu **New mission group** makes an empty one. The backend places it (`create_group`); its header opens with the name `New group` in inline edit, selected (a folded project unfolds for it). In the slim rail the group is created but its name stays `New group`: there is no room for the input.
  - **Rename in place:** double-click the header, `F2`, or the header menu's **Rename** → an input in the header (`aria-label` "Group name"). Enter and blur commit (trimmed; a blank name changes nothing), Escape keeps the name; the header gets the focus back. **Escape on a just-created group cancels it:** while the first name of a group made from a mission (**New group…**) or a selection (**Group N missions…**) is still in edit, Escape deletes the group and puts each mission back in the group it came from, or loose (missions keep their order, so each lands where it was; `cancelNewGroup`). Once that first name is committed (Enter, blur, or the edit ends any other way), Escape is a rename's Escape again. An empty group from the project menu has nothing to put back and keeps today's Escape.
  - **Header menu** (`GroupContextMenu`, right-click, `⇧F10` or the context-menu key): **Rename** (`F2`) · **New mission in this group** (the keyboard path to the header's `+`) · **Tint**: the seven monogram `TINTS` plus **No tint**, as `menuitemradio` swatches with their names as `aria-label` and `title`; picking one applies at once and keeps the menu open; the swatch row is one stop of the `↑`/`↓` walk, entered on the current tint; `←`/`→` move along it and the stop follows the focus, so `↓` from any swatch goes on to the next row · **Ungroup** ("Keeps the missions") when it has missions, **Remove group** when empty. Ungroup shows a toast with **Undo**, which makes a group of the same name and tint around the missions that are still loose (a new group: it opens unfolded, and archived missions of the old group do not return to it; Undo does nothing once the project has been closed or deleted, so it never leaves an empty group nobody can see).
  - **Move to group… from the keyboard (`⌘⌥G`):** on a focused mission row (its monogram or name) or project line, `⌘⌥G` on a Mac (only ⌘: Ctrl+Option is VoiceOver's), `Ctrl+Alt+G` elsewhere (the physical `G`, since Option rewrites the letter) opens a menu at the row with the same choices as the context menu's **Move to group ›** submenu (`MoveToGroupMenu`, sharing `MoveToGroupChoices` with `MoveToGroupItem`): header `Move to group` (`Move N missions to group` for a selection; the moved row's name is its tooltip), the scope's groups (the current one checked and focused first), **New group…**, **Remove from group**. Type-ahead: typing a group's first letters moves to it (a repeated letter walks the rows that start with it). On a selected row of a multi-selection it acts on the whole selection (`Move N missions to group`). When it closes, the row or line gets the focus back. **Rail-scoped:** the chord is handled by the rail's own `keydown` (`isMoveToGroupChord`), so it fires only with the focus on a rail row or project line, never in the rail's search or rename inputs, and never for a key pressed in an editor, the scratchpad or a terminal: there `⌘⌥G` stays CodeMirror's go to line, whose keymap only hears keys pressed in the editor. Not in `GLOBAL_SHORTCUTS`. A group header does not answer it (its menu has the group's own actions).
  - **Move:** mission menu **Move to group ›** opens a submenu beside the row (`MoveToGroupItem`): the project's groups (`menuitemradio`, the current one checked, the others with a dot in their tint), **New group…**, and **Remove from group** for a mission that is in one. It opens on hover (160ms leave grace), click, Enter or `→`; `←` returns to the row; it flips to the left or lifts when the window's edge is near. Moving a mission into a folded group unfolds it. **Drag:** with at least one group in the project and no filter typed, mission rows drag (pointer only; the row is no extra tab stop): dropped on a group (its header or its run) the mission joins it, dropped on the project's loose area it leaves its group; a group header dragged onto a sibling takes its place (`set_group_order` always gets the complete run of siblings). Nothing crosses a project. A ghost (monogram + name, or chevron + name) follows the pointer outside the list's clipping; a header that would accept the drop takes a `--brass-ghost` wash. One `DndContext` serves the four drags (`src/lib/railDnd.ts`): `railCollisions` lets a project meet only projects and project-group headers, a project group only the top-level blocks, and a mission or mission-group header only the targets of its own project; `projectKeyboardCoordinates` gives a project's keyboard reorder (grip, Space, `↑`/`↓`) the projects alone to step between, never a group's drop target, and a step lands on the project whose top or bottom edge it lined the block up with (`closestAlignedEdge`), so a tall project steps past a much shorter one (by centre it stayed over itself). The ghost's `<DragOverlay>` is mounted only while a mission or a mission-group header is dragged: mounted during a project drag (or a project group's) it would make the sortable list treat that drag as overlay-driven, and the project would stop following the pointer (`WorkspaceRail.sections.test.tsx` fails if it is mounted then).
  - **New mission in a group:** a `+` on the header on hover and focus ("New mission in this group"; `tabIndex=-1`, the menu item is the keyboard path) opens the mission creator for that project; the created mission joins the group (`MissionCreator.groupId`; a workspace the backend adopted that already sits in another group is left there).
  - **Slim rail (44px):** the header is a 12px chevron in the group's tint; its tooltip and accessible name are the group's name, it folds the group (`aria-expanded`), and right-click, `⇧F10` or the context-menu key opens the group menu (from the keyboard, beside the chevron, with the focus back on the chevron when it closes; Rename does nothing at this width). The 1px guide stays beside the members' monograms, with 6px of air above and below the group.
  - **Archive:** an archived mission keeps its group (`group_id` stays on its row) and returns to it on restore **if the group still exists**; removing a group clears its members' `group_id`, archived ones included, so a mission whose group is gone comes back loose (a stale id would be drawn loose as well, `layoutMissions`). The Archived workspaces modal shows the group's name before the branch, titled `In the group "<name>": restoring returns it there`, and nothing for a loose mission or a group of another project.
  - **Multi-select:** in the expanded rail, `⌘`-click on a Mac (Ctrl-click elsewhere; on a Mac a Ctrl-click is a right-click and selects nothing) on a mission row's monogram or name toggles it into a selection without opening it, and `⇧`-click selects the run of drawn rows from the anchor (the last row toggled, else the active mission) to it, through groups' members (a folded group's members are out of sight and skipped). A selection lives in one project: selecting in another starts a new one. Selected rows take a static 2px sage bar in the reserved identity edge (unless active, which keeps brass, or working, which keeps the marching edge), the hover ground (`bg-octo-panel-2`) and an ivory name, with `— selected` in the monogram's and the name's accessible names; a hovered row changes only its ground and name, so the edge tells the two apart. The selection holds only rows the rail draws (`railSelectionStore.retain`): a selected mission archived, deleted or reloaded away, or folded out of sight (its group, project or project group folded), leaves it, so the menu's count and its actions match the screen; the selection menu opens only for two or more drawn rows and closes if its selection falls under two. A plain click still opens the mission and clears the selection; Escape in the rail (or with the focus nowhere) clears it, while an Escape a menu, a dialog, an editor or a terminal listens for is left to them; typing a filter or folding the rail to 44px clears it too. Drag is unchanged: a row drags alone, selected or not. Right-click (or `⇧F10`) on a selected row of two or more opens the **selection menu** (`RailSelectionMenu`, `aria-label` "Selected missions"): header `N missions selected`, **Group N missions…** (`FolderPlus`; one `create_group` call with every selected mission as `memberIds`, then the new header opens with `New group` in inline edit), **Move N missions to group ›** (the `MoveToGroupItem` submenu: the project's groups, the common group checked, **New group…** = Group N missions, **Remove from group** when any is grouped; `moveMissionsToGroup` moves the ones not already there in one `set_items_group` call, one transaction: a refusal leaves every one where it was and shows one toast, `Couldn't move the N missions`), **Clear selection**. Right-clicking a row outside the selection clears it and opens that mission's own menu. Missions only: projects have no multi-select (a project already moves with **Move to group ›**, `⌘⌥G` and drag). Pointer-only; the keyboard moves one mission at a time with `⌘⌥G`. _Support:_ `src/stores/railSelectionStore.ts` (`toggle`, `extend`, `selectionRange`), `RailSelectionMenu.tsx`, `WorkspaceRail.tsx` (`pickRow`, `openRowMenu`).
  - _Support:_ `src/components/RailMissionGroup.tsx` (header, run, guide, inline rename), `GroupContextMenu.tsx`, `MoveToGroupItem.tsx` (`MoveToGroupItem`, `MoveToGroupChoices`), `MoveToGroupMenu.tsx`, `WorkspaceRail.tsx` (`SortableProjectGroup`, `CollapsedRail`, `RailDragGhost`, `isMoveToGroupChord`), `src/lib/railGroups.ts` (`layoutMissions`, `filterRailItems`, `ownGroupId`, `resolveRailDrop`: pure, tested), `src/lib/railDnd.ts` (`railCollisions`, `projectKeyboardCoordinates`: tested), `src/lib/groupActions.ts` (`createMissionGroup`, `moveMissionToGroup`, `cancelNewGroup`, `ungroupMissions`), `src/stores/railGroupUiStore.ts` (folds + the group in rename), `src/stores/groupsStore.ts`; `useMenuChrome` uses one selector for the first focus and the `↑`/`↓` walk, `[role^="menuitem"]:not([disabled]):not([tabindex="-1"])`: every kind of menu row (plain, radio, checkbox), minus rows taken out of the tab order (so a swatch row is one stop). It walks the menu that holds the focus, so a submenu is walked on its own; when the focus sits in the menu on something outside the walk, `↑`/`↓` go on from where it stands. A group menu opened from the keyboard returns the focus to its header when it closes. `data-tour`: `rail-group-header`, `rail-group-members`. _Entry:_ mission menu, project menu, group header.
- **Project groups (sections of projects)** — A project group is a named, optionally tinted, foldable section of the rail's top level. It holds projects; a project is in at most one group; groups do not nest; a group that loses every project stays until it is removed. Same concept and store as mission groups (the UI word for both is "group"), drawn differently on purpose. Spec: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-run-mode-and-rail-groups-design.md`](superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-run-mode-and-rail-groups-design.md), Part 1; cheatsheet: design-system §8 "Rail groups".
  - **Signature (expanded rail):** a **hairline** across the rail, then a 26px **caps eyebrow** (mono 9px, tracking 0.25em, mute; sage on hover): the idiom of the rail's "Recently closed" footer. Its projects are the normal project lines, **not indented**, and it draws no guide, so it never looks like a mission group (always-visible chevron, mono label, indented run beside a guide). A group that opens the rail has no hairline above it. Where a group **ends** is drawn by what follows: the next group's hairline, or the closing hairline a loose project takes when it comes right after a group. A fold chevron stands at the right of the eyebrow in the group's tint (mute when untinted); it shows on hover, on focus and while folded, carries a `title` ("Collapse {group}" / "Expand {group}") and folds on click; it is pointer decoration (`aria-hidden`): the eyebrow button is the one tab stop.
  - **Tint:** the group's tint colours its chevron, and the **hexagon** of each of its projects that has no tint of its own (`projectMarkColor`: own tint, else the group's, else mute). A mission's monogram is never recoloured. Palette: the seven monogram `TINTS` plus none.
  - **Order, and pinned projects:** `layoutProjects` never changes the rail's project order (pinned first, then the manual order). A group stands where its **first project** stands and gathers its other projects under it in that same order; loose projects keep their place around it. So **a pinned project stays in its group**: it leads the group, and the group comes up into the pinned run with it; pinning never takes a project out of its group and never moves another group. Unlike mission groups, the groups' own `sortOrder` is not a law between them (projects have a manual order, so a group's place follows its projects); it only orders the **empty** groups, which stand last. A project whose `groupId` names no loaded project group is a plain loose project.
  - **Folded aggregates:** only while folded: `N projects`, and the static attention dot (or the pulse on the chevron, see "Attention"). An empty group reads `empty` in mute, folded or not. Folded over the active mission, the eyebrow reads in ivory (the cue a project's line gives); open, it stays mute.
  - **Fold:** click the eyebrow (`aria-expanded`) or its chevron; `←` folds and `→` unfolds when it has the focus; grid-rows 0fr↔1fr, 280ms. Persisted with the mission groups' folds (`railGroupCollapsed`). A live filter unfolds everything and leaves the stored state alone. Activating a mission inside a folded group unfolds it (the launch restore excepted, as for mission groups).
  - **Create:** project menu **Move to group › New group…** makes a group around that project; it stands where the project stands, and its eyebrow opens with the name `New group` in inline edit, selected. In the slim rail the group is created but its name stays `New group`.
  - **Rename in place:** double-click the eyebrow, `F2`, or the header menu's **Rename** → an input in the eyebrow's own type (`aria-label` "Group name"); Enter and blur commit, Escape keeps the name; the header gets the focus back. **Escape on a just-created group cancels it:** while the first name of a group made from a project is in edit, Escape deletes the group and the project returns to the group it came from, or loose, at its place (the project order never changed; `cancelNewGroup`). A later rename's Escape only keeps the name.
  - **Header menu** (`GroupContextMenu` with `holds="projects"`; right-click, `⇧F10` or the context-menu key): **Rename** (`F2`) · **Tint** swatches · **Move up** / **Move down** (the keyboard's way to move a group: it steps over one top-level block, a loose project or a whole group; each is offered only when the step would show, so not at the rail's ends and not where the pinned-first listing would undo it: a group raised by a pinned project has no step down past an unpinned block. An **empty** group has no project to drag or to stand by: it steps among the empty groups at the rail's foot, trading places with its neighbour there through the groups' own order (`stepEmptySection`, `set_group_order`), and never above a group with projects) · **Ungroup** ("Keeps the projects"; a toast offers **Undo**, which makes a group of the same name and tint around the projects that are still open and still loose) or **Remove group** on an empty one. A menu opened from the keyboard gives the focus back to its header.
  - **Move:** project menu **Move to group ›** (`MoveToGroupItem`, the same submenu the mission menu uses), or `⌘⌥G` on the focused project line (the same choices as a menu of their own; see "Move to group… from the keyboard" under "Mission groups"). **Drag** (no filter typed; a project by its grip, pointer or keyboard). A project's block can be hundreds of pixels tall and is held by a grip at its top, so the **pointer** says which container it is over and only then does the block's centre pick a place (`railCollisions`): (1) over **another group, anywhere on it** (its eyebrow or its projects; a folded group is its eyebrow alone, and its hidden projects are no targets), the project **joins that group as its last project**, always: one landing place, open or folded, and that group's eyebrow shows a `--brass-ghost` wash while the drop would join; (2) over **its own group**, it is reordered among that group's projects, except on that group's own eyebrow, where a drop does nothing; (3) anywhere else it is on the ungrouped top level: it takes the place of the nearest top-level block (a loose project, or beside another group as a whole), and a group's project **leaves its group** for it; on the **ungrouped area** under the rail's last block it goes last (that area is a target only while a project group exists and only under the pointer, `TOP_LOOSE_ID`). The keyboard has no pointer: its steps go from project to project, and a step onto a project of another group stands for that group's header (its eyebrow washed, the group not opened around the block), so the drop joins it, last too. A group dragged by its header moves **as one unit** with its projects (pointer only) and takes the place of the top-level block it is dropped on. **The drop cue:** while a project drag would change membership, the dragged block's own top line says so, right-aligned in the eyebrow type (mono 9px caps, tracking 0.25em): `Into {group}` in brass when the drop would join a group, `Out of {group}` in mute when it would take the project out of its group; nothing when the drop only reorders (same group, or loose to loose) or for a group dragged as a whole. It is drawn over the line's end on the block's ground (absolute, so the block keeps its size), a long name ends in an ellipsis, and it crossfades (`octo-fade-in`) when the target changes. The cue, the target eyebrow's wash and the drop come from one call (`resolveTopDropWithCue`, made in render for the cue and wash, from the target `onDragOver` last reported and the rail as it is now, and on `onDragEnd` for the drop), so the label never disagrees with the result, a reload in mid-drag included. The eyebrow wash stays, for when the block does not cover the eyebrow. dnd-kit's announcements are not configured for the rail (its default screen-reader text is used), so the cue is not announced. The dragged block is an **opaque, lifted surface** at full opacity (`DRAGGED_BLOCK`: the menus' ground and lift, `LIFTED_GROUND` = `bg-octo-panel` + their shadow, a hairline ring, `z-10`), so it occludes the blocks and eyebrows it passes in every theme; a group holding its own dragged project is raised too, since its filled entrance animation makes it a stacking context. It is **moved, never scaled** (`blockShift`: dnd-kit's transform scales a dragged item to the size of what it is over; only its translation is written), and it stays under the pointer over every target: its own list moves it while it is over that list, and `useFollowPointer` moves it by the drag's delta elsewhere. While one of a group's own projects is dragged, that group stops clipping its fold, so the block stays in sight outside the group; the list's scroll is held to the room its own content gave it when the drag began, because a block dragged by a transform past the list's foot would otherwise lengthen the list and auto-scroll would run after it. `resolveTopDrop` decides every drop and returns the full project order to persist, so a group's projects stay one run in `sort_order`; an order the pinned-first listing would undo is not written. **A move and its order land together** (`groupsStore.moveProject`, used by the drag, the menus and `⌘⌥G`): the project's group and the new project order go into the store in one update, so the rail never draws the group jumping in between, and only then are `set_item_group` and `set_project_order` written. If either is refused, both come back as they were (a membership the backend already took is taken back too) and one toast says `Couldn't move {project}` / `Your rail is back as it was.`. A reload that read the old order while a new one was being written lays the new one over it (`beginProjectOrderChange` in `projectStore`, beside the membership guard). A plain reorder (`projectStore.setOrder`) shows at once too, and a refused one is undone with `Couldn't reorder the projects`. Sortable lists: one for the top-level blocks (loose projects and groups), one inside each group.
  - **Attention:** a folded group is the outermost fold, so it carries the beacon or the dot for every mission under it, before the project line or a mission group would (`resolveAttentionCarriers`, `bySection`).
  - **Slim rail (44px):** a group is a **sub-cluster**: its projects' clusters stand together between two hairlines that span the rail's width (the 20px hairline still parts one project from the next, inside a group and outside). There is no room for the name, so each of its projects' marks is titled `group · project` and the flyout's eyebrow starts with the group. Hexagons take the group's tint as in the expanded rail. A group does not fold at this width (a project doesn't either), and an empty group draws nothing; its menu is reached from the expanded rail.
  - _Support:_ `src/components/RailProjectSection.tsx` (hairline, eyebrow, fold, the header as drop target and drag handle), `RailMissionGroup.tsx` (shared: `GroupNameInput`, `groupHeaderKeyDown`, `groupMarkColor`), `GroupContextMenu.tsx`, `ProjectContextMenu.tsx`, `MoveToGroupItem.tsx`, `WorkspaceRail.tsx` (`projectMarkColor`, the top-level layout, `CollapsedRail`), `src/lib/railGroups.ts` (`projectGroupsOf`, `layoutProjects`, `resolveTopDrop`, `resolveTopDropWithCue`, `stepInRail`, `stepEmptySection`, `flattenTop`, `sectionByProject`: pure, tested), `src/lib/railDnd.ts` (`RailTopData`, `railCollisions`, `blockShift`, `useFollowPointer`, `DRAGGED_BLOCK`: tested), `src/lib/menuStyles.ts` (`LIFTED_GROUND`), `src/lib/railFocus.ts` (`holdProjectLineFocus`), `src/lib/groupActions.ts` (`createProjectGroup`, `moveProjectToGroup`, `cancelNewGroup`, `ungroupProjects`), `src/stores/railGroupUiStore.ts`, `src/stores/groupsStore.ts` (`moveProject`), `src/stores/projectStore.ts` (`setOrder`, `arrangeProjects`, `beginProjectOrderChange`). In the code a project group is a "section", because `ProjectGroup` already names a project with its missions. _Entry:_ project menu, the group's header.
- **Recently-closed drawer** — Collapsed-by-default footer "⟲ Recently closed · N" (hidden when none), per-row mute `ProjectMark` (never brass — a closed project is not the active thing) + name + "Restore"; backend caps at 10 newest. _Support:_ `RecentlyClosedDrawer.tsx`, `list_closed_projects`. _Entry:_ rail footer (expanded rail only).
- **Empty state** — "No missions yet" (sans 12, mute, aligned with the names) under an open project with no rows. _Support:_ `WorkspaceRail`.
- **Collision radar (#732)** — Warns when two live (non-archived) workspaces of one project change the same files, before the merge does; it never blocks anything. **Engine:** `project_collisions(projectId)` lists each live workspace whose worktree exists and collects the paths it changes: the committed tree diff from `merge_base(base, HEAD)` to `HEAD` (`git diff --name-only <merge-base>`; base = the workspace's `from_branch`, else the repo's default branch; the newer of the merge bases against `origin/<base>` and `<base>`, so the base moving on never counts) plus HEAD → index + working tree, untracked included (crews leave work uncommitted). Renames count both paths; a delete counts its path. Pairwise, the overlap is the intersection, plus every path on one side under a collapsed `dir/` entry on the other (the more specific path is reported); when both sides changed an overlapping file in **committed** work, an in-memory `merge_trees(merge_base(a, b), a, b)` confirms the conflict (`conflict` severity, with the conflicting files); otherwise `overlap`. Lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Cargo.lock`, `go.sum`, …) are regenerated on merge, so a lockfile conflict is dropped from the conflicting files (and from the "N files" count) before severity is chosen: a pair whose only conflicts are lockfiles, or whose overlap is only lockfiles, is `lockfile` and raises no indicator; a lockfile conflict plus a clean real overlap is `overlap`. Uncommitted-only overlaps count but are never merge-confirmed. **Read-only by construction:** the scan never writes objects, refs, the index or locks (libgit2 may refresh an existing object's timestamp): diffs only read, and the merge runs on an in-memory index with a mempack object backend in front of the ODB, so auto-merged blobs stay in memory (a test hashes the bytes and mtime of every index, plus refs, object count and status, before and after a scan). **Cost bounds:** a project with fewer than two live workspaces is skipped; the committed set is cached per worktree by `(HEAD, merge base)`; merge confirmations by `(head a, head b)`; a project's report is reused for 5 s (`REPORT_TTL`, keyed by the workspace list and every workspace's HEAD, so a commit or a changed list invalidates it at once; a `force` call skips it); past 32 confirmed pairs a scan degrades to file overlap only (`capped`). **Payload bounds:** the uncommitted set comes from a non-recursive pass first (untracked directories as `dir/`, like `git status`); each untracked directory's non-ignored files are counted up to 21 and only one with 20 or fewer is listed file by file, so one with more counts as one `dir/` entry and is never walked whole; a worktree's uncommitted set stops at 2,000 paths (the report says so in `uncommittedCapped`), and each pair sends at most 50 `files` (and 50 `conflictingFiles`) with the rest counted in `truncated` / `conflictingTruncated`; every count and tooltip includes them (*"… +N more"*). The frontend `collisionStore` throttles each project to one scan per 10 s (forced after a commit, which also bypasses the backend TTL), dedupes in-flight scans (a force that arrives mid-scan queues one forced follow-up), and polls the open projects that have two or more workspaces on a worktree every 60 s while the window is visible, plus on window focus, on opening Mission Control and on mounting the Review verdict line. Archiving or deleting a workspace (`workspaceStore.archive` / `remove`) calls `collisionStore.forgetWorkspace`, which drops its entries and every peer's collision with it at once and forces one rescan of its project, so a mark never outlives its only peer (the poll skips a project left with one workspace). **Surfaces** (each only when there is something to say): the rail's per-row `GitCompareArrows` mark (amber `--color-octo-warning` for an overlap, rouge when confirmed; never brass, never the beacon; tooltip one line per other workspace, e.g. *"Overlaps refund-webhooks · 2 files: src/billing/limits.ts, src/billing/plan.ts"* / *"Will conflict with auth-flow in 1 file: …"*; `data-tour="rail-collision"`; it joins the row's demotion floor) and the collapsed flyout's status line; Mission Control's crew-card segment; the Review Companion's verdict line (see §1). **The crew is told too (phase 2):** when a code-writing Direct stage starts (its role's artifact is the worktree diff and it runs in the worktree — `implement`, `fix`), the orchestrator runs one fresh read-only scan of the project's live workspaces and, if the stage's workspace overlaps another, its dossier carries one line per peer: *"Note: workspace `refund-webhooks` is concurrently changing src/billing/limits.ts. Avoid unrelated edits there."* (see §4, Stage input dossier). Free. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/collisions.rs` (`CollisionCache`, `scan`, `scan_throttled`, `is_lockfile`, `scan_inputs`, `concurrent_work_note`), `commands::project_collisions`, `Orchestrator::concurrent_work_note`, `AppState.collisions`; `src/stores/collisionStore.ts`, `src/lib/collisions.ts` (per-workspace derivation + copy), `src/components/CollisionMark.tsx`; polling started in `App.tsx`. _Entry:_ automatic.

### Notable implementation details
- **Worktree mechanics** — `create_worktree` returns the path it actually used and is collision-proof: the libgit2 worktree **slot name and the working-tree path are decoupled from the branch**. It refuses up front if the branch is already checked out elsewhere (git's one-checkout-per-branch rule → friendly error). Otherwise it picks a **free slot name** (reclaiming a genuinely stale `.git/worktrees/<branch>` slot in place — pruned with `valid+locked+working_tree`, then force-removed — but stepping aside to `<branch>-2`, `-3`… when that slot still backs another live worktree, e.g. one whose branch was switched: the old "directory exists" bug) and a **free path** (clearing stale leftovers, suffixing past a live worktree). It never deletes a live worktree or the project root. Creation is serialized process-wide so concurrent creates can't race. `delete_worktree` prunes the slot **by path** (slot names aren't tied to the branch anymore) and never deletes the branch.
- **DB schema — projects:** `id, name, path (UNIQUE), created_at, last_opened`, + `jira_project_key, closed_at, pinned, sort_order, tint, setup_script, group_id, issue_tracker, epiku_project`. **workspaces:** `id, project_id (FK CASCADE), name, task, branch, worktree_path, setup_script, status, created_at, last_active`, + `glyph, tint, test_command, linked_issue_key, issue_link_dismissed, from_branch, group_id, after_workspace_id, after_condition, branch_from_prerequisite, auto_start`.
- **Starts after (data layer, #960 slice 1)** — A mission (workspace) can wait on another mission of the same project. The link lives on the waiting row: nullable `after_workspace_id` (the prerequisite; no FK) and `after_condition` (`run_finished` | `pr_merged`, `db::PREREQUISITE_CONDITIONS`), plus `branch_from_prerequisite` (branch from the prerequisite's branch instead of the base) and `auto_start` (start on its own once the condition holds), both `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. **Rules:** `set_workspace_prerequisite` replaces any earlier link and refuses an unknown condition, a missing or archived prerequisite, a prerequisite of another project, and any link that would close a cycle (a mission waiting on itself included; checked by walking the chain up from the prerequisite in an IMMEDIATE transaction) — each with an English message, leaving the links as they were; `clear_workspace_prerequisite` resets all four columns. Several missions may wait on one. Deleting or archiving a mission clears every link that points at it (`delete_workspace` / `archive_workspace`); restoring it does not bring them back; the archived mission's own link is kept. `list_workspace_prerequisites` lists a project's links, leaving archived missions out (oldest mission first); the app reads them for the waiting state and the staged start (next entry). _Support:_ `db.rs` (`PrerequisiteRow`, `get_workspace_prerequisite`/`set_workspace_prerequisite`/`clear_workspace_prerequisite`/`list_workspace_prerequisites`, `CLEAR_LINKS_TO_WORKSPACE_SQL`), commands `set_workspace_prerequisite` (returns the `PrerequisiteRow`; `autoStart` optional, default false), `clear_workspace_prerequisite` and `list_workspace_prerequisites`; Rust tests `prerequisite_tests`.
- **Starts after: waiting state and staged start (#960 slice 2)** — The mission menu (rail; not on the project's main workspace) has **Start after…** (`Hourglass`; `data-tour="rail-menu-start-after"`). It opens a dialog (`data-tour="starts-after-dialog"`): **Mission**, the other missions of the project to wait on (a `Listbox`); **When**, a `SegmentedControl` of "Run passes last gate" (`run_finished`) or "Pull request merges" (`pr_merged`); and **Start the run on its own** (auto-start, off by default; `data-tour="starts-after-auto-start"`). **Wait for it** saves the link (a refusal, such as a cycle, is toasted in the backend's words). On a mission that already waits, the dialog opens on its link and offers **Stop waiting** (a refused clear is toasted and the dialog stays open). With no other mission it says so. Branching from the prerequisite is not offered yet (`branchFromPrerequisite` stays false). **Waiting state:** the row meta shows a mute `Hourglass` (`data-tour="rail-prerequisite"`) whose title is the wait ("Starts after auth-flow's run passes its last gate" / "Starts after auth-flow's pull request merges"), and the mission's Mission Control card, when it has one, shows the same as one mute line above its micro-track (`data-tour="mission-control-card-prerequisite"`). **`run_finished`** holds once the prerequisite's newest run (drafts skipped) completed, or every gated stage of a run still running or paused is done. A halted (a stage failed), aborted or failed run keeps the mission waiting, and the line adds "That run halted, so this mission keeps waiting" ("was aborted", "failed"). **`pr_merged`** holds once the prerequisite's branch PR reads merged (`find_pr_for_branch` on the prerequisite's own worktree; a prerequisite with no worktree is unreadable, so the mission keeps waiting). **When it checks:** at load (launch, project set, window focus) and on the app's 60 s open-PR poll (which also fires on a workspace switch). GitHub is asked at most once per 50 s per link. A PR merged while the app was closed is found at the next launch. **Staged start:** once a link holds it is cleared (so it is offered once), the waiting mission's launcher is seeded with its brief (the mission's task) and the crew of the prerequisite's newest run, its Direct canvas is set on the launcher, and an info toast ("billing is ready to start") says why and offers **Open it** (the mission's Direct mode). The toast names only what was seeded: brief and crew ("wait in Direct for Begin the run"), the brief alone ("choose a crew", common for `pr_merged` when the prerequisite has no run), the crew alone ("write a brief"), or nothing (no seed; "write a brief and choose a crew"). Nothing begins until **Begin the run**. With auto-start, and a brief and crew to start with, the run begins on its own (success toast "billing started", **Open it**); otherwise it is staged and the toast first says why it didn't start ("It has no crew to start on its own." / "It didn't start on its own." for a refused start, such as the upgrade sheet). **One seed at a time:** the launcher prefill is one slot, so while it holds another mission's unopened seed, a met link with something to seed keeps its link and is staged on a later check, once that seed was taken. Meanwhile its hourglass and Mission Control line say so ("auth-flow's run passed its last gate. Ready to start once you open billing in Direct"); a seed for a mission that no longer exists doesn't hold the slot. A refused auto-start while the slot is taken isn't seeded (its toast says to open it in Direct to begin the run). _Support:_ `src/lib/prerequisite.ts` (`runVerdict`, `prVerdict`, `waitingLine`, `queuedLine`, `metReason`, `stagedText`, `notStartedText`), `stores/prerequisitesStore.ts` (`load`/`save`/`clear`/`check`, `queuedByWs`, `setPrerequisiteOpener`), `StartsAfterDialog.tsx`, `PrerequisiteMark.tsx` (`PrerequisiteMark`, `PrerequisiteCardLine`), `WorkspaceContextMenu` (`onStartAfter`), `App`; the launcher seed goes through `runsStore.setLauncherPrefill`.
- **Rail groups (data layer)** — A group is a named, optionally tinted, one-level container. One concept at two scopes: a `project` group holds projects at the rail's top level, and a `workspace` group holds one project's workspaces (missions) and belongs to that project. The rail shows and edits both: `workspace` groups (see "Mission groups" under the Workspace Rail) and `project` groups (see "Project groups" there). **Rules:** an item is in at most one group (membership is the nullable `group_id` on its own `projects` / `workspaces` row, returned with the rows the rail already loads: `ProjectInfo.groupId`, `Workspace.groupId`); no nesting; a workspace only joins a group of its own project, and a group only holds items of its own scope (refused with an English message otherwise); a group that loses every member stays, and goes only on `delete_group`, which keeps its members and clears their `group_id` in the same transaction (archived workspaces and closed projects included); archiving a workspace keeps its `group_id`, so restoring it returns it to its group if the group still exists; deleting a project deletes its workspace groups (FK cascade). The tint is one of the 7 monogram tints or none, checked on the backend against `db::GROUP_TINTS` (a Rust test keeps that list equal to `monogram.ts` `TINT_NAMES`); no new hue. The name is trimmed and never empty. **Order:** `sort_order` orders the groups of one scope (and, for workspace groups, one project); `create_group` places a new group where its first member sits in rail order (before the first sibling whose own first member comes later; rail order is `list_projects`' for projects and `created_at` for workspaces) and last when it has no members; `set_group_order` rewrites it like `set_project_order`. Whether a group is folded is not stored in the DB (the rail keeps folds in localStorage under `railGroupCollapsed`, like project folds). _Support:_ `db.rs` (`groups` table, `GroupRow`, `list_groups`/`get_group`/`create_group`/`rename_group`/`set_group_tint`/`set_group_order`/`delete_group`/`set_item_group`/`set_items_group`), commands `list_groups`, `create_group`, `rename_group`, `set_group_tint`, `set_group_order`, `delete_group`, `set_item_group`, `set_items_group` (several items of one kind in one transaction: each is checked like `set_item_group` checks one, and one refusal moves none); frontend `lib/types.ts` (`Group`, `GroupScope`), `lib/ipc.ts` (`listGroups`, `createGroup`, `renameGroup`, `setGroupTint`, `setGroupOrder`, `deleteGroup`, `setItemGroup`, `setItemsGroup`), `stores/groupsStore.ts` (`load`, `create`, `rename`, `setTint`, `setOrder`, `remove`, `moveItem`, `moveItems` (one call, rolled back together, one toast; a single item goes through `moveItem`); `pruneProject`; every change but `create` is optimistic and rolls back with an error toast when the backend refuses, and the membership changes patch `projectStore` / `workspaceStore`). **Loading:** `App` calls `load()` at startup and wherever the projects and workspaces are reread (the rail's load effect, window focus, an archived-workspace restore); concurrent calls share one read. **A reload never undoes a change it could not have seen:** `load` waits for group changes in flight and throws away a read that a change started or settled during, then reads again (up to 4 reads); membership changes go through `src/lib/membershipGuard.ts`, which every reload of the rows passes through (`workspaceStore.load` / `loadAllWorkspaces`, `projectStore.loadRecent` / `loadClosed` and the reloads after close, reopen, pin and reorder): a reload that began before a move, a create or an ungroup settled gets that change laid over its rows, and one that began after is trusted (a logical clock, no wall time). The overlay is applied in the step that **commits** the rows to the store (`beginMembershipLoad` → `overlay` → `end`), not when they are read: a batch reload commits after its slowest read, so a move that starts between two reads is kept, and one the backend refuses in between is not brought back. After a successful `load` the stored folds are pruned to the groups that still exist (`railGroupUiStore.prune`). `setOrder` completes the list it is given with the missing siblings, sends nothing for an unchanged order, and rolls back only while every group still sits where that call put it, so a failed reorder never undoes a newer one. Closing or deleting a project prunes its workspace groups from the store (`pruneProject`). The `octopush-mcp` workspace tools return the same workspace rows, so their JSON now carries `groupId`; MCP has no group tools.
- **Customization dual-persistence** — Workspace glyph/tint → DB only. Project name/tint → both localStorage (`projectCustomizations`) and DB, with a one-time migration into the backend.
- **Tint palette** (`monogram.ts`) — 7 named tints (brass, verdigris, rouge, indigo, lavender, smoke, bone), each `{accent, bg}`.
- **URL parsing parity** — `git_url.rs` (Rust) and `parseGitUrl.ts` (TS) handle HTTPS/SCP/ssh/multi-level GitLab/self-hosted hosts identically; the TS mirror keeps clone-name auto-detect instant.

---

## 3. TALK Mode (AI Chat)

### Conversation threads (multi-thread per workspace)
- **Multi-conversation per workspace** — Each workspace holds many persisted chat threads; the active thread's messages load, others stay server-side. Every new thread is **stamped with its mission at birth** (`create_chat_thread` resolves `active_mission_for_workspace` and writes `chat_threads.mission_id`, mirroring `create_run`) — the column was previously written only by the one-shot backfill, so threads created afterward silently lost their mission; live-path attribution keeps mission-scoped rollups honest as work continues. _Support:_ `chatStore.ts`; DB `chat_threads`/`chat_messages`; `list_chat_threads`/`create_chat_thread` (stamps `mission_id`)/`rename_chat_thread`/`delete_chat_thread`. _Entry:_ Companion "Chats" panel (Talk mode).
- **New / select / delete conversation** — New creates an empty "New conversation" thread; select reloads messages and shows the thread as running when its turn still runs in the background; delete removes thread + messages and tears down the thread's TALK shell PTY, falling back to next/new thread. _Support:_ `newThread`/`selectThread`/`deleteThread` (chatStore) → `delete_chat_thread` → `talk_shell.close()` + cascade. _Entry:_ CompanionHistory rows.
- **Conversation switcher (⌘⌥K in Talk, #1153)** — Run's session switcher in Talk's terms, on the same frame (`run/SwitcherFrame.tsx`: top-anchored `ModalShell`, query line, list, key-hint foot): the workspace's conversations in the Chats list's order, each with its title, `here` on the open one, a brass dot and `running ·` on one with a turn running, a pin on a pinned one, and its time meta; filter by title; `↑`/`↓` move, `⏎` switches, `⌘⏎` starts a new conversation from anywhere in it, and the last row "Begin a new conversation" does too. Opens only in Talk and never under another dialog; leaving Talk or the workspace closes it. Also from ⌘K's "Switch conversation…" and the `talk/switcher` tour surface. _Support:_ `chat/ConversationSwitcher.tsx` (`filterChats`), `App.tsx` (`conversationSwitcher`); `chat/ConversationSwitcher.test.tsx`; `data-tour="talk-switcher-input"`, `"talk-switcher-row"`. _Entry:_ ⌘⌥K in Talk.
- **⌘⌥N new conversation (#1153)** — From any mode with an active workspace: switches to Talk and starts a new conversation (as the Chats `+`). Not under a dialog. ⌘N stays New workspace. _Support:_ `useGlobalShortcuts.ts` (`new-conversation`), `App.tsx` (`newConversation`).
- **One running turn per conversation** — Running state belongs to the thread, not the workspace: several conversations of one workspace can each run a turn, each with its own Stop, and each shows the live pulse in the Chats list. **The backend enforces it:** `send_chat_message`, `run_shell_command` and `continue_subagent` refuse with "A turn is already running in this conversation." while a turn or a sub-agent continuation runs on the thread (`ChatEngine::begin_turn` checks and registers under one lock, so two sends can't both pass; `TURN_BUSY`), so a second turn can never share the thread's rows and shell or take over its cancel flag. **One `done`, after the release:** every turn and every continuation that began ends with exactly one `done` stream event, on every path (an answer, a Stop, a cap, an error), sent only once its claim on the thread is released (`TurnEnd`, after the turn's checkpoint is recorded), so a `list_running_threads` read can never list a turn that is over; a refused send sends none. `done` is metadata only (no token totals: the turn's usage rides on its priced row). **Refusals keep the draft:** a send or a `$` command refused before anything of it was saved (a turn running there, the budget cap, no thread) gives the composer its draft back, before anything typed since (`send`'s `onRefused`, `runShell` resolving `false`, `Composer.giveBack`). **The store:** `streamingThreadsByWs` lists each workspace's running threads; `streamingByWs` (and `getStreaming`) is read from it for the shown thread on every change (`streamingPatch`), and a `done` takes only its own thread off. A sub-agent continuation marks its thread running too (`continueSubagent`, `threadOfCall`), so Stop shows and the composer waits until its `done`; the Stop flag the Player reads is per thread (`stopRequestedByThread`). `loadHistory` and `selectThread` ask `list_running_threads(workspaceId)` (threads with a turn or a continuation running, `ChatEngine::running_turns`), so a reloaded view shows a running turn and its Stop again; an answer read before that turn's `done` can't mark it running again (`endedAt`). **Loads can't cross threads:** `loadHistory` and `selectThread` share a load sequence per workspace (`beginLoad`/`applyLoad`), so only the newest load fills the view and only while its thread is shown, and rows that arrived by `chat://message-added` during the read are merged by id instead of lost. **Truncate checks the thread:** `truncate_chat_after(threadId, messageId)` (Regenerate, Edit & resend; `ChatEngine::truncate_after`) is refused with the same busy error while the thread runs a turn, and otherwise first reads the message's thread and refuses, deleting nothing, when it isn't `threadId`'s ("That message isn't part of this conversation, so nothing was deleted."). _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs` (`begin_turn`, `ensure_idle`, `truncate_after`, `running_turns`, `TurnEnd`, `send_agentic`), `commands::list_running_threads`, `db::truncate_chat_after`, `chatStore` (`streamingThreadsByWs`, `streamingPatch`, `rehydrateRunning`, `beginLoad`, `applyLoad`), `CompanionHistory` (`streamingChatIds`).
- **Thread titles: derived, then generated + time meta** (#1137) — **Derived on send:** an untouched default thread is renamed from the first user message (or first `$ cmd`) as it is sent. The derived title reads what was typed (not the `@` blocks appended to it, `typedText`), drops `/skill` tokens, `@file` mentions and fenced code, turns a URL into its ticket key (`…atlassian.net/browse/GUIDE-123` → `GUIDE-123`) or its host and path tail (`github.com/…/pull/918`), collapses whitespace and cuts at a word boundary near 60 characters with `…` (a message that is only a skill keeps it). **Generated after the first answer:** when a thread's first turn ends (its `done`, background threads too) with an answer and its title is still the placeholder or the derived one (`isAutoTitle`), one call titles it: `generate_chat_title` runs on the **fast tier of the conversation's own provider** (`fast_model_on_provider`: the Settings › Models tier map's `fast` when it is one of that provider's models, else that provider's current `haiku`-named model; `auto` reads as the strong tier's provider; a tier mapped on another provider is never used), with the first ask tidied as above (its first 2,000 characters; an ask that is only an `@` mention or code is sent as is, cut the same way) and the first 1,500 characters of the answer, for at most 6 words in the conversation's language, no quotes, no trailing period. An ask that names a ticket key or a tracker URL gets a title led by the key (`GUIDE-123 · Waive virtualenv findings`; `ticketKey`, `UTF-8`-style standards excluded); the reply is cleaned (`cleanGeneratedTitle`: first line, no `Title:` label, quotes or period, six words). The spend of every reply that comes back, a truncated one too (it is kept, not rejected), is billed to the thread in the ledger as surface `talk`, origin `title` (`bill_title_reply` → `record_title_spend`), so it counts in the conversation's cost and the budget gate applies. **Fallback:** no fast tier on that provider (`null`), a failed call or one past 10 s (`TITLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, and a 10 s timeout on the backend call) keeps the derived title. **Never twice, never over yours:** it runs once per thread on its own (`autoTitled`), only on the first turn, never over a title the user renamed or one a fork (`… · fork`) or an import brought, and a rename made while the call runs wins. The active row shows the stored title (derived live only while it is the placeholder), and a new title crossfades in (`.octo-fade-in`, keyed by the title). Meta: clock time for today, then calendar-day `YESTERDAY` / `ND AGO` / date (`formatRelTime`). _Support:_ `chatTitle.ts` (`deriveChatTitle`, `titleSource`, `ticketKey`, `shortUrl`, `deriveChatMeta`, `formatRelTime`), `chatTitleGen.ts` (`titleRequest`, `requestChatTitle`, `cleanGeneratedTitle`, `isAutoTitle`), `chatStore` (`autoTitleThread`, `regenerateTitle`), `commands::generate_chat_title`. _Entry:_ CompanionHistory.
- **Regenerate title** (#1137) — A Chats row action beside rename (`RefreshCw`, "Regenerate title", `data-tour="companion-chat-regenerate-title"`) runs the same call on request, over any title; it waits disabled while the call runs, and when no title comes back the title stays and an info toast ("The title stays as it is") says why: no answer to title yet, no fast model on the conversation's provider (map one in Settings › Models), a budget limit blocking spend, or the call failed or took longer than 10 s. While the first answer's own title call is still running, regenerate makes no second call and says "A title is on its way" instead (`busy`). _Support:_ `chatStore.regenerateTitle` (returns the `TitleFailure`), `chatTitleGen.titleFailureToast`, `App.handleRegenerateTitle`. _Entry:_ CompanionHistory row actions.
- **Default-thread guard / orphan prevention** — `loadHistory` auto-creates a default thread if none exist; `ensureThread` guarantees a real thread before any send; a migration backfills a thread for orphan messages. _Support:_ `chatStore`, `db.rs`.
- **Cross-workspace notifications** — A message arriving for a non-active workspace pings the attention store / rail. _Support:_ `attentionStore.ping`. _Entry:_ rail Talk-icon pulse + chime.

### Streaming responses & the agentic loop
- **Agentic tool-use loop** — Sends messages with tools, executes tool calls, feeds results back, repeats until a final text answer. The folder the tools work in is read from the database by `workspace_id` (the worktree, or the project root while there is none; `with_workspace_path_from_db`, `Db::talk_workspace_path`), never taken from the webview's `workspacePath`. A failed or denied call's result goes back with `is_error: true`, read from its row's stamped `ok` (`context::transcript::tool_row_is_error`) both live and when later turns replay the round, so the cached prefix holds. A thread's history loads in row order (`id`), so a clock that steps back never reorders it. **No round bound by default**: a message runs as many rounds as the answer needs, until the model answers or the user stops it (`chat_history::effective_talk_max_iterations` → `None`, the loop runs unbounded). The optional **"Limit tool turns per message"** switch (Settings › General › Talk; `settings.json` `talkMaxIterations`, `null` = no limit, a set value clamped 5–200) bounds it — one round = one provider response, however many tools it calls in parallel. A per-iteration budget gate (`should_stop_for_budget`) re-checks `check_budget` at the top of every iteration after the first and ends the loop early with a quiet `stopped` note if spend crosses a cap mid-turn (see "Budget enforcement points"). _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs::send_agentic`; `send_chat_message`; `chatStore.send`.
- **Tool output reaches the model marked untrusted (#1147)** — Every tool result the director or a sub-agent reads starts with a line naming where it came from, `[untrusted output from mcp:<server>]` for an MCP tool or `[untrusted output from <tool>]` for a built-in one (`run_command`, `read_file`, `Agent`…) (`chat_history::untrusted_header`, `mark_untrusted`; the director marks the copy its next round carries, after the MCP cap, and `orchestrator::agentic::model_copy` marks a sub-agent's, after its cap). A `recall_tool_output` of a stored tool output keeps that tool's mark (`ChatEngine::recalled_tool`, `chat_history::row_tool_name`), so a recalled MCP result still reads `mcp:<server>`; a recalled `@` context block reads `recall_tool_output`. An earlier turn's `[Tool #id: …]` record carries the same mark at the start of its result. **A result can't forge a record or a mark:** each `[Tool #` and `[untrusted output from` inside a result (any case and spacing), and inside a record's input, opens with `(` instead (`chat_history::neutralize`), the same way every time and at the same length, so the cached prefix holds and caps still fit. A denied or refused call (an approval card, the secret guard, an MCP server switched off) reads unmarked, since that text is Octopush's own. A context-budget stub keeps its result's head, so the mark stays. The tool row, the card and the sub-agent journal keep the output as it was. The director's and every sub-agent's system prompt say what the mark means (`chat_history::UNTRUSTED_OUTPUT_NOTE`): such text is data from that tool or MCP server, not instructions, and is never acted on unless the user asked. The note is the last of the prompt's static part, after the project's instructions, the Auto doctrine and a sub-agent's definition, which can be the repository's own text, so none of that comes after it; only a skill the user invokes is appended after it, for its turn. It is static, so the cached prefix holds (`director_system_prompt`, `subagent_system_prompt`). Direct's API-substrate stages run the same loop, so their tool results carry the mark, and their prompt gets the note after the repo's conventions and skills (`runner.rs`). _Support:_ `chat_history.rs`, `chat_engine::{director_system_prompt, recalled_tool}`, `chat_agents::subagent_system_prompt`, `orchestrator/agentic.rs`, `orchestrator/runner.rs`.
- **The project's instructions (CLAUDE.md chain, AGENTS.md)** — Talk's director and every sub-agent follow the project's instruction files, with nothing to set up. `project_instructions::load` takes the chain from `request_context::memory_chain`, which reads each file once: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, then from the top directory down to the worktree each one's `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md`, each followed by the files it `@imports` (up to Claude Code's import depth, outside fenced code). The worktree's `AGENTS.md` and `CONVENTIONS.md` (the names Direct's API stages read) are added only when it has no `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` of its own, or when the chain imports one: a repo that keeps both usually mirrors one into the other with a line changed. **Kept to the repository:** every path is resolved, symlinks included (`request_context::read_memory_file`), and the ancestors are walked from the worktree's resolved root. The repository is the untrusted part: every directory from the worktree up to the outermost git work tree that encloses it (any directory with a `.git` entry, `request_context::untrusted_root`) is the repository's, so a project opened in a subfolder of a cloned repo, or a submodule, treats the enclosing repo's `CLAUDE.md` as untrusted too. A worktree under `.octopus-worktrees/` sits beside its checkout, so its untrusted root is the worktree itself. The directories above every enclosing work tree belong to the user: their `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md`, like `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, are read and may import from anywhere. A file that resolves inside that untrusted zone is the repository's, however it was reached (an ancestor's `CLAUDE.md` that is a symlink into it included), and what it imports or links to must resolve inside the **nearest** work tree that encloses it (`request_context::nearest_work_tree`), never a wider one: the project's own files stay in the project's own work tree, an outer repo's file stays in that outer repo, and a `.git` in home (a dotfiles repo) or around a folder of clones never lets a cloned repo reach `~/.ssh` or a sibling repo. An import of `~/…`, `../…` or an absolute path that leaves that tree, a symlinked `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` pointing out, or a symlink further down an import chain is listed as "skipped: outside the project" and never read. A project file that imports an ancestor's file adds nothing: that file was already read once, as the user's. Every file is labelled by where it really resolves (relative to the worktree, `~/…` under home, else in full); a repo folder named `~` is labelled `./~/…`, so it can't pass for the user's home. At most 20 skipped files are listed; the rest are counted. **Bounded reads:** the resolved path is opened first, non-blocking and without following a link swapped in since, and the open handle must be a regular file (`fstat`), so a FIFO or device can't hang the turn; a file over 4 MiB is skipped ("over 4 MiB") and at most that much is ever read; the files are read on a blocking thread, off the async runtime (`for_workspace_off_runtime`). A file identical to one already sent (the same text in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and the project's `CLAUDE.md`, or in a parent directory's `CLAUDE.md` and the worktree's) is sent once; an empty or unreadable file is left out, and a worktree with none sends nothing. **Bounds, in bytes:** each file is capped at 16,000 bytes like a Direct dossier section (head and tail kept, plus an 80-byte note, `cap_to`), the whole section at 40,000 bytes (`INSTRUCTIONS_CAP_BYTES`, about Claude Code's own large-CLAUDE.md warning of 40k characters). The worktree's own `CLAUDE.md` (or `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, or the `AGENTS.md` standing in) is budgeted first, so it is never the file left out; the rest follow in load order. A file that fits what is left is sent whole, however small; a larger one is trimmed to what is left, or, with under 1,000 bytes left, named "Left out for length" and not sent. **Placement:** a `# Project instructions` section ("Contents of CLAUDE.md:" per file, in load order) right after the base prompt (the request's own, or Talk's) and before the Auto doctrine and any skill the message invokes (`chat_engine::director_system_prompt`); in a sub-agent after its no-human rules and before its `.claude/agents` definition body (`subagent_system_prompt`). The files are re-read every turn and every sub-agent run, so an edit applies at once, and unchanged files give the same text, so the cached system block holds. The text goes to the conversation's own provider, with the rest of the prompt. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/project_instructions.rs` (`load`, `for_workspace`, `for_workspace_off_runtime`), `request_context.rs` (`memory_chain`, `read_memory_file`, `MemorySkip`), `chat_engine.rs` (`director_system_prompt`), `chat_agents.rs` (`subagent_system_prompt`, `run_subagent_core`). _Entry:_ automatic on every Talk turn; listed in Companion › Conversation ("follows").
- **Streamed final text** — Only the FINAL assistant text is emitted as a `chat://stream` delta (intermediate pre-tool text suppressed); the frontend accumulates a live bubble with a `▊` caret. _Support:_ `ChatStreamEvent`, `ChatCanvas`.
- **Director retries, pacing and timeouts** — Every director request (each round and the forced close) goes through `ChatEngine::director_call` → `providers::complete_cancellable` → `complete_with_retry`, the sub-agents' retry: a transient failure (429, 529/overloaded, 5xx, a connection that couldn't be opened: refused, DNS, connect timeout, or one that dropped after a 200 while the answer's body was arriving: "the connection was lost while the answer was arriving", `ProviderErrorKind::Network`) is retried in place with the same capped exponential backoff (2, 4, 8, 16, 32 s, at most 60 s), honouring `retry-after`, up to `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES` (5); the turn's history is kept, so a blip never costs the work done. **What the provider marks final returns at once** (`providers::classify_status`, shared by both providers through `status_error`): a status with `x-should-retry: false` (`parse_should_retry`) is `Other`, and a 429 with no `retry-after` whose body names a spend or usage limit ("usage limit", "spend limit", "insufficient_quota", "exceeded your current quota", "credit balance") is `ProviderErrorKind::SpendCap`, so a cap no wait can lift shows at once instead of after minutes of backoff. **A request that went out and got no answer is never sent again** (the read timeout, a connection reset or closed while waiting, a body that went silent mid-answer): the provider may still be working on it, and a retry could run it twice, so the turn ends with an error that says so ("… the provider sent no answer before the read timeout (…). It was not retried: the provider may still be working on the request, and sending it again could run it twice. Send your message again to retry.", or "the connection was lost after the request was sent" / "the connection went silent while the answer was arriving"); a cut-off body is never reported as a JSON error (`providers::request_error`, `body_error`). **A model server on this Mac** (a loopback base: `localhost`, `*.localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`; `is_loopback_base`, e.g. Ollama) that refuses the connection gets one retry (`LOCAL_CONNECT_RETRIES`, after 2 s; the notice reads "retry 1 of 1"), then the turn ends with "The model server on this Mac at http://localhost:11434/v1 isn't reachable. Is it running? (…)". Each wait is shown live, never persisted: the backend emits `chat://notice` `{workspaceId, threadId, text, delaySecs}` with the sub-agents' journal words (`retry_notice`, capitalized: "Model overloaded — retrying in 8s (retry 1 of 5)"), the store keeps it per thread (`turnNoticeByThread`) and the Player shows it for `delaySecs` or until the turn moves on (a row, a stream delta, a tool start, the end). **Pacing:** after each response the director applies the sub-agents' rate-limit rule (`orchestrator::agentic::compute_throttle`): when the provider reports less input-token headroom than the round just used, the next request waits for the window to reset (at most 65 s, interruptible by Stop), with the notice "Input-token budget low — pausing 20s for the rate-limit window to reset". **Retries exhausted:** the turn ends with one `error` row that says what happened, that nothing is lost and how to go on, then the provider's message (`final_failure_text`: "Model overloaded, still failing after 5 retries. The conversation is saved: send your message again, or say "continue", to pick up where it left off. (Anthropic API error 529 …)"); an error that isn't retried (auth, bad request, a spend cap, a request that got no answer) fails at once with its own text, except a prompt too long for the model, which the context budget stubs and sends once more (**Context budget (director)**). The row keeps the failure's kind (**Persisted errors**), and its card's "Try again" continues the turn. The thread stays usable: the next message runs as usual. **Timeouts:** the pooled client every LLM call uses (`chat_engine::shared_http_client` → `tls::llm_client`) has a 10 s connect timeout, an idle read timeout of 30 min (`LLM_READ_TIMEOUT`: requests don't stream yet, so an answer's first byte comes only once it is generated, and 64k output tokens at a slow ~40 tokens/s take about 27 minutes) and TCP keep-alive (probe after 30 s idle, every 10 s, 3 probes), so a connection that dies silently fails within about a minute instead of hanging the turn; there is no total timeout, so a long answer is never cut. A connect timeout is retried; a read timeout is not (above). A loopback base goes out on its own pooled client with the connect timeout but **no read bound** and no proxy (`providers::client_for` → `tls::local_llm_client`), so a slow local model is never cut off. _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs` (`director_call`, `fail_turn`, `emit_turn_notice`, `TURN_NOTICE_EVENT`), `providers/mod.rs` (`complete_cancellable`, `Completion`, `retry_notice`, `final_failure_text`), `tls.rs` (`with_stall_guards`, `llm_client`, `local_llm_client`), `chatStore` (`turnNoticeByThread`, `clearTurnNotice`), `chat/OctoStatus.tsx` (`notice`). _Entry:_ Talk, any turn whose provider call fails transiently.
- **The Player (pinned activity figure)** — While a turn runs, a naked stacked figure (The Octo 22px above a one-word serif label) sits pinned bottom-center of the chat canvas — always visible regardless of journal scroll (bottom exit wash + 118px journal padding keep it legible; the "Latest" jump pill lifts to clear it). Eight roles from real signals, priority wait > retry > tool > text > thought: Waiting for you (approval pending — frozen, half-mast eyes, brass label) · the director's **retry / pause notice** while it waits on the provider (the notice itself as the label, e.g. "Model overloaded — retrying in 8s (retry 1 of 5)"; idle body, sage label; see "Director retries, pacing and timeouts") · Reading… (READ/LS/GLOB — reading saccades) · Searching… (GREP/FIND — darting gaze) · Editing…/Writing… (EDIT/WRITE / stream text — typing arms, eyes down) · Running… (BASH — dead still, eyes wide) · Thinking…/Working… (paddle + eye scan). Labels crossfade 220ms; the octopus never moves (single-axis stack). Turn end: ✓ happy-eye beat 500ms, then fade; errors skip the beat. Replaces the old inline Thinking… indicator and the "Generating" dot (the `▊` caret stays). _Support:_ `chat/OctoStatus.tsx` (`roleForActivity`); `ChatCanvas`. _Entry:_ Talk mode, any running turn.
- **Done event & attention ping** — A metadata-only `done` event clears its thread's streaming state (other running threads stay running); chimes/pulses the rail only if not already on that chat; fires even for background threads. _Support:_ `chatStore`, `focus`.
- **Approval card — a command waits on you** — An agent `run_command` that `dangerous_command` flags (`rm -rf`, a force push, `sudo`, `curl | sh`, `git reset --hard`…), from the parent turn or a sub-agent, a commit/push/PR the secret guard stopped (#819), or an MCP write or a file tool reaching outside the workspace (#1147, see the next entry), parks the turn on an inline card (`chat://approval-request` → `ApprovalCard`; `ApprovalBroker::ask`). **No timeout:** the card waits until it is answered; Stop on the conversation and deleting the conversation answer it as a denial (`deny_thread`), and deleting the workspace (or its project) stops every turn of its conversations as Stop would and **retires** it in the broker, so a turn still winding down there is denied at once instead of parking a card nobody can answer (`ChatEngine::cancel_workspace` → `cancel` per thread + `ApprovalBroker::retire_workspace`); if removing the workspace's row then fails, the workspace stays and is reinstated, so its next card isn't denied unseen (`ChatEngine::finish_workspace_delete` → `reinstate_workspace`; its turns stay stopped, as after Stop). A card left alone used to be denied after 5 minutes without a word; nothing is denied silently now. A reloaded webview shows a waiting card again when its conversation opens (`pending_approvals(threadId)` → `ApprovalBroker::pending_for_thread`, `rehydrateApprovals`, like the turn-limit card); a card answered while that read is in flight never comes back (the session's answered call ids, `markAnswered`, bounded at 500), though a live request under the same id is always shown (the secret guard asks again under the same id when its rescan changed). **It reaches you:** while it waits it is the workspace's needs-you state (see "Attention model"): the rail's flag on that workspace under the single-beacon rule (a turn parked on a card leaves the rail's working set, `workingTalkWorkspaces`, so the flag shows instead of the marching edge), the Mode switcher's Talk pulse from another mode, Mission Control's needs-you band ("approval in Talk"), the top-bar mascot, the Dock badge and the menu bar Octo (one per conversation), a chime unless you are looking at that conversation, and a native notification (see "Crew notifications"); nothing that leaves the window carries the command or its arguments, only what kind of thing waits and the workspace. Mission Control and the menu bar open the conversation the oldest card waits in. **At the keyboard:** the card is a focusable `role="group"` named `Approval needed: <command>` (`aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+Enter Escape"`, a brass inset focus ring). **It never takes the focus when it appears**, so a habitual `⌘↵` or Enter meant for the composer can never answer a command nobody read; it takes the focus only from the user: a click, Tab, or **`⌘⌥A`** (Talk only), which focuses the oldest card waiting in the conversation on screen and brings it into view (`focusOldestCard`, `FOCUS_CARD_CHORD`; cards render in arrival order, each carries `data-approval-card`), also ⌘K's "Focus the waiting approval card" (#1153). Only while the card itself has focus: **⌘↵** takes the lead answer (Approve; on the secret card the safe "Leave it out") and **Esc** denies; **plain Enter does nothing**, so a stray Return never approves a destructive command, except on the secret card, where Enter also takes the safe answer. Held keys (`repeat`), IME composition and other chords are ignored, a key on a button inside the card is the button's own, and a handled key stops there, so the composer's own ⌘↵ and the card's never meet; the keys answer only while Talk is the mode on screen, since a card can keep the focus after a mode switch hides it (`cardKeyAnswer`, pure, `talkActive` from `ChatView`'s `active`). Each card carries a visually hidden `role="alert"`, "The turn is waiting on your answer.", so a screen reader hears it as it appears. Titles name the keys and say they answer the card's own focus (card "⌘↵ approves · Esc denies · ⌘⌥A focuses the oldest waiting card", "Approve (⌘↵ with the card focused)", "Deny (Esc with the card focused)"; secret card "⌘↵, Enter or Esc leaves it out · ⌘⌥A focuses the oldest waiting card", "Leave it out (⌘↵, Enter or Esc with the card focused)"). `data-tour="talk-approval"` (`talk-secret-approval` on the secret card). "Approve & don't ask again" grants the thread, never on the secret card or a file card. _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs` (`ApprovalBroker`: `ask`, `await_card`, `park`, `waiting`, `pending_for_thread`, `deny_thread`, `retire_workspace`; `ChatEngine::cancel_workspace`), `commands.rs` (`pending_approvals`, `delete_workspace`), `fleet_status.rs`, `menu_bar.rs`, `chat/ApprovalCard.tsx`, `chatStore` (`syncApprovalAttention`, `showPendingApproval`, `workingTalkWorkspaces`, `rehydrateApprovals`, `markAnswered`), `attentionStore` (`raiseApproval`, `settleApproval`), `lib/attentionFocus.ts`, `lib/approvalNotifications.ts`, `MissionControl.tsx` (`attentionCopy`). _Entry:_ Talk, when the agent asks.
- **What asks before it runs: MCP writes and files outside the workspace (#1147)** — Beside a flagged command, two kinds of tool call park on the approval card, in the director's loop and in every Talk sub-agent (`SubagentGate::check`); `talk_guard` decides and words the card. **MCP writes:** a director call to an MCP tool asks first unless the turn's discovery classed it as one that runs in the conversation's mode (`talk_guard::director_card` → `McpTools::card`, see the next entry; a tool the turn didn't offer asks too); a sub-agent's MCP call is classed the same way, in the thread's mode at the call (`SubagentGate::with_mcp`). The hints are the server's own claims about its tool, not something Octopush checks: a read-only filesystem tool can still read outside the workspace, since its server decides what it may open. The card (`kind: "mcp"`) shows the tool and its arguments as JSON, with no `$`: each string over 160 characters is replaced by its length, anything credential-shaped is redacted (`secret_scan::redact_line`) and the whole is cut to 400 characters (`mcp_args_shown`). Its reason is "MCP tool `<tool>` may change external state (its server does not mark it read-only)", or "(its server marks it destructive)" (`chat_agents::mcp_gate_texts`, with "Sub-agent “<label>”: " in front for a sub-agent); the reason line wraps in full, never cut with "…". A tool that runs without a card runs as before, a server switched off in the conversation is refused without asking, and the thread's "don't ask again" answers an MCP card like a command's (the button's title says so: "Approve this, and stop asking about flagged commands and MCP tool calls for the rest of this conversation (a possible secret, or a file or command reaching outside the workspace, still asks)"). **Files outside the workspace:** `read_file`, `list_files`, `grep`, `write_file` and `edit_file` resolve their target the way the tool will open it (`talk_guard::resolve`: each existing component canonicalized and symlinks followed, a `..` after a link going up from where the link points, a dangling link followed to its target, a missing component kept as written). A target inside the workspace runs as before, and so does a read in a dependency folder a mission links from its main checkout (`node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`; see "Share with new missions"). The main checkout is the project's root as the database has it (`talk_guard::project_root`, `linked_folders`), never read from the workspace's `.git`, which the agent can rewrite, nor taken from where the worktree sits (worktrees live beside the project, in `<parent>/.octopus-worktrees`, so the folder around them is not the project). Any other target (an absolute path, a `..`, a link in the workspace that leads out, or links more than 16 deep, which can't be followed: "its links go too deep to follow"), and any write into the main checkout, asks, as `kind: "read"` or `"write"`. **Checked again once approved** (`chat_engine::guard_card`): after the card, the call is resolved again, and it runs only if it still reaches what the card showed; a link changed while the card waited asks again about where it now leads. `glob` walks the workspace without following links, so it never leaves it. The card names the resolved path (`~/…` under home), never the file, and its reason says what the tool does ("reads a file outside the workspace", "lists a folder…", "searches…", "writes a file…", "edits a file…"). It offers **Allow once** and **Deny** and no "don't ask again": every such access asks, no thread grant answers it, and an "always" answer counts as one approval (`ApprovalBroker::await_card`, `grant_answers`, `record`). Its body reads "Allowing lets the agent read it once, and what it reads goes to your AI provider. Every access outside the workspace asks again." (a write: "Allowing lets the agent write it once."). **Credentials locations** say why and lead with the safe answer: `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.config/gh`, `~/.config/gcloud`, `~/.config/op`, `~/.azure`, `~/.kube`, `~/.docker`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.password-store`, `~/.netrc`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.npmrc`, `~/.pypirc`, Cargo's credentials, `~/.vault-token`, `~/.terraform.d`, `~/.octopush`, `~/.mcp-auth`, all of `~/.claude` and `~/.codex`, `~/.claude.json`, and the keychains (`~/Library/Keychains`, `/Library/Keychains`), each matched as named and where it resolves (a linked `~/.ssh` counts), without case, and asking even in a workspace opened at home; a `grep` of a folder that holds one; and a file whose name marks it as an env file or a key (`secret_scan::is_env_file`, `is_sensitive_name`) outside the workspace, in a linked dependency folder, or anywhere in a workspace that holds home. Such a card (`sensitive`) reads "Possible credentials" and adds "This may hold credentials.", its reason ends with why ("~/.ssh holds SSH keys", "its name marks it as an env file"), **Deny** comes first, and ⌘↵, Enter and Esc all deny (card title "⌘↵, Enter or Esc denies"; an ordinary file card "⌘↵ allows once · Esc denies"). In a sandboxed mission the sandbox itself refuses a write outside the workspace, so only reads ask there; an `edit_file` reads the file first, so it asks as a read ("reads a file to edit it"). A denial tells the model what it wasn't allowed to do and not to retry. Outside the window, the notification reads "An MCP tool call is waiting for your approval" or "A file access outside the workspace is waiting for your approval", and the menu bar "an MCP tool call wants approval" or "a file outside the workspace wants approval": the kind, never the arguments or the path. **Not covered:** a hard link isn't told apart from the file it links. A `run_command` that names such a path asks too (see the next entry), but a command can still reach a path it builds at run time. _Support:_ `talk_guard.rs` (`director_card`, `mcp_card`, `mcp_args_shown`, `Reach::outside_card`, `project_root`, `linked_folders`, `resolve`), `chat_engine.rs` (`guard_card`, `ApprovalBroker::await_card`, `grant_answers`; `ApprovalRequestEvent.kind` / `sensitive`, `ApprovalWait.kind`), `chat_agents.rs` (`SubagentGate`), `menu_bar::talk_label`, `chat/ApprovalCard.tsx`, `chatStore` (`approvalMarks`), `lib/approvalNotifications.ts`. _Entry:_ Talk, when the agent asks.
- **Fewer MCP cards in Edit freely, and lasting trust (#1243)** — In Edit freely an MCP tool runs without a card when its server marks it `readOnlyHint: true`, or `destructiveHint: false`, or sets neither hint and its own name starts with a read verb (`get`, `list`, `search`, `read`, `fetch`, `describe`, `query`, `show`, `find`, `count`, `view`, `lookup`, `check`) followed by `_`, `-` or a capital, and no later word of the name is a conjunction (`and`, `or`, `then`) or a write verb (`delete`, `remove`, `update`, `set`, `create`, `write`, `put`, `post`, `patch`, `modify`, `purge`, `drop`, `insert`, `upsert`, `merge`, `move`, `rename`, `send`, `publish`, `push`, `apply`, `run`, `exec`, `replace`, `execute`, `edit`, `save`, `add`, `reset`, `clear`, `store`, `sync`, `upload`, `commit`, `destroy`, `wipe`, `truncate`; words split at `_`, `-` and camelCase, matched without case), and at least one word follows the verb. `get_report`, `list-items` and `searchCode` read; `search`, `get_`, `checkout_branch`, `get_or_create_issue`, `fetchAndDelete`, `get_AND_x`, `search_replace`, `check_in` and `checkOut` don't (`talk_guard::mcp_class`, `read_verb_name`, `NOT_A_READ`; `McpToolInfo.destructive` and `.annotated`, read from `tools/list`). A tool marked `destructiveHint: true` asks every time, whatever its name or trust, unless this conversation's "don't ask again" is on. **Tool names and hints are the server's own claims:** Octopush doesn't check them, so a write its server names `get_…`, or marks read-only or not destructive, runs without a card. A server that sets `readOnlyHint: false` is taken at its word, whatever the name.
