Plan only still runs only `readOnlyHint` tools and refuses the rest before any card (`permissions::decide`), and Ask first, once it can be set, asks for anything not marked `readOnlyHint`. **Lasting answers:** in Edit freely, the card of a tool not marked destructive also offers two upright-serif phrases on a line of their own (`data-tour="talk-approval-trust"`): **Always allow this tool** (answer `"tool"`) and **Trust <server>** (`"server"`), each also running this call. Their tooltips: "Run this, and let <tool> run without asking in Edit freely, in every conversation, until you revoke it in Settings › Integrations", and "Run this, and let every <server> tool run without asking … (a tool it marks destructive still asks)". The card carries the server and tool (`ToolCard.trust` → `ApprovalRequestEvent.trustServer` / `trustTool`); a lasting answer to a card that offered none counts as one approval (`ApprovalBroker::settle_card`, `record`). Trust is app-wide, not per conversation: one `app_meta` row per server (`mcp_trust:<server>`, JSON `{ server, config, all, tools }`; `mcp::trust`), so it holds in every conversation and after a restart. **It is bound to the server's user-level entry** in `~/.claude/mcp.json`, by a hash of its command, args, env names and values (a Keychain value is `""` in the file) and remote URL (`trust::fingerprint`, kept as `config`; the card carries it, `ToolCard.trust: TrustOffer`). A changed entry lapses it: it no longer applies, the card offers it again, and Settings' save removes it (`trust::prune`); granting under a new entry drops what was kept for the old one. A server whose name the worktree's own `.claude/mcp.json` defines is never offered trust nor covered by it, even when a user-level entry has the same name (`TrustView::read`, `offer`, `covers`). It is read at each call (`ApprovalBroker::mcp_trust`), so a revoke applies to the very next one; a read that fails trusts nothing. **What trust covers:** the server's tools except those it marks `destructiveHint: true`, which still ask even when the server is trusted; only in Edit freely; never a file, command, secret or credentials card. Remote deletes and force pushes made through shell commands are a separate rule (the command check) and ask as before. The thread-wide "Approve & don't ask again" is unchanged. A lasting answer and a revoke emit `mcp://trust-changed` (`ipc.onMcpChanged` listens). Listed with `list_mcp_trust(workspacePath?)` (what still holds for the user-level entries; with a worktree, without the servers its `.claude/mcp.json` defines; `trust::listed`), revoked with `revoke_mcp_trust(server, tool | null)` (null takes back the server-wide trust and leaves tools allowed one by one); `mcpScopeStore.trustByPath` (`""` app-wide) / `loadTrust` / `revokeTrust`; a sub-agent reads trust and mode at each call through `chat_agents::SubagentMcp`. _Support:_ `talk_guard.rs` (`McpClass`, `McpTools`, `McpCheck`), `mcp/trust.rs`, `chat_engine.rs` (`ApprovalDecision::TrustTool` / `TrustServer`, `ApprovalBroker::with_trust`), `chat_agents.rs` (`SubagentGate::with_mcp`), `commands.rs`, `chat/ApprovalCard.tsx`, `stores/mcpScopeStore.ts`; tests in `talk_guard`, `mcp::trust`, `chat_engine` (`an_mcp_card_trusted_in_one_thread_holds_in_every_thread_and_after_a_restart`), `chat_agents` (`a_subagent_follows_the_users_trust_and_the_threads_mode`), `ApprovalCard.test.tsx`. _Entry:_ Talk, when the agent asks; Settings › Integrations.
- **What asks before it runs: commands that name a path outside the workspace (#1201)** — An agent `run_command` (the director's or a sub-agent's) is read for the paths it names before it runs, after the secret guard and before the command check (`talk_guard::Reach::command_card`). Strict on credentials, light elsewhere. **How it reads a command:** every command it runs, nested ones included, goes through the command check's walk with the same caps (`chat_engine::each_command`: `$(…)`, backticks, `bash -c` strings, 4 deep and 64 in all); past the caps the line is read flat, which still sees every word written in it. A small lexer splits each line into words (`chat_engine::command_words`): quoted text stays one word (`git commit -m "…"`, `sed 's|…|…|'`), and it knows redirections (a target counts, `2>` and `>&1` don't), here-documents (the body is data), here-strings, comments, `$'…'` (decoded), `$"…"`, `${…}`, `NAME=` and `--flag=` prefixes, and a leading `@` (`curl -d @file`). Each word is expanded as macOS's bash 3.2 would, from where the command runs: the shared shell's current folder in the director's loop (`TalkShell::cwd`), the workspace for a sub-agent or a sandboxed mission. Braces expand first (`{a,b}`, nested, `{x..y}` ranges; at most 64 words, `brace_expand`), then `~`, `$HOME` and `${HOME}`, then globs against the disk (`*`, `?`, `[…]`, dotfiles only for a pattern that starts with a dot, which also matches `.` and `..`, as bash 3.2 does; `glob_paths`). A `cd` or `pushd` moves where the rest of the line lands, logically as bash does (`cd link && cd ..` goes back up the link's name; `cd -P` goes where it leads); after a `cd` the check can't follow (`cd "$X"`, `cd -`, `popd`), relative words count by name only. Each path is resolved like a file tool's read (`talk_guard::resolve`, links followed). **What asks:** a credentials location (the list in the entry above, as named or where it resolves, without case) or, outside the workspace, a file named like an env file or a key, always asks, with **Deny** first, and is never remembered. A folder that holds one counts too when the command reads whole folders (`walking_segments`: `tar`, `ditto`, `cpio`, `pax`, `7z`, `rsync`, `rg`, `ag`, `ack`, `find`, `fd`, `cat`, `tree` and `python3 -m zipfile` or `tarfile` always; `cp -r`/`-R`/`-a`, `scp -r`, `grep -r`/`-R`, `diff -r`, `gzip -r`/`-R`, `zip -r` and `ls -R` with their recursive flag), so `tar czf x.tgz ~` and `grep -r token ~` lead with Deny while `cd ~`, `ls ~` and `du -sh ~` (sizes only) ask as an ordinary outside read. A word whose expansion the check can't follow (a variable such as `$X`, `$(…)`, a backtick span, `~user`, `~+`, `~-`, an extglob) asks with Deny first when it names a credentials location or file by name (`credential_part`: the names above, `keychains`, `.env`, `id_rsa`, `id_ed25519` and the other SSH key names, `.pem`, `.p12`, `credentials`), read as written, with the expansions left out, and with quotes, brackets and spaces dropped, so a name split across `$(echo ~/.ne )trc` still counts ("reaches ~/.ssh$X/id_rsa through an expansion the check can't follow · it names .ssh, which holds credentials"); otherwise it doesn't ask. A credentials path inside one word of code or prose (`python3 -c "…"`, `eval "…"`, a commit message) asks too. Any other path outside the workspace (`/tmp`, `~/notes`, `..`, a link that leads out) asks as an ordinary outside card, except a read under the system's folders (`SYSTEM_READS`: `/usr`, `/etc`, `/private/etc`, `/opt`, `/Library`, `/System`, `/bin`, `/sbin`, and Homebrew's prefixes) and a read in a folder the user allowed for the conversation. A write (a `>`, `>>` or `&>` target) outside the workspace always asks. Reads in a linked dependency folder don't ask. A program named without a `/` is found on the PATH, so it is no path; one that runs from outside (an executable file), the pseudo-devices (`/dev/null`, `/dev/stdout`, `/dev/fd/…`, `/dev/tty`…) and the body of a here-document or a here-string ask only for a credentials location. A plain name (no `/`) costs one lookup: one that doesn't exist is no path the command reads, and one in a workspace folder stays there unless it is a link. At most 256 paths are resolved in full, 4096 distinct words looked at and 4096 names read by globs, and past any the command asks ("names more paths than the check reads (over 256, or 4096 words)"). **The card** (`kind: "run"`) shows the command with its `$`, the eyebrow "Outside the workspace" (or "Possible credentials"), and the reason "reaches <path> outside the workspace" (`~/…` under home), ending with why for a credentials location ("reaches ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 outside the workspace · ~/.ssh holds SSH keys"; a sub-agent's starts "Sub-agent “<label>”: "). Its body reads "Allowing runs it once, and its output goes to your AI provider. A credentials location always asks.", and its tooltip adds "Octopush reads the paths a command names. A shell can build a path it can't see, so this is a net, not a sandbox." (`RUN_CHECK_LIMITS`). No thread grant answers it. A read outside that isn't a credentials location also offers **Allow reading <folder> for this conversation** (the file's folder, or the folder itself; `ApprovalRequestEvent.rememberDir`, answered as "always"): from then on the conversation's commands read in that folder without asking, until the app restarts, while a write there still asks (`ApprovalBroker::settle_card`, `read_dirs`). A folder that is, holds or is inside a credentials location, as named or where it resolves (`~`, `~/.config`, `/`, a link to one of them), is never offered and never honoured (`Reach::rememberable`): a read there is allowed once at a time. It is checked again once approved (`guard_card`), so a second folder the same command reaches asks next. A denial tells the model which path it wasn't allowed to reach and not to retry. Outside the window it reads "A command reaching outside the workspace is waiting for your approval" (menu bar: "a command reaching outside the workspace wants approval"). **Limits:** it reads the words a command is written with, so a path built at run time (a variable that doesn't name a credentials location, `eval` of a built string, a script that opens it) isn't seen. The macOS sandbox of a sandboxed mission confines writes, not reads. The system folders and the remembered folders apply to commands only; the file tools still ask for every read outside. _Support:_ `talk_guard.rs` (`Reach::command_card`, `scan_line`, `scan_word`, `path_hit`, `reached`, `brace_expand`, `glob_paths`, `walking_segments`, `credential_part`, `named_credential`, `SYSTEM_READS`), `chat_engine.rs` (`each_command`, `command_words`, `CommandWord`, `ApprovalBroker::settle_card`, `read_dirs`), `talk_shell.rs` (`TalkShell::cwd`), `chat_agents.rs` (`SubagentGate::check`), `menu_bar::talk_label`, `chat/ApprovalCard.tsx`, `chatStore` (`approvalMarks`), `lib/approvalNotifications.ts`. _Entry:_ Talk, when the agent asks.
- **Per-message token/cost meta** — Assistant turns show `Nk in · Nk out`, with cost persisted. _Support:_ `ChatMessage.tsx`; `token_engine::compute_cost`.
- **Token-usage recording** — Every billed turn records into the canonical `spend_events` ledger (surface `'talk'`) so Companion CONTEXT + Settings · Usage update. _Support:_ `token_engine::TokenEngine::record` (takes a `surface`; writes `db::record_token_spend`).
- **max_tokens truncation recovery** — If truncated mid-tool-use, error `tool_result`s are injected and the loop retries, at most once in a row: the second round in a row cut at the output limit ends the turn with a quiet `stopped` note ("Stopped: two replies in a row were cut at the output limit mid tool call, so those calls didn't run. Ask for smaller steps, such as one file at a time.", carrying the turn's tokens and cost); a round that isn't cut starts the count again (`TruncationStreak`, `MAX_TRUNCATED_ROUNDS` = 2). Turns are unlimited by default, so without it a model that keeps emitting oversized `write_file` bodies would retry at the full output cap each round. **A final answer cut at the output limit** (`stop_reason` max tokens, no tool calls) is saved as the answer, followed by a quiet `stopped` note: "The answer reached the output limit. Say continue to get the rest." (`cut_answer_note`; with no answer text the note carries the turn's tokens). The note is never replayed to the model, so "continue" picks up from the cut answer. _Support:_ `send_agentic` MaxTokens branch, `finish_with_note`.
- **Forced close at the turn limit (only with a limit switched on)** — Exhausting a configured turn bound no longer throws the work away: the engine appends a "your tool budget is exhausted — write your final answer now" instruction to the last tool result and makes ONE more request (same tool list, so the prompt-cache prefix and Anthropic's tool_use/tools invariant hold). A real answer is persisted as the assistant turn, followed by a quiet `stopped` note ("Reached the N-turn tool limit — answered with what it had. Say "continue" …, or raise or switch off the limit in Settings › General"); an empty/failed close falls back to a persisted `error` row that names the limit and the setting. A "continue" in the same thread resumes with a fresh budget over the rebuilt history. _Support:_ `send_agentic` forced-close tail (mirrors `orchestrator/agentic.rs`); `finish_with_note`.
- **Sub-agents (`Agent` / `Task` tool) — provider-agnostic fan-out** — TALK exposes the tool a Claude Code skill expects, with the same name and shape: `Agent { description, prompt, subagent_type?, model? }` (+ `Task` alias, one schema). Every `Agent` call in ONE assistant response runs **concurrently** (`chat_agents::run_subagents`: a `JoinSet` gated to 8 at a time) — which is exactly how a skill parallelizes, several tool_use blocks in one message — so a fan-out costs the parent **one** turn. Each sub-agent is one `orchestrator::agentic::run_agentic_loop` (the same tool-use loop DIRECT stages run on, over any `LlmProvider`): its own context seeded only with `prompt`, its own system prompt (`subagent_system_prompt`: the task, the optional role, no-human rules, "finish with ONE self-contained report", then the project's instructions, see above), the full workspace tool set (isolated bash, never the shared Talk shell), its own turn bound (none unless configured — see "Limit sub-agent tool turns"), the parent turn's cancel flag (Stop stops the whole crew) and the mission's sandbox roots. `model` overrides the conversation's model per call; `subagent_type` is a role hint. **Depth 1**: sub-agents never receive `Agent`. The parent sees only the final report as the tool result (`report_from_result`: a clean answer passes through; a forced close at the cap is flagged "may be incomplete"; an `ask_director` stop becomes the question itself with "decide, then delegate again"; an unfinished loop is a failed result; a run Stop ended before it answered is marked stopped instead, `mark_stopped`: "Sub-agent stopped: the user stopped the turn after N tool calls, before it reported", never a turn limit it didn't hit), and a malformed call fails fast with the parse error. The persisted `tool` row carries `toolInput: { description, subagentType?, model?, promptChars }` (never the raw prompt) and an `agent` meta object (`ok, finished, closedAtCap, blocked, stopped, model, inputTokens, outputTokens, costUsd, durationMs, toolCalls`). A Stop mid-fan-out still writes every sub-agent's row (see "Stop generating"). The sub-agent's live journal streams as **`chat://agent-log`** `{ workspaceId, threadId, callId, entry }` (`entry` = the `LiveEntry` shape of `run://log`, via `ChatAgentSink` + `LiveEmitter`) and is persisted in `chat_agent_log` per call id (`get_chat_agent_log`) for rehydration. The Talk system prompt tells the model to delegate independent tasks with `Agent` and never emulate parallel sub-agents sequentially. Rendering: see "Crew card" and "Crew journal" under Tool-call cards. **Approval gate inside sub-agents:** a sub-agent's `run_command` that `dangerous_command` flags parks on the SAME approval card the parent turn uses (`ApprovalBroker`, shared by the parent loop and every sub-agent of the turn; the card's reason reads `Sub-agent “<description>”: <reason>`; each request has its own call id `<agent call id>:<n>`), honours the thread's "don't ask again" grant, and is denied by Stop together with the rest of the thread; a denial never touches the workspace and returns as an error tool_result telling the sub-agent not to retry (`chat_agents::SubagentGate` over `orchestrator::agentic::ToolGate`, a pre-execution hook `run_agentic_loop` now takes — DIRECT stages pass none, unattended by design). A sub-agent's commit, push or `gh pr create` meets the secret guard's card first, which the grant never answers (see "Secret guard › Talk's shell"). **A failed run keeps its spend (#1149):** a loop that errors after real rounds (retries exhausted, a context 400, a body that could not be read) returns them with the error (`run_agentic_loop_billed` → `LoopFailure { error, partial }`), so the outcome is `ok: false` with the report `Sub-agent failed: <error>` **and** those rounds' tokens, cost and transcript: the ledger, the thread receipt and the budget see the true spend (`record_subagent_spend`), an `escalate:` retry bills both attempts, and `persist_run` saves the transcript so the run can be continued from its crew journal (a failure before any round completes has nothing to continue). An errored run is not a turn cap: the cap gate does not ask for more turns (`AgentOutcome.errored`, `ran_out_of_turns`). **Spend limit per sub-agent:** with a budget set, the fan-out gives each sub-agent its share of the budget headroom (`db::budget_headroom` ÷ the number of sub-agents in the response, `budget_share`) as the loop's `spend_limit`, so a looping sub-agent stops at its share before the director's next budget check; a definition's `max-cost` caps it further (`subagent_spend_limit`, the lower of the two). Past the limit the round's tool calls are voided and the forced close answers; the report is flagged "reached its spend limit before finishing — this report may be incomplete", and the cap gate does not ask for more turns (`spend_stopped`). The limit, `max-cost` included, is a total for the run: an escalation retry (`escalation_retry`) and each continuation the cap gate grants get only what the attempts so far left of it (`spend_left`), and none starts once it is spent (`has_spend_left`) — the user grants turns, not money. No budget, or a turn sent with the budget override, leaves sub-agents unbounded. A continuation from the crew journal gets the whole headroom at that moment. Known v1 limit: concurrent sub-agents that write share the worktree (as in Claude Code). _Support:_ `chat_agents.rs`, `chat_engine.rs` fan-out pre-pass + `agent_input_for_display`, `db.rs` (`chat_agent_log`, `append_chat_agent_log`, `list_chat_agent_log`), `commands::get_chat_agent_log`, `lib/ipc.ts` (`getChatAgentLog`, `CHAT_AGENT_LOG_EVENT`).
- **Agent definitions (`.claude/agents/*.md` → `subagent_type`)** — The same files that define Claude Code's named sub-agents drive Octopush's, nothing else to set up: `scan_agent_definitions` reads `<worktree>/.claude/agents/*.md` (project) and `~/.claude/agents/*.md` (user; project shadows user shadows the **built-in library** below on a name clash), read like skills (see "Skill discovery": a project file that resolves outside the project, or one over 4 MiB, is skipped unread; agents have no list in the UI, so a skipped one is logged, once per path, `agent <name> skipped: outside the project`), parsing the Claude Code frontmatter — `name`, `description`, `tools` (Claude Code names mapped onto the workspace tools: Read→`read_file`, Write→`write_file`, Edit/MultiEdit→`edit_file`, Bash→`run_command`, Grep, Glob, LS→`list_files`; scoped grants like `Bash(git:*)` count as the base tool; `mcp__…` entries become the definition's MCP grant — see "MCP tools inside sub-agents"; a list that maps to nothing leaves the full set, unless it carries MCP entries, in which case it is MCP-only), `model` (an id; a **tier** `fast`/`balanced`/`strong` or its Claude Code alias `haiku`/`sonnet`/`opus`, resolved through the user's tier map in Settings › Models, then by substring over the configured ids; `inherit`/no match → the conversation's model — `resolve_model_with_tiers`, `tier_for_alias`) — plus keys Claude Code does not read — **`escalate: <tier or model>`** (see "Sub-agent escalation" below) and **`max-cost: 0.50`** (USD, `$0.50` also reads; also `max_cost`/`maxCost`; zero, negative or garbage is no cap): the most one run of that type may spend, across its escalation retry and continuations, before it closes with what it has, the lower of it and the run's budget share applying (see "Sub-agents › Spend limit per sub-agent") — and the body as the agent's instructions. The `Agent` tool description **enumerates the defined types** (`- name: description`) and the `subagent_type` schema names them, as Claude Code's Agent tool does. When a call's `subagent_type` matches (case-sensitive, then case-insensitive), the sub-agent runs with the definition's body appended to its system prompt (`# Agent: name`), restricted to its `tools` (via `run_agentic_loop`'s allowlist, implied grants included), on `pick_subagent_model`'s choice: the call's `model` › the definition's `model`, each resolved the same way (an `Agent` call may ask for `model: "fast"` directly — the tool schema recommends a tier over an id), an unresolvable spec inherits with a warning instead of failing the start › the conversation's model. An unknown `subagent_type` stays a plain role hint. `list_subagent_types` (`ipc.listSubagentTypes`) returns the picker-sized metas for a future UI. The shared frontmatter splitter (`skills::split_frontmatter`) now backs both SKILL.md and agent files. _Support:_ `skills/agents.rs` (`parse_agent_definition`, `map_tools`, `resolve_model`, `find_agent_definition`), `chat_agents.rs` (`agent_tool_definitions(defs)`, `subagent_system_prompt(…, definition)`, `pick_subagent_model`), `chat_engine.rs` fan-out, `commands::list_subagent_types`. Known v1 limit: concurrent sub-agents that write share the worktree (as in Claude Code); the approval gate and the spend limit inside sub-agents are described above. _Support:_ `chat_agents.rs`, `chat_engine.rs` fan-out pre-pass + `agent_input_for_display`, `db.rs` (`chat_agent_log`, `append_chat_agent_log`, `list_chat_agent_log`), `commands::get_chat_agent_log`, `lib/ipc.ts` (`getChatAgentLog`, `CHAT_AGENT_LOG_EVENT`).
- **Built-in tiered agent library (the economy director's crew)** — Octopush ships seven definitions (`skills::builtin_agents`, source `builtin`), each an ordinary Claude Code agent file a project can copy out of `BUILTIN_AGENT_FILES` and override by name: **`explorer`** (fast, read-only: maps code, answers one question, ≤300-word report with `path:line` evidence), **`ticket-reader`** (fast, never edits files, every MCP tool the workspace configures (`mcp__*`) plus the shell for `gh`/`curl`: turns a ticket into a compact brief so the raw JSON never enters the director's context), **`test-runner`** (fast: runs the named tests, reports pass/fail with the failing excerpts, never fixes), **`implementer`** (balanced, full tools, `escalate: strong`: implements a handed plan, runs the relevant tests, reports per-file changes), **`reviewer`** (strong, never edits files, keeps the shell for git: adversarial review of a diff in a fresh context — the quality gate), **`pr-author`** (fast: title + body from the diff, `gh pr create`), **`pr-maintainer`** (balanced, `escalate: strong`: addresses each review comment with a change or a reply, fixes this PR's red checks, pushes with a merge). `explorer` is read-only (no shell); `reviewer`, `test-runner` and `ticket-reader` never receive `write_file`/`edit_file` but keep `run_command` for git, tests and `gh`. **No built-in carries `max-turns`** (the second key Claude Code does not read; `AgentDefinition.max_turns`, parsed from `max-turns`/`max_turns` in a project or user file, zero or garbage = none): a sub-agent runs until it finishes unless the user configures a limit — the **Limit sub-agent tool turns** preference, or a copied-out definition's own `max-turns`, which applies under a set preference (`subagent_iterations`). A run cut at a configured cap is continuable from its journal (see "Sub-agent thread"). Listed by `list_subagent_types` like any definition. _Support:_ `skills/builtin_agents.rs` (`builtin_agent_definitions`), `skills/agents.rs::scan_agent_definitions`.
- **Sub-agent escalation (`escalate:` in a definition)** — When a sub-agent's first attempt **fails** — no usable report (`should_escalate`; a report merely cut off at the turn cap is still a report, and a `blocked` stop is a question for the director that a stronger model cannot answer either, so neither escalates; nor does a run its spend limit stopped, or one with nothing left of that limit, since the strong tier would spend more) — and its definition names an `escalate` tier/model that resolves (`escalation_model`, same rules as `model`) to a *different* model than the attempt ran on, the fan-out reruns it **once** on that model with the original prompt plus a bounded excerpt of how the cheap attempt ended (`escalation_prompt`: "don't trust its conclusions"; a writing role — write/edit/shell tools — is told the tree may already hold the attempt's partial changes: `git status`/`git diff` first, never the same edit twice; `spec_can_write`) — the cascade pattern: cheap first where verification is cheap, strong only when needed. Each attempt gets the full sub-agent turn bound (none unless configured). The sub-agent's journal gets a notice (`escalating to <model>: the <model> attempt failed / hit its turn limit / stopped on a question`); a director Stop cancels the retry. The outcome folds both attempts (`merge_escalated`: the strong attempt's report and ending, both attempts' tokens/cost/duration, `escalatedFrom`, `attempts[]`), and the ledger records **each attempt at its own model's price** (`billed_attempts`). The crew row shows an `escalated` tag (tooltip: from which model to which). DIRECT stages had per-stage escalation already; this is Talk's. _Support:_ `chat_agents.rs` (`should_escalate`, `escalation_model`, `escalation_prompt`, `merge_escalated`, `AgentAttempt`, `run_attempt`), `chat_engine.rs` fan-out ledger loop, `chat/CrewCard.tsx`.
- **Auto policy — the economy director** — The composer's model picker offers **Auto** above the models (`ModelPicker autoOption`; chip reads `Auto · <strong model>`, the row says "director on <model>" or "strong tier not mapped"). Sending with `model: "auto"` (`AUTO_MODEL`) makes the backend run the turn on the **strong tier's model** (`director_model_for_auto`: the tier must be mapped to a configured id, else the send fails with "Auto needs the strong tier mapped … Settings › Models › Model tiers") under the **lean-context doctrine** appended to the Talk system prompt (`director_doctrine(unmapped)`: every broad read — code mapping, many files, test suites, tickets, diffs — goes to sub-agents, several per response, compact reports back; never paste long output into your own context; recall stored output instead of re-reading; agent types by role and tier; always run the `reviewer` before a PR; keep judgment — architecture, trade-offs, the user's real ask — for yourself), and a sub-agent that names **no** model or type runs on the **fast** tier (`AUTO_SUBAGENT_TIER`, `SubagentSpec.policy_auto`; it was balanced until the A/B showed a mid-tier model given a vague task runs 6–9 minutes and costs more than the director's cached rounds — a sub-agent's cost is its loop length, not its per-token price) instead of inheriting the director's strong model (an explicit `model: inherit` still means the director). The doctrine's rule is **one sub-agent, one question, always typed**: narrow questions, several per response when independent; the fast roles are capped at 15 turns and a task that needs more was two questions; only `implementer`/`pr-maintainer` write; never re-verify what a sub-agent reported; a report cut at its cap is partial, not lost — the user can give that sub-agent more turns from its journal, so the director says what is still open instead of re-delegating from scratch. The doctrine only promises what the tier map delivers: when `fast` or `balanced` is unmapped (`unmapped_subagent_tiers`) it says so, so the director knows those roles run on the conversation's model at its price until Settings › Models maps them. The resolved model id is what every downstream row, price and event sees; per-message model overrides remain available in the same picker. The doctrine rests on a structural fact: Talk rebuilds history as text each turn, so a per-message model switch costs one cache-prefix rewrite, never a lost session. _Support:_ `chat_agents.rs` (`AUTO_MODEL`, `AUTO_DIRECTOR_TIER`, `AUTO_SUBAGENT_TIER`, `director_model_for_auto`, `director_doctrine`, `pick_subagent_model`), `chat_engine.rs::send_agentic` (Auto resolution at the top), `lib/policy.ts`, `ModelPicker.tsx`, `chat/Composer.tsx`.
- **Tier mix on the crew card** — The aggregate line ends with the crew's **share of tokens per tier** (`72% fast · 28% strong`, largest-remainder rounded to 100, via `tierMix`/`formatTierMix` over each row's `tier` — the tier the call or definition asked for when the model is that tier's, else the tier its model is mapped to in Settings › Models; `tier_for_outcome`/`tier_of_model`), shown once any row maps to a tier: the director's receipt for how much of the work ran cheap. _Support:_ `lib/policy.ts`, `chat/CrewCard.tsx::crewSummary`, `skills/agents.rs::tier_of_model`, `AgentOutcome.tier`.
- **Thread-attributed ledger** — Every Talk spend row carries the thread it belongs to and who spent it: `spend_events.thread_id` + `origin` (`director` for the turn's own rounds, `subagent:<tool call id>` for each sub-agent attempt; `token_engine::record_in_thread`, `ChatEngine::record_usage` / `record_subagent_spend`). `db::thread_cost(thread_id, strong_prices)` folds a thread's rows into `ThreadCost { spentUsd, subagentsUsd, baselineUsd, strongPriced, calls, cacheHitPct }` — the Companion's conversation cost and the A/B the economy director is judged by (see "Companion · Conversation"). Index `idx_spend_thread`. _Support:_ `db.rs`, `token_engine.rs`, `chat_engine.rs`, `commands::get_thread_cost`.
- **Cache-aware turn accounting** — A turn's assistant row is priced per round with its own cache split (`TurnUsage::add` → `cost_for(model, in, out, cache_read, cache_write)`, summed), instead of the old `cost_for(total_uncached_input, total_output)` that undercounted cache-heavy turns; the row also stores `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_creation_tokens` and **`context_tokens`** (the last prompt's full size) via `set_chat_message_usage`, and `chat://message-added` carries them. The answer's footer reads **`211k in · 94% cached · 2.1k out · $0.42`** (`usageFooter`: the last prompt's size, the share of the turn's prompt tokens served from the cache, the answer tokens, the turn's cost; tooltip explains each). _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs` (`TurnUsage`, `insert_and_emit_priced`), `db.rs` (`chat_messages` columns), `ChatMessage.tsx`.
- **Persisted errors** — Provider/loop errors saved as `role="error"` rows with the failure's kind in the nullable `error_kind` column (`ChatEngine::fail_turn` → `Db::set_chat_error_kind`, `ProviderErrorKind::as_str`: `rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `server_error`, `network`, `auth`, `bad_request`, `spend_cap`, `other`; also on `chat://message-added` as `errorKind`; rows from before it, and the turn-limit error, have none and read as `other`). Each renders as a rouge card that says what happened in words ("The model is overloaded.", "Your API spend limit is reached. Waiting won't lift it.", "The API key is missing or was refused.", "The turn ended on an error."), then what of the turn is kept ("Work up to round 14 is kept.", counting the turn's tool rounds back to its ask; "Your message is kept." with none), then the provider's text, and one upright-serif action for its kind (`data-tour="talk-error-action"`): **Try again** for a transient failure whose retries ran out (only on the thread's last row, while no turn runs), which continues the turn from the thread as it is (`chatStore.continueTurn` → `send_chat_message` with `regenerate: true`, nothing truncated, no new user row; the failed turn's narration and tool results ride on its ask, `build_history` / `transcript::build`); **Configure API key** for an auth failure (a missing Anthropic key is one too); **Copy error details** for anything else, or where the kind's action can't run. A refused send that never became a row (the banner) offers the key when its text names the API key, otherwise its details. A failed turn shows exactly ONE card: the transient banner is suppressed when the post-failure resync brings in a persisted error row with the same text (chatStore `runTurn` catch). _Support:_ `ChatCanvas` `ErrorBlock`, `lib/talkError.ts`.
- **Command check — which agent commands ask (`dangerous_command`)** — An agent `run_command` (the director's or a sub-agent's) parks on the approval card when this heuristic flags it. It is a net before an irreversible step, not a shell parser or a sandbox: a benign command that merely contains a flagged string may ask, and a command built at run time can pass. It flags: a recursive force delete (`rm -rf`, `rm -r -f`, long flags); a force push (`-f`, any `--force…` flag such as `--force-with-lease=…` or `--force-if-includes`, or a `+refspec` such as `+main` or `+HEAD:main`, #1147); a remote delete (`git push --delete`, `-d`, or a `:branch` refspec: "deletes a remote branch or tag (git push)"); `git clean -f`; `find … -delete`; a pipe into a shell (`| sh`, `| /bin/bash`, `| env bash`); a downloaded script run through process substitution or `-c` (`bash <(curl …)`, `source <(curl …)`, `. <(wget …)`, `bash -c "$(curl …)"`, `eval "$(curl …)"`: "runs a downloaded script"); a raw-disk write; `sudo`; `mkfs`; a fork bomb (a function that pipes itself into itself in the background and is then called, any name and spacing, `is_fork_bomb`); `git reset --hard`; a recursive `chmod`/`chown` (`-R` anywhere after the program, or `--recursive`; `chmod -r`, which removes read permission, doesn't count); and a `curl` upload of a dotfile or credentials file (#1147): `-d @f` (or `-d@f`), any `--data…` but `--data-raw`, `--data-urlencode name@f`, `--json @f`, `-F name=@f`, `-F name=<f`, `--form`, `-T f` and `--upload-file f`, where the path has a component starting with a dot (`.env`, `~/.ssh/…`, `.aws/credentials`) or a name the secret guard calls sensitive (`id_rsa`, `*.pem`; `secret_scan::is_sensitive_name`), or standard input (`@-`, `-T -`) when the line feeds it such a file (`< .env`, `cat ~/.aws/credentials |`): "uploads a dotfile or credentials file (curl)". **Nested commands are checked on their own (#1147):** the body of every top-level `$(…)`, `<(…)` and `>(…)`, every backtick span, and the string a shell runs with `-c` (`bash -c "…"`, `sh -ec '…'`, `/bin/zsh -lc …`), one level at a time (`nested_commands`, one pass over each level), to 4 levels and 64 nested commands in all (`MAX_COMMAND_NESTING`, `MAX_NESTED_COMMANDS`; the walk is `each_command`, which the path check of #1201 shares). Past either cap it asks, "nests more commands than the check reads (over 4 deep or 64 in all)", so the check stays linear in the command's length and can't hold up a turn or Stop. Each word has its quotes, a leading `\` and a subshell's parens dropped (`shell_word`), and a command word is matched by its basename, so `/bin/rm` counts as `rm` and `/usr/bin/find` as `find` (`command_name`). Flags still count only within their own command of a chain (`rm -r a && rm -f b` doesn't ask). User-typed `$` commands are never checked (only the secret guard sees them). _Support:_ `chat_engine::{dangerous_command, nested_commands, shell_word, command_name, uploads_dotfile, stdin_from_dotfile, is_fork_bomb, danger_regexes}`.

### Tool-call cards (icon + LABEL)
- **Built-in tools** — `run_command` (bash in workspace dir, exit-code annotation; stdout and stderr merged in the order their lines arrive, each stderr line tagged `[stderr]`, an unfinished line waiting for its newline, `MergedOutput` in `wait_command_bounded`; a long output keeps its **head and tail** with a `… [N chars omitted …]` marker between them, 70/30 when the command succeeded and 30/70 when it failed (by its exit code), so the failing assertion and the summary at the end survive, `chat_history::command_excerpt`. Talk captures up to 4 MB of it (`COMMAND_KEEP_BYTES`, in the shared shell's agent capture `TalkShell::run` and in `run_command_kept` for the sandboxed and fallback paths); past 50 KB (`COMMAND_SHOWN_BYTES`) the tool row keeps the head+tail copy, the whole capture goes to `chat_tool_originals` for recall (`db.set_chat_tool_original_within`), and the model's copy names the row: `call recall_tool_output with message_id N`, within the v2 view cap too, `chat_engine::cut_command_output`, `command_model_copy`. Sub-agents and API-substrate Direct stages read the 50 KB head+tail copy (`execute_tool_cancellable`); a `$` command's card keeps 50 KB, head and tail), `read_file` (100k truncation, the line numbers and the truncation note included; each line reaches the model led by its number, right-aligned in six columns and a tab, the `cat -n` layout, counted from `offset` in a window, `number_lines`; lines are shown without their `\r`), `write_file` (creates parent dirs, overwrites; **never blind**, #1165: a file that already exists is refused with "Error: … already exists and you haven't read it yet" until the agent read it, and with "Error: … changed on disk since you last read it" when it changed after the agent last read or wrote it, so an edit the user made while a turn runs isn't clobbered; a new file is written as before. Each successful read, write or edit records the file's mtime, size and SHA-256 by canonical path; the same size and mtime count as unchanged, otherwise the hash decides, so a touch alone doesn't refuse. The hashing runs off the async runtime and outside the record's lock, which is held only to look a file up or store it. Talk keeps one record per thread in memory (`ChatEngine.file_seen`, checked and updated on the blocking pool, `refusal_off_thread`, `note_off_thread`), each sub-agent and API-substrate Direct stage one per loop (`orchestrator/agentic.rs`); a refused write isn't recorded as a file edit. _Support:_ `file_seen.rs`), `edit_file` (matches raw text first; when that fails and every line of `old_string` carries a read_file line-number prefix, it matches without them, and strips them from `new_string` too when every line of it carries one, `strip_line_numbers`; in a file with CRLF line ends, a multi-line string copied from that view matches with its `\r` restored, in `new_string` too, `edit_from_view`), `list_files`, `grep`, `glob`. In Talk a file tool whose target resolves outside the workspace asks first, and so does a `run_command` that names such a path (see "What asks before it runs"). _Support:_ `tool_definitions()` + `execute_tool` (chat_engine), `talk_guard`.
- **`recall_tool_output` (Talk-only)** — Earlier turns' tool results reach the model abridged (see "History → provider context"); this tool returns the full stored output of a `[Tool #id: …]` row by `message_id`, with optional `offset`/`limit` char paging (default 40k, max 100k per call, a `(chars a-b of total)` header when windowed; on a `talkEngine: "v2"` turn at most the per-result cap less 200 chars, `transcript::recall_limit`). With `block` it returns block N (1-based) of an earlier ask's `@` context instead, by the ask's `message_id` (`db.get_chat_sent_context`, `chat_history::context_block`; "No context block N on message M in this conversation" otherwise). A cut `run_command` output recalls the whole capture (up to 4 MB, paged), an MCP output its original; a row with neither (every row written before) recalls its `result` as before (`chat_history::recall_source`). Scoped to the current thread (`db.get_chat_tool_output`), read-only, added after a skill's `allowed-tools` filter so no skill loses it. The system prompt tells the model to recall rather than re-run. _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs` (`recall_tool_definition`, `ChatEngine::recall_tool_output`), `chat_history::window_text`.
- **Crew card (a response's sub-agents as one surface)** — Adjacent `Agent`/`Task` tool rows of one response are grouped by `buildTimeline` into a single `crew` item, and every in-flight `Agent` call of the running turn renders as one live crew card (they run concurrently) that retires as the resolved rows land. Header: `Bot` icon, `CREW · N` eyebrow, `StageDots` (one dot per sub-agent: running verdigris with a faint halo / done verdigris / failed rouge), an aggregate line (`2 running · 3 done · 1 failed · 61k tokens · $0.42` — only the parts that apply), collapsible via the grid-rows `Reveal`. One row per sub-agent (`.octo-rise-in`): status dot, role glyph (`iconForRole(subagentType)`), description, role, the **live activity line** (`lastActivity` over its `chat://agent-log` entries), a `stopped` / `turn limit` / `needs a decision` ending flag (`data-tour="talk-crew-ending"`), tokens · status · duration (elapsed ticks every 250ms from the backend `startedAt`; reduced motion computes once per render). **Beacon law:** exactly ONE row pulses brass while the crew runs — the longest-running sub-agent (`beaconCallId`, FIFO like the fleet beacon); the others hold a static dot. Clicking a row's title opens its work journal in the Companion (`focusCrewAgent` + `ensureAgentLog`, `aria-pressed` on the focused row); a finished row's `ScrollText` button unfolds its report inline (mono `<pre>`, 256px cap). `recall_tool_output` still renders as a plain `RECALL #id` tool card. The Player reads a running crew as **Delegating…** (`ROLES.delegate`). _Support:_ `chat/CrewCard.tsx` (`crewAgentsFromTools`, `crewAgentsFromLive`, `beaconCallId`, `crewSummary`), `ChatCanvas.tsx`, `chatStore` (`crew` timeline item, `agentLogByCall` fed by `chat://agent-log` and capped at 400 entries in memory, `crewFocusByWs`, `ensureAgentLog` → `getChatAgentLog`), `lib/agentTools.ts` (`isAgentToolName`, `CHAT_AGENT_LOG_EVENT` — store-free so leaf components can import them), `chat/OctoStatus.tsx`, `OctoPlayer.tsx`.
- **Crew journal — the sub-agent's room (Companion, Talk)** — While a sub-agent is focused the Talk Companion **is** that sub-agent: a `‹` back control returns to the Chats/Conversation sections; the eyebrow bar carries `Crew journal` and the status word (`running` / `continuing` in brass, `failed` in rouge, `stopped` in mute); then the sub-agent's description (serif), a mono meta line (`role · model · status · tokens · $cost · duration`, with `stopped` / `done · turn limit` / `needs a decision` endings and `· continued` after a continuation), the **report** (Markdown, scrollable), then `work journal · N` rendered by the same `JournalItems` the Direct stage focus uses (extracted from `StageFocus`), so a sub-agent's evidence reads exactly like a stage's. Live entries stream in; a finished sub-agent's journal is loaded from `chat_agent_log` on focus when nothing is in memory (a reload, a thread switch). Empty states: "Waiting for the first entry." while running, "No journal was kept for this sub-agent." otherwise. Resolves the focused agent from the thread's tool rows first, then live tools (`findCrewAgent`); a focus that no longer resolves renders nothing. _Support:_ `CompanionCrewJournal.tsx`, `Companion.tsx` (talk branch), `direct/JournalItems.tsx`.
- **Sub-agent thread: reply / more turns (continuation)** — A finished sub-agent's room ends in a small composer stuck to the panel's foot: a textarea (`Reply to this sub-agent…`, or `Answer the sub-agent…` when it stopped on a question), a `turns` select (**no limit** / 5 / 15 / 30, default no limit) and a serif phrase — `Let it finish` (no limit), `Give it 15 more turns`, `Reply and continue`, `Answer and continue` / `Continue without an answer` for a blocked run (`continueLabel`; ⌘↵ submits). It calls `continue_subagent(call_id, instruction?, extra_turns)`: the backend loads the run saved in **`chat_agent_runs`** (`call_id`, thread, workspace, the row's `message_id`, the `SubagentSpec` as JSON, the **transcript as the loop left it** — for a blocked run including the asking turn and its `ask_tool_use_id`, `persist_run` after every run) and resumes it on the **model that wrote the transcript** with the same approval gate and MCP grants (`run_one_subagent`, shared with the fan-out; never escalates), the note appended into the trailing tool result (`resume_messages_for_continuation`) or, for a blocked run, the message as the `ask_director` answer (`resume_messages_for_answered_block`); `extra_turns` null = no turn limit on the continuation (the `continuation_note` says so: "You have no turn limit — take the tool turns the work needs"); a number the user picked is honored as is, at least 1. Spend is recorded under the same `subagent:<call id>` origin. When it ends the tool row is **rewritten in place** — the continued report replaces the old one, the meta folds both runs (`merge_continued_meta`: tokens/cost/duration/tool calls summed, `attempts[]` appended, `continued: true`) and its verdict restamped from how the continuation ended (`restamp_continued`, so a stopped run let finish no longer reads as stopped) — and `chat://message-updated {workspaceId, threadId, id, content}` replaces the row by id in the store (`continuingCalls` cleared), so the director's **next turn reads the continued report from history**; a quiet `stopped` note marks it in the thread (`Sub-agent “X” was given 15 more turns — its report was updated.` / `was given the turns it needed` / `was answered and given …`). While it runs the crew row and the room read `continuing` (the room shows a brass pulse and the live journal; `chat://tool-start` on a call id that already has a resolved row marks it continuing instead of opening a second card; Stop on the thread cancels it when no turn is live). Errors (no saved run — a row from before continuations; row or thread deleted) show under the composer. When an assistant answer already follows the row (`directorAnsweredAfter`), the composer says so: the director already went on with this report; a continuation updates it for the next turn and may clash with what the director did since. A row that was continued carries a brass `continued` flag on the crew card. _Support:_ `CompanionCrewJournal.tsx`, `chatStore` (`continueSubagent`, `continuingCalls`, `continueErrorByCall`, `chat://message-updated`), `chat/CrewCard.tsx`, `chat_engine.rs::continue_subagent` (`continuation_note`, `merge_continued_meta`), `chat_agents.rs` (`run_one_subagent`, `persist_run`, `SubagentSpec.resume`, `AgentOutcome.transcript/ask_tool_use_id/continued`), `db.rs` (`chat_agent_runs`, `upsert_chat_agent_run`, `get_chat_agent_run`, `set_chat_agent_run_message`, `update_chat_message_content`), `commands::continue_subagent`.
- **A plan per sub-agent — model · tier · effort, decided before the run and shown from its first second** — At fan-out every `Agent` call is planned (`chat_agents::plan_subagent` → `SubagentPlan { model, tier, effort, askedModel, askedHonored }`) before its live card opens: the resolved model id (never the alias the director wrote), the tier it maps to, and the **effort** it runs at — the definition's `effort:` frontmatter (a third key Claude Code does not read: `low` … `max`) or the tier's default (`default_effort_for_tier`: fast → `low`, balanced → `medium`, strong → `high`; a model outside every tier gets none, i.e. the API default). The plan rides on `chat://tool-start` and the persisted row (`agent_input_for_display`: `model`, `tier`, `effort`, `askedModel`, `askedHonored`), so the crew row reads `implementer · sonnet-4-6 · medium` (`runLine`, `shortModel`; tooltip names the tier) while the run is still going, and the journal's meta line carries `role · model · tier · effort · status`. The journal also opens with a notice `running on <model> · <tier> · effort <level>` (again on an escalation, with the stronger model's tier default). Before this, sub-agents sent no thinking parameter at all — on Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 that is the API's own default of adaptive thinking at `high`, for an explorer as much as for a reviewer. `run_subagent_core` passes the plan's effort into `run_agentic_loop`; a continuation keeps the saved model. _Support:_ `chat_agents.rs` (`SubagentPlan`, `plan_subagent`, `plan_line`, `default_effort_for_tier`), `skills/agents.rs` (`effort`), `chat_engine.rs` (fan-out planning, `agent_plans`), `chat/CrewCard.tsx`, `CompanionCrewJournal.tsx`.
- **Under Auto a typed role keeps its tier** — The director may not lift a typed sub-agent above its definition's tier with the call's `model`: `implementer` + `model: "strong"` (or the strong model's id) still runs balanced under Auto, the plan records `askedModel: "strong"`, `askedHonored: false`, the crew row shows a brass `asked strong` flag (tooltip: "under Auto a typed role keeps its tier") and the journal says so; the escalation to strong still happens when the cheap attempt fails — that is what it is for. The ceiling is judged on the outcome, not the wording: `strong`, the strong model's id and `inherit` (the director's model, which under Auto is the strong tier even when unmapped) all stay balanced; a definition whose `model` is an id rather than an alias gets its tier from the tier map. Asking *down* (`model: "fast"` on an implementer) is honored, as is any ask outside Auto (the user chose the model) and any ask on an untyped call (no role to keep); an honored ask that differs from the resolved id shows as a sage `asked <x>` flag. The doctrine now says: never pass `model` on a typed call; the role carries its tier and effort; if the user names a model, say so in the prompt. _Support:_ `chat_agents.rs::plan_subagent` (`tier_rank`), `DOCTRINE`, `chat/CrewCard.tsx`.
- **Effort reaches Opus 5 and Haiku 5.5, and `low` is really low** — The Anthropic adapter's effort-path allowlist now includes `opus-5` and `haiku-5` (they were missing, so every effort setting was silently dropped on them — Direct stages and fast-tier sub-agents included — and the API default applied); both also accept `xhigh`. On a budget-thinking model (Opus 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5) `Effort::Low` now sends **no** thinking params instead of a 4k budget: the fast tier's sub-agents must not pay for thinking the model never had on its own; `medium` and up still buy a budget. This applies to Direct stages too: a stage set to `low` on Haiku 4.5 no longer thinks. The resolved row and the journal show the effort of the final attempt (`AgentOutcome.effort`), so an escalated run reads `opus-5 · high`, not the cheap attempt's `medium`. _Support:_ `providers/anthropic.rs` (`is_effort_model`, `supports_xhigh`, `thinking_json`).
- **Limit sub-agent tool turns (Settings › General) — off by default, no limit** — Sub-agents have **no turn limit unless one is configured**: a sub-agent runs until it finishes or is stopped, so the director never builds on a report cut mid-work (a crew that "reported turn limit" while the director went on with it was the failure this retires). `settings.subagent_max_turns` (`subagentMaxTurns`) is `null`/unset by default = unlimited (`chat_history::effective_subagent_max_iterations` → `None`; `SubagentSpec.max_iterations: Option<usize>`, `None` runs the loop unbounded); a set value is clamped 5–200 like the Talk turns and a definition's `max-turns` applies under it (`subagent_iterations`: definition ∧ preference, either alone when the other is unset, `None` when both are). Separate from the director's own "Limit tool turns per message", which is off by default too. The row under Settings › General › Talk is a **switch** "Limit sub-agent tool turns" (`GeneralPane` `LimitTurnsRow`, `subagent-turns-row-switch`, `settings/shared.tsx` `Switch`): off = no limit; on writes 25 and reveals a `rounds` stepper (`Reveal`, grid-rows collapse; `Sub-agent tool turns` aria-label), off again writes `null`. _Support:_ `settings.rs`, `chat_history.rs`, `chat_engine.rs` (spec build), `chat_agents.rs`, `settings/GeneralPane.tsx`.
- **Turn-limit gate — a writing sub-agent never hands the director half-done work** — When a sub-agent that can **edit files** (`spec_edits_files`: `write_file`/`edit_file` in its tools, or no definition at all — `implementer`, `pr-maintainer`, an untyped call, a custom definition with Write/Edit; the shell alone does not count, so `test-runner`, `ticket-reader`, `pr-author` and `reviewer` keep their bash and are never gated) runs out of turns mid-work (`ran_out_of_turns`: closed at the cap or unfinished, with a transcript, not a question — only possible when a limit is configured, since by default a sub-agent has none), the fan-out **pauses the director's turn** on an inline card instead of returning the partial report: `chat://subagent-cap {workspaceId, threadId, callId, description, subagentType, turnsUsed}` → `SubagentCapCard` (brass `Hourglass`, "Turn limit reached · the director is waiting", the sub-agent's description and role, a `turns` select 15 / 25 / 50 and the phrase `Give it N more turns`, or `Accept what it has`). The answer (`respond_subagent_cap(call_id, extra_turns?)` → `CapGate::respond`) either resumes the run **inside the same turn** on its saved transcript (`resume_messages_for_continuation` + `continuation_note`, same model, same approval gate and MCP grants, `merge_continued` folds spend/duration/attempts, `continued: true`) — and asks again if it runs out again, as many rounds as the user grants — or accepts the partial report, which then reaches the director marked as such. The journal gets a notice at each step (`hit its N-turn limit mid-work — waiting for you`, `given N more turns`, `partial report accepted by the user`). The answer is a `CapAnswer` — `More(n)`, `Accept`, `Stopped` (Stop on the thread, `CapGate::deny_thread` from `ChatEngine::cancel`), `Timeout` (no answer in 30 minutes, `CAP_GATE_TIMEOUT`) — and the journal names which it was; only `Accept` is logged as the user's acceptance. A continuation that never ran (provider error, could not start) keeps the first run's report, ending and resume point (`merge_continued` with an empty second transcript) and says so in the report, so the gate can ask again. The card counts every budget already spent (`turns_used`: an escalated run took two). A reloaded webview re-reads the cards still waiting when it opens a thread (`pending_subagent_caps(thread_id)` → `CapGate::pending_for_thread`, `chatStore` `rehydrateCaps` on `loadHistory`/`selectThread`), because the parked turn outlives the view; deleting a thread drops its cards. The fan-out's concurrency permit stays held while a card waits, so in a crew larger than 8 a waiting card also holds back the queued ones — the whole turn is parked anyway. Read-only roles are not gated: a partial map is information, not a half-done tree, and the director handles it. There is deliberately **no automatic extension** — a silent extra round only moves the same problem later; the user decides. The doctrine tells the director that a report marked incomplete was the user's choice: do not build on it, say what is done and what is not, and stop. The `chat://subagent-cap` event also pings the workspace rail when another workspace is active. _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs` (`CapGate`, `SubagentCapEvent`, `respond_subagent_cap`), `chat_agents.rs` (`run_one_subagent` gate loop, `ran_out_of_turns`, `merge_continued`), `chatStore` (`pendingCapsByWs`, `respondSubagentCap`), `chat/SubagentCapCard.tsx`, `chat/ChatCanvas.tsx`.
- **Narration — the model's reasoning in the open** — The text the model writes before a round's tool calls is persisted on the `assistant_tool_use` row (as before) **and emitted live** (`chat://message-added`), and the timeline renders it as a `narration` item (`buildTimeline`): a quiet sage line on the work block's hairline (`NarrationLine`, Markdown; see "Turns read apart"), never an answer bubble, so a turn of ten tool rounds reads as a train of thought ("the tests import X, so let me check…") instead of a black box. Rows that are pure bookkeeping (no lead text) stay hidden. Note: Talk sends no extended-thinking budget (`effort: None`); what was invisible was this narration, not hidden thinking. _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs` (the `assistant_tool_use` insert goes through `insert_and_emit_message`), `chatStore::buildTimeline`, `chat/WorkBlock.tsx::NarrationLine`.
- **Resolved tool card (a ledger row)** — One quiet row on the work block's hairline, no border and no fill: the tool's lucide icon (`iconForTool`, with a `title`; the retired `§` stays retired), the mono caps label (`RUN/READ/WRITE/EDIT/LIST/GREP…`, mute), the summary (mono sage, truncated, full text on its `title`), the `$`-command's cwd when it isn't the root, the row's actions, and a mute chevron that is always the last column, so the chevrons of a round line up. The label-and-summary part is the toggle (a `role="button"` with `aria-expanded`, named `LABEL summary`); the chevron is pointer decoration, not a second tab stop. A faint `--brass-faint` wash covers the whole row on hover, and focus rings are inset, so the work block's fold never clips them. It opens to the raw result as before: a mono `<pre>` (256px cap, **Show full output**) with a COPY affordance. See "Card actions" for the row's actions. **Its verdict:** a call that failed keeps the live row's rouge 6px dot on the hairline and a rouge mono meta after the summary, its exit code (`exit 101`) or a short reason (`timed out`, `stopped`, `failed`), titled in words ("Exited with code 101", "Timed out and was stopped", or "Failed: " and the first line of the result; `data-tour="talk-tool-verdict"`, on every such meta, so a tour finds the first); a denied one (the approval card or the secret guard said no, or the conversation has the tool's MCP server turned off) gets the same marks in mute, `denied`, titled with the denial's reason ("Denied, not run: the user declined to approve it (flagged: …)"); a call that passed carries nothing extra. The verdict is part of the toggle's accessible name (`RUN cargo test, Exited with code 101`) and the row's `data-outcome` (`ok` · `failed` · `denied`). It comes from the engine: every `role="tool"` row it writes now carries `ok`, `outcome` (`ok` · `failed` · `denied`), `exitCode` when the shell reported one, and `reason: "stopped"` when the engine stopped the call itself (Stop interrupting the agent's command, or the user stopping a `$` process, `ChatEngine::stop_shell`), so a stopped command reads as `stopped`, not as SIGINT's `exit 130` (`chat_engine::tool_row` → `stamp_outcome`, one builder for every call site; additive keys; the shell's `-1` "no status" is never recorded as a code). **What the engine stamped wins** over any reading of the text. Rows from before carry none, so their verdict is read from text the engine has always written at a fixed place, for `run_command` rows only: a **trailing** `(exit code N)` line other than 0 (the one-line 127 note may follow it; the shared shell's timeout note ends with `(exit code -1)`, so it counts too) and the `Command not run —` denials. Output that only mentions an exit line or a timeout sentence in the middle stays unmarked, and so does anything else, so an unknown is never shown as a failure (`lib/toolVerdict.ts`: `toolVerdict`, `exitCodeFromResult`, `verdictCounts`). Styles stay inline (react-markdown cascade leak) but are tokens only, colours and font stacks alike (`var(--font-mono)`, `var(--font-sans)`). _Support:_ `ToolCallCard.tsx`, `lib/toolVerdict.ts`, `chat_engine::{tool_row, stamp_outcome, ChatEngine::stop_shell}`, `commands::stop_shell_command`, `styles.css` (`.octo-ledger`, `.octo-ledger-head`, `.octo-ledger-actions`, `.octo-ledger-action`), `lib/roleIcons.ts`.
- **Live "running" tool card (a ledger row)** — Between `chat://tool-start`/`tool-end`, each running call is a ledger row like the resolved one (icon · label · summary, mute and sage) on the work hairline, with a fixed-width `running · 0:03` slot timed from the backend's real `startedAt` and a 6px status dot sitting **on** the hairline: verdigris with the calm `.octo-stage-pulse` ring while running (`.octo-stage-pulse-running`; a static halo under reduced motion; never brass, which pulses for what needs you), verdigris or rouge on `tool-end`. It retires by `callId` when the resolved row lands (no flash), so a running call settles into its row in place instead of jumping from a card. The live rows always render in one hairline wrapper after the timeline (`data-role="live-work"`), so a row never remounts as its work block appears; when the turn's work block is the last thing on screen, the wrapper closes the feed's gap (`-mt-6`) and continues its line, its rows flush under a round they will join or 2px under a narration line (the block's own gap), so a row resolves exactly where it ran. _Support:_ `LiveToolCard.tsx`, `chat/ChatCanvas.tsx`, `lib/roleIcons.ts`.
- **write_file body stripping** — Large `content` replaced with `(N chars, written to disk)` for both the live event and the persisted record. _Support:_ `input_for_display`.
- **Card actions** — A tool row's actions are 12px icons with a `title` and an accessible name, in their own slot just before the chevron, shown while the row is hovered or holds focus (they keep their room, so nothing moves; `.octo-ledger-actions`) and brass on hover. WRITE rows: **Open in editor** (`FilePen`), **Reveal in Finder** (`FolderOpen`), **Open in the default browser** (`ExternalLink`, for `.html`). `run_command` rows: **Send to terminal** (`Terminal`; switches to Run and copies the command). _Support:_ ToolCallCard; `navigateToFile`, `revealInFinder`, `openFileInSystem`, `handleRunInTerminal`.
- **File-edit attribution → Review** — `write_file` records `file_edits`; a git-status catch-all credits files changed via `run_command`, so Review can map a change to its agent message. _Support:_ `insert_file_edit`, `git_status_files`; `get_message`.

### Slash commands / Skills
- **`/skill` mentions — per message, several at once, nothing pinned** — A skill is invoked the way a file is referenced: a `/` at line start or after whitespace (anywhere in the message) opens the skill menu filtered by what follows (`findActiveSkillMention`, same trigger rules as `@file`; a query no skill matches closes it, so a `/etc` mid-sentence is left alone; Esc dismisses it; the catalog is re-read from `list_skills` each time the menu opens, so a skill added mid-session is offered; a skill file left unread, `list_skipped_skills`, is named below the skills, muted and not selectable, as `<dir> · skipped: outside the project` or `skipped: over 4 MiB`, matched by the same query (a query that matches only a skipped file keeps the menu open on its row), at most 20 and then "+N more skipped", with its path in the tooltip); Enter/Tab or a click inserts `/name ` at the caret (`applySkillMention`); a hand-typed `/name` works the same. Several skills may ride one message. While drafting, every standalone `/name` the worktree knows is painted with a brass wash *in the sentence* by a scroll-synced backdrop behind the textarea (`SkillHighlights`, same metrics as the textarea, transparent text, padded by the scrollbar width so wrapping stays in step on non-overlay scrollbars) — a skill reads as part of what you are writing, not as an attachment. In the sent message the tokens render as brass chips (`ChatMessage` + `splitBySkillTokens`, tooltip "Skill invoked with this message"). Nothing is pinned to the conversation: the next message starts clean, so a skill never rides on later turns unasked. A `$`-direct line never opens the menu; `/run cmd` is still the shell. The composer help reads "Invoke a skill with this message — several allowed, none sticks". _Support:_ `lib/skillMentions.ts` (`findActiveSkillMention`, `applySkillMention`, `skillTokens`, `extractSkillMentions`, `splitBySkillTokens`), `chat/Composer.tsx`, `chat/SkillHighlights.tsx`, `chat/SlashMenu.tsx`, `chatStore.skillNamesByWs` (`setSkillNames`, loaded by the composer from `list_skills`). The sticky "active skill" chip and `activeSkillByWs` are retired.
- **Skill effect on a turn** — The backend resolves the message's `/name` tokens against the worktree's known skills (`skills::referenced_skills`, the same resolver Direct briefs use: standalone tokens only, so `src/lib` or `and/or` never invoke one; a sentence-ending period closes a token, `/release.md` does not; fenced code blocks are never searched, so a file pasted by `@file` cannot invoke a skill its contents mention — the composer's highlight and the sent chips follow the same rules, `fencedRanges`), taking the turn's text from the last user row (so a regenerate re-invokes the same skills). Each invoked skill's SKILL.md body is appended to the system prompt under `# Skill: <name>` (`skill_prompt_section`, the shape Direct stages share) **for this turn only**. The skills a message or brief names are resolved in the order the text first names them (`referenced_skills`, by first mention, not by name), and their bodies share a cap of 100,000 bytes per turn or stage (`SKILLS_CAP_BYTES`, about 25k tokens) in that order: a body that fits what is left goes whole, a larger one is trimmed to it (beginning and end kept) under a `[Trimmed: …]` note, and with under 1,000 bytes left a skill is replaced by a `[Left out: …]` note; each cut is logged; `allowed-tools` is the union across the invoked skills, and a skill that declares none opens the full set; an allow-list matching no known tool keeps the full set with a warning. The skill the request pins (the legacy `ChatRequest.skill` field) comes first and is sent whole, bounded only by the 4 MiB a skill file may be; it doesn't draw on the named skills' budget, and if the message names it too it is sent once (`skill_prompt_section_with`). _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs` (skills block), `skills/mod.rs::referenced_skills`.
- **The model loads a skill on its own (`Skill`, #1135)** — Every Talk turn lists the worktree's skills (project ∪ user, project shadowing user) in the system prompt under `# Skills`, one line each, `- name: description`, after the project's instructions: sorted by name, each description on one line and cut at 300 characters, the first 50 (`SKILL_LIST_MAX`) and then "and N more, not listed here" (`skills::skill_list_section`). The list depends only on the skill files, so the cached system block holds until one changes. The skills the message names with `/name` (and a pinned `ChatRequest.skill`) are already in the prompt and left out of the list. When the worktree has any skill, the turn's tools carry `Skill { name }` (`skill_tool_definition`), whose bytes never change, after `recall_tool_output` and before `Agent`, whatever the message names. A call returns `# Skill: <name>`, the tools the skill allows (when it names them) and its SKILL.md body (bounded at 100,000 bytes, beginning and end kept) as the tool result, without the untrusted-output mark, since it's instructions to follow like a `/name` skill. An unknown or missing name is an error result naming the skills there are; a skill the message already named, or one already loaded this turn, answers that it's loaded instead of sending the body again (`skills::run_skill_tool`). **`allowed-tools` is checked when each call runs, not by narrowing the tool list,** so the tools stay byte-stable through the turn: after a loaded skill names its tools, a workspace tool outside the union of the loaded skills' lists is refused, before any approval card, with an error result that names the skill ("`write_file` was not run: the skill `audit` you loaded this turn allows only `read_file`…"); its row reads as denied. MCP, `Agent`, `recall_tool_output` and `Skill` calls are never limited, a loaded skill with no `allowed-tools` opens every tool again, and a list naming no workspace tool limits nothing, as on the mention path (`skills::SkillScope::refusal`). The scope lasts for the turn. **Sub-agents** get the same list (after the project's instructions) and the same tool, so a skill can call skills: `chat_agents::SkillSubagentTools` offers `Skill` before the MCP grant, and `SkillSubagentGate` refuses what a loaded skill doesn't allow ahead of the sub-agent's own gate, per run. The work timeline shows the call as a ledger row, book icon, `SKILL` and "used skill <name>" (`ToolCallCard` `summarizeTool`, `roleIcons.iconForTool`; a folded round reads `skill <name>`, `WorkBlock.roundSummary`). Claude Code plugins' skills and agents aren't discovered yet. _Support:_ `skills/mod.rs` (`SKILL_TOOL_NAME`, `skill_list_section`, `skill_tool_definition`, `run_skill_tool`, `SkillScope`), `chat_engine.rs` (skills block, tool loop), `chat_agents.rs` (`run_subagent_core`), `orchestrator/agentic.rs` (`model_copy`).
- **Skill discovery (project ∪ user)** — SKILL.md from `<worktree>/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` and `~/.claude/skills/*`; project shadows user; directories are read in name order. **Kept to the project:** the project's skills and agents are the repository's, read the way its `CLAUDE.md` is (`skills::definition_roots`, `skills::read_definition` over `request_context::read_memory_file`). Each file is resolved, symlinks included, and read only when it lands inside the nearest git work tree around the worktree (`request_context::nearest_work_tree`), so a linked `SKILL.md`, a linked skill directory, a linked `.claude/skills` or a linked agent file that points elsewhere on the Mac, or into an outer repository around the project, is skipped unread ("outside the project"); a link that stays inside is followed. A project in a subfolder of a repository reaches that repository. The user's own `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.claude/agents` are trusted and may link anywhere. A project whose `.claude/skills` or `.claude/agents` resolves to the user's own (home opened as a project, or a `.claude` linked to `~/.claude`) has no project root: those files are read, labelled (`~/.claude/…`) and sourced (`user`) as the user's. **Bounded reads, everywhere:** opened non-blocking, the open handle must be a regular file (`fstat`), so a FIFO or device is passed over without hanging; a file over 4 MiB is skipped ("over 4 MiB"); a file that isn't UTF-8 is still not a definition; frontmatter parsing is unchanged. Skipped entries are listed in the slash menu (skills) and logged once per path and reason (skills and agents, `skills::log_skipped`). _Support:_ `skills/mod.rs` (`scan_skills_in`, `DefinitionScan`, `SkippedDefinition`), `skills/agents.rs` (`scan_agent_files_in`), `commands::list_skipped_skills`.

### @-mentions (context)
- **`@` autocomplete** — Typing `@` opens the "Add context" popover; arrow/Enter/Tab/Esc nav. Rows: `diff` and the first Run session on an empty query (every session for `@ses…`, filtered after `@session:`; ranked files after `@diff:`), then folders (`src/lib/`, ranked by their own name) and files. Typing `#` after a path closes it (a range is being typed). _Support:_ `talkContext.ts` (`contextMentionItems`), `mentions.ts` (`findActiveMention`, `rankFiles`), `MentionPopover.tsx` (`heading`); catalog via `listWorkspaceFiles`, sessions from `terminalsStore`.
- **What a token can name (#962)** — `@path` a whole file; `@path#L10-40` (or `#L10`) a line range; `@folder/` a listing of the folder's files with their sizes (relative paths, at most 500, then "… N more not listed" — never their contents); `@session:<slug>` the last 200 lines a Run session of this workspace shows (slug = the label kebab-cased, `-2` for a repeat; bare `@session` only when the workspace has exactly one), read from the mounted xterm's buffer with wrapped rows rejoined (a wrap on a space keeps it) and ANSI stripped; `@diff` the workspace's uncommitted diff — what is staged, then what isn't staged yet (untracked files included), each under a `# Staged` / `# Not staged` line — and `@diff:<path>` one file's sections of both (a path git quotes in the diff header — non-ASCII, a quote, a backslash — is matched unquoted, `unquoteGitPath`). A token with whitespace in it is quoted whole, `@"docs/my notes.md#L3-9"` or `@"diff:docs/my notes.md"` (`quoteToken`); the `@` popover and Review's "Ask Talk about this" insert that form for such a path. Tokens that name nothing the workspace has stay prose. A message attaches at most 10 mentions (`MAX_MENTIONS`, `capRefs`); past that the later tokens are sent as plain text and the chip row ends with an amber "10 at most · N more sent as text" (`talk-context-cap`). _Support:_ `talkContext.ts` (`extractContextRefs`, `capRefs`, `quoteToken`, `parseLineRange`, `sessionRefs`, `diffForFile`, `unquoteGitPath`, `joinDiffs`, `joinWrappedRows`, `formatFolderListing`, `tailLines`, `stripAnsi`), `terminalBuffers.ts` (registered by `TerminalPane`).
- **Context chips** — Above the textarea, one chip per resolved token (`ContextChips.tsx`; icon per kind, short label `a.ts#L10-40` · `lib/` · session label · `diff · a.ts`, its token count; tooltip names the kind, the token and "≈ N tokens"; the first chip is `talk-context-chip`). Each block is resolved 250ms after the token appears to estimate it (chars/4), and the chips' tokens are added to the composer's cost line. A token is resolved once while its estimate is in flight — typing on never discards it and starts another diff read or folder stat — and the blocks resolved together read the diff once (`resolveContextBlocks`). An estimate is dropped when its token leaves the draft and on send, so a token added back (or in the next draft) is estimated afresh. The textarea is `talk-composer-input`. The chips mirror the text: × removes the token from the draft (`removeContextToken`). A block the estimate found it can't include (non-text, too large, a range past the end, a named pipe) is a muted, dashed chip with no count, whose tooltip reads "Not included: a named pipe, not a file · @.env" (`missingByToken`, #1190).
- **Expansion on send** — Each token is resolved again at send (so a session or diff that moved on goes fresh) into a fenced block appended to the message: a whole file headed by its path (read with a 64k cap; non-text noted), a range headed `path · lines 10–40 of 120` (streamed by `read_file_lines`, which stops after the range's last line, so a range of a large file never reads all of it; `of N` only when the read reached the file's end, and a range past the end says how many lines the file has), a folder `src/lib/ · folder listing, 42 files`, a session `Run session "dev" · last 200 lines`, the diff `Workspace diff (uncommitted)` / `Diff of path (uncommitted)` in a `diff` fence. Every block is capped at 64k characters with a "(cut at 64k characters)" note at its end — except a session, which keeps its newest lines, cuts the oldest ("… (cut at 64k characters, older lines left out)" first) and counts only the lines it sent in its heading (`capTail`). One that can't be read says `_(not included: …)_` instead of vanishing; a named pipe, socket, device or folder in place of a file says so ("a named pipe, not a file", `notAFileReason`), and is refused at once rather than waited on (`fs_safe`, #1190). Where each block sits is saved on the user row (#1150): `withContext` appends the blocks to the typed text and records `[{token, kind, label, tokens, start, end, notIncluded?}]` (UTF-16 offsets into the content; `notIncluded` says why a block was left out or couldn't be read), sent as `contextBlocks` on `send_chat_message` and stored in `chat_messages.context_blocks` when its spans fit the message (`chat_history::context_spans`). The content stays the full text the model received, so the turn itself is unchanged. Each fence is longer than any run of backticks in its block (`fenced`), so a Markdown file or a diff holding a fence can't close the block early; the skill resolvers read fences the same way (a fence closes only on a bare line of at least as many backticks, `fencedRanges` / `skills::outside_fences`). _Support:_ `talkContextResolve.ts` (`resolveContextBlock`, `resolveContextBlocks`, `withContext`, `joinBlocks`); `chatStore.runTurn` (`pendingContext`: the spans join the user row when `chat://message-added` brings it); `readFileChecked`, `readFileLines` (`read_file_lines`), `fileMeta`, `getStagedDiff`, `getGitDiff`.
- **Secret guard on context blocks (#1046)** — Before a message with `@` blocks is sent, the secret guard's detectors read each block as it would be sent (a whole file, a range numbered from its first line, a folder listing, a session's output, a diff), one scan per block so every flagged block is known (`secret_scan_text` → `secret_scan::text_files`, the commit guard's rules, your saved credentials included; nothing leaves the Mac). A diff is read per file, as that file's own lines: each section is labelled by its path (unquoted), without the `+`/`-`/space prefix, numbered from its hunk headers, the text git writes after a hunk header's `@@ … @@` (the nearest earlier line that starts with a letter, `_` or `$`, sent with the diff) read as that file's line before the hunk, and a new or untracked file counts as a whole file, so the rules a path decides apply as in a commit: an untracked `.env`'s `DB_PASSWORD=…`, an `id_rsa` or `*.pem`, an MCP config, and the test, lockfile and docs exemptions (`talkContext.ts::diffScanInputs`). On a finding the composer holds the message and shows the secret guard's confirm (`SecretGuardDialog`, `action="message"`): "This message attaches what looks like a GitHub token in src/a.ts:3." — the kind and where (a file's path, else the block's `@token`) and the masked preview, never the value. **Leave it out** is the default: the message goes without the flagged blocks, each replaced by `<token> _(not included: possible secret)_`; **Send regardless** sends them for this one message. Escape (closing the confirm) sends nothing and puts the draft back in the composer; leaving the workspace while a message is held does the same in that workspace's composer (`chatStore.seedComposer`). A block whose scan can't run is held too: the confirm leads with "This message's @diff couldn't be checked." (the block's `@token`, whatever its kind; with findings as well, the same sentence sits under the lead instead of the 16 MB note), **Leave it out** stays the default, and a block left out reads `<token> _(not included: couldn't be checked for secrets)_`. Off when Settings › General › Safety's guard is off. _Support:_ `talkContextResolve.ts` (`scanContextBlocks`, `joinBlocks`), `ipc.secretScanText`, `chat/Composer.tsx` (`contextGuard`, `cancelContextGuard`), `secretGuard.ts` (`guardHeadline`, `uncheckedNote`, `overrideLabel`; `SecretRefusal.unchecked`).

### Attachments (images)
- **Image attachments** — PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, ≤ 5 MB, via paste / drag-drop / paperclip picker; removable thumbnails; image-only sends allowed. _Support:_ `attachments.ts`, `AttachmentTray.tsx`; `read_attachment` (magic-byte sniffing); attached as multimodal `LlmBlock::Image` blocks.
- **Images stay in the conversation** (#1159) — An ask's images are kept on this Mac as content-addressed files (`<sha256>.<ext>` in `~/Library/Application Support/octopush/chat-attachments/`, the same picture sent twice is one file), one `chat_attachments(message_id, path, media_type)` row each, so a follow-up ("and the button at the bottom?") can refer to an image sent earlier. Every later turn puts them back on the ask that carried them, after its text, so they stay byte-stable in the cached prefix; they go only to the conversation's provider, as on the turn that sent them.
