The ask being answered always carries its own images; earlier ones stay while the history with them fits in half the usable window (`ContextBudget::share(TARGET_PCT)`, 1,600 tokens an image), at most 20 images and 20 MB of them per request, and past that go first, oldest first, each replaced by `[image omitted]` (a file that is gone reads the same). An image that can't be saved still goes with its own turn. A fork's copies name the same files. These delete the rows, and each file once no row names it: deleting the conversation; a truncate (Regenerate, Edit & resend); deleting the workspace, whether from the rail or when a Routine discards a fresh workspace; and deleting the project, archived workspaces included. Each of those `Db` calls returns the files it freed, so no caller can leave one behind. Threads from before keep their text-only history. _Support:_ `chat_attachments.rs` (`save`, `for_history`, `earlier_kept`, `attach`, `remove`); `db.rs` (`add_chat_attachment`, `list_chat_attachments`, `delete_chat_thread`, `truncate_chat_after`, `delete_workspace`, `delete_project`); `chat_history::build_history_landing`, `transcript::build_landing`.

### Effort selector
- **Generation effort (Swift/Standard/Deep) — reasoning effort and output cap** — Segmented control; each preset sets the director's reasoning on every request of the turn (each round and the forced close, `chat_engine::director_request` / `forced_close_request`) and its output-token cap (Swift 8192, Standard 32768, Deep 64000; `EFFORT_MAX_TOKENS` → `ChatRequest.max_tokens`). The reasoning (`chatStore` `EFFORT_REASONING` → `ChatRequest.effort` → `LlmRequest.effort`): **Standard** (the default) sends **no** effort and no thinking settings, so every model keeps its own default effort and thinking. **Swift** never reasons more than Standard on any model: the composer sends `low`, which the turn runs as the internal `Effort::Least` (never read from a request). An Anthropic effort model gets `output_config.effort:"low"` alone, so its effort drops below its default (`high`, or `medium` on Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5) and thinking is never turned on (Opus 4.6–4.8 and Sonnet 4.6 think only when asked); an OpenAI reasoning model gets its lowest level, `none` on GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6.1 Terra (`effort_off_level`) and `low` elsewhere; a model without effort control gets nothing (a chat model such as gpt-4o, a local model, a legacy Claude, or one that thinks only with a budget: Opus 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5). **Deep** is the most the model takes: effort `max` on Opus 4.6–5.5, Sonnet 4.6–5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5–5.2 and Mythos 5–5.2 (adaptive thinking), `max` on GPT-6 and `high` on the o-series and GPT-5, and on a budget-only model thinking enabled with a 24,576-token budget (`thinking_json`, `effective_effort_level`, `reasoning_effort_level`); a model with neither gets only the cap. The per-model lists follow Claude's thinking and effort tables; a model that can't be checked against them gets no effort. **Sub-agents keep their own tier's effort** (`plan_subagent`, see "A plan per sub-agent"): the preset applies to the director only. **Reasoning replayed within a turn:** each tool round's response is replayed on the next round with its content blocks verbatim (`tool_round_turn`, as `run_agentic_loop` does): its signed thinking blocks on Anthropic, its encrypted reasoning items on the OpenAI Responses API. That keeps the reasoning behind the tool calls, and it adds those blocks' tokens to every later round's input for the rest of the turn (cached like the rest of the prefix). A round cut off at the cap mid-tool-use is rebuilt from its text and tool calls, but keeps its leading signed `thinking` / `redacted_thinking` blocks in front (`providers::truncated_round_turn`, shared with the sub-agent and Direct loop `run_agentic_loop`), since with a thinking budget on the API rejects a final assistant turn that doesn't start with one; a trailing, cut-off block is never replayed. Earlier turns reach the model as text, so their reasoning isn't carried. The tooltips say what each preset sends and the cap (`EffortSelector` `OPTIONS`, tested against both maps). _Support:_ `EffortSelector.tsx`; `chatStore` `EFFORT_REASONING`, `EFFORT_MAX_TOKENS`; `chat_engine.rs` (`ChatRequest.effort`, `director_request`, `forced_close_request`, `tool_round_turn`, `truncated_round_turn`); `providers/mod.rs` (`Effort::Least`), `providers/anthropic.rs` (`is_effort_model`, `is_budget_model`, `thinking_json`, `effective_effort_level`), `providers/openai_compat.rs` (`build_request`, `reasoning_effort_level`, `effort_off_level`). _Entry:_ composer control bar.

### `$`-direct shell in chat (hybrid terminal)
- **`$ <cmd>` / `/run <cmd>` direct execution** — Runs a command in the thread's persistent bash shell, bypassing the LLM (zero tokens); persists `$ cmd` as a user turn + output as a `role="tool"` RUN card (icon-labeled, retired the `§ RUN` prefix) so the agent sees it next turn. `\$…` escapes to literal text. _Support:_ `shellCommand.ts::parseShellCommand`; `chatStore.runShell` → `run_shell_command` → `chat_engine::run_shell_command`.
- **Persistent per-thread shell** — One bash PTY per thread keeps cwd/env across commands; reuses the `octopush-pty-server` daemon in capture mode (echo off, marker-wrapped commands with a per-session nonce). _Support:_ `talk_shell.rs`.
- **Commands run as written: no `!` history expansion, no TAB completion** — The shared shell is an interactive bash that reads each command (`$` commands and the agent's `run_command`) through readline, typed as written (`TalkShell::run`), so two interactive features used to rewrite them: history expansion made `node -e "if (!x) …"`, `git commit -m "Fix it!"` or (on macOS's bash 3.2) `echo "done!"` fail with "event not found" without running, and TAB completion dropped a heredoc's tabs (a broken Makefile) or, with many matches, asked "Display all N possibilities?" and ate the next character. The shell's init, sent on every spawn and reattach (so a shell from an older build gets it too), now runs `set +H; bind 'set disable-completion on'` (`talk_shell::SHELL_INPUT_AS_WRITTEN`, in `init_and_wait_ready`): `!` stays literal and a TAB is inserted as itself. `PROMPT_COMMAND` repeats `set +H` before every prompt, so a command or sourced script that turns history expansion back on doesn't keep it on for the next command. So in a `$` command, `!!` and `!$` don't expand either: they reach bash as typed. A live process's own input is unaffected. Sub-agents' and sandboxed commands run non-interactive `bash -c`, which never had either. _Support:_ `talk_shell.rs` (`init_and_wait_ready`, e2e `commands_with_a_bang_or_a_tab_run_as_written`, `a_shell_from_an_older_build_runs_commands_as_written_after_reattach`).
- **Login-shell PATH for every Talk shell (#1087)** — An app opened from the Dock or Finder starts with launchd's minimal PATH (`/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`), where tools from Homebrew, nvm, asdf, pyenv and the like aren't found. Every shell Talk runs gets the PATH CLI stages spawn with (`cli_runner::resolved_cli_path`: the login shell's PATH from `login_shell_env`, then the app's, then common bin dirs) and no other login-shell variable: the shared per-thread shell (`$` commands and the agent's `run_command`), the agent's `run_command` outside it (a sandboxed mission, or the isolated fallback while the shared shell is busy), sub-agents' commands and API-substrate Direct stages (both through `chat_engine::execute_tool_cancellable`). All of them run `/bin/bash` (`talk_shell::TALK_BASH`), never a bare `bash` looked up on that PATH, so Homebrew's bash or a conda/nix wrapper can't make the agent's commands behave differently from the user's. The shared shell is spawned with that PATH and sets it again once its prompt is up (`talk_shell::apply_login_path`), because `bash -l` sources `/etc/profile`, whose `path_helper` moves the system dirs ahead of it. A shell variable (`__octo_lp`) makes that happen once per shell: a PATH change made in the shell survives a restart, and a shell started by an older build gets the PATH on its first reattach. When the login shell gave no PATH (its probe failed or timed out, see "CLI environment & PATH resolution"), the step is skipped and the shell keeps `bash -l`'s PATH, since the fallback would put `/usr/bin` ahead of Homebrew (`cli_runner::login_env_path`). In a sandboxed mission the cache redirections stay and PATH is set after them; the profile confines writes only, so tools on that PATH run. A command that exits 127 gets one more line in its result, "`gh` wasn't found (the command ran with your login shell's PATH).", naming the program from bash's last `command not found` (or `No such file or directory`) line; a path such as `./run.sh` or `/opt/x/tool` isn't looked up on the PATH, so its line is just "`./run.sh` wasn't found.", and with no program to name it reads "A program in this command wasn't found (…)". So the model doesn't take a PATH miss as not installed (`chat_engine::not_found_note`). _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs` (`execute_tool_cancellable`, `wait_command_bounded`, `format_command_output`), `talk_shell.rs` (`spawn_bash`, `apply_login_path`), `orchestrator/cli_runner.rs` (`resolved_cli_path`, `login_env_path`; test seam `with_login_shell_env`).
- **cwd badge** — After a `cd`, a brass terminal badge shows the shell's working dir (relative, abbreviated). _Support:_ `chatStore` `shellCwdByThread`; `chat://shell-exit`.
- **Output capping** — `$`-direct output capped at 50k bytes with a truncation note. _Support:_ `talk_shell` `cap_output`.

### Live process panel & pinned mini-terminal
- **Promotion to live process** — A command not finishing within ~1500ms becomes a live process (dev servers/watchers stream instead of blocking the turn); the thread's shell is "busy" until it exits. _Support:_ `RunOutcome::{Done,Live,Busy}`, `LiveRun` (talk_shell); `chat://shell-live-start`.
- **Pinned mini-terminal (xterm)** — A bottom-pinned panel renders the live process via xterm.js (raw ANSI), with a Stop button; mounts on start, unmounts on exit. _Support:_ `LiveProcessPanel.tsx` + `TerminalView.tsx`; `chatStore` `liveProcessByThread`.
- **Race-free buffered output** — An always-on store listener buffers `chat://shell-output` chunks (capped) so the panel never loses output to a mount race. _Support:_ `chatStore` `liveOutputByCallId`.
- **Stop process (Ctrl-C)** — Sends SIGINT; the streamer then resolves the RUN card. _Support:_ `stop_shell_command` → `talk_shell.interrupt`.

### Savings ledger / cost (Companion)
- **Conversation cost (ledger)** — See "Companion · Conversation": `spent` / `of which sub-agents` / `saved vs all-strong`, read from the thread-attributed ledger (`get_thread_cost`). The message-row `SavingsLedger` is retired. _Entry:_ Companion (Talk).
- **Inline cost preview** — Composer shows an estimated per-message cost + token count (assumes 30% output ratio), on one line (`≈ $0.02 · 3k tokens`). _Support:_ `cost.ts`, `chat/ComposerEstimate.tsx`, `.octo-estimate*` in `styles.css`. _Entry:_ composer control bar. The estimate and Send/Stop are one group held to the right. The estimate is a fixed slot (design-system S1/S2): one nowrap, tabular line with a `ch`-based width, present (empty) even with nothing to estimate, so changing figures never wrap it or grow the bar. As the bar narrows it sheds on its own demotion ladder (container `.octo-composerbar`): "tokens" at ≤ 640px, the count at ≤ 520px, the cost is the floor; the full line stays in its tooltip. Only when even the cost alone doesn't fit does the group wrap, whole, onto a second line rather than overflow.
- **Context-window usage** — The Conversation section's meter shows the last turn's **last prompt size** (`contextTokens`) vs the active model's max context. _Support:_ `App.tsx`, `CompanionContext`.

### Composer (input bar)
- **Autosizing textarea + Enter-to-send** — Enter sends, ⇧↵ newline, grows to 8 lines; placeholder `"Ask anything…   @ file · / skill · $ run a command"`. _Support:_ `Composer.tsx`.
- **Prompt history** — ↑/↓ navigate per-workspace history; Esc exits. _Support:_ `Composer.tsx`.
- **Model picker** — Per-turn model selection (default: the review tier, `claude-sonnet-5-5`; `helperModelNow("review")`). _Support:_ `ModelPicker`; `chatStore` `model`.
- **Send / Stop crossfade** — Single button slot crossfades Send (brass) ↔ Stop (rouge); disabled when nothing to send / over budget. _Support:_ `FadeSwap`, `ComposerActionButton`.
- **Budget hard-stop + override** — Sending blocked when over workspace/global budget (`BUDGET_CAP_MSG`), with an "Override for this turn" one-shot. _Support:_ `budgetsStore`, `BudgetErrorBlock`.

### Cancel / stop
- **Esc stops the turn (#1153)** — `Esc` stops the running turn of the conversation Talk shows, the same `chatStore.stop` as the Stop button, whose title reads "Stop (Esc)". Only a bare `Esc` that nothing closer used, while Talk is the mode on screen, with the focus inside the Talk view or on nothing (the composer is disabled during a turn, so its focus falls to the body), no `ModalShell`, menu, listbox or popover open, and not in a code editor or terminal (Talk's terminal seat keeps its `Esc`). **Never from an approval card:** with the key or the focus on a card or anything inside it, `Esc` doesn't stop the turn, checked on its own (`APPROVAL_CARD_SELECTOR`), not only through the card's `stopPropagation`: a focused card answers its own `Esc` (deny), and a button inside one keeps its own keys. _Support:_ `chat/talkEscape.ts` (`escStopsTurn`, `useEscStopsTurn`) via `ChatView.tsx` (`active`); `chat/talkEscape.test.tsx`.
- **Stop generating** — Cancels the in-flight agentic turn for the active thread; persists a `role="stopped"` marker ("Stopped. Changes made before the stop stay; rewind files from your last message to undo them.", `STOPPED_NOTE`) and emits `done`. **A restart mid-turn** leaves the same kind of note: on boot, every thread not running whose last row is a turn's `user`, `tool` or `assistant_tool_use` row (not a `$` command's) gets "Interrupted by an app restart." (`Db::note_interrupted_talk_turns`, `RESTART_NOTE`, from `lib.rs` setup). Keyed by thread. **The provider request in flight is abandoned at once:** each director request, its retry backoff and a rate-limit pause are raced against the turn's cancel flag (`providers::or_cancelled`, which looks at the flag every 100 ms), and dropping the request closes its connection, so Stop no longer waits for a whole answer; the turn closes with the same note, every row of the rounds before it stays, and the abandoned request leaves none. A Stop during an approval card denies it. **Built-in tools stop too, and never hold the runtime (#1155):** every built-in workspace tool (`read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `list_files`, `grep`, `glob`) and every `run_command` off the shared shell (a sandboxed or Plan only mission, and the isolated fallback shell when the shared shell is busy) runs on a blocking thread with the turn's cancel flag (`run_confined` → `run_command_kept`; other built-ins `run_builtin` → `execute_tool_cancellable`), so a long grep or build never stalls another workspace's turn. Stop kills a command's process group within about 100 ms and ends a grep or glob walk between files ("Search stopped after N matches."), and the tool row reads as stopped; once Stop landed the fallback shell never starts its command (`run_fallback_shell`). The fallback is bounded by the command's own timeout, not an outer one that left the process running. `read_file` reads only as far as what it returns: a line window (`offset`/`limit`) is streamed and stops at its last line (its header reads "(lines 2-4; more follow)" when the file goes on, "(lines 2-4 of 10)" when the window reached the end), and a whole-file read stops at its 100 KB cap, so paging a large file never loads all of it (`read_line_window`, `read_file_head`). **A Stop during a sub-agent fan-out keeps the crew's work (#1148):** the tool loop still writes the `tool` row of every `Agent` call whose outcome the fan-out holds, feeds it back and links its saved run (`set_chat_agent_run_message`), so each finished report stays in the thread and in the next turn's history and its spend stays matched by a row; a sub-agent Stop cut off reads as stopped (`ok: false`, row `reason: "stopped"`, meta `stopped: true`) and can be let finish from its journal. Only the round's other calls that hadn't started are skipped (`kept_after_stop`), then the turn closes with the note. _Support:_ `chatStore.stop` → `cancel_chat` → `ChatEngine.cancel`; `ChatEngine::director_call`; `chat_engine::{kept_after_stop, run_builtin, run_fallback_shell, read_line_window}`; `chat_agents::{was_stopped, mark_stopped}`. _Entry:_ Stop button while streaming.

### Permission modes (#1146)
- **One policy for the director and every sub-agent** — `permissions.rs` decides each Talk tool call before it runs: `decide(mode, call, ctx)` → `Allow`, `Ask { reason, preview }` or `Deny { message }`. Tools are classed Read (`read_file`, `list_files`, `grep`, `glob`), Write (`write_file`, `edit_file`, and any tool the policy doesn't know yet), Exec (`run_command`), Net (MCP), Delegate (`Agent`/`Task`) and Meta (recall, `Skill`, `ask_director`, `submit_verdict`, `ask_stage`). A mode only makes Talk stricter: whatever it allows still meets the file and MCP cards (`talk_guard`), the command check and the secret guard, and no mode answers their cards. The director decides every call of a round before anything runs; a sub-agent's loop checks each call through `ModeGate` (a `ToolGate`) ahead of its approval gate.
- **Plan only** — Writes and edits are refused. `run_command` skips the shared shell and runs under the read-only seatbelt profile (`sandbox_roots = Some([])`: the workspace can be read, only temp files written), for the director and for sub-agents, so no command allowlist is needed. It runs off the turn's runtime thread and Stop kills it, as in Edit freely (`chat_engine::run_confined`). A command that a refused write broke ends with a note saying it ran on the read-only sandbox (`READ_ONLY_NOTE`). An MCP tool runs only when its server marks it `readOnlyHint` (the turn's discovery); any other MCP name is refused, whatever its name or the user's trust (#1243). `Agent` starts untyped calls (and types nobody defined), whose sub-agents inherit Plan only through `ModeGate` and the sandbox, and agent types whose tools can't write; a defined type with `write_file`, `edit_file` or `run_command` is refused (`chat_agents::delegate_writes`).
- **Plan only changes nothing elsewhere, by a heuristic** — The read-only sandbox doesn't stop the network, so Plan only also refuses a command whose words say it changes something remote (`permissions::remote_effect`). It reads the words as the command check does: every command the line runs, nested ones included (`each_command`), each word as the shell splits it (`command_words`: quotes, redirections, here-documents), past shell keywords and wrappers (`then`, `do`, `else`, `if`, `while`, `!`, `eval`, `time`, `exec`, `nohup`, `xargs`, `command`, `env`, `sudo`, `timeout`…). Refused: `git push` and `git send-email`; `gh` verbs that change GitHub (`create`, `merge`, `close`, `comment`, `edit`, `delete`, `review`, … in any group but `alias`/`config`/`extension`/`auth`), and `gh api` with a method other than GET or with fields; `hub` (`pull-request`, `create`, `fork`, `delete`, its `api`, and the git and gh writes above); `curl` with a method other than GET/HEAD, a data, form, JSON or upload flag (`-G` keeps data a query), or a config file (`-K`/`--config`, which can name any of them); `wget` with `--post-*`/`--body-*` or a non-GET `--method`; httpie (`http`/`https`/`xh`) with a method other than GET/HEAD or a data item (`a=b`, `a:=1`, `a@file`); `publish`/`unpublish`/`yank`/`upload` from npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, npx, cargo, pip, poetry, uv, twine and gem, anywhere past the flags, release tools (`semantic-release`, `release-it`, `np`), and the same through `python -m` (`python -m twine upload`); `docker`/`podman push`; and `kubectl`, `helm` and `terraform` changes (`apply`, `delete`, `upgrade`, `destroy`, …). Reading and fetching run (`git fetch`, `gh pr view`, `gh api` GETs, `curl` downloads). It reads words, not traffic: a tool it doesn't know, or a script that pushes, gets past it, and a command that only names one of these words as an argument may be refused. A command nested deeper than the check reads is refused.
- **Ask first (#1231)** — Each file change and each command that doesn't only read parks on an approval card (`permissions::ask_card`, asked through the `ApprovalBroker` like every Talk card, checked again once approved by `chat_engine::guard_card`). `write_file` and `edit_file` cards (kind `edit`) carry a `diff` on the `chat://approval-request` event: the file as it is against the file as the call would leave it (the edit computed by `chat_engine::apply_edit`, the same function `edit_file` runs), a unified diff of the changed lines with three lines of context (`permissions::unified_diff`), at most 300 lines with the rest counted, each line redacted (`secret_scan::redact_line`) and cut to 400 bytes. A path outside the workspace or in a credentials location, a file named like an env file or a key, a binary file or one over 2 MB gets no preview, so the card never reads it; the card names the path, and the outside-workspace card still asks after it. Once approved, the call runs only if its diff is still the one the card showed: a file that changed while the card waited asks again with the new diff. A `run_command` card (kind `exec`) shows the command; it parks unless every command in it only reads (`permissions::reads_only`, read with `each_command` and `command_words` like the command check): `ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `grep`, `diff`, `pwd`, `echo`, `stat`, `which`, and `git status`/`diff`/`log`/`show`/`blame`/`ls-files`/`rev-parse` with the subcommand first and no `--output` or `--ext-diff`, with no output redirected except to `/dev/null`. Anything that check can't tell asks: a variable or a path as the program, an assignment before it, a wrapper or a shell keyword, a script, or nesting past its caps. Denied, the call gets a fixed tool result (`ASK_DECLINED_CHANGE` / `ASK_DECLINED_COMMAND`) and nothing runs. These cards offer no "don't ask again" and a thread's grant never answers them (`CardKind::grantable`); Edit freely is the mode for that. Sub-agents inherit it: `ModeGate` asks through `ToolGate::ask_first` on the sub-agent's approval gate, on the same broker, and the card names the sub-agent; a gate with nobody to ask refuses (`CANNOT_ASK`). The menu bar names such a card "a file change wants approval" or "a command wants approval".
- **Edit freely** — Today's behaviour, unchanged; every conversation that never set a mode is in it.
- **No mode loosens the guards** — A call Ask first lets through, or that the user approves on its card, still meets the credential and outside-workspace cards, the command check and the secret guard, exactly as in Edit freely, and its output keeps the untrusted mark.
- **The tool list never changes with the mode** — Every mode sends the same tools; a refused call gets a fixed tool result that names the mode and what it refused (`permissions::plan_refusal`), which is not marked untrusted and records no file edit, so the prompt cache holds across a switch.
- **Per conversation, persisted, read at each round** — `chat_threads.permission_mode` (NULL = Edit freely), set through `set_thread_permission_mode(threadId, "plan" | "ask" | "edit")` and read through `get_thread_permission_mode(threadId)` → `{ stored, effective }` (`effective` is `plan` while the workspace's active mission is read-only; `ipc.getThreadPermissionMode` / `setThreadPermissionMode`); a fork keeps it. The director reads it at each round boundary, so a change applies from the next round, and a change during a turn leaves one quiet note row (role `stopped`, `permissions::mode_note`: "Mode switched to Ask first from this round on.") before the first round that runs in the new mode, so the record shows which mode each round ran under; the v2 transcript skips it (`permissions::is_mode_note`), so the turn still replays byte for byte. A sub-agent reads it as it starts (Plan only puts its whole run on the read-only sandbox) and again at each call, so a switch to Plan only reaches a running sub-agent; a sub-agent's saved run keeps the mission's own roots, so a continuation is narrowed by the mode at that time. A read error counts as Plan only.
- **A mission can only narrow it** — In a workspace whose active mission is read-only (`git_isolation = "readonly"`), Plan only is forced whatever the conversation says; its refusals name the read-only mission and offer no switch to Edit freely, which doesn't exist there. A mode never widens a mission's sandbox (`permissions::effective`, `exec_roots`). The user's own `$` commands are not agent tool calls and stay outside the modes. All modes are on Free.
- **Ship nothing (#1239)** — In a workspace whose active mission ships nothing (`mission::ships_nothing`: a non-delivering intent such as `test` that isn't `readonly`), every mode refuses, before the mode decides: a `run_command` whose words change something elsewhere (`permissions::remote_effect_local`), with *"Not run: this mission runs everything locally and ships nothing, so no command that changes something elsewhere ({what}). Note it in your findings instead."*, and an MCP tool its server doesn't mark `readOnlyHint`, with *"Not called: this mission ships nothing, and this MCP tool's server doesn't mark it read-only. Use a read-only tool, or note the step in your findings."* Neither offers a switch to another mode. Writes, edits, builds, installs, local commits and other local commands run as the mode allows; in Plan only, its own rules still apply on top. `remote_effect_local` is the same walk as `remote_effect` with one difference: a `curl`, `wget` or httpie request whose every URL host is loopback (`localhost`, `*.localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8` in four decimal parts, `[::1]`; httpie's `:3000` too) counts as local. A request with no URL it can read, userinfo or an escape in the host, a port that isn't digits, a proxy named on the line (a flag, `HTTPS_PROXY=…`, `env`, `export`), `--resolve`/`--connect-to`/`--unix-socket`/`--config` (and their abbreviations), or wget's `-i`/`-B`/`-e` stays remote, and so does a host that only looks local (`localhost.example.com`, `127.0.0.1.example.com`). `remote_effect` and Plan only are unchanged. The director resolves the posture with the turn's mission (`PolicyCtx::ships_nothing`); a sub-agent's `ModeGate` reads it from the workspace's active mission as it starts (`chat_agents::mode_gate`). A mission read that fails counts as ship-nothing. A crew can't start in such a mission (`orchestrator::launch::launch_run`: *"Crews don't run in a mission that ships nothing. Test it in Talk."*). **Not caught yet:** a script or build step that pushes on its own, and a proxy set in an earlier command of the shared shell or in a tool's config file. The ContextHeader shows the posture as a mute `PackageX` glyph beside the sandbox `Shield` (`data-tour="context-ships-nothing"`, title *"Runs locally, ships nothing: pushes, pull requests and publishes an agent asks for are refused"*; `lib/missionIntent.ts` `shipsNothing`).
- **Not yet** — There is no control for the mode in this release, and the approval card doesn't render the diff yet: the Composer's mode control, its shortcut and the card's diff view come in the next slice of #1231.

### Checkpoints — rewind files to a turn, fork from it (#958)
- **A checkpoint before every turn that can write** — When an agentic turn starts (`send_agentic`, right after the user row is persisted), the worktree is snapshotted as a commit under a private ref `refs/octopush/talk/<thread>/<message>`, built through a **temporary index** seeded from a copy of the real one (so only changed files are hashed; the index, and the scratch work tree a rewind uses to read a snapshot's ignore rules, each live in their own private directory with an unpredictable name, created by the `tempfile` crate and removed afterwards); the user's index, HEAD and branch never move and ignored files are never read. The files to hash are listed first (`git ls-files --modified --deleted --others --exclude-standard`) and then added with `git update-index`, so tracked and untracked files are captured and edits by `write_file`, `run_command` and sub-agents are all covered: it snapshots the tree, not the tool calls. A regenerate keeps the first attempt's checkpoint; a read-only mission (`sandbox_roots == Some([])`) takes none; `$`-direct commands take none; a repo with no commit yet works (parentless commit); nothing happens unless the workspace is the **top** of a git worktree (`is_repo`: `rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree --show-prefix` must answer `true` with an empty prefix), so a plain folder that only sits inside a parent repository (a home directory under git) never snapshots the parent's tree. Snapshot commits carry a fixed `Octopush` identity, so a machine with no git identity still gets them. When the turn ends — on every exit path, a Stop or an error included — `send_agentic` records `<message>-after` (`AfterTurn::record`), how the turn left the tree, before it releases the turn's cancel registration, so the turn still counts as running and no rewind can race that snapshot. All checkpoint git work (the snapshots of `send_agentic` and every checkpoint command) runs on a blocking thread (`talk_checkpoints::off_runtime` → `spawn_blocking`), never on an async runtime worker. _Support:_ `talk_checkpoints.rs` (`snapshot_with`, `is_repo`, `capture_before`, `AfterTurn`, `off_runtime`), `chat_engine.rs::send_agentic` (`TurnHold`).
- **Where checkpoints are stored, and what never is** — A checkpoint is a set of ordinary git objects in the repository's own git directory, under `refs/octopush/talk/*`. That directory is shared by every worktree of the repository, and **untracked (non-ignored) files are stored there as git objects too**; the rewind dialog says so (`data-tour="talk-rewind-storage"`). A command that copies every ref (`git push --mirror`) would copy these as well. Never stored: git-ignored files; an untracked embedded repository; submodule contents; and any file whose **name** the Secret guard treats as sensitive (`secret_scan::is_sensitive_name`: `.env` and `.env.*` except the templates, SSH private key names, `.pem`, `.p12`/`.pfx`/`.jks`, `.key`, `.claude/settings.local.json`), tracked or not: such a path is dropped from the snapshot's index, so a rewind never writes or removes it. Checkpoints are deleted with their thread (`delete_chat_thread` → `prune_thread`), with their workspace when it is **deleted or archived** (`commands::prune_talk_checkpoints_of` → `prune_threads`: before the worktree is removed on delete, and on the internal path that archives an ephemeral mission's workspace, `archive_workspace_internal`; after it on archive, from the project root, so an archive of merged missions called off at its last check keeps them), and any older than 30 days are pruned whenever a new one is taken (`MAX_AGE_DAYS`, `prune_older_than` over `%(committerdate:unix)`). A turn later dropped by Regenerate or Edit-and-resend keeps its ref until then. Deleting a ref makes its objects unreachable; git removes them at its next garbage collection. _Support:_ `talk_checkpoints.rs` (`snapshot_with`, `prune_thread`, `prune_threads`, `prune_older_than`), `secret_scan::is_sensitive_name`, `db::{chat_thread_worktree, chat_thread_ids}`, `commands::{delete_chat_thread, delete_workspace, archive_workspace}`.
- **A snapshot has a budget; past it the turn has no checkpoint** — A snapshot runs before the turn starts, so it is bounded (`Budget::DEFAULT`): at most **5,000** changed or untracked files, **200 MB** of them, and **20 seconds**. The limits are checked on the file listing, before anything is hashed, so a refused snapshot adds nothing to `.git/objects`; a git command still running at the deadline is killed. Past the budget (or when the snapshot fails for another reason) the turn runs without a checkpoint and a marker `refs/octopush/talk/<thread>/<message>-skipped` records why. In the conversation that turn shows a muted `CircleSlash` mark where Rewind would be (`data-tour="talk-turn-no-checkpoint"`, hover/focus row), titled `This turn has no checkpoint: <reason>` (`more than 5000 changed or untracked files`, `more than 200 MB of changed or untracked files`, `reading the changed files took too long`). A regenerate of that turn takes no late checkpoint either: the state before its first attempt is gone. A preview, rewind or undo whose own snapshot is over the budget is refused with "The files can't be compared right now: …". _Support:_ `talk_checkpoints.rs` (`Budget`, `snapshot_with`, `run_until`, `capture_before_with`, `mark_skipped`, `checkpoints`), `commands::list_talk_checkpoints`, `chat/ChatCanvas.tsx` (`MessageRow` `noCheckpoint`), `lib/talkRewind.ts` (`skippedLabel`).
- **Rewind files to here** — Hovering a user turn that has a checkpoint shows a `History` icon (`Rewind files to here`, `data-tour="talk-turn-rewind"`) beside Fork/Edit/Copy (a user turn's action row is `data-tour="talk-turn-actions"`; it is also shown, as on hover, while a tour points at it or at one of its actions); the list comes from `list_talk_checkpoints(threadId)` (ref names), re-read when a turn ends. Every checkpoint command takes the thread id only: the backend reads the workspace and its worktree from the database (`db::chat_thread_home`), never from the webview. It opens `RewindDialog` (`ModalShell`, no click-outside) which first calls `preview_talk_rewind`: a fresh snapshot of the tree now (`current`) diffed against the checkpoint with `git diff-tree -r -z --no-renames` (`parse_raw_diff`; submodule entries skipped), each file listed as `restore` (gone now, back after), `remove` (created since) or `revert`, and every file **changed outside this conversation** since that turn — between one turn's `-after` and the next turn's checkpoint, or since the last turn ended (by the director, another conversation, a terminal; `outside_paths`) — flagged `changed outside` in amber with a line saying the rewind undoes that too (`data-tour="talk-rewind-outside"`). Edits made by someone else *during* a turn can't be told apart from the turn's own. Nothing is written until **Rewind the files** (`data-tour="talk-rewind-confirm"`); `rewind_talk_files(threadId, messageId, expected)` re-snapshots and refuses ("The files changed since the preview. Look at the rewind again.") if the tree no longer matches the preview. It also refuses while **anything else may be writing to that worktree** (`commands::ensure_worktree_is_idle`): a turn or sub-agent continuation on this thread, a turn on any other conversation of a workspace checked out at the same folder (`db::chat_threads_sharing_worktree`, `ChatEngine::any_running`), or a Direct run that is running or paused there (`db::has_active_run_at`). It writes **only the files that differ** — deletions first (only files are removed, and a folder only once it is empty), then `git checkout-index` from a temporary index of the checkpoint, without `-f` for files that are new on disk — so a case-only rename on macOS can't delete what it just restored and unchanged files keep their mtimes. The conversation is kept: a quiet `stopped` note is added (`Files rewound to before “<turn's first line, 40 chars>” · N files`, plus ` · N left untouched` and ` · stopped part-way` when they apply; `commands::{rewind_note, rewind_note_tail}`); the model isn't told beyond that note's place in the thread (notes aren't replayed), so say so in your next message if it matters. _Support:_ `talk_checkpoints.rs` (`preview`, `rewind`, `plan`, `apply`, `outside_paths`), `commands::{list_talk_checkpoints, preview_talk_rewind, rewind_talk_files, ensure_worktree_is_idle}`, `chat/RewindDialog.tsx`, `chat/ChatCanvas.tsx` (`MessageRow` `onRewind`), `lib/talkRewind.ts`, `chatStore.refreshThread`.
- **What a rewind leaves untouched** — What counts as ignored depends on the `.gitignore` in the tree at that moment, and a turn can change it, so a rewind and its undo never trust one side alone (`talk_checkpoints::plan`). A path that differs is **left as it is on disk**, and listed, when: it is git-ignored under the rules on disk now **or** under the `.gitignore` files of the snapshot being restored (`protected_paths`: `git check-ignore --no-index` in the worktree, then again in a scratch work tree holding only the destination's `.gitignore` files; a tracked file that matches a rule counts too) — `git-ignored`; its name is sensitive — `sensitive name` (such a file is in no snapshot, so it can't show in the diff; a **tracked** one whose content differs from the last commit is listed all the same, `changed_sensitive`: `git diff --name-only HEAD`, compared in memory, nothing stored, so an edit a turn made to it is never passed over in silence; an untracked one can't be told from your own and is not listed); the path is to be restored but something the current snapshot doesn't hold is on disk there, a folder is in its place and still holds anything after the rewind's own removals, or a parent path is a file or a symbolic link — `not in the snapshot`; git can't say whether it is ignored — `couldn't be checked`; it couldn't be removed — `couldn't be removed`. A folder is never removed to place a file. The dialog lists these under "N paths differ but are left untouched." (`data-tour="talk-rewind-untouched"`, each with its reason and a `title`), the toast counts them (`Rewound N files; M left untouched.`) and so does the thread note. The dialog's closing lines say that staged changes, the branch and any file git-ignored now or at that turn are left alone. _Support:_ `talk_checkpoints.rs` (`plan`, `protected_paths`, `check_ignore`, `apply`, `Untouched`, `RewindOutcome`), `lib/talkRewind.ts` (`UNTOUCHED_LABEL`, `UNTOUCHED_TITLE`, `untouchedNote`, `rewoundTitle`), `chat/RewindDialog.tsx`.
- **Undo the rewind** — The replaced tree is kept under `refs/octopush/talk/<thread>/undo`, and the tree the rewind left under `<thread>/rewound`. The dialog says the notice that follows offers an undo for a few seconds: the success toast (`Rewound N files.`, 12s) carries **Undo the rewind** → `undo_talk_rewind(threadId)`, which refuses under the same "nothing else is writing to this worktree" rule as a rewind and refuses, writing nothing, when the files no longer match what the rewind left ("The files changed since the rewind, so it can't be undone without losing those changes.") — it never silently reverts a later turn's or the user's edits. Otherwise it puts the replaced tree back under the same rules as a rewind (so it too leaves ignored, sensitive and unknown paths untouched and reports them), deletes both refs (an undo is used once) and adds a `Rewind undone` note; a refusal shows as a `Couldn't undo the rewind.` toast with the reason. **A rewind that stops part-way** (a file can't be written) is not an error that hides the undo: `rewind_talk_files` answers with `error` set, the dialog stays open with "The rewind stopped part-way.", how many files were changed and the reason, and its own **Undo the rewind** button (`data-tour="talk-rewind-undo"`); a `<thread>/partial` marker is kept, and rewinding again from that half-rewound state keeps the **first** undo target, so the undo still goes back to before the first attempt (a later rewind from any other state starts a fresh undo). An undo that stops part-way keeps its target and can be run again. If the state a rewind left can't be snapshotted, no undo is offered and the dialog says so. _Support:_ `talk_checkpoints::{rewind, undo, outcome, record_left}`, `commands::undo_talk_rewind`, `RewindDialog`.
- **What a turn changed (#1152)** — Under the answer of a finished turn that took a checkpoint, a ledger row (`chat/TurnChanges.tsx`, `.octo-rise-in`, `data-tour="talk-turn-changes"`): the `FileDiff` icon (tooltip *"Files this turn changed"*), *"4 files changed · +38 −6"* (counts left out when every file is binary), the file names (`MidTruncate`, every full path in its `title`), **Review these changes** (upright serif, `data-tour="talk-turn-changes-review"`) and a `History` icon, *Rewind files to here*, which opens the same `RewindDialog` as the turn's hover action. `talk_turn_changes(threadId, messageId)` diffs the turn's checkpoint against its `-after` (`git diff-tree -r -z --no-renames` for each file's status, then `--numstat` for its counts, `parse_numstat`; submodule entries skipped) and returns `[{path, status: added|deleted|modified, added, removed}]`, binary files counting 0/0; it returns none when either ref is missing (a turn that took no checkpoint, one interrupted before its `-after`) or the turn changed nothing, so read-only turns show no row. The snapshots cover the whole tree, so edits made by `run_command` and sub-agents are counted too. The row appears only once the turn has ended (the turn in flight, a regenerate included, shows none) and reads its refs once, as it mounts. It runs on a blocking thread (`off_runtime`) and resolves the worktree from the thread id. **Review these changes** opens Review's *This turn* scope on that turn (§5). _Support:_ `talk_checkpoints::{turn_refs, turn_changes, parse_numstat, TurnChange}`, `commands::talk_turn_changes`, `ipc.talkTurnChanges`, `lib/turnChanges.ts` (`turnChangesSummary`, `turnChangesNames`, `turnLabel`, `turnEnds`), `chat/ChatCanvas.tsx` (`turnChangesAfter`).
- **Fork from here** — Every user turn also offers a `GitFork` icon (`Fork from here`, `data-tour="talk-turn-fork"`): `fork_chat_thread(threadId, messageId)` creates `<title> · fork` in the same workspace holding a copy of every row **before** that turn (role, content, model, tokens, cost, cache split, original timestamps; sub-agent journals and file-edit attribution are not copied), copies those turns' checkpoints to the new thread's message ids (`copy_to_fork`), and returns the turn's text (for an ask sent with `@` context, what was typed, so its tokens resolve again on send; `context_blocks` is copied with the rows), which the new thread's composer takes once as its draft (`chatStore.forkThread` → `composerSeedByWs` → `Composer` `takeComposerSeed`), so you can send it again or change it first; a message already half-typed in the composer is kept, with the turn's text added after it, and so is a seed the composer hasn't taken yet when a second fork follows (`forkThread` appends). Turns without a checkpoint keep their "no checkpoint" marker in the fork. The original thread is untouched; the fork becomes the active thread. The copy runs in one transaction, so a failure part-way leaves no half-copied fork. **Both:** the dialog's **Rewind and fork from here** rewinds the files, then forks from the same turn; once the files are rewound the dialog closes and the undo toast appears, and a failed fork is reported in its own toast ("The files are rewound, but the fork failed."). _Support:_ `db::fork_chat_thread`, `commands::fork_chat_thread`, `talk_checkpoints::copy_to_fork`, `chatStore` (`forkThread`, `composerSeedByWs`, `takeComposerSeed`), `chat/Composer.tsx`.

### Message rendering / export
- **Editorial assistant rendering** — Assistant content splits into a lead "key phrase" (Spectral upright-serif display) + markdown body; eyebrow `— ModelName` in **mute** mono (brass marks the director's turns, not the model's; see "Turns read apart"); full markdown renderer in Onyx & Brass tokens. The lead is the first sentence on the reply's first line: a `.`/`!`/`?` (or a run of them, with any closing quote or parenthesis) ends it only when whitespace or the end of the text follows, so a version (`v0.4.141`), a number (`3.5`), a file name (`index.ts`) or a domain never splits; nothing inside inline code, a markdown link or a URL ends it, nor does an ellipsis or an abbreviation (`e.g.`, `i.e.`, `etc.`, `vs.`). The lead is elevated only when it is plain prose plus inline code, at most 160 chars, with a body after it: a lead carrying a URL, an email, a link, emphasis, a strikethrough pair or HTML stays in the body, and so does a reply that opens with block markdown (fence, heading, list, quote, table). The serif line renders only paragraphs and inline code (`allowedElements`), so it can never show raw syntax or a link. _Support:_ `parseKeyPhrase.ts`, `ChatMessage.tsx`. **GitHub-flavored Markdown is on** for model prose (`chat/ChatMarkdown.tsx`: `remark-gfm` + the chat-tuned component map, shared by the assistant body, the key phrase, and sub-agent reports on the crew card and in the Companion crew journal): tables render as tables (sticky brass header row, scroll box) instead of collapsing into one paragraph, task lists as read-only brass checkboxes, strikethrough in mute. Tool OUTPUT is not prose and keeps its mono `<pre>` in the tool cards. _Support:_ `chat/ChatMarkdown.tsx` (`makeMarkdownComponents`, `looksLikeFilePath`, `REMARK_PLUGINS`).
- **User-turn rendering** — The text **as written** on the **panel surface**: a `bg-octo-panel` inset with a hairline border and a 6px radius (`data-tour="talk-turn-ask"`), the one filled surface in the thread that isn't code, so your turns read apart from the model's at a glance however long the conversation gets. Its header carries the brass eyebrow `— You`, the turn's hover/focus actions (Rewind files to here, Fork from here, Edit & resend, Copy message; see "Rewind files to here") and the time it was sent (`<time>`, mono mute, English and 24-hour on every system locale: the clock time today `14:02`, `Nov 23, 14:02` on another day, `Dec 30, 2025, 14:02` in an earlier year; the full date and time on hover, `Tue, Dec 30, 2025, 14:02`; `turnTime`, `turnTimeFull`). Line breaks, indentation and typed bullets survive the send (`whitespace-pre-wrap`; an unbroken token such as a digest wraps with `break-words`). The user's text is never re-parsed as Markdown — a pasted log, stack trace or snippet keeps its `#`, `*`, `<tags>` and indented lines. **An ask sent with `@` context** (#1150) shows only what you typed; under it sits a row of the composer's chips (`data-tour="talk-turn-context"`: kind icon, label such as `a.ts#L10-40`, `≈ 1k`; tooltip "File · @src/a.ts#L10-40 · ≈ 1k tokens · Show the block"). A chip opens its block in place, as the model received it, through the grid-rows `Reveal` (brass while open, `aria-expanded`): a mono `<pre>` capped at 256px, with "Show full block" / "Show less" past 15 lines; one block is open at a time. A block left out (a possible secret, one the scan couldn't check, or one that couldn't be read) is a muted dashed chip titled "Not included: possible secret" (or its reason), with nothing to open. A row without `context_blocks`, or with spans that don't fit its content (`parseSentContext`), renders exactly as before. Copy on a user turn copies what was typed, without the header or the blocks; an ask with context also offers **Copy with context** (`CopyPlus`), which copies the full text sent. **Edit & resend** on such an ask edits the typed text with its `@` tokens, and Resend resolves them again, as at send (`expandDraft`: fresh reads, the secret guard scans each block; with no composer to ask in, a flagged or unchecked block is left out and its chip says so). While they resolve, the turn's actions are disabled, so a second Resend can't race the first. _Support:_ `ChatMessage.tsx` (user branch, `turnTime`; guarded by `ChatMessage.test.tsx`), `chat/SentContext.tsx`, `lib/sentContext.ts` (`parseSentContext`, `typedText`, `blockBody`), `chat/ChatCanvas.tsx` (`MessageRow` passes the actions into the header; `resendEdit`).
- **Turns read apart: the ask, the work, the answer** — A Talk thread reads in three registers. **The ask** is the panel inset above. **The work** is one `WorkBlock` per run of the model's narration and tool calls between two other items (`groupWork` in `lib/talkWork.ts`; a message, crew card or error ends the run): a single hairline on the left (`border-l border-octo-hairline`, `data-tour="talk-work"`) with the narration lines and one quiet ledger row per call hung from it, all mute and sage, no brass; the turn's running calls continue the same line (see the live tool card). Inside it, calls in a row are a **round**; a round of more than five calls (`ROUND_FOLD_AT`) folds into one summary row (`data-tour="talk-work-fold"`, fades in): a chevron, `N tool calls` and a one-line digest (`edit sync.rs, settings.rs · run cargo test sync`: calls of one kind in a row joined, paths shortened to file names; `roundSummary`), which opens in place on the grid-rows `Reveal`. Folded, a round's rows can't show their verdicts, so its count says them: `6 tool calls · 1 failed` in rouge, `· 1 denied` in mute, and its title too ("Show the 6 tool calls (1 failed, 1 denied): …"); a round of passes adds nothing (`verdictCounts`). The `Reveal` reaches 16px into the hairline's gutter, so a row's verdict dot on the hairline is never clipped. A round **never folds while its turn is streaming**: it folds when the turn ends, and stays open if the reader's focus is in it. A work block is the turn in flight's (`live`) when a turn is streaming, it comes after the last user turn **and** its first row is newer than the highest message id on screen when the turn started (`streamSinceByWs`, set by `runTurn` and `runShell`, read after a regenerate or edit has truncated the view). The backend saves the new user row a moment after streaming starts (later still for a `$` command, after its secret scan), so without that mark the previous turn's folded rounds would briefly reopen; the mark survives a thread switch, so a running thread shown again still reads as live. Every round renders as one tree (the rows always under the same `Reveal`, with stable keys), so a round growing from five to six calls, or folding, never remounts its rows: an opened row stays open and a focused one keeps focus. `WorkBlock` is memoised, so streaming deltas don't re-render the work. **The answer** is flush, with the model's eyebrow in mute and its serif key phrase (see "Editorial assistant rendering"). Brass in a thread goes to `— You`; the model's eyebrow and the tool rows don't spend it. **Semantics:** the thread is a `<section aria-label="Conversation">` (not `role="feed"`, whose keyboard model it doesn't implement); each user turn is an `<article aria-label="You, 14:02">`, each answer an `<article>` named after its model, each work block an `<article aria-label="Work, 7 tool calls">` whose rounds are `role="group"` "N tool calls"; every ledger row and the fold are buttons with `aria-expanded`. Each turn's actions are inside its article: an ask's in its header (right after it in focus order), an answer's last (after its text). Crew cards, approvals and the streaming answer render as before. _Support:_ `lib/talkWork.ts` (`groupWork`, `ROUND_FOLD_AT`, `toolCallCount`), `chat/WorkBlock.tsx` (`WorkBlock`, `NarrationLine`, `roundSummary`), `chat/ChatCanvas.tsx`, `ChatMessage.tsx`; tests `talkWork.test.ts`, `WorkBlock.test.tsx`, `ChatView.test.tsx`; demo scenario `talk-work`.
- **Clickable file paths** — File-path-shaped inline code becomes an "Open in editor" button. _Support:_ `looksLikeFilePath` (ChatMessage).
- **Per-message copy** — Hover-revealed Copy on each message row. _Support:_ `useCopyFeedback`.
- **Copy conversation as Markdown (TALK threads)** — Renders the whole thread to portable Markdown (user/assistant sections; tool rows become a `### TOOL_NAME` heading with the parsed command/result in fenced blocks — no `§` prefix) and copies it to the clipboard. _Support:_ `lib/exportConversation.ts` (`conversationToMarkdown`), `App.tsx` `handleExportChat`; `copyToClipboard`. _Entry:_ the thread list's `ClipboardCopy` action (title and aria-label "Copy conversation as Markdown").
- **Session recap / export (RUN-mode sessions)** — `get_session_recap` builds a `SessionRecap` (tokens, cost, duration, model, timestamps); `export_session_json`/`export_session_csv` bundle session + events + recap. _Support:_ `session_recap.rs`. _Note:_ operates on RUN-mode **sessions**, not TALK threads.

### MCP tools in chat
- **MCP tool injection** — Each turn appends tools from configured + reachable MCP servers (namespaced `mcp__server__tool`), discovered off-thread with a 20s timeout. Servers the user switched off in the conversation (Companion "can use") are left out of discovery and never started for it (`chat_agents::discover_thread_mcp_tools`, the one path the turn, the sub-agent fan-out and a sub-agent continuation discover through; `McpRegistry::list_tools_except`). What a turn offers is fixed at its start, but every MCP call re-reads the thread's list (`mcp_off_refusal`): a server turned off mid-turn is refused from its next call without reaching the server — "<server> is turned off in this conversation, so its tools are unavailable here. The user can turn it back on in the Companion's "can use" row." — and one turned back on mid-turn runs again (a call to a server not offered this turn can still be copied from an earlier turn). After discovery the turn, the fan-out and a continuation emit `mcp://status-changed`, so the Companion's chips re-read their status. **Stable order:** discovery lists the tools by server name, then tool name (`mcp::sort_tools`, applied by `list_tools`, `list_tools_except` and Settings' Test, `test_connect`; servers also start in name order), and the director and every sub-agent build their definitions from that list (`chat_agents::mcp_llm_tool`), so the same config gives byte-identical tool JSON on every turn: the tool list is where the provider's prompt cache starts, and the old per-read `HashMap` order changed it almost every turn. A server that fails or is switched off drops out without moving the others. Talk's default system prompt (`default_talk_system_prompt`) says these tools come from MCP servers Octopush runs, managed in Settings › Integrations (where one can be reconnected), and never to point the user to Claude Code's `/mcp` or `claude mcp` commands for them (other commands, such as a `which npx` hint, may still reach the user). _Support:_ `chat_engine::send_agentic`, `default_talk_system_prompt`; `chat_agents::{discover_thread_mcp_tools, thread_mcp_off, mcp_off_refusal}`, `McpRegistry::list_tools_except` (`mcp/scope.rs`).
- **MCP tool invocation** — `mcp__`-prefixed tool names route to their server via `mcp::call_bounded` (60s, `CALL_TIMEOUT`). A timeout **stops the process that call was on** (`McpRegistry::abort_call`: the call records its connection's process before its request goes out (`CallTarget`), and only that one is stopped (`abort_connection`), so a newer process started meanwhile with another config — an entry edited by hand, or a worktree defining the server differently — keeps running; a call still waiting on a start stops that handshake (`abort_start`), and one that gets its connection only after the bound never sends its request; the whole process group is killed through a handle held outside the connection lock — the connection and its process travel together in one registry entry — so even a request blocked mid-read, or a handshake that never answers `initialize` (`pending`), returns with EOF; the group signal is sent only while the child is unreaped, never to a reusable pid; a connection is evicted after an error only if it is still the cached one, so a sibling's fresh re-spawn survives) — a call reported as timed out can never complete later in the background; the error tells the model the server was stopped and that a request it had already sent may still have landed. The next call re-spawns the server. Concurrent first callers of a server (a sub-agent fan-out) spawn it once (per-server connect lock). **Failures are classified (`McpCallError`):** a failure on the wire — the server couldn't start, its handshake failed, the process exited, a pipe broke (`RpcError::Transport`), or the 60s bound — drops that server's cached connection, so the next call spawns a fresh process; the failed call itself is never retried (it may already have reached the server). A tool that reports its own failure (`isError: true`) is an ordinary result, and a JSON-RPC `error` answer (`McpCallError::Server`) comes back as a failed tool result; in both cases the server is alive and its connection stays. **What the model reads:** a connection failure is "Octopush's connection to <server> failed: <reason>. The user can reconnect it in Settings › Integrations." (`connection_failure_text`; the server's own stdout/stderr, if any, follows as a "Server output:" block — redacted line by line (`secret_scan::redact_line`: provider key prefixes, `TOKEN=…`-style assignments, `Bearer …`, URL passwords, plus an OAuth `code=…`) and cut to its last 1 KiB (`SERVER_OUTPUT_CAP`, from a line start, after "… (earlier output cut)"); a timeout adds that the server was stopped); a JSON-RPC error is "<server> answered with an error: … If it keeps failing, the user can reconnect it in Settings › Integrations."; an unknown server is "No MCP server named <server> is configured for this project. Talk's MCP servers are managed in Settings › Integrations." **What a result becomes:** `mcp::content::render_call_result` joins the result's text blocks (and a `resource`'s text) in order, one per line, and replaces base64 payloads with a short placeholder only where they are known to be binary: an `image` or `audio` block and a `resource` blob (`[image omitted: image/png, 48 KB]`, `[resource file:///a.pdf omitted: application/pdf, 12 KB]`); a base64 `data:` URL of 256+ characters anywhere in text (`[data URL omitted: image/png, 48 KB]`); and, in a text block that is JSON (an object or array) and in the JSON fallback, a string value of 256+ base64 characters whose decoded first bytes are the magic number of PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, PDF, zip or gzip (`[base64 PNG data omitted: 48 KB]`, replaced where it stands, so the rest of the JSON keeps its formatting). Every other base64 stays as it is, such as a Kubernetes secret, a JWT, base64 of text or a bare base64 text block, because it is ordinary developer output and the cap below bounds it. A `resource_link` reads `[resource link: <uri>]`; a result with no readable block falls back to its JSON, with the same payloads replaced. This scrubbed text is what the director and a sub-agent read, what the tool card shows and what later turns replay (the row's `result`). The unscrubbed rendering (a binary block as its JSON) is kept, when it differs, in its own table (`chat_tool_originals`, up to 1 MB per call, `ORIGINAL_CAP_BYTES`, cut on a char boundary, with its full size), never in the row the webview receives on a new message or a thread load; `recall_tool_output` returns it, followed by "[original output truncated: the first N of M bytes were kept]" past the cap (`db::{set_chat_tool_original, get_chat_tool_original}`, `chat_history::recall_source`; a row without one recalls its `result`). **The director caps MCP results** like the sub-agents cap tool results: the copy its next round carries keeps at most 24 KB (`TOOL_RESULT_CAP_BYTES`), head and tail, with the gap marker "… [N chars omitted — call recall_tool_output with message_id <row> for the full output]"; the tool row keeps the whole result for `recall_tool_output` and the card (`chat_history::tool_result_for_model`). Built-in tools keep their own caps (on `talkEngine: "v2"`, every result is capped once from the model's window: **Append-only transcript**). _Support:_ `mcp/mod.rs` (`call_bounded`, `abort_call`, `CallTarget`, `ChildHandle`, `ensure`, `McpCallError`, `connection_failure_text`), `mcp/content.rs`, `is_mcp_tool`; cards render `MCP` label.
- **MCP tools inside sub-agents** — A Talk sub-agent (`Agent` tool) is offered the workspace's MCP tools too: the fan-out discovers them once per response (off-thread, 20s bound), minus the servers switched off in the parent conversation (`discover_thread_mcp_tools`, also on a sub-agent's continuation, which re-reads the thread's list when it resumes; a running sub-agent keeps the tools it started with, even if one of their servers is turned off meanwhile), and each sub-agent sees the subset its definition grants (`McpSubagentTools::granted`), executed through the loop's `ExternalTools` hook (`orchestrator::agentic::ExternalTools` — caller-owned tools outside the workspace allowlist; a call runs off-thread with the same 60s bound and an error comes back as an error tool_result). Grants follow Claude Code's agent-file vocabulary in the definition's `tools` list: `mcp__server__tool` for one tool, `mcp__server` (or `mcp__server__*`) for a whole server, `mcp__*` (or `mcp`) for all; no `tools` list = every server; a list with no `mcp__` entry = none; a list that is MCP-only (or whose other entries map to nothing) is a complete allowlist — MCP tools and **no** workspace tools (`skills::agents::McpGrant`, `split_mcp_entries`). An untyped `Agent` call gets them all. **Writes ask first:** an MCP tool that may write, classed as the director's are (`talk_guard::McpTools`, #1243: in Edit freely a read tool or a trusted one runs), goes through the sub-agent's approval gate like a dangerous command (`SubagentGate::with_mcp`, `mcp_gate_texts`: "may change external state"); a denial never reaches the server and reads back as an error tool_result — the loop offers every external call to the gate before executing it. Calls to one server queue on a per-fan-out turnstile (`mcp_turnstiles`) so the 60s bound covers the wire, not the wait for a sibling sub-agent; a timeout stops the server (`call_bounded`), so a timed-out call never completes later; a request the server had already sent may still have landed, and the error says so. The built-in `ticket-reader` grants `mcp__*`, so a Jira/Linear/GitHub MCP server reachable from the workspace is how it reads a ticket first. _Support:_ `chat_agents.rs` (`McpSubagentTools`), `orchestrator/agentic.rs` (`ExternalTools`, `run_agentic_loop` `external`), `skills/agents.rs` (`McpGrant`, `split_mcp_entries`), `chat_engine.rs` (passes `McpRegistry` to `run_subagents`).

### Notable implementation details
- **Streaming** — Not token-by-token; `send_agentic` runs a synchronous agentic loop and emits the whole FINAL assistant text as one `chat://stream` delta, then a metadata `done`; per-tool `chat://tool-start`/`tool-end` drive live cards; every persisted row broadcasts via `chat://message-added`; a retry or rate-limit wait sends a live `chat://notice` (never persisted). All events routed by `workspaceId` + optional `threadId`, gated by `isActiveThread`.
- **Shell-in-chat** — Per-thread persistent bash PTY on the shared daemon (capture mode with nonce markers, ANSI stripped, exit code + `$PWD` recovered); ~1500ms promotion window streams long commands via `chat://shell-output`.
- **History → provider context** — `send_agentic` rebuilds context from DB rows through `chat_history::build_history` (pure, unit-tested). `role="tool"` rows become `[Tool #id: name | Input | Result]` summaries under a **settle-once, monotone allowance** instead of the old flat 500-char cut: results from the turn just before the message keep up to 6k chars (`TOOL_RESULT_FRESH`, funded newest-first within a 40k `TOOL_HISTORY_FRESH_EXTRA`), every older result keeps one final 1.5k (`TOOL_RESULT_SETTLED`) — two sizes, not a fade, because each rewrite of an old row invalidates the provider's prompt cache from that row to the end of the thread; a row is rewritten exactly once (the turn after it ran, at the tail). The thread-wide 80k budget is counted over **settled** sizes only, so it only grows as rows are appended and the collapse it drives — the **oldest** rows to a 200-char stub in **20k blocks** (`TOOL_HISTORY_COLLAPSE_BLOCK`) — only ever moves forward: a stubbed row stays stubbed, a settled row is never rewritten until the boundary reaches it, and a tool-heavy turn settling cannot un-stub anything. Each excerpt is **head + tail** (70/30 — the tail is where exit codes and errors live) with a `[N chars omitted — call recall_tool_output with message_id …]` gap marker; tool inputs cap at 600 chars. `assistant_tool_use` rows contribute the model's lead-in prose in order with the summaries, so a continued turn reads as one narrative; an `assistant` row closes the turn; orphans (a `$`-direct output, a capped/errored turn) ride on the next user turn; consecutive same-role turns merge (Anthropic 400 guard); `error`/`stopped` never replayed. **`@` context blocks** (#1150): the ask being answered (the last user row) goes out whole; from the next turn on, each block of 8k chars or more (`CONTEXT_BLOCK_SHORTEN_MIN`) of an earlier ask with `context_blocks` is shortened, once, to head + tail within the 1.5k settled allowance, with a `[N chars omitted — call recall_tool_output with message_id M and block K for the full block]` marker. The shortened form is a pure function of the row, so it is byte-stable from then on; that one full-to-shortened change is the accepted exception to rows being a function of the row alone (one cache write from that row on, the turn after it was sent). Smaller blocks and the typed text are re-sent whole. Shortened blocks count against the 80k thread budget at their settled size from their own turn on (`plan_tool_history_with`), so they make the oldest tool rows collapse sooner and are never stubbed themselves. A row without `context_blocks` replays verbatim, as before. **Images** (#1159): an ask with kept images (see "Images stay in the conversation") makes its turn even with no text, and `build_history_landing` says which turn holds it, so `chat_attachments::attach` puts its images back there (or `[image omitted]` notes once the budget has no room); a thread without them builds exactly as before. On a `talkEngine: "v2"` turn, the **Append-only transcript** below replaces this builder (`transcript::build_landing` does the same). _Support:_ `chat_history.rs` (`build_history`, `build_history_landing`, `plan_tool_history_with`, `excerpt_head_tail`, `context_spans`, `abridge_context`).
- **Append-only transcript (Talk engine v2, behind `talkEngine`)** — With `"talkEngine": "v2"` in `settings.json` (no toggle yet; unset is `legacy`, and a value this build doesn't know reads as `legacy`), a Talk turn starts from `context::transcript::build` instead of `build_history`, and every stored row renders as a function of itself, not of its age. So each turn's first request starts with the messages the previous turn's last request sent (that turn's thinking aside, below), and the provider's prompt cache can hold across turns (the cache breakpoints are B3). **Capped once:** each tool result is capped when it is written, to 5% of the model's window (`view_cap`: window × 3.5 chars per token × 5%, between 2,000 and 100,000 chars; an MCP result keeps the 24 KB MCP cap), head and tail with "… [N chars omitted — call recall_tool_output with message_id <row> for the full output]" (`model_view`), then put under its source's untrusted header with forged `[Tool #` records and marks in it neutralized (`chat_history::mark_untrusted`, **Tool output reaches the model marked untrusted**; a denial or refusal stays unmarked), so the mark is stored and replayed with the text. A `recall_tool_output` result is capped the same way; on a v2 turn one call returns at most the cap less 200 chars (`recall_limit`), so its window fits. The loop sends that text in the rounds that follow, the row keeps it in `chat_messages.model_view` with the call's `tool_use_id`, and later turns replay it byte for byte; `content` keeps the full output for recall and the card. **Rounds replay as pairs:** an `assistant_tool_use` row keeps its round verbatim with its origin model in `raw_json` (`RoundRecord {model, raw, text, toolUses}`), so a finished turn replays as the same tool_use and tool_result pairs, then its answer. The current turn's rounds go out with their signed thinking (the loop's own copies); a prior turn's are replayed without `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` blocks, the rest in their order, so they cost no thinking tokens later and read the same whatever this turn's effort. The blocks go only to the model that wrote them; after a model switch, or for an OpenAI Responses round, the round is rebuilt from its text and tool calls. **Text otherwise:** a turn that can't replay as pairs (rows written before this or on a `legacy` turn; a stopped or failed turn, whose last round no answer closes; a round missing a column, or with another row inside it; a turn whose ask is empty) renders as text the way `build_history` does. Those tool rows keep legacy's thread-wide bound: the 1.5k settled allowance whatever their age, the oldest collapsing to 200-char stubs in 20k blocks once the settled total, shortened `@` blocks counted, passes 80k (`plan_tool_history_with`), so a long legacy thread fits on v2 wherever it fits on legacy. The ask being answered goes out whole, and `@` blocks of 8k chars or more are shortened once from the next turn, as above. **Context stubs persist:** when the context budget guard stubs a v2 result (at a round boundary, or for the retry after a context-length error), the stub becomes the row's model view (`set_chat_tool_stub`, via `chat_engine::keep_stubs`), so later turns replay the stubbed request byte for byte instead of re-sending the whole result. A stub is under the guard's 1,000-char floor, so a result is stubbed once; its head keeps the untrusted mark, and it names the row for recall. The guard's stubs name the transcript's rows too (`tool_rows`). Apart from that stub, a row's columns are written once (`set_chat_round`, `set_chat_tool_view` leave a row that has one as it is). A continued sub-agent's rewrite drops its row's model view (`update_chat_message_content`), so the director's next turn reads the new report, with that turn as text. A fork doesn't copy the columns (a model view names its own row for recall), so the fork's rows replay as text with their own ids. The webview never receives the columns (`ChatMessageRow` skips them). A turn's request still changes once, from the message where it happens, after: a prior turn's thinking (dropped when the turn ends), image attachments (sent only with their own turn), the forced close's instruction on the last result, and a round cut off at `max_tokens` (not stored). _Support:_ `context/transcript.rs` (`build`, `rows`, `RoundRecord`, `model_view`, `view_cap`, `recall_limit`, `tool_rows`), `context/budget.rs` (`Stubbed::ids`, `AfterFailure::stubbed`), `db.rs` (`set_chat_round`, `set_chat_tool_view`, `set_chat_tool_stub`; columns `raw_json`, `tool_use_id`, `model_view`), `settings.rs` (`TalkEngine`), `chat_engine.rs` (`run_agentic_turn`, `keep_stubs`). _Entry:_ `settings.json` `talkEngine`.
- **Context budget (director)** — Inside a turn, tool results ride whole in the rounds that follow (a `read_file` up to 100 KB; on `talkEngine: "v2"`, capped once from the window, see **Append-only transcript**), so before every director request `context::budget::ContextGuard` estimates the prompt: the last response's real prompt size (input + cache reads + cache writes) plus chars/3.5 of what changed since, times the model's calibration (chars/3.5 of the whole request on the turn's first one). An image counts a fixed 1,600 tokens (`IMAGE_TOKENS`), never its base64 length. The budget is the window the catalog gives the model (`cli_runner::catalog_context_window`, an id with `[1m]` 1M) or, for a model the catalog doesn't list, an assumed 100k (`DEFAULT_WINDOW_TOKENS`), less the output reserve (the request's `max_tokens`, at most half the window). **Past 70% of it** (`SOFT_PCT`), older rounds' tool results over 1,000 chars are replaced **in the request only**, oldest round first and a whole round at a time, until the estimate is back at 50% (`TARGET_PCT`, so the prompt-cache rewrite a stub costs stays rare). A stub is the result's head and tail (600 chars) with "… [N chars omitted to fit the model's context window — call recall_tool_output with message_id <row> for the full output]" (a result with no stored row says to re-run the tool instead); `budget::stub` is a pure function, so a stubbed request is byte-stable after it. The last two rounds are never stubbed (past 90%, `HARD_PCT`, only the last); assistant turns are never edited, so signed thinking goes out as it came and every tool_use keeps its result. Stored rows never change, and old threads read as before; on `talkEngine: "v2"` a stubbed result's stub becomes its row's model view, once, so later turns replay it (**Append-only transcript**). The Player shows it for 8 s: "Context window filling (118k of 200k tokens) — shortened 6 earlier tool results in this request; the model can recall them" ("of an assumed 100k tokens: the catalog doesn't list this model's window" for an unknown model; "as this model reported" for a reported window). **Calibration:** each answered request's real prompt size over its chars/3.5 estimate feeds a moving average (weight 0.3, each reading held to 0.25–4×), so a local model's tokenizer converges; a request that carries an image, or a server that reports no usage, gives no reading. Since earlier images stay in the conversation (#1159), a thread with a kept image sends one on nearly every request, so its requests give the calibration no reading until the budget has replaced every earlier image with `[image omitted]`. **A prompt too long:** a non-transient provider error in a documented context-length shape (`is_context_overflow`: the Anthropic API's "prompt is too long" and "exceed context limit", the OpenAI API's `context_length_exceeded` code and "maximum context length is" message, the llama.cpp server's `exceed_context_size_error`; a `max_tokens` above the model's output limit doesn't match) no longer ends the turn the first time in a round. The prompt size the error reports becomes a calibration reading; a lower window it reports (at least 4,096 tokens) becomes the one trusted for the model, except for an id that names its window (`[1m]`, never lowered). Without either figure, only the retry is sized for 85% of the estimate of the refused request, and nothing is kept. The request is stubbed to fit, with only the last round whole, and sent once more ("Prompt too long for this model — shortened 5 earlier tool results to fit 120k tokens, retrying once"). A second refusal in the same round, or one nothing can be stubbed for, ends the turn with the provider's error as before: a history from earlier turns that alone overfills the window still ends the turn (compaction is a later slice). The decision is `ContextGuard::after_failure` (save what was learned, retry once, else fail). A prompt that fits with its answer raises a lower learned window to that size, and clears it once it reaches the catalog's. What is learned (calibration, a reported window, and the catalog window it was lowered from) is kept per model in `app_meta` (`context_budget:<model>`, JSON); a lowered window stops applying once the catalog's window for the model changes (Settings › Models). The forced close passes the guard too. Sub-agents and Direct stages keep their own guard (Agentic loop internals), measured with the same `message_chars`. _Support:_ `context/budget.rs` (`ContextBudget::{for_model, with_fixed_window}`, `ContextGuard::{before_round, sent, observed, after_failure, stub_notice}`, `stub`, `is_context_overflow`, `load_learned`, `save_learned`), `chat_engine.rs` (`run_agentic_turn`, `guard_context`, `save_context_budget`). _Entry:_ automatic on a long Talk turn.
- **DB tables** — `chat_threads` (id, workspace_id FK, mission_id nullable, title, created_at, updated_at, mcp_disabled nullable, permission_mode nullable) and `chat_messages` (id, workspace_id FK, thread_id, role, content, model, input/output_tokens, cost_usd, created_at, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, context_tokens, context_blocks nullable: a user row's `@` block spans, #1150). Roles: `user, assistant, assistant_tool_use, tool, error, stopped`. `chat_agent_runs` (call_id PK, thread_id, workspace_id, message_id, spec_json, transcript_json, model, updated_at) holds each sub-agent run for continuation. `chat_tool_originals` (message_id PK → `chat_messages(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE, thread_id, content, total_bytes) holds the capped original of an MCP output for recall.
- **Provider routing** — `resolve_provider(model)` → `ProviderRouter::find_model` selects Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible, per-provider key + base-URL override.

---

## 4. RUN / Direct Mode (Pipeline Orchestration)

The flagship feature: compose pipelines of stages (each an AI agent with a role/model/substrate/tools/checkpoint/loop), run them, gate with checkpoints, iterate with review loops, recover from halts, and track cost/budget against an all-premium baseline.

### Pipelines — templates & authoring model
- **Pipeline templates** — A named, reusable graph of stages; each stage is one AI agent. Stored as templates, instantiated per-run. _Support:_ `pipelines` + `pipeline_stages` tables; `list_pipelines`, `get_pipeline`.
- **7 built-in pipelines (seeded, idempotent)** — `db.rs::seed_builtin_pipelines`: **Feature Factory** (plan→plan_review→implement✓→code_review✓ loop→test✓), **Bugfix relay** (repro→fix✓→verify✓ loop), **Plan & review** (plan→critique→refine✓, linear), **Ship it** (plan→implement✓→code_review✓ gated loop→test✓→**pull_request**✓ cli — the issue-to-PR crew), **Claude Code build** (plan(api)→implement(cli)✓→code_review(cli)✓ loop→test(cli)✓), **Greenfield** (prompt genesis — see below), and **Perf probe** (see below). Stage models come from the builtin lineup's tags (`provider_router::builtin_anthropic_model_tagged`): the stages that used Haiku 4.5 seed the `fast` tier (today `claude-haiku-5-5`): Feature Factory's plan, plan_review, code_review and test; Bugfix relay's repro and verify; Plan & review's critique; the plan, code_review and test stages of Ship it and Claude Code build; and Greenfield's "Review the increment". Every other stage, the ones that used Sonnet 4.6, seeds the `balanced` tier (`claude-sonnet-5-5`). That includes Plan & review's plan and refine, Greenfield's "Choose the stack", "Scaffold", "First increment" and "Verify honestly", and all three Perf probe stages. Only a fresh seed reads them; crews already in the database are never rewritten, so a saved crew's cost never changes silently. `every_suggested_model_is_a_builtin` fails if any seeded stage uses a legacy id. A one-shot UPDATE retrofits loop config onto pre-loop builtin installs.
- **Perf probe pipeline (the `perf` mission crew) — free** — Seeded by `seed_perf_probe_pipeline` (idempotent on the name). A **read-only** performance investigation the "Chase a regression" intent stages: **Measure** (`critique` role, tools overridden to `read_file`/`list_files`/`run_command`) → **Find the regression** (same read+run tools; identifies the slow function/query/allocation with evidence, comparing git history) → **Report** (`gated`; read-only tools; writes the findings as the stage artifact — the regression, the evidence, a *recommended* fix in words, and the honest boundary of what it could/couldn't measure).
