It never edits code (the `perf` mission is `readonly`, so the sandbox enforces it; the tool allowlists also omit `write_file`). **Read-only scope (honest):** because a readonly mission's sandbox confines writes to temp (not the workspace), the probe reads the code + git history and runs **existing** tooling — a benchmark that's already built, `time`, a profiler on a built binary, or complexity analysis. A run that must **compile fresh** (writing build artifacts into the workspace `target/`/`dist/`) is out of scope for a read-only mission — the probe says so in its honest-boundary note; to profile a fresh build, use a writer mission. To *apply* a fix, the director begins a `fix` mission. A normal builtin — forkable. _Support:_ `db.rs::seed_perf_probe_pipeline`; `MissionCreator` `perf` intent card; `PipelineSetup` intent→pipeline default. _Entry:_ a `perf` mission **default-selects** it in the Direct launcher (`INTENT_PIPELINE`); also pickable there.
- **Greenfield pipeline (prompt genesis crew) — free** — The builtin that knows how to be *born* into an empty repo, seeded by `seed_greenfield_pipeline` (idempotent on the name; carries per-stage `instructions`, so it seeds separately from the simple `defs`). The arc (director's G3 decisions: crew-chooses-the-stack, gated after the plan; ends at a **local repo**, never pushes/opens a PR): **plan** "Choose the stack" (**gated** ✓ — reads the brief, picks the *simplest* stack that satisfies it, proposes the structure + a first verifiable increment, and declares what it will NOT attempt; the director approves before any code) → **implement** "Scaffold" (structure + manifests + `.gitignore`, no features) → **implement** "First increment" (the smallest slice that actually runs) → **code_review** "Review the increment" (gated ×2 loop to the increment, bar = "a competent first slice") → **test** "Verify honestly" (runs what's runnable, then writes an honest `README.md`: how to run it, what was verified, and what could **not** be verified here — never overclaims). All-api (a new user has no `claude` CLI). Prompt genesis preselects this crew (`handleGenesis` resolves "Greenfield" ahead of Feature Factory). It's a normal builtin — appears in the launcher picker, forkable, library-syncs if forked. _Support:_ `db.rs::seed_greenfield_pipeline`; `App.handleGenesis` (preselect). _Entry:_ genesis stages it automatically; also selectable in the Direct launcher.
- **Custom pipelines (create / fork / update)** — `save_pipeline` has 3 modes: create new; **fork a builtin to a new custom copy** (builtin never mutated); update a custom in place (transactional). _Support:_ `save_pipeline`; `pipelineStore.save`. _Entry:_ builder "Save as my copy" / "Save pipeline".
- **Delete pipeline** — Custom only; builtins protected. _Support:_ `delete_pipeline`. _Entry:_ builder footer two-step.
- **Pipeline validation** — `validate_pipeline_stages`: ≥1 stage; role must exist; substrate ∈ {api,cli}; non-empty model; `max_iterations` 1..=100; parents form an acyclic DAG; tools a subset of `KNOWN_TOOLS`; instructions ≤ 8000 chars; loop config rules (target requires `can_loop` role, flow-ancestor, mode ∈ {gated,auto}, max loop-backs 1..=9 — `db::MAX_LOOP_ITERATIONS`, the same bound as the builder's "Max loop-backs" stepper, `builder/graph.ts::MAX_LOOP_ITERATIONS`). `pipeline_stage_issues` runs the same rules and returns every stage's first problem (the crew import's per-stage errors); it can count not-yet-saved roles as existing. _Support:_ `db.rs`.
- **Portable crews: export (Free)** — Any saved pipeline can leave the Mac as a versioned, human-readable `*.octocrew.json` file: `{ octocrew: 1, minApp, pipeline: { name, description, stages: StageDraft[] }, roles: RoleDef[] }`. `stages` is exactly the `save_pipeline` / `describe_pipeline_schema` contract (role, model, substrate, checkpoint, loops, max turns, effort, escalation, tools, custom name, instructions, parents, canvas position); `roles` holds only the **custom** roles the stages reference (built-ins ship with every Octopush). The file never carries API keys, provider URLs, workspace paths, pipeline ids or run history (tested). **Export crew…** opens a native save dialog from Rust (`bugfix-relay.octocrew.json` by default) and toasts the path; **Copy crew as JSON** puts the same text on the clipboard. Both export the pipeline as last saved. Library sync stays the Pro convenience; files are manual and Free. _Support:_ `crew.rs` (`export`, `to_json`, `file_name`); `export_crew`, `save_crew_file`; `lib/crew.ts` (`exportCrewFile`, `copyCrewJson`). _Entry:_ builder top-right toolbar (`Download` / `Copy` icons, saved pipelines only) · right-click a launcher pipeline ticket.
- **Portable crews: import is a review, never an execution** — A crew is prompt text plus tool permissions, so import opens a `ModalShell` review sheet and saves nothing until the user confirms. The sheet lists every stage: its label and **writer** or **read-only** (by the scheduler's own `orchestrator::stage_read_only` rule), then one wrapping row each (never one truncated line) for role, substrate (`runs on API` / `CLI`), model and effort, escalation (`escalates to <model> · effort <e>`), loop (`Loops back to stage N · auto · up to ×K`) and "waits for you" on checkpoints; "may commit, push and run release commands" for action roles; its full instructions in mono; and each custom role's full prompt. An **API** stage shows its tools (its allowlist, else the role's defaults) with `run_command` / `write_file` / `edit_file` called out in amber. The tool allowlist only applies on the API path, so a **CLI** stage shows no tool list: an amber line names the shell it really gets, by `cli_runner::dialect_for_model` (`Full shell · Claude Code (all permissions)` — `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; `Full shell · Codex (workspace-write sandbox)`, or `Shell · Codex (read-only sandbox)` for a read-only Codex review), and a `tools` list on a CLI stage is shown as a non-blocking warning. The stage header counts CLI stages (`N with a full shell (CLI)`), and an amber note says CLI stages run with the user's shell and git credentials and that Claude Code stages may also load the repo's `.claude/settings.json` hooks and `.mcp.json` servers. Models absent from the enabled providers' catalog or that the app can't price are listed under **models to check** as `not in your catalog · unpriced` (never as free), each with a `ModelPicker` replacement that re-previews and is applied on import (agent and escalation models). A role key that is taken here is **suffixed** (`triage` → `triage-2`) and the stages re-pointed, never overwritten (built-ins included); an identical custom role is reused. The file is untrusted (it may come from a cloned repo). `crew::parse` refuses text over 512 KB (pasted text too), more than 64 stages (`MAX_CREW_STAGES`) or 32 roles (`MAX_CREW_ROLES`). Every string field (name, description, role key, label, description and prompt, stage role, custom name, instructions, model ids, substrate, tools, loop mode) is checked for hidden characters — every Unicode `Cf` (format), `Zl` and `Zp` code point (a hand-written Unicode 15.1 table, `crew::CF_ZL_ZP`: bidi controls and marks, zero-width characters, tags, the BOM, soft hyphen, U+2028/2029 …), all variation selectors U+FE00–FE0F and U+E0100–E01EF (except the parts of an ordinary emoji, `crew::hidden_mask`: one U+FE0E/FE0F right after an emoji base or in a keycap, as in ⚠️ ✔️ ❤️ 1️⃣, and one U+200D between two Extended_Pictographic characters, the first maybe followed by its U+FE0F or skin tone, as in 👩‍💻, 🏳️‍🌈 or 👨🏽‍💻 — so a crew exported with emoji imports back; runs, other selectors and stray joiners still block), the combining grapheme joiner U+034F, Mongolian variation selectors U+180B–180F, the Hangul fillers U+115F/1160/3164/FFA0, and C0/C1 controls other than `\n` and `\t` — which block the import and are shown escaped (`\u{202e}`), never raw. Role keys in the file must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$`; labels, custom names and model ids are ≤ 128 characters, the name ≤ 120 and descriptions ≤ 2,000. A stage that names a role the file defines but can't import is blocked rather than falling back to a local role with that key (references are checked on the file's own keys before any rename). An imported role's `tokenEstIn` / `tokenEstOut` are reset to the local defaults (4,000 / 1,000), never trusted. The file then goes through the same validator as `save_pipeline`, plus role checks (key, label, prompt ≤ 32,000 chars, substrate, tools); an invalid crew shows each stage's first problem on the stage, naming the stage once (`crew::stage_message`: `Stage 1 instructions are too long …`, `Stage 2: unknown tool 'x'`; `save_pipeline`'s own messages are unchanged), and file-level problems at the top, and **Add this crew to my library** stays disabled. Newer formats or `minApp` versions are refused with an "update the app" sentence; a pre-release suffix is ignored in the comparison (`0.4.117-beta.2` counts as 0.4.117), and a build that reads format 1 always accepts the format's own floor. Export writes a fixed floor per format (`crew::CREW_MIN_APP` = 0.4.117, the first version that ships format 1), never the exporting app's own version, so teammates on different patch versions can share files. Confirming saves new roles and a new custom pipeline (rolled back if the save fails), reloads the library and toasts; it **never starts a run**, and the result is a normal editable custom pipeline. Ways in: palette **Import a crew…** (paste box + "choose a .octocrew.json file", which reads through `read_crew_file`: opened `O_NONBLOCK` so a FIFO can't hang the app, the opened handle must be a regular file ≤ 512 KB, at most 512 KB + 1 bytes are read, then UTF-8 decoded; the user's own pick may be a symlink), the launcher's **import a crew** link, dropping a `.json` file on the Direct launcher or the builder canvas, and pasting JSON into the sheet. _Support:_ `crew.rs` (`parse`, `preview`, `import`, `read_file`); `preview_crew`, `import_crew`, `read_crew_file`; `CrewImportSheet.tsx` (`CrewImportHost`, mounted in `App.tsx`); `stores/crewImportStore.ts`; `lib/crew.ts` (`openDroppedCrew`, `pickCrewFile`, `flaggedModels`).
- **Crews committed in the repo (`From this repo`)** — The Direct launcher lists `<worktree>/.octopush/crews/*.octocrew.json` (the same worktree-rooted discovery as `.claude/skills`) under **from this repo**: name and stage count, read-only. `list_repo_crews` returns names and counts only (description ≤ 280 characters, problem ≤ 240; a name with hidden characters lists the file name and the problem instead), never the file text; **Fork into my library** reads the file then through `read_repo_crew` (a plain `*.octocrew.json` name inside the folder, opened `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, same size cap) and opens the import review sheet on it; nothing runs from the repo file directly. The folder is re-read every time the launcher opens, so an edit on disk shows the next time; symlinks are skipped (symlinked files, and a symlinked `.octopush` or `.octopush/crews` folder lists nothing), at most 50 files are listed, and an invalid file is listed with its problem instead of hidden. _Support:_ `crew.rs` (`scan_repo`, `read_repo_crew`); `list_repo_crews`, `read_repo_crew`; `PipelineSetup.tsx`.

### Node-based visual pipeline builder
- **React Flow node graph (DAG authoring)** — Zoomable canvas (minZoom 0.4, maxZoom 1.75, fitView with a 10% margin a side on load and after Tidy, `FIT_PADDING`, written as a percentage because v13 reads a bare number as pixels; dotted brass bg, Controls, MiniMap) on `@xyflow/react` 13. It follows the **app** theme, never the macOS appearance: `forceColorMode` comes from the active theme's ground (`flowColorMode`: light for Vellum, dark for Onyx and until a theme is loaded), and the bare `.octo-flow` rule in `styles.css` sets every `--xy-*` variable the library would otherwise fill with its own `light-dark()` palette (pane, background pattern, edges, connection line, selection rectangle, edge labels, controls, minimap incl. mask and nodes, attribution, handles, default nodes) from tokens; `builder/flowTheme.test.ts` checks that rule against the installed library's stylesheet. A press on a stage becomes a drag only after `NODE_DRAG_THRESHOLD` (4px) of travel, so a click with a little jitter still selects and records no undo step. _Support:_ `PipelineBuilder.tsx`, `builder/flowTheme.ts`, `builder/graph.ts`, `builder/StageNode.tsx`, `builder/edges.tsx`. _Entry:_ DirectCanvas builder state.
- **Bottom-right view cluster (responsive minimap)** — Controls and MiniMap both dock bottom-right (Controls steps its bottom margin to clear the MiniMap when shown); the MiniMap fades out (opacity + `pointer-events:none`, 220ms) once the flow wrapper's own width drops below 560px, tracked live via a `ResizeObserver` on the canvas (not the window, so it reacts to the stage dock opening/closing too). _Support:_ `PipelineBuilder.tsx` (`MINIMAP_MIN_CANVAS`, `canvasWidth`, `miniMapShown`).
- **Stage nodes** — 228px card: role icon (`lib/roleIcons.ts` `iconForRole`, brass when selected else sage) + title + "{archetype} · {shortModel}" (a brass "· {effort}" is appended when reasoning effort is set, and a brass "· ↑ {model}" when an escalation policy is set); a checkpointed stage's `⟜` gate mark sits in the header, just before the icon; substrate chip (cli=purple/api=blue); 4 sage tool dots; validation marker; remove X (last-node guard). _Support:_ `StageNode.tsx`.
- **Add / connect / remove stages** — Add via palette drag (`application/octopush-archetype`) or click-to-add; connect by dragging handles (rejects self-connection, duplicate edges, cycles via `flowAncestors`); remove blocked below 1 stage. _Support:_ `graph.ts` `topoOrder` (Kahn sort), `flowAncestors`.
- **Flow & loop edges** — `FlowEdge` = brass smooth-step hairline with arrowhead; `LoopEdge` = dashed brass arc with centered `⟲ ×{loopMax}` pill (+ `· auto`). _Support:_ `builder/edges.tsx`.
- **Edge hover/select states, disconnect & reconnect-drag** — Edge strokes are CSS-owned (`.octo-flow` block) so interaction can restyle them: a calm `brass-rule-dim` hairline at rest (loop = dashed `brass-dim`), `brass-line` on hover, full brass when selected, plus a forgiving ±8px grab halo around each 9px handle. A selected edge draws above the cards (v13's `elevateEdgesOnSelect` default, kept: when several edges share a handle, the selected one's reconnect anchor is the one that takes the drag). A selected edge shows a midpoint ✕ pill (`DisconnectPill`, works on loop edges too — offset above the `⟲` badge so both stay legible) or **Backspace/Delete** (`deleteKeyCode`) to disconnect. Dragging an edge's end onto the pane **deletes** it; dragging onto another handle **re-routes** it, guarded by `reconnectAllowed` (mirrors the connect rules — no self-link, no duplicate, no cycle; a loop edge keeps its review-stage source and may only retarget within that stage's flow-ancestors). _Support:_ `builder/edges.tsx` (`DisconnectPill`), `builder/graph.ts` (`reconnectAllowed`), `styles.css` `.octo-flow` edge rules, `PipelineBuilder.tsx` (`onReconnect`/`onReconnectStart`/`onReconnectEnd`/`onDisconnectEdge`).
- **Node palette (collapsible)** — 188px "Stages" well; roles grouped "Plan & design"/"Build"/"Review"/"Action"/"Your roles"; each item draggable, with a role icon, Lock(builtin)/`custom` badge, `⟲` loop marker, hover "Fork & edit"; footer "New role"; list capped `max-h-[min(48vh,420px)]` so it never overruns a short window. Collapses on demand to a "Stages" pill (`ChevronsUpDown` to expand / `ChevronsDownUp` to collapse), open state owned by the builder so it survives re-renders. _Support:_ `NodePalette.tsx`, `PipelineBuilder.tsx` (`paletteOpen`).
- **Docked stage inspector** — A 320px column outside the flow canvas's own overflow (`PipelineBuilder.tsx`'s dock `div`, structurally unclippable by the canvas or the footer bar), full height, scrolling internally. Opens when a node is selected, animates its width in/out (280ms `ease-[var(--ease-octo)]`), and keeps its content mounted through the close transition so it never pops. Closes via **Escape** (suppressed while the Role Editor modal owns it), clicking the canvas pane, or its own **✕**. Body is grouped into sections — Identity (Name, Archetype), Engine (Model, Reasoning, **Escalate on failure**), Execution (Substrate, Approval gate, Tools, Max turns), Instructions, and a `⟲ Loop` section revealed for `can_loop` archetypes — with the escalation controls (model picker + effort segment, ~180px most stages never touch) collapsed behind an "Escalate on failure" disclosure (chevron rotates open, a brass dot marks it configured). _Support:_ `PipelineBuilder.tsx` (`dockOpen`/`dockNode`), `StageInspector.tsx`, `primitives/Reveal.tsx`.
- **Live graph validation** — Mirrors the backend; blockers (no nodes, flow cycle, no model, max-turns out of range, empty/unknown tools, loop on non-review, multiple loops per source, loop target not a flow-ancestor) and amber warnings (CLI without a Claude model, `diff` artifact without `write_file`, `tests` without write/run, orphan node, auto-loop note). Save disabled while any blocker stands. _Support:_ `builder/graph.ts` `validateGraph`.
- **Graph ↔ backend serialization** — `graphToStageDrafts` compiles canvas → position-based `StageDraft[]` (topo-ordered, parents mapped, loop derived, `tools=null` for CLI, coords round-tripped); `draftToGraph` reopens a saved pipeline (legacy no-parents → auto-laid-out linear chain). _Support:_ `builder/graph.ts`.
- **Undo / redo** — A pure snapshot stack (`GraphSnapshot{nodes,edges}`, 100-deep cap) records the graph **before** every mutation — add node, connect, patch a node's data (coalesced per field-set so a typing burst is one step), set/clear a loop, drag a node (pre-drag position; a click is not a drag, see `NODE_DRAG_THRESHOLD`), and delete (node ✕, Backspace on nodes/edges) — and clears the redo stack on a new action. Top-right canvas toolbar: ghost Undo/Redo icon buttons, disabled at the stack ends. `⌘Z` / `⇧⌘Z` (`Ctrl` elsewhere) fire the same actions, suppressed while a text input/textarea/contenteditable has focus so field-native undo isn't hijacked. _Support:_ `builder/history.ts` (`createHistory`/`pushSnapshot`/`undo`/`redo`/`canUndo`/`canRedo`), `PipelineBuilder.tsx` (`pushHistory`/`applyUndo`/`applyRedo`).
- **Tidy auto-layout** — `tidyLayout` re-lays the graph on a layered grid: depth = longest flow-path from an entry node (topological order via Kahn's sort), one row per depth top-to-bottom; within a row, nodes **keep their current left-to-right order** so the author's arrangement survives the tidy. A cyclic flow is a no-op (validation already blocks save on cycles). Triggered from the top-right toolbar's `Network` icon; animates via `.octo-flow--tidying` (node-transform transition, actively-dragged nodes excluded, respects `prefers-reduced-motion`) then `fitView`s once positions settle; recorded as a **single** undo step. _Support:_ `builder/graph.ts` (`tidyLayout`, `TIDY_ROW_GAP`/`TIDY_COL_GAP`), `PipelineBuilder.tsx` (`runTidy`), `styles.css` (`.octo-flow--tidying`).
- **First-use connect hint chip** — A bottom-center chip ("Drag from a stage's edge to connect it") appears once ≥2 stages exist with no flow edge between any of them; dismissible via its own ✕ (persists `octo.builder.hint.connect` to `localStorage` so it never reappears) or implicitly once the author connects a first edge; fades in/out by opacity rather than mounting/unmounting. _Support:_ `PipelineBuilder.tsx` (`HINT_KEY`, `hintVisible`).

### Stage roles & the role editor
- **15 built-in roles (data-driven, seeded)** — `orchestrator/roles.rs::builtin_roles`: `plan, plan_review(loop), implement, code_review(loop), test, repro, fix, verify(loop), critique(loop), refine, architect, security_review(loop), pull_request(action/cli), merge(action/cli), release(action/cli)`. Each `RoleDef` carries label, prompt_body, artifact_kind, environment, can_loop, default_tools, default_substrate, default_checkpoint, token estimates. Builtins are **upserted on every migrate**, so prompt improvements reach existing installs. _Support:_ `roles` table; `list_roles`; `rolesStore`.
- **Prompt quality doctrine (crew-output-quality pass)** — Every producing role carries an **output contract** (named sections the next stage relies on: plan → Goal/Files/Steps/Edge cases/Acceptance criteria; repro → Repro/Root cause/Fix direction) and a definition of done (implement: build/lint/test if available, no stubs/TODOs, no drive-by refactors). Every reviewing role carries a **BLOCKING-vs-MINOR severity rubric**, a verify-before-reporting bar, and **"nits alone never send work back"** (anti rubber-stamp + anti nitpick-loop). `fix`/`verify`/`critique` are **purpose-specific** (fix targets the reproduced ROOT CAUSE; verify confirms **by execution** — re-runs the repro + suite; critique reviews any artifact, not just plans). `test` must **actually run** the suite ("running is not optional"). Action roles gained safety bars (PR: never commit secrets/junk; merge: never on red/pending checks, proceeds with a note when the repo has none; release: abort on dirty tree). Guarded by tests (`builtin_role_prompts_are_purpose_specific_not_clones`, `reviewer_prompts_carry_a_severity_rubric_and_anti_rubber_stamp_bar`). _Support:_ `roles.rs`.
- **Artifact kinds** — `Plan | Review | Tests | Diff | Note`; determines dossier labels and whether the artifact refs the worktree. _Support:_ `orchestrator/types.rs`.
- **Role environment contract** — `Worktree` = headless worker, never touches git (`PREAMBLE_WORKTREE`); `Action` = may commit/push/run git/gh/release (`PREAMBLE_ACTION`, defaults to CLI + checkpoint). _Support:_ `RoleEnvironment`; `compose_system_prompt`.
- **Read-only roles (repro, verify, reviewers)** — A role whose artifact is `review` in the `Worktree` environment is read-only (`read_only::role_is_read_only`): the builtins `repro`, `verify`, `plan_review`, `code_review`, `critique` and `security_review`, plus any custom role of that shape. Such a stage investigates, runs and reports; it never edits files or writes git history (#847: a Bugfix relay's Reproduce and Verify stages had each applied the change and committed it). It may still run commands, since a reproducer runs the failing scenario, a verifier re-runs the repro and the suite and a reviewer runs the build. Four layers: (1) every substrate's system prompt carries `roles::READ_ONLY_CLAUSE` right after the preamble ("do not create, edit, move or delete files… no commit, add, stash, reset, checkout, restore, merge, rebase or push… scratch scripts go in a temp dir outside the workspace"), and `repro`'s own prompt adds "Do not fix it yourself or modify files"; (2) **API** stages lose `write_file`/`edit_file` from their effective allowlist, whatever the stage's own list says (a seeded builtin stage has no list, which used to mean the full set); when a custom role's saved allowlist did include them, the stage journal says so ("This role is read-only, so `write_file`, `edit_file` were removed from its tool allowlist for this stage", `read_only::stripped_write_tools_notice`, on either substrate). `read_only::ReadOnlyGitGate` refuses, with an error tool result, a `write_file`/`edit_file` call anyway (API execution dispatches tools by name without checking the allowlist) and a `run_command` that runs a git write (`git_write_in`: `add, am, apply, checkout, cherry-pick, clean, commit, merge, mv, pull, push, rebase, reset, restore, revert, rm, stash, switch`; global options like `-C`/`-c`/`--git-dir`/`--work-tree`/`--attr-source` are skipped, with their value whether it is joined by `=` or a separate argument; quoted text is never read as a command but still counts as one word, so a quoted value (`git --git-dir "/w/.git" commit`) is skipped like any other; `status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`, `branch`, `stash list` and `stash show` stay allowed); (3) **Claude Code** stages deny `Write,Edit,MultiEdit,NotebookEdit` plus one `Bash(git <sub>:*)` rule per git write above in `--disallowedTools` (fresh and `--resume`d, `cli_runner::review_disallowed_tools`). Bash rules are prefix rules, so `stash` gets its write forms instead (`read_only::CLI_STASH_DENY_RULES`: `Bash(git stash)` for the bare command, `Bash(git stash -*)` for an option-led push like `-u`, and `push`, `save`, `pop`, `apply`, `drop`, `clear`, `branch`, `store`, `create`, `import`, `export`), which leaves `git stash list`/`show` allowed; options placed before the subcommand (`git -C dir stash pop`) can't be expressed as a prefix rule and slip past every git rule alike; (4) **Codex** stages run in `--sandbox read-only`. A shell command can still write a file (`echo >> f`) or hide git behind `sh -c`, so it is a guardrail, not a sandbox: the orchestrator's "⚠ this stage created git commit(s)" journal notice stays as the backstop. Writer roles are unchanged: `implement`, `fix`, `refine`, `test` (Tests writes the test files it runs), the plan-kind roles, and the action roles (`pull_request`, `merge`, `release`), which commit by design. _Support:_ `orchestrator/read_only.rs`, `roles.rs` (`READ_ONLY_CLAUSE`, `compose_stage_system_prompt`), `runner.rs`, `cli_runner.rs` (`review_disallowed_tools`), `orchestrator/mod.rs` (the stripped-tools notice).
- **Tool presets** — `ro()`=[read_file,list_files,grep,glob], `run_()`=+run_command, `full()`=+write_file+edit_file+run_command. **Reviewers can execute:** `code_review` and `security_review` carry `run_()` (not `ro()`) so they can run `git diff`/grep/the test suite to verify what they certify (crew-quality pass); with `grep`/`glob` in `ro()`, even read-only reviewers (`plan_review`, `critique`) can locate and verify code instead of paging directories. _Support:_ `roles.rs`.
- **Workspace tool surface (API substrate)** — Seven tools (`KNOWN_TOOLS`): `read_file` (with optional `offset`/`limit` line windows for large files; char-boundary-safe truncation), `list_files`, **`grep`** (recursive regex content search respecting `.gitignore`, with path/glob/case filters and capped results), **`glob`** (recursive file finding by pattern), `write_file`, **`edit_file`** (exact-string replacement with a uniqueness guard and `replace_all` — targeted edits that can't drop the rest of a file; sandbox-aware), and `run_command` (**bounded**: default 600s wall-clock timeout, per-call `timeout_secs` up to 3600, process-group kill, director-cancel poll — a hung command can no longer freeze a stage). Tools execute off-thread (`spawn_blocking`) so a slow tool never pins the tokio runtime. **Back-compat allowlist expansion:** stage allowlists saved before the new tools existed keep working — read access implies `grep`/`glob`, `write_file` implies `edit_file` (resolved in `run_agentic_loop`). _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs` (`execute_tool_cancellable`, `tool_definitions`), `db.rs::KNOWN_TOOLS`, `agentic.rs` allowlist expansion, builder `graph.ts::TOOLS`, `RoleEditor` `TOOL_KEYS`, `ToolCallCard` labels.
- **Custom role editor** — Conversational "prompt-as-hero" modal: name (auto-derives snake_case key), key, environment flip, description, prompt body, and a natural-language brief with inline `ChipMenu` dropdowns (artifact kind, environment, tools, loop, substrate, checkpoint). Built-ins always fork on save. _Support:_ `RoleEditor.tsx`; `save_role`. _Entry:_ palette "New role" / edit pencil.
- **Delete role (referential-integrity guarded)** — Rejects builtin deletion and any role still referenced. _Support:_ `delete_role`.

### Stage substrates & execution
- **API substrate (in-app agentic loop)** — `ApiRunner` runs a stage through `run_agentic_loop`: resolves provider, composes system prompt, builds the input dossier, runs a tool-use loop bounded by `max_iterations`, returns exact token usage + cost. _Support:_ `orchestrator/runner.rs`, `agentic.rs`.
- **Per-stage reasoning effort (the cost/quality lever)** — Each stage carries an optional `effort` (`Effort` enum: `low·medium·high·xhigh·max`; `null`/absent = **off**, no thinking — today's default). It's **editor-set** in the pipeline builder (the Stage inspector's Reasoning control) — and equally **authorable over `octopush-mcp`** (`create_pipeline`/`update_pipeline`, documented in `describe_pipeline_schema`) — persisted on `pipeline_stages`, copied to `run_stages` at `create_run`, and read into `StageSpec.effort` → `LlmRequest.effort`. It's the atomic knob the cost model rests on: a cheap model thinking deeply on synthesis stages, barely thinking on mechanical ones. **On the CLI substrate it reaches Claude Code** (#475): a Claude Code stage gets `--effort <level>` appended to `claude -p` (fresh and `--resume` runs alike, `CliDialect::effort_args`), and an inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` — which Claude Code ranks above `--effort` — is removed from that stage's environment (`CliDialect::stage_env_remove`, after the login-shell env) so the stage's own level wins. The same level is also set as `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT` (`CliDialect::stage_effort_env`, over any inherited export), because Claude Code no longer carries `--effort` to subagents on another model — so a `low` stage's Explore/Task subagents don't run at a higher default; a subagent's own `effort` frontmatter still wins, and a CLI older than 2.1.316 just ignores the variable. A stage with no effort passes no flag and no variable and keeps the CLI's per-model default (and the user's export, if any), which is why its null segment reads **Auto** (not Off) on a Claude Code stage. The launch notice names it (`launching claude · {model} · {level} effort`). A Claude Code older than the tested floor (`TESTED_CLAUDE_FLOOR`, the recorded `claude --help` that lists `--effort`) never gets the flag — the journal says the stage runs at the CLI's default — and the inspector folds the control away (`Reveal`) and folds in "Update Claude Code (x.y.z or newer) to set reasoning on this stage." in its place (`lib/claudeCli.ts` `cliTooOldForEffort`, the same version probe as the launcher's update note). **Codex CLI stages take effort too** (#613), as the one-off config override `-c model_reasoning_effort="<level>"`, placed before the trailing `-` (prompt from stdin) in `codex exec`'s argv (`CliDialect::effort_args` / `push_effort_args`); Codex resolves `--config` overrides above its config file. Codex's levels vary by model and Codex sends the level to the API unchanged, so the level is **clamped to what the model lists in Codex's bundled model catalog** (`supported_reasoning_levels` in openai/codex `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json`, copied with its commit into `src/lib/codexEffortLevels.json` — one table read by `cli_runner::codex_effort_level` via `include_str!` and by `lib/claudeCli.ts` `codexEffortLevel`): a listed level passes unchanged, an unlisted one becomes the highest listed level below it, or the lowest listed one when none is below (`clamp_to_listed_levels`, mirrored by `clampToListedLevels`; e.g. `max` → `xhigh` on `gpt-5.5`; `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra`, the `gpt-5.6-*` models and `codex-auto-review` list `max`; `gpt-6.2-astra` and `gpt-6.2-sol` aren't in the copy, so a Codex stage on them gets no override and its control is disabled, as below). The model id is matched the way Codex matches it: case-insensitively, the **longest catalog slug that prefixes the id** (so `gpt-5.5-2026-03-01` gets `gpt-5.5`'s levels), then once more with one leading `namespace/` stripped (`openai/gpt-5.5`; `a/b/gpt-5.5` stays unknown) (`codex_effort_levels` / `codexEffortLevels`). A model missing from the catalog (e.g. `gpt-5-codex`, `o3`, `o4-mini`) or one listing no levels gets **no** `-c` override at all and keeps Codex's own default, and the journal says so — "{model} isn't in Octopush's copy of Codex's model catalog" or "lists no reasoning levels in Codex's model catalog" (`CliDialect::unpassed_effort_notice`); no effort passes nothing either. No environment variable is set or removed for Codex. The control on a Codex stage reads Auto…Max (Auto: "Codex's own default effort for this model"; a segment the model doesn't list says what it runs as, `codexClampTitle`: "Runs as XHi on this model in Codex, the highest level it lists below Max" on `gpt-5.5`, or "…, the lowest level it lists" when clamped up; on a model without known levels the control is disabled and says it runs at Codex's default — the reason sits on a non-disabled wrapper the pointer passes through to, since WebKit may not hover a disabled button), and never shows the Claude Code update hint. The journal's launch line names the level the CLI gets (`launching codex · gpt-5.5 · xhigh effort`). One rule decides where effort applies — `cli_runner::effort_applies(substrate, model)` (mirrored by `lib/claudeCli.ts` `effortApplies`): API always, CLI on Claude Code, and on Codex for a model the catalog lists with levels; the brass effort pill on `StageNode`, `StageFlow` (judged on the launcher's model override) and `RunFlow` (judged on the model the stage ran on — `escalateModel` once it escalated) follows it. A contract test checks `--effort` and all five level tokens against the recorded `claude --help`; Codex contract tests pin the `-c` override's place and form, with and without an effort, the per-catalog `max` mapping, and that a model outside the catalog gets no `-c`. **Model-capability mapping** (pure, unit-tested, Anthropic): effort-capable models (Opus 4.6–5.5, Sonnet 4.6–5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5–5.2, Mythos 5–5.2; Opus 4.5 is not one, see below) get `output_config.effort:"<level>"` + `thinking:{type:"adaptive"}`, where the **level is clamped per model** (`effective_effort_level`) so we never 400 — only Opus 4.7/4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5 accept `xhigh`; Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 (the default) fold `xhigh`→`high` but keep `max`; an unknown effort-path id folds both `xhigh` and `max`→`high`. The models whose only thinking mode is the manual budget form and which reject `adaptive` with a 400 (`opus-4-5`, `haiku-4-5`, `sonnet-4-5`, `sonnet-4-0`, per Claude's per-model thinking table; Opus 4.5 used to be on the adaptive path, which 400s) instead get `thinking:{type:"enabled", budget_tokens:N}` (N = low 4096 / med 8192 / high 16384 / xhigh·max 24576, clamped `[1024, max_tokens-1]`) with **no** `output_config`. A model that can't be checked against those tables is in no list and gets no effort. Classification is a strict **allowlist** (`is_effort_model` / `is_budget_model`): a legacy (`claude-3-5-*`) or unknown id matches neither, so it gets **no thinking params at all** (effort silently ignored — never 400 a non-thinker). `temperature` is never sent (current models 400 on it with thinking). Effort also raises the `max_tokens` floor (`max_tokens_for`: none/low/med 32768 · high 48000 · xhigh/max 64000) so deep thinking doesn't truncate the answer. With thinking + tool use, a completed assistant turn's **full content-block array is captured verbatim and replayed in order** (`LlmResponse.raw_content` → `AssistantWithTools.raw`) so signed thinking survives and interleaved thinking/tool_use ordering is preserved (reordering 400s); the max_tokens-truncation retry path never replays a cut-off turn verbatim (it can carry an unsigned partial thinking block): it rebuilds from text + tool_uses, with the turn's leading signed `thinking` / `redacted_thinking` blocks kept in front, since with a thinking budget on the API rejects an assistant turn that doesn't start with one (`providers::truncated_round_turn`, the same helper Talk's director uses). OpenAI-compat maps `effort` → `reasoning_effort` **only on reasoning models** (o1/o3/o4, GPT-5, GPT-6 — omitted on gpt-4o): GPT-6 takes all five levels as-is (on the Responses API, as `reasoning.effort`), the o-series and GPT-5 fold xhigh·max to high (`reasoning_effort_level`); **effort off on GPT-6** (on the Responses API, i.e. `api.openai.com`) is `reasoning.effort: "none"` on GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6.1 Terra (bare id or a dated `-YYYY-MM-DD` snapshot only; another suffix such as `gpt-6-sol-pro` is treated as a different model), while GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol and any other GPT-6 id get no `reasoning` (they 400 on `none`) and so run at OpenAI's default, `medium` (`effort_off_level`); a GPT-6 id behind a gateway (Chat Completions, any host but `api.openai.com`) gets the stage's effort as `reasoning_effort`, all five levels as-is, while Off sends nothing there (`effort_off_level` is used only on the Responses path), so it runs at `medium`. The API inspector's Off segment and the Reasoning label's tooltip say which applies to the stage's model (`lib/apiEffort.ts` `apiEffortOffTitle`, mirroring `effort_off_level`); it picks the token-cap key by class: reasoning models use `max_completion_tokens` (they 400 on `max_tokens`; `max_output_tokens` on the Responses API), chat models use `max_tokens`; both pass through unclamped. _Support:_ `providers/mod.rs` (`Effort`, `raw_content`), `providers/anthropic.rs` (`is_effort_model`/`is_budget_model`/`effective_effort_level`/`thinking_json`), `providers/openai_compat.rs` (`openai_supports_reasoning`), `orchestrator/agentic.rs` (`max_tokens_for`), `db.rs` (`effort` column on `pipeline_stages`/`run_stages`), `builder/StageInspector.tsx`. Design record: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-14-per-stage-effort-design.md`.
- **Automatic model escalation (per stage)** — A stage can carry an optional **escalation policy** — `escalate_model` (a stronger model to retry with) and/or `escalate_effort` (a higher effort to bump to on the retry; it applies wherever base effort does — API, Claude Code and Codex CLI stages). A stage **has a policy iff either field is set**. It's **editor-set** in the Stage inspector's **"Escalate on failure"** control (an escalate-model picker with a "— none —" clear + an escalate-effort segmented control that follows the base effort's rules, judged on the escalation model — enabled for Claude Code and Codex, hidden on a too-old Claude Code) — and equally **authorable over `octopush-mcp`** (`create_pipeline`/`update_pipeline`, documented in `describe_pipeline_schema`) — persisted on `pipeline_stages`, copied to `run_stages` at `create_run`. **Trigger = a stage FAILS** (`StageStatus::Failed` — includes the agentic loop exhausting `max_iterations` unfinished): the drive's Failed arm calls `try_escalate`, which retries the stage **once** at the strong tier before halting — "pay the expensive tier on a *proven* failure, not by default". `try_escalate` re-reads the fresh stage row (the Failed arm's clone is pre-run state) and mirrors the re-run reset the reject/loop-back paths use: it **archives** the failed base-tier attempt to `stage_iterations`, **retires** its spend (so `recompute_run_cost` keeps counting it and the budget gate stays honest), **resets** the stage to pending **preserving** the existing feedback (and loop counter/session), sets the sticky `escalated` flag, and appends a live journal notice (`↑ Escalating to {model} after a failed attempt`); the drive `continue`s and re-runs the now-pending stage. It escalates only when the tier would ACTUALLY change (`escalate_model` ≠ base, or an `escalate_effort` ≠ base where effort applies — API, or a CLI stage — judged on the escalation model, and on the CLI by the level each CLI actually gets (so `xhigh` → `max` on a Codex model that doesn't list `max`, like `gpt-5.5`, is no change, and an effort-only bump on a model outside Codex's catalog is none either) — unless the escalation model runs on Claude Code and the session's cached `claude --version` is older than the floor, where `--effort` is dropped; `escalation_changes_tier`, shared with the loop-cap escalation) — an old-Claude-Code effort-only policy, or a same-model one, halts instead of burning an identical retry. **Spec resolution** (`run_stage_once`): an escalated stage resolves `agent_model` = `escalate_model` (falling back to the base when only effort was bumped) and `effort` = `escalate_effort.or(base)` — the **base fields stay on the row** for history/display. **Bounded to exactly one escalation**: a second failure hits `try_escalate` → already-escalated → halt. Because the flag is sticky, any later re-run (a review loop-back, a manual reject) also uses the strong tier for free. **`escalate_model` applies to BOTH substrates** (a plain model swap on the spec; the CLI runner reads `agent_model` too); **`escalate_effort` applies to the API and to CLI stages** (Claude Code's `--effort`, Codex's `-c model_reasoning_effort`). **A blocked stage (`ask_director` → `awaiting_checkpoint`) and an aborted run NEVER escalate** — only the Failed arm calls `try_escalate`. **Budget/detached-compatible for free**: the per-run budget gate runs before a stage starts (an escalated retry over budget pauses for budget), and escalation converts a would-be-halt into a `continue` within the same drive segment, so a detached worker re-runs the escalated stage in-segment exactly as the in-process app does. A run-stage that escalated shows a brass `↑ {model}` badge on its `RunFlow` meta line; the authoring surfaces (`StageNode`, `StageFlow`) show the policy as a brass `↑ {model}` hint. **Ungated** (a reliability property, like per-stage effort and the escape valve). _Support:_ `orchestrator/mod.rs` (`try_escalate`, `drive_inner` Failed arm, `run_stage_once` spec resolution), `db.rs` (`escalate_model`/`escalate_effort` on `pipeline_stages`+`run_stages`, `escalated` on `run_stages`, `set_run_stage_escalated`, `RunStageRow`/`PipelineStageRow`/`StageDraft`), `builder/StageInspector.tsx` + `builder/graph.ts`, `RunFlow.tsx`/`direct/StageFlow.tsx`/`builder/StageNode.tsx` badges, `lib/ipc.ts`. Design record: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-14-auto-escalation-design.md`.
- **Agentic loop internals** — Per-stage tool allowlist (with implied-grant expansion for the newer tools; the API substrate only — a CLI stage ignores it and runs with a full shell); transient-error retry with backoff + journal narration; proactive rate-limit throttle; tool results capped at 24KB fed back; cancel flag checked each iteration **and threaded into `run_command`** (a director stop kills an in-flight command's process group). **Context-window guard:** before each request the history estimate (chars/4, `context::budget::message_chars`) is checked against the model's `max_context` from the provider catalog (conservative default when unknown, `DEFAULT_WINDOW_TOKENS`); past 70% fill (`SOFT_PCT`) the OLDEST tool results are compacted to a stub with a "re-run the tool if needed" marker (newest 4 messages never touched) — small-window models no longer die mid-stage on an unfixable context 400. **Forced close at the cap:** exhausting `max_iterations` triggers ONE final tool-less request ("write your final answer with what you have"); a real answer completes the stage with the artifact annotated as possibly incomplete instead of discarding the work — an empty/failed close keeps the old failure path. _Support:_ `agentic.rs` (`compact_history`, forced-close tail), `runner.rs` (closed-at-cap annotation).
- **Repo conventions reach API stages** — Every API-substrate stage's system prompt carries the workspace's `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`/`CONVENTIONS.md` (capped; mirrored files deduped by content) — the CLI reads these itself, but a non-Claude implementer used to work blind to the project's rules. Each file is read like Talk's instructions (`request_context::read_memory_file`): one that resolves outside the workspace (a symlink out of it) or is over 4 MiB is skipped. _Support:_ `runner.rs::repo_conventions_section`.
- **Inter-stage consultation (`ask_stage`)** — An API stage with completed upstream stages carries an `ask_stage` tool: the question is answered by the PEER stage's own model (one-shot, tool-less) seeded with its archived artifact + journal digest — asking the mind that did the work instead of guessing from its paper. Peers follow the dossier's ancestry rule; consultation spend is priced at the peer model's rate and folded into the asking stage's cost and budget check; failures come back as error tool results. _Support:_ `agentic.rs` (`PeerStage`, `ask_stage_tool`, `answer_ask_stage`), `StageContext.peers` built in `run_stage_once`.
- **CLI dialects (multi-provider CLI substrate)** — The stage's MODEL selects which CLI runs a `cli`-substrate stage: `claude-*` → **Claude Code** (unchanged), OpenAI-family ids (`gpt-*`, `o1/o3/o4*`, `codex*`) → **Codex CLI** (`codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check -m <model> -C <worktree>`, prompt via stdin with the system prompt inlined — codex has no system-prompt flag (`-C` names the stage's worktree, so a resume on Codex 0.172.0+, which otherwise restores the thread's saved working directory, never runs elsewhere); read-only reviews map to codex's native `--sandbox read-only` (refused inside a sandboxed mission, see below); writers run in codex's own `--sandbox workspace-write`, with the rest set by `-c` config overrides (the mechanism the effort already uses, so no flag `codex exec` might reject): `approval_policy="never"`, so they never stop for an approval prompt; `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true`, so `gh` and package downloads reach the network (Octopush's own Seatbelt profile also confines writes only). A writer's commands may write the worktree, codex's temp dirs (`$TMPDIR`, `/tmp`) and one more root: the stage's own **build cache**. Codex's sandbox can't write `~/.npm` or `~/.cargo`, so the runner gives the stage the same cache redirect a sandboxed mission gets (`CARGO_HOME`, `npm_config_cache`, `YARN_CACHE_FOLDER`, pnpm's store, `GOPATH`/`GOCACHE`/`GOMODCACHE`, `GRADLE_USER_HOME`, `DENO_DIR`, `PIP_CACHE_DIR`), pointing into `~/Library/Caches/octopush/build-cache/<workspace>/<mode>` (0700, in the workspace's cache dir and kept apart from a sandboxed mission's root, `sandbox::codex_build_cache`; removed with the workspace or after 30 days unused), and adds that root with `-c sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=["<root>"]` (`cli_runner::codex_writable_root_args`). So `npm install` and `cargo build` work in the stage without it touching the user's real caches or `~/.cargo/config.toml`; if the root can't be made, the journal says so and the stage runs without it. **Git can't write in these stages:** codex keeps `<worktree>/.git` and the gitdir it resolves to read-only, and a linked worktree's objects and refs live in the common dir outside the worktree, so `git add`, `commit`, `stash`, `fetch`, `checkout -b` and therefore `git push` fail in every Codex writer stage outside a sandboxed mission. Octopush doesn't widen that on purpose: codex's writable roots can't deny a path inside a root the way the Seatbelt rules do, and a linked worktree's git dir holds `commondir` and `config.worktree`, which would let a stage point git at config and hooks it planted. An Action role (one that may commit and push) on such a stage is warned about twice: before the run, the Direct launcher shows an amber line under the foot ("Ship runs on Codex, whose sandbox keeps .git read-only, so it can't commit or push. Pick a Claude model for it.", `lib/claudeCli.ts::codexCommitNote`, with the launcher's model overrides and the mission's isolation; the run can still begin), and the stage journal repeats it at launch ("… Give this stage a Claude model.", `cli_runner::codex_git_notice`). A Claude model avoids it; so does a sandboxed mission, but both lines recommend only a Claude model until a sandboxed Codex mission (fresh and resumed) has been checked on a Mac. On top of codex's own protection, the runner checks the worktree's `.git` entry (for a linked worktree, its `gitdir:` pointer file): it records the entry before the stage (`sandbox::GitEntry`) and, after it, `sandbox::restore_git_entry` compares it. If the pointer file changed, the changed entry is moved to `.git.changed-by-stage` and the original written back before anything runs git there, and the stage fails with a message saying so, keeping its spend (`cli_runner::fail_keeping_usage`). A main checkout's `.git` dir that becomes something else fails the stage with a "don't run git there" message, and a plain dir that gains a `.git` is left alone. The choices are `cli_runner::codex_write_scope` / `guards_git_entry`, unit-tested; the restore is tested on a real linked worktree. Only inside a sandboxed mission (`exec_isolation = "sandbox"`) does a writer get `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`: Octopush's Seatbelt profile confines the process, and such a stage runs with its own `CODEX_HOME` and an unsandboxed sign-in preflight (see Sandboxed execution; not yet checked with a real `codex exec`). Codex's own Seatbelt can't nest inside the profile (a nested `sandbox-exec` fails with EPERM, pinned by a macOS test), so a **read-only** Codex stage in a sandboxed or readonly mission is refused at launch ("A read-only Codex stage can't run in a sandboxed mission yet. Give this stage a Claude model.", `cli_runner::codex_read_only_refusal`), and the Direct launcher shows the same line in amber before the run begins (`lib/claudeCli.ts::codexReadOnlySandboxNote`, `data-tour="direct-launcher-codex-read-only"`; the run can still begin). The journal's launch line names it: `launching codex · gpt-6.1-terra · workspace-write sandbox`. Contract tests pin the flags' order and form, with and without an effort, read-only unchanged; a unit test checks that a writer outside a sandboxed mission never gets the bypass flag and a read-only stage never does). Unknown ids fall back to claude. Codex has no terminal `result` event: the outcome is assembled from the accumulated stream (LAST assistant message = artifact, `turn.failed`/`error` = failure, `thread.started` = session id), tolerant of BOTH the modern thread-event schema and the legacy `msg`-shape; usage comes from `turn.completed` (cached input split out for pricing, cost via the catalog — codex reports no USD). **Codex sessions resume with `codex exec resume`** (#682): a Codex stage whose session can be continued (Resume, an answered block, or a review loop-back when it is the loop target, see Loop-back mechanics) runs `codex exec <the fresh run's flags> resume <session_id> -` with the follow-up on stdin (`CliDialect::resume_argv` / `resume_prompt`; answered questions read "Your director answered your questions: …", a loop-back's findings "A reviewer sent your earlier work in this session back with these findings: …"). Every flag of the fresh run stays in front of `resume`, because `resume` takes no `--sandbox` and no `-C/--cd` (recorded `codex exec resume --help`, `src-tauri/tests/fixtures/codex/0.169.0/`). Since Codex 0.172.0 (openai/codex #62194) a resume restores the thread's saved sandbox permissions, working directory and workspace roots unless the invocation overrides them, so Octopush overrides all three: `-C <worktree>` pins the working directory to the stage's worktree, `--sandbox` (or, in a sandboxed mission, the bypass flag) and the `approval_policy` and network `-c` overrides pin the permissions, and the writable-root `-c` override pins the extra root. The effort and writable-root `-c` overrides go in just before the trailing `-`, after `resume <session_id>`, which `resume` accepts too. So on 0.169.0 and 0.172.0 alike a read-only review stays read-only in its worktree and a writer keeps `workspace-write`, network on, its build-cache writable root and its effort. It is gated on a once-per-app-session probe of `codex exec resume --help` (`agent_adapter::codex_exec_resume_supported`); without the subcommand the stage runs fresh and the journal says why. A resumed thread's `turn.completed` usage is the **thread's running total**, so each Codex attempt stores the total its session reported (`run_stages.session_usage`, only when its last turn completed) and a resume subtracts it (`usage_since`); a session whose total is unknown is not resumed, so nothing is counted twice. The subtraction is skipped when it can't be trusted: if any field of the resumed total is below the stored baseline (`SessionUsage::since` returns `None`), or Codex reports usage for another session id than the one resumed, the attempt counts the raw usage, the stage is flagged `usage not reported` and the journal says why (`usage_drift_notice`, the stage's only usage line: the drive skips its generic "cost is unknown" line via `CliOutcomeMeta::usage_unreported_journaled`), so a resumed stage never records ~0 for work it did. When the resume fails before any assistant message (an unknown session: exit 1, `thread/resume failed: no rollout found …`; an argument error; a `turn.failed` on the first request) or Codex answers with another session id, the stage runs **fresh once** with the feedback in the prompt and the journal says why (`codex_resume_failure`): "Codex could not resume this stage's session (…)" when the reason is a resume problem (another session id, an unknown session, an argument error, a full context window; `is_resume_problem`), otherwise (quota, auth, network…) "Codex failed before answering on the resumed session (…); running fresh once" (`codex_resume_failure_notice`); both attempts' spend is kept, and the failed attempt's unknown spend still flags the stage `usage not reported` even when the fresh run finishes (`StageOutcome.cli.usage_unreported`, `merge_resume_fallback`). A resuming Codex stage still gets the full dossier, worktree diff included, for that fallback. Contract tests (`codex_contract.rs`) check the argv against the recorded help, the probe, the unknown-session fallback and the fold of a resumed stream. The builder warns when a CLI stage's model matches no dialect; the launcher/inspector model pickers allow Anthropic + OpenAI for CLI stages. Derived-from-model instead of a `cli_dialect` column (no migration, the model picker is the selector); the dialect seam (`CliDialect`) keeps an explicit override or a Gemini dialect addable later. _Support:_ `cli_runner.rs` (`CliDialect`, `CodexWriteScope`, `sandbox_label`, `dialect_for_model`, `codex_fold_event`, `codex_usage_from_event`, `build_codex_outcome`, `codex_resume_failure`, `is_resume_problem`, `codex_resume_failure_notice`, `usage_since`, `usage_drift_notice`, `merge_resume_fallback`), `agent_adapter::codex_exec_resume_supported`, `codex_contract.rs`, `builder/graph.ts::cliDialectSupported`, `StageFlow`/`StageInspector` pickers.
- **CLI substrate (headless Claude Code)** — `CliRunner` spawns `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --model … --append-system-prompt … --permission-mode bypassPermissions --max-turns N --settings '{"permissions":{"blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories":true}}'` in the worktree, streams NDJSON, parses the terminal `result` event. A read-only role (repro, verify, reviewers) also denies the git writes, `Bash(git commit:*)` and the rest (see "Read-only roles"). **File edits stay in the worktree:** every Claude stage, fresh or `--resume`d and read-only or not, carries the inline `--settings` above, so Write/Edit/NotebookEdit refuse paths outside the stage's working directories even under `bypassPermissions` (no file edits in the main checkout, a sibling workspace or `~/`). The guard needs Claude Code ≥ 2.1.314; older CLIs ignore the key, so it is off there. A refused write comes back as an `is_error` tool_result and shows in the stage journal as a failed tool call with the CLI's reason. Bash isn't covered by this setting and stays unconfined unless the mission runs sandboxed (`exec_isolation = "sandbox"`, Seatbelt on macOS). **File reads stay in the worktree in a mission the user chose to sandbox:** when the mission's own `exec_isolation` is `sandbox`, a Claude stage's `--settings` (fresh and resumed) also sets `"blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories":true` (`CLAUDE_SANDBOXED_STAGE_SETTINGS`, swapped in by `confine_reads_in_sandbox`), so Read/Grep/Glob can't pull `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws` or a sibling repo into the agent's context. The setting reaches Bash too: a shell command that Claude Code's checker sees reading outside the working directories asks for permission, which a headless stage refuses; a read the checker can't see (a script or build tool opening a file itself) still succeeds, because the Seatbelt profile denies writes only. Such a stage also gets `--add-dir` for exactly two dirs: its build-cache root and its own temp dir, which `TMPDIR` points at (`~/Library/Caches/octopush/tmp/<key>`, see Sandboxed execution; `sandbox_read_dir_args`, appended through `sandbox::prepare_with` once both exist, fresh and resumed). So it can still read its own temp files and the npm/cargo caches `sandbox_cache_env` redirects there. The user-wide `$TMPDIR` is not added: other apps', workspaces' and stages' files sit there, and Claude Code loads `.claude/skills`, agents and commands from every `--add-dir` dir, so any process could plant skills in the stage. Both dirs are keyed by workspace, write roots, the mission's own exec choice and the read guard (`sandbox::CacheTenant`, `cli_cache_tenant`), so the only launches that can write them are read-confined Claude stages of the same workspace, access mode and exec choice, which share them. A readonly mission's stages can't write the worktree, so this matters most there: a readonly review with exec choice `none` (reads open), a Codex stage, TALK's or an API-substrate stage's `run_command` and a Codex writer outside the sandbox each get their own cache root (and a Claude stage its own temp dir), never a read-confined stage's. Every other mission keeps the write guard only, because its agents read dependency sources outside the worktree — a review/probe (`readonly`) mission with exec choice `none` included, even though its sandbox is forced on: `confine_reads_in_sandbox` is keyed on `StageContext.exec_choice` (the mission's own choice, derived with the effective tier by `sandbox::stage_isolation`), not on `exec_isolation`. The read guard needs Claude Code ≥ 2.1.257; on an older known version the key is ignored and the journal's launch line says `· file reads not confined (Claude Code 2.1.257+ needed)` (`read_guard_label`). A unit test pins this for every writer (`only_equally_confined_claude_stages_can_write_the_dirs_a_read_confined_stage_add_dirs`). Unit tests pin both keys on the sandboxed argv and only the write key otherwise, including a readonly mission with exec choice `none` (write key only) and `sandbox` (both keys), and the `--add-dir` dirs (the cache root and temp dir only, never the user-wide `$TMPDIR`; deduped; only when reads are confined). Codex writer stages run in codex's own `workspace-write` sandbox, which covers their shell commands too: they may write the worktree, codex's temp dirs and their own build cache (where npm, cargo & co. are redirected), with the network on, but not the worktree's git data, so they can't commit or push; a changed `.git` pointer is put back after the stage (see CLI dialects). **No interactive questions:** every Claude stage, fresh or `--resume`d, passes `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion` — nobody can answer Claude Code's question tool headless (since 2.1.321 `-p` refuses it and the model guesses), so a question can only come out in the final message, where the question-as-result guard below parks it for the director. If an older CLI's stream still carries an `AskUserQuestion` call, the journal adds "the agent tried to ask a question; it was refused" after it. **The workspace stays put:** the same list also denies Claude Code's worktree tools, `EnterWorktree,ExitWorktree` (`WORKTREE_TOOLS`, #1002), on every Claude stage, fresh or resumed. A stage's workspace is the worktree Octopush made for it, which Review, Collision radar and the diff snapshots watch, so the stage can't use those tools to move its work to a worktree Octopush doesn't track, or to remove a worktree another session works in (Claude Code's ExitWorktree before 2.1.330 could). Bash isn't covered by this denial: a stage can still run `git worktree …` or `cd` elsewhere through Bash, unconfined unless the mission runs sandboxed. **Read-only reviewers:** a worktree review stage adds `Write,Edit,MultiEdit,NotebookEdit` to that same list plus the git-write `Bash(…)` rules (one flag, one comma list: `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion,EnterWorktree,ExitWorktree,Write,Edit,MultiEdit,NotebookEdit,Bash(git add:*),…`, built by `review_disallowed_tools`; Bash itself stays — reviewers run builds/tests), so a CLI reviewer can no longer "fix" the diff it certifies; Action roles keep write access. Unit tests pin the flag once per argv, the tool once in it and the reviewer's write denial, for writer, reviewer and resumed stages. **Question-as-result guard:** a Done outcome whose final line is a person-addressed question ("Should I…?", "Do you want…?") parks as a director block (same flow as `ask_director`) instead of flowing downstream disguised as a result. **Honest spend on stop:** per-turn usage is summed from the streamed assistant events, so a stop/idle-timeout/60-min-cap reports estimated tokens + catalog-priced cost instead of zero. _Support:_ `cli_runner.rs` (`CLAUDE_STAGE_SETTINGS`, `CLAUDE_SANDBOXED_STAGE_SETTINGS`, `confine_reads_in_sandbox`, `sandbox_read_dir_args`, `read_guard_label`, `ASK_USER_QUESTION_TOOL`, `WORKTREE_TOOLS`, `REVIEW_DISALLOWED_TOOLS`, `review_disallowed_tools`, `cli_disallowed_tools`, `detect_trailing_question`, `usage_from_stream_event`, `failed_stage_with_usage`), `live.rs` (`ASK_USER_QUESTION_REFUSED`).
- **Claude plan windows from `rate_limit_event`** — A Claude Code stage on a Claude Pro/Max plan streams `rate_limit_event` lines; `plan_windows_from_stream_event` reads their `rate_limit_info` into `PlanWindow { kind, utilization (fraction), resets_at (epoch s; ms tolerated), status, overage_status, using_overage }`: the event's subject window (`rateLimitType`, kept verbatim when unknown) with top-level `utilization` or its `unifiedWindows` entry, plus every other `unifiedWindows` window (status only when it is `allowed`). Every field is optional; an event without `rate_limit_info` yields nothing. The session's auth comes from `system/init` `apiKeySource` (`"none"` ⇒ subscription, anything else ⇒ API key, absent ⇒ unknown, `cli_auth_from_init`); an API-key session's events are never recorded. The windows go out as `plan://updated` through `LiveEmitter::plan_windows`; `PersistingSink` keeps the latest per kind in `app_meta` (`claude_plan:<kind>` → `PlanSnapshot` JSON with `seen_at`) — a later event without `utilization` or `status` (a window described in passing) keeps the last figure and status — so a `rejected` window stays rejected — only while `resets_at` is unchanged. Detached workers write the same rows. Read back by `get_claude_plan`. No outbound traffic, no credential reads. A stage stopped by a `rejected` window parks its run until the reset (see Halt detection › "Claude plan limit park"); plan-covered spend is still priced at API rates. Contract tests run the synthetic `stream-json/subscriber-rate-limit.jsonl` fixture (with/without `unifiedWindows`, with/without top-level `utilization`, unknown `rateLimitType`). _Support:_ `cli_runner.rs`, `live.rs`, `persist.rs`, `claude_plan.rs`, `claude_code_contract.rs`.
- **Claude sign-in end from `credential_expires_at`** — On Claude Code 2.1.318+ a stage's stream-json `result` event carries `credential_expires_at`, when the stored claude.ai sign-in ends; `cli_runner::credential_expiry_from_result` reads it (RFC 3339 text or epoch seconds/milliseconds; absent, null or unreadable → nothing, so older CLIs behave as before) from any session not classed as API-key, `LiveEmitter::login_expiry` emits `claude-login://updated`, and `PersistingSink` keeps the latest value with its `seenAt` in `app_meta` `claude_login:expiry` (`claude_login.rs`; detached workers and Routines included; never a journal entry). Read by Settings › General › Readiness's Claude auth row (§10) and by the **sign-in note** (`ClaudeLoginNote`): within 10 days of the end an amber mono line "Your Claude sign-in ends 12 Dec · sign in again so overnight crews keep running · `claude auth login`", rouge once it has passed ("…ended 3 Nov · CLI stages and Routines can't run until you sign in again"), hidden otherwise. An Anthropic key in Settings › Models doesn't hide it: `cli_runner` never passes that key to `claude`, so `get_claude_login` returns the stored end whether or not a key is set; its `title` gives the report's age. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is different: `claude` inherits the app's environment plus the login shell's (`login_shell_env()`), so if it is set there Claude Code may use it. A session whose `system/init` reports an API-key source (`apiKeySource` other than `"none"`) no longer uses the sign-in and never reports a new end, so its init clears the stored one (`cli_runner::forward_plan_and_login` → `LiveEmitter::login_cleared`, `claude-login://updated` with `expiresAt: null`; `PersistingSink` deletes `claude_login:expiry`), and the note and the Readiness row stop showing it. Otherwise the stored date changes when a later stage reports a new one, or when an explicit Readiness **Check again** reads a new `loginExpiresAt` from `claude auth status --json` (written back through `claude_login::record`, same event; `loggedIn: false` clears it instead, `claude_login::apply_probe`, event with `expiresAt: null`), so after signing in again the note clears on Check again or the next Claude Code 2.1.318+ stage. It sits under Mission Control's header (`data-tour="mission-control-login-expiry"`) and above Settings › Routines' list (`data-tour="routines-login-expiry"`); it loads on mount and on `claude-login://updated`. Stages add no network and no credential reads; Readiness's `claude auth status` runs only on an explicit Check again. _Support:_ `orchestrator/cli_runner.rs`, `orchestrator/live.rs`, `orchestrator/persist.rs`, `claude_login.rs`, command `get_claude_login`; `src/lib/claudeLogin.ts`, `stores/claudeLoginStore.ts`, `components/ClaudeLoginNote.tsx`; contract fixture `stream-json/subscriber-login-expiry.jsonl` (synthetic).
- **CLI environment & PATH resolution** — Captures the user's full login+interactive shell env once (`SHELL -lic 'env -0'`) so a GUI-launched app inherits PATH/exports; resolves the `claude` executable across login PATH ∪ inherited ∪ common dirs. The probe (`probe_login_shell_env`) runs with no stdin in its own process group and is bounded at 8s (`LOGIN_SHELL_PROBE_TIMEOUT`): when the shell already exited cleanly and only a job it started still holds the output pipe, the group is killed and the env the shell printed is kept (with its own warning); otherwise an rc file that blocks gets its whole group killed, one warning in the app log, and no login env, so the PATH is the app's plus the common dirs (`~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, …). App setup reads it once in the background so the first Talk command, stage or MCP server rarely waits. _Support:_ `login_shell_env`, `probe_login_shell_env`, `resolved_cli_path`; `lib.rs` setup.
- **Quiet Claude Code in crews and Routines (opt-in, #703)** — Settings › Privacy toggle "Quiet Claude Code in crews and Routines", **off by default** (`settings.json` `quietClaudeCode`, `serde(default)` ⇒ `false`). When on, every Claude Code CLI stage — fresh, `--resume`d, in-process or in the detached worker (`octopush-run-worker` → `drive_segment`) — is spawned with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`, which per Claude Code's env-var reference disables its auto-updates, telemetry, error reporting, `/feedback`, release notes and availability checks, and also feature-flag fetching, so Remote Control and other flag-gated features are unavailable in those sessions. The setting is read from `settings.json` when each stage starts (`settings::quiet_claude_code`, into `StageContext.quiet_claude_code`), so a toggle reaches the next stage, a resume or the next detached segment without a restart. The variable is set by `CliDialect::stage_quiet_env` inside `cli_runner::apply_stage_env`, the one place a stage's env is applied (beside `stage_env`'s pins and the effort env); Codex stages never get it. A Routine's crew stages get it through the same spawn, and its own shell commands — the fire condition and a fresh worktree's setup script — get it too (`routines::routine_quiet_env`), so a `claude` they start is quiet as well. **Off sets nothing and removes nothing:** the docs say even `0` disables the traffic, so no value is written and a user's own export is left alone. **Run terminals and Talk are never affected** (`commands::run_terminal_env` builds the Run PTY env from the context guard and `OCTOPUSH_MODEL` only). The toggle's helper text quotes what it stops and what stops working; the sentence under it says what Claude Code stages may send when it is off (see Settings › Privacy). Contract tests: `claude_code_contract.rs` `quiet_claude_code_*` (fresh, resumed, Codex), `tests.rs` `quiet_claude_code_reaches_fresh_and_resumed_stages_from_settings`, `quiet_claude_code_reaches_a_detached_segment_from_settings`, `routine_commands_get_the_quiet_variable_only_when_on`, `run_terminal_env_is_untouched_by_quiet_claude_code`. _Support:_ `settings.rs`, `orchestrator/cli_runner.rs` (`QUIET_TRAFFIC_ENV`, `stage_quiet_env`, `apply_stage_env`), `orchestrator/runner.rs`, `orchestrator/mod.rs`, `routines.rs`, `PrivacyPane.tsx` (`QuietClaudeCodeRow`, `data-tour="settings-quiet-claude-code"`). _Entry:_ Settings › Privacy.
- **CLI timeouts** — Idle (300s silence) + absolute (3600s) with distinct honest messages; stderr drained concurrently. **Long commands (Claude Code):** the read loop pairs each `tool_use` block of an `assistant` event with the `tool_result` carrying its id in a `user` event (`OpenTools`; a result for an id that never opened changes nothing). While a Bash or PowerShell call is open, the idle window is `max(300s, BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS from the stage env, default 600s) + 60s` (`command_idle_window`, `ReadLimits::command_idle`; 11 minutes by default), since Claude Code itself waits that long on a foreground command that prints nothing to the stream; the 60-minute cap is unchanged. The first time a stage stays silent past 5 minutes on that account the journal says "waiting on a long command (up to 11 min)". An idle stop names the open call when there is one — "claude timed out — Bash `npm test` gave no result for 11 minutes" (`idle_timeout_message`; the command's first line, ≤ 60 chars) — and the halt card shows that line with "Claude Code was still waiting on it" (`stageHalt.ts`). **API retry waits (Claude Code):** a `system/api_retry` event carries the delay the CLI will wait before its next attempt (`retry_delay_ms`), so the next silence may last that delay, capped at 300s, plus the plain 5-minute window: about 10 minutes at most (`retry_idle_window`, `MAX_RETRY_DELAY`, parsed by `live::api_retry_delay`). 300s is the ceiling Claude Code 2.1.323 set for `CLAUDE_CODE_OVERLOADED_RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS`, which applies only to 529 overload backoff; a 429 `Retry-After` wait or a wait under `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG` can be longer, and Octopush caps those at 300s too, so a stage silent through a longer wait still times out. The next line of any other kind goes back to the plain window, and a retry without a numeric delay changes nothing. A stall that still trips after a retry says so — "claude timed out — no output for 10 minutes after an API retry (overloaded)" (`IdleStall.after_retry`) — and the halt card reads "No answer for 10 minutes after an API retry (overloaded)". **Stalls before the first request (Claude Code):** the read loop notes the stage's `system/init` and whether any later line showed a request going out — an `assistant`, `stream_event`, `rate_limit_event` or `system/api_retry` (`shows_a_request`; sticky once seen). A plain idle stall after init and before any of those is named for what it is — "claude timed out — Claude Code sent no request in 5 minutes" (`IdleStall.before_first_request`) — which points at a proxy or the CLI, not the brief or the model. When the probed CLI version is known and below 2.1.327 (`CLAUDE_FIRST_REQUEST_HANG_FIX`), the line adds "; Claude Code 2.1.327 fixes a hang before the first request when a model's settings fetch stalls (for example at a proxy). Update Claude Code"; an unknown version adds nothing. The halt card reads "Claude Code sent no request in 5 minutes", with that update as its remedy, or "Check any proxy between Claude Code and the API" on a newer CLI, and Re-run first. Every other stall keeps its message. Codex keeps the plain 5-minute window. **Settle after `result` (Claude Code):** recent `claude -p` stays open after its turn to wait for background work it started (a dev server, a watch build). The stage's hand-off is the terminal `result` event, so 30s after it arrives (`SETTLE_AFTER_RESULT_SECS`, counted from the result, not reset by later output) a still-open CLI is stopped with the graceful process-group stop (`stop_cli_child`, so a background server it started goes too), the `result` line is taken as authoritative (status, artifact, usage and cost, like the idle-timeout salvage) and the journal notes "stage finished · stopped background work it left running". Every Claude stage also gets `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=25000` (`BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`, `CliDialect::stage_env`), so the CLI's own subagent and Monitor waits stop at 25s and it can exit on its own before the 30s settle, and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FAST_MODE=1`, so a stage never switches to fast mode (billed at twice the standard rate) on its own, and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MCP_TASK_BACKGROUND=1` (fresh and `--resume` alike), so an MCP tool call the server runs as a task finishes inside the call instead of moving to the background (Claude Code 2.1.319+) and still running when the stage settles — a defensive pin, since the changelog scopes that behaviour to the terminal; Run-mode terminals keep it. Every Claude stage also gets `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIR_WATCH=0` (fresh and `--resume` alike), so a stage keeps the `.claude/skills` it started with instead of reloading them when the stage rewrites a skill file in its worktree (on its own or prompted by text it read), on Claude Code 2.1.321+ (older CLIs ignore the variable); Run-mode terminals keep the reload. Every Claude stage also gets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_PROGRESS_SUMMARIES=1` (fresh and `--resume` alike, over any inherited value; #722), which turns off subagent progress summaries and the billed requests that write them on Claude Code 2.1.318+ (older CLIs ignore the variable); no stage reads them — the journal leaves those system events out and the pane shows tool calls and the result. Run-mode terminals keep them. Codex has no terminal event and never settles early. _Support:_ `cli_runner.rs` (`read_stream`, `ReadLimits`, `OpenTools`, `IdleStall`, `ReadEnd::Settled`), contract tests in `claude_code_contract.rs`, the settle-then-group-stop grandchild test in `tests.rs` (`a_settled_stage_stops_the_background_work_it_left_running`), the open-call, retry window and pre-request stall tests in `tests.rs` (`cli_command_idle_tests`), the init-only stream contract test (`stream_json_a_hang_before_the_first_request_is_named`, fixture `claude-code/2.1.326/stream-json/init-only.jsonl`).
- **Gateway models' context window (Claude Code)** — Claude Code 2.1.323 assumes a 1M window for a model id it doesn't recognize, and a session on a smaller window "can fail every turn until `/clear`" once full, which a headless stage can't do. So a Claude stage whose model isn't a builtin Anthropic catalog id, and whose window in the provider catalog (the user's own custom model entries included, `ProviderRouter::find_model`) is below 1M, tells Claude Code the real window with `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=<max_context>`. The builtin check runs on the normalized id (`token_engine::normalize_model_id`, `is_builtin_claude_model`), so `bedrock/claude-haiku-4-5` and `us.anthropic.claude-…-v1:0` count as builtin and get nothing. Ids that don't start with `claude-` (`gpt-4o` at 128K, a 512K model) already honoured that variable before Claude Code 2.1.325 (whose changelog entry says it "also" covers unrecognized `claude-` ids), so they get it alone and never `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT`, which is process-wide and would also cap a subagent on a builtin 1M model. Ids that start with `claude-` (a gateway's `claude-sonnet-latest`) get it from 2.1.325 on; below 2.1.325, by the version the stage probed before spawning (`agent_adapter::claude_cli_version_cached`; an unknown version counts as old), a window of 200K or less also gets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1`, which keeps 200K. A window below 200K can't be expressed on 2.1.323–324: such a stage runs with 200K assumed, and one between 200K and 1M with 1M. Claude Code then compacts before the window fills. Builtin Claude models, unknown windows and windows of 1M or more get nothing. A value the user's login-shell env already sets is never overridden (each variable separately). The window comes from the model entry, and Settings › Models' `ModelDialog` fills a new custom model's max context with 200000, so set the model's real window there; a 1M gateway model left at 200000 compacts early, and a smaller one left at 200000 can still fill. Set on fresh and `--resume` runs alike, in-process and detached; Codex stages and Run-mode terminals never get it. _Support:_ `cli_runner.rs` (`context_window_env`, `is_builtin_claude_model`, `stage_context_env`, `apply_stage_env`, `MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS_ENV`, `DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT_ENV`, `CLAUDE_PREFIXED_MAX_CONTEXT_FLOOR`); contract tests in `claude_code_contract.rs`.
- **Model substitution (Claude Code)** — Org or user settings (`availableModels`/`deniedModels`) can make Claude Code run another model than `--model`; since 2.1.323 `claude -p` warns on stderr only in text output, so a stream-json stage stays silent. On a Claude stage's `system/init` event the runner compares its `model` to the stage's requested model (`same_model`: equal after `token_engine::normalize_model_id`, which handles gateway prefixes, Bedrock/Vertex suffixes, dated snapshots, dotted gateway versions and `[1m]`; a Claude Code alias such as `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, `opusplan` or `default` covers any id of its family, so `sonnet` vs `claude-sonnet-5-5` is no alarm). When they differ, the journal says "ran on Sonnet 5.5, not Opus 5.5 — Claude Code's model settings picked another model" (catalog display names, `ran_on_notice`), the outcome carries the model (`CliOutcomeMeta.ran_model`), and the drive records it on the stage (`run_stages.ran_model`, set before the attempt's completion and cleared on reset). The spend ledger attributes the attempt to that model (`record_direct_spend` reads `COALESCE(ran_model, agent_model)`, so Usage and savings follow what ran), a stop's estimated cost is priced at it, and `get_run` prices the unpriced check with it and returns it as `ranModel`. The stage card's meta line shows an amber "ran on sonnet-5-5" note (`data-tour="direct-stage-ran-on"`) and the ledger's per-stage row adds "· ran on sonnet-5-5"; both tooltips name the model asked for and say the cost is for the one that ran.
