A missing or unparseable `model` changes nothing, and so does a provider-native id with no Claude family (`has_claude_family`: no `claude-*` id or Claude Code alias after normalising — a Bedrock application-inference-profile ARN from `modelOverrides` or `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL`, a Microsoft Foundry deployment name) when the stage asked for a Claude model: it counts as unknown, not a substitution, so there is no note and the cost stays on the requested model. Codex has no such event. _Support:_ `cli_runner.rs` (`init_model`, `same_model`, `substituted_model`, `ran_on_notice`), `orchestrator/mod.rs` (`set_run_stage_ran_model`), `db.rs` (`ran_model` column, `ran_models`), `commands::get_run`; frontend `RunFlow.tsx`, `RunLedger.tsx`, `lib/modelLabel.ts` (`ranOnNote`, `ranOnTitle`); tests in `tests.rs` (`ran_model_tests`, `a_stage_that_ran_on_another_model_is_attributed_to_it`) and the init contract test in `claude_code_contract.rs`.
- **Claude Code sub-agent hierarchy in the journal** — A CLI stage's `stream-json` events that belong to a native Claude Code sub-agent carry `parent_tool_use_id`; `entries_from_stream_event` tags every entry from such an event with `parent` (the spawning `Agent`/`Task` tool_use id) and the spawning `tool` entry with `agentId`, showing the sub-agent's `description` as its hint instead of the prompt. `JournalItems` renders tagged entries one level in (hairline + indent) under their spawner, pairing a result with its tool line only at the same level, so a stage that fans out reads as a tree instead of a flat interleaving; `LiveEntry` gained the optional `parent`/`agentId` tags (`LiveEntryHierarchy`). Persisted `stage_log` rows keep the tags, so archived attempts keep the tree. _Support:_ `orchestrator/live.rs`, `lib/ipc.ts`, `direct/JournalItems.tsx`.
- **Uniform runner abstraction** — Both substrates implement `AgentRunner::run(stage, input, ctx) -> StageOutcome`; the orchestrator never branches on substrate. _Support:_ `runner.rs`.
- **Stage input dossier (cross-stage handoff)** — Each stage receives the run task, a one-line pipeline breadcrumb, and **every feeding stage's live artifact** as a section (transitive flow-ancestors; sibling branches don't leak; artifacts nulled by a reset never ride). **Multi-section, budgeted:** the freshest section of each kind renders at the full ~16K cap as the primary input; older same-kind sections render **compact** (4K, labeled as earlier context) instead of being evicted — two reviews from different stages both reach the downstream fix stage now; a 60K global dossier budget drops compact sections oldest-first. **Loop memory:** a stage that has archived attempts also receives a compact digest of them (what each attempt was, which model ran it, what feedback/failure closed it — last 5, snipped) with an explicit anti-oscillation instruction. **Reviewers see the actual code:** when feeding artifacts ref the worktree, the **live diff — any commits made during the run, plus staged + unstaged — is captured and embedded** between `BEGIN/END GIT DIFF` markers (not a ``` fence), capped head+tail **with an explicit truncation notice** and a shared-workspace caveat. Best-effort: capture failure/empty diff falls back to the "inspect with your tools" hint; skipped for CLI-resume stages (input discarded). **Concurrent work (collision radar, #732):** a code-writing stage (artifact kind `diff`, worktree environment — `implement`, `fix`) whose workspace changes the same files as another live workspace of the project gets one line per peer after the code-changes block — *"Note: workspace `refund-webhooks` is concurrently changing src/billing/limits.ts. Avoid unrelated edits there."* — confirmed conflicts first, lockfiles left out (a lockfile-only overlap adds nothing), at most 3 peers (then *"Note: N more workspaces of this project change files you may touch."*) and 5 files per peer (then *"and N more files"*); nothing when there is no overlap, the project has one live workspace, or the stage resumes a CLI session. _Support:_ `orchestrator::full_worktree_diff` (committed segment via the earliest stage baseline's parent), `assemble_stage_input`, `attempt_history_digest`, `Orchestrator::concurrent_work_note` + `collisions::concurrent_work_note`, `StageInput` (`sections`/`full_detail`/`history`/`worktree_diff`/`concurrent_work`), `user_input_for`.
- **Mid-pipeline commit detection** — A stage that moves HEAD despite the never-commit contract gets a `⚠` journal notice with the commit range, and the committed work stays visible in the run diff (see the dossier's committed segment) instead of silently vanishing from the reviewer's view. _Support:_ `run_stage_once` head tracking, `git_ops::head_sha`/`range_diff_text`.

- **Ship a GitHub issue** — In the launcher's brief card: a quiet `CircleDot` (issue) entry ("ship an issue") opens a picker of the repo's **open GitHub issues** (`gh issue list` in the login shell, mirroring `list_prs`). **Preflight first** (`github_ship_readiness`): no github.com origin → honest dead end; `gh` unauthenticated → "run `gh auth login`" guidance — the crew's `pull_request` stage would otherwise fail mid-run AFTER building the change. Picking an issue **folds it into the task** (`composeIssueTask`: `Ship GitHub issue #N — title` + body capped at 4KB with an explicit truncation note + `include "Closes #N"` instruction — the task reaches every stage's prompt, so the PR stage closes the issue) and **selects the "Ship it" builtin**. Deliberately does NOT touch `linked_issue_key` (Jira-semantic everywhere — a `#N` there would be fed to the Jira client). All issue values render as inert text. _Support:_ `GithubIssuePicker.tsx`, `lib/shipIssue.ts`, commands `list_github_issues`/`github_ship_readiness` (+ `github.rs::issues_from_json`/`ShipReadiness`). _Entry:_ Direct launcher → brief card → "ship an issue".

### Runs — lifecycle & control
- **Create run (draft)** — Copies pipeline_stages into a private `run_stages` copy, applies positional `(position, model)` overrides, inserts as `draft`. _Support:_ `create_run`; `runsStore.begin`.
- **Start run (background drive)** — Spawns the drive as a `tokio` task; persists optional budget. _Support:_ `start_run` → `orch.start_run`.
- **Run status lifecycle** — `draft → running → paused → completed | aborted | failed`. _Support:_ `RunStatus`; status meta in `runStatus.ts`.
- **Stage status lifecycle** — `pending → running → {awaiting_checkpoint | done | failed}`. _Support:_ `StageStatus`; `runStatus.ts`.
- **Parallel branch execution (authored DAGs, write-set gated)** — The drive schedules by READY SET, not first-non-done: in an authored graph, every pending stage whose parents are all `done` is ready, and each batch runs **all ready read-only stages concurrently plus at most ONE writer** (the worktree is a shared blackboard — two concurrent writers is silent corruption, so writers serialize in position order and land in later batches). Read-only = an API stage whose allowlist grants no `write_file`/`edit_file`/`run_command`, or a CLI worktree review (which runs under the tool denial / codex read-only sandbox); anything else — including unknown toolsets — counts as a writer. Outcomes are processed in position order once the batch closes (a park in one branch doesn't swallow a sibling's loop-back), and the run pauses ONCE at the end if any outcome demands it — an independent sibling that was ready alongside a gated branch still runs in that batch. One cancel flag per batch: "Stop" stops everything in flight. Boundary gates (run/scope budget, director pause) fire per batch with the earliest ready stage as the checkpoint carrier; a conscious budget override releases exactly one stage, not a batch. **Legacy linear runs (no recorded parents) stay strictly serial, byte-for-byte.** Phase 2 (isolated worktrees per branch with join-merge, allowing concurrent writers) remains designed-not-built — see the design note. _Support:_ `drive_inner` ready-set/batch loop, `stage_is_read_only`, `handle_stage_outcome` (orchestrator/mod.rs).
- **Director pause** — Parks the next pending stage at the boundary. _Support:_ `request_run_pause`; a quiet `Pause` `IconButton` in the run header (`DirectCanvas`) — always mounted, opacity-faded + disabled while a control isn't applicable.
- **Stop current stage** — Real cancellation: API loop halts at next check; the CLI stage stops the CLI and every process it started (dev servers, watch builds, test runners) — the CLI runs in its own process group and gets SIGINT, then SIGTERM (5 s grace each), then the group gets SIGKILL; the same graceful stop ends a stage that hits its idle or 60-minute cap. Usage streamed before the stop is still recorded. Stage lands `failed` in halt-recovery. _Support:_ `stop_stage`; `stop_cli_child` (`orchestrator/cli_runner.rs`); a `CircleStop` `IconButton` in the run header (`DirectCanvas`).
- **Abort run** — Marks `aborted` AND kills the in-flight stage. Every **Abort** on the decision bar (checkpoint, halted stage, plan-limit park) asks first (#849): a `ModalShell` dialog, "End this run here?", explains the run can't be resumed and the worktree keeps what the stages wrote; **Keep the run** (focused, also Escape) cancels, the upright-serif rouge **Abort the run** (`--rouge-border` outline) confirms. _Support:_ `abort_run`; `RunControlBar` (`useAbortConfirm`).
- **One executing run per workspace** — `start_run` rejects a concurrent running/paused run in the same workspace (runs share one worktree); UI gate disables "Begin the run". _Support:_ `has_concurrent_run`; `runsStore.hasExecutingRun`.
- **Claude Code version preflight (never blocks)** — When the selected crew has a CLI stage that runs on Claude Code (overrides applied; OpenAI-family models run on Codex and don't count), the launcher shows an amber "Update Claude Code (x.y.z or newer recommended) · installed a.b.c" note with the reason (wrong token usage skews costs; sandbox rules skipped on resumed sessions) when the installed CLI is older than `TESTED_CLAUDE_FLOOR` — x.y.z is `ClaudeCliVersion::recommended`, the higher of the floor and the security fix the CLI lacks (today 2.1.325, since 2.1.314 itself lacks it), so following it clears both notes; "Begin the run" stays enabled. When that note doesn't show but the installed CLI lacks a sandbox/permission fix in `agent_adapter::CLAUDE_SECURITY_FIXES` (a (version, reason) table kept apart from the floor so a row never forces a fixture re-record; rows, oldest first: "2.1.319 fixes a sandbox escape when creating a worktree", "2.1.321 fixes a read-only Bash command running outside the sandbox without a prompt", "2.1.323 fixes the Bash sandbox switching off mid-session" and "2.1.325 fixes the Bash sandbox not fully protecting a worktree's settings, hooks and shared git folder"; a test keeps them in version order), the same note reads "Update Claude Code: 2.1.325 fixes the Bash sandbox not fully protecting a worktree's settings, hooks and shared git folder · installed a.b.c" (the newest fix it is below). Every Claude Code CLI stage also journals each applicable warning once as a `notice` before it spawns (`ClaudeCliVersion::stage_notices`: tested floor, then security). Unknown or missing versions never warn. A prerelease counts as its release (`2.1.319-beta.1` has the 2.1.319 fix). The launcher and the stage journals read the cached version (see Settings › Integrations "Installed Claude Code version"); a Readiness check clears that cache, so after an update they stop warning on the next launcher open or stage, without a restart. _Support:_ `PipelineSetup.tsx` (`data-tour="direct-launcher-cli-version"`), `lib/claudeCli.ts` (`crewUsesClaudeCode`, `claudeUpdateLabel`, `claudeSecurityLabel`); `CliRunner::run` (`agent_adapter::ClaudeCliVersion::update_notice` / `security_notice`).
- **Model needs a newer Claude Code (never blocks)** — When a Claude Code CLI stage's model (overrides applied) or its escalation model needs a newer CLI than the installed one (`agent_adapter::CLAUDE_MODEL_FLOORS`, see §8), the launcher shows one amber mono line under the foot: "Fable 5.2 needs Claude Code 2.1.321 or newer — this Mac has 2.1.316." (tooltip: a stage on it may not run until Claude Code is updated; the run can still begin). With several such models it names the one needing the newest CLI. A Codex CLI stage escalating to a Claude model counts too (the escalation runs on Claude Code), so the launcher reads the CLI version whenever any such model is present; the update and security notes still show only for crews whose own stages run Claude Code. Once the launcher's version read answers with a known version, it calls `claude_model_floor_note(models)`, which reads the backend's cached version without waiting or probing (`claude_cli_version_cached`, as stage escalation does). No line when the CLI isn't found or its version is unknown, nor for API stages or Codex-dialect models. _Support:_ `PipelineSetup.tsx` (`data-tour="direct-launcher-model-floor"`), `lib/claudeCli.ts` (`crewClaudeModels`, `modelFloorLabel`), `ipc.claudeModelFloorNote`; `agent_adapter::model_floor_note`.
- **A Claude Code release to skip (never blocks)** — Some single releases break something a crew relies on and the next one puts it back. `agent_adapter::CLAUDE_KNOWN_BAD_RELEASES` lists them as (version, reason, scope), matched exactly (a prerelease counts as its release), never as a floor; today one row: 2.1.329 "drops the retry gateway models need when a max_tokens error names a lower limit; 2.1.330 restores it", scope `GatewayStages`. The release-watch routine adds rows the way it adds `CLAUDE_SECURITY_FIXES` rows. `ClaudeCliVersion::known_bad` carries the matching row. Three places say it: the Readiness card's Claude Code row turns amber with "Claude Code 2.1.329 drops … ; 2.1.330 restores it. Update Claude Code." whatever the crew (a missing security fix shows first); the Direct launcher shows one amber mono line under the foot, "Claude Code 2.1.329 drops …. A stage on a gateway model may fail every turn; update Claude Code.", only when a Claude Code CLI stage's model (overrides applied) or escalation model is a gateway model — `cli_runner::is_gateway_model`: neither a built-in Anthropic id nor a Claude Code alias (`sonnet`, `opusplan`…) — via `claude_known_bad_note(models)`, which reads the cached version and is only called when the version read named a known bad release; and when such a stage fails with an error that mentions `max_tokens` on that release, `cli_runner::with_known_bad_release` puts "Skip Claude Code 2.1.329 on a gateway model: it … Update Claude Code, then resume or re-run." before the CLI's own error, which the run bar's halt cause reads as "Claude Code 2.1.329 is a release to skip on a gateway model" with that remedy (`stageHalt.ts`). Unknown versions never warn. _Support:_ `PipelineSetup.tsx` (`data-tour="direct-launcher-known-bad"`), `ipc.claudeKnownBadNote`, `lib/stageHalt.ts`; `agent_adapter::{known_bad_release, known_bad_launch_note, known_bad_stage_error}`, `readiness::claude_check`, `commands::claude_known_bad_note`.
- **Codex Action stage can't commit (never blocks)** — When a CLI stage of the selected crew has an Action role (one that may commit, push and run release commands) and its model (overrides applied) runs on Codex, and the workspace's mission isn't sandboxed, the launcher shows one amber mono line under the foot: "Ship runs on Codex, whose sandbox keeps .git read-only, so it can't commit or push. Pick a Claude model for it." (several stages are named together: "Ship and Release run on Codex, … so they can't … Pick a Claude model for them."; it recommends only a Claude model until a sandboxed Codex mission has been checked on a Mac; tooltip: Codex keeps the worktree's git data read-only in its own sandbox; the run can still begin). The launcher loads the roles if nothing loaded them yet. The stage journal repeats it when such a stage launches. _Support:_ `PipelineSetup.tsx` (`data-tour="direct-launcher-codex-commit"`), `lib/claudeCli.ts::codexCommitNote`, `stores/rolesStore.ts`; `cli_runner::codex_git_notice` (see CLI dialects).
- **Read-only Codex stage in a sandboxed mission (never blocks)** — When a CLI stage of the selected crew runs on Codex (overrides applied) with a read-only role (a `review` artifact in the worktree environment) and the workspace's mission runs sandboxed (`exec_isolation = "sandbox"`, or a `readonly` mission, which forces the sandbox on), the launcher shows one amber mono line under the foot: "A read-only Codex stage can't run in a sandboxed mission yet. Give this stage a Claude model." (tooltip: Codex's own read-only sandbox can't run inside Octopush's, so the stage would fail when it starts; the run can still begin). The stage fails at launch with the same line (`cli_runner::codex_read_only_refusal`, see CLI dialects). _Support:_ `PipelineSetup.tsx` (`data-tour="direct-launcher-codex-read-only"`), `lib/claudeCli.ts::codexReadOnlySandboxNote`.
- **Codex will skip an untrusted repo's `.codex/` config (never blocks)** — Codex loads project-scoped config (`.codex/config.toml`, project hooks, rules, MCP servers) only for a project trusted in Codex, and `codex exec` keeps it off in an untrusted one. When the selected crew has a CLI stage that runs on Codex (overrides applied; `crewUsesCodex`) and Codex would find a `.codex/` directory for the worktree (the worktree path and its ancestors up to the project root, the nearest one with a `.git` file or dir, as Codex discovers project layers; a linked worktree's own `.git` file makes it the root, so the main checkout's `.codex/` doesn't count), the launcher asks `codex_trust_note(workspacePath)`. The backend reads Codex's config files the way Codex merges them: `/etc/codex/config.toml`, then `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` (`CODEX_HOME` from the login-shell environment, else `~/.codex`), then `$CODEX_HOME/managed_config.toml`, then `/etc/codex/managed_config.toml`, a later file's entry winning for the same key. It looks up `[projects."<path>"].trust_level` for the worktree path first, then the main checkout's root (a linked worktree's `.git` file → its `commondir`, as Codex's `resolve_root_git_project_for_trust` does), canonical spelling before the given one; only entries with a `trust_level` count. Anything but `trusted` means Codex skips the layers, and the two states get their own copy (`CodexTrust::NoDecision` / `CodexTrust::Untrusted`). With no saved decision, the launcher shows one amber mono line, "Codex will ignore this repo's .codex/ settings and MCP servers: the project isn't trusted in Codex.", and under it in sage "To trust it, open Codex in the repo once and accept, or run `codex exec --trust` there yourself. Octopush never changes your Codex config. The run can still begin." For a project marked `trust_level = "untrusted"`, the line ends "the project is marked untrusted in Codex." and the sage line reads "To trust it, change its trust_level from "untrusted" to "trusted" in ~/.codex/config.toml yourself. Octopush never changes your Codex config. The run can still begin." (no `--trust` advice: it doesn't apply to a saved decision). Each Codex stage journals the same text as a `notice` before it spawns. Octopush only reads these files: it never writes the user's Codex config and never passes a trust flag. A missing user config, any unreadable or unparsable file, or an unexpected `trust_level` value counts as unknown and shows nothing; so does a repo without `.codex/`. Trust set only through macOS MDM or cloud config isn't read. _Support:_ `codex_trust.rs` (`project_trust`, `main_repo_root`, `trust_in`, `has_codex_dir`, `untrusted_note`, `CODEX_UNTRUSTED_NOTE`, `CODEX_TRUST_HOW`, `CODEX_MARKED_UNTRUSTED_NOTE`, `CODEX_MARKED_UNTRUSTED_HOW`), command `codex_trust_note`, `ipc.codexTrustNote`, `lib/claudeCli.ts` (`crewUsesCodex`), `PipelineSetup.tsx` (`data-tour="direct-launcher-codex-trust"`), the journal notice in `CliRunner::run_attempt`.
- **What the repo's own hooks, MCP servers and skill shell commands run (read-only, never blocks)** — Claude Code loads a repo's committed `.claude/settings.json` (hooks, `statusLine`), `.mcp.json` (MCP servers), `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` and `.claude/commands/**/*.md` in every Claude Code CLI stage; a skill or command runs its inline shell commands as it loads, without asking. When the selected crew has a CLI stage that runs on Claude Code (overrides applied; `crewUsesClaudeCode`), the launcher asks `repo_hooks_notice(workspacePath)` (`spawn_blocking`), which reads those files in the worktree, never `settings.local.json`. It returns each hook under `hooks.<Event>[].hooks[]` of type `command` (its command), `http` (its URL) or `mcp_tool` (`server · tool`), with its event and matcher (events in name order, entries in file order; `prompt`/`agent` hooks and entries missing their target are left out); the `statusLine` command; each `mcpServers.<name>` with a `command` (+ `args`) or a `url` (in name order); and each skill shell command (`skillShells`: `{ skill, command }`) — every `` !`…` `` whose `!` starts a line or follows whitespace (to the next backtick on the line, empty spans left out) and the body of every fenced block opened with ```` ```! ```` (to its closing fence or the end of the file), skills first (named by folder), then commands (named by path under `.claude/commands` without `.md`; symlinked folders not followed, 8 folders deep and 1,000 files at most), each in name order (`parse_skill_shell`). It also returns a SHA-256 over the canonical JSON (object keys sorted, no whitespace) of every returned entry's raw JSON (the skill shell commands as `{skill, command}`, added only when there are some, so a repo without any keeps its hash), so it is stable across key order and formatting and changes when any entry does (env values and headers included); nothing uses it yet. A missing, unreadable, over-1 MB or malformed file reads as empty, and when none of the files runs anything the launcher shows nothing. Otherwise a calm sage line sits under the launch line, "This repo's own Claude Code config runs 2 hooks, a status line, 1 MCP server and 3 skill shell commands." (", and it runs inside the sandbox." in a sandboxed mission: `exec_isolation = "sandbox"` or a `readonly` mission), with one mute mono row per entry ("PreToolUse Bash · ./scripts/guard.sh", "statusLine · ~/.claude/status.sh", "MCP db · npx -y db-mcp", "Runs as the skill loads · /deploy · git status --short", a fenced block's lines joined by "; "; truncated, the full row on hover). It asks for no acknowledgement and never gates Begin or a Routine. _Support:_ `repo_hooks.rs` (`parse_settings`, `parse_mcp`, `parse_skill_shell`, `canonical_json`, `from_texts`, `from_sources`, `read`), command `repo_hooks_notice`, `ipc.repoHooksNotice`, `lib/repoHooks.ts` (`repoHooksLine`, `repoHooksItems`), `PipelineSetup.tsx` (`data-tour="direct-launcher-repo-hooks"`).
- **Don't run skill shell commands in crews (per project, off by default)** — Under the repo-config notice, while the selected crew has a Claude Code CLI stage and either the repo's skills or commands run shell commands or the project already has it on, the launcher shows a settings `Switch` "Don't run skill shell commands in crews" with the mute line "Every Claude Code stage of this project's crews and Routines loads skills and commands without running their shell commands. This covers your own and plugin skills in those stages too." It reads `skill_shell_off(workspaceId)` and writes `set_skill_shell_off(workspaceId, off)` (the workspace's project; `projects.skill_shell_off`, `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`); a failed write puts the switch back. Each stage reads it from the DB when it starts (`Db::workspace_skill_shell_off` → `StageContext.skill_shell_off`, so Direct runs, Routines and the detached worker alike), and a Claude CLI stage, fresh or resumed, gets `"disableSkillShellExecution":true` merged into its `--settings` beside the write/read guards and the inner-sandbox override (`cli_runner::disable_skill_shell`, after `confine_reads_in_sandbox`). Claude Code then puts `[shell command execution disabled by policy]` where each command would have run. The launch line in the run journal adds "skill shell commands off for this project: skills and commands load without running them". Codex stages are left alone. Octopush never adds a `PreSkillShellCommand` hook: before Claude Code 2.1.332 a settings file naming it opens a dialog at start, which no one answers under `-p`. _Support:_ `db.rs` (`get_project_skill_shell_off`, `set_project_skill_shell_off`, `workspace_skill_shell_off`), commands `skill_shell_off` / `set_skill_shell_off`, `ipc.skillShellOff` / `ipc.setSkillShellOff`, `cli_runner.rs` (`disable_skill_shell`, `SKILL_SHELL_OFF_LABEL`), `lib/repoHooks.ts` (`SKILL_SHELL_OFF_LABEL`, `SKILL_SHELL_OFF_NOTE`), `PipelineSetup.tsx` (`data-tour="direct-launcher-skill-shell-off"`); contract test `stream_json_skill_shell_off_is_accepted_and_runs_nothing` (synthetic `2.1.332` fixture).
- **Superseded model: offer the switch (never automatic)** — Pipelines name model ids explicitly, so a crew built on a model the catalog marks as replaced stays on it. When a stage of the selected crew uses such a model, as its model or its escalation model, the launcher shows one quiet line above the crew's description: "Fable 5.1 → Fable 5.2: about 20% cheaper per token." (the percent is computed from the catalog's input prices; no line when an edited price makes the replacement no cheaper on input or output). **Switch this crew** saves that pipeline once through `save_pipeline` and its validator, with every stage model and escalation model on the old id moved to the new one and everything else saved as it was. A builtin is forked as "<name> (custom)", as the builder does, and the launcher selects the fork. Launcher overrides on the old id are dropped. A refused save shows a "Couldn't switch this crew" toast and leaves the line. **Keep 5.1** hides the line for that pipeline and model, persisted in the frontend (`localStorage` `octo-superseded-models`), so another crew still asks, and so does a model superseded later. When a Claude Code CLI stage would move and the installed CLI is known to be too old for the replacement, the line adds the floor note "Fable 5.2 needs Claude Code 2.1.321 or newer." in amber. Only `claude-fable-5-1` → `claude-fable-5-2` is marked today (`ModelInfo.superseded_by`, builtin metadata re-applied to `providers.json` on every load). Routine `stageOverrides` and custom roles aren't checked. _Support:_ `direct/SupersededModelLine.tsx` (`data-tour="pipeline-model-superseded"`) in `PipelineSetup.tsx`; `lib/supersededModels.ts` (`supersessionMap`, `pipelineSupersessions`, `supersededLine`, `switchedDraft`); `stores/supersededModelStore.ts`; `provider_router::backfill_superseded_by`.
- **Retiring model: warn before the stage fails (switch only on confirm)** — Providers refuse requests to a model after its published retirement date, and a crew keeps the ids it names. `token_engine::MODEL_RETIREMENTS`, next to the price table, lists (id prefix, name, retirement date, replacement), from Anthropic's model deprecations page; today only `claude-sonnet-4-5` → 2026-11-30 → `claude-sonnet-5-5`. A prefix matches first-party Claude API ids only: the trimmed id itself, or the id followed by `-` and a `YYYYMMDD` date, so the dated `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` counts. Bedrock and Vertex ids (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0`, `claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929`) never match: partner platforms set their own schedules, and Switch would rewrite them to a bare first-party id and change the provider (`token_engine::model_retirement`; command `model_retirements(models)`, asked once per id per session). The frontend does the date math in whole UTC days (`lib/modelRetirement.ts`): nothing until 30 days before the date (`RETIREMENT_NOTICE_DAYS`), then an amber mono line under the launcher foot when a stage of the selected crew uses the model, as its model, its launcher override or its escalation model: "Sonnet 4.5 retires Nov 30, so 2 stages on it will fail from then on." From the day after the date, the line turns rouge: "Sonnet 4.5 retired Nov 30, so a stage on it will fail." The year shows when it isn't this year. **Switch to Sonnet 5.5** first asks inline ("Every stage of this crew on Sonnet 4.5, escalations included, moves to Sonnet 5.5." · **Switch this crew** · **Not now**). It then saves only that pipeline through `save_pipeline`, moving every dated or undated id of the model to the replacement (`switchedDraft` takes several ids). A builtin is forked as "<name> (custom)" and selected, launcher picks of the old ids are dropped, and a refused save toasts "Couldn't switch this crew" and keeps the line. When only a launcher pick uses the model, the line shows without the switch. It never blocks Begin. Readiness and Settings › Routines show the same notice (see Settings panes and Routines). _Support:_ `direct/RetiringModelLine.tsx` (`data-tour="direct-launcher-model-retirement"`) in `PipelineSetup.tsx`; `lib/modelRetirement.ts` (`retirementPhase`, `crewRetirements`, `retirementLine`, `loadModelRetirements`); `hooks/useModelRetirements.ts`; `ipc.modelRetirements`.
- **Interrupted-run recovery (startup)** — Stages stuck `running` after a crash are stamped `failed` (`INTERRUPTED_STAGE_ERROR`); runs re-parked `paused`; the amber Resume affordance keys off the "interrupted" prefix. _Support:_ `db.recover_interrupted_runs`.

### Checkpoints, gates & review loops
- **Checkpoint gates** — A `checkpoint=true` stage parks `awaiting_checkpoint` + run `paused` on completion. Every "decision" park (a gate, a question, a halted stage) is also what "Notify me elsewhere" sends, when it is on (§1 Toasts & notifications). _Support:_ `checkpoint` column; `drive_inner`.
- **Secret guard hold (Action stages)** — Before a stage whose role runs in the **Action** environment (`pull_request`, `merge`, `release`, or a custom Action role) starts, the drive scans the worktree's changes against the workspace's base (see §6 "Secret guard"). A finding, a **partial** scan (16 MB budget) or a worktree the scan **can't read** (fail closed: a detached run or Routine never ships unchecked) parks the stage **never started** (`awaiting_checkpoint`, run `paused`), stores `run_stages.secret_hold` (JSON `SecretHold`: the first 50 findings without values, `total`, `partial`, `unreadable`, the fingerprint described in §6, `acknowledged`; the scan runs on `spawn_blocking`), journals "Held before the pull request: possible secret · GitHub token in tests/fixtures.ts:12" (or "… the secret guard couldn't read the worktree's changes, so nothing was checked", or "… · scanned the first 16 MB; the rest wasn't checked") and fires the same `run://checkpoint` `reason:"decision"` a gate does — so the needs-you band, the native notification and the beacon come for free; a detached run or a **Routine**-fired run parks the same way and never opens the PR on its own. The decision bar shows a rouge "possible secret" eyebrow and "Held before Pull request: possible secret · …" (`data-tour="direct-secret-hold"`, tooltip lists every finding), and its approve becomes **Proceed regardless** / **Proceed past them**: approving acknowledges exactly those findings (it does **not** carry the budget override, so a budget gate still fires) and the re-drive journals "secret guard: the director approved proceeding · …". A different set of findings at the re-drive (a new key added) holds again; findings removed from the worktree let it start; a reset (re-run) clears the hold. The setting off skips the check and clears a stale hold at the next drive. _Support:_ `Orchestrator::secret_gate`, `apply_checkpoint_action` (Approve arm), `secret_hold_stage_label` (orchestrator/mod.rs); `db.set_stage_secret_hold`; `RunControlBar.tsx`; `lib/secretGuard.ts` `holdSummary`.
- **Review loops — two modes** — A review stage (`can_loop`) can route work back to a `loop_target`. **Gated:** the run pauses; the human chooses Send-back vs Approve-anyway. **Auto:** the orchestrator loops target↔review automatically on a changes-requested verdict until it passes or hits the cap. **Structured verdicts (API):** auto-loop API stages carry a `submit_verdict` tool (`pass`/`changes_requested` + full findings — the findings become the review artifact); a tool call parses identically on every provider, where the `VERDICT:` text sentinel depended on model compliance. The sentinel still parses as a fallback and remains the CLI's only channel. When the auto loop DOES fall back to a human gate, the journal says why (no machine-readable verdict, or cap reached). _Support:_ `LoopMode`; loop columns; `agentic.rs` (`submit_verdict_tool`), `parse_verdict`, `roles.rs` (`VERDICT_TOOL_INSTRUCTION`/`VERDICT_INSTRUCTION`).
- **Loop-back mechanics** — Resets the contiguous `[target..=review]` range (restricted to flow-ancestors) to `pending`, forwards the reviewer's findings as feedback to **every stage in the reset window** (not just the target — the review artifact is nulled by the reset, so intermediate stages used to re-run blind), archives erased attempts, retires their cost, bumps the loop counter, **refreshes inner review stages' loop budgets** (a nested loop no longer arrives pre-exhausted on the second outer pass), and re-drives. The **loop target, if it is a Codex CLI writer** with findings to act on and a resumable session, **continues that session** (`codex exec resume`, the findings as the prompt) instead of re-reading the repo and the whole dossier. Every other stage in the window re-runs fresh with the refreshed dossier, a Codex writer included (its input, the target's new output, changed); so do Claude stages, reviews (a re-review must not anchor on its own verdict) and a loop-back that comes with an escalation. Whether the target is a read-only review or a Codex stage is judged on its effective model (escalation applied). Cap reached with changes still requested → the loop TARGET's unused **escalation policy fires** (one strong-tier loop-back, journal-narrated) before the run surrenders to a checkpoint. _Support:_ `loop_back`, `try_escalate_loop_target`, `db.increment_loop_iteration`, `db.retire_stage_cost`, `db.set_stage_loop_iterations`.
- **Checkpoint actions (full vocabulary)** — `resolve_checkpoint`: **Approve** (accept & continue; a failed stage's partial work is accepted via a synthesized artifact), **Reject** {feedback, model_override, max_turns_override} (re-run the single stage), **SendBack** {feedback} (loop the review back to its target), **Resume** {max_turns_override} (recover a halted stage; CLI `--resume`s the same session), **Discard** (revert the worktree to the failed stage's baseline), **Edit** (artifact edited out-of-band; continue), **AnswerBlocker** {answers} (answer a stage that parked itself via `ask_director` — see the escape valve below), **Abort**. _Support:_ `CheckpointAction`; `runsStore.resolve`; `RunControlBar`.
- **Escape valve — ask the director (`ask_director`)** — A DIRECT stage that hits a decision only the director can make (a genuine ambiguity, a missing spec/credential, contradictory requirements) **stops and asks instead of guessing**: it calls the `ask_director` tool with a one-line `summary` and structured `questions`, each carrying a **recommended default**. The tool is appended to the agentic loop **after** the per-stage allowlist filter (so it survives a review stage's read-only tools) and is **DIRECT-only** — never in TALK's shared `build_llm_tools`. On the call the loop **stops** (asking supersedes acting: any co-requested tool_use is discarded; the `BlockedAsk`/`BlockedQuestion` structs are tolerant — every field defaults and the underscore fields accept both camelCase and snake_case, so a well-formed multi-question ask never collapses; only genuinely garbage input degrades, and even then it salvages **all** array elements) and the runner returns a **blocked outcome**; the drive persists the questions to `run_stages.blocked_questions`, parks the stage `awaiting_checkpoint`, and fires the **same** `emit_checkpoint(reason:"decision")` a gate uses — so the crew "needs you" notification and the attention beacon fire unchanged (no new `StageStatus`; a block is just another checkpoint, distinguished by `blocked_questions IS NOT NULL`). The director answers via **`answer_blocker(run_id, stage_id, answers, source?)`** (from the Direct answer form, or from Mission Control's `?` card with `source: "mission_control"`): when every resolved answer is its recommended default, and none of those defaults is blank, the stage journal gets the notice "✓ Director accepted the recommended defaults" (+ " (from Mission Control)" for that source; `answers_are_defaults`/`accepted_defaults_notice`), so accepting stays visible and auditable. The decisions (each paired with its recommended default) become the stage's re-run **feedback**, `blocked_questions` clears, the asking spend is retired, and the stage resumes. **Conversation continuation (API):** the blocking stage's conversation transcript (including the asking turn, with raw content blocks so signed thinking replays) is persisted to `run_stages.blocked_transcript` while parked; the answered re-run **continues that conversation** — the answers arrive as the ask call's tool_result (sibling tool calls from the asking turn get explicit not-executed results) — so the exploration that produced the question is never re-run or re-paid. Consume-once: cleared when the answered run starts and by `prepare_rerun`; a missing/corrupt transcript falls back to the fresh-run-with-feedback path. A block is **answer-only**: `apply_checkpoint_action` refuses Approve/Reject/SendBack on a stage with `blocked_questions` (only AnswerBlocker, or Abort, proceed) and refuses AnswerBlocker on a non-block — a stale click can't mark a block done with an empty hand-off. A block also stamps `started_at`, so it is **not** treated as an editable un-begun park (`update_run_stage`/`StageFocus` require `started_at IS NULL`, not just "no artifact"). **Recommended-default fast path:** the answer UI pre-fills each input with the default, so accepting is one click. **API-substrate only** (CLI stages own their own interaction model): the carve-out is a separate `ASK_DIRECTOR_CLAUSE` appended by `compose_system_prompt(can_ask_director=true)` for API stages **only** — CLI stages keep the strict never-ask preamble intact (they have no such tool). **Ungated** (core trust, like crew notifications). _Support:_ `agentic.rs` (`ask_director_tool`/`parse_ask_director`, `AgenticResult.blocked`), `types.rs` (tolerant `BlockedAsk`/`BlockedQuestion`, `StageOutcome.blocked`, `CheckpointAction::AnswerBlocker`), `runner.rs`, `orchestrator/mod.rs` (`run_stage_once` block-park, `format_blocker_feedback`, `apply_checkpoint_action` answer-only guard), `db.rs` (`run_stages.blocked_questions` + `set_run_stage_blocked`; `update_run_stage` un-begun guard), `commands::answer_blocker`, `roles.rs` (`ASK_DIRECTOR_CLAUSE` + `compose_system_prompt(can_ask_director)`); frontend `RunControlBar` `BlockedAskBar`, `MissionControl` block indicator, `StageFocus` un-begun guard, `runsStore.answerBlocker`, `ipc.answerBlocker`/`BlockedAsk`; design record `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-14-escape-valve-design.md`. _Entry:_ automatic when a stage blocks; answered from the decision bar, or defaults accepted from Mission Control's `?` card.
- **Decision bar UI (state-adaptive)** — `RunControlBar.tsx` switches on status: TerminalBar ("Run it again"), **DraftBar** (a STAGED run — e.g. authored by `octopush-mcp` `create_run` — mono `draft` word, serif-phrase primary CTA **"Begin this run"** → `runsStore.start` → `start_run(runId, null)` + detail refresh, and a **discard** control via `abort_run`; a refused start (quota/concurrency gate) shows the upgrade sheet and leaves the draft intact — never a dead end), DecisionBar (checkpoint/halt, with Resume/Re-run turn-budget Stepper, Accept-partial, Discard-with-confirm, "why this halted" disclosure, feedback editor for reject/send-back, loop-state banner), **BlockedAskBar** (the escape valve: when a parked stage carries `blockedQuestions`, the decision gives way to **"The crew asked you"** — one input per question pre-filled with its recommended default, plus **"Send answers"** and **"Accept all defaults"**). While a run is simply running the bar renders **nothing** — pause/stop/abort live as the header's `IconButton`s instead (see Director controls above), and the single brass beacon (`lib/beacon.ts` `beaconAnchor`) sits on the DraftBar/DecisionBar's primary CTA or, mid-run, on the running stage's card in `RunFlow` — never on this bar. A started draft behaves exactly like a launcher-started run (checkpoints, gates, ledger); `hasExecutingRun` still counts only running/paused. _Entry:_ bottom command bar.
- **Inline comments at a gate (#957)** — While a stage is parked at its checkpoint gate with a text artifact (a plan, a review, any hand-off text; the run not finished, the current attempt on screen), the focus pane renders the artifact as a readable Markdown document (`ChatMarkdown`, sans body, `data-tour="direct-gate-document"`) instead of mono text; a mute "Select a passage, then Comment. From the keyboard: ↑ ↓ and ⏎." sits under it. The document is rendered once per text (memoised), so typing a note or a parent's re-render never rebuilds it. **A selection is left alone:** selecting a passage (drag, or Shift+arrows) only puts a small brass **Comment** button under its end (`.octo-pop-in`, title "Comment on this passage"; pressing it doesn't collapse the selection), so copying from the artifact works as anywhere else; the composer opens only from that button. **Keyboard path:** the document takes focus (Tab), `↓`/`↑` move a cursor over its passages (the leaf blocks: paragraphs, list items, headings, code blocks, quotes, table cells; brass-ghost wash with a brass-dim edge, `[data-comment-cursor]`), `⏎` opens the composer on the marked passage (or on a selection), `Esc` or leaving the document puts the cursor away; Shift+arrows stay the engine's. The composer sits under the document (`.octo-rise-in`, sticky at the pane's bottom, `data-tour="direct-gate-comment-compose"`; the shared `comments/CommentComposer.tsx`, the same one Review's "Ask for a change" uses): the quoted passage, a note field ("What should change here…"), **Add the comment** (⌘⏎ / Ctrl+⏎, only with a note) and Cancel (Escape). With the composer open, selecting another passage changes nothing until **Comment** is used, which points the composer at it and keeps the note typed so far. Comments list under the document as "your comments · N" (`data-tour="direct-gate-comments"`) in **document order** (by where the passage starts in the rendered text, not when it was added), each with its quote, note and a remove `X`; where WebKit's CSS Custom Highlight API is available the passages are marked in the text (`::highlight(octo-comment)`: brass-ghost wash, brass-dim underline), and the marks are laid again whenever the rendered text nodes change. Quotes collapse whitespace and are cut at 600 characters. With comments, the decision bar's line reads "**Plan**: 2 comments go with your decision." (`data-tour="direct-gate-comment-count"`). **Reject** and **Send back** carry them as structured feedback, the free text becoming the optional overall note ("2 comments on the output go with it, in document order."): "The director commented on 2 passages of the output, in document order:", then `1. On "<quote>":` + the note for each, then "Overall note: …" (`composeGateFeedback`); the backend is unchanged, so a send-back still prefixes the reviewer's findings. Review's **Send to the agent**, when it sends this gate back, carries them too, in the same message as its diff comments (#1051). The comments are cleared only once the decision is applied (`runsStore.resolveGate`: the gate's stage moved off this attempt); a refused Reject or Send back leaves them, and so does one the run accepts and then refuses in the background (a `run://error` recorded in `runsStore.runErrors` while the gate still waits; an info toast says "Nothing changed" and that the comments are still on the gate). An approve refused that late also takes its guidance back out and keeps the comments. **Approve with comments** (the Approve label when a stage that hasn't begun follows; tooltip "Your comments go to Implement as guidance") first writes the comments, for this one pass, into the instructions of every stage the gate hands off to (as in the orchestrator, a run is a flow graph as soon as any stage has `parents`: then the stages listing the gate as a parent, a parentless stage being a root; only with no `parents` anywhere, the next position) through `update_run_stage`, then approves. The guidance is a fenced block ("[Director's comments from the gate of stage 1, for this pass only]", "The director approved Plan with these comments; take them into account:", the same list, "[End of the director's comments from stage 1]") after the stage's own instructions, so it can be taken out again: a later approve of the same gate replaces it (never stacks) or, with no comments, removes it. A bracket that would read as one of the fence lines inside a quote or a note is written as a parenthesis, so removal always takes the whole block. One approve of a gate runs at a time (`runsStore.approvingGates`): a second click while the first is in flight does nothing, and the button is disabled meanwhile. If the approve is refused, the run is read again: only when the gate is still parked on the same attempt (`awaiting_checkpoint`, same `finishedAt`) is the guidance removed and the comments kept; a refusal because the gate was already decided leaves the guidance where it is, for the stage that is about to run with it. If a stage refuses the edit while the gate still waits, nothing is approved, guidance already written to other stages is taken back, the comments stay and an info toast says "Not approved yet"; if the gate was decided meanwhile, the toast says "Nothing changed" instead and nothing is taken back. The block is visible in the next stage's instructions editor while it waits. Limits: the guidance stays in the instructions of a stage that already ran with it, and a gate approved by any route other than Direct's decision bar does not take out an earlier pass's guidance. With no stage that hasn't begun, the bar says so before the click ("**Plan**: 2 comments. No stage follows to take them: Approve leaves them out, Reject or Send back carries them."), the button reads **Approve without comments** (tooltip "No stage that hasn't begun follows, so approving sets your comments aside") and the comments are set aside once that approve went through. Comments are in-memory drafts keyed by stage and attempt (`gateKey`: id + `finishedAt`), cleared once a decision carrying them went through, so a stage that loops back and parks again starts clean; what was sent stays on the archived attempt ("sent back with"). The brief and the stages' output contracts are unchanged. _Support:_ `components/comments/CommentableDocument.tsx` (`textOffset`, `rangeAt`; reusable for other documents), `lib/gateComments.ts` (`normalizeQuote`, `inDocumentOrder`, `composeGateFeedback`, `withGuidance`, `withoutGuidance`, `nextStages`, `gateKey`), `stores/gateCommentsStore.ts`, `runsStore.approveWithComments` / `resolveGate`, `StageFocus.tsx`, `RunControlBar.tsx` (`nextStageLabel`), `DirectCanvas.tsx`, `styles.css`. _Entry:_ Direct, a run parked at a gate.

### Live orchestration view
- **Structured live activity channel (`run://log`)** — Both substrates emit `LiveEntry` entries (`text`, `tool {name,hint}`, `tool_result {ok,detail}`, `notice`) through one `LiveEmitter`. _Support:_ `orchestrator/live.rs`; `runsStore` `liveByStage` (200-entry ring buffer per stage).
- **CLI substrate launch notice** — A CLI stage's journal opens with `launching {binary} · {model}` (plus `· resuming session` on a `--resume` run, and on Codex, last, `· codex 0.169.0` when `codex --version` answered: `agent_adapter::codex_cli_version`, cached per session and cleared by each Readiness check; `CliDialect::version_label`) the moment the process spawns — since the model id silently selects the dialect (B6), the journal names which CLI is actually driving. **Codex stream tripwire:** if codex streams ≥10 JSON lines and none matches a schema `codex_fold_event` recognizes (the codex CLI's JSON contract drifts across versions), a one-time notice says the live journal may stay quiet until the stage settles — silence is never unexplained. _Support:_ `cli_runner.rs` (spawn notice, read-loop tripwire).
- **Claude Code retries and load errors in the journal** — A Claude Code `system/api_retry` event becomes a notice `retrying · {error} · attempt {n}/{max} · in {s}s` (unknown causes print as-is), so a retrying stage no longer looks frozen; repeats for the same cause within 10 s are collapsed (`RetryThrottle`, reset when the model next answers). A `system/notification` event (e.g. "Fast mode disabled · usage credits exhausted") becomes a notice with its message as-is, first line only, read from `text`, else `message`, else `notification`; one with no text adds nothing. A `system/init` that lists `mcp_server_errors` / `plugin_errors` adds one notice each — `MCP server '{name}' skipped: {message}`, `plugin '{plugin}' failed to load: {message}` — since a skipped `--mcp-config` entry gives no other warning when stderr is captured. _Support:_ `orchestrator/live.rs` `entries_from_stream_event`, `RetryThrottle`; `cli_runner.rs` read loop; contract fixtures `stream-json/api-retry.jsonl`, `notification.jsonl` (synthetic), `init-with-load-errors.jsonl`.
- **Tool calls Claude Code refused** — Every Claude CLI stage runs with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, and since 2.1.326 Claude Code denies some calls there when nobody can be asked. `parse_cli_result` reads the `result` event's `permission_denials` (`tool_name`, `tool_input`; a missing or malformed list reads as none) into `CliOutcomeMeta.refused_calls`, and the runner journals one notice per call: `refused · {tool} · {hint}`, the hint being `tool_input.command`, else `file_path`, else `path`, on one line, passed through the secret guard's `redact_line` (your own credentials, provider token prefixes, AWS key ids, credential-named `NAME=value` and `key: "…"` assignments, bearer tokens, URL passwords → `[redacted]`), then cut to 80 characters; repeats of the same tool and hint collapse into `×n`. The drive stores the total on `run_stages.refused_calls` (cleared by a re-run or a later attempt with none; `get_run` → `refusedCalls`), and the stage reads a muted amber `N tool calls refused` (no brass: it isn't a gate; tooltip `REFUSED_CALLS_TITLE`) after the verdict or tokens on its run-track card's at-rest live line (`data-tour="direct-stage-refused"`) and beside the tokens in the focus pane's header (`data-tour="direct-focus-refused"`) — hidden in both while the stage is running again or an abort cut it, so a loop-back attempt never shows the last attempt's count. A refusal notice is never read as the card's verdict (`lastNotice` skips the `refused · ` prefix). The stage still settles as it would have: a writer stage (diff or tests) that otherwise succeeded is `done`, and its artifact — the next stage's hand-off — ends with "Claude Code refused these tool calls during this stage, so they never ran…" and the list, so a review stage can check them. _Support:_ `cli_runner.rs` (`refused_calls`, `refused_notice`, `refused_handoff`, `parse_cli_result_redacting`), `secret_scan::redact_line`, `db::set_run_stage_refused_calls` / `refused_call_counts`, `lib/refusedCalls.ts`, `RunFlow.tsx`, `StageFocus.tsx`; contract fixture `2.1.326/stream-json/result-with-denials.jsonl` (synthetic).
- **Living pipeline rail (depth of field + single beacon)** — One horizontally-scrolling rail of per-stage cards, governed by two laws. **Depth of field:** the SUBJECT — running / awaiting-checkpoint / failed / selected — renders at full ink, 210px wide: role icon + serif title + status glyph, then a status word + fixed-width elapsed timer, a fixed-height live-activity/verdict/tokens line (a running stage with no activity yet reads a mute "waiting for first tool call" there, `data-tour="direct-stage-waiting"` — the one place that waiting state shows), and a meta line (arabic position · model — short (`opus-5-5`) while running · while running, the stage's context reading `ctx 71%` when it fits (see "Stage context meter") · brass effort when set · brass `↑ {model}` when the stage escalated · substrate pill), plus a loop badge `⟲ {iter}/{max}` when looping. Every other stage recedes to a dimmed ESSENCE — 150px, 38% opacity rising to 70% on hover/focus — showing just role icon + role title + status glyph + arabic position · cost · tokens on one nowrap line (#874): tokens in the compact essence format (`fmtTokensShort`: `↑18k ↓3.1k`, no decimal from 10k up, millions as `M`), and when position + cost + tokens would overflow the card (`essenceShedsTokens`, 17ch) the token pair sheds through `.octo-demote-shed` — position and cost are the floor, the full figures stay in the line's tooltip (`fmtTokensFull`: `↑1.24M ↓31.0k`, millions as `M`, never `1240.0k`) and in sr-only text ("1.24M input, 31.0k output tokens"), since a shed pair is `visibility:hidden` to screen readers too (#937); the cost goes through `formatEstimateUsd`, so a positive cost under a cent reads `<$0.01`; an unknown cost reads mute `unreported` (`usageUnreported`; "usage not reported" is 18ch and never fits, so the label's tooltip opens "Usage not reported." before `USAGE_UNREPORTED_TITLE`, and a shed line's tooltip says "usage not reported") or `unpriced` (`unpricedModel`, `unpricedTitle`), never `$0.00`, and that label is what the shed measures; nothing is dropped, the SUBJECT's full detail is one click away in the focus pane. Transient-halt cards show amber `⟳` "stalled" in either geometry. **An aborted run's frozen stage** (the abort never rewrites the stage row, so it stays `running` / `awaiting_checkpoint`) reads as aborted instead (#891): the mute `■` from `runStatusMeta("aborted")`, the word `aborted`, a hairline border (the selected `brass-dim`/`brass-ghost` skin while it is the selected card, #904), no timer, no beacon, and the live line "the run ended at this stage" — never verdigris running, "waiting for first tool call" or brass review (`RunFlow`'s `runAborted` prop, fed by `DirectCanvas`). On an aborted run every gate card's `⟜` is mute, not brass, with the tooltip "Checkpoint — the run ended" (#904). **Single beacon:** cards never pulse on their own — only the one card matching `beaconStageId` (from `lib/beacon.ts`'s `beaconAnchor` selector) carries `octo-stage-pulse` (a static halo under `prefers-reduced-motion`); a running beacon pulses in its own verdigris (`octo-stage-pulse-running`, verdigris halo under reduced motion), so only a card that needs you — an awaiting gate — ever shows a brass border or halo. Cards are joined by solid 1px connectors — brass once the previous stage is `done`, hairline ahead (no gradients, no `⟶` ornament); a checkpointed card's own header carries its `⟜` gate mark instead of a connector glyph. Role icons come from `lib/roleIcons.ts` (`iconForRole`), each with a `title` tooltip — the retired `§` prefix is gone. Prev/next chevrons (`RunFlowNav`) appear only once the rail actually overflows: "Earlier stages" at the rail's left edge, "Later stages" at its right, each disabled at its scroll end; while an edge hides stages it fades out (a 32px `mask-image` edge-fade, `railEdgeFade`; overflow read by `useRailEdges`), so a connector whose stage is scrolled away fades rather than leading in from nothing. _Support:_ `RunFlow.tsx`, `RunFlowNav.tsx`, `lib/beacon.ts`, `lib/roleIcons.ts`, `lib/runStatus.ts` (`runStatusMeta`).
- **Stage context meter (Claude CLI stages; #895)** — How full a running Claude CLI stage's context window is, before Claude Code compacts it. **Reading:** in `cli_runner`'s stream fold, `ContextWatch` takes each top-level `assistant` event (`context_from_stream_event`: input + cache read + cache write of the message's usage, the same definition as Talk's `contextTokens`; a sub-agent's message (`parent_tool_use_id` set), the CLI's `<synthetic>` notices and a message with no prompt tokens are skipped) and hands a reading on only when it changed — the CLI repeats a message's usage on every content block, so at most one per message. The window follows the stage's configured model — or the model Claude Code ran it on instead (`ran_model`) — never the message's `message.model`, which drops a `[1m]` suffix: an id carrying `[1m]` gets 1M (`stage_context_window`), any other the catalog's `max_context` (`catalog_context_window` → `token_engine::catalog().find_model`, the catalog Talk's meter and Run's Context section read, gateway and custom entries included), looked up once per model; `None` when the catalog doesn't list it. **Transport:** `LiveEmitter::context` emits `run://context` `{ runId, stageId, contextTokens, contextWindow }` — not a journal entry; `PersistingSink` writes it onto the stage row (`run_stages.context_tokens` / `context_window`, nullable, `db::set_run_stage_context`) and forwards it, so an in-process run's app hears it at once. A detached run's worker has a null live sink: the bridge reads the run's readings each tick (`db::stage_contexts`) and re-emits each change as `run://context` through the raw sink (a stage whose reading is gone, null). `get_run` carries `contextTokens` / `contextWindow` per stage, so a reload or an adopted run shows the stored value. `runsStore.applyContext` keeps the newest event per stage in `liveContextByStage`, which wins over the stage row (`currentContext`), so a `get_run` refresh that lands after a newer event never brings an older value back. A stage (re)start (`set_run_stage_status` → `running`) clears the row and emits a cleared `run://context` (the bridge relays the clear for detached runs); a re-run's reset clears the row too; a finished stage keeps its final value. **Display:** `stageContextReading` gives two forms, toned alike by `contextTone` (Talk's thresholds, on the exact share): mute, `text-octo-warning` from 80%, `text-octo-rouge` from 95%. The focus pane's mono `ctx 142k / 200k` through `formatContextTokens` (tooltip "Context: 142,000 of 200,000 tokens (71%), the prompt of the stage's latest message"); the running card's shorter `ctx 71%` (tooltip "Context: 142k of 200k tokens"). The percentage is rounded down (`contextPercent`: 99.9% reads 99%, so 100% only means a full window). Hidden when the window is unknown (never a guessed 200k), when the reading is over the window (never `400k / 200k`), before the first message, and on Codex and API stages (their streams carry no per-message prompt size). On the **run-track card** only while the stage runs (`data-tour="direct-stage-context"`): a rung of the subject meta line's E2 ladder after the model (`octo-demote`), mounted shed while there is no reading so it grows in through the rung's own motion; a running card names its model short (`shortModel`: `opus-5-5`, full id in its `title`), and `subjectShedsContext` (30ch: 180px of 10px mono) counts the card's `ctx 71%` and sheds it first, whole, when position, the short model name, the shown notes (ran on · effort · escalation) and the substrate pill leave no room — `2 · opus-5-5 · ctx 71% · CLI` is 25ch, so it fits a plain running card and sheds beside an effort, escalation or ran-on note; a shed reading keeps its figures in sr-only text. In the **focus pane header** always (`data-tour="direct-focus-context"`, `.octo-pop-in`), beside the tokens, for a running stage and a finished stage's final value; hidden while an archived attempt is on screen and on a pending stage. _Support:_ `cli_runner.rs` (`context_from_stream_event`, `ContextWatch`, `stage_context_window`, `catalog_context_window`), `orchestrator/mod.rs` (the cleared reading at a stage start), `live.rs` (`RUN_CONTEXT_EVENT`, `LiveEmitter::context`), `persist.rs`, `bridge.rs` (`context_changes`), `db.rs` (`context_tokens`/`context_window` migration, `set_run_stage_context`, `stage_contexts`), `commands::get_run`; `lib/stageMeta.ts` (`stageContextReading`, `contextPercent`, `contextToneClass`, `subjectShedsContext`, `currentContext`), `RunFlow.tsx`, `StageFocus.tsx`, `runsStore` (`applyContext`, `liveContextByStage`), `RUN_EVENTS.context`. _Entry:_ automatic on a running Claude CLI stage.
- **Work journal / focus pane** — Selected stage's work, two-row header: row 1 is role lucide icon (`roleIcons.ts` `iconForRole`, `title` tooltip — the `§` prefix is retired) + mono uppercase role eyebrow + model + iteration-history navigator + director controls (gate toggle, edit/edit-&-re-run, re-run) + the context reading (see "Stage context meter") + tokens (mute) / cost (ivory `.octo-tabular`: a cost is data, so brass stays on the role eyebrow); row 2 is the serif stage title. Journal entries render as flat icon lines — tool icon (`iconForTool`) + tool name + hint + ✓/✕ + truncated result detail — no boxed tool cards. Modes: archived-attempt, failed (sticky halt banner), artifact (text + `SnapshotDiff` or live `DiffViewer`), running (live journal directly under the header — the old static brass-dot + role-verb marker is retired; the **inline Player** at its tail narrates instead; before the first entry lands the slot stays empty and the inline Player's "Thinking…" is the pane's one waiting indicator, while the stage's run-track card says "waiting for first tool call" in its live line), idle. **The Player in DIRECT** — the same Octo figure and roles as TALK (`direct/StageOctoStatus.tsx` over the shared `OctoPlayer`, `placement="inline"`), but rendered inline as a row (octopus, then label) instead of pinned at the canvas bottom (TALK keeps the pinned bottom-center default; no wash or bottom padding in DIRECT). Where it sits: while the stage runs with the live journal shown (`running` mode) it is docked at the journal's tail inside the scroll flow, so it follows the newest line; in every other active state — a checkpoint gate (`awaiting_checkpoint`) over an artifact and its diff, or a budget/director park in idle mode — it sits right under the stage header, outside the scroller, so the brass "Waiting for you" stays in view however long the diff is; after a stage ends it plays its exit (✓ beat / fade) where it was. Roles from `roleForStage` — `awaiting_checkpoint` → Waiting for you (brass, frozen); newest journal entry: tool → its family (Reading…/Searching…/Editing…/Running…), prose → Writing…, else Thinking…; a `done` stage earns the ✓ beat, a `failed` one leaves quietly; switching focused stages hard-resets (identity = stage id); hidden while viewing archived attempts. **Aborted run:** an abort leaves the stage it stopped on frozen at `running`/`awaiting_checkpoint`, so when the run is `aborted` the Player leaves quietly (no ✓ beat) and the pane shows a muted mono `■ aborted · the run ended at this stage` row under the header (`.octo-fade-in`, `data-testid="stage-aborted"`) instead of "Waiting for you" (#844). The reveal-after-finish drawer is labelled plain "work journal · N" (no `§`). _Support:_ `StageFocus.tsx`; `direct/StageOctoStatus.tsx`; `OctoPlayer.tsx`; `lib/roleIcons.ts`.
- **Journal persistence** — `PersistingSink` mirrors every `run://log` entry into `stage_log` (reset events → marker rows) so journals survive reloads and loop-backs. `StageFocus` refills an empty in-memory journal from the log's current segment for any stage that is no longer streaming: a non-running stage, and a stage an abort froze at `running`, so the journal of an aborted run is back after a relaunch (#891). _Support:_ `orchestrator/persist.rs`; `get_stage_log`; `StageFocus.tsx` + `runsStore.hydrateLog`.
- **Bridge per-run fault isolation** — The detached bridge's tick handles each leased run independently: a run whose relay errors is logged (`bridge tick failed for run`) and skipped for that tick, never allowed to abort the tick chain and silence every other run's live journal. _Support:_ `orchestrator/bridge.rs` `bridge_tick`.
- **Run header** — Stage `n/m` counter + "the brief" eyebrow over the (truncated) run task. _Support:_ `DirectCanvas`.

### Iteration history & diff snapshots
- **Archived stage attempts** — Before every reset, `archive_stage_attempt` snapshots the stage into `stage_iterations` (ordinal, role, model, status, artifact, error, cost, tokens, `closing_feedback`, `diff_snapshot`). _Support:_ `list_stage_iterations`.
- **Iteration navigator** — `‹ attempt N of M ›` when archives exist; viewing a past attempt shows its artifact/error, cost, "sent back with" feedback, journal segment, and `SnapshotDiff`. _Support:_ `StageFocus.tsx`.
- **Stage diff snapshots** — On a code-bearing stage finish (`refs_worktree`), the worktree diff is captured (capped 512KB) so the focus pane shows the worktree as that stage left it, frozen. _Support:_ `capture_stage_diff_snapshot`; `git_ops::get_diff_text`.
- **Focus-follows-action** — A pinned running stage that finishes auto-clears the pin so focus returns to the active stage. _Support:_ `DirectCanvas`.

### Director hot controls (mid-run redirection)
- **Hot-edit a pending stage** — Gate toggle (`⟜ gate` TogglePill: gated ↔ automatic hand-off) and an **"Edit stage"** modal (instructions, model, turn budget, loop mode for looping reviews) on any stage the run hasn't reached — live, no pipeline recreation, no restart, no reload. Edits touch only the run's own `run_stages` row (the template is never modified) and are honored when the stage builds its spec. _Support:_ `update_run_stage` (commands.rs → `db::update_run_stage`, guards: run non-terminal, stage un-begun); `runsStore.updateStage` (optimistic + `refreshDetail` reconcile); StageFocus header controls.
- **Field edits on a parked, un-begun stage** — A stage parked **before it began** (a budget park or a director pause, which hold the next stage with no work done) still takes field edits; the park itself is released via approve/reject, so toggling the gate while parked is rejected with a clear error. "No artifact yet" is the no-work-done discriminator: pre-work parks produce nothing, while a checkpoint **gate** park holds a *finished* stage's hand-off (artifact present) and is redirected via the decision bar or a re-run instead. _Support:_ `db::update_run_stage` `parked_unbegun` branch; StageFocus `fieldsEditable`.
- **Re-run from here** — A finished (done/failed) stage — and everything downstream — re-runs **in place**: downstream checkpoint parks are invalidated and archived, CLI sessions are never resumed (`session_id`/`resume_pending` cleared), loop counters restart, spend is retired onto the run (append, never reset). Offered on paused/completed/**failed** runs and on running runs **parked** at a checkpoint (`runBlocked`); guarded by an inline "discards downstream" confirm; mutually exclusive with concurrent resolve/rerun via the run's active-slot claim. _Support:_ `rerun_from_stage` → `prepare_rerun`/`resume_claimed_drive`; StageFocus `rerunnable` + confirm Reveal.
- **Re-run after changes** — A finished stage's Edit button becomes **"Edit & re-run stage"**: the same modal (plus the gate toggle as a field) whose primary action **"Save & re-run from here"** ships the director's patch WITH the re-run, atomically — validated before anything resets (a bad patch leaves the run untouched), applied once the stage is back to pending, honored by the re-driven spec. _Support:_ `StageRerunPatch` riding `rerun_from_stage`; `db::validate_stage_patch_fields`/`apply_run_stage_patch`; shared wire encoding `stagePatchArgs` in `ipc.ts`.

### Cost estimation & budget enforcement
- **Pre-run cost estimate, from this Mac's history** — The launcher foot reads `est. $0.40–$1.10 · saves ~62% vs all-premium`. For each stage, `Db::stage_token_samples` takes the tokens of the 20 most recent stages of the same `(role, effort)` in **completed** runs (Direct `spend_events` joined to `run_stages` by `source_id`, summed over every attempt, so loop-backs count; the stage being estimated keys by its effort on API and CLI stages alike — `effort_applies` on the launcher's chosen model — and every sample keys by its stored effort; a one-time migration (`codex_stage_effort_cleared_v1` in `app_meta`) cleared `effort`/`escalate_effort` on CLI run stages of **completed or aborted** runs that last ran on a Codex model (`escalate_model` once escalated, else `agent_model`) before Codex took an effort — stages of draft, running or paused runs, including budget-parked and retryable failed ones, keep theirs and run with it — so they count as no effort, as they ran, and the run view shows no effort pill on them). Those tokens are **re-priced at the stage's currently chosen model** (`prices_in`, catalog-first), so swapping a model gives the right figure instead of reusing old dollars. The range is the p25–p75 of the re-priced samples (linear-interpolated `cost::percentile`); the central figure is the median; the baseline re-prices the median tokens at the premium reference model. **Cold start:** with fewer than 3 samples a stage uses its role's built-in token prior (`token_est_in/out`) as the low end and 3× it as the high end, and the line adds "· rough" (tooltip says why). Hovering the range shows one line per stage (`role · model · effort  $low–$high  (N past runs | rough | unpriced)`). Changing a stage's model re-estimates in place (the previous figure stays until the new one lands; switching crew clears it to "estimating…"; if the estimate call fails, the figure is dropped and the line reads "est. unavailable" rather than keeping a figure for models no longer selected). Returns `{estimateUsd, lowUsd, highUsd, baselineUsd, unpricedModels, unpricedStages, perStage[], confidence: "history" | "rough"}`. **Unpriced:** a stage model with no price is left out of every figure, its breakdown line reads "unpriced", the range reads "est. unpriced" when nothing is priced (never $0), and the foot shows "· {model} unpriced" (tooltip explains it is not counted as spend or savings); with a budget set and unpriced stages it adds "· budget not enforceable: N stage(s) unpriced" (rouge — the budget gate compares billed cost, which an unpriced stage never adds to). Local-only: reads the local DB, no network. _Support:_ `estimate_run_cost` → `Db::stage_token_samples`, `orchestrator/cost.rs::estimate_run` (`StagePlan`, `StageEstimate`, `percentile`), `PipelineSetup.tsx` (`data-tour="direct-launcher-estimate"`), `lib/cost.ts` (`estimateRangeText`, `estimateSavingsText`, `estimateBreakdownTitle`, `unpricedTitle`).
- **Crew report card & right-sizing suggestions (#983)** — How each stage of a crew did in this Mac's latest runs of that pipeline, and what that suggests. `Db::stage_outcomes` reads every stage of the pipeline's settled runs (completed, failed or aborted; newest first) with its archived failed attempts (`stage_iterations`) and its `direct` spend per model that ran it; `orchestrator/crew_report.rs::build_report` keeps, per current stage, its latest 20 counted runs at the same position (cut where the position last held another role, so a role change starts a new record; an aborted run counts only its finished stages). Per stage: runs, **first pass** (done with no loop-back, no escalation and no failed attempt), **loop-backs** (a review's `loop_iterations` charged to the stage at its `loop_target_position`, not to the reviewer), escalated and halted counts, the median cost per run (every attempt summed) and the median per model; a stage with an unpriced attempt has no dollar figure (never $0). **Rules** (deterministic, only at `MIN_RUNS` = 8 or more; below it nothing is said): **start strong** — escalated in ≥ 50% of runs and an escalation model set: the saving compares the median actual cost with the same runs on the escalation model from the start (an escalated run at its strong attempts' cost, the others' tokens re-priced at it), shown only when both models are priced and dropped when it isn't cheaper; the edit sets the stage on the escalation model and clears its escalation model. **Try a lighter tier** — first pass ≥ 90% and no escalation, with a cheaper tier from the same provider (`next_lighter_tier`: a curated catalog model priced lower on input and output, a context window at least as large, not superseded or retiring; the dearest such): the edit sets the cheaper model and keeps the current escalation model or sets the current model as one, so the safety net stays; the saving re-prices the stage's tokens at the cheaper model (`prices_in`). **Loop hotspot** — ≥ 1.5 loop-backs per run: informational, names the review that sends it back. **Launcher:** beside the estimate in the foot, one sans line `1 suggestion · Plan escalates in 7 of 10 runs` (`data-tour="direct-launcher-suggestion"`; only with a suggestion) opens a `MenuSurface` with each suggestion in full and its serif phrase ("Start Plan on Opus 5.5", "Try Haiku 5.5 on Code review", "Open this crew in the builder", which opens the builder on the crew); an edit asks first ("Change this crew" / "Not now"), then saves the pipeline (a builtin is forked as "… (custom)" and the launcher follows the fork; a launcher model pick on that stage is dropped); a hotspot opens the builder. Every dollar figure reads "(estimate)". **Builder:** the stage inspector's collapsible **Track record** section (grid-rows `Reveal`, after the engine group; `data-tour="builder-stage-track-record"`; saved stages only) shows `20 runs · first pass 85% · loops 0.3 · escalated 10% · median $0.42` (tooltip: what each figure counts, halts, cost by model), a 10-outcome `StageDots` micro-history in the `outcome` tone (sage first pass · amber rework · rouge halt, oldest left; never brass), and each suggestion with its phrase, which patches the draft (undoable; kept only on save); below 8 runs: "Track record appears after 8 runs of this crew." Read-only and local: no network, nothing switches on its own. _Support:_ `get_crew_report` → `Db::stage_outcomes`, `orchestrator/crew_report.rs` (`build_report`, `next_lighter_tier`, `MIN_RUNS`, `WINDOW`), `ipc.getCrewReport`, `lib/crewReport.ts`, `direct/CrewSuggestionLine.tsx` via `PipelineSetup.tsx`, `builder/TrackRecord.tsx` via `StageInspector.tsx` / `PipelineBuilder.tsx`, `direct/StageDots.tsx` (`tone="outcome"`).
- **Live cost & all-premium baseline** — Per-stage actual cost accumulated; baseline re-prices the same tokens at the **premium reference model** (highest blended price among enabled providers; per-pipeline overridable). Includes retired (looped/rejected) cost so re-runs count truthfully. _Support:_ `orchestrator/cost.rs`; `recompute_run_cost`; `run://cost`.
- **Cost ledger strip** — Savings-first: "saved $X · N% under all-premium" / "spent $Y"; budget fragment — plus "· budget not enforceable: N stage(s) unpriced" (rouge, tooltip names the models) when the run has a budget and stages on an unpriced model or with usage not reported (`get_run` flags each stage `unpricedModel`, resolved after the DB lock, and `usageUnreported`); no progress bar (the printed percentage is the one encoding of the savings share); expandable per-stage breakdown (an unpriced stage that burned tokens reads "unpriced", never "$0.00"). **Usage not reported:** Codex reports tokens only in `turn.completed` (or legacy `token_count`), so a Codex CLI stage that fails (director Stop, the idle stall, the 60-minute cap, a `turn.failed`, a crash) while its last turn has no usage event — a `turn.started` with no `turn.completed` after it (`CodexAccum.turn_open`), or no usage event at all after the model did work (`CodexAccum.activity`: a `turn.started`, an `item.*` or a legacy agent `msg`; a stopped stage is flagged whenever it streamed no usage; only a failure before Codex starts a turn, such as a bad flag, no login at launch or an `error` before `turn.started`, provably spent nothing and stays unflagged; a turn that started and then failed, such as a 401 from an expired login or a 400 for an unknown model, is flagged, because the stream can't show whether it spent anything) — gets the `USAGE_UNREPORTED` marker line in its error (`cli_runner::stopped_stage`, `build_codex_outcome`; the halt line keeps the cause alone), keeping the usage its earlier turns did report; the drive sets the sticky `run_stages.usage_unreported` column (kept across re-runs — the unknown spend was burned) and journals "codex stopped before reporting usage, so this stage's cost is unknown" once. The stage stays at 0 tokens, out of spend and savings, and its breakdown cell reads "usage not reported" in the unpriced styling (a later attempt that did report reads "$0.20 + usage not reported"); it counts toward the budget-not-enforceable note. The collapsed strip also reads "· N stage(s) usage not reported" (mute, tabular, tooltip says the cost is unknown) right after the spent figure whenever any stage is flagged, budget or not, so unknown spend never reads as a bare $0.00. **Stopped Claude stages** (director Stop, stall, 60-minute cap — no `result` event, so no `total_cost_usd`), and a Claude stage whose stream reaches EOF with no `result` line (a crashed or killed CLI: "claude produced no result: …", `cli_runner::claude_no_result_stage`), are an estimate from the streamed `assistant` events, kept latest-per-message-id, and each message is priced at **its own model** (`message.model`, read by `usage_from_stream_event`; subagent messages often run on another model than the stage) and speed: `cli_runner::streamed_estimate` groups the messages by (model, fast) and prices each group through `prices_at_speed` for that model, each message on its own so it pays its own long-prompt tier (Pricing engine, "Per-request price tiers"), falling back to the stage model when an event names none. A group with no price — an unknown subagent model, or a fast message on a model with no fast rate — is never billed at another rate and never read as $0: the error gets the `USAGE_UNPRICED` marker line naming the models ("part of this stage's streamed usage has no price, so that part of its cost is unknown (claude-opus-5-5 (fast))"), the drive flags the stage `usage_unreported` and journals that line once, the stage keeps only the priced messages' tokens and cost (so the baseline never counts the unknown part as saved), and its cell reads "$0.20 + usage not reported". A stage whose usage is all its own unpriced model at standard speed is unchanged (it already reads "unpriced" from its model). Token-less messages and Claude Code's `<synthetic>` placeholder messages (its own error replies, such as `model_not_found`) are never counted as unpriced. A flagged stage whose recorded tokens were all on unpriced message models writes its $0 ledger row with `cost_basis = "unpriced"` (`Db::record_direct_spend` reads `run_stages.attempt_usage_unreported`, the same flag for the current attempt only, cleared when an attempt starts), never a free "computed" row; a later attempt that reported its usage is labelled by its own model, so a re-run on a $0 model never reads "unpriced" because of an earlier attempt. The tooltip names both causes.
