The success path (`total_cost_usd`) is unchanged; the 2.1.314 recordings pin `message.model` on every assistant event, and a synthetic 2.1.325 fixture covers an Opus stage stopped mid-Haiku-subagent (`data-tour="direct-ledger-strip"` on the strip, `direct-ledger-usage-unreported` on the strip's fragment, `direct-ledger-usage-unreported-stage` on the breakdown cell). A one-shot completion "moment" (`octo-sweep` + The Octo at 20px in `pushed` state — one rise, brass halo, happy eyes). _Support:_ `RunLedger.tsx`; `runStatus.ts`; `icons/OctoMark.tsx`.
- **Budget enforcement (between-stage gate + intra-stage stop)** — Optional per-run `budget_usd`; before a pending stage starts, if spend ≥ budget the stage parks `awaiting_checkpoint` + run `paused` with a budget notice. Approving is a conscious override. **Intra-stage (API):** the agentic loop receives the run's remaining headroom when the stage starts; once the stage's own spend (peer consultations included) crosses it, the current turn's tool calls are voided and the forced-close path produces an annotated artifact — a single 100-turn stage can no longer blow far past the cap unchecked. A stage started via the conscious override runs unmetered, as the override intends. An API stage whose loop errors after real rounds (retries exhausted, a context 400) keeps those rounds' tokens and cost on the failed stage, and their conversation, so Resume continues there instead of re-paying (`run_agentic_loop_billed`, #1149). **Intra-stage (Claude Code CLI):** the same headroom is passed as `--max-budget-usd` (the headroom rounded down to cents, at least $0.01; a `--resume`d stage then adds the session's prior reported total, so its cap always sits above what the session already spent, since a resumed run reports the conversation's whole total), and the journal says so — the cap is Claude Code's own estimated API-equivalent cost, which can differ from the actual bill. A stop there (`error_max_budget_usd`) keeps its spend and session and parks the run at the halt decision with the budget notice ("Claude stopped at the run's budget"); it **never escalates** (a strong-tier retry would spend more). Resume continues the same session within whatever budget is left (its cap is the remaining headroom on top of the session's prior reported total, recorded on the stage row when Resume or an answered block sets `resume_pending`); if the budget is used up, the drive's budget gate parks the stage and asks before it continues. Accept-partial and discard work as for any halt. Codex CLI stages have no such flag and rely on the between-stage gate. _Support:_ `pause_for_budget`, budget gate in `drive_inner`, `StageContext.spend_limit` → `run_agentic_loop` / `cli_budget_cap` + `max_budget_args` in `CliRunner::run`; `parse_cli_result` / `is_budget_stop` (skipped by `try_escalate`), `StageSpec.resume_prior_cost_usd`; `haltCause` (`lib/stageHalt.ts`); `set_run_budget`.

### Entitlement & quota (premium — enforcement live)
- **Signed entitlement token (#582; dormant until a key is compiled in)** — the plan no longer has to come from the unsigned `plan` string in the `octopush` / `clerk-oauth-session` keychain item (rewriting it to `"pro"` unlocked the client-side Pro gates). `octopush-api`'s `POST /api/entitlement` (Bearer Clerk token) signs `{v:1, sub, plan, iat, exp}` with Ed25519, a **30-day lease** (`LEASE_DAYS`); the token is `v1.<b64url claims>.<b64url sig>`, signature over `"v1.<b64url claims>"`, deliberately **not** a JWT (no algorithm field). `verify_token` refuses tokens over 4 KiB before decoding, then checks shape → strict signature (`verify_strict`; weak/small-order public keys are refused when parsing) → only then parses claims → `v == 1` → `sub` is the signed-in user → not past `exp`; `iat` is not checked (only the server signs, and a check would refuse fresh tokens on a Mac whose clock runs slow). **Resolution** (`Entitlement::resolve`, behind `Entitlement::current`): **`ENTITLEMENT_PUBLIC_KEY` empty** (the shipped state) → the legacy session plan, byte-identical to before, and no token is fetched or read; **key set** → a valid token's plan, and *anything else* (signed out, no token, forged, tampered, wrong version, another user's, expired) → **Free**. The token lives in the keychain beside the session (`octopush` / `entitlement-token`, read once per launch) and is **refreshed on launch** (background), **after sign-in** (background) **after checkout returns** (`auth_sync_plan`, awaited), and from **`auth_refresh`** (the post-checkout poll) whenever Clerk's session plan disagrees with the token's (`token_lags_session`), all over `tls::client_builder()`; a refresh that changes the effective plan emits **`entitlement-changed`**, which `entitlementStore` (subscribed once via `ipc.onEntitlementChanged`) answers by reloading; a refresh is skipped entirely while no key is compiled in. **Every failed refresh keeps the cached token** (offline, 401, 503 `not_provisioned`, a response that does not verify), so only 30 days with no successful refresh end the lease; the exception is a validly signed token for a different user, which clears the cache. A token is stored only if the same user is still signed in when the response arrives (`decide_refresh`). **Ending the session clears it** (`auth::clear_session`: sign-out and a revoked refresh token); a store or clear that lands while the keychain is being read wins over that read (`load_token`). **With a key, the client-side sync gates follow the token too** (`sync::sync_active` → `Entitlement::current`), and the server still re-checks the plan on every sync call. **What it does not stop:** a rebuilt binary bypasses it; and the token is not bound to this Mac: `sub` comes from the same unsigned keychain session, so another Pro user's token plus an edited `sub` (with no refresh token, so nothing re-checks it) gives Pro until that token's `exp`. **Before the key is switched on**, the Privacy pane's `OUTBOUND` line and the website's privacy page must change in the same PR, because every signed-in user then POSTs to octopush-api on launch, sign-in, checkout and the `auth_refresh` poll whether or not sync is on (checklist on `ENTITLEMENT_PUBLIC_KEY`). _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/entitlement_token.rs` (`ENTITLEMENT_PUBLIC_KEY`, `verify_token`, `store_token`/`load_token`/`clear_token`, `refresh`/`spawn_refresh`/`decide_refresh`/`token_lags_session`/`set_app_handle`; the refresh URL honours `sync::test_net`'s base override), `entitlement.rs::resolve`, `auth::keychain_entry`, `auth::clear_session`, `commands::auth_begin_sign_in`/`auth_refresh`/`auth_sync_plan`, `lib.rs` setup, `src/stores/entitlementStore.ts` + `ipc.onEntitlementChanged`; server side `octopush-api` `api/entitlement.ts` + `api/_lib/entitlement.ts`, key generated by its `scripts/entitlement-keygen.mjs`. Tests in `entitlement_token.rs` use a fixed clock and an injected test key against the real `verify_token`, including tokens minted by the TypeScript issuer. _Entry:_ automatic.
- **Runs-left ledger fragment** — Folded into the launcher's run-grammar ledger foot (the standalone `DirectRunsMeter` component is retired): a quiet "N runs left" fragment for capped plans or "N runs this month" when uncapped, tinted sage while comfortable, amber past 80% of the cap, rouge at the cap (uncapped stays mute). _Support:_ `PipelineSetup.tsx` (`runsTone`), `useEntitlement` hook, `entitlementStore`; command `direct_run_usage` → `db.count_started_runs_this_month` (runs that have *left* `draft` — i.e. been started — since the start of the month). _Entry:_ Direct launcher ledger foot.
- **Run quota + concurrency gates (live)** — `start_run` consults the current entitlement before driving a run; both gates return `AppError::UpgradeRequired { feature, used, limit }`, which the frontend catches (`runsStore.begin` → `isUpgradeRequired`) to show a feature-aware **upgrade sheet** (`UpgradeSheet.tsx` + `upgradeStore`, mounted globally) with an "Upgrade to Pro" button that opens the Dodo checkout. **(1) Monthly Direct-run cap** — over `FREE_DIRECT_RUNS_PER_MONTH` (=25) for non-Pro → `feature: "direct.unlimited"`. **(2) Parallel/background runs** — Free / signed-out may run **only one Direct run at a time across all workspaces**; starting a 2nd while one is `running`/`paused` returns `feature: "runs.parallel"`. **Pro** (`RUNS_PARALLEL`) runs **multiple workspaces concurrently** (each run drives as an independent background task — for Pro, a **detached worker process**; see *Detached runs*). _Same-workspace_ concurrency stays blocked for **everyone** (`orchestrator::has_concurrent_run`) — git-worktree safety. The plan comes from the signed-in user's Clerk `public_metadata.plan` (`entitlement::current` → `for_plan`), or from the signed entitlement token once a key is compiled in (see above). _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/entitlement.rs` (`Entitlement`, `for_plan`, `check_direct_run_quota`, `has_feature`, `feature::RUNS_PARALLEL`, `FREE_DIRECT_RUNS_PER_MONTH`), `db::count_active_runs_excluding`, both gates in `commands::start_run`; command `get_entitlement`. See [`docs/premium/`](premium/) (incl. `pro-real-implementation-plan.md`).

### Halt detection & recovery
- **Halt classification** — `isTransientHalt` (`runStatus.ts`) detects recoverable substrate faults (interrupted/crash, rate limit, overloaded, `API error 429|529|5xx`, timeout, connection reset, DNS — each on word boundaries) to choose the amber Resume affordance; when that Resume (or a plan-limit wait's "Resume the stage") holds the beacon it pulses amber, never brass (`.octo-stage-pulse-warning`). Mirrors backend `ProviderErrorKind::is_transient`. A hook-deferred tool halt (`isDeferredToolHalt`, `stageHalt.ts`) is never transient, so a tool name like `mcp__cloudflare-dns__…` or a "timed out" stderr tail can't flip it to "awaiting retry"; `DecisionBar` also skips the check whenever the cause sets `preferRerun`.
- **Halt cause copy** — `haltCause(error, maxIterations)` maps `error_max_turns`, `error_max_budget_usd`, "could not save its session", the hook-deferred `(terminal_reason: …)` markers, `error_during_execution`, "sent no request in" (a stall before the first request; its remedy is the Claude Code update when the backend named one), "no output for", "exceeded … cap" to plain-English title+remedy. A deferred-tool cause, or a stall before the first request, sets `preferRerun`: the halt banner's primary action is then **Re-run · N turns** with a secondary **Resume** (the session is kept), instead of the usual Resume-first order. Whenever Re-run is the primary action (a deferred tool, or no session to resume), a secondary **Re-run with feedback** opens the feedback editor first, as on the review path; the re-run keeps the chosen turn budget. _Support:_ `stageHalt.ts`, `DecisionBar` (`RunControlBar.tsx`).
- **Hook-deferred tool calls** — Claude Code ≥ 2.1.319 reports `terminal_reason` on the `result` event. A run whose PreToolUse hook deferred a call (`permissionDecision: "defer"`, only from the user's own hook settings; Octopush configures none) ends with `terminal_reason: "tool_deferred"` as a clean `success` with empty text and exit 0. `parse_cli_result` matches the reason (never the English notice) before every other branch and fails the stage instead of reading it as done: "A hook paused ‹call› before it ran. Resume once it may run, or re-run the stage." A `--resume` whose deferred tool is gone (an MCP server removed, a built-in tool now disallowed) ends with `terminal_reason: "tool_deferred_unavailable"`, `is_error: true` and exit 1. It fails with "The resumed session was waiting to run ‹call›, which isn't available anymore. Reconnect it and resume, drop the call and continue, or re-run the stage fresh.", not as a session-not-saved stage. The call comes from `deferred_tool_use` (`id`, `name`, `input`) as the tool-call cards show it (`deferred_call_preview`): the tool, then ` · ` and the card's one-line hint of the input (`live::tool_hint`: its command, path, …), redacted by the secret guard and cut to 80 chars like a refused call's hint — "A hook paused Bash · npm publish --tag beta before it ran." `mcp__‹server›__‹tool›` reads "‹tool› (MCP server ‹server›)", and any name that doesn't split cleanly (a `__` inside a part) is shown whole. The halt bar and the journal's "⏹ Stage halted —" line read that first line. Both keep the session id and the spend, and `try_escalate` skips both, because a stronger model meets the same hook. Resume still sends its usual prompt on stdin. Older CLIs send no `terminal_reason`, and nothing changes for them. **Dropping a gone tool's call:** on a `tool_deferred_unavailable` halt with a resumable session, the run bar's secondary actions read **Reconnect and resume** (the ordinary Resume, once the tool is back) and **Drop the call and continue** (`data-tour="direct-halt-drop-call"`; acts at once, no confirm). The drop is the `drop_call` checkpoint action (`CheckpointAction::DropDeferredCall`, refused on any other stage). It resumes like Resume and sets `run_stages.drop_deferred_pending`, so the stage's next run, and only that one, gets `drop_deferred_call` on its `StageSpec`. That `--resume` runs with `CLAUDE_CODE_DROP_UNAVAILABLE_DEFERRED_TOOL=1` (`drop_deferred_env`) and `DROP_DEFERRED_PROMPT` on stdin (`CliDialect::resume_stdin`) instead of the nudge, so Claude gets an error as the call's result and carries on without it. _Support:_ `TOOL_DEFERRED`/`DEFERRED_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE`, `is_tool_deferred`/`is_deferred_tool_unavailable`, `deferred_tool_label`, `deferred_call_preview`, `DROP_DEFERRED_TOOL_ENV` (`cli_runner.rs`); `isDeferredToolUnavailable` (`stageHalt.ts`); synthetic fixtures in `tests/fixtures/claude-code/2.1.319/` (a `SYNTHETIC` marker, not a recording).
- **Finished but session not saved (exit 1 after success)** — Claude Code ≥ 2.1.317 makes `claude -p` exit 1 when a full disk or quota loses its transcript or a `~/.claude.json` write, after a `success` result. `parse_cli_result` treats a non-zero exit with `is_error: false`, `subtype: "success"` and non-empty text as its own case: the stage fails with "Claude Code finished the work but exited with an error — it could not save its session (disk full or quota?)…", plus the stderr tail and the free space on the worktree's volume (`statvfs`, `with_free_space`); it keeps the result as the stage artifact (so Review shows it and Approve accepts the real result instead of a synthesized stub), drops the session id (so the run bar offers only Re-run, which starts a fresh session rather than `--resume`-ing a transcript that was never written), and `try_escalate` skips it — a stronger model will not free the disk. Other non-zero exits (`is_error`, budget stop, bad subtype, empty result) are unchanged. _Support:_ `SESSION_NOT_SAVED`/`is_session_not_saved` (`cli_runner.rs`), Failed arm of `run_stage_once` + Approve arm (`orchestrator/mod.rs`).
- **Claude plan limit park (auto-resume at `resetsAt`)** — A Claude Code CLI stage on a Claude Pro/Max plan that hits a plan window is parked, not failed for a decision. **Detection:** the read loop feeds every stream event of a session that isn't API-key authenticated to `PlanLimitWatch` (`cli_runner.rs`): a `rate_limit_event` whose `rate_limit_info.status` is `rejected` with `isUsingOverage: false` and a `resetsAt` records the wall (`PlanLimit { window, resets_at }`); the same window reported `allowed`/`allowed_warning` again clears it; an `assistant` event with `error: "rate_limit"` (the CLI's synthetic "You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets …" notice) is remembered. Only the stage's own top-level messages count (one with a `parent_tool_use_id`, a sub-agent's, is ignored). `apply_plan_limit` then turns the outcome into a plan stop when the stream showed a wall and the stage failed with the CLI's limit notice or with that rejection as the last rate-limit event before the result (a failure after a later allowed request has another cause) — or "finished" with the CLI's own limit notice as its reply (a success-shaped result is a stop too, its notice never an artifact). The error reads "Paused by your Claude plan — the 5-hour window is used up until it resets." plus `PLAN_LIMIT_MARKER` `(plan_limit)` and the CLI's own words; spend and session id are kept; a budget stop, deferred tool or unsaved session keeps its own cause. `rejected` with `isUsingOverage: true` (extra usage serves the request) is not a stop. API-key users see no change. **Park:** the stage halts like any failure (journal `⏹ Stage halted — Paused by your Claude plan…`), never escalates (`try_escalate` skips `is_plan_limit`), and the run pauses at the batch boundary — never mid-stage; a sibling already running in the batch finishes. A plan-limited stage's checkpoint fires after every sibling in the batch is handled, so a sibling's gate or halt is known when the park's reason is decided. `Orchestrator::park_for_plan` (`orchestrator/plan_wait.rs`) persists the wait on the `runs` row (`plan_window`, `plan_resets_at`, `plan_resume_at`, `plan_resume_count`; `RunRow.plan_wait` / `Run.planWait`) and schedules the automatic resume at `resetsAt + 90 s + 0–60 s jitter` (`park_decision`, pure), journaling "Paused by your Claude plan · resumes at 19:40". The run waits for the director instead (no `plan_resume_at`, journal says why) when the run's budget is spent, when **3 automatic resumes** already ran into the wall (`AUTO_RESUME_CAP`; the count resets when the director acts — any `dispatch_checkpoint` — or a stage finishes), or when the window resets more than 8 days away. **Stale report (#1109):** a rejection whose `resetsAt` is already past (Claude Code before 2.1.332 can report a limit after it reset) is stale (`plan_wait::stale_count`, counted in a row on `runs.plan_stale_count`; a report with a reset still ahead, the director acting or a stage finishing starts it over). The first resumes once at `now + 90 s + jitter`, even past the cap, journaling "Claude Code reported a plan limit that had already reset · resumes at 19:40, not counted as an automatic resume"; its claim doesn't count toward `AUTO_RESUME_CAP` (`Db::claim_plan_resume` / `restore_plan_resume` skip it while `plan_stale_count > 0`) and its resume journals "Resuming after a plan limit that had already reset · not counted as an automatic resume". A second in a row (`STALE_RESUMES` = 1) waits for the director (`DirectorReason::StaleReport`, a `decision` checkpoint, so Notify me elsewhere sends `plan_limit`; the uncounted resume sends nothing), the journal and the `PlanWaitBar` reading `STALE_REPORT_NOTICE`: "Claude Code reported a plan limit that had already reset. Claude Code 2.1.332 fixes this. Update Claude Code, then Resume." (`planWait.planWaitWhy`, with the sentence "paused by a plan limit that had already reset" and Mission Control's "plan limit · already reset"; `Run.planWait.staleCount`, the constant and copy pinned by `planWait.test.ts`). Within one batch the park's own stale report isn't counted twice. **Resume:** the app's scheduler tick (30 s, beside Routines, for Free and Pro) lists due runs (`list_due_plan_resumes`) and `claim_plan_resume`s each — a compare-and-set on `plan_resume_at` (`Db::claim_plan_resume`), so the app and a waiting detached worker can race and exactly one resumes; it re-checks the budget (spent ⇒ the run waits for you, "decision" checkpoint, `PlanClaim::NeedsYou`), applies the ordinary **Resume** to **every** plan-limited stage of the run (several branches that hit the wall together all resume, each on its own session; same dossier, `--resume`; checkpoints still hold) and journals "Claude plan window reset · resuming (automatic resume n of 3)", then drives it on the run's own substrate: a detached worker for a detached run (`runs.detached`, `spawn_detached_segment`, in-process fallback), else in-process. The claim itself does not clear the schedule: it moves the resume 60 s out (`RETRY_SECS`), and only applying the Resume ends the park, so a claimant that fails or dies between claim and apply leaves the park due again. A Resume that can't be applied (another driver holds the run, a database error) puts the park back, due again in 60 s and not counted against the cap (`Db::restore_plan_resume`, retried a few times, `PlanClaim::Retry`) — only if the schedule is still the claim's own (or the failed apply cleared the park): a director who turned the automatic resume off meanwhile keeps it off, and the apply itself re-checks the schedule and doesn't resume a cancelled one (`PlanClaim::NotClaimed`). A claim that finds no plan stage left on a paused run whose stages are pending, with nothing waiting for a decision and no driver (no in-process drive, no live worker lease — a Resume applied only in part), journals "Claude plan window reset · the resume didn't finish, so it waits for you" and returns `PlanClaim::NeedsYou`, so a waiting worker posts "The crew needs you" instead of exiting quietly (`plan_wait::stalled`); after 10 consecutive failed applies (`MAX_PLAN_RETRIES`, counted on the row in `runs.plan_retry_count` so the app and a detached worker share one count and a restart keeps it; the director acting — a decision, a re-run, turning the automatic resume off — or a stage finishing starts it over) it stops retrying and waits for the director (`PlanClaim::NeedsYou`, a `decision` checkpoint, journal "Couldn't resume automatically after 10 tries"). A budget of 0 counts as no budget, as in the drive's budget gate. When stages of one batch hit different windows, the park keeps the one that resets last. A re-run (`prepare_rerun`) that resets every plan-limited stage ends the park, and any re-run gives a fresh allowance of automatic resumes. A director's manual Resume of a plan-limited stage likewise resumes all of them; resolving a sibling (approving its gate, resuming its real halt) leaves the plan park and its schedule in place. The schedule lives in the DB, so it survives an app restart. **Detached runs:** a worker whose segment parks with a resume scheduled doesn't exit; it releases its lease, waits (wall-clock polling every 15 s, so a Mac asleep through the reset resumes soon after waking), claims the resume itself, re-takes its lease and drives on — so an overnight crew resumes with Octopush closed; with the app gone it posts "Paused by your Claude plan" (· resumes at 19:40) and "Crew resumed". It waits only when the plan is all that waits (`plan_wait::worker_plan_wait`: a resume scheduled and no `otherHold`); a segment that parks beside a sibling's halt, gate or question ends the worker with "The crew needs you" instead (the app's scheduler resumes the plan stages later). It exits when the director resumes or aborts. When it stops waiting on a run that is still paused with a stage only the director can move (`plan_wait::needs_director`: the resume was turned off or handed to the director, the claim found the plan stages resolved while a sibling waits, its budget is spent, or applies kept failing) it posts "The crew needs you" with the app gone (`announce`). A database error while waiting is retried with backoff (1 s doubling to the 15 s poll, about 15 minutes in all, `MAX_DB_RETRIES`) instead of being read as a lost claim; past that it also posts "The crew needs you". Re-taking the lease after the wait retries a database error (about a minute) before it gives up and posts "The crew needs you"; a lease held by another driver ends the worker quietly, since that driver runs the resume. Notifications need the app gone; with the app open its own events tell the director. **Events:** while a resume is scheduled and the only stages waiting are plan limits (`plan_wait::only_plan_holds`), the park's `run://checkpoint` carries `reason: "plan_limit"` (`park_reason`, also the bridge's), not `decision`; a sibling's real halt, gate or question makes it `decision`. The run row carries the same answer as `planWait.otherHold` (a stage `failed` without the plan marker, or `awaiting_checkpoint`), which the Dock badge (`fleet_status::plan_waiting`), the fleet chip and Mission Control (`isPlanWaiting`) read; `needsYou.fixtures.json`'s `planWait` cases pin Rust and TS. **Director:** the decision bar's `PlanWaitBar` (`data-tour="direct-plan-wait"`, warning tone, `Hourglass` + mono `plan limit`) reads "{Stage} paused by your Claude plan · resumes at 19:40" (or "· the 5-hour window resets at 19:40" when it waits for you), with **Resume now** (the ordinary `resolve_checkpoint("resume")`; resolving a plan-limited stage, and abort, clears the park) and **Don't resume automatically** (`cancel_plan_resume`, `data-tour="direct-plan-wait-cancel"`: the run stays parked for a manual Resume, journal "Automatic resume turned off · resume when you're ready", a silent `director` checkpoint) plus Abort; once it waits for you, **Resume the stage** is the decision and takes the beacon. A scheduled park never takes the beacon (`beaconAnchor({ planWaiting })` → calm) — but only while the blocked stage is itself the plan limit: a blocked stage that is a real halt or a gate still takes it. When a sibling's gate, halt or question waits beside the plan limit (`otherHold`), the canvas puts that stage first (`planWait.pickBlockedStage`): its decision bar shows instead of the `PlanWaitBar` and takes the beacon, and the plan wait shows on the fleet surfaces. Every decision passes the stage it is about — the canvas the stage its bar shows, Mission Control's Resume now the plan-limited stage, the automatic resume the plan-limited stage it claimed — so none falls back to the first resolvable stage of the run (`stageId` is required in `ipc.resolveCheckpoint(runId, stageId, action, opts)` and `runsStore.resolve`; the backend's `stage_id` stays optional, `None` only in Rust tests): a named stage that is no longer waiting (decided elsewhere meanwhile) is refused with "This stage was already decided — refresh to see what's waiting." (`Orchestrator::check_named_stage` in `dispatch_checkpoint`, checked again in `apply_checkpoint_action`; Abort and no `stageId` are unaffected), which `runsStore.resolve` shows as a calm info toast before it refreshes the run. The bar fades in (`.octo-fade-in`); the cap is one constant, `AUTO_RESUME_CAP` in `plan_wait.rs` and `planWait.ts` (pinned by `planWait.test.ts`). `haltCause` names it "Paused by your Claude plan"; `isTransientHalt` treats it as transient (amber stalled card). _Support:_ `orchestrator/plan_wait.rs`, `cli_runner.rs` (`PlanLimitWatch`, `apply_plan_limit`, `is_plan_limit`, `plan_window_name`), `orchestrator/mod.rs` (Failed arm, `try_escalate`, `handle_stage_outcome`, `apply_checkpoint_action`, `abort_run`), `bridge.rs`, `routines.rs` (tick), `bin/octopush-run-worker/main.rs` (`wait_for_plan_reset`), `db.rs` (`set_run_plan_wait`/`clear_run_plan_wait`/`cancel_plan_resume`/`claim_plan_resume`/`reset_plan_resume_count`/`plan_resume_count`/`list_due_plan_resumes`), `commands::cancel_plan_resume`; frontend `lib/planWait.ts`, `RunControlBar.tsx` (`PlanWaitBar`), `runsStore.cancelPlanResume`, `ipc.cancelPlanResume`; contract fixture `stream-json/subscriber-rate-limit-rejected.jsonl` (synthetic). _Entry:_ automatic when a Claude plan window is used up.
- **Refused stage settings (Claude Code ≥ 2.1.323)** — When `--settings` that turn the sandbox on fail validation, `claude -p` stops at start-up instead of running Bash unsandboxed and names the invalid setting (2.1.326 still emits a `result` event: `error_during_execution`, `is_error: true`, `num_turns: 0`, the reason in `errors[]`, `startup_failure_reason: "sandbox_required_unavailable"`, exit 1). `parse_cli_result` anchors on the real signal (`refused_setting`): `startup_failure_reason: "sandbox_required_unavailable"`, or a line of `errors[]`, else stderr, that starts "Sandbox required but unavailable" and says "failed validation" (any other "failed validation" line, e.g. a gateway probe's, does not count). It never takes over a budget stop, a max-turns stop or a result with `num_turns > 0`. It reads the first such line (else the first `errors[]` entry) and fails the stage with "Claude Code refused the stage's settings: <that line>" (plus the stderr tail) instead of "claude stopped early (error_during_execution)"; a stage with no `result` event and such a stderr line gets the same error. The halt banner shows that line as its title. Such a stage is never escalated (`is_settings_refused`; a stronger model starts with the same settings) and keeps no session to resume. Octopush's own stage `--settings` carry no `sandbox` key, and in a 2.1.326 recording an invalid `--settings` value with the sandbox on only in the user's `settings.json` did not stop start-up, so this is a guard. _Support:_ `cli_runner.rs` (`SETTINGS_REFUSED`, `refused_setting`, `settings_refused_error`), the 2.1.326 fixtures `stream-json/settings-refused.{jsonl,stderr.txt}` and `stream_json_refused_settings_name_the_setting` in `claude_code_contract.rs`.
- **Halt journal entry** — A terminal `⏹ Stage halted — {first error line}` notice is appended; the agentic cap emits "iteration cap reached". _Support:_ `record_halt`.
- **Session capture & CLI Resume** — The CLI session id is persisted on each finish; Resume `--resume`s the same session with a fresh turn budget on Claude Code; a Codex stage runs `codex exec resume <id>` when its session's reported total is recorded (else it re-runs fresh; see CLI dialects). _Support:_ `session_id`/`resume_pending`/`session_usage` columns; `build_cli_args_resume`, `CliDialect::resume_argv`, `Orchestrator::cli_session_resumable`.
- **Empty-resume guard (Claude Code)** — A resumed Claude stage (a director Resume, or an answered `ask_director` block) whose `--resume` comes back on an empty conversation is stopped as soon as its stream shows it (best effort: a tool its first reply asked for may already have started) and re-run fresh once, with the full input dossier and, after an answered block, the director's answers (a plain Resume carries no feedback). It counts as empty when its `system/init` names another session than the one resumed, or when its first top-level reply reads less than 15% of the context the stage last reported (under 8K tokens when none was recorded). The journal says "resume came back empty: Claude Code opened a new conversation (…). The stage runs fresh, with its full input." (ending "…with its full input and your answers." when the stage carries non-blank feedback), and on a known CLI below 2.1.330 adds "Claude Code 2.1.330 fixes --resume opening an empty session; update Claude Code." (an unknown version never does). Both attempts' spend is kept. A resuming CLI stage therefore always gets its dossier and live diff assembled. _Support:_ `ResumeWatch`, `EmptyResume`, `empty_resume_notice`, `CLAUDE_EMPTY_RESUME_FIX`, `CliRunner::run_stage` (`cli_runner.rs`); `resume_context_tokens` column (`keep_stage_resume_context`, set by Resume and AnswerBlocker before the reset), `StageSpec::resume_context_tokens`; fixture `claude-code/2.1.329/stream-json/resume-empty.jsonl`.
- **API transcript continuation on Resume** — An API stage that halts *unfinished* (turn cap, intra-stage budget stop, director stop) persists its in-flight conversation (`blocked_transcript`, empty `ask_tool_use_id` = the continuation flavor); a director **Resume** re-runs by CONTINUING that exact conversation with the fresh turn budget — completed exploration is never re-paid (the API analogue of CLI `--resume`). Reject, loop-backs, escalation, and stage re-runs clear the transcript instead: those are defined as fresh attempts (and may swap models, where replaying signed thinking blocks would be rejected). _Support:_ `resume_messages_for_continuation` + unfinished-exit capture (`agentic.rs`), Failed-arm persist in `run_stage_once`, `archive_and_reset_stage(preserve_transcript)` (`orchestrator/mod.rs`).
- **Turn-budget override on recovery** — Resume/Reject carry `max_turns_override` (UI default = current ×2 for an `error_max_turns` halt). _Support:_ DecisionBar Stepper; `set_stage_max_iterations`.
- **Accept partial work** — Approving a **failed** stage (other than a finished-but-unsaved one, which keeps its own result) synthesizes a role-shaped artifact (preserving burned cost) + salvages the journal, completes it `done` without writing the ledger again (`accept_run_stage_partial`), drives on. _Support:_ Approve arm, `salvage_journal_text`.
- **Discard (per-stage baseline revert)** — A baseline (dangling commit of the worktree at stage start, captured via a temporary git index) is snapshotted before each stage; Discard makes the worktree byte-identical to that baseline. _Support:_ `orchestrator/git_baseline.rs`; `baseline_commit` column.

### Run navigation & the run hub
- **Viewed-run vs executing-run decoupling** — Three-state per-workspace view: absent=active run, `null`=launcher, runId=that run. _Support:_ `runsStore` `getViewedRunId`/`selectRun`.
- **DirectCanvas (RUN-mode shell)** — Crossfades between builder, launcher/empty, and the active run layout (run header + RunFlow + StageFocus + RunLedger + RunControlBar). _Support:_ `DirectCanvas.tsx`.
- **"Run it again" (re-launch prefill)** — Terminal runs offer "Run it again": seeds a one-shot launcher prefill `{task, pipelineId, overrides}`. _Support:_ `LauncherPrefill`; TerminalBar.
- **Launcher ("The Commission")** — One composition surface, not a wizard (the roman step framing, "— direct" eyebrow, and animated brass gradient rule are all retired): serif title "Direct the work" + sans subtitle "A crew of agents, your brief, one run." The brief is a serif textarea on panel with a linked-issue chip (when the run carries a tracker issue) and a `⌘⏎ to begin` hint. The ensemble is a horizontally-scrolling depth-of-field `PipelineTicket` rail + "Compose a new one", with the selected pipeline's `StageFlow` crew line beneath it. The foot is a run-grammar ledger (savings, cost, runs-left) plus the budget input and the **unattended-readiness affordance**; "Begin the run" is a ghost until brief + ensemble + quota + concurrency all hold, then turns solid brass carrying the single beacon (`lib/beacon.ts`'s `launcherReady` arm). _Support:_ `PipelineSetup.tsx`, `direct/PipelineTicket.tsx`, `direct/StageFlow.tsx`, `lib/beacon.ts`. _Entry:_ Direct tab with no active run; `⌘⏎` begins the run once ready.
- **Unattended readiness (launcher foot)** — Makes "run this crew while you walk away" an explicit, visible decision instead of an invisible automatic one. A **Free** user sees a locked **`Unattended · Pro`** chip (`Lock`) — clicking opens the `runs.detached` upsell ("Let your crews run while you're away — detached, surviving app quit, with a native ping when a crew needs you or finishes"), turning the previously-silent in-process fallback into a discoverable Pro capability. A **Pro** user sees a quiet **`Moon` "Runs unattended"** confirmation (the crew keeps going even if you quit — detachment is automatic for Pro). **The sandbox affordance is separate and FREE for everyone** (security is never gated): a **`Shield` toggle** — brass **"sandbox it"** to confine, verdigris **"sandboxed"** to turn it back OFF, after the same confirmation as the header's Shield (`SandboxOffDialog`, #1230) (the escape valve when a build must write outside the workspace — e.g. a genesis project, which is sandboxed by default). It sets `exec_isolation` on the *existing* mission via `update_mission` (accepts `exec_isolation`) → `missionsStore.setExecIsolation` → `db::update_mission_exec_isolation`. Composes the already-shipped detached worker (v0.4.8) + sandbox (M3.1/M3.1b) + crew notifications (v0.4.7) into one coherent launch-time affordance. _Support:_ `src/components/UnattendedReadiness.tsx`, `PipelineSetup.tsx` foot, `useEntitlement().hasFeature("runs.detached")`, `upgradeStore` + `UpgradeSheet` `runs.detached` branch, `missionsStore.setExecIsolation` → `ipc.updateMission` → `commands::update_mission` (+ `exec_isolation`). _Entry:_ Direct launcher foot.
- **Launcher crew editor** — The selected ensemble's crew at rest is one quiet line (role icon + name, an overridden model in mute, a brass `· {effort}` when reasoning effort is set, a brass `· ↑ {model}` when an escalation policy is set, `⟜` on a gated stage, `⟲ ×N` on a looping review); a pencil icon unfolds a `Reveal` editor of per-stage cards with in-place `ModelPicker` overrides (a CLI stage allows Anthropic and OpenAI models, since the model picks Claude Code or Codex), substrate chip, a brass effort chip, a brass `↑ {model}` escalation chip, tool dots, gate/loop badges — launch-time model tuning only, and it folds again when the ticket selection changes. _Support:_ `direct/StageFlow.tsx`.
- **Pipeline ticket** — 184px selector card in the depth-of-field rail: the selected ticket at full ink, the rest receding to 38% opacity (rising to 70% on hover/focus); `&` brass seal for builtins, name (truncates with an ellipsis; the full name is the card's tooltip — rows are `w-full min-w-0` and the card is `overflow-hidden`, so a long name never draws over the next ticket in WebKit), a neutral "shape" tone `StageDots` line (every dot sage, only the gate ring carries meaning), "N stages", hover/focus-revealed pencil icon → builder. _Support:_ `direct/PipelineTicket.tsx`, `direct/StageDots.tsx`.

### Notable implementation details
- **Orchestrator architecture** — `Orchestrator` (`orchestrator/mod.rs`) drives runs as background tokio tasks, one stage at a time, pausing at checkpoints; enforces a single active drive per run, holds per-run cancel flags + pause requests, routes every emit through a `PersistingSink`. The `EventSink` trait decouples it from Tauri for testability.
- **Drive loop** — Pick lowest non-`done` stage; complete the run if none; check budget gate then director-pause; run the stage; on a block (`ask_director`) → paused+checkpoint carrying the questions; on Failed → **try one automatic escalation** (`try_escalate`: a stage with an escalation policy that hasn't used it retries once at the strong tier, else) paused+checkpoint; on Done → auto-loop verdict decision before the gated pause. Aborts mid-stage always win.
- **DB tables** — `pipelines`, `pipeline_stages` (+ pos/parents/tools/custom_name/instructions/loop/max_iterations/effort/escalate_model/escalate_effort), `runs` (+ cost/baseline/reference_model/retired/budget/linked_issue_key), `run_stages` (private per-run copy + status/tokens/cost/artifact/feedback/error/loop/diff_snapshot/session_id/resume_pending/baseline_commit/effort/blocked_questions/escalate_model/escalate_effort/escalated/secret_hold), `roles`, `stage_log`, `stage_iterations`, `run_events`. The `effort` column (nullable TEXT, the `Effort` token; NULL = off) is additive on `pipeline_stages` and `run_stages`; `blocked_questions` (nullable TEXT, JSON `BlockedAsk`) and `blocked_transcript` (nullable TEXT, JSON `BlockedTranscript` — conversation-continuation state for both an `ask_director` block and an unfinished failure awaiting Resume, never serialized to the frontend) are additive on `run_stages` (the `ask_director` escape valve); the escalation policy — `escalate_model` (nullable TEXT), `escalate_effort` (nullable TEXT) — is additive on both, and `escalated` (INTEGER DEFAULT 0, sticky run-state) is additive on `run_stages`.
- **Tauri events** — `run://stage-update`, `run://cost`, `run://checkpoint`, `run://error`, `run://log`. Subscribed once in `runsStore`.
- **Worktree as the blackboard** — Stages never commit (handoff = worktree + structured artifact); all runs in a workspace share the one worktree, which is why only one executes at a time. A completed run leaves changes uncommitted for Review mode.
- **Shared micro-track primitive** — `direct/StageDots.tsx` is the universal stage-dot track: "status" tone colors by run state (done verdigris; running verdigris with a faint `--verdigris-strong` halo; awaiting a gate brass; failed rouge; stalled amber; pending hairline; a gated stage keeps its `--brass-dim` ring) so brass on a dot always means a crew waits on you — never just "busy", "shape" tone is the neutral launcher-ticket variant (every dot sage, only the gate ring carries meaning), and "pager" tone is the What's new modal's page indicator (`seen` / `current` / `upcoming`; the current page is the one brass dot, no run status reused). Now consumed by `PipelineTicket`'s ticket shape line.

---

## 5. REVIEW Mode (Diff, Editor & AI Review)

### Mode shell & layout
- **3-column Review canvas** — Left `ReviewSidebar` (Changes/Files navigator) · center `ReviewCanvas` (Diff/Editor) · right `CompanionReview` (change intelligence). _Support:_ `App.tsx`, `ReviewCanvas.tsx`. _Entry:_ ModeSwitcher → Review.
- **Diff ⇄ Editor view toggle** — Segmented control (LayoutList "Diff" / PenLine "Editor"); controlled by parent so any surface can deep-link. _Support:_ `ReviewCanvas.tsx`. _Entry:_ canvas toolbar.
- **Toolbar demotion ladder + "More" menu** — The canvas toolbar is a query container (`.octo-reviewbar`) with one rung: when the toolbar itself is ≤ 600px wide (narrower than at a 1280×800 window, where the folded sidebar leaves it about 676px) the secondary toggles (Inline/Side-by-side, ±WS, Tests) shed together (`.octo-demote-secondary`, animated width, leaves the tab order) and a `MoreHorizontal` "More view options" button grows in their place (`.octo-reviewbar-more`). Its menu (`.octo-menu-enter`, `role="menu"`) holds the same controls — layout as radio items, Ignore whitespace as a checkbox item, Tests opening the test-command popover — and closes on pick, Escape, an outside click, a switch to the editor view, or the toolbar widening past 600px (`REVIEWBAR_MORE_BELOW`, where its trigger sheds). It works from the keyboard like the other menus: opening focuses the first item, ↑/↓ (and Home/End) move between items, Tab closes it, and closing on a pick or Escape returns focus to the trigger. The More and Tests buttons sit on `border-octo-border-strong`, the control edge token. Brass is held to one action: Accept all is the only brass button at rest; AI is a ghost button in mute ink on the control edge (`border-octo-border-strong`), and AI, More and Tests turn brass only while open (a running test shows its spinner, not brass). Diff/Editor, AI and Accept all are the floor and never shed. The menu and the test popover are anchored to the header (a rung's `overflow: hidden` would clip them); the header's z-index lifts them over the diff and the AI drawer, and the canvas root is `isolate` so that z-index stays inside the canvas and the ContextHeader's popovers still paint above it. _Support:_ `ReviewCanvas.tsx` (`MoreItem`), `styles.css`. _Entry:_ canvas toolbar when it is ≤ 600px wide (`data-tour="review-toolbar-more"`).
- **Deep-link navigation to file/line** — `navigateToFile(path, "diff"|"editor", line?)` switches mode, opens the file or scrolls the diff, optionally reveals a line. _Support:_ `App.tsx`. _Entry:_ terminal links, chat links, Files tree, AI findings, Changes rows.

### Diff viewer (read & triage)
- **Continuous hybrid diff** — files → sticky hunk rails → syntax-highlighted, word-diffed lines (not cards). A changed word's fill (`.wd-add` / `.wd-del`) carries the theme's text ink instead of its syntax ink, which would fall under AA on the fill (`lib/contrast.ts` `WORD_DIFF_*_ALPHA`). _Support:_ `review/DiffView.tsx` → `FileDiffSection` → `HunkRail` + `DiffLines`; `lib/diffParser.ts::parseFullDiff`.
- **Per-hunk rail** — Sticky brass-bordered bar: human range (one nowrap line), `+adds`/`−dels`, focused state, Accept / Reject / Why? buttons (Why? only in the read-only Since base view; Why? and Revert in This turn). Accept is a ghost button in sage on the control edge (`border-octo-border-strong`) that turns brass only on hover (the toolbar's Accept all is the one brass action). The actions are `shrink-0` and always show whole; on a narrow canvas the range is the elastic atom and ellipsizes, with its full text in its `title`. _Support:_ `review/HunkRail.tsx`.
- **Accept hunk** — Stages just that hunk (`git apply --cached -p1`). _Support:_ `ipc.stageHunk` → `stage_hunk`.
- **Reject hunk + undo** — Reverse-applies (`git apply --reverse`), shows a 6s undo bar; undo re-applies (`apply_hunk`). _Support:_ `ipc.revertHunk`/`applyHunk`; `friendly_git_error`.
- **Accept all** — Stages every change (`git add -A`). The toolbar's one brass action. _Support:_ `stage_all_changes`. _Entry:_ toolbar (`data-tour="review-accept-all"`).
- **Inline vs Side-by-side** — Persisted toggle; SBS pairs del/add runs into two synced columns with cross-pane word-diff. _Support:_ `reviewPrefsStore.readingMode`, `DiffLines.tsx`.
- **Ignore-whitespace toggle** — Persisted; hides whitespace-only changes. _Support:_ `reviewPrefsStore.ignoreWhitespace`.
- **Syntax highlighting in diff** — Every language the editor highlights, stream modes included (Go, Kotlin, Scala, Groovy, Dart, Protocol Buffers, Sass, Shell, C, C++, C#, Swift, Ruby, SQL, Lua, TOML, Dockerfile, properties), through the same parsers (`editorLanguages.ts::languageFor`) and a class-only HighlightStyle that mirrors the editor theme tag for tag. Highlighted **in context**, not line by line: for a modified file the section reads the file on disk (≤ 1 MB, once it is expanded) and rebuilds both sides up to the last hunk — the old side by reverse-applying the hunks — then parses each side once and maps the tokens onto the rows, so a hunk that opens inside a Javadoc, block comment, docstring or multi-line string colours those lines as comment/string. New and deleted files, larger files, or a file that changed since the diff was taken fall back to parsing each hunk's old and new side as one document. Word-diff marks are laid over the syntax classes, so changed lines keep their colours. Bounded memo per (language, document). _Support:_ `lib/diffSyntax.ts` (`highlightFile`, `rebuildSides`, `highlightHunk`, `overlaySegments`), `review/FileDiffSection.tsx` (`ipc.readFileChecked`), `review/DiffLines.tsx`.
- **Word-level diff** — LCS over tokenized runs between paired removed/added lines (cap 400 tokens). _Support:_ `lib/wordDiff.ts`.
- **Per-row line-number gutters** — Old + new line numbers, `+`/`−`/space sign column. _Support:_ `DiffLines.tsx`.
- **File header** — Change-type badge (NEW in verdigris, DELETED in rouge, MODIFIED in mute mono like the hunk count; status is never brass), path, then at the row's end the collapse chevron, hunk count and "mark viewed". The path is the only elastic item: middle-truncated through `<MidTruncate>` with the file name pinned (`pathTail`) and the full path in its `title`, in a `flex-1 min-w-0` cell so it elides into a definite width (a cell sized from its own text let WebKit cut the path with no ellipsis, #868), and its head keeps its own ellipsis after every measuring pass (the hold is inline on the head, design-system E1, #872); every other atom is `flex-none` + nowrap. The row is a query container (`.octo-filehead`) whose one demotion rung sheds the hunk count at ≤ 420px. _Support:_ `FileDiffSection.tsx`, `styles.css`.
- **Collapse / "viewed"** — Collapse a file; marking viewed auto-collapses. A mark remembers the content fingerprint of each hunk the file had (`hunkFingerprint`, FNV-1a over row kind + text, line numbers ignored); when a refetch brings a hunk it didn't have (the file changed again, e.g. the agent's next pass), the mark drops, the file expands and a quiet verdigris "changed since viewed" chip (`data-tour="review-file-changed"`) sits in its header until it is re-marked. Accepting or rejecting a hunk only removes fingerprints, so it keeps the mark. Marks reset when the workspace changes. _Support:_ `review/DiffView.tsx`, `review/FileDiffSection.tsx`, `lib/diffParser.ts`.
- **Keyboard triage** — `j`/`k`/↓/↑ move hunk focus, `]`/`[` jump file, `Space` fold, `a` accept hunk, `x` reject, `A` accept whole file, `v` viewed, `o` open in editor, `w` why, `m` ask for a change on the focused hunk (working tree only), `/` focus filter, `c` focus commit, `?` toggle help. _Support:_ `review/useDiffKeyboard.ts`.
- **Jump-to-change / flash** — Scrolls a section (and a specific new-line row) into view and flash-highlights; toasts "Not in the current diff" on miss. _Support:_ `lib/diffJump.ts`.
- **Since base (committed view, #851)** — Direct crews commit their work, so Review can also show what the workspace **committed** since its base, not only the working tree. `get_committed_diff(workspaceId, ignoreWhitespace)` diffs the merge base tree → HEAD tree (renames paired; working-tree and untracked changes never in it) and counts the commits on HEAD since the merge base (capped at 10,000). The base and merge base are the collision radar's and Mission Control's diff size's: `collisions::workspace_base` (the workspace's `from_branch`, else the project's default branch) and `collisions::resolve_merge_base` (the newer of the merge bases with `origin/<base>` and `<base>`). It runs on a blocking thread with a 5 s timeout (`null` on timeout, an unknown workspace, or a path that is not a git repo; a workspace without a worktree path diffs the project path), and the answer is cached per worktree by (HEAD, merge base, whitespace mode, base name), so the 3 s Review poll rebuilds no patch until a commit lands, and a workspace whose base branch changes at the same merge base gets the new `base` label (#903). App fetches it beside the working diff in Review only, after a commit from the Changes rail too, into `reviewSourceStore` (equal answers are dropped). **Which view:** with no commits ahead there is only the working tree (no toggle). With commits ahead, the canvas toolbar's left end shows a mono segmented control *Working tree* / *Since base · N commits* (`data-tour="review-diff-source"`; the committed segment's tooltip names the base and merge base). Without a pick it defaults to the working tree when that has changes (today's view) and to the commits when the tree is clean; a pick holds per workspace until restart (`resolveReviewSource`). The default is **pinned once Review has shown it** (`reviewSourceStore.pinDefault`, from `hooks/useReviewDefaultPin.ts`), so a crew touching a file never switches a reader of Since base to the working tree mid-read; the pin comes only from answers fetched during this Review visit for this workspace (App's `reviewAnswers`: the git status and committed answer of one Review refresh, tagged with the workspace id and dropped on a workspace switch or on leaving Review), never from the previous workspace's status or a committed answer cached from an earlier visit. A pinned Working tree stays on the working tree even after a crew commits everything: the canvas reads *"The working tree is clean."* and the **Read what was committed** link remains there to switch to Since base. An explicit pick still wins, and leaving Review drops the pins (`clearPins`), so the next visit starts from the default (#903). On a narrow canvas the toggle is on the toolbar's ladder: at ≤ 600px (`.octo-reviewbar`) the committed segment sheds its count (`.octo-demote-source-count`), reading *Since base*; both segments are the floor, and the count stays in the button's accessible name and the lock's tooltip (#903). A jump from the Changes rail, the secret guard's **Show it** or a provenance chip while Since base is on screen switches to the working tree first (an explicit pick) instead of toasting "Not in the current diff" (#903). In the mode band's tail a committed diff cut by the 1 MiB cap counts its files as a floor, "N+ files changed" (`isDiffTruncated`, `reviewTailParts`'s `partial`). **Read-only:** the committed view shows a `Lock` icon beside the toggle (*"Read-only: N commits since main, already committed. Accept and Reject act on the working tree."*, `data-tour="review-diff-readonly"`); its hunk rails carry only *Why?*, `a`/`x`/`A` do nothing and the `?` help leaves them out (`keyboardHelpLine`), Accept all is hidden; the AI pass reviews the committed diff. It highlights hunks against the file on disk only while the working tree is clean. Switching source starts the diff's viewed/collapsed marks fresh. _Support:_ `git_ops::committed_diff` / `CommittedDiff` (base, merge base, HEAD short SHAs, commit count, diff), `commands::get_committed_diff`; `ipc.getCommittedDiff`, `stores/reviewSourceStore.ts`, `lib/reviewSource.ts`, `ReviewCanvas.tsx` (`source`, `commitsAhead`, `onSourceChange`), `DiffView` / `FileDiffSection` / `HunkRail` (`readOnly`), `App.tsx`. _Entry:_ Review › canvas toolbar.
- **This turn (a Talk turn's changes, #1152)** — A third scope in the same *Diff source* control: Talk's **Review these changes** (§3) sets the turn on the workspace (`reviewSourceStore.openTurn` → `turnByWs` + a `turn` pick), switches to Review and its diff view, and a mono *This turn* segment (`data-tour="review-diff-turn"`, its tooltip naming the turn's ask) appears after Working tree and Since base; the control then shows even with no commits ahead (Since base still only with some). It stays for the session until another turn replaces it; Working tree or Since base switch away, and a jump from the Changes rail, the secret guard or a provenance chip switches to the working tree first. `resolveReviewSource` shows a `turn` pick only while a turn is set. The diff is `talk_turn_diff(threadId, messageId, ignoreWhitespace)`: the unified diff between the turn's checkpoint and `-after` (`git_ops::commits_diff`, renames not paired, so each hunk reverses on its own path; empty when either ref is missing), read once per turn and whitespace mode (`hooks/useTurnDiff.ts`), not on the 3 s poll; it includes shell and sub-agent edits. **Triage:** nothing to accept (the change is already in the tree), so Accept, `a`, `A`, Accept all and Ask for a change are absent; each hunk rail carries *Why?* and **Revert** (`x`), which reverse-applies that hunk to the **working tree only** (`revert_hunk`, `git apply --reverse`, never the index). `git apply` writes nothing unless the whole hunk still applies, so a hunk whose lines changed since the turn leaves the tree untouched and a toast says *"This hunk changed since the turn."* (only for that error, `lib/turnChanges.ts` `isStaleHunkError`; with ±WS on, the toast says the hunk can't be reverted with whitespace ignored, and any other failure shows *"Couldn't reject hunk"* with git's error); a revert that applied shows *"Hunk reverted in the working tree."* with Undo. The turn's diff itself stays as recorded. Hunks are highlighted without the file on disk (it may have moved on), the `?` help reads *"x revert in the working tree"* (`keyboardHelpLine`), and the empty state reads *"This turn left the files as they were."* only once the diff has been read: while it loads, one muted line says *"Reading this turn's changes…"*, and a failed read says *"This turn's changes couldn't be read."* with the error (`useTurnDiff` returns `{ diff }` or `{ error }`; App passes `turnRead`). The mode band's tail counts the turn diff's files. _Support:_ `commands::talk_turn_diff`, `git_ops::commits_diff`, `ipc.talkTurnDiff`, `hooks/useTurnDiff.ts`, `stores/reviewSourceStore.ts` (`turnByWs`, `openTurn`), `lib/reviewSource.ts`, `ReviewCanvas.tsx` (`turn`), `DiffView` / `FileDiffSection` / `HunkRail` (`revertOnly`), `review/EmptyDiffState.tsx`, `App.tsx`. _Entry:_ Talk › a turn's changes row › Review these changes.
- **Empty diff state** — By case: "N files staged." + commit guidance; *"The working tree is clean."* + *"This workspace's work is committed: N commits since main."* and an upright-serif **Read what was committed** link that switches to Since base (only when Working tree is on screen, picked or pinned, with commits ahead); *"Nothing to review."* + *"No uncommitted changes, and no commits since main…"*; in Since base, *"The N commits since main leave the code as it was."*, or with ±WS on (whitespace-only commits hidden) *"With whitespace ignored, the N commits since main change nothing."* (#903) _Support:_ `review/EmptyDiffState.tsx` (`emptyDiffCopy`).
- **"Why?" drawer (agent origin)** — Traces a file's edit to the agent turn (role, timestamp, model, message) that produced it; explains hand-written changes. _Support:_ `ReviewCanvas.WhyDrawer`; `listFileEdits` + `getMessage`.
- **Ask for a change (review comments, #956)** — Steer the agent from the diff, like a PR review. In the working-tree view, the hunk rail's `MessageSquarePlus` icon ("Ask for a change (m)", `data-tour="review-hunk-comment"`) or `m` on the focused hunk opens an inline field under the hunk for the whole hunk (`m` on a folded file opens the file first); clicking a line number picks that line and shift-clicking another line of the same hunk extends the pick to a range (picked rows carry a brass-dim inset edge). From the keyboard, `m` opens the field on the whole hunk and, in the field, `⌥↓`/`⌥↑` pick a line (the hunk's first row going down, its last going up, then one row on past the range's edge) and `⌥⇧↓`/`⌥⇧↑` extend the range from where it began, the field keeping the focus and the note (`reviewComments.stepPick`); the field's header says so ("⌥↑ ⌥↓ lines · ⇧ extends", `data-tour="review-comment-pick-keys"`), and so does the `?` help. Plain arrows stay the field's. The field (`data-tour="review-comment-composer"`) names the place: `src/a.ts:12–18`, always lines of one side, the new side whenever a picked row has a new-side line, and old-side lines marked `src/a.ts:12 (removed)` only when every picked row is a deletion. **Ask for this change** or `⌘⏎` adds the comment, Escape or Cancel drops it. The field is the shared comment composer (`comments/CommentComposer.tsx`), the same one a Direct gate's document uses. The typed note belongs to the workspace, not to the field or the diff view (`reviewCommentsStore.draftByWs`): a workspace switch under the diff view leaves a half-typed note waiting in its own workspace, and the field is there again with it on the way back, on the line it was picked on. App tags the diff with the workspace it was fetched for (`gitDiffWs` → `DiffView`'s `diffWorkspaceId`, null between a switch and its fetch and outside Review), and the draft is neither re-anchored nor shown nor flushed to the tray until the diff on screen is its workspace's; picking another line or another hunk moves the field there with the note, folding the file keeps it, and a refetch never drops it: the field follows its hunk to a new index, stays open marked "this hunk changed; the comment keeps the lines it quoted" when the hunk itself changed (the comment is then added as outdated), and when the file left the diff a non-empty note is added to the tray as an outdated comment with a "Your comment was kept" toast. Each comment is anchored to its hunk's `hunkFingerprint` (the one the viewed marks use) and keeps the quoted rows (signed `+`/`-`/space), capped at 20 rows of 240 characters each (`MAX_QUOTE_LINES`, `MAX_QUOTE_LINE_CHARS`) with the count of rows left out; it shows under its hunk with a remove `×`. The comments collect in the Review Companion's **For the agent · N** tray under the verdict (`data-tour="review-companion-comments"`, unfolds on the grid-rows Reveal only while there is one): each comment's place (click jumps to it in the diff; to the file for a comment on removed lines), up to three quoted lines, "… N more lines not quoted" when the quote was capped, its note and a remove `×`; a comment whose hunk changed or left the diff (accepted, rejected or edited again) carries a mute **outdated** chip and is still sent with its quote. **Send to the agent** (`data-tour="review-companion-send-comments"`) sends them all as one message, each comment a quoted block under its backticked place, a capped quote ending with "… N more lines not quoted", an outdated one marked "(this hunk has changed since)", without Talk's staged attachments (they stay staged), and empties the tray; a send that was refused before it went out (budget cap, no thread, a turn the backend refused before taking the message, a refused checkpoint) puts the comments back, ahead of any added meanwhile; a refusal in the app's own checks (budget cap, no thread, a refused checkpoint) also leaves the app in Review. When the workspace's latest Direct run has not ended (`runStatus.isTerminalRun`, the rule the run bar uses: an aborted, completed or failed run has no gate, even though an abort leaves its parked stage at `awaiting_checkpoint`) and is parked at a gated review loop that can still send back (the same rule as the run bar's "Send back to …", `reviewComments.sendBackGate`, not at its iteration cap), the message is that gate's **Send-back** feedback (`resolve(…, "send_back", { feedback })`), carrying in the same message the comments written inline on the gate's output (#957), after the Review comments under "On Reviewer's output at the gate:" in `composeGateFeedback`'s form (`sendReviewComments.sendBackMessage`); those stay on the gate until the send-back is applied (then cleared, as a decision bar send-back clears them) and are never taken off it by a refusal; the hint beside the button adds ", with 2 comments on Reviewer" (`data-tour="review-companion-gate-comments"`) while the gate has any. Once the run accepted it, the app switches to Direct; otherwise it is a user turn in the workspace's open Talk thread (Talk makes one if none) and the app switches to Talk as soon as the turn is dispatched (`chatStore.send`'s `onDispatched`: the budget and thread checks passed and the turn has started), not when it ends, which can be minutes later. A Talk turn that fails after that restores nothing when the message is already in the thread (sending again would deliver it twice); it restores the comments only when the thread on screen doesn't hold the message. Either switch happens only if the workspace the comments were sent from is still the one on screen; otherwise the app stays where the director is and a "Comments sent" toast says where they went. An accepted send-back is then confirmed: without detached runs the backend applies it in the background, so the tray watches the run until the gate's stage moved; a `run://error` that arrives while the stage still waits (recorded in `runsStore.runErrors` after the run is read again) puts the comments back with a "Comments not sent" toast. A mono hint beside the button says which ("as send-back to Implementer" / "in Talk"); while Talk is still answering, the button waits. Comments are per workspace and session-local (never persisted); none in the read-only Since base view. _Support:_ `lib/reviewComments.ts` (`commentAnchor`, `commentLocation`, `reanchorDraft`, `liveHunkKeys`, `isOutdated`, `commentsMessage`, `sendBackGate`, also used by `DirectCanvas`), `lib/sendReviewComments.ts` (`commentTarget`, `sendReviewComments`), `stores/reviewCommentsStore.ts` (comments, the drafts per workspace, the live hunk keys `DiffView` publishes), `comments/CommentComposer.tsx`, `review/HunkComments.tsx`, `review/CommentTray.tsx`, `DiffLines` (row pick), `DiffView` (draft). Backend: `Orchestrator::check_run_open` refuses every checkpoint action but Abort on a run that has ended ("This run is aborted — nothing is waiting for a decision."), in `dispatch_checkpoint` and again in `apply_checkpoint_action`, before anything changes; `runsStore.resolve` shows it as the same calm info toast as a stale stage.
- **"Open a pull request" (Review)** — Upright-serif CTA under "Publish/Push" in the ChangesPanel, shown once the branch is published, a PR lookup found none (right after a push the panel looks it up instead of waiting for the 60s poll), the branch isn't the repo default, and a remote is on GitHub; when `gh` is missing or signed out it shows "Run gh auth login…" instead. Opens the PR composer (§6). Also ⌘K → Actions and `⌘⇧P`. _Support:_ `ChangesPanel.tsx`, `stores/prStore.ts`, `github_ship_readiness`. _Entry:_ Review → ChangesPanel (`data-tour="review-open-pr"`).
- **Read-only DiffViewer (Direct reuse)** — Plain files→hunks renderer, no actions; shares `diffLineStyle` with the review surface. _Support:_ `DiffViewer.tsx`, `lib/diffLineStyle.ts`.

### File explorer (Files tab in review)
- **Changes ⇄ Files navigator** — Tab switcher (+ changed-count badge); collapses to a 44px icon strip (persisted); the strip's active icon is a brass wash with no outline. On a narrow sidebar the tab labels truncate (icons + `title` tooltips stay) and the panel eyebrows (`ChangesPanel`, `CompanionFileTree`) are `min-w-0 overflow-hidden`, so the switcher never draws over the canvas's Diff/Editor toggle. _Support:_ `ReviewSidebar.tsx`.
- **Collapsed by default on a narrow Review area** — When the Review area (sidebar + canvas, measured on the parent row with a `ResizeObserver`) is narrower than 760px (`AUTO_COLLAPSE_BELOW`), the navigator shows its 44px icon strip whatever the stored preference, so the diff keeps its width. Expanding it there (strip, `c` focus-commit, `⌘⇧E` reveal) lasts until the area crosses the threshold again and never overwrites the stored `reviewSidebarCollapsed`; widening past 760px restores the stored preference. An unmeasured (hidden) area keeps the last answer. _Support:_ `ReviewSidebar.tsx`. _Entry:_ automatic (`data-tour="review-sidebar"`).
- **Resizable navigator** — A 4px `separator` on the sidebar's right edge (mirror of the Companion's): drag to resize between 200–640px (default 280), double-click to reset, or focus it and use ←/→ (Shift = larger step), Home/End for min/max. The canvas always keeps at least 360px (CSS `max-width`), whatever the stored width. Width persists in `localStorage` (`reviewSidebarWidth`); an unmount mid-drag releases the body cursor and window listeners; the width transition is suspended during a live drag so the edge tracks the cursor. _Support:_ `ReviewSidebar.tsx`.
- **Lazy windowed file tree** — Flat-row model, per-folder lazy load (`readDirectory`), virtualized 24px rows; expansion/focus cached per workspace. _Support:_ `CompanionFileTree.tsx`, `lib/useVirtualRows`.
- **No truncated names — horizontal scroll** — Labels never ellipsize; deep nesting makes the tree scroll horizontally. Because only windowed rows are mounted, the content width is pinned to an estimate of the widest row across the whole flat list (`contentMinWidth`), so the horizontal scrollbar stays stable while rows mount/unmount. _Support:_ `CompanionFileTree.tsx`.
- **File-type icons + tints** — Category-based lucide icon + Atelier tint; changed files override to brass. _Support:_ `lib/fileIcons.ts`.
- **Show-ignored toggle** — Reveals `.gitignore`d files (persisted per root). _Support:_ `reviewPrefsStore.showIgnoredFiles`.
- **Tree filter** — Case-insensitive substring over loaded folders, keeps ancestors, highlights matches, count; Esc clears. _Support:_ `CompanionFileTree.tsx`.
- **Keyboard tree nav (roving tabindex)** — ↑/↓ move, →/← expand/collapse, Home/End, Enter/Space activate, ContextMenu/Shift+F10 menu. _Support:_ `CompanionFileTree.tsx`.
- **Open file marked in the tree** — The file open in the editor carries the rail's own "you are here" optic: a 2px brass left edge + resting `--brass-ghost` tint (hover steps up to `--brass-glow` rather than replacing it), `aria-current="true"`, tooltip "Open in the editor". Shown whenever its row is visible; the tree is never moved to produce it. _Support:_ `CompanionFileTree.tsx` (`activePath`), fed from `editorStore.getActivePath`. _Entry:_ automatic in Review.
- **Reveal in tree (on demand, never automatic)** — The tree deliberately does **not** follow the editor — clicking through a diff would keep shifting it under the reader. Instead it registers a `locate(absPath)` (the `registerFocusCommit` shape) that expands the file's ancestors, **fetches** each one (expansion alone does not load a folder), clears any active filter, scrolls the virtual window to the row and focuses it. A path outside the worktree is ignored. Called from the editor breadcrumb's `⌖ Reveal` or `⌘⇧E`. _Support:_ `CompanionFileTree.tsx` (`registerLocate`), `ReviewSidebar.tsx` pass-through, `App.tsx` (`locateInTreeFn`). _Entry:_ breadcrumb button · `⌘⇧E`.
- **Editor breadcrumb** — Above the editor pane: the open file's path relative to the worktree root as `dir › dir › file.tsx` (mono, mute, filename in ivory, truncating), plus the `⌖ Reveal` control. Renders nothing when no file is open; the reveal control is omitted when no tree is listening. _Support:_ `src/components/EditorBreadcrumb.tsx`. _Entry:_ Review → Editor.
- **Context menu + file ops** — Reveal in Finder, Open in system, Open in terminal, Copy path + New file / New folder / Rename / Delete (with confirm). _Support:_ `FileTreeContextMenu`, `FileNameDialog`; `fsCreateFile/fsCreateDir/fsRename/fsDelete`.

### Code editor (CodeMirror 6)
- **Open files as tabs** — Opens via guarded read; existing tabs reactivate; binary/oversize handled. _Support:_ `editorStore.openFile`, `EditorTabs.tsx`, `EditorPane.tsx`. _Entry:_ Files tree, diff `o`, AI finding "Edit", Changes "open in editor".
- **Editor tabs** — Filename, dirty dot, close button, active underline; keyboard nav (←/→/Home/End) + HTML5 drag-reorder; close → next-active fallback. _Support:_ `EditorTabs.tsx`, `editorStore`.
- **Per-tab state preservation** — Each tab's full `EditorState` (undo/cursor/scroll) cached and restored on switch. _Support:_ `EditorPane` `stateCache`.
- **Edit & save (⌘S)** — Manual save with external-change guard. _Support:_ `editorStore.saveActive`, `write_file`.
- **Cheap keystrokes** — Typing doesn't copy the document into the store per key. The first keystroke sets the file's `pendingEdit` flag (`markEdited`, one store write, which lights the tab's dirty dot); the text is copied 250 ms after typing pauses (`CONTENT_SYNC_MS`), or at once on save, tab switch and unmount. Dirtiness is `isFileDirty` — `pendingEdit` or content ≠ saved — everywhere it's judged, so the silent focus reload never swaps a buffer with unsynced keys. Before this, every key ran `doc.toString()` and re-rendered the pane, the tab bar and the Review canvas. _Support:_ `editorStore` (`markEdited`, `isFileDirty`), `EditorPane` (`scheduleSync`/`flushContent`).
- **Syntax per language** — Two tiers, shared by the Review editor, Quick View and the Review diff.
  - **Full grammar** (Lezer: a syntax tree, so code folding, tree-backed go-to-definition where `definitionTree.ts` knows the grammar, and tree-aware diff highlighting): JavaScript (`.js` `.mjs` `.cjs`), JSX (`.jsx`), TypeScript (`.ts` `.mts` `.cts`, **without JSX**, so `<T>(x) => x` and `<Foo>expr` read as generics and casts), TSX (`.tsx`), Rust, Python, Java, JSON (`.json` `.jsonc`; comments in `.jsonc` show as errors), Markdown (`.md` `.markdown` `.mdx`), HTML (`.html` `.htm`, plus `.vue` and `.svelte` read as HTML), CSS (`.css`), SCSS (`.scss`) and Sass (`.sass`, the indented syntax), XML (`.xml` `.svg`), YAML, Go, C (`.c`), C++ (`.cpp` `.cc` `.cxx` `.hpp` `.hh` `.hxx`; C and C++ share the C++ grammar), SQL (standard dialect), PHP (`.php`; HTML outside `<?php … ?>`). **`.h` is C++ when the workspace has C++ sources** (`.cpp` `.cc` `.cxx` `.hpp` `.hh`), C otherwise: the editor lists the workspace once per session (`list_workspace_files`) the first time it opens a `.h` file, and remembers the answer per workspace root.
  - **Basic** (stream modes from `@codemirror/legacy-modes`: highlighting only, no tree): Shell (sh/bash/zsh), TOML, Dockerfile (also matched by the `Dockerfile` / `Dockerfile.*` file name), properties (ini/cfg/conf/env/properties), Ruby, Swift, C#, Kotlin (`.kt` `.kts`), Scala, Groovy (`.groovy` `.gradle`), Dart, Protocol Buffers (`.proto`), Lua.
  - **Plain text** (no grammar installed yet): HCL/Terraform (`.tf` `.hcl`), GraphQL, Makefile, and any other extension.
  - **Loaded on first use** — every grammar is its own lazy chunk (a dynamic `import()` per `LangId`, memoised; C reuses the C++ chunk), so none of them is in the initial bundle. The Review editor, Quick View and the Scratchpad open a file with whatever grammar has already loaded and install the rest through a language `Compartment` once it lands (a tab left before then picks it up when it comes back). The Review diff highlights only from loaded grammars: `FileDiffSection` starts the load at mount, beside its disk read, and highlights again when it resolves, so a cold grammar shows plain rows only until its chunk arrives and a warm one colours the first render. A failed chunk reads as plain text and is fetched again on the next request. `editorLanguages.bundle.test.ts` builds the whole app with the project's `vite.config.ts` (in memory) and fails if any grammar is in what a window loads at startup — the entry, `App` and `QuickViewApp` chunks and everything they import statically — or if a grammar isn't a lazy chunk of its own.
  _Support:_ `lib/editorLang.ts` (extension → `LangId`, `JS_DIALECTS`, `hasCppSources`), `lib/editorLanguages.ts` (`loadLanguageSupport`, `loadLanguage`, `loadedLanguageSupport`, `loadedLanguage`), `lib/diffSyntax.ts` (`diffGrammarReady`, `loadDiffGrammar`), `editorStore.openFile` / `openAsJump({ root })` (the `.h` decision).
- **Atelier syntax theme** — Each kind of code has its own palette ink: keywords (and modifiers, `this`) = brass, types/classes/tags = state-blue, function and method names (call and definition, builtins like `echo`) = state-purple, strings = verdigris (not sage, which reads too close to the comments' mute), numbers and constants (booleans, `null`/`nil`, atoms, special variables like shell `$FOO`) = sage, annotations/decorators/macros (`@Override`, `@` included, a whole Rust attribute like `#[derive(Debug)]`, `println!`) = amber, properties and plain text = ivory, comments and punctuation = mute (upright, never italic); Markdown headings brass and bold. One table (`lib/syntaxPalette.ts`) drives both the editor and the Review diff's `.tok-*` classes, so both colour alike. Stream-mode token names are mapped onto those kinds before CodeMirror resolves them (`def`, a declared name, stays plain unless it names a function: after `fun`/`func`/`def`/`function` or before a `(`, so Kotlin `val x` and `class K` or Swift `let s` read plain; `builtin` → builtin call, `variable-3` → type, `qualifier` → modifier, an identifier followed by `(` → call; shell's `def` is a variable), and Java annotations and Rust attributes get their own rules. Rebuilt live from CSS tokens on `octo:theme`. CodeMirror's `dark` flag is derived from the active theme's background luminance, so the vellum light theme no longer gets the library's dark-mode defaults. **State-blue and state-purple switch with the ground** (themeStore, from `tokens.ts`: the Onyx values on a dark theme, `#2f5a7e` / `#6a4682` on Vellum, AA on every Vellum surface), and verdigris/amber are already per-theme, so every syntax ink clears 4.5:1 in both themes. `syntaxPalette.coverage.test.ts` parses a fixture per supported language and fails if any emitted tag has no rule. Known gap: Java declaration names and Go `pkg.Func` calls still read as plain/property, because a contextual grammar rule can't override the package's own context-free one. _Support:_ `lib/syntaxPalette.ts`, `editor/atelierTheme.ts`, `lib/diffSyntax.ts`, `lib/editorLanguages.ts`, `lib/tokens.ts` (`vellumInks`, `stateInks`), `stores/themeStore.ts`, `lib/contrast.isDarkBackground`.
- **Find / replace overlay (⌘F)** — Floating card: match case, whole word, regex, "n of m" tally, next/prev, replace, replace all; seeds from selection. ⌘G/F3 next/prev still work. _Support:_ `editor/EditorSearch.tsx`.
- **Match highlighting** — Octopush emits the match marks itself, because `@codemirror/search`'s own highlighter only runs while its docked panel is open and the ⌘F overlay replaces that panel. A low-precedence ViewPlugin decorates the visible ranges (widened past each boundary so a straddling match isn't lost, capped at 2000 marks) using CodeMirror's own `cm-searchMatch` / `cm-searchMatch-selected` classes, tagging the selected range as current. Match positions are cached, so moving the cursor re-tags the current match without re-running the search. It stands down while the native panel is open — `⌘G`/`F3` can still open it — so the two highlighters never double-paint. _Support:_ `editor/searchHighlight.ts`, wired in `EditorPane`.
- **Theme-solved match colours** — Every match wears an accent wash + 1px ring and a 2px radius; the current match is an inverted seal (solid accent, background-coloured ink) so the two differ by weight, not by a few points of alpha. The wash alpha is **solved per theme** — the smallest value clearing a 1.50 contrast step against that theme's background (23.5% on atelier, 29.5% on vellum) — because one fixed alpha reads very differently on onyx vs cream. Matched text also owns its foreground (`--octo-match-ink`), applied to the mark *and its descendants* since a syntax span nests inside it: a wash costs whatever sits on it ~34% of its contrast, which body text absorbs but comments don't. _Support:_ `lib/contrast.ts` (`solveMatchWashAlpha`, `isDarkBackground`), `themeStore` (`--octo-match*` tokens), `editor/atelierTheme.ts`.
- **Symbol occurrence highlighting** — Resting the caret on an identifier (or selecting exactly one) washes every other whole-word use of it in the file, and marks the one that reads as its **definition** with a brass underline. Whole-word only, so `id` never lights up `width`; skips matches inside comments and strings (read off the syntax tree); ignores language keywords (`isNavigableSymbol`) and multi-caret selections. **Stands down while a ⌘F query is live** so the two highlight layers never double-paint — and because a `setSearchQuery` transaction changes neither doc, selection nor viewport, the plugin watches the query as a **fourth wake signal** of its own; without it the wash both painted under a live query and stayed dark after one was cleared. Scans only the visible ranges (capped at 1000 marks). The whole-document definition scan runs on a symbol change or an edit, under a hard **256 KB** ceiling (~6 ms): typing an identifier changes the symbol on every keystroke, so the edit path and the symbol path are one path, and an earlier 2 MB ceiling meant ~50 ms per keystroke — about 20 fps. Past the ceiling the definition simply goes unmarked; occurrences still highlight and ⌘-click still finds it, scanning once on demand. Shared with the scratchpad editor. _Support:_ `editor/symbolIndex.ts`, `editor/symbolHighlight.ts`; tokens `--octo-symbol*`.
- **Go to definition (⌘/Ctrl-click · `F12`)** — ⌘-click (Ctrl elsewhere) an identifier — or press `F12` on it — to jump to where it is declared. Holding the modifier underlines the identifier under the pointer in brass and turns the cursor into a pointer, so the gesture is visible before it's used; the click is swallowed before CodeMirror's own "add a caret" default sees it (`⌘D`/`⌘⇧L` remain the multi-cursor routes). The pointer hit is checked against the identifier's own glyph box on **both axes** (`resolvePointerTarget`): `posAtCoords` answers with the *nearest* position, so without the check a ⌘-click in the blank margin right of a line — or anywhere in the empty space below the last line, since `.cm-content` is at least as tall as its scroller — silently navigated to whatever identifier was nearest. **Resolution is nearest-scope-first:** the open document (synchronous, skipping the occurrence that was clicked), then the whole workspace via `search_workspace_text`, with a "Looking for …" chip in the editor's corner while that runs.
