Clicking a symbol while **already standing on its own declaration** (the `declaration`/`signature` tiers) reports that rather than escalating — the workspace search would drop the reader into an unrelated same-named declaration, or claim nothing declares a symbol they are looking straight at. **Keywords and type keywords never start a search:** when the open file has no candidate, ⌘-click or `F12` on `if`, `const`, `static`, `int` or `void` answers "No definition found in this workspace — X is part of the language" instead of escalating. The screen runs only after the in-file tier, so a word one language reserves still jumps where the open file declares it (C's `struct foo *self`, Go's `val := m[k]`). In JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, Rust, Python, Go, C and C++ the **Lezer syntax tree** decides (`editor/definitionTree.ts` `classifyClick`: every grammar names keyword tokens after their text, plus Java's and C/C++'s `PrimitiveType`, the boolean literals (`BooleanLiteral` in JavaScript/TypeScript and Java, `Boolean` in Python and Rust, `Bool` in Go, `True`/`False` in C/C++), Go's `Nil`, C/C++'s `TypeSize` (`unsigned`, `long`), `Access` (`public`) and `VirtualSpecifier` (`override`, `final`), Rust's primitive `TypeIdentifier`s, Go's predeclared types plus `iota` and `nil` (`TypeName`/`VariableName` nodes), and TypeScript's primitive `TypeName`s (`boolean`, `string`, `number`, `any`, `unknown`, `never`, `void`, `object`, `bigint`, `symbol`, `undefined`, `null`); the grammars' identifier nodes are excluded, so a class called `Definition` or a type called `TypeIdentifier` is still a name), so a Python variable called `final` still resolves. Elsewhere, or when the tree has no answer, `isReservedWord(lang, name)` (`symbolIndex.ts`) checks **the active file's language only**: one list per language (JS/TS, Java, Rust, Python, Go, C, C++, C#, Kotlin, Swift, Ruby, Lua) of its keywords, primitive types and literals, so `val` is refused in Kotlin but searched in Go, and `self` in Rust but not in C or Python. Words a language lets code use as member names stay out (`new`, `delete`, `default` in JavaScript), as do ordinary names such as `type`, `get`, `use` and `record`; other languages fall back to the statement heads (`if`, `for`, `while`, …). A built-in class such as `String` or `Integer` is searched (a workspace may declare its own), and since every line mentioning it only uses it as a type, the answer is the same "No definition found in this workspace" toast. Note `isNavigableSymbol` gates the **ambient wash only**, never navigation. **The tree also vets in-file candidates** (`classifySite`): a line-heuristic hit the tree knows is not a declaration (a JavaScript `run = 5` re-assignment, a Java return type, a Go `total = count` without `:=`) is dropped. Go's declarations are its `DefName` nodes (func, type, var, const, `:=`, parameters) and the `FieldName` of a method, struct field or interface method. C and C++ get the keyword answer only: their declarators nest too many ways for the tree to veto a candidate safely, so the line heuristic alone decides there. C is parsed with the C++ grammar, so C++-only keywords (`class`, `new`, `delete`, `this`, `template`, `namespace`, `private`, `nullptr`, `operator`, … — `CPP_ONLY_KEYWORDS`) are ordinary names in a C file: ⌘-click on `dev->class` or a `struct node *new` still searches the workspace. `bool`, `true` and `false` stay keywords in both. **A lone weak candidate does not jump:** when the open file's only other candidate is a bare `foo = …` binding that no tree confirmed, the lookup falls through to the workspace tier instead of jumping without asking. Go's `x := …` is not weak — it declares by definition, so a lone `resp := http.Get(u)` still jumps, and ⌘-clicking it reports "Already at the definition". Every request bumps a generation and retires the previous "Looking for …" chip, escalating or not, so a scan still in flight can neither land afterwards and drag the reader out of a file they already jumped to, nor leave its chip stranded on screen. The escalation asks the backend for a **whole-word** match (`search_workspace_text`'s `whole_word` flag, boundaries `[A-Za-z0-9_$]` — the same rule the editor's own word scan uses): as a plain substring scan, looking up `run` spent the entire 500-hit cap on `running`, `runtime` and `rerun` and then reported that nothing declared it. ⌘⇧F itself deliberately stays substring — a human typing a fragment expects fragments back. A still-**saturated** search reports "Too many matches to narrow" pointing at ⌘⇧F — never "nothing declares it", which is a claim the search never actually made. The cap is mirrored in `lib/definitionSearch.ts` behind a drift test against `commands.rs`. There is no language server — the definition test is a **conservative line-shape heuristic** scored in three tiers (`declaration` 100: a declaring keyword in front — `function`/`fun`/`fn`/`def`/`class`/`type`/`struct`/`let`/`var`/…, or a binding modifier (`const`/`static`/`readonly`/`final`) followed by **neither another name nor the end of the line** — or the declarator of a **typed declaration**: annotations/attributes (`@Bean`, `[HttpGet]`), modifiers, at most one type, then the name, closed by `=`, `;`, `{` (C# properties), `=>`, `[`, a `: Type` annotation or a parameter list — covering Java fields and methods, C# properties, C/C++ prototypes, pointers and `typedef`s (`typedef struct node_s node_t;` declares `node_t`), local typed variables and Kotlin `fun f() = …`. Pointer and reference declarators (`*`, `&`) are read only in C/C++ (`scoreOptionsFor`, by language or extension); elsewhere `total * rate;` multiplies and declares nothing. **A declaration split after its type** (`public static Integer` ⏎ `esperaSugerida(…) {`, `static int` ⏎ `helper(void)`): a line holding only modifiers and a type never declares that type; in the open file (`findDefinitions`) such a line is read together with the next one, so the name on the next line resolves, while a workspace search preview of the head alone scores nothing. **The type in front of a declaration is never its name:** `public static Integer esperaSugerida()` declares `esperaSugerida`, `const char *name` declares `name`, and `impl Display for Foo`, `package com.acme` and a re-export such as `export default App;` declare nothing (so a default-exported component found by the workspace search jumps to its `function App()` rather than tying with the re-export in a picker). Go writes `name Type`, so `.go` files (by language in the editor, by extension in the workspace ranking — `scoreOptionsFor`) read `const limit Duration` name-first; `signature` 70: a parameter list that **closes on the same line**, followed by nothing but a return type before the body opens, with only modifiers in front (Go receivers included); `assignment` 40: `foo =` / `foo :=`). The balanced-parenthesis requirement is what separates a declaration from a call that merely ends in a brace — `defineConfig({`, `describe("suite", {` and `register(name, {` never close theirs, and a looser rule read all three as declarations. It refuses calls, control statements, member access, imports and callbacks rather than guessing. _Support:_ `editor/symbolNav.ts`, `editor/symbolIndex.ts`, `editor/definitionTree.ts`, `lib/definitionSearch.ts`.
- **Cross-file definition ranking & picker** — Workspace hits are filtered to lines that read as definitions, then ranked: +12 same file extension, +6 same directory, −30 test file, −40 vendored/build output, −10 `.d.ts`; the line the reader asked from is dropped. One candidate — or a winner a full confidence tier (30 points) clear of the runner-up — is opened directly; anything closer opens the **definition picker** (file · line · source line, arrow keys + Enter) rather than guessing. Nothing plausible at all → an info toast naming the symbol. _Support:_ `lib/definitionSearch.ts` (`rankDefinitionHits`, `chooseDefinition`), `editor/DefinitionPicker.tsx`.
- **Back / forward (`⌃−` / `⌃⇧−`; `Ctrl+Alt+−` / `Ctrl+Shift+−` on Windows and Linux)** — Every jump leaves a trail: go to definition (in-file or cross-file), a definition-picker choice, `⌘⌥G` go to line, and every open through `navigateToFile` (`⌘P`, ⌘⇧F results, the file tree). `⌃−` returns to where the last jump started — reopening the file if its tab was closed since — and puts back the exact selection and scroll; `⌃⇧−` goes forward again, and a fresh jump clears the forward trail. **A go-to-definition stop is the occurrence asked about**, with the caret on it: a ⌘-click swallows the mousedown and never moves the caret, so recording the selection would send Back to the right scroll but leave the caret on a line far off screen. The origin is taken when the request starts, before the workspace search is awaited, and a definition-picker choice keeps the origin of the request that opened the picker. Opens go through `openAsJump`, which takes the origin before the open and records it only once the file is actually open: declining the large-file confirm leaves no stop, and reopening the file already in front with no line to go to (`⌘P` to the current file) adds none. A stop whose file was moved or deleted since is spent: the step fails with an info toast naming the file ("Couldn't reopen file"); a stop whose file has since grown past the large-file limit is spent the same way, with the same title and a body saying it is too large to open here. Xcode's chords on macOS. Elsewhere `Mod` is `Ctrl`, so `Ctrl+−` stays the font-size chord and Back is `Ctrl+Alt+−` (VS Code's Linux chord; `Alt+←` would take CodeMirror's syntax-cursor binding). No global shortcut, CodeMirror binding or other editor binding uses them on either platform (`navKeys.test.ts` resolves every chord both ways). **Per workspace**, capped at 50 stops, and the same place twice in a row is one stop. Go to line is CodeMirror's own dialog, which jumps on submit rather than on the key, so `EditorPane` notes where `⌘⌥G` was pressed and records it on the first selection change after the dialog closes (a click in the text while it is open doesn't count). The dialog closes itself one microtask before its jump lands, so a close alone drops the origin only after that task: Escape or bad input records nothing. The pane checks the dialog with `getDialog` (a state-field read) only while a `⌘⌥G` is pending, never a DOM query per transaction. The editor column scrolls, not `.cm-scroller` — the editor grows to its content — so the scroll offset is the host's `scrollTop`, restored after CodeMirror's next measure; if the file shrank below the old selection since, the selection is clamped and centred instead. _Support:_ `editorStore` (`navByWs`, `recordLocation`, `openAsJump`, `navigateBack`/`navigateForward`, `setLocationProvider`, `PendingReveal.restore`), `EditorPane`, `editor/navKeys.ts`.
- **Multi-cursor / select-all-occurrences (⌘⇧L)** — One cursor per occurrence; plus rectangular selection (Alt-drag), `⌘D` next-occurrence. _Support:_ `editor/multiCursor.ts`.
- **Diff gutter** — Brass bar on added lines; rouge `▾` with deletion-run count on removed-after lines. _Support:_ `editor/diffGutter.ts`.
- **Next / previous change (`⌥F7` / `⇧⌥F7`)** — Steps the caret through the diff gutter's changes, so a reviewer can walk an agent's edits in one file: a run of consecutive marked lines is one stop, the caret lands at its first line, centred, and the steps wrap at either end. With no changes in the file the key falls through. On Apple keyboards the chords need `fn` (`fn⌥F7`) unless **Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys** is on in macOS's Keyboard settings. The commands read the same markers the gutter draws (a facet), so they never disagree with it. _Support:_ `editor/diffGutter.ts` (`changeStarts`, `nextChangeLine`, `gotoNextChange`/`gotoPrevChange`).
- **Code folding (`⌘⌥[` / `⌘⌥]`)** — Fold or unfold the block at the caret from the keyboard, as well as from the fold gutter (shown with line numbers); `⌃⌥[` / `⌃⌥]` fold or unfold everything. CodeMirror's `foldKeymap`, which also works with line numbers hidden. _Support:_ `EditorPane`.
- **Blame gutter** — Per-line `shaShort author` (collapsing same-commit runs); native tooltip; global "Toggle blame" command; re-fetches on switch/save. _Support:_ `editor/blameGutter.ts`, `blameStore.ts`, `blame_file`.
- **Editor status bar** — Language dot, Ln/Col, "N selections", "Ask Talk about this" (below), "blame: saved version" note, "disk changed" chip; right: Spaces (cycle), Wrap, Ln#, font −/Aa/+. _Support:_ `EditorStatusBar.tsx`, `editorPrefsStore`.
- **Ask Talk about this (#962)** — While the main selection is non-empty, the status bar shows a brass `MessageSquareText` "Ask Talk about this" (`review-editor-ask-talk`, tooltip "Ask Talk about lines 5–10"). It queues `@path#L5-10 ` (`#L5` for one line; a whole-line drag ending at the next line's start ends on the line above, `editor/selectionLines.ts`) for the workspace's Talk draft and switches to Talk; the composer appends it on its own word, caret after it. The editor's selection is left as it was, so it is still highlighted back in Review. Only shown for files inside the worktree. While the file has unsaved edits the button is disabled and muted, tooltip "Save the file first: Talk reads the lines from disk, not your unsaved edits", because the range is read from disk (`askTalkUnsaved`, from `isFileDirty`). The only editor hand-off — no other editing features. _Support:_ `EditorPane.tsx` (`askTalk`), `chatStore` `draftInsertByWs` (`queueDraftInsert` / `takeDraftInsert`), `navigate({kind:"mode"})`.
- **Open-at-line reveal** — One-shot cursor placement + center-scroll once the file is active. **Held, not spent, while the editor column is hidden:** Markdown reading mode collapses `EditorPane` to zero width, and `ModeOverlay` hides the whole Review canvas at *unchanged* width — scrolling either does nothing, so the reveal waits and is re-applied the moment the column is back. Released by polling (120 ms) rather than a `ResizeObserver`, because the `ModeOverlay` case never resizes; **dropped after 10 s** so a stale jump can't ambush the reader later, the same rule the Markdown jump follows. Visibility is read with `checkVisibility`, not a zero-width test, because "no width" is also what an environment with no layout engine reports. _Support:_ `editorStore.pendingReveal`, `EditorPane` (`isHostVisible`, `hostVisibleTick`).
- **Binary file pane** — lucide `FileWarning` icon + "Binary" (retired the `§ Binary` glyph), name, size, reason, Reveal in Finder / Open in system. _Support:_ `EditorBinaryPane.tsx`.

### Markdown documents (`.md` / `.markdown` / `.mdx`)
- **Three view modes — Source · Split · Reading** — A markdown tab picks one of three layouts from an icon-only segmented control in the REVIEW toolbar (`Code` / `Columns2` / `BookOpen`, brass when active), shown **only** in Editor view and only for a markdown tab. `⌥⌘M` cycles source → split → reading while the control is on screen — REVIEW is the visible mode **and** the tab qualifies (bound in `ReviewCanvas`, not `App`, because that is the only surface it applies to; `ModeOverlay` keeps its children mounted, so the canvas takes an `active` prop rather than assuming it is on screen). It keys off the physical `KeyM` (macOS turns ⌥M into "µ") and stands down on `defaultPrevented`/`repeat`, the house rule for a CodeMirror-adjacent binding. **The editor never unmounts:** a hidden column collapses to zero width, so CodeMirror keeps its undo history, folds, scroll position and per-tab state across every switch. The choice is one persisted pref shared by the whole app (`octo-review-prefs`), and a pre-existing `mdPreview: boolean` migrates on rehydrate (`false` → source, `true` → split) through a **`version: 1` migration** — zustand only writes the store back after a real version bump, so doing it there (rather than in `merge`) is what actually drops the dead key from storage. A non-markdown tab always renders editor-only regardless of the pref. _Support:_ `reviewPrefsStore` (`mdView`, `setMdView`, `cycleMdView`, `isMdView`, legacy merge), `ReviewCanvas.tsx` `MD_VIEWS`, `editor/EditorWithPreview.tsx`. _Entry:_ REVIEW toolbar · `⌥⌘M`.
- **Draggable split ratio** — In split, a divider drags the source column between 25% and 75%; the live width is local state while dragging and the ratio is committed to the persisted store once on release (no per-pixel localStorage writes). Double-click resets to 50/50. An in-flight drag is aborted if the divider goes away (mode left split, tab flipped to non-markdown) or the component unmounts. _Support:_ `EditorWithPreview`, `reviewPrefsStore.mdPreviewSplit` + `clampSplit` (re-clamped on rehydrate).
- **Rendered document** — GFM (`remark-gfm`) rendered with the Onyx & Brass document type scale (serif headings, brass list markers and inline code, hairline tables). **No `rehype-raw`:** embedded HTML stays inert text. Renders the live editor buffer, so it tracks unsaved edits (refreshing once typing pauses — see *Cheap keystrokes*). _Support:_ `editor/MarkdownPreview.tsx`, `lib/markdownComponents.tsx`.
- **Jump to source** — Every rendered block carries `data-md-line`, the 1-based source line the parser recorded for it (innermost wins: a list item beats its list, a table row beats its table). Hovering a block reveals a brass line-number marker in the left margin — the discoverable path — and clicking it places the caret on that line; `⌘`/`Ctrl`-click anywhere in a block does the same (the editor idiom, and it collides with neither drag-selection nor links, which an unmodified click leaves entirely alone). The marker is measured against the document wrapper with rects, not `offsetTop` (a `<tr>`'s offsetParent is its `<table>`), holds its position while the pointer crosses the gutter to reach it, and hides when the buffer changes underneath it. The jump reuses the same one-shot reveal the file tree and ⌘⇧F search use. From **reading**, the jump opens split first and **defers** the reveal until the width transition lands — revealing mid-animation would scroll CodeMirror against a zero-width viewport. The deferred reveal re-checks at fire time and is dropped if the user switched tabs or flipped back to reading inside the window, so a stale jump can never ambush them later. _Support:_ `markdownComponents.lineAttr`, `MarkdownPreview` (`blockFor`, margin marker), `editorStore.revealLine`, `EditorWithPreview.jumpToLine`.
- **Selectable rendered prose** — The app sets `user-select: none` on `<body>`; the preview opts back in via `.octo-selectable`, so a paragraph can be selected and copied as prose (without its markdown). _Support:_ `styles.css` `.octo-selectable` (the general selectable-island class, renamed from `.chat-selectable`), `MarkdownPreview`.

### Editor reliability & file I/O
- **Guarded read** — Sniffs for NUL (binary), 50 MB cap, UTF-8 validation; returns Text / Binary / UnsupportedEncoding / TooLarge. Runs off the async workers (`spawn_blocking`). _Support:_ `read_file_checked`.
- **Only regular files are read** (#1190) — A path that is (or links to) a named pipe, socket, device or folder is refused at once with a plain error, e.g. ".env is a named pipe, not a file (a secrets manager may serve it). Octopush doesn't read it.", which the editor shows in its "Could not open file" toast instead of hanging. The path is stat'ed (following symlinks), opened with `O_NONBLOCK` and checked again by the open handle, so a pipe swapped in between can't block either; reads are size-capped. `read_file`, `read_file_checked`, `read_file_lines` (Talk's `@file` and `@file#L…`) and the secret guard's worktree reads go through it; the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md chain reader already opened files the same way (`request_context::read_memory_file`), and `@folder` only stats. _Support:_ `fs_safe.rs` (`open_regular`, `read_regular`, `read_regular_text`, `refusal`).
- **Large-file confirm** — Files >2 MB prompt before opening; "TooLarge" re-reads with no cap on confirm. _Support:_ `editorStore`, `App.confirmLargeFile`.
- **External-change detection** — On focus / tab re-visible, stat (`file_meta`) vs tracked mtime; clean buffers silently reload, dirty buffers flag the "disk changed" chip. _Support:_ `editorStore.checkActiveAgainstDisk`.
- **Save conflict dialog** — When disk changed/deleted under a dirty buffer, ⌘S opens a 3-way ConfirmDialog (Overwrite / Reload / Keep editing). _Support:_ `editorStore.saveConflict`.
- **Save-failure toast** — Write errors surface. _Support:_ `editorStore.saveActive`.

### Editor preferences (persisted)
- **Soft wrap / Font size / Tab width / Line numbers** — Toggles + steppers; live-reconfigure via CodeMirror compartments; persisted as `octo-editor-prefs` in localStorage. _Support:_ `editorPrefsStore.ts`.

### AI review pass
- **Request review** — Manual, one-shot model call over the working-tree `gitDiff` (not an agent). _Support:_ `aiReviewStore.run` → `ipc.aiComplete(model, AI_REVIEW_SYSTEM, buildReviewPrompt(diff), {jsonSchema})`. _Entry:_ toolbar Sparkles "AI" → drawer "Review this change" (arrow-suffix CTA retired).
- **AI drawer** — Slides over the diff (slim header, model picker, run/re-review CTA, finding count); collapse persisted per workspace. _Support:_ `review/AiReviewPanel.tsx`.
- **Per-workspace model picker** — Default: the review tier from the builtin tag lookup (`claude-sonnet-5-5`), not pinned, so it follows the lineup; a pick is persisted; a persisted pick no longer in the live catalog is dropped (the workspace goes back to the default, with a one-time toast). _Support:_ `aiReviewStore.modelFor/setModel`, `lib/helperModels.ts`.
- **Structured findings** — `summary` + findings `{severity, category, title, detail, file, line}`; schema-forced tool call; tolerant `parseAiReview` fallback. _Support:_ `lib/aiReview.ts`.
- **Severities** — high (rouge), medium (amber), low (mute); ordered high-first. **Categories** — bug · missing-test · security · style · perf · other. _Support:_ `AiFindingCard`.
- **Finding → diff / editor** — `file:line` (no arrow suffix — retired) scrolls + flashes the diff; PenLine "Edit" opens the file in the editor at the line. _Support:_ `AiFindingCard`.
- **Stale detection** — Result cached by FNV-1a diff hash; "diff changed — re-run" when the changeset moves. _Support:_ `aiReviewStore`.
- **Partial reads, said out loud** (#943) — Before the call, `fitReviewDiff(diff, maxContext)` drops the backend's 1 MiB truncation marker and, when the prompt's estimated tokens (UTF-8 bytes ÷ 3) exceed the model's catalog `maxContext` minus 8192 for the answer and room for the prompt's wording, keeps whole files from the start while they fit (a first file too big on its own is cut at a line and recorded as `cutFile`). When the window can't hold even one changed line (a small user-added model), the review fails before the call with "This model's context window is too small to review this change." A model not in the catalog skips the window fit. A cut diff gets a prompt note worded after what happened (cut inside a named file, at a file boundary, by the 1 MiB cap, or both): the diff is partial, don't report missing code or the cut, and up to 30 of the left-out paths. The result keeps `partial {readFiles, totalFiles, omitted, cutFile}` (also while stale), and the drawer shows a mute line under the summary: "Read the first 2 of 14 files; the rest wasn't reviewed." (hover lists the files left out), "Read the first part of package-lock.json; …" (or "…, the first of 3 files; …") when a file was read only in part (hover names it), "Read the first 3 files; …" when the 1 MiB cap hid the total, or "Read the first 1 MB of the diff; …"; a clean partial result reads "No issues in what was read.". _Support:_ `lib/aiReview.ts` (`fitReviewDiff`, `buildReviewPrompt`, `partialReviewLine`), `aiReviewStore.run` (`ipc.listModels`), `AiReviewPanel` (`data-tour="ai-review-partial"`).

### AI-assisted conflict resolution
- **Resolve-with-AI** — Reads the conflicted file, asks the workspace's review model for a fully merged version, previews in mono, applies via `write_file` + `mark_conflict_resolved`; warns if markers remain; 48k-char limit. _Support:_ `ConflictAiModal.tsx`, `lib/aiConflict.ts`. _Entry:_ ChangesPanel conflict row → Sparkles.
- **Manual side-take + continue** — OURS/THEIRS (rebase-aware), open-in-editor, Continue/Abort. _Support:_ `ChangesPanel`, `resolveConflictTake` (see §6).

### Test runner drawer
- **Run tests** — Toolbar FlaskConical (or "More" → Tests on a narrow canvas) → popover test-command input; runs via login shell, 60s timeout. _Support:_ `ReviewCanvas.handleRunTests` → `run_test_command`.
- **Persist command** — Saved per workspace. _Support:_ `set_workspace_test_command`.
- **Auto-detect default** — package.json→`npm test`, Cargo.toml→`cargo test`, pytest→`pytest`. _Support:_ `detect_default_test_command`.
- **Result drawer** — Pass/fail "exit N" badge, selectable stdout/stderr; Esc dismisses. _Support:_ `review/TestDrawer.tsx`.

### Notable implementation details
- **AI primitive (`ai_complete`)** is the single shared one-shot model call for AI review, conflict resolution, and commit-message drafting. `resolve_provider(model)` routes to the Rust provider path. **Helper models** — the callers don't hard-code an id: `lib/helperModels.ts` `resolveHelperModel(tier)` asks `suggest_model` (the builtin tag lookup, `builtin_anthropic_model_tagged`) once per session — `review` (`code_review` → `balanced`, today `claude-sonnet-5-5`) for AI review, commit and PR drafts, `fast` (`quick_fix` → `fast`, today `claude-haiku-5-5`) for the workspace rename — and falls back to those ids when the backend can't answer. Synchronous defaults (a new builder stage, the Talk model, the AI review picker) read `helperModelIds.ts` `helperModelNow(tier)`; `App` looks both tiers up on mount. With `json_schema` it forces a single named tool call; token usage recorded into the canonical `spend_events` ledger (surface `'review'` with a workspace, else `'adhoc'`).
- **CodeMirror setup** — `EditorPane` hand-builds extensions (no `basicSetup`): gutters, drawSelection, rectangularSelection, history, bracketMatching, search, match + symbol-occurrence highlighting, the ⌘-click definition plugin, a custom keymap, language extension, themed via compartment, diffGutter, an updateListener pushing line/col/selection-count (and the document text **only on an actual edit** — it runs on every transaction, including each one the ⌘-hover plugin dispatches to repaint its underline, and serialising the buffer there cost as much as the edit itself; `setPos` also returns the previous object when nothing moved, so React bails out instead of re-rendering the pane); six live-reconfigurable compartments (blame, lineNum, tab, wrap, font, theme).
- **Diff parsing** — `parseFullDiff` (full review structure with `rawText` for `git apply -p1`) and `parseDiffForFile` (editor gutter markers).
- **Two diff surfaces stay in sync** via the shared `lib/diffLineStyle.ts`; three extension tables (`fileIcons`, `languageDetection`, `editorLang`) agree on `getExtension`.

---

## 6. Git & GitHub

### Git status & change detection
- **Working-tree status (libgit2)** — Branch, ahead/behind, has-upstream, conflict count, in-progress operation, and per-file `FileChange` (`path`, `status`, `staged`/`unstaged`/`conflicted` from libgit2 status flags; untracked included). _Support:_ `git_ops::status_files`/`get_status`; `get_git_status` (splits the cheap file-walk from the slow ahead/behind). _Entry:_ `ChangesPanel` polls every 5s.
- **Ahead/behind vs upstream (timed)** — Graph walk under a 3s timeout; on timeout (or when it can't compute) sets `aheadBehindKnown=false` with ahead/behind 0, and the Review Companion's sync line shows "—" rather than a misleading "Up to date with origin" (the Changes panel only shows "N ahead" above 0, so it shows nothing). _Support:_ `git_ops::ahead_behind`, `get_git_status`; `CompanionReview.tsx`.
- **In-progress operation detection** — Maps `RepositoryState` to `merge`/`rebase`/`cherry-pick`. _Support:_ `git_ops::operation_state`. _Entry:_ drives the conflict section + Continue/Abort.
- **Fast dirty check (rail)** — `is_dirty` (no untracked recursion) + `dirty_ahead_behind`. _Support:_ `git_ops`.
- **Per-workspace git summary (batch)** — One `WorkspaceGitSummary{dirty, ahead, behind}` per worktree; per-worktree timeouts; a single unreadable worktree defaults to clean. _Support:_ `workspaces_git_summary`. _Entry:_ rail chips.
- **Branch listing** — `{local, remote}` with the default (HEAD) branch promoted first; remote as `origin/dev`, `*/HEAD` excluded. _Support:_ `list_branches`. _Entry:_ GitOpsMenu, base picker.

### Diff reading (git operations side)
- **Working-tree diff** — `diff_index_to_workdir` with untracked synthesized as "new file" diffs, optional `ignore_whitespace`, capped at 1 MiB with a truncation marker. _Support:_ `get_git_diff`.
- **Staged diff** — HEAD-tree → index (`git diff --cached`). _Support:_ `get_staged_diff`. _Entry:_ AI commit-message drafting.
- **Commit log (paginated)** — First-parent revwalk, `skip`/`limit`; each `CommitInfo{sha, shaShort, summary, authorName, timestampMs}`. _Support:_ `git_log`. _Entry:_ `HistoryModal` (page 50).
- **Commit diff** — One commit vs its first parent (root vs empty tree). _Support:_ `commit_diff`. _Entry:_ click-to-expand in HistoryModal.
- **Last commit** — `(shortSha, subject, body)` of HEAD or null. _Support:_ `get_last_commit`. _Entry:_ amend prefill.
- **Blame** — Per-line blame vs HEAD; friendly errors for no-history / >1 MiB. _Support:_ `blame_file`. _Entry:_ editor gutter (§5).

### Staging & unstaging
- **Stage / unstage single file** — `git add` / `git restore --staged` (fallback `git reset HEAD`). _Support:_ `stage_file`/`unstage_file`. _Entry:_ Unstaged/Staged rows in ChangesPanel.
- **Stage all / unstage all** — `git add -A` / `git reset HEAD`. _Support:_ `stage_all_changes`/`unstage_all_changes`.
- **Stage / apply / revert hunk** — Tempfile + `git apply --cached`/`-p1`/`--reverse`. _Support:_ `stage_hunk`/`apply_hunk`/`revert_hunk` (§5 diff UI).

### Commit & amend
- **Commit staged changes** — `git commit -F "$OCTOPUSH_COMMIT_MSG_FILE"` through the user's **login shell** so gitconfig identity, hooks, and signing behave like the terminal; the message goes to a temp file named in the environment (deleted afterwards), never into the command line, so any message is safe under sh, bash, zsh and fish (`commit_in_login_shell`, shared with Amend); rejects empty; returns the new short SHA. Guarded by the **secret guard** first (staged diff; see "Secret guard" below): a finding opens the guard's confirm instead of committing. _Support:_ `commit_changes` (holds git_lock; `allow_findings` = the fingerprint of the findings the user confirmed, rescanned every call). _Entry:_ Commit button / `c` shortcut.
- **Amend last commit** — `git commit --amend -F` (message via the environment, as for Commit); prefills subject+body from last commit; warns "Last commit is pushed — amending rewrites history" when ahead 0 + upstream. Same secret guard as Commit (staged diff). _Support:_ `amend_commit` (`allow_findings`). _Entry:_ "Amend last commit" checkbox.
- **AI-drafted commit message** — Fetches the staged diff, sends it (the review helper model, `claude-sonnet-5-5`) with `COMMIT_SYSTEM` (≤50-char subject + optional body) and a 12k-char-capped prompt. _Support:_ `lib/commitMessage.ts`, `ChangesPanel.handleDraft` → `ai_complete`. _Entry:_ "✨ Draft" button.
- **Initial-commit healing** — On project open, ensures HEAD exists and captures on-disk files (fresh "Initial commit" or amends a legacy empty-tree HEAD). _Support:_ `git_ops::ensure_initial_commit`.

### Discard & file operations
- **Discard file** — Tracked → `git restore --staged --worktree`; untracked → drain index + delete worktree copy; containment guard refuses paths outside the workspace. _Support:_ `discard_file`; `ConfirmDialog`. _Entry:_ per-row `×`.
- **File-tree ops (rename/create-file/create-dir/delete)** — All via `contained_path` (refuses paths outside the workspace, the root itself, or anything with a `.git` component); create validates a single component. _Support:_ `fs_rename`/`fs_create_file`/`fs_create_dir`/`fs_delete`. _Entry:_ file-tree context menu.

### Push / pull / fetch (sync)
- **Push / publish branch** — Secret guard first (the commits being pushed; see "Secret guard" below), then refuses detached HEAD, then `git push --set-upstream origin '<branch>'` via login shell. _Support:_ `push_branch` (`allow_findings`). _Entry:_ "Publish branch" / "Push to origin · N ahead".
- **Fetch** — `git fetch` via login shell, under git_lock. _Support:_ `fetch_changes`.
- **Pull (strategy-selectable)** — `--ff-only`/`--rebase`/`--no-rebase`; outcome classified `ok`/`diverged`/`conflict`/`error` via `classify_pull`. _Support:_ `pull`. _Entry:_ "Pull" button; diverged → Reconcile modal (Merge/Rebase).
- **Reconcile diverged** — Modal offering Merge or Rebase; re-runs the pull. _Support:_ `ChangesPanel`.

### Secret guard (#730)
- **What it checks, and when** — A local, offline scan of only what is about to leave the Mac, never the whole repo: **commit / amend** — the staged diff (HEAD → index); **push** — every commit the push sends, each against its first parent (so a key added and removed again is still caught), from the branch as it is on the remote the push goes to (`origin/<branch>`, whatever upstream the branch tracks; `secret_scan::push_target_base`, #859), else — while the branch isn't on `origin` yet — the branch's upstream, else the remote's default branch (`origin/HEAD`, `origin/main`, `origin/master`), else every commit on no remote-tracking ref (`--not --remotes`; the whole history only when the repo has no remote refs at all); **pull request** — the commits since the merge base with the PR's base (resolved like the PR, `pr_target`); **a crew's Action stage** — the branch's commits since the workspace's base plus the uncommitted worktree (staged, unstaged and untracked, ignored files excluded). Only added lines are read; push, PR and crew ranges over 200 commits fall back to one net diff (the on-demand branch scan has no cap); a scan reads at most 16 MB of added lines and shows at most 50 findings while counting all of them. A blob larger than 16 MB is never loaded as text (`DiffOptions::max_size`); its size is checked in the diff's per-file callback, where libgit2 knows it (in the tree-to-tree diffs of push, PR and a crew's committed range it is still 0 when the deltas are listed; a binary-flagged blob whose size is still unknown has it read from the object database header), and it makes the scan partial. **Long lines:** every rule reads the whole line — prefixed provider keys, your own credentials, AWS keys, private keys and `.env` credentials — so a key past column 16K of a minified bundle is still found; only the generic `api_key = "…"` assignment rule looks at the first 16 KB of a line and skips the rest (that alone doesn't make the scan partial). A scan that hits the 16 MB budget, or skips a blob past 16 MB, is **partial**: it is never treated as clean — the confirm (or the crew's hold) says "Scanned the first 16 MB; the rest wasn't checked." and needs the same explicit confirm as a finding. The git2 scan runs on a blocking thread (`spawn_blocking`) so the UI never stalls. A 5,000-line diff scans well under a click's latency, and one multi-MB line of 100k distinct tokens scans in linear time (bounded tests). _Support:_ `secret_scan.rs` (`staged_files`, `push_files`, `pr_files`, `worktree_files` → `Collected { files, partial, scope, unscanned }`, `collect_added`, `scan_collected`).
- **Detectors (precision first)** — Prefixed tokens at their real lengths: Anthropic `sk-ant-…`, OpenAI `sk-proj-` / `sk-svcacct-` / `sk-admin-`, legacy `sk-…T3BlbkFJ…` and 48-char `sk-…`, GitHub `ghp_` / `gho_` / `ghu_` / `ghs_` / `ghr_` (36) and `github_pat_`, Stripe `sk_live_` / `rk_live_`, Slack `xox[abprs]-`, Google `AIza` (35); OpenRouter `sk-or-v1-` (64 hex), xAI `xai-` (80), Groq `gsk_` (52), Hugging Face `hf_` (34 letters), GitLab `glpat-`, npm `npm_` (36), Slack app-level `xapp-`; an AWS access key id (`AKIA` / `ASIA`) only with a 40-char secret key named within 5 lines or bare on the same line; a PEM `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----` header only with key material under it (the next line, added or unchanged, so an added header over a key body already in the file asks; or an inline `\n…`) or a legacy encrypted key's `Proc-Type:` line, so code that merely mentions the header is quiet; **by name, whatever the file holds (even empty), when newly added** — an `id_rsa` / `id_ed25519`-style file ("SSH private key file"), any `*.pem` ("PEM file", so a public certificate committed as `.pem` asks too), any `*.p12` / `*.pfx` / `*.jks` ("certificate or keystore file"), a `*.key` ("private key file") unless it starts like a zip archive (`PK\x03\x04`, so a Keynote document stays quiet, though one past the 16 MB scan budget leaves the scan partial, which asks; a blob past 16 MB is never loaded whole for this, only its first 4 bytes are streamed, and in a push/PR range it stays quiet only if every add of that path was a zip) and `.claude/settings.local.json` at any depth ("Claude Code local settings"; Octopush's own hooks file there is git-excluded, so it never asks), while an edit to one already tracked doesn't; in `.env` / `.env.*` files (not `.example`, `.sample`, `.template`, `.dist`, `.defaults`, `.schema`, `.tpl`), a credential-named variable (`KEY`, `SECRET`, `TOKEN`, `PASSWORD`, `PWD`, `PRIVATE`, `CREDENTIAL`, `AUTH`) with a real value (not empty, a `$REF`, a boolean, a number or a URL without credentials); in an MCP config (`.mcp.json`, `.claude/mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, at any depth), an `env`-shaped `"UPPER_SNAKE": "value"` pair with a credential-named key and a real value by the same filters (`${GITHUB_TOKEN}` / `${env:…}` references are placeholders) — "credential in an MCP config (DB_PASSWORD)"; a provider token there is listed once, as that token; and a generic `api_key` / `secret` / `access_token` / `auth_token` / `password` string assignment, 20+ chars, above 4 bits/char of entropy with letters and digits — or, since hex can't pass 4 bits/char, a hex value of 32+ chars with letters and digits above 3 bits/char whose name isn't a digest's (`hash`, `digest`, `checksum`, `sha1`, `sha256`, `md5`) — kept out of test paths (`test/`, `tests/`, `spec/`, `fixtures/`, `__mocks__/`, `*.test.*`, …) and lockfiles. **Public by design, so quiet:** a Firebase web config's `apiKey: "AIza…"` (within 8 lines of `authDomain` / `firebaseapp.com` / `messagingSenderId` / `storageBucket`), a `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` value (in `.env` files and code; a prefixed provider secret there, like `sk_live_`, still is one) and an example JWT (`eyJ….eyJ….…`) in prose docs (`.md`, `.mdx`, `.rst`, `.adoc`, `.txt`). Placeholders never match (`xxxx`, `your-key`, `<…>`, `EXAMPLE`, `REDACTED`, `changeme`, long single-character runs, too few distinct characters), and a prefixed token's body must look random. **"That's your key" canary:** the credentials Octopush itself holds — provider API keys, saved git host tokens and the Jira API token from `~/.octopush/settings.json`, 12+ chars — are matched as exact values in memory; a hit reads "your Anthropic API key" and wins over a pattern matching the same value; another key on the same line is still its own finding. _Support:_ `secret_scan.rs` (`TOKEN_RULES`, `sensitive_file`, `is_mcp_config` / `MCP_ENV_PAIR`, `is_hex_secret`, `known_secrets_from`, `is_placeholder`, `shannon_entropy`).
- **Privacy** — A finding is `{file, line, rule, kind, yours, preview?}`: never the value or a hash of it. **Masked preview (#820):** `preview` is, for a prefixed provider token or an AWS key id only, the provider's public prefix from a fixed list (`sk-ant-`, `sk-proj-`, `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `AKIA`, …; never a character of the random part) plus `…` and the last 4 characters (`sk-ant-…9fQ2`, `secret_scan::masked_preview`); every other rule — `.env` and MCP credentials, the generic assignment, your own saved keys — previews the tail alone (`…4bYw`, `masked_tail`), so a password that happens to start with `sk-` or `AKIA` keeps none of its start; only when 16+ characters follow the prefix; none for a whole-file finding or a private key, and an AWS finding previews its key id, never the secret key beside it. Only the confirm dialog and the branch scan show it: the refusal's Display, `refusal_summary`, the journal notice and a Direct hold (`SecretHold::from_report` strips it, since the hold is persisted with the run) never carry it. Nothing logs, persists or sends a candidate value; known credentials print `[redacted]` in `Debug`; an interactive scan (commit, push, PR) that can't read the repository logs only its error and never blocks (the git command reports the real problem). The fingerprint binding an override (below) keys each finding with an HMAC-SHA256 of the matched value under a random per-install key (`~/.octopush/secret-guard.key`, 0600, so a detached worker and a restarted app agree on an approved hold; written to a synced temp file and linked into place, so a crash never leaves an empty key, and a corrupt key file is replaced; an unreadable one logs a warning and that process falls back to a key of its own, so an approved hold asks again — `load_or_create_key_in`); those per-value hashes stay inside `secret_scan.rs` — only the aggregate fingerprint is returned or stored. Tests assert no secret (nor its last 8 chars) appears in a finding's Debug/JSON, the error's Display/IPC form, the summary, the journal notice, the persisted hold, the run events, the stage rows sent to the UI or the database. _Support:_ `secret_scan.rs`; `tests.rs` `secret_guard_tests`, `secret_guard_orchestrator_tests`.
- **The refusal and the confirm** — `commit_changes`, `amend_commit`, `push_branch` and `create_pull_request` rescan on every call and return `AppError::SecretsFound { findings, total, partial, fingerprint }` (IPC `{kind:"SecretsFound", message, findings, total, partial, fingerprint}`) unless `allow_findings` equals the fresh scan's fingerprint. The fingerprint covers the action's scope (`commit` — amend included —, `push`, `pr`, `worktree`, so a confirm for one action never passes another), **every** value any rule flagged (file, line, rule, a keyed hash of the value; every rule runs on every line, so a provider key never hides a generic secret, an AWS key or a `.env` credential on the same line; each flagged value on a line is its own finding, deduplicated by span in linear time, and a value inside one already listed on that line, such as an `.env` value that is a GitHub token, is hashed but not listed twice, as is a provider token only partly overlapping one of your own keys; a private key's value is its whole block, from the header's own column (not the start of its line) through the matching `-----END …-----` line, stopping before another private-key header, bounded to 64 KB; a line of the block the diff didn't add — unchanged inside the key, or its rest after the last added line — is read from the file's new side, its blob or the worktree file (`secret_scan::pem_unchanged`, `AddedFile::unchanged`), so two keys alike only in their added lines ask separately; the new side is read only when a block reaches a line the diff didn't add (`secret_scan::pem_needs_new_side`; never for a newly added file), that read counts against the 16 MB scan budget less the added lines the diff already counted, and one past what is left marks the scan partial with the file listed as unread; a new side that doesn't hold the diff's added lines at their numbers (a clean filter such as Git LFS or git-crypt, or a file rewritten since) lends no lines, so the block is hashed from the added lines only; in a push, PR or branch scan each commit's key is walked within that commit's own lines (`AddedFile::segments`); a key with no END line runs on through the unchanged text below it to the next header, the end of the file or 64 KB, so editing that text asks again), the total and the partial flag and, for a partial scan, what wasn't read (each skipped file as path and blob id, or, for a worktree file git hasn't hashed yet, as path with its size, mtime, inode and ctime; each commit the budget never reached; fingerprint format `v3`, so a hold approved before this asks again) — not just the 50 shown — so a confirm applies only to exactly what the dialog showed: a key added or edited after the dialog, or one past the cap, gets a new refusal with the new findings. The frontend (`lib/secretGuard.ts` `secretRefusal`) opens `SecretGuardDialog` (`ModalShell`, `data-tour="secret-guard-dialog"`): rouge mono eyebrow "Possible secret", an upright-serif lead naming kind and place ("This change adds what looks like an Anthropic API key in tests/fixtures.ts:12." / "This push …" / "This pull request …"; several findings list kind · file:line · masked preview, capped at 5 + "and N more" counted against the total; a single finding shows its masked preview on a mono line under the lead (`data-tour="secret-guard-preview"`; tooltip "Only a provider's prefix and the last four characters, to tell keys apart"); the closing line reads "… Octopush shows only a provider's prefix and the last four characters, and never stores the value."; a partial scan adds "Scanned the first 16 MB; the rest wasn't checked." (`data-tour="secret-guard-partial"`), and with nothing found the lead reads "This change is too large to check in full."), "It matches a key you saved in Octopush." for a canary hit, and two choices: **Leave it out** (default focus, also Escape; in Review it jumps to the first finding's file diff, in the PR composer it leaves an inline "Held: …" note) and the explicit **Commit regardless** / **Push regardless** / **Open it regardless**, which re-runs that one action with `allowFindings` = the refusal's fingerprint (the next action asks again). _Support:_ `SecretGuardDialog.tsx`; `ChangesPanel.tsx`; `PrComposer.tsx`.
- **Before the commit button (#835)** — The Review Companion previews the staged diff's scan and, when Commit would stop, says so in its verdict ("N staged · the secret guard will ask first.") and one line under it ("possible secret · GitHub token in src/a.ts:3" + **Show it**). The preview (`secret_scan_staged` → `ScanPreview { findings, total, partial }`, `null` with the guard off) carries no fingerprint and enforces nothing. See the Review Companion's "Secret guard verdict line". _Support:_ `secret_scan::preview`; `CompanionReview.tsx`.
- **Setting** — Settings › General › Safety › **Guard commits against secrets** (`data-tour="settings-secret-guard"`), on by default on Free and Pro alike (`secretGuardEnabled`, `None` ⇒ on); off skips every scan, so the commit, push, PR and crew paths behave exactly as before. _Support:_ `GeneralPane.tsx` `SecretGuardRow`; `settings.rs`; `secret_scan::guard_enabled`.
- **Scan this branch's commits (#820)** — In the Review Companion's Branch & publish section, under "N commits ahead of main" (only with commits since the base), an upright-serif link **Scan this branch's commits** (`ShieldCheck`, `data-tour="review-companion-scan-branch"`; tooltip "Check every commit since main for possible secrets. Changes nothing.") runs the guard's rules over every commit since the merge base with the workspace's base — resolved like Review's "Since base" view (`collisions::resolve_merge_base`), each commit against its first parent so a key added and removed again is found; unlike push and PR there is no 200-commit cap and never a net diff, only the same 16 MB budget, whose exhaustion makes the result partial — on demand only, never automatically, and whether or not the guard's switch is on. While it runs: "Scanning 3 commits…". Then (`data-tour="review-companion-scan-result"`, `.octo-fade-in`): a verdigris `ShieldCheck` with "No possible secrets in 3 commits." (partial and clean: "Nothing found in the first 16 MB; the rest wasn't checked."), or a rouge `ShieldAlert` with "2 possible secrets in this branch's commits.", up to 5 rows of kind · file:line · masked preview + "and N more", the partial note when it applies and "A later commit that removes a key leaves it in the history: rotate a real one."; the link then reads **Scan again**. A failure (no merge base) reads "Couldn't read this branch's commits.". The result is dropped when the branch's commits, HEAD, merge base or base change, so an amend or a rewrite that keeps the commit count clears it too. Read-only: no fingerprint, nothing blocked or changed. _Support:_ `secret_scan_branch` → `secret_scan::scan_now` + `branch_files` (scope `history`); `BranchSecretScan` in `CompanionReview.tsx`; `lib/secretGuard.ts` `branchScanSummary`; `ipc.secretScanBranch`.
- **Talk's shell (#819)** — A Talk command that commits, pushes or opens a pull request is scanned before it runs, whether the agent issues it (`run_command`, from the parent turn or a sub-agent's `SubagentGate`) or you type it (`$`-direct). `secret_scan::shell_plan` reads each shell segment (split on `;`, `|`, `&`, newlines; `git -C dir …` and `/usr/bin/git` understood) for `git commit`, `git push` and `gh pr create` (its `--base` / `-B` / `--base=`), and `shell_files` scans only what they would send, as one scan with scope `shell`: a plain commit → the staged diff; a commit in a command that also stages (`git add` / `git stage` in any segment, or `commit -a` / `--all`) → every uncommitted change, staged, unstaged and untracked (`uncommitted_files`); a push → the unpushed commits, from the branch's upstream (a typed `git push` goes there, not necessarily to `origin`, so the Push button's `origin/<branch>` start, #859, doesn't apply here); `gh pr create` → the PR's commits onto its `--base`, else the repo's default branch (`git_ops::repo_default_branch`). A heuristic over the text that errs towards scanning. **Agent commands** park on a secret variant of the inline approval card (`ApprovalCard`, `data-tour="talk-secret-approval"`; rouge eyebrow "Possible secret", the reason "possible secret · Anthropic API key in a.ts:3 and 2 more" — kind and file:line only, sub-agents prefixed "Sub-agent “…”:"; when the command also stages, "This command also stages files, so the check covered every uncommitted change, not only what is staged."; then "Approving runs it once, for exactly these findings."): **Leave it out** (brass, first) or **Run regardless**, and no "don't ask again". A thread's "Approve & don't ask again" grant never answers it (`ApprovalBroker::await_secret_approval`; an "always" sent to it counts as one approval and grants nothing, `ApprovalBroker::record`), and the approval is bound to the fingerprint: the command runs only if a rescan finds exactly what the card showed, else the card asks again (`chat_engine::guard_agent_command`). Denied, the model reads "Command not run — the secret guard found … in what it would commit or push, and the user declined. …", with kinds and places, never a value. The secret check runs before the destructive-command check, and a denial skips it. **`$` commands** (`ShellRequest.allowFindings`) are refused with `SecretsFound` before anything is shown or persisted; the Talk composer opens `SecretGuardDialog` ("This command adds what looks like …", **Leave it out** / **Run regardless**), and Run regardless re-runs that one command with the refusal's fingerprint (`chatStore.shellSecretByWs`, `resolveShellSecret`). The guard switched off: both paths behave as before. The scan reads the workspace's repository, wherever the Talk shell has `cd`'d. _Support:_ `secret_scan.rs` (`shell_plan`, `shell_files`, `uncommitted_files`, `guarded_scan`); `chat_engine.rs`; `chat_agents.rs` `SubagentGate`; `ApprovalCard.tsx`; `Composer.tsx`; `chatStore.ts`.
- **Talk's context blocks (#1046)** — The `@` blocks a Talk message attaches (files, ranges, folder listings, `@session` output, `@diff`) are scanned before the turn is sent, with the same confirm (`action="message"`, "Send regardless"), also when a block's scan can't run; "Leave it out" sends the message without the flagged blocks, and Escape sends nothing and gives the draft back. A diff is scanned per file by its path, hunk headers' function context included (`diffScanInputs`), so the path rules (`.env`, key files, MCP configs) apply as in a commit. No fingerprint: the composer scans exactly the blocks it then sends. See "@-mentions (context)" under Talk. _Support:_ `secret_scan_text`, `secret_scan::text_files`, `talkContextResolve.ts` (`scanContextBlocks`).
- **Not covered (yet)** — A crew stage that commits inside its own run (only the boundary before an Action stage is checked), and a scan of the repository's history before the branch's base. Remembered dismissals are out by design (#820): an override covers one fingerprint for one act, so a real key can't slip through later unseen. MCP configs: a lower-case or camelCase key in an `env` block (only `UPPER_SNAKE` names are read as env entries), a value with an escaped quote, and user-level configs outside the repo. The file-level rules: a key file, keystore or `.claude/settings.local.json` that was already tracked (only adding one asks), other key-file names (`*.keystore`, `*.p8`, …), and a `.key` file whose content starts like a zip archive, which is treated as a document and checked by the content rules only. Hex secrets: one shorter than 32 chars, one under a name outside the generic rule's (`token`, `key` alone), and a hex value spread over string concatenation. The Companion's preview covers the staged diff only — not the push, the pull request or the unstaged changes.

### Branch / stash / advanced ops (GitOpsMenu)
- **Switch branch** — `git switch` via login shell; worktree-aware friendly errors ("checked out in another workspace"). _Support:_ `switch_branch`. _Entry:_ GitOpsMenu branch list.
- **Create + switch branch** — Idempotent create (local/remote base) then switch. _Support:_ `create_and_switch_branch`. _Entry:_ "Create branch…" → `FileNameDialog` (`validateRefName`).
- **Stash push / list / pop / drop** — `git stash -u` (with optional message), newest-first list, pop (conflicts surface as error), drop. _Support:_ `stash_push`/`stash_list`/`stash_pop`/`stash_drop`. _Entry:_ "Stash changes…", "Stashes…" → `StashesModal`.
- **Clean untracked** — `git clean -fd` (with `LC_ALL=C`); returns removed paths. _Support:_ `clean_untracked`. _Entry:_ "Clean untracked…" → ConfirmDialog.
- **Reset HEAD** — `git reset --soft|--mixed|--hard <target>`. _Support:_ `reset_head`. _Entry:_ per-commit reset in HistoryModal → `ResetDialog`.
- **Cherry-pick** — `git cherry-pick` (no editor); conflict is a tagged outcome (enters cherry-pick state). _Support:_ `cherry_pick`. _Entry:_ per-commit cherry icon.
- **Tags create / list** — Lightweight tag at a SHA or HEAD; alphabetical list. _Support:_ `create_tag`/`list_tags`. _Entry:_ per-commit tag icon → `FileNameDialog` (`validateTagName`).

### Conflict resolution
- **Conflict section** — Shown when conflicted>0 or operation present; header "N conflicts · <op>"; during a **rebase** side labels swap (ours→UPSTREAM, theirs→MINE). _Support:_ `ChangesPanel`.
- **Take ours / take theirs** — `git checkout --ours|--theirs` then `git add`, under one git_lock. _Support:_ `resolve_conflict_take`. _Entry:_ OURS/THEIRS chips.
- **Mark resolved** — `git add` clears the unmerged state. _Support:_ `mark_conflict_resolved` (used by ConflictAiModal).
- **AI conflict resolution** — (See §5.) _Support:_ `ConflictAiModal.tsx`.
- **Continue / abort operation** — `git <op> --continue`/`--abort` (no editor); continue outcome `ok`/`moreConflicts`/`error`. _Support:_ `continue_operation`/`abort_operation`. _Entry:_ "Continue <op>" (only when conflicts cleared) / "Abort" → ConfirmDialog.

### GitHub & pull requests
- **PR-state model** — `PrState` enum `open`/`draft`/`merged`/`closed` collapsing GitHub's `state`+`draft`+`merged_at`; handles REST and `gh` shapes. _Support:_ `github.rs::pr_from_json`.
- **Find PR for current branch** — Reads branch + `origin` URL; bails for non-github.com / detached / no origin. Strategy: `gh pr list … --head` then REST fallback (auth: saved github.com PAT → `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN`; unauth OK for public). Results live in `prStore.byWorkspace` (`null` = looked up, none). For open/draft PRs it also fills `Pr.checks` (`{ state: passing|pending|failing, failing: [{ name, runId }] }`): from `statusCheckRollup` in the same `gh pr list` call (check runs and commit statuses), or, on the REST path and only with a token (unauthenticated, the 60s poll already spends the hourly limit), from `GET /commits/{head.sha}/check-runs`. Absent on any error. _Support:_ `find_pr_for_branch`, `github.rs::checks_from_gh_rollup` / `checks_from_rest_check_runs`, `stores/prStore.ts`. _Entry:_ ContextHeader PR chip (polled per switch + 60s; a PR opened in the app shows at once).
- **PR composer ("Open a pull request")** — `ModalShell` (no click-outside; Escape closes). Preflights with `github_ship_readiness` and dead-ends honestly on no GitHub remote / `gh` not signed in. When ready: base branch via `BaseBranchPicker` (default `workspace.fromBranch`, else the repo default), editable title + Markdown body, an "Open as a draft" `TogglePill` switch (`Draft`), and a neutral Sparkles "draft again" button. On open it drafts once through `ai_complete` (the review helper model, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, budget-gated, spend attributed to the workspace; the note under the form names the model and its cost, or `· unpriced` when the cost is zero or unknown — never `$0`) from `pr_draft_context` — `git diff base...HEAD` (merge base → HEAD, prompt-capped at 12k chars), the commit subjects, the workspace task, the linked ticket and the "How this change was built" provenance (agent turns + model per turn from `list_file_edits`/`get_message`). With a repo PR template (`.github/pull_request_template.md` and GitHub's other lookup paths) it fills that template; otherwise Summary · Changes · How it was built · Testing. Picking another base re-drafts against it; when the human has already edited the title or body their text is kept and only the diff is re-checked ("Your edits are kept — draft again to write it against X"). When the branch has no diff and no commits against the base the composer says "This branch has no changes against X yet." and the create button stays disabled. A GitHub issue key (`42`, `#42`, `owner/repo#42`) adds `Closes #N` once; a Jira key or an Epiku story id (`ST-1.1`, `lib/detectIssueKey.ts` `isIssueKey`) prefixes the title. A failed draft leaves the form editable (title seeded from the task). It never opens from the repo's default branch (`BranchList.repoDefault`: `origin/HEAD`, else main/master; the composer says so instead of drafting) or from a branch onto itself (checked before any push, and again by `create_pull_request`). Create pushes unpublished commits first, then `create_pull_request` runs `gh pr create --base --head --title [--draft] --body-file <tmp>` in the login shell (base, head, title and body file reach `gh` as environment variables, so no user text is spliced into the command under bash, zsh or fish). `git_ops::pr_target` decides where it goes, and the draft's diff uses the same answer: a base picked on any remote (`upstream/x`) opens against `x` on that remote's repo; a bare base lives on gh's default repo (`remote.<r>.gh-resolved = base`, what `gh repo set-default` writes), else `origin`. That repo is passed as `--repo` (`owner/repo`, or `host/owner/repo` off github.com), and the head as `owner:branch` when the branch's push remote (its upstream, else `origin`) belongs to another owner — a fork. The branch-onto-itself check compares against the base with its remote stripped. It then stores the PR for the chip and toasts "Pull request #N opened" with "View on GitHub". Failures show inline and keep the composer open. **Secret guard:** the push and `create_pull_request` are scanned and confirmed **separately** — a refused push shows "This push …" with **Push regardless**; once it lands, the PR's own scan shows "This pull request …" with **Open it regardless** before the PR opens. Each confirm carries only its own fingerprint, so one override never covers both; Escape closes only the confirm. _Support:_ `PrComposer.tsx`, `lib/prDraft.ts` (`bareBase`), `github.rs` (`find_pr_template`, `pr_create_command`, `pr_head_label`, `gh_repo_arg`, `pr_from_create_output`), `git_ops::{pr_target, branch_pr_context}`, `pr_draft_context`, `create_pull_request`. _Entry:_ Review CTA, ⌘K → Actions, `⌘⇧P` — only when the active workspace is on a named branch, and not while a code editor or terminal has focus (`data-tour="pr-composer-create"` on its CTA).
- **Open PRs for project (batch)** — `gh pr list --state open …`; never errors (empty on gh-missing/unauthed). _Support:_ `open_prs_for_project`. _Entry:_ rail PR indicators (15s throttle).
- **Merged-and-clean missions (batch)** — `gh pr list --state merged … headRefOid --limit 300` (`merged_heads_in`; the 300 most recent merges, so an older one is simply not offered), then each non-root worktree of the project whose branch has a merged PR (the latest per branch, `parse_merged_heads`) is kept only when its HEAD is exactly that PR's head commit and it has no changes or untracked files (`merged_archive_skip` / `is_merged_and_clean`; an unreadable status counts as changed). Each one also lists its **local files**: git-ignored paths (an ignored folder once, as `dir/`, untracked folders included: one holding only ignored files, like `db/dev.sqlite` under `*.sqlite`, is listed as `db/`; a folder is listed only while it holds, at any depth, a file that isn't exempt, so an empty folder or a `.claude/` holding only Octopush's hooks is not; the walk skips dependency and build folders whole rather than counting them, and a folder with more than `LOCAL_FILES_WALK_CAP` (2,000) other entries counts as holding local files; symlinks are not followed and count as files) other than dependency, build and cache folders (`node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`, `dist`, `build`, `target`, `.next`, `.cache`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.turbo`, `.parcel-cache`, `.gradle`), `.DS_Store`, and the `.claude/settings.local.json` Octopush writes while it holds nothing but Octopush's hooks (`is_hooks_only_settings`, via `agent_adapter::strip_claude_hooks`): restore writes those again. Once Claude Code has saved anything else there, such as its "don't ask again" choices, the file is a local file like any other (`git_ops::local_ignored_files` / `is_rebuildable_ignored` / `folder_holds_local_files`). Errs when the merged PRs can't be read; the store then tries again no sooner than 5 minutes later, on a later refresh (`MERGED_RETRY_MS`). _Support:_ `merged_workspaces`, `workspaceStore.loadMergedPrs` → `mergedPrByWs` + `localFilesByWs`. _Entry:_ rides `loadProjectPrs` (15s throttle): on a project's first open-PR read of the session, then only when a workspace's open PR left the open list, never on every focus refresh; also after an archive skipped something and after Undo. Feeds the rail's "merged · archive?" (#963).
- **Archive merged missions (re-checked)** — `archive_merged_workspaces(projectId, projectPath, workspaceIds, localFilesOk)` reads the merged PRs again and, for each mission, archives it (as `archive_workspace` does, branch kept) only if it still passes right then: still an active mission of the project with a non-root worktree; no Talk turn on any conversation of a workspace at that folder and no Direct run `running`/`paused` there (`worktree_busy`, `Db::chat_threads_at_worktree`, `has_active_run_at`; a failed read counts as busy); clean; HEAD exactly the merged PR's head; and no local files but those `localFilesOk` names for the mission (the exact paths its confirm showed: a `local.db` that appeared after the confirm named `.env` skips it). Activity, dirt and local files are checked once more right before the worktree is deleted (`worktree_busy` then `changed_since_named`, inside `archive_workspace_at`); a mission that fails then is left in place, untouched, with that reason, and its Talk checkpoints are pruned only after the worktree is gone. Returns `{ archived, skipped: [{ workspaceId, reason }] }` with reason `busy` · `changed` · `moved` · `local-files` · `unverified` (the merged PRs couldn't be read) · `gone` · `failed`. _Support:_ `merged_archive_check`, `merged_archive_skip`, `changed_since_named`, `archive_workspace_at`, `archiveMerged.ts`.
- **List PRs ("start from a PR")** — `gh pr list …`; friendly empty state if gh missing. _Support:_ `list_prs`. _Entry:_ `PrPicker` in MissionCreator.
- **Ensure PR branch (fetch head)** — No-op if the branch exists, else `git fetch origin 'pull/<n>/head:<branch>'` (works for fork PRs). _Support:_ `ensure_pr_branch`.
- **Save git credentials** — Persists `{username, token}` per host to `~/.octopush/settings.json`. _Support:_ `save_git_credentials`. _Entry:_ only the private-clone flow (`NewProjectFlow.tsx`, after a successful clone with "Remember for {host}" ticked, the default); there is no Settings entry. Consumed by PR lookups and clone.

### Notable implementation details
- **git2 vs shell-out boundary** — Read/inspect ops use libgit2 (status, diffs, log, blame, branch/stash list, create_branch, tags, worktree lifecycle). Mutating/auth-sensitive ops shell out so they inherit the user's full git environment: commit, amend, push, fetch, pull, switch, cherry-pick, continue/abort, reset, clean, stage/unstage, hunk apply, conflict take, discard, PR-branch fetch.
- **Auth model** — Push/pull/fetch/switch/commit/cherry-pick/continue/abort run via the user's **login shell** (`$SHELL -l -c`) so SSH agents, the osxkeychain helper, and `~/.gitconfig` behave as in a terminal. Clone runs under `env LC_ALL=C` (`build_clone_command`), with the URL and target path passed as `"$OCTOPUSH_CLONE_URL"` / `"$OCTOPUSH_CLONE_TARGET"` environment variables, never spliced into the command. User text (commit messages, PR titles, URLs, paths) always travels through the environment (`login_shell_output`), since fish reads `\'` inside single quotes as an escape; only refs and SHAs, which can't contain a backslash, are single-quoted (`git_ops::quote_git_ref`), and only after `git_ops::is_git_ref_arg` (a hex SHA, or a valid branch name not starting with `-`) or `is_hex_sha` (cherry-pick) accepts them, so `switch_branch`, `cherry_pick`, `ensure_pr_branch` (the PR's head ref, in `github::pr_fetch_command`) and `push_branch` (the current branch, in `push_command`) refuse anything else before a shell runs, the last two with an error that doesn't repeat the name ("isn't a valid branch name"), and the `gh pr list --head` lookup falls back to the API; `gh api` check-runs reads its path from `OCTOPUSH_GH_API_PATH` the same way; a credentialed retry uses a `GIT_ASKPASS` tempfile fed from env vars, bypasses stored helpers (`-c credential.helper=`), clones from the URL with `username@` embedded when it names no user, and on success — if Remember is set and the askpass actually answered — stores the credential through the helpers (`git credential approve` via the login shell, 15 s timeout, best effort). Progress is read per `\r` redraw (`take_terminal_segments`), so the bar moves within a phase. PR lookups use the saved github.com PAT or `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN`, preferring `gh`.
- **The git lock** — `git_lock.rs` keeps a global per-path async mutex so two mutating ops on the same worktree can't interleave; read-only commands take no lock.
- **PR state classification** lives entirely in `github.rs`; the frontend only maps `PrState` → color/glyph. The pure classifiers (`classify_pull`, `classify_continue`, `friendly_switch_error`, `pr_from_json`, `parse_git_url`) are heavily unit-tested.
