## 7. Terminals, PTY Daemon & Sessions

### PTY Daemon — out-of-process architecture
- **Standalone PTY daemon (`octopush-pty-server`)** — A separate Rust binary that owns ALL pseudo-terminals so shells survive Octopush restarts/auto-updates. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/bin/octopush-pty-server/*`; bundled as a sibling binary. _Entry:_ auto-spawned on app launch by `pty_daemon::ensure_daemon_running()`.
- **Detached spawn** — Launched with `setsid()` + null stdio so it escapes Octopush's process group and is adopted by launchd. _Support:_ `pty_daemon.rs::spawn_detached`.
- **Binary resolution** — Sibling of `current_exe()`, then `$PATH`, then `target/debug/…`. _Support:_ `resolve_daemon_binary`.
- **Unix domain socket** — Newline-delimited JSON-RPC at `~/.octopush/pty-server.sock` (chmod 0700). _Support:_ `pty_daemon.rs`, `main.rs`.
- **PID-file double-start protection** — `~/.octopush/pty-server.pid`; a second instance verifies the PID is alive AND is an `octopush-pty` process before exiting. _Support:_ `main.rs::acquire_pid_file`.
- **Protocol version handshake / stale-daemon replacement** — Reuses a running daemon across version bumps if `protocol_version` matches (`EXPECTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 2`); on mismatch SIGTERMs the old daemon and spawns the new one. _Support:_ `query_daemon_protocol`, `kill_existing_daemon`.
- **Idle auto-exit** — Exits when zero live PTYs AND zero clients for `OCTOPUSH_PTY_AUTO_EXIT_SECS` (default 3600s). _Support:_ `server.rs` idle thread.
- **Clean shutdown + crash recovery** — SIGTERM/SIGINT removes pid/socket; a stale socket is unlinked on startup; orphan scrollback logs swept. _Support:_ `main.rs`, `storage.rs`.
- **fd-limit raising** — Raises `RLIMIT_NOFILE` so terminal spawns don't fail with EMFILE. _Support:_ `main.rs::raise_fd_limit`.
- **Daemon log** — `~/.octopush/pty-server.log`, rotated at 5 MiB. _Support:_ `storage.rs`.

### Daemon socket protocol
- **Request methods** — `list_terminals`, `spawn`, `attach{since_seq?}`, `detach`, `write`, `resize`, `kill{signal?}`, `remove`, `shutdown`, `version`. _Support:_ `protocol.rs`, `server.rs::dispatch`.
- **Streaming events** — `data{id,seq,bytes}`, `exit{id,code?}`, `error{id,message}`, `attention{id}`, `foreground{id,busy,command?}`, `replay_done{id}` (once per `attach`, after the last replayed chunk — see **OSC 52 clipboard writes**). _Support:_ `protocol.rs::Event`.
- **Per-connection model** — Each connection on its own thread; a writer thread drains an unbounded channel; on disconnect, only that connection's attachments detach. _Support:_ `server.rs::handle_connection`.

### Scrollback persistence & replay
- **Dual buffering: ring + disk** — Each chunk gets a monotonic `seq`, stored in a 64 KiB ring buffer AND appended to a disk log. _Support:_ `session.rs::push_output`.
- **Disk-backed log** — `~/.octopush/pty-state/<id>.log`, capped at 1 MiB by rotation. _Support:_ `storage.rs`.
- **Scrollback replay on attach** — Atomic snapshot under the lock: full disk log replay if `since_seq` is older than the ring, else ring backlog; live data streams after with no overlap. _Support:_ `server.rs::cmd_attach`.
- **Sessions outlive their shells** — A session is kept after its shell exits (for replay) but its fds are released eagerly. _Support:_ `server.rs`, `session.rs`.

### Spawning, attaching & terminal lifecycle (daemon side)
- **Spawn a shell** — Opens a PTY via `portable_pty`, launches `$SHELL` (or `/bin/zsh`) as a login shell in `cwd`. The shell inherits the daemon's whole environment (`portable_pty`'s `CommandBuilder` starts from the daemon's own env; the explicit `HOME`/`USER`/`LANG`/`LC_*`/… re-apply is a subset of it) plus `TERM`/`COLORTERM`, then the caller env is merged last — which is how the app-side **UTF-8 locale on every spawn** (below) reaches the shell even on a daemon that predates it. _Support:_ `server.rs::cmd_spawn` (command built by `server.rs::build_shell_command`; real-PTY smoke tests in `pty_smoke_tests.rs`).
- **Duplicate-id / respawn-in-place** — A spawn for a live id is refused; an EXITED id is replaced in place (log deleted, seqs restart). _Support:_ `cmd_spawn`.
- **Write / resize / kill / remove** — base64 write; PtySize resize; SIGTERM/SIGKILL kill (session retained); `remove` SIGKILLs the process group + deletes the log. _Support:_ `cmd_write`/`cmd_resize`/`cmd_kill`/`cmd_remove`.

### Attention detection (daemon-side)
- **"Waiting for input" detection** — A 1s thread fires `Event::Attention` on (A) command-finished (fg pgroup returns to the shell) or (B) TUI-parked (fg child <1% CPU for two ticks + ≥2s quiet). _Support:_ `server.rs` attention thread, `session.rs::check_attention`.
- **False-positive gating** — Requires ≥200 bytes since last alert; a 3s post-attach grace; baselines wiped on attach. _Support:_ `session.rs`.

### App-side daemon client
- **`DaemonClient`** — One `UnixStream`; a reader thread multiplexes responses (per-`reqid` waiters, 5s timeout) and per-terminal event subscribers. _Support:_ `pty_client.rs`.
- **Single-subscriber-per-terminal routing** — A re-attach replaces the prior subscriber so each byte renders once. _Support:_ `pty_client.rs::attach`.
- **Self-healing reconnect** — On socket EOF the next call re-runs `ensure_daemon_running()` and swaps in a fresh socket. _Support:_ `try_reconnect`.
- **Stub client (degraded mode)** — If the daemon binary is absent, a pre-broken stub lets Octopush still launch and heals on first reconnect. _Support:_ `pty_client.rs::stub`.
- **`PtyManager` + Tauri event bridge** — Forwards `TermEvent`s as `pty://data`/`pty://exit`/`pty://attention`/`pty://foreground`/`pty://reattached`; `pty://data` carries `replay: true` for every chunk of a reattach until the daemon's `replay_done` (a fresh spawn is live from the start; a daemon without the marker leaves a reattached pane tagged as history for good). _Support:_ `pty_manager.rs`.
- **UTF-8 locale on every spawn** — `DaemonClient::spawn` completes the caller env in two steps. First it forwards the app's own `LANG`/`LC_ALL`/`LC_CTYPE` (where the caller set none), so the shell follows *this* app's launch environment rather than whatever the long-lived daemon was started with (a Finder launch has none, a dev launch from a terminal has the user's). Then, if the effective `LC_CTYPE` still isn't UTF-8, it sets `LANG` (`en_US.UTF-8` on macOS, `C.UTF-8` elsewhere) when `LANG` and `LC_CTYPE` are both unset, else only `LC_CTYPE` — a non-UTF-8 `LC_CTYPE` is overridden even beside a UTF-8 `LANG`, since it beats `LANG`. An explicit `LC_ALL` is respected as is, a UTF-8 effective ctype leaves everything untouched, and the user's own rc files still win, as in Terminal.app; an `LC_ALL` in the daemon's own environment is the one thing this can't beat. Why: a Finder/Dock launch carries no `LANG`/`LC_*`, so Octopush shells ran in the `C` locale and `pbcopy` — which Claude Code's fullscreen renderer runs for its copy-on-select — wrote non-ASCII text to the clipboard as Mac Roman mojibake (`ó` → `√≥`, `á` → `√°`) in every app you pasted into. Applies to every fresh spawn (RUN terminals and the Talk per-thread shell share the funnel); a shell that survived an app restart keeps the environment it was born with until it is re-created. _Support:_ `pty_client.rs::with_utf8_locale` / `with_utf8_locale_from` / `utf8_locale_fixup`; tests `pty_locale_tests`.
- **`spawn_or_attach` + `OutputHook`** — Reattaches a running id (replays scrollback) or spawns fresh; an optional `OutputHook` runs per chunk for token scanning. _Support:_ `pty_manager.rs`.
- **Setup terminal session** — The one session spawned by the backend rather than a Run pane: `create_workspace` starts a fresh worktree's setup script in a `setup` terminal whose daemon "shell" is the setup runner (env `OCTOPUSH_SETUP_SCRIPT`); the pane reattaches to it like any surviving session. Full entry in §2 "Setup terminal". _Support:_ `commands.rs::spawn_terminal_session` (shared with `spawn_or_attach_terminal`), `workspace_setup.rs`.

### Backend commands & session model
- **Session commands** — `create_session` (UUID, ContextGuard env, token hook, mark Active), `list_sessions`, `write_to_session`/`write_text_to_session`, `resize_session`, `kill_session`, `delete_session`. _Support:_ `commands.rs`.
- **Terminal commands (Run mode)** — `list_terminals`, `create_terminal`, `rename_terminal`, `reorder_terminals` (the session line's drag: renumbers `position` in one transaction), `delete_terminal` (DB-first, then daemon `remove`). _Support:_ `commands.rs`; `terminals` table.
- **PTY-bridge commands** — `spawn_or_attach_terminal` → `{mode:"Spawned"|"Reattached", pid?}`; `list_pty_sessions` (swallows daemon errors → empty for graceful degradation). _Support:_ `commands.rs`.
- **Foreground command reporting** — The daemon's `foreground` event carries `{id, busy, command?}`: on the transition **into** busy it resolves the foreground process's argv summary (basename + up to two **non-flag** args, capped at 96 chars — flags are dropped so a three-token window still carries the subcommand `npm --silent run dev` hides behind) via `KERN_PROCARGS2` on macOS (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline` on Linux, for the day the daemon is ported — it is macOS-only today). argv, not just the executable name: every JS toolchain reports its leader as `node`. Empty argv entries are counted rather than skipped, so the take-window can't slide into `envp` and leak `KEY=value`. Resolved once per state change, never per tick; omitted from the wire when the platform can't answer, which the frontend treats as "unknown role", never as an error. A client (re)attach **clears the daemon's busy latch** so a session that was already mid-command when the app restarted reports its true state on the next tick instead of looking idle. **Degradation:** the protocol version is unchanged, so an app update that reuses a still-running older daemon gets no `command` until that daemon exits — sessions then keep the neutral role and busy ones read "running". Feeds `lib/sessionRole.ts`. _Support:_ `session.rs` (`foreground_command`, `parse_procargs2`, `summarise_argv`, `emit_foreground`, `on_attach`), `server.rs` tick, `pty_client.rs` `TermEvent::Foreground`, `pty_manager.rs` `PtyForegroundEvent`.
- **Session record & statuses** — `Session{id, name, color, icon, project_root, agent(provider/model/…), token_budget, tokens_used, status, context_files, tags, …}`; status `Active|Idle|Paused|Completed|Error`. _Support:_ `session.rs`.

### Session restore & env injection
- **`restore_active_sessions`** — On `.setup()`, re-spawns a PTY for each `Active`/`Idle` session, re-applying ContextGuard env + the token hook; marks `Error` on failure. _Support:_ `lib.rs`.
- **`ContextGuard::auto_configure`** — Produces the isolated PTY env: `HISTFILE` (per-session isolated history), `OCTOPUSH_PROJECT_TYPE` (Rust/Node/Python/Go/Java/Ruby/Unknown), `OCTOPUSH_GIT_BRANCH`; `set_ports` adds the workspace's `OCTOPUSH_PORT` / `OCTOPUSH_PORT_COUNT` / `CONDUCTOR_PORT` when the session's root is a workspace's worktree (see "Workspace ports"). _Support:_ `context_guard.rs`.
- **Context-file detection** — Detects `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `CONVENTIONS.md` (stored on the session, not exported). _Support:_ `context_guard.rs`.
- **`OCTOPUSH_MODEL` injection** — `create_session` injects the model id so CLI agents can read it. _Support:_ `commands.rs`.
- **Token-scan output hook** — The per-chunk `OutputHook` runs `token_engine::scan_pty_output` → `TokenEngine.record`. _Support:_ `commands.rs`, `lib.rs`.

### xterm.js front-end (TerminalPane)
- **Terminal instance** — `@xterm/xterm` 6 (DOM renderer) with cursorBlink, JetBrains Mono, 10000-line scrollback. The font stack (`XTERM_FONT_FAMILY`, `src/lib/xtermTheme.ts`) ends with installed Nerd Font faces (`NERD_FONT_FALLBACKS`: Symbols Nerd Font, JetBrainsMono Nerd Font, MesloLGS NF, …) before `monospace`, so prompt icons in the Private Use Area (a starship branch icon, powerline separators) draw from them instead of as empty boxes; letters keep JetBrains Mono. Theme is built live from the active Octopush theme's tokens (`getXtermTheme()`), not a fixed palette, so RUN & TALK terminals stay legible under every theme including the light "vellum" theme — reassigned on the `octo:theme` event without remounting. xterm 6 scrolls through its own overlay scrollbar (VS Code's scrollable element) rather than a native one on `.xterm-viewport`; its thumb is tinted from the same theme (`scrollbarSlider*` = `--color-octo-border`, `--color-octo-border-strong` on hover/drag). _Support:_ `TerminalPane.tsx`, `TerminalView.tsx`, `lib/xtermTheme.ts`, `stores/themeStore.ts`.
- **Option/Alt + arrow word jumps** — Option+Left/Right moves by word at a shell prompt (macOS sends `ESC b` / `ESC f`; elsewhere Alt+arrows send the Ctrl+arrow sequences). xterm.js 6 dropped this mapping (xtermjs/xterm.js#5346), so the custom key handler re-creates xterm 5's exact bytes and feeds them through `term.input(…, true)` → `onData` → PTY; only plain Alt+arrow is rewritten. _Support:_ `lib/xtermAltArrow.ts` (`legacyAltArrowSequence`), `TerminalPane.tsx`, `chat/TerminalView.tsx`.
- **FitAddon + ResizeObserver** — Fits xterm; debounced resize sends `resizeSession` only on actual change; refits on visible toggle + `layoutVersion` bumps. _Support:_ `TerminalPane.tsx`.
- **WebLinksAddon + file-path link provider** — Linkifies URLs; path-shaped tokens (with `:line[:col]`) become clickable links routing to Review/editor. _Support:_ `TerminalPane.tsx`.
- **Clipboard bridge** — Cmd-C / Ctrl-Shift-C / right-click-with-selection copy via `term.getSelection()` (native Tauri clipboard, byte-safe). Covers xterm's own selection only: a TUI that captures the mouse (Claude Code's fullscreen renderer) owns click-and-drag and copies by itself from inside the PTY (`pbcopy` on macOS, or OSC 52 — see below), which is why the shell's locale matters — see **UTF-8 locale on every spawn**. Hold **Option** while dragging to get a native xterm selection anyway (next bullet). _Support:_ `TerminalPane.tsx`.
- **Option-drag forces native selection (macOS)** — xterm's `macOptionClickForcesSelection` is on. While a program owns the mouse (Claude Code's fullscreen renderer, tmux with mouse on, vim `mouse=a`) xterm on macOS otherwise offers **no** modifier at all for a selection of its own (Shift only works on other platforms — `SelectionService.shouldForceSelection`), so Option+drag is the escape hatch back to a native selection and the clipboard bridge; it is also the key Claude Code's own hint names for xterm.js terminals. Option+click therefore no longer reaches a mouse-mode program — and xterm's alt-click-moves-cursor (the arrow-key burst that walks the cursor to the clicked cell, meant for a shell prompt) is switched off per gesture while a program tracks the mouse (`term.modes.mouseTrackingMode`, checked on `mousedown`), so the click sends the program nothing at all. Plain clicks, and shells with mouse mode off (where Option+click still repositions the cursor), are untouched. _Support:_ `TerminalPane.tsx` (Terminal options + the `mousedown` capture hook).
- **OSC 52 clipboard writes** — A program in the PTY can set the system clipboard with `ESC ] 52 ; Pc ; Pd ST` (Claude Code's fullscreen copy-on-select over SSH and in builds that copy via OSC 52 only, tmux `set-clipboard`, neovim, helix): the payload is base64-decoded to bytes and read as UTF-8 (never `atob`-as-text — the Latin-1 bug behind xterm.js#6002), then written through `copyToClipboard` (native Tauri clipboard). **Write-only:** a `?` query is swallowed and never answered, so a program can never read the clipboard; an empty payload (clear) is ignored; payloads over 4 MiB of base64 are dropped; `Pc` is not inspected (any selection target writes the system clipboard). **History never reaches the clipboard:** the daemon ends every `attach` replay with a `replay_done` marker and the app tags each `pty://data` chunk before it with `replay: true`; the pane feeds xterm through `attachOsc52Clipboard`, which holds the gate while any tagged chunk is still unparsed (xterm parses in order and runs a write's callback after its chunk), so an OSC 52 inside replayed scrollback — or inside a live chunk queued behind it — is never honored, whatever the terminal answers or the user types meanwhile. A fresh spawn is live from the start; a reattach to a daemon that predates the marker stays tagged as history for good (OSC 52 off in that pane until the daemon is replaced — the safe failure). **Policy:** only while the pane is on screen *and* the Octopush window has focus, so a hidden workspace or an Octopush behind another app can't swap the clipboard under you; every program copy is announced with a toast (“Copied from the terminal”), since the user pressed nothing in Octopush; copies are paced to one per 500 ms with the newest payload winning, so a looping program can neither thrash the clipboard nor spam toasts. _Support:_ `src/lib/osc52.ts` (`decodeOsc52`, `attachOsc52Clipboard`, `OSC52_MAX_BASE64`, `OSC52_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`), `TerminalPane.tsx` (policy + `pty://data` feed), `pty_manager.rs` (`PtyDataEvent.replay`, `start_reader_thread`), daemon `protocol.rs::Event::ReplayDone` + `server.rs::cmd_attach`; tests `osc52.test.ts` (against the real xterm), `TerminalPane.test.tsx`, daemon `scrollback_replay_on_reattach`.
- **Reattach SIGWINCH "wiggle"** — On `pty://reattached`, briefly resizes cols to force alt-screen TUIs (Claude Code/vim/htop) to redraw. _Support:_ `TerminalPane.tsx`.
- **Attention surfacing** — `pty://attention` and xterm's `onBell` ping `attentionStore` only when the pane is NOT visible, carrying the **terminal id** so Run's session line can mark the session that rang rather than the whole workspace, and the event's **`reason`** (`AttentionFlag.reason`: `idle` from the daemon, `permission` / `input` from Claude Code's hooks; null for the bell). A hook reason also fires a native notification ("Claude Code needs you" · "<workspace> — waiting on permission" / "— waiting on your input") unless the pane is on screen and Octopush is focused, under Settings › General's "Notify when a crew needs you". **Off-screen hook waits, per session:** a `permission` / `input` ping for a hidden pane updates the workspace flag as before (Mission Control's band and the mode pulse are unchanged) and also opens a wait for that terminal in `attentionStore.waitsByTerminal` (`{ workspaceId, reason, since }`; `since` stays at the first ping, a bell or idle ping leaves it alone), so two waiting sessions keep two marks on the session line and in the ⌘⌥K switcher. A wait clears when that session is focused, typed into, settles (`pty://settled`) or is closed (`clearsWait`, `clearWait`, `clearForTerminal`); the workspace flag clears with it only when the flag is that same hook wait. **On-screen panes:** a hook reason for a pane that IS on screen (a Run pane or Talk's seat) raises no flag but marks the session in `attentionStore.waitingByTerminal`, and its caption appends a quiet mono suffix *· waiting on permission* / *· waiting on your input* (mute ink, one static 6px brass dot, no pulse; it fades in and out through `FadeSwap`). The mark clears when the user types or pastes into the pane (xterm's own replies to terminal queries and mouse reports also come through `onData` but don't count — `lib/xtermReports.ts` `isTypedInput`), the pane becomes the focused one, `pty://settled` (Claude Code's `Stop` hook) arrives, the pane leaves the screen, or the session is closed. The daemon's `idle` guess, an event with no `reason` (an older daemon or CLI) and the bell never mark a shown pane; without hooks (an older Claude Code, or the setting off) nothing is marked and everything behaves as before. _Support:_ `TerminalPane.tsx`, `attentionStore` (`waitingByTerminal`, `setShownWaiting`, `waitsByTerminal`, `clearWait`), `lib/attentionFocus.ts` (`nextShownWaiting`, `clearsWait`), `run/SessionLine.tsx`, `run/SessionSwitcher.tsx` (`orderWaitingFirst`), `lib/xtermReports.ts`, `run/PaneWaiting.tsx`, `run/RunPanes.tsx`, `chat/TalkSeat.tsx`, `terminalsStore.deleteTerminal`, `src/lib/claudeWaiting.ts` (`claudeWaitReason`, `claudeWaitingCopy`, `decideClaudeWaitingNotification`, `notifyClaudeWaiting`).
- **Claude Code hook signals (on by default; #287)** — Behind `claudeHooksEnabled` in `~/.octopush/settings.json`: unset means on, only `false` is off (`claude_hooks::hooks_enabled`, `.unwrap_or(true)`). Toggle: Settings › General › Attention, "Let Claude Code say what it's waiting on" (`data-tour="settings-claude-hooks"`; reads `claudeHooksEnabled ?? true`, saves an explicit `true`/`false`). Its helper text says what the hooks do: the file they are written to, that they also say which Claude Code session each terminal runs (what Run's Context section reads), and that nothing they report leaves the Mac. With the setting off Context is simply not drawn; nothing prompts for it. When the setting is on, the Claude Code version is known and ≥ `TESTED_CLAUDE_FLOOR`, and the worktree is one Octopush made (managed, under `.octopus-worktrees/`), creating or restoring a workspace (app or `octopush-mcp`), and every app launch for each active workspace Octopush made (so one created before the update gets them too), merges seven command hooks into `<worktree>/.claude/settings.local.json`. Five `async` attention hooks: `Notification` `permission_prompt`, `Notification` `idle_prompt`, `Notification` `elicitation_dialog`, `Notification` `elicitation_url_dialog` (an MCP server asking for input through a form or a URL; #594) and `Stop`. Two session hooks, with no matcher (every source and reason): `SessionStart` (`async`) and `SessionEnd` (synchronous, so it lands before the process is gone), which say which Claude Code session a Run terminal runs (see **Session usage** under "Companion · Run"). The synchronous hook normally costs a few milliseconds at exit. When Octopush's database is write-locked its insert waits, and that wait is bounded by Claude Code's own budget for `SessionEnd` hooks (1.5 s by default, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS`): past it Claude Code drops the hook and exits, the end is not recorded, and the terminal keeps that session until another starts there. The session hooks run `'<octopush-mcp>' hook >/dev/null 2>&1 --octopush-hook`: Claude Code adds a `SessionStart` hook's stdout to the conversation, so the shell discards both streams whatever the binary does (it prints nothing anyway), and the marker still ends the command (`agent_adapter::session_hook_command`; a test runs it over a binary that prints to both). A worktree hooked by an earlier version gets the two new events at the next launch, by the same sweep, with nothing for the user to do; a Claude Code session already running then keeps the hooks it started with until it is restarted. The attention hooks run `'<octopush-mcp>' hook --kind permission --octopush-hook`, `… hook --kind input --octopush-hook` (the idle and both elicitation matchers, so an MCP question reads "waiting on your input") and `… hook --octopush-hook`: the matcher Claude Code fired on decides the signal, and the payload's `notification_type` is read only when no `--kind` was passed (a hook installed before it). The merge keeps every user key and hook; ours are found by the `--octopush-hook` marker, so a re-install replaces them; a file that isn't JSON is never written. `/.claude/settings.local.json` is appended once to the repo's shared `info/exclude` under `# added by Octopush (Claude Code hooks)`; if that can't be written, or git still doesn't ignore the file (it is tracked in the repo), nothing is installed. Archive and delete strip our entries before the worktree goes, and delete the file only if nothing else was in it. Turning the toggle off strips them from every active managed worktree at once (and turning it back on installs them again): `save_settings` compares the setting before and after (`claude_hooks::toggled`) and runs `claude_hooks::sync_all_workspaces` off the UI path, which the launch also runs; with the setting off at launch it strips too. Sweeps run one at a time, a newer sweep cancels an older one at its next workspace, and the setting is re-read before each workspace, so a quick off-then-on can't leave a worktree stripped (#539). The settings file is written through a temp sibling with a unique name per write, then renamed into place. The main checkout's working tree and `~/.claude` are never touched. Every Run terminal gets `OCTOPUSH_TERMINAL_ID`. The hook reads the stdin payload and queues `(terminal, signal, session_id)` in `hook_signals`, with no message text or transcript path; it records nothing outside an Octopush terminal, prints nothing and always exits 0. Each row is stamped with when the hook fired, noted as the hook process starts and before it touches the database (`record_hook_at`), not when the row was written: rows queue in write order, and a hook that waited on the database is written late. It also reads its own `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` (`cli` for the terminal UI, `sdk-cli` for `claude -p`, seen live on 2.1.327): a print-mode or SDK session, such as a `claude -p` the agent itself runs, inherits the terminal's id but is not the terminal's session, so it is never linked. Its `SessionStart` and its `SessionEnd` are both queued as an end of that session, which sets it aside from its first moment (see **Session usage**), and its other signals are queued without its session id (`agent_adapter::interactive_entrypoint`). Every second the app drains the queue and, only while the setting is on, emits `pty://attention` with `reason: "permission" | "input"`, `pty://settled` for `Stop`, or `pty://claude-session` for a session start or end (after recording it; these two say nothing about attention and don't mark the terminal as hook-driven). Rows older than 10 seconds are dropped; with the setting off every drained row is dropped, so the table never grows and nothing replays when it is turned back on. Once a terminal has delivered a signal, the daemon's idle heuristic is quiet for it while the setting is on, including after `Stop`; turning the setting off brings the heuristic back. Mission Control's terminal card reads "waiting on permission" / "waiting on your input" for a hook reason (see **Attention surfacing** for the notification). _Support:_ `agent_adapter.rs` (`merge_claude_hooks`, `strip_claude_hooks`, `install_claude_hooks`, `remove_claude_hooks`, `parse_hook_event`, `ClaudeCliVersion::supports_hooks`), `claude_hooks.rs` (gating, `info/exclude`, `hook_kind`, `record_hook`, `record_hook_at`, `remember_sessions`, `poll_once`, poller), `GeneralPane.tsx` (`ClaudeHooksRow`), `MissionControl.tsx` (`attentionCopy`), `db.rs` (`hook_signals`, `terminal_claude_session`, `ended_claude_sessions`), `octopush-mcp/main.rs` (`hook` mode), `pty_manager.rs`, `commands.rs`; contract fixtures `hooks/*.json` (2.1.314 synthetic; 2.1.327 `session-*.json` recorded live).
- **PTY survives unmount** — Cleanup disposes xterm but never kills the PTY; only an explicit close (a pane caption's **Close session** or the switcher's `⌫`) triggers `deleteTerminal`. App mounts a `TerminalPane` for EVERY `(workspace, terminal)` pair. _Support:_ `TerminalPane.tsx`, `App.tsx`.

### UI surfaces
- **Run session surfaces** — `SessionLine` (the mode band's right track) · `PaneCaption` in `RunPanes` (each session's one home) · `SessionSwitcher` (⌘⌥K) · `CompanionRun` (Context · Changes · Mission). Full entries in §1 under "Run · session navigation" and "Companion · Run". _Support:_ `src/components/run/*`, `CompanionRun.tsx`.
- **SessionSidebar / NewSessionDialog** — The legacy "session" model UI: header with The Octo at 18px (static; replaced the 🐙 emoji — the empty state's 4xl 🐙 is likewise now a 40px idle Octo) + "Octopush", a session list with status dot, icon, name, project•model, cost•tokens, budget gauge, tags; new-session dialog with template/name/root/model (an Atelier `Listbox`, "Default (agent decides)" as a real option; sets `OCTOPUSH_MODEL`)/icon/color/tags. _Support:_ `SessionSidebar.tsx`, `NewSessionDialog.tsx` (predates the Atelier redesign). _Entry:_ none: nothing mounts them today, and `⌘T` was never bound to a key.

### Notable implementation details
- **Why out-of-process** — PTYs are owned by their spawner; the split lets shells survive app restarts/auto-updates (like JetBrains/VS Code). Protocol v2 forces a one-time daemon replacement that deploys the eager-fd-release + `remove` fixes; running a pre-v2 and v2 build simultaneously makes them fight over the single daemon.
- **Restart flow** — App quits → daemon + shells keep running. Relaunch → reconnect, `list_terminals` reconciles DB rows with live daemon ids (`running`/`restored`); each `TerminalPane` calls `spawn_or_attach` (replays scrollback, fires `pty://reattached`).
- **Env injection summary** — Curated host-env allowlist + `TERM`/`COLORTERM` (daemon) → `HISTFILE`/`OCTOPUSH_PROJECT_TYPE`/`OCTOPUSH_GIT_BRANCH` (ContextGuard) → `OCTOPUSH_MODEL` (session create); every workspace Run terminal also gets `OCTOPUSH_TERMINAL_ID` and the workspace's `OCTOPUSH_PORT`/`OCTOPUSH_PORT_COUNT`/`CONDUCTOR_PORT`. Login shell in the project cwd.
