## 8. Providers, Models, Tokens, Budgets & Usage

### Provider abstraction & wire protocols
- **`LlmProvider` trait** — One normalized `complete(api_base, api_key, req, client) -> LlmResponse` so `chat_engine`/`ai_complete`/orchestrator stay provider-agnostic. **Streaming seam (Talk engine v2, A1):** `stream(…, sink)` hands `sink` each `StreamEvent` (`Text`, `ToolStart{index,id,name}`, `ToolInput{index,partial}`, `ToolEnd{index}`, `Reset`) and returns the same assembled `LlmResponse` as `complete` (usage, `raw_content`), so pricing and replay don't move; an answer whose stream carried no usage is `usage_unreported` (its 0 tokens are unknown, not free: callers record it on the usage-not-reported path, `unpriced` in the ledger, never as $0; Talk takes it up when it streams, A5); the default calls `complete` and emits the whole text as one `Text`, so a provider without streaming of its own (the test providers) works unchanged; Anthropic (A1) and OpenAI-compatible (A2) stream. `stream_with_retry` is `complete_cancellable` for a streamed call: the same backoff, `retry-after`, notices and local-server rule, each attempt raced against the turn's cancel; a transient failure after something streamed emits `Reset`, then retries; a remote stream that sends nothing for its adapter's bound after its 200 (`stream_idle` with `anthropic::STREAM_IDLE`, 60 s, as Anthropic pings while it works, or `openai_compat::STREAM_IDLE`, 600 s, as OpenAI-compatible servers promise no keep-alive) fails for good, never retried, like a dropped body (`silent_stream_error`: the provider may still be generating, so a retry could run and bill the request twice; a model server on this Mac has no idle bound); a stream that ends before the provider says the answer is complete is final too (`cut_off_error`). The SSE reader flushes at the end of the body, so an event whose closing blank line is a lone CR isn't lost; a `null` count in `message_delta`'s `usage` never replaces a real one. **Nothing calls it yet:** Talk, Direct and the sub-agents still use `complete`; the director moves to streaming in A5. _Support:_ `providers/mod.rs` (`LlmRequest`, `LlmMessage`, `LlmContent`, `LlmBlock` {Text, Image}, `LlmTool`, `LlmResponse`, `LlmStopReason`, `StreamEvent`, `stream_with_retry`), `providers/sse.rs` (`SseParser`, `SseReader`, `ByteSource`, `Body`).
- **Anthropic protocol adapter** — POSTs `{base}/v1/messages` with `x-api-key` and `anthropic-version`, and no beta header (the 128k-output beta served only Claude 3.7 Sonnet, which no catalog model is); the URL join is idempotent (a base already ending in `/v1` or `/v1/messages` never doubles to `/v1/v1/messages`; gateway subpaths like `…/anthropic` are preserved); maps tools to `input_schema`, images as base64; parses `usage` incl. cache-read/creation. Requires a key. **Streams** (`stream`): the same request with `stream: true`, read as Messages server-sent events and folded back into the message a whole response carries (`StreamedMessage`: `message_start`, each block's start/deltas/stop at its `index`, `message_delta`'s `stop_reason` and cumulative `usage`, `message_stop`; text, thinking and signature deltas, tool input JSON assembled from its pieces; `ping` and unknown events skipped), then parsed by the same `parse_response`; an `error` event is classified like its HTTP status (`overloaded_error` as 529). _Support:_ `providers/anthropic.rs::messages_url`, `post_messages`, `read_stream`.
- **Prompt caching (Anthropic, F7)** — For **repeated-prefix** requests the Anthropic adapter drops ephemeral `cache_control` breakpoints at the tail of each cache region — the last tool, the system block (promoted to a text-block array), and the last block of the last message (≤3 of the 4 allowed) — so context re-sent within the cache TTL bills at ~0.1× on a hit instead of full input price; each request's trailing breakpoint becomes the next request's cached prefix, which is what makes an agentic loop's growing history cache incrementally. It's **opt-in per call** via `LlmRequest.cache`: **on** for the TALK agentic loop and DIRECT stage loops (system + tool schemas + prior turns re-sent every iteration); **off** for REVIEW/`ai_complete` one-shots and forced-`tool_choice` structured calls, where a cache write would be a wasted 1.25× surcharge with no read to repay it. Below the model's minimum cacheable prefix the API silently skips caching (no error, no charge). GA on current models — no beta header needed; the default 5-minute TTL fits loop iterations (seconds apart) and continued chat. Cache-hit tokens are parsed (`parse_response`) and priced cache-aware (`token_engine::cost_for`). **Anthropic-only:** OpenAI-compatible providers cache automatically (we already read their `cached_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens`), local models don't cache — neither needs or reads `cache`. _Support:_ `providers/anthropic.rs::build_request` + `mark_message_cache_breakpoint`; `LlmRequest.cache` set at `chat_engine::send_agentic`, `orchestrator/agentic.rs`, `commands::build_ai_request`.
- **OpenAI-compatible adapter** — POSTs `{base}/chat/completions` with optional `Authorization: Bearer` (skipped when key empty, for Ollama); a Talk turn's requests to OpenAI's own host (`api.openai.com`, Chat Completions and Responses) carry `prompt_cache_key`, a hash of the thread id (never its title; `providers::prompt_cache_key`, `openai_compat::with_cache_key`), so they route to the same cache; other OpenAI-compatible servers never get the field; the URL join is idempotent (a pasted full endpoint isn't doubled); tools as functions, images as data URLs; parses `tool_calls`, `finish_reason`, `usage`. Covers OpenAI, DeepSeek, Ollama, vllm, llama.cpp, LMStudio, LocalAI. **GPT-6 models (any id containing `gpt-6`) go to `{base}/responses` instead, but only when the base URL's host is `api.openai.com`** (parsed, case-insensitive; a GPT-6 id behind LiteLLM, OpenRouter, a custom OpenAI-compatible provider or a base-URL override to another host stays on Chat Completions, since such a gateway may not speak Responses, and so keeps the tool limits above), because on Chat Completions they take no tools at all (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol/Terra) or only with `reasoning_effort: "none"` (GPT-6 Sol/Luna): the system prompt as the first input item, a `developer` message (`input_text`; none when it's empty), never the top-level `instructions`, which GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol append after `input`, outside the cacheable prefix (so on GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol a long Talk or stage prompt stays in the cacheable prefix and later turns can read it from cache; replayed turns hold only output items, so it is never repeated), then history as input items (results as `function_call_output`, images as `input_image`), flat function tools with `strict: false` (an omitted `strict` would make Responses attempt strict mode; Chat Completions is non-strict by default), `max_output_tokens`, `reasoning.effort` (effort off → `none` where the model accepts it, see per-stage effort), `store: false` (stateless, nothing kept server-side) with `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`. **Reasoning replay between tool turns:** when a turn returns reasoning items that all carry `encrypted_content`, `parse_responses_response` keeps its reasoning, message and `function_call` output items verbatim and in order in `raw_content`, behind an origin item naming the model, the configured provider and the `/responses` endpoint (never sent); the next request replays them before the `function_call_output`s, with the calls' `fc_…` ids, so the model keeps its reasoning across the tool loop. They are replayed only to the same model, provider and endpoint (`responses_replay`), since encrypted reasoning only decrypts for the org whose key produced it: a turn from another model (escalation), another configured provider or endpoint (a transcript resumed under a different provider or base URL), an origin item missing any of the three (written before they were recorded), the max-tokens truncation retry (empty raw), a turn without encrypted reasoning, or an Anthropic turn's content blocks is rebuilt from text + tool uses (`function_call` by `call_id`, no item id), and the Anthropic serializer never replays a Responses raw (`is_responses_raw`). The check compares the configured provider's name and base URL, not its key: changing the API key on the same provider (say, to a key from another org) is not detected, and its reasoning is still replayed. Talk turns are not replayed (Talk keeps no raw). The `encrypted_content` is kept locally with the rest of the turn, in `run_stages.blocked_transcript` (a parked or stopped stage) and `chat_agent_runs.transcript_json` (Talk sub-agent runs), the same places Anthropic's signed thinking is stored, and is only ever sent back to the provider and endpoint that produced it. The context-window guard counts it at its decoded size, 3/4 of the base64 length (`responses_raw_chars`): replayed reasoning still occupies the model's context window, so leaving it out would let a long reasoning stage overflow without compacting, while counting the base64 text itself would compact too early. Parses `output_text`, `refusal` parts (the explanation becomes visible text and the turn stops as `Other("refusal")` when there are no tool calls — with tool calls it stays a tool-use turn — never an empty end turn), `function_call` items, `status`/`incomplete_details` (`max_output_tokens` → max-tokens stop) and `usage.input_tokens_details` cached/written slices. On Chat Completions, a `message.refusal` explanation likewise becomes visible text (after any content) and a turn with no tool calls that stopped (`stop` or no reason) ends as `Other("refusal")`; a `length` cut keeps its max-tokens stop. **Streams (Talk engine v2, A2)** (`stream`): the same request with `stream: true` (Chat Completions also asks `stream_options: {include_usage: true}`, so the last chunk carries usage; Responses reports it unasked), `complete` and `stream` sharing one POST and error mapping (`post`, `Api`). The events are folded back into the body a whole response carries and parsed by the same `parse_response` / `parse_responses_response`, so text, refusal, tool uses, stop reason, cached and written usage and the encrypted-reasoning `raw_content` match `complete`: on Chat Completions the chunks' `content`, `refusal` (set apart after the text, as the whole parse does), `tool_calls` by `index` (a piece without one is the call at its place in the chunk's array; the first id and name stand, arguments assembled from pieces; a call whose pieces came before its name, or that came whole in one piece, starts with everything so far), `finish_reason`, the usage chunk and `[DONE]`; every call ends with the choice, since the format never marks one call's end; on Responses `output_text` / `refusal` deltas, `function_call` items by `output_index` (`ToolStart` at `output_item.added`, arguments deltas, `ToolEnd` at `output_item.done`) and the final `response.completed` / `response.incomplete` (its `output` filled from the closed items should it leave them out). A failure the stream reports (an `error` payload in a chunk, `response.failed`, an `error` event) is classified like the HTTP status it stands for (a numeric `code`, `server_error`, `rate_limit_exceeded`, `invalid_request_error` / `invalid_prompt`; anything else final), so `stream_with_retry` resets and retries the transient ones. A server that answers 400 naming `stream_options` is asked once more without it (unbilled, nothing streamed yet; any other 400 is never sent twice), and an answer without a usage chunk is `usage_unreported`. A server that ignores `stream` and answers `application/json` is read as `complete` reads it, its text sent as one `Text`; a Chat Completions stream that ends after its `finish_reason` without `[DONE]` has answered, one that ends before it (or a Responses stream before its final event) is final (`cut_off_error`). Silence past 600 s (`openai_compat::STREAM_IDLE`) is final; a model server on this Mac has no idle bound, as on Anthropic. An invalid tool-call argument string still becomes `{}`, as in `complete` (#1158). _Support:_ `providers/openai_compat.rs::chat_completions_url`, `uses_responses_api`, `is_openai_api_host`, `responses_url`, `build_responses_request`, `effort_off_level`, `parse_responses_response`, `responses_replay`, `responses_raw_chars`, `is_responses_raw`, `parse_response`, `post`, `rejects_stream_options`, `is_json`, `Api`, `STREAM_IDLE`; `providers/openai_compat/streaming.rs` (`read_stream`, `ChatChunks`, `ResponsesEvents`, `stream_error`); `orchestrator/agentic.rs::message_chars`.
- **Rate-limit headroom parsing** — Anthropic remaining-input-tokens + reset → `RateLimitSnapshot` so the agentic loop paces itself. _Support:_ `anthropic.rs::parse_rate_limit`.
- **Transient-failure retry** — `complete_with_retry` retries only transient errors (429, 529, 5xx, a connection that couldn't be opened, a body-read failure after a 200 that wasn't a timeout), honoring `retry-after`; capped exponential backoff (max 60s, `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 5`), interruptible by a director stop. What the provider marks final returns at once: `x-should-retry: false` on any status, and a spend-cap 429 (no `retry-after`, a body naming a spend or usage limit: `ProviderErrorKind::SpendCap`), both providers through `classify_status`. A request that went out and got no answer (a read timeout, a connection lost while waiting, a body that went silent) is final and says it wasn't retried (`request_error`, `body_error`); a loopback base that refuses the connection gets one retry (`LOCAL_CONNECT_RETRIES`) and then reads "The model server on this Mac at … isn't reachable. Is it running?". That one-retry budget covers every `Network` failure on a loopback base, so a connection reset mid-body there also gets one retry and then ends final (`into_final`): Talk's card offers "Copy error details" rather than "Try again", with the same "connection was lost" text. Sub-agents, Direct stages and the Talk director use it; the director's `complete_cancellable` also races the call against the turn's cancel flag (`or_cancelled`), so a Stop abandons the request in flight. Every caller narrates a wait with `retry_notice`. _Support:_ `providers/mod.rs`.
- **Stalled-connection guards** — The pooled client every remote LLM call goes through (`tls::llm_client`, built on `tls::client_builder`) sets a 10 s connect timeout, a 30 min idle read timeout (`LLM_READ_TIMEOUT`, sized for a long non-streamed answer) and TCP keep-alive (30 s idle, 10 s interval, 3 probes); no total timeout. A stalled or silently dropped connection ends in an error instead of a request that never returns; it is not retried, because the request had already gone out (see "Transient-failure retry"). Both providers send a loopback base (`providers::is_loopback_base`) on `tls::local_llm_client` instead: connect timeout, no read bound, no proxy (`providers::client_for`). _Support:_ `tls.rs` (`with_stall_guards`, `llm_client`, `local_llm_client`), `providers/mod.rs` (`client_for`), `chat_engine::shared_http_client`.

### Provider & model catalog (`provider_router.rs`)
- **`ProviderConfig`** — `name`, `api_base`, `api_key_env`, `models`, `rate_limits`, `enabled`, `protocol` (anthropic | openai-compatible), `local` (true ⇒ UI hides key, base URL editable). Persisted to `~/.octopush/providers.json`. _Support:_ `provider_router.rs`.
- **`ModelInfo` (per model)** — `id`, `display_name`, `input_cost_per_m`, `output_cost_per_m`, `cache_read_cost_per_m`, `cache_creation_cost_per_m`, `max_context`, `supports_vision`, `supports_tools`, `tags` (curated pills), `max_output` (the most output tokens one request may ask for; serialized `maxOutput`, omitted when unset). **Output cap (#1157):** every Talk round and forced close (`chat_engine::turn_max_tokens`, the cap looked up once per turn into `ChatRequest.max_output`) and every Direct stage and Talk sub-agent request (`orchestrator::agentic`, `clamp_to_model_output`) sends `max_tokens` clamped to it (`clamp_output`), so a model that takes less than Deep's 64,000 is never refused for asking too much. Builtin caps: 128,000 for the current Anthropic lineup, Opus 4.6 and the GPT-6.x models; 64,000 for the other Anthropic models and DeepSeek Reasoner; 16,384 for GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini; 8,192 for DeepSeek Chat; none for the Ollama models (a local server doesn't refuse a larger value). A custom model without a cap is sent as asked. _Support:_ `provider_router.rs` (`clamp_output`, `model_max_output`, `clamp_to_model_output`).
- **Built-in provider defaults (4)** — **anthropic** — current: claude-fable-5-2 $8/$40, claude-opus-5-5 $4/$20, claude-sonnet-5-5 $2/$10, claude-haiku-5-5 $0.10/$0.50 (1M context each; listed first so they lead the picker's tag-based Recommended rows); previous: claude-fable-5-1 ($10/$50), claude-fable-5, claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-5 ($2/$10), claude-haiku-4-5 ($1/$5); legacy: claude-opus-4-6 ($5/$25), claude-sonnet-4-6 ($3/$15); **openai** (gpt-6.2-astra — $8/$40, cached input $0.40, 30-minute cache writes $10, tag most capable — and gpt-6.2-sol — $2/$10, cached input $0.10, writes $2.50, tag coding — 1,050,000-token context each, listed first, text-only until image input is confirmed; gpt-6.1-terra — $1/$5, cached input $0.05, 30-minute cache writes $1.25, 1,050,000-token context, image input, tag balanced — gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini; GPT-6 Astra, Sol and Luna and GPT-6.1 Sol are priced but deliberately not listed, so Talk can use them only after they are added in Settings › Models); **deepseek** (deepseek-chat, deepseek-reasoner); **ollama** (local, free: llama3.3, qwen2.5-coder, deepseek-r1). _Support:_ `builtin_providers()`.
- **Catalog load + migrations** — `ProviderRouter::load()` seeds defaults on first run and applies on-disk migrations (protocol coercion, re-enable, backfill cache costs/tags/models, `backfill_builtin_vision` turning image input on for a saved GPT-6.1 Terra entry without touching its other fields, `backfill_superseded_by` copying the builtin `superseded_by` (Fable 5.1 → Fable 5.2, §4) onto saved entries, `backfill_max_output` copying each builtin output cap onto saved entries of the same provider and id, the builtin value winning, append missing builtins); reloaded fresh on every request (edits apply to the next message, no restart). _Support:_ `provider_router.rs::load`.
- **`list_models` (enabled-only, cost-sorted)** / **`find_model`** / **`suggest_model(TaskType)`** (8 task types → the first builtin Anthropic model tagged `best reasoning` / `balanced` / `fast` — today claude-opus-5-5 / claude-sonnet-5-5 / claude-haiku-5-5, else the first builtin Anthropic model — with reason + cost tier; no UI calls it yet) / **`validate_providers`**. _Support:_ commands `list_models`, `suggest_model`, `save_providers`, `get_default_providers`.
- **API keys & base-URL overrides stored separately** — keys/overrides live in `~/.octopush/settings.json` (`providerKeys`, `providerBaseUrls`), NOT in providers.json.
- **Claude Code version per model** — `agent_adapter::CLAUDE_MODEL_FLOORS` lists models a Claude Code CLI stage can only launch on a new enough CLI, as (normalized id, display name, oldest version), from the upstream model docs: `claude-fable-5-2` (Fable 5.2) needs 2.1.321, `claude-fable-5-1` (Fable 5.1) needs 2.1.257. `claude_model_floor` matches on `token_engine::normalize_model_id`, so gateway prefixes, dotted versions and dated snapshots count; `model_floor_note` picks the model needing the newest CLI the known version is below (an unknown version never matches). It drives the Direct launcher's amber "needs Claude Code" line (§4) and never blocks a run; a test keeps every row a normalized id and an `x.y.z`. _Support:_ `agent_adapter.rs`, command `claude_model_floor_note`.

### Provider/Model management UI (Settings → Models)
- **Model tiers** — Below the catalog: three provider-agnostic names — **Fast**, **Balanced**, **Strong** — each mapped to one configured model with a `ModelPicker` (+ clear ✕); each row's description names the aliases it answers to (`haiku`/`fast`, `sonnet`/`balanced`, `opus`/`strong`) in mono, like the intro (`TierDescription` turns the copy's backticked spans into `font-mono` spans), persisted read-modify-write as `settings.json` `modelTiers`. A sub-agent definition's `model: haiku` and an `Agent` call's `model: "fast"` both resolve here, so the same skill runs on whatever provider this machine uses; an unmapped tier falls back to a substring match over the configured ids. _Support:_ `settings/ModelTiersSection.tsx`, `settings.rs` (`model_tiers`), `skills/agents.rs` (`resolve_model_with_tiers`).
- **Master-detail editor** — Provider list + detail pane; an "Unsaved changes" bar appears when the working copy diverges; Save validates server-side then read-modify-writes settings.json (merging keys/baseUrls so it doesn't wipe other settings) and re-fetches models. _Support:_ `settings/ModelsPane.tsx`.
- **Provider detail** — local/cloud tag, API-key field (password + show/hide, hidden for local), Base URL field with a per-protocol endpoint hint ("Requests go to base URL + /v1/messages" or "+ /chat/completions"), Models list (`data-tour="settings-models-list"`; plain rows on one hairline, no frame per row: id, $in/out, ctx, and Edit/Remove as borderless quiet icon buttons with titles, shown on row hover or keyboard focus), "Bring in another model" (`data-tour="settings-models-add-model"`; ghost serif button — brass on this pane marks only the selected provider, the active nav item, the eyebrow and the unsaved bar's "Save changes"), "Reset to defaults" / "Remove". _Support:_ `ModelsPane.tsx`.
- **Add a provider (2-step wizard)** — Opened from "Connect another provider" under the provider list (`data-tour="settings-models-add-provider"`; ghost serif phrase — strong control edge (`border-octo-border-strong`, not the panel hairline), sage, ivory on hover — no plus glyph). Name, protocol (Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible), "Runs locally" toggle; step 2 base URL with a per-protocol placeholder + endpoint hint (Anthropic gateways: use the gateway's Anthropic root, e.g. `…/anthropic`). Step indicator is arabic (`1 · 2`), not Roman. _Support:_ `settings/AddProviderDialog.tsx`.
- **Add/Edit model dialog** — id (dedup-checked), displayName, inputCostPerM, outputCostPerM, maxContext; preserves non-edited fields. _Support:_ `settings/ModelDialog.tsx`.
- **Remove provider/model confirmation** — Routed through `ConfirmDialog`; removing a provider prunes its keys/baseUrls. _Support:_ `ModelsPane.tsx`.
- **Pricing refresh footer** — "Pricing · {relative time}" + spin-on-fetch refresh; refuses while there are unsaved edits; "Updated X of Y". _Support:_ `ModelsPane.tsx`.

### Pricing engine
- **In-process pricing table** — `builtin_prices(model) -> Option<ModelPrices>` (input / 5-min cache write / cache hit / output per million, from Anthropic's official pricing page, 2026-10-29; Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 2026-11-09): Fable 5.2 ($8 / $10 / $0.20 / $40) / 5.1 / 5, Mythos 5.2 (same as Fable 5.2; priced so its transcripts count, not in the catalog — limited availability), Opus 5.5 / 5 / 4.8 / 4.7 / 4.6 / 4.5 / 4.1 / 4, Sonnet 5.5 / 5 / 4.6 / 4.5 / 4, Haiku 5.5 / 4.5 / 3.5, GPT-6.1 Terra ($1 input / $1.25 cache write / $0.05 cached input / $5 output per million; writes at the default 30-minute retention, which is all Octopush requests — 12-hour writes are $2.50; OpenAI model and pricing pages, 2026-11-10), the rest of GPT-6 at the short-context input / 30-minute write / cached input / output columns of OpenAI's API pricing page (2026-11-17; the >272K-input long-context tier is a per-request tier, below): GPT-6.2 Astra ($8 / $10 / $0.40 / $40), GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.1 Sol ($2 / $2.50 / $0.10 / $10), GPT-6 Astra ($10 / $12.50 / $1 / $50), GPT-6 Sol ($2 / $2.50 / $0.20 / $10), GPT-6 Luna ($0.10 / $0.125 / $0.01 / $0.50) (GPT-6 Astra / Sol / Luna and GPT-6.1 Sol are not in the built-in catalog: their prices count for Codex stages and Claude Code sessions, and for Talk turns and API stages only once the model is added in Settings › Models), GPT-4o / 4o-mini (OpenAI model pages, 2026-11-08: cached input $1.25 / $0.075 per million; no cache-write charge, so writes cost the input price). **An unknown model is unpriced (`None`), never $0.** `cost_per_token` wraps the table (0.0 for unknown, legacy callers). Every builtin catalog model must match the table on every column, cache read and write included (`builtin_catalog_matches_pricing_table`; only explicitly free or local entries skip the cache columns), so OpenAI's `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` (split out of `prompt_tokens` as cache reads and cache writes by `openai_compat.rs`; Codex CLI stages split `cached_input_tokens` and `cache_write_input_tokens` out of `input_tokens` the same way in `codex_usage_from_event`) bill at the cached and cache-write rates on the catalog-first path too. The stale-price migration moves a GPT-6.1 Terra entry saved with writes at the input price ($1.00) to $1.25. A catalog entry with a $0 cache-write price and a non-zero input price (a model added in Settings → Models, e.g. through a LiteLLM gateway) bills its cache writes at the input price (`effective_write_per_m` in `prices_in`), so split-out OpenAI and Codex writes never bill at $0; an explicitly free model ($0 input) stays free. _Support:_ `token_engine.rs`.
- **1-hour cache writes** — `ModelPrices::cache_creation_1h_per_m` is 2× base input for every Claude model (pricing page, 2026-10-31; e.g. Fable 5.1 $20 vs $12.50 for 5-minute writes), derived by `one_hour_write_per_m` for the builtin table and catalog entries alike, so a user-edited input price scales it; non-Claude models price every write at the 5-minute rate. `one_hour_cache_writes` reads `usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` (clamped to `cache_creation_input_tokens`), and `cost_split` / `request_cost_split` / `cost_for_split` / `stage_cost_split` price that share at the 1-hour rate and the rest at the 5-minute rate. Applied to Claude Code transcript lines (`TranscriptUsage::cache_creation_1h_tokens`), the PTY `usage` block, and streamed `claude -p` usage (`CliUsage::cache_creation_1h_input_tokens`, used for the estimate when no `result` event arrives). Usage without the breakdown — and Octopush's own API calls, which only set 5-minute breakpoints — prices as before. The Haiku 5.5 long-prompt tier scales the 1-hour column too. _Support:_ `token_engine.rs`, `transcripts.rs`, `orchestrator/cli_runner.rs`, `orchestrator/cost.rs`.
- **Fast-mode pricing** — A Claude Code fast-mode request carries `usage.speed: "fast"` (`usage_speed`, `is_fast`). `fast_prices(model, base)` doubles every column of the model's standard price (input, output, cache hit, both cache-write TTLs — so the cache multipliers apply on top) for **Opus 5 and Opus 4.8** at $10/$50 per MTok (code.claude.com/docs/en/fast-mode, 2026-11-03) and **Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2** at $16/$80 (a cache hit $0.40, a 5-minute write $20, a 1-hour write $32; the fast-mode page and the pricing page's fast-mode table, 2026-11-26), dated, Bedrock and gateway spellings included through `normalize_model_id`; a user-edited catalog price scales with it. Fast mode on any other model (Opus 5.5 included, #473; Sonnet) is **unpriced**, never billed at the standard rate. `prices_at_speed` applies this on Claude Code transcript lines (`TranscriptUsage::speed`), the re-pricer (`RepriceCandidate::speed`, so a fast row stays unpriced instead of getting the standard rate), and the streamed-usage estimate of a DIRECT stage that stopped or timed out before its `result` event (`CliUsage::fast`, `cli_runner::streamed_cost`). A finished DIRECT stage keeps the CLI's own `total_cost_usd`. The ledger stores the request's speed in the nullable `spend_events.speed` column (`'fast'` / `'standard'`; NULL on older rows, rows without a reported speed, and aggregated rows such as DIRECT stages). Rows ingested before this change keep their standard-rate cost. _Support:_ `token_engine.rs`, `transcripts.rs`, `db.rs` (`SpendEvent::speed`, `plan_reprice`), `orchestrator/cli_runner.rs`.
- **Model id normalization** — `normalize_model_id` strips, in order: a `provider/` path prefix (LiteLLM `bedrock/…`, `anthropic/…`, `ollama/…`, an inference-profile ARN), a cross-region Bedrock prefix (`us.` / `eu.` / `apac.` / `global.` / `jp.` / `au.` / `ca.` / `us-gov.`) and `anthropic.`, `[1m]`-style suffixes, Vertex `@version`, a Bedrock version (`-v1:0`; a bare `-v1` only on an `anthropic.` id, so `deepseek-v3` stays), an Ollama `:tag`, and a trailing `-YYYYMMDD`; then, on a `claude-` id only, a `.` between digits becomes `-` (gateway aliases like `anthropic/claude-opus-4.8` → `claude-opus-4-8`; `qwen2.5-coder` and `gpt-4.1` stay exact). Lookups stay exact-match on the result, so `us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5-20261001-v1:0` and `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5-v1:0` price as their base model. Used by `find_model` (after an exact match) and the gateway reconciliation. _Support:_ `token_engine.rs`, `provider_router.rs::find_model`, `gateway::canonical_model`.
- **Per-request price tiers** — `long_prompt_tier(model)` is a per-model table of a prompt-token threshold and per-column multipliers (input, cache hit, cache write — both TTLs — and output), applied to the resolved base price so a user-edited catalog price scales. Haiku 5.5 bills 5× on every column (0.50 / 0.625 / 0.05 / 2.50) when one request's prompt (input + cache read + cache write) exceeds 100K tokens. Every GPT-6 model (GPT-6.2 Astra / Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra / Sol, GPT-6 Astra / Sol / Luna) bills OpenAI's long-context rates — 2× input, cached input and cache writes, 1.5× output, e.g. Terra $2 / $2.50 / $0.10 / $7.50 and GPT-6.2 Astra $16 / $20 / $0.80 / $60 — when one request's input (fresh + cached + written) exceeds 272,000 tokens (OpenAI's API pricing page, 2026-11-17); exactly 272,000 stays on the short tier. `request_prices` / `request_cost` / `request_cost_for` apply them on per-request paths: Talk director rounds (`record_request_in_thread`, `TurnUsage::add`), one-shot AI calls (`ai_complete`), Claude Code transcript lines, the PTY `usage` block, re-priced single-request ledger rows (`RepriceCandidate::single_request`), API-substrate DIRECT stages and Talk sub-agents (`run_agentic_loop` adds each response's cost to `AgenticResult::cost_usd` through `request_cost_for`; its mid-stage budget stop and `ask_stage` consultations use the same per-request figure; a sub-agent's ledger row takes each attempt's own `AgentAttempt::cost_usd` in `ChatEngine::record_subagent_spend`, so the conversation cost, Logbook and savings see the long tier), and the streamed estimate of a stopped, stalled or crashed Claude Code CLI stage (`streamed_estimate` prices each streamed `assistant` message, deduplicated by message id, through `request_cost_split`; `CliUsage::one_request` marks those messages). Two paths can still under-count a long-prompt request: a finished Claude Code CLI stage books Claude Code's own `total_cost_usd`, so it under-counts only if that figure leaves out the long tier; and a Codex CLI stage reports only turn totals (`turn.completed`), so it keeps the short tier. _Support:_ `token_engine.rs`, `db::plan_reprice`, `orchestrator/agentic.rs`, `orchestrator/cli_runner.rs`, `chat_engine.rs`.
- **Pricing authority & unpriced spend** — `prices_for(model)` = `prices_in(catalog(), model)`: a catalog entry is an explicit price, `$0` included (Ollama, or a model deliberately priced at zero); a `provider/model` id whose prefix names a **local** provider is free; then `builtin_prices`; else `None`. `catalog()` caches the loaded `ProviderRouter` per `providers.json` path and (mtime, size), so pricing never reloads/rewrites the file per lookup. A $0-with-tokens row of an unpriced model is stamped `cost_basis = 'unpriced'`: Talk/RUN/adhoc resolve the price in `TokenEngine` **before** the DB lock and pass the basis down (`record_token_spend_with_basis`; the DB layer does not load the catalog), DIRECT via `record_direct_spend` (cached lookup), Claude Code transcripts (prices resolved before the lock). **Unpriced usage is excluded from every saving:** `thread_cost` leaves it out of `baseline_usd` (Talk "saved vs all-strong") and reports `unpriced_calls` / `unpriced_models`; DIRECT `recompute_run_cost` leaves every stage that burned tokens at $0 out of the baseline (regardless of whether its model is priced now, so recomputing an old $0 run never counts it as 100% saved), and `retire_stage_cost` keeps $0 attempts out of the retired baseline counters; `estimate_run_cost` (pure `orchestrator::cost::estimate_run`) leaves unpriced stage models out of the range, the estimate and the baseline (their per-stage low/high are `null`, shown as "unpriced"); so the **Logbook** savings (`Σ max(baseline − cost, 0)` over runs) and **Cloud vs local** (savings come only from local-model tokens; an unknown model is cloud at $0) never count unpriced spend as saved. _Support:_ `token_engine.rs` (`catalog`, `prices_in`, `prices_for`, `is_priced`, `basis_for`, `ledger_cost_basis`), `db.rs` (`thread_cost`, `retire_stage_cost`, `usage_report`), `orchestrator/mod.rs::recompute_run_cost`, `orchestrator/cost.rs::estimate_run`, `commands.rs::estimate_run_cost`.
- **Ledger re-price & one-time migrations** — `commands::reprice_ledger` runs once at startup (`lib.rs` setup, background), after **Refresh pricing**, and from **Price them now** — one call at a time (`REPRICE_LEDGER_LOCK`, held for the whole check-run-set of each flag, so overlapping calls can't run a one-time pass twice and scale DIRECT stages twice). It resolves prices with one cached catalog load **outside** the DB lock (`db::plan_reprice`), then writes each batch in one savepoint (`apply_reprice`: per-row new costs, bulk `WHERE id IN (…)` re-classification — still-unknown → `'unpriced'`, now explicitly $0 → back to `'computed'`). Normally it scans only `'unpriced'` rows; the one-time passes are gated by `app_meta` flags: **`ledger_unpriced_classify_v1`** classifies legacy `'computed'` $0 rows (recorded before the ledger told unknown from free), and **`ledger_stale_price_fix_2026_10_v1`** corrects spend billed at the wrong builtin Opus 4.6 ($15/$75 → $5/$25) and Sonnet 5 ($3/$15 → $2/$10) prices — `'computed'` ledger rows are recomputed from their tokens, and DIRECT `run_stages` costs, run totals and (for runs whose reference model was one of them) baselines are scaled by the uniform correction factor (`db::fix_stale_direct_prices`; retired attempts carry no model and are left as they are). GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini (cached input billed at the full input price) are in that pass for fresh installs; installs that already ran it get a ledger-only pass for those two models under **`ledger_stale_price_fix_2026_11_gpt4o_v1`** (their change is not a uniform rescale, so DIRECT stages are never scaled). Each pass recomputes rows from stored tokens at the current price, so a re-run changes nothing. _Support:_ `commands.rs` (`reprice_ledger`, `fix_stale_prices`), `db.rs` (`reprice_candidates`, `stale_price_candidates`, `apply_reprice`, `fix_stale_direct_prices`, `RepriceCandidate`, `RepricePlan`).
- **Stale builtin price migration (catalog)** — On `ProviderRouter::load`, an on-disk model on **any** provider (builtin or custom) still carrying a known-wrong shipped default (`STALE_BUILTIN_PRICES`: Opus 4.6 at $15/$75 and Sonnet 5 at $3/$15, each also in the post-cache-backfill shape; GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini with cache read and write at $0) is reset to the current builtin price; any other value is a user edit and is kept. Newly shipped builtin models are backfilled at their builtin position (current models first), not appended. _Support:_ `provider_router.rs::migrate_stale_builtin_prices`.
- **Catalog location & deterministic lookup** — `providers.json` lives in `$OCTOPUSH_CONFIG_DIR` when set, else `~/.octopush` (`provider_router::config_path`); under `cfg(test)` a per-thread temp dir (`TestConfigDir`) or a per-process temp dir — tests never touch the real home. When two providers expose the same id, `find_model` picks deterministically: enabled first, the user's own providers before the builtins, then by name. _Support:_ `provider_router.rs`.
- **Cost computation (two paths)** — `compute_cost` (hardcoded table) and `compute_cost_with_prices` (explicit `ModelInfo` prices; non-Anthropic cache billed at input rate); `record` prefers the catalog-price path. _Support:_ `token_engine.rs`.
- **Pricing refresh from LiteLLM** — Fetches BerriAI/litellm's `model_prices_and_context_window.json`, converts per-token → per-million, updates matching model ids in providers.json by exact id, hot-reloads the router, stamps `last_pricing_refresh`. _Support:_ `commands.rs::refresh_pricing`.
- **Inline per-message cost preview** — `estimatePerMessageCost` (assumes 30% output ratio), `formatPerMessageCost`. _Support:_ `lib/cost.ts`.

### CLI agent adapters (`agent_adapter.rs`)
- **`AgentAdapter` trait** — `name`, `display_name`, `build_command(model, cwd)`, `parse_token_usage`, `supports_hot_swap`. _Support:_ `agent_adapter.rs`.
- **Claude Code adapter** — `claude --model <model>`; token parsing via `scan_pty_output`; no hot-swap. **Aider adapter** — `aider --model <model>`; parses "Tokens: N sent, N received"; hot-swap true. **Custom adapter** — arbitrary command/args. _Support:_ `agent_adapter.rs`.
- **Full Claude Code prompt for gateway-named Claude models (Direct CLI stages)** — Claude Code 2.1.330 gives an unrecognized model name the shorter system prompt, gateway names containing "sonnet" or "haiku" included. A Claude Code stage whose model normalizes (`token_engine::normalize_model_id`, the pricing engine's normaliser for dotted and prefixed ids) to a builtin Anthropic catalog id, but whose string isn't that canonical `claude-*` id (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`, `claude-haiku-4.5`, `bedrock/claude-haiku-4-5`, `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5-v1:0`; a `[1m]` suffix or a dated snapshot still counts as canonical), gets `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT=0`, so it keeps the full prompt Claude Code's tools were tuned for, and its launch line adds "· full Claude Code prompt (gateway name)". Canonical ids, non-Claude gateway models (local, Ollama, `claude-sonnet-latest` and other names no catalog id matches) and Codex stages get nothing; a value the user's login-shell env already sets is never overridden. Set on fresh and `--resume` runs alike through `apply_stage_env`. _Support:_ `cli_runner.rs` (`system_prompt_env`, `stage_system_prompt_env`, `system_prompt_label`, `SIMPLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT_ENV`); contract tests in `claude_code_contract.rs`.
- **Adapter registry** — `list_adapters` → `AdapterInfo`. **`switch_agent`** — updates the session's `agent.model` in the DB; if a PTY is running the new model takes effect on restart (no live hot-swap yet). _Support:_ `commands.rs`.

### Token engine
- **`TokenEvent` schema** — `{session_id, timestamp, input/output/cache_read/cache_creation_tokens, model, cost_usd}`; the transport shape passed to `record`. Persisted into the canonical `spend_events` ledger (not the retired `token_events` table). _Support:_ `token_engine.rs`, `db.rs`.
- **`TokenEngine::record(event, surface)`** — Computes cost if 0 (catalog-aware), then writes one `spend_events` row via `record_token_spend` (surface + namespace-derived workspace/project/source attribution — no more `session_id` overload), and increments the legacy session aggregate. _Support:_ `token_engine.rs`, `db::record_token_spend`.
- **Three recording modes** — **API usage** (authoritative): chat engine + `ai_complete` + DIRECT stages record real counts. **Claude Code transcripts (RUN, authoritative)**: `transcripts::TranscriptIngestor` reads `~/.claude/projects/<cwd, non-alphanumerics → '-'>/**/*.jsonl` for every RUN session's `project_root` and every workspace worktree (as written and canonicalized; Claude Code use elsewhere on the machine is not Octopush spend) — and, since Claude Code caps that directory name at **200 characters** and appends `-<hash>` to a longer one, a long worktree path (a ticket-titled worktree gets there easily) is resolved to the capped directory too (`project_dirs_for` / `project_dirs_among` over one listing per pass: the exact name when it exists, plus an existing `<first 200>-<hash>` directory **whose transcripts say they were written from that cwd** — two long paths can share their first 200 characters and the hash is Claude Code's, so a capped directory is claimed by its lines' `cwd`, never by its name; the PTY scanner's `has_transcript_dir` uses the same resolution), takes each `type:"assistant"` line's `message.model` + `usage` (input · cache read · cache write · output), folds the per-content-block lines of one message into one row keyed **`cc:<requestId>`** (globally unique — a `--resume`d session rewriting old turns adds nothing; `cc:msg:<id>` without a request id) and **updates** that row when a later block of the same message lands after the poll (`upsert_spend_event_by_key`), prices it through `prices_for` (once per model per pass) — a fast-mode line (`usage.speed: "fast"`) at the fast-mode rate, or unpriced on a model without one (see **Fast-mode pricing**), with its speed stored on the row — attributes it to the most recently active session on that root (`source_id`) and/or the workspace/project, stamps the **mission that existed at the message's timestamp** (`mission_for_workspace_at`), and records surface `run`. **Direct stages are never metered twice:** a Direct Claude CLI stage's `claude -p` session writes its transcript into the same worktree directory, but its spend is already the stage's `direct` row — so every session id a stage attempt reports is kept for good in `direct_cli_sessions(session_id, run_id, stage_id, created_at)` (`record_direct_cli_session`, called by the drive for every attempt and by `set_stage_session`; `run_stages.session_id` is overwritten per attempt), and the ingestor skips that session's file and every sub-agent file under `<session>/` (`direct_session_of`). A file an earlier pass already read (mid-stage, before the id was known, or before #861) is re-read once and its `run` rows deleted by request key (`drop_direct_file` → `delete_run_spend_by_keys`; `direct` rows are never touched), then its offset dropped so later passes skip it unread. The drive does this itself the moment a stage attempt reports its session id (`transcripts::drop_direct_session`, called beside `record_direct_cli_session` in `run_stage_once`; it looks for `<session>.jsonl` and `<session>/**` in every project directory), before the stage's `direct` row and the next budget check (on the blocking pool, `spawn_blocking`, #890) — so `check_budget`, the Talk entry gate and the AI-review gate no longer wait up to 60s for the next pass to see the duplicate go (#863). A pass whose snapshot of Direct sessions predates the stage's report can't put those rows back: `ingest_file` re-checks the file's session against `direct_cli_sessions` under the DB lock, inside its savepoint, and writes nothing (not even the offset) for a Direct session (`Db::any_direct_cli_session`, #890). The drive records the session before it drops, so either that check sees it, or the pass's rows land first and the drop removes them. If the drop itself fails (logged, never fatal to the stage), the rows stay until the next pass removes them, so the gates can briefly see that stage counted twice. A one-time migration (`direct_cli_sessions_backfill_v1`) seeds the table from `run_stages.session_id` and `session_usage`, so duplicates recorded before the fix are removed on the next pass. A background pass that inserted or removed rows emits `octo://spend-ingested` (`ipc.onSpendIngested`), and `useMissionLogbook` re-reads on it. Session counters and the Logbook activity span move only for messages from the last 10 minutes — historical rows never fake activity now. Files are read incrementally from a per-file byte offset (`app_meta` `cc_transcript:<path>`; a partial trailing line waits; non-UTF-8 bytes are lossily decoded; a file that fails is logged and skipped without stopping the pass), each file's rows in one savepoint, polled every 60s in the background and (throttled to 30s, fire-and-forget) whenever the Usage page reads. **PTY scraping** (fallback): `scan_pty_output` matches an embedded `usage` JSON block or a Claude-Code "Total cost: …" summary line — matched against the text as the screen shows it, since Claude Code's TUI places words with cursor moves (`ESC[<col>G`) instead of spaces (`token_engine::screen_text`, only for a chunk that contains `Total`) — model `unknown`, cache 0; the summary is the session's running total, so a repeat (a second `/cost`, a redraw) records nothing and a larger total records only the difference (last total per source in `app_meta` `pty_scan_total:<id>`; a lower one is a new `claude` run and counts whole) — and **never double-counts a transcript-metered run**: the scanner drops the event when the source's cwd (a session's root or a terminal's worktree, `run_cwd_for_source`) has a Claude Code transcript directory or the source is flagged `transcript_seen:<id>` (every session on the root and every terminal of the workspace is flagged on each pass), and the first time a cwd's transcripts are read, its already-scraped rows from that point on are deleted (`delete_scraped_run_spend`) — the exact rows supersede the scrape, on upgrade too. Terminal scrapes are attributed to the terminal's workspace at write time (`record_token_spend` resolves `terminals → workspace`), so they count against workspace/project budgets and show under the workspace's name. _Support:_ `chat_engine.rs`, `commands.rs`, `token_engine.rs`, `transcripts.rs` (`parse_transcript_line`, `read_new_entries`, `project_dir_name`, `project_dirs_for`, `has_transcript_dir`, `direct_session_of`, `drop_direct_file`, `drop_direct_session`), `AppState.transcripts`, `lib.rs` setup poll, `db.rs` (`upsert_spend_event_by_key`, `insert_spend_event_if_new`, `delete_scraped_run_spend`, `list_workspace_paths`, `workspace_by_path`, `session_ids_for_root`, `terminal_ids_for_workspace`, `run_cwd_for_source`, `mission_for_workspace_at`, `direct_cli_sessions`, `record_direct_cli_session`, `direct_cli_session_ids`, `delete_run_spend_by_keys`).
- **Canonical spend ledger (`spend_events`, Phase 2)** — A dedicated ledger table with an explicit `surface` (`talk`/`run`/`direct`/`review`/`adhoc`), denormalized `project_id`/`workspace_id` (project attribution survives a workspace deletion), `provider_cost_usd`/`computed_cost_usd` + `cost_basis`, and an `idempotency_key` (dedupe via `INSERT OR IGNORE`). **DIRECT run spend is now recorded here** — `complete_run_stage` mirrors each stage completion into the ledger **with its cache split** (`StageOutcome.cache_read_tokens` / `cache_creation_tokens`, from the API loop's `AgenticResult` or the CLI stream's `CliUsage`; one row per completion, so every re-run/looped attempt stays counted), fixing the gap where orchestrator spend was invisible to Usage and budgets. Accepting a halted stage's partial work re-closes it through `accept_run_stage_partial` (status/artifact only) so the attempt's spend is not mirrored a second time. A one-shot migration backfills historical DIRECT runs from `run_stages`. TALK/RUN/REVIEW still write `token_events`; the **`all_spend` SQL view** unions both so every Usage/budget reader sees the complete picture. _Support:_ `db.rs` (`spend_events`, `all_spend`, `insert_spend_event`, `record_direct_spend`).
- **`token_report`** — `TokenReport{total_input/output/cached, total_cost, cost_by_session, cost_by_model, hourly_trend, budget_remaining, projected_daily_cost}`, read from the `all_spend` view (so DIRECT is included in totals, cost-by-model, trend, and projection). _Support:_ `db.rs`; `get_token_report`; `tokenStore.ts`.
- **Per-session token budget (legacy)** — `budget_status(session_id)` token-count gauge; `set_token_budget`. _Support:_ `token_engine.rs`.
- **Session export** — `export_session_json`/`export_session_csv`. _Support:_ `commands.rs`.

### Budgets (dollar-based, scoped, enforced)
- **`BudgetRow` schema** — `{scope_type, scope_id, period, limit_usd}` keyed unique on (scope, id, period). Scopes: `global`/`workspace`/`project`; periods: `daily`/`monthly`. _Support:_ `db.rs`; `list_budgets`/`set_budget`/`clear_budget`.
- **`period_spend`** — Sums `cost_usd` + tokens since start of the day/month in the user's **local** timezone (F13: budgets reset at local midnight, not 00:00 UTC) per scope. _Support:_ `db.rs` (`period_since_utc`); `current_spend`.
- **`check_budget` (backend gate)** — Given a workspace, checks global + its project + workspace budgets × daily/monthly against `period_spend`; returns the first breached scope or `Allow`. The single backend enforcement primitive. **`budget_headroom`** reads the same budgets: the smallest `limit − spent` among them, never below zero, `None` with no budget set — what Talk's sub-agents split as their spend limits. _Support:_ `db.rs::check_budget`, `budget_headroom`, `BudgetVerdict`.
- **Backend budget enforcement (REVIEW)** — `ai_complete` (AI review / conflict / commit-draft — previously ungated) blocks up front via `check_budget`, returning `AppError::BudgetExceeded` (`kind == "BudgetExceeded"`, with scope/spent/limit). _Support:_ `commands.rs::ai_complete`, `error.rs`.
- **Budgets store** — Caches spend per `scope:id:period`, tracks `notifiedThresholds`, `overrideActive`. _Support:_ `budgetsStore.ts`.
- **Hard-cap enforcement** — Before a TALK send, `isOverBudget("workspace") || isOverBudget("global")` blocks with `BUDGET_CAP_MSG`; a one-shot per-turn Override. _Support:_ `chatStore`, `budgetsStore`.
- **Threshold warning toasts (50/80/100%)** — On each finished stream, fires once per (scope:period:threshold). _Support:_ `App.tsx`.
- **Budgets UI (Settings → Usage)** — "Add a budget" (scope/period/limit), grouped rows with inline-editable limit, "Spent: $X · N%", a tinted progress bar, Remove. _Support:_ `settings/UsagePane.tsx`.

### Usage analytics & charts (Settings → Usage)
- **One report, one period, one mode** — The page reads a single `get_usage_report(start, end, surface?, utcOffsetMinutes)` (`db::usage_report`, straight from `spend_events`) every 10s. **Period** segmented control: Today · 7 days · 30 days · This month · Custom (From/To date inputs, whole local days; an inverted range falls back to 30 days) — presets start at local midnight and end now; the page opens on **Today**. Every request carries a sequence number and an answer that is not the latest request's is dropped (report and gateway alike), so switching from a slow period to a fast one never shows the slow period's figures when they land last; the gateway section empties on a period change rather than show the previous period's; the cloud-vs-local breakdown rides the report's sequence. **Mode** segmented control: All · Talk · Run · Review · Direct — scopes every section; the "By mode" cards toggle the same filter (`aria-pressed`). Day buckets and the active-day count follow the viewer's calendar (`utc_offset_minutes` applied in SQL), not UTC's. The analytics crossfade (`.octo-fade-in`) on a period/mode change (budgets/export sit outside the keyed subtree, so an open budget dialog survives); the range is recomputed on every 10s poll, so a preset's end moves with the clock and "Today" rolls over at midnight. **While the ledger is read** the page keeps its shape: before the first answer `UsageSkeleton` lays out a ledger with spend in its real order — the headline stats (real labels, quiet bars for the figures), four By mode cards, the trend panel, three Where it went rows, two By model rows and the Tokens panel (real row labels and note) — with the Claude plan card, Budgets and Export below as usual, and the figures crossfade in (`.octo-fade-in`). Each placeholder is built from the same class strings as the section that replaces it (shared shell constants, `Stat`/`Row` themselves; the figures are invisible text behind a quiet `bg-octo-panel-2` bar, so each line keeps its real height), and a test checks the shells match. Only the row counts are a guess: a ledger with more or fewer sources or models, no trend, or the pricing/unpriced notices still moves what sits below by that difference. After a period/mode change the previous figures stay until the new answer lands (stale-while-revalidate, tracked by `reportKey`). Both cases show a mono `reading the ledger…` status in the filter bar. Its slot stays mounted and fades out, so the bar never shifts. A failed read belongs to the filter it was asked for: it shows its error row and no status, and before any report it shows no skeleton either (the 10s poll retries); switching period or mode after an error hides that error and shows the status (and the skeleton, if nothing has loaded) while the new read is on its way. _Support:_ `UsagePane.tsx` (`periodRange`, `UsageSkeleton`; `data-tour="usage-headline"`), `commands::get_usage_report`, `db.rs::usage_report` + `UsageReport`/`UsageSlice`/`SurfaceUsage`/`ModelUsage`/`SourceUsage`/`UsageTrendPoint`, `ipc.getUsageReport`.
- **Gateway reconciliation (LiteLLM) — what the gateway billed against what the ledger recorded** — When a provider's base URL fronts an LLM gateway, the gateway is the only party that sees every request: Claude Code's service calls (titles, summaries, on the small model) and its prompt-cache upkeep (full cached context, near-zero output, sub-second) are billed there but never written to its transcripts, so RUN can only account for the turns; and a gateway-side **key budget** is what a provider 429 `budget_exceeded` refers to. The Usage page therefore shows a **Gateway** section (`GatewaySection`, `usage-gateway`) whenever one is detected: eyebrow `Gateway · LiteLLM · <host>` with the gap on the right (`$2.57 · 26% not in the ledger`, or `in step with the ledger`), three stats — **Gateway billed** (requests · tokens, cache included), **In the ledger** (the ledger's rows for the models the gateway served, all four token buckets), **Not in the ledger** (gateway minus ledger, share of billed) — a **key budget** line when the gateway enforces one (`Key budget exhausted · $7061 of $5400 · resets …`, rouge when over; tooltip: a provider 429 “budget exceeded” refers to this figure, not an Octopush budget), per-model rows (`gateway N · ledger N`, gateway cost, `+$gap` in brass), and, when the gateway's request logs were readable, the **unmatched requests** line (`39 gateway requests match no ledger row ($2.57): 25 × claude-sonnet-5 $2.15 · 14 × kimi …`) — each gateway request id matched against every id the ledger's rows carry: the request id a RUN row is keyed on (`cc:<request id>` / `cc:msg:<id>`, bare) and the provider's message id recorded beside it (`spend_events.provider_msg_id`, written by the transcript ingester; NULL on rows ingested before it existed). Through a gateway, Claude Code gets no `request-id` header, so RUN rows are keyed on the message id the gateway minted (`msg_bdrk_…`, unique per call). Ledger models with no gateway counterpart are left out and named (`Not compared: local-llm`); a reading with no model breakdown at all is compared against the whole ledger instead. The comparison is always **every mode**: the gateway saw every request, so the page's Mode filter neither scopes nor re-fetches the section, which says so when the filter is on (`Compared against every mode, not only the one selected above.`). On the `key` basis the gateway's figure is a running total since the key's last reset, so no gap is computed or coloured. **Detection, not configuration:** every enabled cloud provider with a key — the settings file's, else the provider's env var (`api_key_env`), as the calls resolve it — is probed once (its base URL as the calls use it, in any shape the Anthropic adapter accepts: `…`, `…/anthropic`, `…/v1`, `…/anthropic/v1/messages`; first-party hosts and localhost are never probed), the result — positive or negative — cached 10 minutes; the gateway's answer per period (start, and end to the minute — a preset's end moves with the clock) cached 60s, so the page's 10s poll asks the gateway at most once a minute; a provider or settings save (`save_providers`, `save_settings`) invalidates both. A gateway that is down or unreadable hides the section, never fails the page. **Four readings, best first** (`basis`): `logs` — `GET /spend/logs?api_key=<hash>&start_date&end_date&summarize=false` (a day wide on each side, cut to the instant; failed requests excluded), per request — without `summarize=false` the endpoint's legacy default answers per-day totals, which are recognised and never mistaken for an empty log; a log LiteLLM cut to its 10,000 most recent rows (`x-litellm-spend-logs-truncated`) carries a lower-bound note; `daily` — `GET /user/daily/activity?api_key=<hash>` (the tables are keyed on whole UTC days whatever is asked, with a caveat in the section; `successful_requests` when reported, zero included, else `api_requests`); `daily` again from the per-day summary a deployment too old to know `summarize` answered to the first request (spend per model per day, no request counts or tokens) when the daily tables gave nothing; `key` — only `GET /key/info`'s running total, with no period. A readable reading that reports nothing is shown as a quiet period (`The gateway logged no requests for this key in the period.`), never as "running total only". The eyebrow also names a ledger above the gateway (`$14.08 in the ledger the gateway did not bill`) rather than calling the two sides in step. `GET /key/info` answering with an `info` object is what identifies LiteLLM (key hash `token`, alias, spend, `max_budget`, `budget_reset_at`). **Model parity, gateway-agnostic, three ways best first:** the name the gateway says the client *asked for* is the ledger's own name, so a gateway that records it (LiteLLM: `model_group` per log row, `breakdown.model_groups` per day) is compared on it; an **equivalence learned from a matched request** — a gateway id found in a ledger row pairs the two names whatever either side calls the model, remembered per gateway kind in `app_meta` (`gateway_alias:<kind>:<canonical gateway name>` → canonical ledger name, `GatewayReconciliation.learned_aliases`, `db::meta_list_prefix` / `meta_set_many`, best effort) and applied to aggregates and unmatched rows from then on — only an unambiguous lesson is kept: a gateway name pairing with two ledger models in the period teaches nothing, a known name is never overwritten, a row with no model name (`unknown`) is not a name; and last the canonical form (last path segment, then the catalog's normalization: `bedrock/eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` ≡ `claude-sonnet-5`). No vendor-specific suffix rule is needed for parity. The daily reading is started in the background while the logs are read, so it is already under way when the logs turn out empty or unreadable, and is dropped unread when they suffice. **Extensible:** `gateway::SpendGateway` is the contract (`identify`, `spend`), `gateway::gateways()` the registry — a new gateway is one file and one line. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/gateway/mod.rs` (`SpendGateway`, `GatewayIdentity`, `GatewaySpend`, `reconcile`, `GatewayCache`, `detect`, `canonical_model`), `gateway/litellm.rs` (`root_url`, `parse_key_info`, `parse_spend_logs`, `parse_spend_summary`, `parse_daily_activity`), `commands::get_gateway_reconciliation`, `db::ledger_ids_with_model_between` + `db::set_spend_provider_msg_id`, `transcripts::TranscriptUsage.message_id`, `AppState.gateways`, `settings/GatewaySection.tsx` (`gapSummary`, `budgetLine`), `UsagePane.tsx`, `ipc.getGatewayReconciliation`, `types.GatewayReconciliation`. _Entry:_ Settings › Usage, after the Tokens section, when a provider's base URL is a LiteLLM proxy.
- **Honest cache hit ratio** — `cache_read ÷ (input + cache_read + cache_write)`: the share of prompt tokens served from cache. A cache **write is a miss** (billed at a premium, only repaid by a later read), and a slice whose rows never reported cache tokens shows **"—"** with "no cache data reported" rather than a fake 0% (`cache_tracked`). The previous figure divided read+write by input+output and could exceed 100%. Every card, model row and source row carries its own ratio with the formula in a tooltip; the **Tokens** section splits *Input, uncached · Cache read · Cache write · Output*. _Support:_ `db.rs::cache_hit_pct`, `UsagePane.tsx` (`HIT_TITLE`).
- **What every request carries (backend, #959)** — `get_request_context(projectId)` answers, per project, the fixed context Claude Code sends on every request and what it costs; the Settings › Usage section that shows it follows in a second PR. **Measured total:** the smallest first main-thread request (input + cache read + cache write; inline sub-agent lines skipped) over the project's 20 most recently written session transcripts — its root and every workspace worktree, as written and canonicalized; Direct stages' CLI sessions (`direct_cli_sessions`) and sub-agent files left out. It is an upper bound on the fixed part (it still holds one short first message). **Price:** at the model of most first requests — `uncachedUsd` at its input price (per-request tiers applied), `usualUsd` at the input-side rate (input, cache reads, cache writes; output excluded; fast-mode requests excluded) its requests in those sessions actually paid per prompt token — and `cacheHitPct` of those sessions (`db::cache_hit_pct`); both prices `null` for an unpriced model, never $0. **Items, each an estimate** (bytes ÷ 4, rounded up; no tokenizer, no `count_tokens`, nothing leaves the Mac): the CLAUDE.md chain (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, then every ancestor directory top-down to the project's `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, each followed by its `@path` imports outside code fences up to 5 deep, each file once — `AGENTS.md` counts only when imported; read by the same resolver Talk uses, `request_context::memory_chain`: the directories from the project up to the outermost git work tree enclosing it are the repository's, and what a file that resolves in there imports or links to must stay inside the nearest work tree around that file, so an import or symlink out of it is left out unread, like a file over 4 MiB; the user's files, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and those of the directories above every enclosing work tree, may import from anywhere; the answer lists the files left out as `skipped: [{ label, path, reason }]`, at most 20, and counts the rest in `moreSkipped`), **Skills** (name + description of every `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`, project then user, project shadowing) and **Agents** (the same for `.claude/agents/*.md`), each read by the skills or agents reader itself (`skills::scan_skills_in`, `skills::agents::scan_agent_files_in`), so a file that reader skips is not counted. Fitted to the measured total: scaled down to add up to it when they exceed it, otherwise the rest is one **MCP and built-in tools, by difference** row (MCP servers are never started or contacted). Ranked largest first; with no transcript the raw estimates stand and the total is `null`. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/request_context.rs` (`request_context`, `apportion`, `memory_files`, `memory_imports`, `skills_item`, `agents_item`, `session_files`, `first_request`), `commands::get_request_context`, `ipc.getRequestContext`, `types.RequestContext` / `CarriedItem`.
- **Headline stats** — **Cost** (calls · tokens under it), **Per active day** (cost ÷ local days that had any spend — replaces the old "Projected / day", which was last-hour × 24 and read $0 whenever the last hour was quiet), **Last 24 hours** (rolling, independent of the period), **Cache hit**. An **unpriced calls** line appears when `cost_basis = 'unpriced'` rows exist (a model the catalog did not know, or had no price for, when it ran — left out of totals and savings, not counted as free; a local model's $0, a subscription-covered or provider-reported $0 is a real price, not a gap) with a **Price them now** phrase (`reprice_spend` → `db::reprice_unpriced`: every `'unpriced'` or legacy `'computed'` row at $0 with tokens is re-priced with `prices_for` as the catalog stands; rows whose model is still unpriced stay at $0 and are marked `'unpriced'`; toast with the count). **Refresh pricing** does the same automatically after the fetch (`RefreshPricingResult.eventsRepriced`, mentioned in its toast) — so a model assigned before its price was fetched (the $0.00 Opus rows) is priced on the next refresh, not lost. _Support:_ `UsagePane.tsx`; `UsageReport.perActiveDayUsd` / `last24hUsd` / `unpricedCalls`.
- **Organization pricing note (#1111)** — When this Mac's managed Claude Code settings carry a `modelPricing` table (managed scope only, Claude Code 2.1.242+), a muted line under the headline says so: `Your organization set Claude Code's rates on this Mac (0.85× every cost · own rates for claude-sonnet-4-6).`, that a finished Claude Code stage is booked at Claude Code's own figure (`total_cost_usd`), which uses those rates, as does a stage's `--max-budget-usd` cap, while Talk, stopped, stalled or crashed stages and the all-premium savings baseline use list prices (so totals, budgets and savings can mix the two bases), and that rates set from the admin console aren't visible to Octopush. Its tooltip lists each override row (`claude-sonnet-4-6: $2.4 in · $12 out · $0.24 cache read · $3 cache write per MTok`). Read once when the page opens; hidden with no table or when the read fails. Nothing is re-priced and the cap is unchanged. **Reader (read-only):** the configuration profile `/Library/Managed Preferences/com.anthropic.claudecode.plist` (through `/usr/bin/plutil -convert json -o -`, ignored when absent or unconvertible), then `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json` and every `managed-settings.d/*.json` by name (hidden, non-`.json` and non-object files skipped), merged like Claude Code: a later file replaces a single value and merges nested blocks key by key, so `overrides` merges per model ID. Between the profile and the files, the default `managedSourcesBehavior: "first-wins"` uses only the first source that sets any policy key (`managedSourcesBehavior` and `wslInheritsWindowsSettings` don't count); under `"merge"` the higher-ranked source's `modelPricing` applies. A `multiplier` outside (0, 10] is dropped, and so is an override row missing one of `input`/`output`/`cacheRead`/`cacheWrite` or with a rate outside 0–10000 USD/MTok; the rest is kept. Remote (server-managed) settings come first in Claude Code's order and can't be seen. _Support:_ `agent_adapter.rs` (`parse_model_pricing`, `merge_managed_files`, `managed_model_pricing`, `read_managed_settings_files`, `read_managed_model_pricing`, `ModelPricing`/`ModelRates`), `commands::managed_model_pricing`, `ipc.managedModelPricing`, `settings/ManagedPricingNote.tsx` (`data-tour="usage-managed-pricing"`); contract fixtures `tests/fixtures/claude-code/2.1.242/`.
- **By mode** — One card per surface with spend in the period (Talk / Run / Review / Direct / Ad hoc; empty state "Nothing billed in this period."): cost, a share-of-total bar in the mode's colour, `N calls · tokens · hit %`. One stable hue per mode across the page (`surfaceColor` over `useChartColors().series`). _Support:_ `UsagePane.tsx`.
- **Cost by hour / by day** — Recharts area of cost per bucket: hourly for a window of ≤48h, daily beyond (`trend_bucket`); tooltip shows cost and tokens. _Support:_ `UsagePane.tsx`; `UsageReport.trend`.
- **Where it went** — Replaces the truncated-id bar chart: one row per workspace (TALK/REVIEW/DIRECT and RUN sessions opened on a worktree) or RUN session, **labelled by its full name** (tooltip carries it; the raw id only when nothing is named — "unattributed"), with `workspace · <project>` / `run session`, last activity, `N calls · tokens · hit %`, cost, and a **stacked per-mode bar** (width relative to the top spender; a legend appears when more than one mode is present). Top 25 by cost. _Support:_ `UsagePane.tsx` (`SourceRow`); `db.rs::usage_report` `by_source` (`COALESCE(workspace_id, terminal's workspace, source_id)` LEFT-joined to workspaces, sessions and projects, plus a per-(source, surface) split).
- **By model** — Rows with the model id, `calls · tokens · hit %`, cost and a share bar. A model whose calls are all unpriced reads **unpriced** (muted) instead of "$0.00", with a tooltip naming the model; a model with some unpriced calls keeps its figure and says how many are unpriced in the tooltip. _Support:_ `UsagePane.tsx`, `lib/cost.ts::modelCostCell`; `UsageReport.byModel[].unpricedCalls`.
- **Stale-pricing nudge** — When the LiteLLM pricing catalog is older than 14 days (or was never refreshed) a quiet warning row explains costs may be off and offers **Refresh pricing** (calls `refresh_pricing`, toasts the count, reloads). `pricing_refreshed_at` rides on the report from `settings.last_pricing_refresh`. _Support:_ `UsagePane.tsx` (`pricingAgeDays`, `PRICING_STALE_DAYS`).
- **Cloud vs local** — Shown only when local models produced tokens in the period: Cloud spend, Local volume, Est. savings (`get_usage_breakdown` over the same range). Savings come only from local-model tokens (resolved through `find_model`, so tagged Ollama ids count as local); unpriced usage is cloud at $0 and is never counted as saved. _Support:_ `UsagePane.tsx`.
- **Claude plan card** — Shown only once a Claude Code stage on a Claude Pro/Max plan has reported (§4 "Claude plan windows"): one row per window (5-hour, weekly, per-model weekly, any kind Claude Code adds later), with used % (or `limit reached` / `reset since`), a bar in sage / amber (≥ 80%) / rouge (rejected), `resets <time> · as of <age>` and `using extra usage` when the CLI says so; the same calm warning as the Companion line near a limit. Row names in the body face; the bar's width eases with the canonical `--ease-octo`. Drops week-stale windows like the Companion line (hidden once none is left). Loads on mount and reloads on `plan://updated` (no poll; a 30s clock keeps ages and `reset since` true). Plan-covered spend is not relabelled yet (still priced at API rates). _Support:_ `settings/ClaudePlanCard.tsx`, `lib/claudePlan.ts`, `stores/claudePlanStore.ts`; `get_claude_plan` (`data-tour="usage-claude-plan"`).
- **Budgets** — The Budgets section (above) now sits below the analytics. _Support:_ `UsagePane.tsx`.
- **CSV export ("Export ledger")** — Exports **the selected period** via `exportTokenEventsCsv` → save dialog (no separate date pickers). _Support:_ `UsagePane.tsx`; `export_token_events_csv`.
- **Legacy `get_token_report`** — Still serves the session sidebar / App total (`tokenStore`); the Usage page no longer reads it.

### Model picker / switcher
- **ModelPicker** — Chip dropdown (provider-color dot): optional **Auto** row pinned on top (`autoOption`, Talk composer only — the economy director, see §"Auto policy"), Local-only filter, Recommended (depth/speed/cost), Recents (last 3), per-provider groups with `$in/$out · ctx` + tag pills; optional `allowedProviders` (e.g. CLI stages → Anthropic). The catalog is shared (`providersStore`) and live: a model added or edited in Settings › Models shows up without a remount — Settings refreshes the store after saving, and the picker re-reads the catalog (and the tier map) every time it opens. _Support:_ `ModelPicker.tsx`, `stores/providersStore.ts`. _Entry:_ TALK composer, Direct stage flow.
- **ModelSwitcher** — Titlebar popover grouped by provider with a cost badge ($/$$/$$$) + meta; selecting calls `switchAgent`. _Support:_ `ModelSwitcher.tsx`. _Entry:_ titlebar. (Its old `⌘⇧M` binding was retired; `⌘⇧M` now opens Mission Control.)

### "Zero wasted tokens / cost savings" value proposition
- **All-premium savings baseline** — Savings computed against the priciest configured model for the tokens actually used; `savingsVsBaseline` floored at $0; `aggregateSavings` across runs. _Support:_ `lib/runStatus.ts`.
- **TALK conversation cost** — "saved vs all-strong · $X · N%" under "spent $X", from the ledger. _Support:_ `CompanionContext.tsx`, `db::thread_cost`.
- **Direct run ledger** — "{pct}% under all-premium"; completion "This run saved $X…". _Support:_ `RunLedger.tsx`.
- **Grouped currency figures** — Amounts read with thousands separators ("$85,393.45", never "$85393.45") through one formatter, `formatUsd` (`Intl.NumberFormat` en-US, two decimals), in the Direct Companion (Runs ledger, run rows, current run), the run ledger strip, Mission Control (fleet ledger, card spend and saving, "While you were away"), the launcher estimate, the run track's stage cards, the stage focus sheet, the halt bar, the run history sheet, the Logbook (room, card and Markdown export), Settings › Usage (cost chart tooltip, budget limit and spend), the Companion's budget rows, Logbook mission line and crew journal, Talk's conversation cost (spent, sub-agents, saved vs all-strong), the Talk message footer, the PR composer's draft cost, the Talk crew card, the "Crew finished" notification and the budget toasts. The backend's budget messages (the "budget reached — $1,234.50 of $1,000.00 spent" journal notices, a budget-stop halt, the budget-exceeded error) group the same way through `token_engine::format_usd`. Settings › Usage totals keep their page rule (cents under $100, whole dollars from there) and are grouped too ("$12,843"). Only the sub-cent branch keeps its own precision: under a cent, Talk's cost lines and message footer show three decimals ("$0.004") and the PR composer's draft cost four. _Support:_ `lib/cost.ts::formatUsd`, `CompanionContext.tsx::usd`, `settings/shared.tsx::usd`; `lib/cost.lint.test.ts` fails on any `$${x.toFixed(2)}` outside `cost.ts`.
- **Local-model savings estimate** — `usage_breakdown` classifies cloud/local and estimates local savings at the blended (input+output)/2 rate of the **cheapest enabled non-local model in the catalog** (falls back to ~$0.21/M if none), instead of a stale hardcoded constant. _Support:_ `db.rs::usage_breakdown`.
- **Tagline** — "The IDE for agentic developers — eight arms, zero wasted tokens." _Support:_ `settings/AboutPane.tsx`.

### Notable implementation details
- **Two protocols, not N vendors** — Adding any vendor/gateway means choosing `anthropic` or `openai-compatible`; no per-vendor code.
- **Two stores split** — providers.json (catalog incl. pricing/context) vs settings.json (`providerKeys`, `providerBaseUrls`, `last_pricing_refresh`). Keys never leave the device except in requests to providers.
- **Token-event schema** — one canonical `spend_events` ledger holds **all** surfaces (TALK/RUN/REVIEW/DIRECT) with explicit `surface` + denormalized project/workspace attribution + `source_id` + idempotency; the `all_spend` view reads it (projecting `session_id = COALESCE(workspace_id, source_id)`), and project-scope budgets/savings join `all_spend → workspaces`. The old `token_events` table is retired to read-only history (migrated in via a one-shot backfill).
- **Budget enforcement points** — TALK is now gated on **both** sides: the client pre-send fast-path (workspace/global + one-shot override) **and** an authoritative backend `check_budget` gate in `send_chat_message` (also enforces project-scope budgets the client can't see, and catches direct-IPC bypass; the client threads an `overrideBudget` flag so a conscious per-turn override skips it, and a backend `BudgetExceeded` — `isBudgetExceeded` — surfaces the same cap message + override affordance). REVIEW/`ai_complete` gates the same way; DIRECT parks between stages on **both** its own run `budget_usd` cap **and** the global/project/workspace budgets via `check_budget` (`pause_for_scope_budget` — same approve/override release path), so a run can't blow through a scope budget it now counts against. **TALK also enforces mid-turn**: the agentic loop re-checks `check_budget` at the top of every iteration after the first (`should_stop_for_budget`), so a turn that starts under budget can't blow past a cap across its up-to-25 provider calls — on a breach it ends the turn with a quiet `stopped` note ("Budget cap reached — turn stopped. Override to continue.", via `finish_budget_capped`) and the next send hits the entry gate that surfaces the Override affordance. The same conscious per-turn `overrideBudget` flag that authorizes the turn's first call also bypasses the mid-turn gate for the whole turn — so no separate backend override grant is needed. A sub-agent fan-out runs inside one director round, so each sub-agent also stops at its share of the headroom (see "Sub-agents › Spend limit per sub-agent"); the override lifts that too. Post-turn threshold toasts unchanged. Two budget systems coexist: dollar-scoped budgets (the live UX) and a legacy per-session token budget (the token "remaining" gauge).
- **PTY token scraping is best-effort and fragile by design** — the authoritative path is API usage recorded by `chat_engine`/`ai_complete`.
