## 9. Integrations: Jira, MCP & Skills

Four distinct integration surfaces: (1) Jira issue tracking, (2) Octopush as an MCP **client** (connecting out to other MCP servers), (3) "Connect to Claude Code" (registering Octopush's own MCP server), (4) the standalone `octopush-mcp` **server**. Plus Skills.

### Jira — backend
- **Tracker-agnostic `Issue` model** — Normalized shape: `key, summary, statusName, statusCategory, issueType, priority?, url, parentKey?, subtask, hierarchyLevel`, + inline `blocks`/`blockedBy`/`subtasks`. _Support:_ `issue_tracker/mod.rs` (`IssueTracker` trait).
- **Status category normalization** — Jira `statusCategory.key` → Todo/InProgress/Done/Unknown. _Support:_ `status_category_from_key`.
- **"My issues" JQL** — `assignee = currentUser() AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY status, priority`. _Support:_ `my_issues_jql()`.
- **Branch→key detection (Rust)** — Extracts the first `[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+(\.\d+)*` key from a branch: a Jira key (`PROJ-123`) or an Epiku story id with dotted numbers (`ST-2.3`, `HU-1.1`). A dot extends a key only when a digit follows it, so Jira keys match exactly as before (`PROJ-123.fix` → `PROJ-123`). _Support:_ `detect_issue_key`; `src/lib/branchName.fixtures.json` pins the dotted cases for `workspace::branch_from_task` and `branchFromTask`.
- **Jira Cloud auth (HTTP Basic)** — `base64(email:api_token)`; config `{baseUrl, email, apiToken}`. _Support:_ `issue_tracker/jira.rs`.
- **Endpoints** — `list_my_issues` (`POST /rest/api/3/search/jql`), `get_issue` (`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}` with issuelinks+subtasks+description; the description, Atlassian Document Format or a plain string, becomes plain text: paragraphs, headings, `- ` list items, fenced code blocks, hard breaks, mention text and card URLs, cut at 8,000 characters with a closing "(cut at 8,000 characters)", `jira::description_text`; list endpoints leave it `None`), `list_issues_in_epic` (`parent = EPIC` with a legacy `"Epic Link"` fallback). _Support:_ `jira.rs`.
- **Link parsing** — Blocks/blocked-by from `issuelinks` (only "Blocks" type); subtasks from the inline array. _Support:_ `parse_issuelinks`, `parse_subtasks`.
- **Credential storage** — Jira's token in `~/.octopush/settings.json` under `issueTracker` (Epiku's is in the Keychain, below). _Support:_ `settings.rs`.
- **Commands** — `list_my_issues`, `get_issue`, `list_issues_in_epic` (each with an optional `projectId`, see Epiku › Per-project tracker), `get_issue_tracker_config`, `save_issue_tracker_config`, `update_workspace_link`, `update_project_jira_key`. _Support:_ `commands.rs`.

### Epiku — backend (read-only adapter, #1127)
- **Adapter** — `issue_tracker/epiku.rs` implements `IssueTracker` for Epiku. The commands below reach it; no screen does yet (Settings › Issue tracking's Epiku entry and the per-project choice follow in #1127's last part).
- **Per-project tracker** — Each project reads Jira, Epiku or none (`projects.issue_tracker`); no choice yet means Jira wherever Jira is configured (base URL, email and token all set, `JiraConfig::is_complete`), so nothing changes for existing users, and a chosen tracker that isn't configured reads as none (`issue_tracker::resolve_tracker`). An Epiku project may read its own Epiku project (`projects.epiku_project`) instead of the one in Settings. `list_my_issues`, `get_issue` and `list_issues_in_epic` take an optional `projectId` and dispatch to that project's tracker (`commands::project_tracker`); without one they read Jira, as before. Commands: `get_project_issue_tracker` → `{ choice, epikuProject, active }`, `set_project_issue_tracker` (validated by `validate_project_choice`).
- **Connection and token** — `save_epiku_config(baseUrl, project, token?)` keeps the base URL and project in `settings.json` (`epiku`; carried over by whole-file saves, `save_settings_from_ui`) and the token in the login Keychain (service `octopush-epiku`, account = the normalized base URL, `epiku::token_store`). No token keeps the saved one for the same URL only; a token is never sent to another URL, and a new URL drops the old URL's token (`save_connection`). Nothing is sent to Epiku on save. `get_epiku_config` → `{ baseUrl, project, hasToken }` (the token never goes back to the frontend); `remove_epiku_config` forgets both; `check_epiku_connection` is the "Connected" gate (`GET /api/historias?proyecto=<id>` answering 200, the story count back).
- **Requests** — `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and the query only: every request names the project (`?proyecto=<id>`; Epiku would otherwise answer for its default project), plus a story id in the path (percent-encoded) or an epic id (`epica`). No assignee filter is sent (Epiku has none yet), and no code, diffs, prompts or agent output ever go to Epiku. Octopush never writes to it. A 20 s timeout per read, and redirects are never followed (`redirect::Policy::none`), so the token never goes anywhere else; a 3xx reads "Epiku answered with a redirect, which Octopush doesn't follow with your token." _Support:_ `EpikuClient::get`, `http_client`.
- **Endpoints** — `list_my_issues`: `GET /api/historias?proyecto=<id>&detalle=true` (every story; the summary has no owner or resolved links), minus done stories; `get_issue`: `GET /api/historias/{id}?proyecto=<id>`; `list_issues_in_epic`: `GET /api/historias?proyecto=<id>&epica=<epic>` (Epiku's epics are explicit, never derived from the id), minus done stories; `check_connection` (the future "Connected" gate): `GET /api/historias?proyecto=<id>` answering 200 with a story list.
- **Mapping** — `estado` → `backlog` Backlog/Todo · `curso` In progress/InProgress · `bloqueada` Blocked/InProgress · `hecha` Done/Done · anything else shown as it is under Unknown (`status_from_estado`); `prioridad` `alta`/`normal` → High/Normal; type `Story` (blockers: `epica` → Epic, `externo` → External, with no state when Epiku gives none); `parentKey` = the epic id; `blockedBy` = `bloqueantes`, `blocks` = `desbloquea` (one story only: the summary lists bare ids, so list rows carry no links); `description` = one story's `markdown`, cut like Jira's (`jira::description_text`; list rows carry none). Every link opens the board on the project, `<base>/?proyecto=<id>` (Epiku has no per-story page). _Support:_ `issue_from_story`.
- **Errors** — 401 "Epiku rejected the token."; 400 `proyecto_invalido`; 404 `proyecto_no_encontrado` "Project not found, or not readable with this token."; 404 `no_encontrada`; a 404 without Epiku's JSON `error` field "This Epiku doesn't have that endpoint."; a success that isn't Epiku JSON "That URL didn't answer like Epiku." The token never appears in a message. _Support:_ `describe_failure`.
- **Config checks** — Base URL `https://`, or `http://` to this Mac only, no query, fragment or credentials (`normalized_base_url`); project id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,38}[a-z0-9]$` (`valid_project_id`); `EpikuConfig { baseUrl, project }` holds no token (it is meant for the Keychain).
- **Contract tests** — Recorded synthetic responses (`sample-project`, `ST-1.1`, `sample-person`) in `src-tauri/tests/fixtures/epiku/`, served by a local test server that also checks each request carries only the token and the query.

### Jira — frontend
- **`issuesStore`** — Assigned-not-done list (`load()`), per-key detail cache (`loadDetail` — the only place links/subtasks exist), epic-backlog cache (`loadEpic`). _Support:_ `issuesStore.ts`. **Per project (#1127):** `setProject(projectId)` (App, on every active-project switch and after a tracker setting is saved) reads the project's tracker (`get_project_issue_tracker`) into `tracker` and scopes the caches: `jira` for every Jira project (one list serves them all), `epiku:<project>` for an Epiku one. A scope change empties them, and an answer for a scope the user has left never lands. Every call carries `projectId`, so the backend dispatches it to that project's tracker. `trackerByProject` keeps each open project's choice (workspace menu, ticket picker, Issue tracking modal).
- **`parentIssuesStore`** — `loadParent`/`loadAncestors(key, depth)` for the parent chain, with the active project's id; nothing under Epiku (a story's parent is its epic, which isn't a story). _Support:_ `parentIssuesStore.ts`.
- **`useActiveIssue(key)`** — Resolves an issue preferring the detail cache; one network call per active-key change. _Support:_ `hooks/useActiveIssue.ts`.
- **Branch→key detection (TS mirror)** — `detectIssueKey` + `detectIssueKeyForProject` (only accepts a key matching the project prefix), same pattern as the Rust one, dotted Epiku ids included; `isIssueKey` (one whole key) backs the inline picker's exact-key fallback and the PR draft's title prefix; `detectTrackerKey(branch, tracker, jiraKey, isKnownStory)` (header, Companion, workspace menu) takes, under Epiku, the first dotted id that is one of the project's loaded stories or one `getIssue` read (`issuesStore.isKnownStory` / `useKnownStory`), so a dotted token that isn't a story (`UTF-8.1`, `NODE-20.11`, `RFC-1.0`) links nothing, offers no Change/Unlink and fetches nothing; otherwise the project-key rule. Under Jira a key is always undotted: `detectIssueKeyForProject` gives `PROJ-12` for `PROJ-12.5` (`jiraKeyOf`), and so does Rust's `workspace::branch_from_task` (`issue_tracker::jira_key`). _Support:_ `lib/detectIssueKey.ts`.
- **Linkage + selectors** — `resolveLinkage` (manual link wins → branch-detected → unlinked), `resolveJiraProjectKey`, `selectBacklog` (`wholeList` for Epiku)/`selectBlocking`/`selectBlockedBy`/`selectSubtasksOrSiblings`/`selectEpicSiblings`/`resolveEpicKey`/`selectElsewhereIssues`; `issueTypeToken` (type → color). _Support:_ `lib/issueTrackerSelectors.ts`.

### Jira — UI surfaces
- **Active-ticket header / PR chip** — See §1 (ContextHeader). _Support:_ `ContextHeader.tsx`.
- **WorkContext pills panel + workspace jump chip + Elsewhere** — See §1 (Companion). _Support:_ `WorkContextPanel.tsx`, `ElsewhereFooter`/`ElsewhereModal`.

- **Inline ticket picker** — Scope toggle (PROJECT vs All), fuzzy search over cached tickets, exact-key fallback for a Jira key or a dotted Epiku id (`isIssueKey`, verified via `getIssue`). _Support:_ `InlineTicketPicker.tsx`.

### In-app MCP client (Octopush → other MCP servers)
- **Config shape & sources** — Claude-Code-compatible `{ "mcpServers": { "<name>": { command, args, env } } }` from `~/.claude/mcp.json` (user) ∪ `<worktree>/.claude/mcp.json` (project overrides user). Any other key of an entry (`cwd`, `type`, `disabled`, another client's own fields) is kept as it was (`McpServerConfig.extra`, `serde(flatten)`), so a save from Settings never drops it. An entry may also carry `remote` (see "Remote servers"), written only when present (`skip_serializing_if`), so older entries read and write unchanged. **Per-entry parsing** (`parse_entry`): one entry Octopush can't read never hides the others. An entry without `command` in the shape other MCP clients write by hand, `{ "type": "http" | "streamable-http" | "sse", "url": …, "headers": { … } }`, is read into the Remote form's choices: `remote.url`, `transport` `http-only` (http) or `sse-only` (sse), `auth: "headers"` with each header's value in `env` under its `OCTOPUSH_MCP_H_<NAME>` var (or `auth: "oauth"` when it has no headers); its other keys stay in `extra`, and `type`/`url`/`headers` give way to the bridge on the next save. Any other entry it can't run (no `command`, another `type`) is skipped with a warning in the log, and a save from Settings writes it back as it was unless a server now has its name (`save_config_at`). _Support:_ `mcp/mod.rs`.
- **Remote servers (the mcp-remote bridge)** — Octopush speaks only stdio, so a remote server runs through `mcp-remote`, which Octopush builds from the Settings form's choices, stored per entry as `remote: { url, auth: "oauth"|"token"|"headers", header_names, transport: "auto"|"http-only"|"sse-only", client_id }` (every field defaults when missing, so a hand-edited block still parses; unknown values read as the defaults). `mcp::remote::apply_bridge` writes the entry's `command` (`npx` resolved the way CLI stages find it, `resolve_npx`; the bare name if it isn't found) and `args`: `-y mcp-remote@^0.16 <url>` (held to the 0.16 line, the latest on npm as of 2026-11, for its `${VAR}` expansion in the client info, its `mcp-remote-v1` sign-in store that Clear sign-in reads, and its security fixes: header values never logged, a failed JSON parse never quoting a secret; `BRIDGE_PACKAGE`), then `--header Name:${OCTOPUSH_MCP_H_<NAME>}` per header (no space after the colon; the env var's name is `OCTOPUSH_MCP_H_` plus the header name upper-cased, any other character than a letter or digit as `_`, `header_env`), `--static-oauth-client-info {"client_id":…}` for a pre-registered OAuth client (with `"client_secret":"${OCTOPUSH_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET}"` when one is set; recent mcp-remote releases expand `${VAR}` in it), `--transport http-only|sse-only` unless Automatic, then the user's own **extra arguments** as written (`remote.extra_args`, one per line in Advanced: `--enable-proxy` behind a proxy, `--allow-http`, `--resource <uri>`…), which survive every save. Header values never sit in the args: they travel in the entry's `env`, which mcp-remote interpolates, and a token, a header marked secret and the client secret live in the login Keychain (see "Secrets in the login Keychain"), so `mcp.json` holds `""` for them: `apply_bridge` always lists the token's and the client secret's env names in `secret_env`, and drops a removed header's or an unused client secret's. Token is the `Authorization` header with its value prefixed `Bearer ` (once). Custom headers keep names mcp-remote accepts (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`), each once. Stale bridge env vars (a removed header's, an unused client secret) are dropped; other env the entry has (a CA path) is kept. The bridge is rebuilt on every save (`with_bridges`, inside `save_mcp_config`), before every Test/Reconnect, and whenever Talk loads its servers (`load_server_configs`), so a hand-edited `remote` block runs the same everywhere; `command`/`args`/`env` stay in the file, so other readers of `mcp.json` still run it. At spawn, a remote entry whose saved absolute `npx` no longer exists (a Node upgrade under nvm) looks `npx` up again on the PATH (`spawn_plan`). Browser (OAuth) sign-in is mcp-remote's: the first connection opens the browser, and mcp-remote keeps the sign-in in `~/.mcp-auth`. **What leaves the Mac:** the requests mcp-remote makes to the server's URL (and its sign-in pages), and npx fetching `mcp-remote` (the newest 0.16.x) from the npm registry the first time; once a 0.16.x is in npx's cache, npx runs it without checking the registry for a newer one. _Support:_ `mcp/remote.rs` (`RemoteConfig`, `apply_bridge`, `bridge_args`, `header_env`, `with_bridges`, `resolve_npx`).
- **Secrets in the login Keychain** — An entry lists in `secret_env` (`serde default`, written only when not empty) the env names whose values live in the macOS login Keychain, service `octopush-mcp`, account `<server>/<ENV_NAME>` (`mcp::secrets`, through the `keyring` crate); in `mcp.json` each of those env values is written as `""`, never the secret. **At spawn** (Talk's registry and Settings' Test/Reconnect) `secrets::resolve` reads them into the child's environment; a missing one fails the start before anything runs: "The value for <NAME> isn't in the Keychain; edit <server> to enter it." (classified as "The value for <NAME> isn't in the Keychain." · "Edit the server to enter it."). Settings' Test and Reconnect take the names to read from the saved entry, never from the config the form sends. Resolved values are scrubbed from any failure text (`secrets::scrub`): each value, and a `Bearer …` / `Basic …` one without its scheme too, longest first (4 characters or more), in Settings' Test/Reconnect and in what Talk's model reads of a call that broke on the wire (`redact_call_failure`). Each item is read at most once per launch and then served from memory (`Keychain` cache), since an ad-hoc-signed build prompts on every read. **Only user-level entries** can name Keychain items: a project's `.claude/mcp.json` entries get their `secret_env` dropped on load, after their bridge is rebuilt (which would list a token's name), in `load_server_configs`, so a repo's file never gets the user's secrets into a command it chose; that file is never rewritten. **Saving** (`mcp::save_user_servers`, inside `save_mcp_config`): the values the form sent apart (`secrets`: server → env name → value) join the entries (`merge_new_values`), remote bridges are rebuilt, then `secrets::plan_secrets` moves every `secret_env` value out of the entries (a value is a new one to store; `""` keeps the saved one) and plans the Keychain changes; every name to keep there must be a valid env name (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, `check_names`, so the `<server>/<NAME>` account splits one way only), else nothing is written; new values and a renamed server's items (copied, `renamed`: new name → old; every source is read before anything is written, so two servers swapping names keep their own values) are written first, each overwritten value remembered: a Keychain write that fails puts back what was written and stops the save before `mcp.json` is touched, and a file write that fails puts the Keychain back too (`Undo`); then the file is written without them; then items no entry names any more (a deleted server's, a renamed server's old ones, a name no longer secret) are deleted (a failure is logged). A name listed with no value whose saved entry still holds a plain value (a migration whose Keychain write failed, a stale form) keeps that value rather than storing nothing. A server whose secret values changed is restarted for Talk even though its entry reads the same (`McpRegistry::apply_save`). **Migration:** on every save, any user-level env value whose name matches `TOKEN|KEY|SECRET|PASSWORD|AUTH|BEARER` (case-insensitive, `looks_secret`), is a valid env name, isn't empty or a `$VAR` reference and isn't in the entry's `plain_env` (the names the user chose to keep in the file with "Keep in Keychain" off) moves into the Keychain and is listed in `secret_env`. Remote header env vars are left to the form's own choice. Secret values are never sent back to the frontend: `get_mcp_config` and the save return the entries as written. **Data flow:** secrets stay on this Mac in the login Keychain; nothing new leaves the Mac. Rust tests use an in-memory store (`MemoryStore`), never the real Keychain. _Support:_ `mcp/secrets.rs` (`SecretStore`, `Keychain`, `resolve`, `plan_secrets`, `apply_before_save`, `apply_after_save`, `merge_new_values`, `looks_secret`, `scrub`), `mcp/mod.rs` (`save_user_servers`, `load_server_configs`, `McpRegistry::with_secrets`, `test_connect_with`).
- **Clear sign-in** — `clear_mcp_sign_in(name, config)` deletes mcp-remote's saved browser sign-in for a Browser (OAuth) entry and resets Talk's connection to it (`reset_server`, since a running bridge holds its tokens in memory), then emits `mcp://status-changed` so the Companion's chips refresh; it returns how many files went. mcp-remote names its files `<md5 of the URL>_<what>` (`_tokens.json`, `_client_info.json`, `_code_verifier_<state>.txt`, `_debug.log`, …) in its store directory (`mcp-remote-v1`, or `mcp-remote-<version>` in releases before its store stopped following the package version) under `MCP_REMOTE_CONFIG_DIR` (the entry's env, then the app's) or `~/.mcp-auth`. The hash covers the URL plus any headers or `--resource`-style parameters; a Browser (OAuth) entry Octopush builds has none, so `sign_in_files` deletes every `<md5(url)>_*` file in the base and each `mcp-remote-*` directory and nothing else (MD5 implemented in `remote.rs`, only for this lookup). Token and Custom headers entries have no sign-in, and the command refuses them. _Support:_ `mcp/remote.rs` (`clear_sign_in`, `sign_in_files`, `md5_hex`), `commands::clear_mcp_sign_in`.
- **stdio JSON-RPC client** — Newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0; handshake `initialize` → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/list`; replies method-not-found to server→client requests. _Support:_ `mcp/mod.rs`.
- **Spawn: command and PATH** — Talk's servers and Settings' Test/Reconnect start a server the way CLI stages start theirs (`spawn_plan`): the process gets the CLI stages' PATH (`cli_runner::resolved_cli_path`: the login shell's ∪ the app's ∪ common bin dirs), with an absolute command's own dir first (an nvm `npx` finds its sibling `node`); a bare command (`npx`, `uvx`) is resolved on that PATH (`resolve_executable`); a command with a slash runs as given. A server whose `env` sets PATH keeps it, and its command is looked up there. Only PATH comes from the login shell: the rest of the process's environment is the app's plus the server's `env`, as before. Relative PATH entries (`.`, `bin`) are skipped, in the lookup (`resolve_executable`, which CLI stages share) and in the PATH the server gets. A bare command found nowhere fails before spawning with "Octopush couldn't find `npx` on the PATH Octopush searched (/opt/homebrew/bin:…). Use its full path (run `which npx` in Terminal)." ("on the server's own PATH (…)" when its `env` sets one). Each server runs in its own process group. _Support:_ `mcp/mod.rs` (`spawn_plan`, `McpRegistry::spawn`).
- **Tool namespacing** — Tools surface as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. _Support:_ `mcp/mod.rs`.
- **Lazy registry with failure memory** — Servers spawned on first use and cached; a cached connection serves only the config it was started with (`Entry.cfg`, `cached`), so an entry edited by hand — or a project config naming the server differently — starts a fresh process on its next use. A server that failed to start is skipped for the rest of the session while its config is the one that failed (`Failure`, with its reason; a later call's error repeats only its first line, so the server's output reaches the model once); a changed entry or a reset tries it again. A connection whose call failed on the wire is evicted (see §3 "MCP tool invocation"). **Saving restarts what changed:** `save_mcp_config` compares the old and new user-level entries (`changed_servers`: changed, removed or added) and resets each (`McpRegistry::apply_config_change` → `reset_server`): its process is killed through the same handle the timeout abort uses (a call in flight on it fails with a connection error; nothing waits on the connection's lock), a start still in its handshake is killed too, and its failure memory is cleared. A reset is counted per server (`resets`): a start that began before it neither caches its process nor records its failure, so a save racing a first call can't leave the old config's process behind (`finish_start`: a start that completed after a reset is dropped and its process stopped). _Support:_ `McpRegistry` (`ensure`, `finish_start`, `cached`, `reset_server`, `apply_config_change`, `stop`), `changed_servers`.
- **Test connection** — `test_connect` spawns + handshakes + lists tools without touching the cache. _Support:_ `McpRegistry::test_connect`.
- **Classified connection failures** — A failed Test or Reconnect is classified in Rust (`mcp::classify_failure_with(reason, known)` → `McpFailure { summary, hint, detail }`, `mcp/failure.rs`) and returned as `AppError::McpFailure`, serialized `{ kind: "McpFailure", message, summary, hint, detail }`. **Redaction, a best effort for text on screen:** every line of the summary and the details is redacted first (`redact_output_line`): the server's own env values that could be credentials (`known_secrets`, `could_be_credential`, `secret_scan::KnownSecret`; 4 characters or more: a remote bridge's header and client-secret values always; under a name that reads as one, `TOKEN|KEY|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|AUTH|BEARER|CREDENTIAL|PRIVATE`; a URL with a path or a query, such as a webhook URL; or 20+ characters mixing letters and digits that aren't a host or path; a `Bearer …` / `Basic …` value is known without its scheme too, so an echoed bare token goes; never PATH, a path or a plain number, so `production` or a bare host stays readable), what `secret_scan::redact_line` catches (provider key prefixes, `TOKEN=…`-style assignments, `Bearer …`, URL passwords), OAuth `code=…`, `Basic …` when its value looks like base64 (not "basic authentication"), bare JWTs, quoted values under secret-ish keys at any length (`"client_secret": "…"`, `"refresh_token": "…"`, `"password": "…"`) and header lines with secret-ish names (`Authorization: …`, `X-API-Key: …`; not an error class such as `InvalidTokenError: …`, which keeps its message). A credential in a shape none of these covers can still show. Talk's connection failures get the same env-value redaction (`McpRegistry::connect`), so neither the model nor Settings sees an echoed env value. Matching ignores mcp-remote's `[pid]` line prefix. **The ending decides:** a timed-out sign-in, the callback port in use, auth, refused, DNS and network-timeout causes are read only from the lines that say how it ended (from the first `Fatal` line, else from the last line that reads as an error, `decisive`), so mcp-remote's routine 401 on its way into a browser sign-in doesn't make a later failure read as rejected credentials. Known causes, in this order: OAuth Dynamic Client Registration rejected at any status, or an older bridge's "does not support dynamic client registration" ("This server doesn't support automatic sign-in." · "Use a token, or the OAuth client ID its admins give you."); Octopush's own lookup failure ("Octopush couldn't find `npx` on the PATH Octopush searched." · "Use its full path (run `which npx` in Terminal)."; the PATH searched stays in the details); a spawn of an absolute command that doesn't exist; a program the server itself couldn't start (Node's `spawn uvx ENOENT`, `env: node: No such file or directory`, a shell's `sh: npx: command not found` / `zsh: command not found: npx`); the smoke test's own 120s timeout ("The server didn't answer within 120s." · finish a browser sign-in, then test again); a browser sign-in that timed out ("Signing in timed out." · "Finish signing in in the browser window that opened, then test again."); the OAuth callback port taken (`EADDRINUSE`, "The sign-in callback port is in use."); connection refused; a host that doesn't resolve (`ENOTFOUND`, naming the host when it can); a network timeout (`ETIMEDOUT`, undici's connect/headers/body timeouts); HTTP 401/403 next to a status word (`HTTP 401`, `HTTP/1.1 403`, `status code (403)`; never a pid, a stack frame's `:401:` or a URL's port), `Unauthorized`, `Forbidden`, `invalid_token`, error classes such as `InvalidTokenError` / `TokenExpiredError` / `AuthorizationError`, and the like ("The server rejected the credentials."). Otherwise the summary is the ending's first line that reads as an error (else the first such line, else the first line), skipping lines that are only an `Error:` label, without its label, a JSON-RPC error answer reduced to its message, cut at 160 characters; a server that exited with no output reads "The server exited before it answered." · "Run its command in Terminal to see why.". The details are the whole reason and server output as printed: stdout's first 20 non-JSON lines and stderr's first 2 KiB of lines plus its last 2 KiB ("… (N lines cut)" between, `StderrLog`), so a late "Fatal error" after a long log is kept. Talk's model-facing text (`connection_failure_text`) keeps its 1 KiB tail. _Support:_ `mcp/failure.rs`, `mcp/mod.rs` (`redact_output_line`, `known_secrets`, `StderrLog`), `error.rs` (`AppError::McpFailure`), `commands::smoke_test_mcp_server`.
- **Commands** — `list_mcp_tools`, `list_mcp_server_status` (each configured server's registry state, spawning nothing), `get_thread_mcp_disabled` / `set_thread_mcp_server` (a conversation's off list; the setter changes one server), `get_mcp_config`, `save_mcp_config(servers, secrets?, renamed?)` (rebuilds every remote entry's bridge, moves secret values to the Keychain, saves, renames the server in conversations' off lists (`renamed`: new name → old; its Keychain items move too), then resets every changed or removed server and every server whose secret values changed, and emits `mcp://config-changed`; returns the entries as saved, without any secret value), `test_mcp_server` (rebuilds a remote entry's bridge first; 120s timeout, for OAuth bridges that wait on a browser sign-in), `reconnect_mcp_server` (`reset_server`, emits `mcp://status-changed`, then the same smoke test as `test_mcp_server`), `clear_mcp_sign_in`. _Support:_ `commands.rs`.
- **Settings → MCP Servers** — Per-row card (Test / Reconnect / Edit / Remove) + an add/edit form; duplicate-name guarded. **Trust (#1243):** under a row, what Talk's MCP cards were told to stop asking about: "Runs without asking in Talk's Edit freely, in every conversation:", then "every tool (one it marks destructive still asks)" and each tool always allowed (mono), each line with a mute `ShieldCheck` and an `X` icon button (title "Revoke: its next call asks again"; aria-label "Revoke <tool>" or "Revoke the trust in <server>"). Trust is bound to a row's entry, so a server without one has none; a save that changes an entry drops its trust, and the list reads again. A failed revoke re-reads the list and toasts "Couldn't revoke the trust". The section is `data-tour="settings-mcp-servers"`, a trust block `settings-mcp-trust`. The intro reads "Model Context Protocol servers whose tools become available to Talk: a local command Octopush runs, or a remote URL it reaches through mcp-remote, which npx fetches the first time (Node required). A Token sign-in, an OAuth client secret and the values you mark Keep in Keychain stay on this Mac, in your login Keychain; a browser sign-in stays in ~/.mcp-auth." (`mcp-remote` and `~/.mcp-auth` in sage mono) A remote row shows a `Globe` icon (tooltip "Remote server") and its URL (truncated, full URL as its `title`) instead of the bridge's command line; an entry without `remote` (including an old hand-written `npx mcp-remote` bridge) is a local command and edits as before. **The form** (`McpServerForm`, fading in with `.octo-fade-in`) opens with a `SegmentedControl` **Local command | Remote URL** (`data-tour="settings-mcp-type"`), then Name; the kind's fields crossfade (`FadeSwap`), and both kinds' fields stay in the draft, so switching back loses nothing. Local: Command, Args (one per line), and Env as Name / value rows ("Add a variable"; names `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, each once: "env names use letters, digits and _" / "each variable once"), each with a **Keep in Keychain** switch (lucide `KeyRound`, `role="switch"`, tooltip "Keep in Keychain", brass when on) and a titled remove icon. The switch starts on for a new row whose name looks like a credential (`looksSecret`: `TOKEN|KEY|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|AUTH|BEARER|CREDENTIAL|PRIVATE|COOKIE|SESSION`) and follows the name until the user sets it (`renameRow`); a secret row's value is masked (`type="password"`). A saved secret shows an empty value with the placeholder "•••• saved" and stays saved unless a new value is typed; renaming its variable means a new value. A plain value that the save's migration would move (`TOKEN|KEY|SECRET|PASSWORD|AUTH|BEARER`) loads with the switch on; turning the switch off for such a name records it in `plain_env`. Turning it off on a saved value needs the value typed again ("type the value to store it in plain text" beside a disabled Save; the same for a secret header), since the form never holds the saved value and saving nothing would delete it. Remote: URL (an `https://` URL, or `http://` on `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` only, as mcp-remote 0.16 allows, or any `http://` URL with `--allow-http` among the extra arguments; else "use an https:// URL (http only for localhost or 127.0.0.1)" beside Save, which stays disabled), then **Sign-in** as a `SegmentedControl`: **Browser (OAuth)**, the default (a note that the first connection opens the browser and mcp-remote keeps the sign-in in ~/.mcp-auth); **Token** (one masked `type="password"` field, "Sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Kept in your login Keychain.", "•••• saved" once saved); or **Custom headers** (Name / value rows, each with a titled remove icon, plus "Add a header"; each row has the same Keep in Keychain switch, on by default for a secret-looking name (`Authorization`, `X-Api-Key`, `Cookie`, `X-Session`…), and a secret row's value is masked; names must be `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` and unique, "header names use letters, digits, - and _" / "each header once"). The sign-in's fields crossfade too. An **Advanced** disclosure (`ChevronRight` + `<Reveal>`, collapsed unless it holds a client ID or a non-Automatic transport) holds, for Browser (OAuth), an OAuth client ID and a masked client secret (enabled once there is an ID; always kept in the Keychain, "•••• saved" once saved, with an `X` icon button, "Forget the saved client secret (the client ID stays)"; one containing `"` or `\` is refused, "the client secret can't contain \" or \\", since mcp-remote puts it into the client info's JSON before parsing it) for a server without automatic registration, a **Transport** `SegmentedControl` (Automatic / HTTP only / SSE only), and **Extra arguments (one per line)**, "Added to the mcp-remote command line as written. Anything here shows in the process list, so keep secrets in Token or Custom headers." (Advanced also opens on its own when it holds any). Save stays disabled until the kind's required fields are filled (`draftComplete`: name; a command; or a URL, plus a token or a named header; and every secret row has a value, typed or saved). The draft becomes the entry in `mcpDraft.ts` (`configFromDraft` → `{ config, secrets }`: the entry with `""` for every secret, its `secret_env` and `plain_env`, and the typed secret values apart, which the section sends as `save_mcp_config`'s `secrets` with the rename as `renamed`; a remote draft is sent as `remote` + its plain header env values, keeping a remote entry's other env and every field the form doesn't show; `draftFrom` reads it back, a saved secret as saved, a token without its `Bearer ` prefix), and the section shows the entries the backend returns, the latest save's only (a sequence number drops an earlier save's late answer). A save that fails re-reads the saved config (`get_mcp_config`; the list from before the save if that fails too), so the list never keeps the optimistic `""` of a value the Keychain refused. Editing a saved Browser (OAuth) server adds **Clear sign-in** at the form's right ("Forget the browser sign-in saved for this server; its next connection signs in again"; toast "Sign-in cleared" or "No saved sign-in for this server"). "Add MCP server" carries `data-tour="settings-mcp-add"`. **Test** runs a separate one-shot process and never touches Talk's connection. **Reconnect** (a `RefreshCw` icon button, tooltip "Reconnect: restart Talk's connection to this server, then test it", `aria-label` "Reconnect <name>"; the first row's carries `data-tour="settings-mcp-reconnect"`) stops Talk's cached connection to the server and forgets a start failure (`reconnect_mcp_server`), then runs the same smoke test: "Reconnecting…" while it runs, then "Reconnected · N tools" or the error; Talk's next call spawns the server afresh. Test and Reconnect are disabled while either runs; result lines fade in (`.octo-fade-in`). Each server has a generation, bumped when its entry is saved, renamed or removed: a Test or Reconnect started before then drops its result instead of showing it on the entry that replaced it. **A failed Test or Reconnect** shows the classified failure (see "Classified connection failures"): an `AlertTriangle` and the summary, then the hint, both rouge and selectable; under them a mono "Details" disclosure (`ChevronRight` turning 90°, `aria-expanded`) unfolds through `<Reveal>` to the full redacted output in a selectable (`.octo-selectable`), wrapped (`whitespace-pre-wrap break-words`, no `break-all`), scrollable (`max-h-48 overflow-auto`) mono block with a Copy icon button (lucide `Copy`, tooltip and `aria-label` "Copy the full output"; `copyToClipboard`, toast "Output copied"). A rejection that isn't an `McpFailure` (an IPC error) shows its own first line, with the whole text as the details (`mcpFailureFrom`). **Edit** (a `Pencil` icon button, tooltip "Edit server", `aria-label` "Edit <name>"; the first row's carries `data-tour="settings-mcp-edit"`) turns that row into the same form, prefilled (`draftFrom`: args one per line, env as rows), fading in (`.octo-fade-in`). "Save changes" replaces the entry; a rename drops the old name, guarded against another server's name ("name already exists"; its own name isn't a duplicate). The save goes through `save_mcp_config` (a rename passes `renamed`, so its Keychain items move and conversations that had the server off keep it off), so the changed (or renamed: old and new) entry is restarted for Talk, and the row's old test result is dropped. "Cancel" closes the form and leaves the saved entry as it was. One form is open at a time: while one is, the other rows' Edit and "Add MCP server" are disabled; a row's Edit also waits while its own Test or Reconnect runs (tooltip "Edit server (once its test finishes)"). The duplicate check is an own-property check (`Object.hasOwn`), so a name such as `constructor` isn't taken. _Support:_ `settings/McpServersSection.tsx` (`FailureLine`, `mcpFailureFrom`), `settings/McpServerForm.tsx`, `settings/mcpDraft.ts` (`draftFrom`, `configFromDraft`, `draftProblem`, `draftComplete`, `headerEnv`, `looksSecret`, `renameRow`, `rowSaved`), `ipc.reconnectMcpServer`, `ipc.saveMcpConfig`, `ipc.clearMcpSignIn`.

### "Connect to Claude Code" (Octopush's server → Claude Code config)
- **One-click registration** — If `claude mcp get octopush` (3 s, `run_probe`) already shows a user-scope stdio entry whose `Command` is exactly the bundled binary with no `Args`, Connect reports Connected without touching the config. Otherwise it removes any existing `octopush` entry then runs `claude mcp add octopush -s user -- <binary>` (idempotent across upgrades). Each `remove`/`add` runs through the readiness module's bounded spawn (`run_probe`: in its own process group, stdout and stderr read while it runs so a long reply can't fill a pipe) with a 20 s `CLI_TIMEOUT` — past Claude Code's own config-lock wait — and at it the whole process group is killed (anything the CLI spawned too); a timeout counts as a held lock (one retry, then busy). The pipes are read in chunks and each keeps at most its first 64 KiB (`OUTPUT_CAP`; the rest is read and dropped, so a chatty CLI can't grow Octopush's memory). The exit is detected without reaping (`waitid` with `WNOWAIT`), and the group is killed then, while the unreaped child still holds its pid and group id: whatever the CLI left running in its process group dies with it, holding its output or not (`run_status_probe` too), and the signal can never reach a reused pid. A leftover that called `setsid` has left the group and isn't stopped. When `waitid` can't tell (any error but `EINTR`), the fallback `try_wait` reaps under the in-flight lock and untracks the pid in the same step, and that probe's group is then never signalled (`reap_untracked`, `Exit::Reaped`). The output is then collected for at most 250 ms more (`DRAIN_FLOOR`, a hard limit), so something that left the group holding the pipe can't make the probe wait out the timeout; each reader thread only `read`s once `poll` says that won't block (50 ms at a time) and stops, closing its end, once the probe has returned, so a leftover that called `setsid` can't keep it blocked either. A probe still running when Octopush quits is killed with its group (`readiness::kill_in_flight` on `RunEvent::Exit`, under the same lock a probe untracks itself with before its reap). The `add` is the exception (`Step::on_quit` → `OnQuit::Finish`, run through `run_probe_on_quit`): quitting waits up to 2 s (`QUIT_GRACE`) for it to finish before killing it, since by then `remove` may have succeeded and a killed `add` would leave Octopush unregistered. The whole press also holds a connect-level mark (`readiness::finish_before_quit`, a `Finishing` guard) that quit waits on within the same 2 s, so a quit after `remove` but before `add` spawns (the 1 s pause before a busy retry included) still lets the `add` start; quit waits only while a Connect press or an `add` is under way. Once quitting has begun (`readiness::quitting`) Connect starts no `remove` and skips its verifying `claude mcp get` (reported as unconfirmed), so nothing it spawns outlives the app but a restoring `add`. Failure messages quote at most 300 characters of the CLI's output (`shown`, with "…"). The whole press shares one 30 s `CONNECT_BUDGET`: the pre-check, `remove`, `add`, retries and the verify each get what is left, capped at their own timeout; a call with nothing left isn't started (a `remove`/`add` reads as busy, the verify as unconfirmed), and the lock retry is skipped when its 1 s pause would use up the rest. A `remove` that says the server doesn't exist is fine; any other `remove` failure is shown instead of discarded. When `remove` or `add` fails on Claude Code's config lock (2.1.318+ waits for it or exits 1; matched on lock phrases such as `ELOCKED`, "acquire lock", "lock file", "is locked", "is busy", so words like `blocked` or a path containing `lock` don't count), it retries once after 1 s, then reports "Claude Code's config is busy — try again in a moment" beside the manual command. After a successful `add`, `registered` comes from a follow-up `claude mcp get octopush`, not the add exit code (another job's save can still replace the entry). If that `mcp get` times out or can't start, Connect says Claude Code didn't confirm it in time and to press Connect to Claude Code again in a moment (the card has no separate status check; Connect is idempotent and re-runs the verify), rather than claiming the entry is missing. When `remove` succeeded but the `add` then fails, times out or stays busy, the message says the previous Octopush registration was removed and that pressing Connect to Claude Code again restores it (the manual command stays on the card). _Support:_ `mcp_setup.rs::connect`, `connect_flow`, `run_cli`, `registered_with`, `classify_failure`, `verification_from`.
- **Status probe timeout** — `claude mcp get octopush` runs through the readiness module's `run_status_probe` (output discarded) with `CHECK_TIMEOUT` (3 s, killed past it), so a slow CLI can't stall the Settings card. On the card a timeout reads as not registered. _Support:_ `mcp_setup.rs::is_registered`.
- **Binary & CLI resolution** — `octopush-mcp` sibling-of-exe → `$PATH` → dev trees; `claude` via `$PATH` → well-known absolute locations (GUI apps don't inherit shell PATH). _Support:_ `resolve_mcp_binary`, `resolve_claude_cli`.
- **Status + manual fallback** — `McpStatus{binaryPath?, binaryFound, claudeFound, registered, manualCommand}`; always hands back a copy-pasteable `claude mcp add …`. _Support:_ commands `mcp_connection_status`, `connect_claude_code`.
- **Settings "Coding Agents" card** — Connected/Not-connected dot, "Connect/Reconnect" button, read-only manual command + Copy. _Support:_ `IntegrationsPane.tsx` `ClaudeCodeCard`.
- **Installed Claude Code version** — The card shows the CLI version (`CLI 2.1.316`, tooltip names the tested version) and, when it is older than the tested floor, an amber "Update Claude Code (x.y.z or newer recommended)" row with the reason (x.y.z = the higher of the floor and the missing security fix); at or above the floor but below a `CLAUDE_SECURITY_FIXES` row, the same amber row names the newest one it lacks (today "Update Claude Code: 2.1.325 fixes the Bash sandbox not fully protecting a worktree's settings, hooks and shared git folder"), as Readiness and the launcher do (`data-tour="settings-claude-cli-update"`). Nothing shows when the CLI isn't found. The version comes from `claude --version` run with the same login-shell PATH and environment as CLI stages (10s timeout, killed past it), parsed to `x.y.z` (`2.1.316 (Claude Code)` → `2.1.316`) and cached until the next Readiness check (backend `VersionCache`, cleared by `forget_claude_cli_version` when `readiness::run_all` starts; frontend `loadClaudeCliVersion`, cleared by `readinessStore.check`). The backend probes outside the cache's lock, so a forget or a reader never waits on a probe; a probe a forget overtook isn't stored as current. Only one probe runs per generation (`VersionState::probing`): callers that arrive while it runs wait on a condvar (the lock let go) and get its answer, so concurrent first callers spawn one `claude --version`, not one each; a forget lets the next caller probe afresh, and a probe that panics still clears the flag (`ProbingGuard`). Stage escalation reads the last answer without waiting (`claude_cli_version_cached`, `try_lock`), kept through a Readiness check, so an old CLI's effort-only escalation still halts; a probe overtaken by a newer one never replaces that answer (each answer keeps the generation its probe started in). `TESTED_CLAUDE_FLOOR` (`agent_adapter.rs`) is the contract-fixture version; a contract test keeps it naming a recorded fixture, and the release-watch routine bumps it with them. _Support:_ `agent_adapter::claude_cli_version`, `parse_claude_version`, `version_below`; command `claude_cli_version`; `ipc.claudeCliVersion`; `data-tour="settings-claude-code-card"`, `"settings-claude-cli-version"`.

### The `octopush-mcp` standalone server binary
- **What/transport/scope** — A sidecar `[[bin]]` exposing a **read-and-author** slice of Octopush over JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio, reusing `octopush_lib::db` against the same SQLite store (WAL-safe while the app is open). **Never executes runs or spends tokens**; the one git mutation it performs is materialising a workspace's worktree (`create_workspace`). _Support:_ `bin/octopush-mcp/main.rs`; doc `docs/octopush-mcp.md`.
- **Protocol handshake** — Negotiates version (latest `2025-06-18`; also `2025-03-26`, `2024-11-05`), advertises `tools`, returns `instructions`; tool errors in-band (`isError: true`). _Support:_ `protocol.rs`.
- **Exposed tools (25)** — _reference:_ `describe_pipeline_schema` (now also documents the `customRoles` authoring contract). _read:_ `list_pipelines`, `get_pipeline`, `list_roles`, `list_projects`, `list_workspaces`, `get_workspace`, `list_missions`, `get_mission`, `list_runs`, `get_run`, `list_routines`. _author:_ `create_pipeline` (validated DAG), `update_pipeline` (forks a builtin / edits a custom), `delete_pipeline` (builtins protected), `save_role`/`delete_role` (see role authoring below), `create_routine`/`update_routine`/`delete_routine`/`set_routine_enabled` (see routine authoring below), `link_workspace_issue` (metadata-only), `create_mission` (authors a mission — build/fix/design/probe/test/… — via the shared `mission.rs`; an omitted `gitIsolation` defaults by intent: `readonly` for review/probe/perf, `ephemeral` for test, `worktree` otherwise; code work usually comes free via `create_workspace`), `create_run` (stages a DIRECT run in **`draft`** — not started), `create_workspace` (ensures a worktree-backed workspace via the shared `workspace::create`; an explicit branch is used **verbatim** (validated git ref), a task-derived branch is the wizard's short one (`workspace::branch_from_task`: the project's ticket key first, up to four words, ≤ 60, `-2`/`-3` when taken); adopts an already-checked-out branch rather than failing; returns `status: created|adopted|existed|restored`; **pairs the workspace with a mission** (default intent `build`, or pass `intent`) so MCP-created workspaces match the app's "no workspace without a mission" guarantee; appears in the rail on next focus/refresh). `create_pipeline`/`update_pipeline` author the **same per-stage knobs the app builder does**, including per-stage reasoning **`effort`** and the model-escalation policy (**`escalateModel`**/**`escalateEffort`**) — see the authoring contract below. The DB handle is a `Mutex<Db>` so `create_workspace` locks per-op, never across its git checkout. _Support:_ `tools.rs`.
- **Role authoring over MCP (`save_role`/`delete_role`)** — an agent can author the **custom roles a good pipeline depends on**, not just reference the built-ins. `save_role` creates/updates a custom role from just `label` + `promptBody` (every other field defaults to the app's new-role values: `artifactKind` note, `environment` worktree, `defaultTools` [read_file, list_files], `defaultSubstrate` api, `canLoop`/`defaultCheckpoint` false, `tokenEstIn`/`tokenEstOut` 4000/1000); the `key` (a stage's `role`) is derived from the label with the **exact** app algorithm (`deriveRoleKey`) when omitted, and always returned. Routes through the same `db.upsert_role`/`get_role`/`role_in_use`/`delete_role` the app command uses — **built-in keys are protected** (a save that would overwrite one, or a delete of one, is refused), out-of-enum `artifactKind`/`environment` is a **clean tool error** (typed `RoleDef` deserialize) and an unknown `defaultTools` entry or `defaultSubstrate` (stored on `RoleDef` as a plain `Vec<String>`/`String`, not enums) is rejected by an explicit check matching the advertised enums, and a role **still used by any pipeline/run stage** cannot be deleted. Like `delete_pipeline`, an MCP save/delete does **not** push to the Pro cloud library from the MCP process (edit once in-app to sync). _Support:_ `tools.rs` (`save_role`/`delete_role`/`list_roles`/`derive_role_key`), `db::upsert_role`/`role_in_use`. Design record: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-mcp-authoring-parity-design.md`.
- **Routine authoring over MCP (`create_routine`/`update_routine`/`delete_routine`/`set_routine_enabled`)** — an agent can author **scheduled crews** (Pro routines), the full in-app Routines surface minus immediate firing. **Author-only, safe by default:** `create_routine` creates the routine **DISABLED** unless `enabled:true` is passed — authoring never silently schedules token spend; the user enables it in-app or the agent enables it on explicit instruction (`set_routine_enabled`). There is deliberately **no `run_routine_now`** (firing a crew *now* is execution, which stays in the app, like launching a run). An enabled routine fires only while the app runs and the plan includes `routines.scheduled` (**re-checked at fire time**, so an MCP-authored routine can't fire for a non-entitled user). `create_routine`/`update_routine` share one payload deserialized into the typed `RoutineInput` and validated through the **same** `octopush_lib::routines::{validate_routine, validate_schedule, next_due}` the app command uses, plus **referential-integrity checks** the agent needs (project/pipeline exist; `fixed` mode requires a `fixedWorkspaceId` that exists and belongs to the project; `fresh` must fire ≤ once/day — `daily` or `recurring{once}`) so a dangling routine is rejected up front, not left to fail at fire time. `scheduleKind` `interval` (seconds-as-string ≥ 60), `daily` (`HH:MM`), or **`recurring`** (a JSON-string `{days, time}` spec — the same Days × Times model the app builder produces, documented with an example in the tool schema; more legible to an agent than cron); `stageModelOverrides` (`[position, model]` pairs) round-trip through the stored JSON string; the optional `fireCondition` (exit-0 pre-fire gate) is carried through. `update_routine` leaves `enabled` untouched; `delete_routine` is ungated (matches the app). _Support:_ `tools.rs` (`create_routine`/`update_routine`/`delete_routine`/`set_routine_enabled`/`list_routines`/`build_routine_input`), `db::insert_routine`/`update_routine`/`set_routine_enabled`, `routines::{validate_routine,validate_schedule,next_due}`. Design record: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-mcp-authoring-parity-design.md`.
- **Pipeline authoring contract** — Same `§3.7` validator as the app's `save_pipeline` (roles, loops on review roles, acyclic parents, substrate, tools subset, maxIterations 1..100, loopMaxIterations 1..9 when looping, instructions ≤8000). Per-stage inputs include the **cost/quality knobs**: `effort` (`low|medium|high|xhigh|max`; null/omit = off; on `cli` passed to Claude Code as `--effort` and to Codex as `-c model_reasoning_effort` (clamped to the levels the model lists in Codex's model catalog; not passed on a model the catalog doesn't list); on `api` takes effect only on reasoning-capable models — current Claude families + budget-path Haiku 4.5/Sonnet 4.5, where higher levels auto-clamp to the model's max; on legacy/unknown/non-Claude ids it is **silently ignored**, not clamped) and the escalation policy `escalateModel` (retry once on stage failure **only if it raises the tier** above `agentModel`; api+cli) / `escalateEffort` (api and cli; retries only when higher than the base effort). Both round-trip through the exact `StageDraft`→`save_pipeline` path the app uses; `save_pipeline` normalizes a whitespace-only `escalateModel` to none, and an out-of-enum `effort`/`escalateEffort` is a clean per-stage tool error (never a panic). `describe_pipeline_schema` documents these fields with their real semantics, the effort/escalation **rules**, a `runtimeBehaviors` section (the `ask_director` **escape valve** — an **API-substrate** stage may pause to ask the director when blocked; a `cli` stage never self-blocks, use a checkpoint/escalation there; plus **auto-escalation** guidance), and an annotated example that sets `effort` + `escalateModel`. _Support:_ `tools.rs`.
- **Registration & namespacing** — `claude mcp add octopush -- <binary>`; tools appear as `mcp__octopush__<tool>`. Roadmap (not yet): execution control-plane, TALK/REVIEW surfaces, issue-tracker reads. _Support:_ `docs/octopush-mcp.md`.

### Skills
- **Discovery** — `<name>/SKILL.md` from `<worktree>/.claude/skills/*` (project) and `~/.claude/skills/*` (user); project shadows user. A project skill that resolves outside the project, or any skill over 4 MiB, is skipped unread; FIFOs and devices are passed over (see "Skill discovery (project ∪ user)"). _Support:_ `skills/mod.rs`.
- **Frontmatter parsing** — Hand-rolled (no YAML dep): requires a `---` fence; fields `name` (required), `description`, `allowed-tools`/`tools`. _Support:_ `skills/mod.rs::parse_skill`.
- **Command + chat usage** — `list_skills` → `SkillMeta[]`; `list_skipped_skills` → `SkippedDefinition[]` (`name`, `label`, `path`, `reason`), the files left unread, which the slash menu names; a selected skill appends its body to the system prompt and optionally restricts the turn's tools; the model can also load a listed skill itself with the `Skill` tool, in Talk and in sub-agents (§3 "The model loads a skill on its own"). _Support:_ `commands.rs`, `chat_engine.rs`. _Entry:_ `/` SlashMenu (§3).

### Notable implementation details
- **Where config lives** — Jira creds in `settings.json`; Epiku's base URL and project in `settings.json` (`epiku`) and its token in the login Keychain (service `octopush-epiku`, account = the base URL); per-project Jira key, tracker choice and Epiku project + per-workspace `linked_issue_key` in SQLite; MCP-client servers in `~/.claude/mcp.json` (user) + `<repo>/.claude/mcp.json` (project), the user-level ones' secrets in the login Keychain (service `octopush-mcp`); skills in `.claude/skills/*`; Claude-Code registration of octopush-mcp lives in Claude Code's own user-scope config.
- **MCP registry/transport** — Two directions: **client** (Octopush spawns external stdio servers, lazy-cached, namespaced `mcp__server__tool`, routed in the chat loop) and **server** (Octopush *is* a stdio MCP server for terminal CLIs). Both hand-rolled JSON-RPC 2.0 over newline-delimited stdio.
- **octopush-mcp safety scope** — communicated three ways (server `instructions`, each tool's description, the doc): never executes, never spends tokens, never mutates git (the lone git touch is `create_workspace`'s worktree); runs land in `draft` for the user to launch from the app's DIRECT mode; **routines are authored DISABLED by default and there is no `run_routine_now`** (the scheduler — in the app, gated per fire — is the only thing that ever fires one); drives the same DB whether or not the app is running.
