## 10. Settings, Theming, Updates & Platform

### Settings shell & navigation
- **Settings overlay** — Full-screen overlay (not a modal); header eyebrow `Preferences` + The Octo at 18px (static) + `Octopush` wordmark in Fraunces (`.brand-wordmark`) + `ESC · CLOSE`. _Support:_ `Settings.tsx`; `icons/OctoMark.tsx`. _Entry:_ top-bar gear; `⌘,` (General); `⌘⇧T` (Usage).
- **Grouped master-detail nav** — 4 groups: **Setup** (General, Editor), **Intelligence** (Models, Usage), **Connections** (Integrations), **App** (Appearance, Shortcuts, Privacy, About). Every row is 32px with a 1px border slot (transparent at rest) and its label in 13px sans in every state; the active row only changes colour (brass text on a brass-ghost ground with a brass-dim border), so switching tabs never moves the rows. Pane crossfades. _Support:_ `lib/settingsTabs.ts`, `Settings.tsx`.
- **Escape handling** — Capture-phase Esc closes but always `preventDefault`s (never exits macOS full-screen); defers to a stacked ModalShell; ignores Esc in inputs. _Support:_ `Settings.tsx`.

### Settings panes
- **General** — First, the **Readiness** card (*"Is this Mac ready for a crew?"*, `data-tour="settings-readiness-card"`): one row per local check — **Claude Code** found + its version against the tested floor (`TESTED_CLAUDE_FLOOR`, #278's parser; missing = rouge *Failed* + `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, older than the floor = amber *Warning* with "Update to x.y.z or newer" naming the higher of the floor and the missing security fix (2.1.325 today) + `…@latest`; at or above the floor but below a row of `CLAUDE_SECURITY_FIXES` = amber *Warning* with the fix "Update Claude Code: 2.1.325 fixes the Bash sandbox not fully protecting a worktree's settings, hooks and shared git folder." and the same `…@latest` command; otherwise, exactly a `CLAUDE_KNOWN_BAD_RELEASES` release = amber *Warning* with "Claude Code 2.1.329 drops the retry gateway models need when a max_tokens error names a lower limit; 2.1.330 restores it. Update Claude Code." and that command — never blocked, never for an unknown version; below rows of `CLAUDE_RECOMMENDED_FIXES`, whatever its status, the row also carries a sage note listing every missing fix, oldest first (`agent_adapter::claude_recommended_fixes` → `ReadinessCheck.recommended`, formatted by `claudeCli.claudeRecommendedNote`, `data-tour="settings-readiness-claude-note"`): one fix reads "Recommended: Claude Code 2.1.332 fixes a usage limit being reported as reached after it had already reset.", several read "Recommended: Claude Code 2.1.332. 2.1.331 fixes …. 2.1.332 fixes …." Each row has an audience (`RecommendedAudience`): `run` (2.1.330, ExitWorktree removing a worktree another session is using) shows only while a Run-mode session runs Claude Code (a running terminal whose `agentCli` is `claude`); `any` (2.1.330, settings changes lost when several Claude Code processes save them at once; 2.1.331, MCP tool calls hanging up to 30 minutes on some malformed replies from a local or WebSocket server; 2.1.332, a usage limit reported as reached after it had already reset, which a crew's plan-limit park otherwise has to catch, see "Claude plan limit park") shows to anyone on an older Claude Code, Run session or not (no crews gate: every install has the builtin crews' Claude Code CLI stages, so it would always be open). These are no security fixes, so they never warn a stage or the launcher), **Claude auth** (with no stored claude.ai sign-in end, an Anthropic key in settings or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → "API key", otherwise amber "Subscription" — CLI stages use the `claude` login, API stages need a key; with a stored claude.ai sign-in end, key or not (the Settings key never signs Claude Code in) — the `credential_expires_at` a CLI stage's stream-json `result` reported on Claude Code 2.1.318+, kept in `app_meta` `claude_login:expiry` by `claude_login.rs`, read from the db; on an explicit **Check again** / **Run the check** (never the automatic pass when the pane opens or the first-run invite checks, since whether `claude auth status` contacts the network isn't known — `readinessStore.check({ explicit: true })` → `readiness_check` `askClaude`) Readiness also runs `claude auth status --json` (`agent_adapter::probe_claude_login`, through `readiness::run_probe_terminating`: up to 15 s (`CLAUDE_AUTH_STATUS_TIMEOUT`, since it may refresh the OAuth token and interrupting that can sign you out), then SIGTERM to its process group and 2 s to exit before SIGKILL, and `OnQuit::Leave` (`CLAUDE_AUTH_STATUS_ON_QUIT`): quitting neither kills nor waits for it, so a token refresh still under way finishes on its own in its process group after Octopush exits; output capped; the account details it prints stay in memory; the card waits for it on Check again) and reads it tri-state (`parse_claude_auth_status` → `ClaudeLoginProbe`): `SignedIn(end)` from `loginExpiresAt` (Claude Code 2.1.318+; RFC 3339 or epoch seconds/milliseconds), `SignedOut` on `loggedIn: false`, `Unknown` otherwise; a probed date wins over the stored one (`readiness::login_end`) and is written back through `claude_login::record` with a `claude-login://updated` event, so the launcher and the sign-in notes agree; signed out clears the stored date (`claude_login::apply_probe` → `clear`, event with `expiresAt: null`) and the row shows the no-sign-in state ("API key" with a key, else amber "Subscription"); a failed probe, a timeout or a missing field (`Unknown`) falls back to the stored date — it reads verdigris "Signed in · until 12 Dec" while more than 10 days away, amber "Sign-in ends 12 Dec" within 10 days with the fix "Sign in again before it ends so overnight crews keep running" and `claude auth login` to copy, and rouge *Failed* "Sign-in ended 3 Nov" once it has passed, with the fix "CLI stages and Routines can't run on it. Sign in again, then Check again." — or, when `claude --version` is older than 2.1.318 (`CLAUDE_LOGIN_END_SINCE`, whose `claude auth status` can't report a new date), "…Sign in again, and update Claude Code to 2.1.318 or newer so Check again can read the new date." (`readiness::auth_check_on`) (**Check again** asks `claude auth status` for the new date; the next plan stage also replaces it, and the next API-key stage clears it, see "Claude sign-in end from `credential_expires_at`") and the same command; older CLIs never report it, so the row stays "Subscription". The `claude auth status` fixtures (`2.1.319/auth-status/*.json`) are synthetic), **Codex CLI** (`data-tour="settings-readiness-codex"`; only when a saved pipeline has a `cli` stage whose model or escalation model resolves to `CliDialect::Codex`, or a Routine's per-stage model override puts one there — `readiness::wants_codex`, read from the db by `readiness_check`: `codex` resolved on the login-shell PATH like the other commands; missing = amber *Warning* "Not found" + `npm i -g @openai/codex`; found = verdigris "Found · 0.170.0" on the automatic pass; on an explicit **Check again** only, like `claude auth status`, it runs `codex login status` through `readiness::run_status_probe_terminating` (3 s, then SIGTERM to its process group and 1 s before SIGKILL, `OnQuit::Leave`, stdout/stderr to `/dev/null` so what it prints is never read) and reads its exit code alone: 0 = verdigris "Signed in · 0.170.0", non-zero = amber "Not signed in" + `codex login`. On every pass, beside it, `codex --version` (local, no network, 3 s) gives the version from its `codex-cli X.Y.Z` line (`agent_adapter::parse_codex_version`, pinned by the `codex/<version>/version.txt` fixture); output it can't read shows "· version unknown" and never warns. A version below the newest `CODEX_SECURITY_FIXES` row (0.170.0 today) turns the found/signed-in row amber *Warning*, e.g. "Signed in · 0.169.0", with the fix "Update Codex: 0.170.0 fixes permission updates and child threads losing sandbox restrictions." and `npm i -g @openai/codex`; sign-in problems show first. Each check clears the session's cached Codex version too), **git** (`git --version`; missing or the command-line-tools stub = *Failed* + `xcode-select --install`), **GitHub CLI** (`gh auth token --hostname github.com`, which only looks up gh's stored credential and never contacts GitHub — unlike `gh auth status` — with stdout/stderr sent to `/dev/null` so the token is never read, only the exit status, and gh's update notifiers off; ok = "Token found", missing or signed out = *Warning* + `brew install gh` / `gh auth login`), **Disk space** (`data-tour="settings-readiness-disk"`; free space on the home volume from `perf::home_disk`, the same reading as the footer, no new command: ok shows "84 GB free"; under 10 GB (`DISK_WARN_BYTES`) amber with the fix "Crews create worktrees and run setup scripts; free some space or archive old workspaces."; under 2 GB (`DISK_FAIL_BYTES`) rouge *Failed*; when not ok a serif **"See what this workspace caches"** closes Settings and opens the footer's perf popover with its Workspace Caches section (`perfStore.detailsOpen`); a volume that can't be read (total 0) shows no row) and **Ollama** (only when the Ollama provider is enabled and its base URL is loopback: a TCP connect, every resolved address sharing the one 3 s budget; not running = *Warning* + `ollama serve`). Last, a **Crew models** row (`data-tour="settings-readiness-models"`), built in the frontend from the saved pipelines and the Routines with their model overrides (`modelRetirement.readinessRetirementCheck`; the stores load on open if needed). It shows only while one of them uses a model in `MODEL_RETIREMENTS` within 30 days of its retirement, as amber *Warning* "Sonnet 4.5 · retires Nov 30", or after it, as rouge *Failed*. Its fix names the crews and Routines that will fail, says to switch each crew to the replacement from the Direct launcher and that a Routine which only inherits a custom crew's model follows its crew. It promises the switch for no other Routine: one on a builtin crew is told the switch saves "<name> (custom)" and to edit the Routine to use that copy, and one whose own stage overrides pick the model is told the routine editor can't change them, so to compose it again and delete the old one (the same per-Routine copy as the Routines tooltip, `routineRetirementFix`). With several such models it shows the most urgent one and counts the rest. A check whose thread breaks shows an amber "Check failed to run" (no timeout claim, no command). Each row: a status glyph with a `title` (verdigris ok, amber warning, rouge failure; a check that didn't answer in **3 s** shows a clock and *Timed out*), the label, the live value (`.octo-tabular`), the status word, and when not ok a one-line fix plus the command with a copy button. Rows enter with `.octo-rise-in`; a status this build doesn't know shows a mute circle and *Unknown*. The result slot always answers: mute *"Not checked yet."* with the CTA reading **"Run the check"** before the first run, a "Checking this Mac…" spinner on the first run (later re-checks keep the previous rows on screen until the new answer lands), the rows, or — when the backend answers with no list — a mute "No checks came back…" line; under a result a mono mute **"CHECKED 2M AGO"** meta (`data-tour="settings-readiness-checked"`, `checkedAt` in the store, refreshed every 30 s, full time in its `title`). Checks run once when the pane opens and on the serif **"Check again"** (`data-tour="settings-readiness-again"`); the commands resolve on the login-shell PATH, run in parallel off the UI thread (`spawn_blocking`), each killed at 3 s, never cached; each check also clears the session's cached Claude Code version, so the launcher, Settings › Integrations and the stage journals see an update without a restart. No telemetry. _Support:_ `settings/ReadinessCard.tsx`, `stores/readinessStore.ts` (shared with the first-run invite), command `readiness_check` → `src-tauri/src/readiness.rs`. Then workspace defaults (default mode), **Talk › "Limit tool turns per message"** and **"Limit sub-agent tool turns"** (`LimitTurnsRow`: a switch, **off by default = no limit**; on writes 25 and reveals a `rounds` Stepper 5–200 in steps of 5, off again writes `null`; read-modify-writes `settings.json` `talkMaxIterations` / `subagentMaxTurns`, "Saved" confirmation — the bounds of the Talk agentic loop and of one sub-agent run, see §3), and Attention toggles ("Play sound…", "Notify when a crew needs you" — crews, Claude Code waiting in a terminal you can't see, and a Talk approval card — then **"Notify me elsewhere"**, the opt-in webhook with its URL field, "Send a test" and the preview of the message's fields, off by default, see §1 Toasts & notifications — **"Show in menu bar"** (the menu bar Octo, `menuBarEnabled`, on unless saved as `false`, `data-tour="settings-menu-bar"`, see §10 "OS-integration"), and "Let Claude Code say what it's waiting on", `claudeHooksEnabled`, on unless saved as `false`, `data-tour="settings-claude-hooks"`; see §Terminal "Claude Code hook signals"). A **Safety** section holds **Guard commits against secrets** (on by default; see §6 "Secret guard"). _Support:_ `GeneralPane.tsx`; `attentionStore`; `notifyPrefsStore`; `settings.rs`.
- **Editor** — Word wrap, Font size (10–22), Tab width (2/4/8), Line numbers, and an "Editor command" override (e.g. `code`/`cursor`; blank = autodetect, shows detected editors). _Support:_ `EditorPane.tsx`; `editorPrefsStore` + `settings.json`; `detectEditors`.
- **Appearance** — Theme picker: a 2-column grid of live-swatch cards built from each theme's palette; click applies instantly. Names show in title case (`porcelain-indigo` → "Porcelain & Indigo"; unknown hand-written names title-case per word). The current family (Atelier, Vellum, Mossbank, Porcelain & Indigo, Ember) comes first; the pre-redesign palettes (Dark, Midnight, Solarized Dark) sit in a **Legacy** group below, and the lead mentions them only when that group has themes in it. _Support:_ `AppearancePane.tsx`; `lib/themeNames.ts` (`themeLabel`, `isLegacyTheme`); `themeStore`.
- **Usage** — Token/cost dashboard + budgets (see §8). _Support:_ `UsagePane.tsx`.
- **Shortcuts** — Read-only keymap reference (see Appendix C). Its Talk group lists send, newline, `Esc` stop, `⌘⌥N` new conversation, `⌘⌥K` switch conversation, `⌘⌥A` focus the oldest waiting approval card and the card's `⌘↵` / `Esc`; its Run group, `⌘⌥K` switch session (#1153). Each keybinding is a mono chip in mute on the hairline chip (like the palette's shortcut hints); brass stays on the eyebrow and the active nav item. Labels show the real keys (Toggle companion reads `⌘\`, one backslash; a test rejects doubled backslashes). The mode rows come from `MODES` / `MODE_SHORTCUTS`, so they list Run `⌘⇧1`, Talk `⌘⇧2`, Review `⌘⇧3`, Direct `⌘⇧D` in switcher order (the Run row carries `data-tour="settings-shortcuts-modes"`). Groups: Navigation, Actions, **Rail** (`⌘⌥G` move to a group, `⇧F10` row menu, `⌘`-click · `⇧`-click select missions, `Esc` clear the selection), **Talk** (`↵` send, `⇧↵` new line, `Esc` stop the running turn, `⌘⌥N` new conversation, `⌘⌥K` switch conversation, `⌘⌥A` focus the oldest waiting approval card, and the card's `⌘↵` and `Esc`), **Run** (`⌘⌥K` switch session). _Support:_ `ShortcutsPane.tsx`.
- **Privacy** — A statement that must stay **exactly true** (the website quotes it): subtitle "Your work stays on this Mac, unless you turn on sync."; data stored on this Mac in `~/Library/Application Support/octopush/octopush.db` (runs and custom pipelines leave only if sync is on), then the line "API keys: stored in `~/.octopush/settings.json`. MCP servers you add in Settings: `~/.claude/mcp.json`. A Token sign-in, an OAuth client secret and the values you mark Keep in Keychain go to the macOS Keychain, and mcp-remote keeps a browser sign-in in `~/.mcp-auth`. A project's own `.claude/mcp.json` stays as written. Your account session lives in the macOS Keychain too." (every path an ivory code chip; "Keep in Keychain" is the tooltip of the MCP form's key-icon switch), and an exhaustive **"Outbound traffic, only to:"** list (`OUTBOUND`) — AI providers you configure (Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible, local models); Clerk sign-in + Dodo Payments checkout when you use your account; Octopush's sync service only if you turn on sync; "A webhook URL you set in Notify me elsewhere, only if you turn it on or send a test — a fixed label, the project's name and the mission's title (the start of its task), never code, diffs, the crew's questions or agent output." (#964); integrations you connect (Jira, GitHub, a LiteLLM gateway, MCP servers) and your git remotes; update checks (`octopush.sh/update/latest.json`, GitHub releases); LiteLLM's public pricing table on GitHub when you refresh pricing — then "No analytics, no telemetry." and a note that agent CLIs Octopush launches (Claude Code, Codex) follow their own telemetry policies (`AGENT_CLI_NOTE`). Below it, the pane's one control: the **"Quiet Claude Code in crews and Routines"** toggle (off by default; `ToggleRow`, `data-tour="settings-quiet-claude-code"`, switch `quiet-claude-code-switch`; read-modify-write of `quietClaudeCode`, and a failed save puts the switch back) whose helper text, with the variable as a code chip, reads "Crew stages and Routines start Claude Code with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`. Claude Code then skips its auto-updates, telemetry, error reporting, release notes and availability checks. Features that need feature-flag fetching, such as Remote Control, don't work in those sessions. Your model requests to Anthropic still go out as usual. Run terminals are not affected.", and directly under it the sentence "When this is off, Claude Code in crew stages and Routines can also make its own nonessential calls (auto-update checks, telemetry, error reports), as described in Claude Code's documentation." (`QUIET_OFF_NOTE`). Both are owner-approved privacy copy (#703); see CLI substrate › Quiet Claude Code. The sign-in confirmation page (`auth.rs::callback_html`) is fully self-contained — no web fonts or other third-party requests (cargo-tested). A new outbound destination must be added to `OUTBOUND` in the same change. _Support:_ `PrivacyPane.tsx` (+ `PrivacyPane.test.tsx`).
- **About** — The Octo at 48px (static) above the pane header; installed version + "Look for a newer version" (upright serif, ghost button); renders the updater flow (when up to date, the status line carries the one mono "Checked just now" meta); footer links, both plain sans reference links (GitHub repo, **What's in this version** — reopens the What's new dialog for the installed version, `data-tour="about-whats-new"`), then the Ed25519-signature note. _Support:_ `AboutPane.tsx`; `icons/OctoMark.tsx`; `updaterStore`.
- **Integrations** — Hosts Issue tracking (§9), MCP Servers (§9), and the Claude Code "Connect" card (§9). _Support:_ `IntegrationsPane.tsx`.
- **Account (premium — P1 + P2)** — Sign in / out, reach Clerk's hosted account portal, and **upgrade to Pro**. Signed-out shows a "Sign in" CTA (which becomes "Waiting for your browser…" with a **Cancel** ghost button while a sign-in is in flight); signed-in shows the identity, a **plan badge (Free/Pro)**, "Manage your account ↗" (opens the Clerk portal) + "Sign out of Octopush" (upright-serif ghost buttons, like the other panes' actions), and — when Free — an **"Upgrade to Pro"** button that opens a Dodo Payments checkout link in the browser. A **Sync** section holds the two **opt-in cloud-sync toggles** (`ToggleRow`, both **off by default**): **"Sync run history across your Macs"** (metadata + per-stage journals, artifacts and size-capped diff snapshots) and **"Sync custom pipelines & roles"**, over the note *"Both are off until you turn them on, and apply only to the account that turned them on; signing out turns both off. Turning this off stops future uploads. Data already synced stays on Octopush's servers."* Turning **on** is Pro-only: Free/signed-out users see an OFF toggle **disabled** with a `title` ("Requires Pro" / "Sign in with a Pro account to sync") beside the existing Upgrade button — but an ON toggle stays **actionable so it can always be turned off** (`title` "Requires Pro to turn on. You can still turn it off."), so a lapsed subscription never leaves uploads armed for a silent resume. A row **dims only when it is truly unavailable** (locked and off, per `syncRowState`); an off row the account can turn on stays at full ink, with the off state carried by the switch alone, and a write in flight only blocks the switch (`ToggleRow` `busy` → `aria-busy`) without dimming. The pane reloads the prefs on mount/sign-in change without overwriting a just-written value; a failed write keeps the toggle where it was and shows "Couldn't change sync: …". Copy lives in `SYNC_COPY`. **Last sync attempt (#518):** under each toggle that is **on**, one muted mono line (`SyncStatusNote`, `.octo-fade-in`, `data-tour` `settings-account-sync-history-status` / `settings-account-sync-library-status`) shows the last push attempt: **"Last sent 14:02 · 3 runs"** (library: "items"; singular "1 run"/"1 item"), **"Last attempt failed 14:02 · HTTP 503 · Octopush retries with the next run"** (amber `text-octo-warning`; the `· HTTP n` segment is dropped for a network error). The time is local `HH:mm`, prefixed with the date ("Nov 8", plus the year when not this year) when it isn't today (`lib/syncStatusLine.ts`). An off toggle, no record, or an unreadable `get_sync_status` shows nothing. **Unsent library items (#799):** under the library toggle, while it is on and the sync service refused items, one amber mono line (`SyncUnsentNote`, `.octo-fade-in`, `data-tour` `settings-account-sync-library-unsent`) names them and why — *Not synced · pipeline "Big crew" (over the 64,000-byte limit) · role "Reviewer" (edit time over a day ahead of the sync service) · +1 more* (two named, then a count; the tooltip lists every one). Reasons: `oversize` "over the 64,000-byte limit", `bad_stamp` "unreadable edit time", `future_stamp` "edit time over a day ahead of the sync service", anything else "refused by the sync service" (`lib/syncStatusLine.ts` `syncUnsentLine`/`rejectionReason`). `get_sync_status` fills each item's local name (a pipeline's name, a role's label) at read time and leaves out items no longer in the local library (`commands::name_library_rejections`); names are never stored. _Mechanism:_ `sync::record_push` records every `push_runs` / `push_run_detail` / `push_library_items` attempt that made a request — `Sent`/`Failed`, never `Disabled`, `Empty` or `SignedOut` (a signed-out push only follows a revoked, already-cleared session, whose owner-bound status reads off anyway), and nothing if the toggle's flag went off mid-push (re-checked under the settings write lock when persisting) — as `SyncAttempt { at, outcome, count, httpStatus }` per `SyncKind`, in memory (seeded from disk on first use) **and** in `settings.json` `lastSyncAttempt` (**exactly those four fields** — no payloads, run titles or error bodies), so it survives a restart. Count = runs in the metadata batch / library items attempted; a run-detail push counts its one run, but a *successful* detail push never overwrites an existing record (it never turns "500 runs" into "1 run" and never hides a metadata failure). The disk write runs off the push path (`spawn_blocking`), only when something visible changed (outcome, count, status or the displayed minute), and its failure is only logged; every settings read-modify-write now goes through one lock (`settings::update_settings`) so this background writer can't resurrect a value another writer just changed. Turning a toggle off drops that kind's record, as does turning it back on or the opt-in moving to another account (a record never carries over); sign-out drops both. `save_settings` carries the field over from disk. The store reloads it on pane mount, on a toggle change and after each backfill. _Support:_ `settings/AccountPane.tsx`, `syncPrefsStore` (`get_sync_prefs`/`set_sync_pref` — turn-on is Pro-gated server-side too; `get_sync_status` → `status`/`loadStatus`), `useAuth`/`useEntitlement` hooks, `authStore`; commands `auth_begin_sign_in`/`auth_cancel_sign_in`/`auth_status`/`auth_refresh`/`auth_sync_plan`/`auth_sign_out`/`auth_account_portal_url`/`billing_checkout_url`; `lib/awaitPro.ts`. _Entry:_ Settings → Account (App group). _Mechanism:_ the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + **PKCE (S256)** **public-client** flow runs in the Rust core (`src-tauri/src/auth.rs`) — opens the system browser to Clerk, captures the redirect on a `127.0.0.1:8976` loopback (cancellable mid-flight) that serves a **branded Atelier confirmation page** (onyx/brass, distinct success + error states, dynamic text HTML-escaped), exchanges the code (**no client secret**), fetches `/oauth/userinfo`, and stores the session in the macOS **Keychain** (`keyring`). `auth_status` **silently refreshes** the access token when expired (signs out only on a revoked token, never on a transient/offline failure). **The plan rides on the OAuth session:** sign-in requests the Clerk **`public_metadata`** scope and reads `public_metadata.plan` (e.g. "pro") from userinfo into the session; `entitlement::current()` maps it to the entitlement (Pro = uncapped + all features). `auth_refresh` re-fetches userinfo to pick up a plan change. **After checkout the app auto-detects the upgrade** (`awaitPro.ts`): a bounded ~2-min lightweight poll (`auth_refresh`, no token rotation) **plus** a single forced token refresh (`auth_sync_plan`) when the window regains focus — a freshly-minted access token carries the latest `public_metadata`, so the badge + gates flip to **Pro on their own** (with a success toast), no manual sign-out/in. **"Upgrade"** (`billing.rs`) opens a Dodo **static checkout link** for the **live** $20/mo Pro product, stamped with the user's email + `metadata_clerk_user_id` (so a server-side webhook can map the subscription back **by Clerk id, not email**) — the desktop holds **no payment secret**. The plan is set server-side by a **Dodo→Clerk webhook** (a Vercel Function in the separate `octopush-api` repo) on `subscription.active`/`cancelled` (the webhook verifies against both the live and test signing secrets), and the **Free Direct-run cap (25/mo) is live** for non-Pro. **Dodo runs in live mode** (checkout host + product id baked into `billing.rs`), and **Clerk runs on the production instance** (custom domain `clerk.octopush.sh`; the public-client OAuth `client_id` + instance are baked into `auth.rs`, and the Account Portal resolves to `accounts.octopush.sh`).
- **Shared pane primitives** — `PaneHeader`, `SectionLabel`, `ToggleRow` (optional `disabled` + `title` for a not-currently-actionable setting, dimming over `--dur-quick`; optional `busy` while a write is in flight — the switch is blocked, the row carries `aria-busy` and a progress cursor, and nothing dims; `Switch` takes `disabled` and a required `ariaLabel` — the setting's title — which names the textless switch for screen readers and is its hover tooltip unless a more specific `title` is passed; `ToggleRow` passes its label and `title` through), `Stat`, `Row`, `useChartColors` (live CSS-var theme colors for Recharts). _Support:_ `settings/shared.tsx`.

### Theming
- **Backend theme store** — Themes persisted to `~/.octopush/theme.json`. `get_theme` returns **`null` when the file is absent** rather than defaulting to atelier, so the frontend can tell "chose dark" from "has not chosen". _Support:_ `theme.rs::load_stored_theme`; `get_theme`/`set_theme`/`list_themes`.
- **Follows the OS until you choose** — With no stored choice, `themeStore.load()` seeds from **`prefers-color-scheme`** (light → vellum, dark → atelier) and keeps tracking it live via a `matchMedia` listener, so a light-desktop user gets vellum on first launch. The seed is **never persisted** — writing it would freeze the app to whatever the desktop happened to be at first launch. Picking any theme persists it and ends the tracking for good (`followingSystem`). _Support:_ `themeStore.ts`.
- **No theme flash on launch** — `themeStore` mirrors the applied theme to `localStorage` (`octo:theme`), and an inline script in `index.html` reads it **synchronously before first paint** to set `color-scheme` and the ground tokens. Without it the window painted onyx for several frames before the async IPC resolved — a dark flash on every vellum launch. First-ever launch falls back to the `prefers-color-scheme` seed so it matches what the store is about to pick. _Support:_ `index.html`, `themeStore.ts`.
- **`color-scheme` follows the theme** — Declared per theme from the background's luminance, so native scrollbars, form controls and the caret match. It was previously a hardcoded `<meta name="color-scheme" content="dark">`, which left vellum with dark native chrome on cream. _Support:_ `themeStore.ts`, `lib/contrast.isDarkBackground`.
- **`ThemeConfig`** — name + 15 color fields (bg, panel, panel_2, border, **border_strong**, accent, accent_dim, success, warning, danger, text, text_dim, text_muted, terminal_bg). **Two border tiers:** `border` is the decorative hairline that divides panels; `border_strong` is the boundary for *interactive* chrome and clears **WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1** on every surface — a requirement that applies to controls, not to panel dividers. Native form controls (`<input>`/`<textarea>`/`<select>`) rest on `border-octo-border-strong` — **60 of 86 scanned, and zero remain on the hairline**; the other 26 carry no resting border at all by design (inline-edit fields and in-panel search boxes that are transparent at rest and hint on hover), where 1.4.11 has no resting boundary to govern. A vitest gate fails the build if a control regresses to the hairline, if the token loses all consumers, or if its tag scanner loses sync. It resolves shared class constants and inspects inline `style`, because the first version read only class literals inside the tag — which is exactly how nine settings inputs kept the hairline while the suite stayed green. Also covered: elements that *declare* a control role (`role="switch"`/`"combobox"`/`"radiogroup"`/`"tablist"` — `TogglePill`, the `ToggleRow` switch, `Listbox`'s combobox trigger, `SegmentedControl`'s track, the builder's tool toggles) and surfaces handed down via a `triggerClassName` prop, including its **default parameter binding** — without which `Listbox`'s own default surface was scanned but never resolved. Deliberately out of scope: bare text-labelled `<button>`s, and single-side borders like `border-b`, which are dividers rather than control outlines. Focus states keep `focus:border-octo-brass`, which clears 3:1 in every theme. `border_strong` is serde-defaulted so a pre-existing `theme.json` still loads. _Support:_ `theme.rs`.
- **9 built-in themes** — Brand default **atelier** (onyx/brass; first = default). Premium: **vellum** (only light theme), **mossbank**, **porcelain-indigo**, **ember**. Legacy: **dark**, **midnight**, **solarized-dark**. _Support:_ `theme.rs::builtin_themes`.
- **Vellum is contrast-solved, not inverted** — Every ink clears **AA (4.5:1) against the worst of the theme's three surfaces**, `bg`/`panel`/`panel_2` — `panel_2` being the hover/popover ground, where a token that passes on the canvas can still fail. Inks darken along their own hue while *gaining* saturation (on cream, contrast runs the opposite direction from onyx), and **`accent_dim` inverts its meaning**: the brighter sibling on onyx becomes the deeper chestnut on cream. The ground is off-white and the ink off-black by design — `#000`-on-`#fff` is 21:1, which halates for astigmatic readers across a full-screen IDE. Vellum's **hairline is also deliberately stronger** than atelier's reads on onyx (1.63:1 vs 1.28:1): a light theme cannot lift a surface by brightening it, so its borders carry structure the dark theme gets for free. _Support:_ `theme.rs`; gated by `vellum_clears_wcag_aa_on_every_surface` + `vellum_avoids_the_halation_extremes` (cargo) and mirrored in `contrast.test.ts` (vitest).
- **Theme application** — `themeStore.apply()` → `applyThemeToDom()` writes ~45 CSS custom properties on `document.documentElement` (legacy `--color-octo-*` + canonical semantic tokens), **derives every alpha family from the live theme** — accent (`--brass-*`), success (`--verdigris-*`), danger (`--rouge-*`), warning (`--warning-*`) and the `--onyx-40` scrim — declares `color-scheme`, mirrors to `localStorage`, sets body bg, then dispatches an `octo:theme` event so CodeMirror/Recharts reconfigure. Previously the status alphas were frozen at the atelier hues, so vellum tinted rows with a palette the user wasn't running. _Support:_ `themeStore.ts`.
- **Solved diff-row tints** — `--diff-add-bg` / `--diff-del-bg` are solved per theme against that theme's own background to hold **one constant perceptual step** (`DIFF_TINT_TARGET`), instead of the flat `rgba(…, 0.08)` literals `diffLineStyle.ts` used to return — the dark palette's hues at an alpha tuned against near-black. Solving also equalises the pair: verdigris and rouge don't share a luminance, so a flat 8% rendered added and deleted rows at visibly different weights even on atelier. _Support:_ `lib/contrast.solveTintAlpha`, `themeStore.ts`, `lib/diffLineStyle.ts`.
- **Theme-aware mark weight** — `--brass-line` (solid connectors, The Octo's back-arm row) is the one accent alpha that is not a fixed step: 55% on dark themes, **75% on light**, because a light-accent stroke at 55% over cream leaves the silhouette too thin to read. _Support:_ `themeStore.ts`, `icons/OctoMark.tsx`.
- **`tokens.ts`** — Typed JS mirror of the static Atelier tokens (fonts, easing, durations) for runtime inline styles. _Support:_ `lib/tokens.ts`.

### Auto-update (tauri-plugin-updater)
- **Updater store** — Phases `idle|checking|available|no-update|downloading|installing|error`; `checkForUpdates(interactive)`, `installAndRelaunch()`; plus `channel`, `skippedVersion`, `alertPending`/`alertOpen`, `loadPrefs()`, `setChannel()`, `launchCheck()`, `flushAlert()`, `dismissAlert()`, `skipVersion()`. Calls Rust over IPC (`ipc.updaterCheck` / `ipc.updaterInstall`, progress on a Tauri `Channel`) instead of the JS plugin, so the manifest follows the channel; relaunch stays on `plugin-process`. Concurrent checks share one in-flight call; a channel switch invalidates results of checks started before it; a skipped version stays quiet on background checks. Background failures stay silent. _Support:_ `updaterStore.ts`, `ipc.ts`.
- **Rust check / install** — `updater_check` builds `app.updater_builder()` (pubkey from `plugins.updater` config) and, for beta, overrides `.endpoints(...)`; returns `UpdateInfo {version, currentVersion, date (manifest pub_date), body (notes), channel}` and keeps the `Update` with its channel in managed `PendingUpdate` (cleared by `set_update_channel`; a check that finishes after the channel changed is dropped, and `updater_install` refuses an update found on another channel). `updater_install(onEvent)` downloads + installs it, streaming `Started{contentLength}` / `Progress{chunkLength}` / `Finished`. The default comparator (remote > installed) is kept, so nothing ever downgrades. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/updater.rs`, `commands.rs`.
- **Update channel (Stable / Beta)** — `settings.json` `updateChannel` (`stable` default | `beta`; any other value reads as `stable`, #642); `get_update_channel` / `set_update_channel` are its only accessors and `save_settings` carries it over from disk (like the sync opt-ins), so a stale pane save can't flip it. Stable = the `tauri.conf.json` endpoints; Beta = `https://octopush.sh/update/beta.json` → GitHub `releases/download/beta-channel/latest.json` (`updater::endpoints_for`, pure). Switching to Beta runs an interactive check; switching back to Stable drops any offered beta and re-checks quietly (never downgrades). _Entry:_ Settings › About › **Update channel** (`data-tour="about-update-channel"`).
- **Launch update alert** — Once the window is visible + 1.5s, `UpdateNotifier` runs `launchCheck()` (silent). If an update is available and isn't the skipped version, a `ModalShell` dialog shows the eyebrow "Update available", "Octopush X is ready.", release date · channel · installed version, and the manifest notes rendered as sanitized Markdown (`ReleaseNotes`); actions **Install and relaunch** (progress inline), **Later** (this launch; also silences the toast), **Skip this version** (persisted as `skippedUpdateVersion` via `set_skipped_update_version`, carried over by `save_settings`; a newer version alerts again). While any other dialog is open (a `ModalShell` — e.g. a Direct checkpoint — or any `aria-modal` surface) the alert is queued and retried every second. _Support:_ `UpdateAlert.tsx`, `UpdateNotifier.tsx`, `updaterStore.isBlockingSurfaceOpen`.
- **Release-notes renderer** — `ReleaseNotes` renders untrusted manifest Markdown with `react-markdown` + GFM and the document renderers: raw HTML skipped, images never loaded (alt text only), unsafe URL schemes stripped, links (http(s)/mailto only) open in the browser via `open_file_in_system`. _Support:_ `ReleaseNotes.tsx`.
- **UpdateNotifier toast** — Re-checks every 6 hours; visible only when an update is available/installing/error, the launch alert isn't up or queued, and the version wasn't dismissed or skipped; a **What's new** link that opens the version's GitHub release page in the browser (not the What's new dialog), progress bar, **Later** / **Install and relaunch**. Updates verified with an Ed25519 signature. _Support:_ `UpdateNotifier.tsx`.
- **About pane updater** — Installed version, **Look for a newer version** (`data-tour="about-check-updates"`), the Update channel control, an available update's notes (rendered Markdown) with **Install and relaunch**, and **In vX.Y.Z** notes for the installed version when known — bundled `whats-new/<version>/notes.md`, else the notes remembered (localStorage) when the update was installed from the app. _Support:_ `AboutPane.tsx`, `lib/releaseNotes.ts`.
- **Updater endpoint (host-indirected)** — `plugins.updater.endpoints` prefers `https://octopush.sh/update/latest.json` (a 302 to the GitHub release asset, so binaries can move hosts without breaking installed apps), falling back to the raw `releases/latest/download/latest.json`. The updater signature is inline in `latest.json` (no separate `.sig` fetch). _Support:_ `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`; the redirect lives in the `octopush-web` repo (`vercel.json`). See [`docs/RELEASING.md`](RELEASING.md). _Entry:_ automatic.
- **Release channels + notes (publishing side)** — Every tag publishes a GitHub prerelease on the **beta** channel (never GitHub "latest") and uploads its `latest.json` to the moving `beta-channel` release (which never moves backwards); the owner promotes a beta to **stable** (`releases/latest`) with `.github/workflows/promote.yml`. Release bodies and `latest.json` `notes` (≤ 4000 chars, what the update toast/alert shows) come from `whats-new/<version>/notes.md` when present, else the generic "Octopush <version>". A nightly routine (`scripts/routines/release-beta.sh`) cuts patch betas from `main`. _Support:_ `scripts/release.mjs`, `scripts/release-lib.mjs` (+ `release.test.mjs`), `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/workflows/promote.yml`, `scripts/routines/release-beta.sh` (+ `scripts/release-beta.test.mjs`). See [`docs/RELEASING.md`](RELEASING.md). _Entry:_ automatic.

### Outbound HTTPS trust (eMudhra compromised-key denylist)
- **Compromised eMudhra CA keys are refused on the Rust core's HTTP clients** — Every HTTP client the Rust core builds (LLM providers and gateways, Jira, the GitHub PR lookup, Clerk sign-in / token refresh / userinfo, cloud sync, the pricing refresh, the detached run worker) starts from `tls::client_builder()`: rustls (ring provider) on the **OS trust store** (`rustls-platform-verifier` — Security.framework on macOS, CryptoAPI on Windows, the system CA bundle on Linux — so keychain-trusted corporate roots keep working) behind a `DenylistVerifier` for the eight eMudhra intermediate CAs compromised in October 2026. It refuses a chain when any certificate in it (a) has one of the eight compromised **keys** (the SPKI SHA-256 set Go hard-codes for CVE-2026-111943; keyed on the key, so Sectigo's cross-signs match too) or (b) was **issued under one of the eight compromised names** (DER subject bytes taken from Mozilla's incident data and checked against those keys; matched exactly and also after normalization — case-folded, whitespace-collapsed, any ASN.1 string type — so a PrintableString or lower-cased re-encoding is caught too), so a server cannot dodge the key check by sending only a forged leaf. Both checks run on the chain the server **presents**, before the OS evaluates it. On **macOS** Octopush then runs the one `SecTrust` evaluation itself (same SSL policy as `rustls-platform-verifier`, with the handshake's verify date and stapled OCSP response): **the chain must evaluate successfully** — any evaluation error rejects the connection — and the chain `SecTrust` built (including intermediates it fetched via AIA or found in the keychain) is checked again; only a final anchor the minimal DER walk cannot parse is skipped, so a quirky corporate/MDM root cannot break every connection. On Linux the platform verifier does no AIA fetching, so the presented chain is the path; Windows (not shipped) gets the presented-chain checks only. A refused chain fails the request with `the server's certificate chain contains a compromised eMudhra intermediate CA key (SPKI SHA-256 …)` or `… was issued by the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA "EM … CA - G3x"`, appended to the request error (or log line) by `tls::describe_request_error` at the provider, gateway, Jira, sign-in and token-refresh, sync pull/push, pricing and GitHub call sites; an unparseable certificate fails closed. Denylist refusals and TLS version/suite mismatches are **not retried** by the provider retry layer (`providers::request_error` classifies them as non-transient); a token refresh that hits one keeps the session (no sign-out on a forged certificate). **TLS 1.2+ with modern suites only:** rustls + ring speaks TLS 1.2 and 1.3 with ECDHE key exchange and AES-GCM / ChaCha20-Poly1305 (no TLS 1.0/1.1, no RSA key exchange, no CBC, no DHE, no P-521 server keys). A server or proxy that offers only older options fails the handshake with `TLS handshake failed (…). Octopush requires TLS 1.2 or newer with modern cipher suites …`; there is no automatic fallback to native-tls on a handshake failure. ALPN is pinned to HTTP/1.1, matching the previous `native-tls-no-alpn` backend, so provider streaming is unchanged; the system proxy is honoured as before. Only if the platform verifier cannot start at all (no CA bundle) does the client fall back to reqwest's default native-tls backend, logging one warning. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/tls.rs` (`DISTRUSTED_SPKI_SHA256`, `DISTRUSTED_CA_SUBJECTS`, `subject_public_key_info`, `issuer_name`, `DenylistVerifier` (`platform`), `normalized_name`, `evaluate_on_macos`, `rustls_client_config`, `client_builder`/`client`, `tls_failure`/`is_permanent_tls_failure`/`describe_request_error`), `providers::request_error`; callers `chat_engine::shared_http_client`, `gateway::http_client`, `issue_tracker::jira::JiraClient::new`, `auth.rs`, `commands.rs` (`refresh_pricing`, `find_pr_for_branch`). _Entry:_ automatic.
- **Out of the denylist's reach (OS-level trust only)** — The Tauri updater's own client (reqwest 0.13 on the same platform verifier; update payloads are Ed25519-signed regardless of transport), the WebView, `git` fetch/push (the system `git`), and the agent CLIs Octopush spawns (`claude`, …) use their own TLS stacks and trust stores. Keeping macOS, the Linux `ca-certificates` package and those tools current is what protects them. _Support:_ n/a. _Entry:_ n/a.

### Performance monitor
- **Backend sampling** — `get_perf_stats` samples processes via `sysinfo` into three groups: **app** (main + macOS "responsible" WebKit helpers via FFI), **daemon** (`octopush-pty-server` only), **total** — each with `rss_bytes`, `cpu_pct`, `process_count`; plus home-volume disk free/total. Persistent `PerfState(Mutex<System>)` for CPU deltas. _Support:_ `perf.rs`; `get_perf_stats`.
- **Perf store + footer bar** — Polls every 2000ms (skips when hidden); `PerfMonitorBar` shows `⌗` total RSS · `CPU N%` · disk free, plus the rail-collapse toggle; a popover lists App + Daemon rows and workspace caches (its open state is `perfStore.detailsOpen`, so the Readiness card's disk row can open it). _Support:_ `perfStore.ts`, `PerfMonitorBar.tsx`.
- **Low-disk launcher line** — Under 2 GB free on the home volume (`LOW_DISK_BYTES`, `src/lib/diskSpace.ts`, the same line as the Readiness card's rouge), the Direct launcher shows one mono amber line above "Begin the run" (`data-tour="direct-launcher-low-disk"`): "Only 1.4 GB free — this run may fail when the disk fills", with the worktree/setup-script reason in its `title`. It never blocks the launch, follows the footer's 2 s reading, and stays hidden without a reading. _Support:_ `PipelineSetup.tsx`, `lowDiskLine`.

### Disk-cache / workspace-cache monitor
- **Backend cache scan** — `get_workspace_cache_sizes` sums known build/cache dirs (target, node_modules, dist, build, .next, .nuxt, .gradle, __pycache__, .venv, venv, .turbo, out). _Support:_ `perf.rs`.
- **Cache UI** — A "Workspace Caches" section in the perf popover. _Support:_ `PerfMonitorBar.tsx`.

### Scratchpad
- **Scratchpad store** — Multi-tab in-memory notes/code editor (`tabs{id,name,content,language}`, `activeTabId`); create/delete/rename/setContent/setLanguage. **No persistence** (session-scoped). _Support:_ `scratchpadStore.ts`.
- **Scratchpad UI** — Right column of a draggable split (`CanvasSplit`); `ScratchpadTabsBar` + `ScratchpadCodeEditor` (CodeMirror 6, live syntax for js/ts/python/rust/java/json/markdown/html/css/xml/yaml through the shared lazy grammars of `editorLanguages.ts` (`scratchpadLang` maps a tab's language to a `LangId`; the grammar sits in a language `Compartment` and is installed when it lands), shared Atelier editor theme); double-click to rename a tab, `+` adds. _Support:_ `ScratchpadEditor.tsx` et al. _Entry:_ top-bar NotebookPen / `ScratchpadIcon`.
- **Scratchpad find / replace (⌘F)** — The same `EditorSearch` overlay and theme-solved match highlighting as the REVIEW editor: match case, whole word, regex, "n of m" tally, next/prev, replace, replace all. The overlay's label and placeholder read "Find in tab" here (`scope` prop). Closes — and clears its query, so no highlight lingers — whenever the view is rebuilt (tab switch, and a rename, which re-detects the language) or the scratchpad is hidden, since `CanvasSplit` keeps it mounted. _Support:_ `ScratchpadCodeEditor.tsx`, `editor/EditorSearch.tsx`, `editor/searchHighlight.ts`.
- **Scratchpad symbol highlighting** — The same occurrence highlighting as the REVIEW editor (caret on an identifier washes its other uses and underlines its definition). The ⌘-click jump is deliberately **not** wired here: a scratchpad tab has no workspace to resolve a definition against. _Support:_ `ScratchpadCodeEditor.tsx`, `editor/symbolHighlight.ts`.
- **Scratchpad editor shortcuts** — `⌘F` find · `⌘G`/`F3` next/prev · `⌘D` select next occurrence · `⌘⇧L` select all matching · `⌘⌥G` go to line (all from `searchKeymap`) · `Tab` indent. _Support:_ `ScratchpadCodeEditor.tsx`.
- **Scratchpad follows theme switches** — The editor theme is held in a compartment and rebuilt on `octo:theme`, like `EditorPane`, so the whole surface (including the search-match tokens) tracks the active theme. _Support:_ `ScratchpadCodeEditor.tsx`, `editor/atelierTheme.buildEditorTheme`.

### OS-integration / platform utilities
- **`open_file_in_system`** — OS default opener (macOS `open`, Linux `xdg-open`). _Entry:_ file-tree "Open with default app", issue URLs, "What's new".
- **`reveal_in_finder`** — `open -R` (macOS). _Entry:_ "Reveal in Finder".
- **Dock badge (needs-you count)** — The Dock icon carries the number of runs that need the director (across every workspace, the fleet chip's `{n} needs you`) **plus the Talk conversations whose approval card waits on you** (one per conversation however many cards it holds: `ApprovalBroker::waiting` → `fleet_status::talk_conversations` → `FleetStatus.talk`; `badge()` = crews + conversations; the fleet chip stays the crews' own), cleared at 0, and stays current while the window is closed. A card raised or answered refreshes it (`ApprovalBroker::ask` → `refresh_later`). Derived in Rust, so it never depends on the webview: `fleet_status::derive` counts `paused` runs from `list_active_runs` (except a Claude plan park with an automatic resume scheduled, `fleet_status::plan_waiting`, which counts in flight), and `TauriEventSink` refreshes it (coalesced ~250ms, off the emitter's thread, set only when the count changes) on every `run://checkpoint` / `run://stage-update` / `run://cost` / `run://error`, detached-bridge re-emits included, plus once at launch and after `delete_workspace` / `delete_project` (their runs cascade-delete without a run event) and `rename_workspace` (the menu bar names crews by workspace). Set with `set_badge_count` from Rust (no JS capability); a platform without a Dock badge logs the failure once, not on every refresh. `src/lib/needsYou.fixtures.json` pins Rust's `needs_you` / fleet split to the TS `needsYou` / `fleetCounts` the chip reads; both test suites read it. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/fleet_status.rs`, `orchestrator/events.rs`, `src/lib/runStatus.ts`. _Entry:_ automatic.
- **Menu bar Octo (status item, #718)** — A macOS menu bar status item for the crews that need you, so a missed gate shows outside the window too. **Icon:** The Octo as a monochrome **template** image (`icon_as_template`: macOS inks it for a light or dark menu bar, so no colour and no brass reach the system chrome), 16pt wide in an 18pt square, in three still poses of its rig — `idle` (at rest), `working` (eyes at the end of their scan, first and third arms raised a full 2.4u stroke, so it reads apart from idle at 18pt) and `blocked` (needs you: eyes at half-mast) — chosen like the top-bar mascot: any crew needs you > a run is `running` > idle (a Claude plan park that resumes on its own is neither). It never animates, so it never takes the beacon from the app. `src-tauri/icons/tray/{idle,working,blocked}Template@2x.png` (36px, loaded with `include_image!`; tray-icon draws it 18pt tall, so there is no 1x file), rendered from the `OctoRig` geometry by `scripts/tray-icons.py`. **Title:** the needs-you count (the Dock badge's number) beside the icon, only above 0. **Tooltip:** "Octopush — 2 crews need you" / "Octopush — 1 crew working" / "Octopush — idle". **Menu (native, `tauri::menu`):** a disabled count line ("2 crews need you" / "No crew needs you"); then one item per crew that needs you, **longest-waiting first** (time in state as Mission Control keeps it: a status change this session saw, else the run's creation; ties by run id), reading `{workspace} · {stage} — {reason}` (`auth-flow · Reviewer — at the gate`; the workspace's name, else the task's first line; the stage's custom name, else its role's label; names cut to 32 / 24 characters); past 10 crews a disabled "and 3 more"; a separator; **Open Octopush** (shows the window); **Quit Octopush** (the system Quit, same as ⌘Q, so unsaved Quick View edits still ask). Reasons, in Mission Control's precedence (a stopped stage, then a question, then a gate): `stalled` (a stage stopped on a transient fault Resume answers: rate limit, overload, 5xx, network, the relaunch's `interrupted` stamp — `fleet_status::is_transient_halt`, the Rust twin of TS `isTransientHalt`, both pinned by `src/lib/transientHalt.fixtures.json`), `halted` (a stage failed on a standing fault), `plan limit` (a Claude plan limit waiting for the director), `asked you` (`ask_director`), `possible secret` (a secret-guard hold), `budget reached` (a stage parked before it began with the run's budget spent, the drive's own `plan_wait::budget_spent`), `at the gate` (a finished stage's checkpoint or review-loop decision), `paused` (parked before a stage otherwise: the director's own pause or a spending limit outside the run). **Choosing a crew** shows the window and emits `octo://open-run` `{runId, workspaceId, projectId, projectPath}` to `main` (the lookup runs off the main thread); `App.tsx` closes everything the tour's `close-overlays` route closes (Settings, the palettes, Mission Control, the Logbook; one `closeOverlays`) and lands on that workspace's **Direct** surface, opening its project by the payload's path when it isn't the open one, like "Continue in the workspace". **One source of truth:** `fleet_status::refresh` (the Dock badge's refresh: the same events, coalescing and launch pass) reads `list_active_runs` once and hands it to `menu_bar::update`, so the title, the menu and the badge count the same `needs_you` runs; what each waits on comes from `Db::list_parked_stages` (paused runs joined to their blocked stages: status, title, started, asked, secret hold, plan limit — never artifacts or diffs), read only while the item shows and something needs you. The item is redrawn only when what it shows changed (icon, title, tooltip and menu each compared). **Talk approvals:** a Talk conversation whose approval card waits on you is listed with the crews, by how long it waited (`menu_bar::TalkWaiting`, its oldest card, ids `menu-bar:talk:<thread>`), reading `{workspace} · Talk — a command wants approval` (`— a commit or push wants approval` for the secret guard's card; "a workspace" when it has no name; never the command or its arguments), and counts in the title, the count line and the tooltip ("1 crew and 1 conversation need you", "2 conversations need you"). Choosing one emits `octo://open-talk` `{threadId, workspaceId, projectId, projectPath}` (looked up off the main thread with `Db::chat_thread_home`); `App.tsx` lands on that workspace's **Talk** with that conversation shown (chosen before the project loads, so `loadHistory` keeps it). Other Talk and terminal attention live in the webview. Nothing it shows leaves the Mac. **Setting:** `menuBarEnabled` in `settings.json`, on unless saved `false` (`menu_bar::enabled`); `save_settings` redraws at once: the item is built the first time it's wanted (its menu handler registered once), then only redrawn, shown or hidden, and always drawn before it is shown, so turning it back on never flashes stale content. macOS only. _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/menu_bar.rs` (the pure model: `model`, `waiting`, `reason`, `track_since`, unit-tested), `fleet_status.rs`, `db.rs` (`list_parked_stages`), `settings.rs`, `commands.rs` (`save_settings`), `lib.rs` (`menu_bar::setup`), `Cargo.toml` (Tauri `tray-icon` feature); `src/App.tsx`, `lib/ipc.ts` (`onOpenRunFromMenuBar`, `onOpenTalkFromMenuBar`), `settings/GeneralPane.tsx`. _Entry:_ the menu bar.
- **`open_in_terminal`** — `open -a Terminal` (macOS); Linux terminal fallbacks. _Entry:_ "Open in terminal".
- **`detect_editors` / `open_in_editor`** — Detects VS Code (`code`), Cursor (`cursor`), Zed (`zed`), Sublime (`subl`), IntelliJ (`idea`) on PATH; opens via the configured override else the first detected, falling back to the system opener. _Entry:_ Editor pane + rail "Open in editor".

### Open With & Quick View (files from the OS)
- **File associations** — The bundle registers Octopush as an **Editor** with `LSHandlerRank` **Alternate** for text and source files: plain text/logs, Markdown, JSON, YAML, TOML, ini/conf/env, CSV/TSV, JS/TS, Rust, Python, Java, Go, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Kotlin, C/C++/C#, Lua, SQL, shell, HTML/CSS/XML/SVG. Octopush appears under Finder's **right-click → Open With** without becoming the default app for any type. On macOS one entry also declares the system content types (`public.plain-text`, `public.source-code`, `public.json`, …), so any text-conforming file lists it. **Linux** registers via the `.desktop` `MimeType=` list (entries carrying a `mimeType`; `text/plain` covers text subtypes). **Windows registers nothing** (`tauri.windows.conf.json` empties the list): Tauri's installers write `HKCR\.ext` as the *default* handler, which would take `.txt`/`.js`/`.html` away from the user's editor — "Open with → Choose another app → Octopush" still works, since the file arrives in `argv`. Registration only happens for an **installed** bundle (`/Applications`); `tauri:dev` registers nothing. _Support:_ `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` `bundle.fileAssociations`, `src-tauri/tauri.windows.conf.json`.
- **Receiving files** — macOS delivers files as `RunEvent::Opened` (cold and warm start); Windows/Linux pass them in `argv` on a cold start, and `tauri-plugin-single-instance` forwards a second launch's `argv` + `cwd` to the running instance (a second launch with no file just focuses the main window). The plugin is **release-only**: its lock is keyed on the bundle identifier, so in a debug build it would make `tauri:dev` hand off to an installed Octopush and exit. `file_args` keeps only paths that exist as regular files (relative paths resolve against the launch `cwd`; `file://` URLs are decoded; flags skipped; non-UTF-8 names handled via `args_os`). Paths are canonicalized with `dunce` (no Windows `\\?\` verbatim prefix). _Support:_ `src-tauri/src/file_open.rs`, the `app.run` event loop in `lib.rs`.
- **Hidden-until-needed main window** — `main` starts with `visible: false`. On `RunEvent::Ready` a 400ms grace timer shows it unless a file arrived, so launching Octopush **by opening a file** shows only the Quick View (the flag is set only once a window was actually built, so a failed open still shows main). macOS: clicking the Dock icon (or relaunching from Finder/Spotlight — `RunEvent::Reopen`) shows main whenever it's hidden, even with Quick Views on screen. **On macOS closing main always hides it** (`prevent_close` + `hide`, leaving fullscreen first so no empty black Space is left behind) instead of quitting, so the Routines scheduler, in-process runs, the detached bridge, crew notifications and the Dock badge keep going; ⌘Q and the app menu's Quit never send a close request, so they still quit. Windows/Linux: closing main while Quick Views are open **hides** it rather than destroying it, so it can always come back; when the last Quick View closes and main is hidden, the app exits instead of lingering invisibly. _Support:_ `lib.rs`, `file_open::{show_main, main_visible, hide_main_on_close}`.
- **Quick View window** — Each file opens in its own lightweight window (`quickview-N`, 960×720, the macOS overlay title bar); opening a file that's already showing focuses its window. The window mounts `QuickViewApp` instead of the Atelier shell (`main.tsx` routes on the window label and lazy-loads only that window's root, so a Quick View never loads `App` or the stores' app-wide event listeners; the window asks Rust which file it shows via `quickview_path`). Header: the Octo mark, file name (serif), a brass unsaved dot, the location (`workspace · relative/path` when inside a workspace, else the absolute path), then icon controls with tooltips — **Preview/Source** toggle (rendered kinds only), **Format JSON** (JSON only), **Save (⌘S)**, **Reveal in Finder** (labelled per platform: *Show in Explorer* / *Show in folder*; `reveal_in_finder` uses `explorer /select,` on Windows and opens the containing folder with `xdg-open` on Linux), **Open Octopush** (shows the main window — the way back after a file-launch) — and, when a workspace holds the file, the serif CTA **"Continue in the workspace"**. A mono status line shows language · line count · saved/unsaved, plus save or JSON-parse errors. _Support:_ `src/quickview/QuickViewApp.tsx`, `file_open::open_quickview`. _Entry:_ Finder Open With / double-click / `octopush <file>`.
- **Format-aware rendering** — Markdown → the Review editor's `MarkdownPreview` (GFM, embedded HTML inert; **remote images are not fetched** — shown as a named placeholder — since a file of unknown origin could carry tracking pixels); CSV/TSV → a table with a sticky header row and row numbers (RFC 4180 parser: quoted fields, `""` escapes, delimiters/newlines inside quotes; first 2,000 rows rendered); SVG → drawn through an `<img>` data URL so scripts in the file never run; HTML → a fully sandboxed `<iframe sandbox="">` (no scripts, no same-origin) with a CSP injected after the doctype that blocks all network fetches (inline styles and `data:` images still render). Rendered kinds open in **Preview**; everything else opens in **Source**. JSON's **Format** re-indents with 2 spaces as one undoable change: only whitespace between tokens changes — numbers, strings and keys are copied verbatim, so integers beyond 2^53, `1.0`/`1e3` spellings and duplicate keys survive (no `JSON.parse`/`stringify` round-trip). Invalid JSON (incl. JSONC comments) reports the parse error and leaves the buffer alone. _Support:_ `src/quickview/QuickViewPreviews.tsx`, `src/quickview/quickViewFormat.ts`.
- **Editing in Quick View** — Always editable: CodeMirror with the Atelier theme (follows theme changes made in the main window — `themeStore.apply` broadcasts `octo://theme`, Quick View `adopt`s it), the shared language map, the ⌘F find/replace overlay, occurrence highlighting, and the persisted editor preferences (wrap, font size, tab width, line numbers). The editor never unmounts when switching to Preview, so undo history and the caret survive; the preview renders the live buffer. **Line endings are preserved**: a CRLF file is edited with CodeMirror's `lineSeparator` set to `\r\n` and written back via `sliceDoc()`, so saving never converts it to LF. Dirty state compares the editor's document structurally with the last saved one (undoing back to it clears the mark); for documents over 1 MB the dirty check and preview refresh wait for a 150 ms pause in typing. **⌘S** works from either layout. Saving reuses the Review editor's **external-change guard**: if the file's mtime moved since it was read, the save stops and a banner offers **"Take the version on disk"** or **"Keep my edits"** (overwrite). On window focus the file is re-stat'ed: a clean buffer silently reloads, a dirty one gets the banner, a deleted file is flagged ("Saving will recreate it"). **Closing with unsaved edits** asks first (Keep editing · Save, then close · Close without saving) — on the window's close button and on **app quit (⌘Q)**: each Quick View reports its dirty state (`quickview_set_dirty`), and `RunEvent::ExitRequested` is held while one is dirty, focusing that window and asking it to confirm (`octo://confirm-close`). The conflict banner collapses with the grid-rows idiom. Binary, non-UTF-8, and over-50MB files show an empty state with **"Show it in Finder"**. _Support:_ `src/quickview/QuickViewEditor.tsx`, `ipc.{readFileChecked,writeFile,fileMeta,onCloseRequested,destroyCurrentWindow}`.
- **Continue in the workspace** — Resolves the file to the workspace whose root most specifically contains it (`workspace_for_path`: longest matching worktree root; a workspace without its own worktree uses the project path; paths canonicalized). The CTA saves pending edits, then `open_path_in_workspace` shows and focuses the main window and emits `octo://open-in-workspace` `{projectId, workspaceId, relativePath}`; `App.tsx` switches project/workspace the same way a rail click does (opening the project by the path in the payload, so it works before the recent-projects list loads) and opens the file — by absolute path — in the Review editor once that workspace is active; a request that can't land expires after 10 s. Among workspaces sharing one root, the first-created wins. _Support:_ `file_open::{workspace_for_path, open_path_in_workspace, match_workspace}`, `App.tsx` listener.

### Notable implementation details
- **Settings persistence (backend)** — `AppSettings` → `~/.octopush/settings.json` (pretty JSON, camelCase): `provider_keys`, `provider_base_urls`, `git_credentials`, `last_pricing_refresh`, `issue_tracker`, `editor_command`. Legacy `anthropicApiKey`/`openaiApiKey` migrated into `provider_keys`. Full-file last-write-wins (single-window app; callers read-modify-write). **A value a build can't read never strands the file (#641, #642):** every enum-valued field is parsed leniently — `updateChannel` (the only enum field today, via `settings::enum_or_default`) reads as its default `stable` on a well-formed value it doesn't know (an unknown variant or a wrong shape; malformed JSON inside the value still fails the file), e.g. a channel written by a newer build before a downgrade, and `lastSyncAttempt` drops only the entry it can't read — so every other key still loads and saves go through. A file that still doesn't parse (broken JSON, a wrong type elsewhere) reads as defaults and is **never overwritten**: every writer refuses with "Your change wasn't saved: settings.json couldn't be read, so it was left unchanged.", and at launch an error toast (the existing `Toasts` channel, 20s) titled "settings.json couldn't be read" says "Octopush is showing default settings and won't save changes until {path} is fixed. The file was left unchanged." with the file's full path; toasts live in module state in `Toasts.tsx`, so the notice survives the swap from the Welcome view's `ToastContainer` to the shell's when launch restore opens the last project, and a long path wraps (`unreadable_settings_path` → `src/lib/settingsNotice.ts`, called once from `App.tsx`; path only, never the contents).
- **Editor prefs persistence (frontend)** — `editorPrefsStore` uses zustand `persist` to `localStorage` (`octo-editor-prefs`); only the editor *command* round-trips through `settings.json`.
- **Theme tokens are runtime CSS variables**, re-derived per theme (accent/success/danger/warning alpha families, solved diff tints, the `color-scheme` declaration) and broadcast via `octo:theme` so canvas/editor/chart surfaces stay in sync. A pre-paint script in `index.html` applies the ground tokens from a `localStorage` mirror before React mounts.
- **Palette drift is gated** — The pre-paint script in `index.html` and the two vitest palette tables restate theme colours because they can't import the Rust source. `themePalette.drift.test.ts` parses `theme.rs` and fails if any of them desync — otherwise the script would paint last release's ground for a frame and the suites would keep passing against colours the app no longer ships.
- **Contrast is enforced, not reviewed** — `contrast.ts` implements WCAG 2.1 relative luminance and is mirrored in `theme.rs`'s test module, so a palette regression breaks `cargo test`/`npm test` rather than a design review. Every theme's `text`, `text_dim`, `text_muted` and `accent` clear AA on all three surfaces, and the ramp is asserted to stay ordered (`muted ≤ dim ≤ text`) so a token can't be lifted past the threshold and end up louder than the tier above it. **One documented exclusion:** `solarized-dark`, whose upstream text ramp is not AA-capable — measured on Solarized's own surfaces, base0 is 4.75:1/4.11:1 and base01 2.79:1/2.42:1. Named in `NOT_AA_CAPABLE` rather than left as a silent hole, and scoped to the text ramp only: `border_strong` is an Octopush token, so its 3:1 floor is asserted for every theme without exception. The first-paint copy of atelier in `src/styles.css` is asserted against `theme.rs` too — from the Rust side via `include_str!`, because vitest stubs `.css` imports to an empty string and the same check would pass vacuously on the frontend.

## Appendix A — Backend command index

All Tauri commands are registered in `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` (`invoke_handler`) and implemented in `commands.rs`. Grouped as in the source:

- **Open With / Quick View** (`file_open.rs`) — `quickview_path`, `open_quickview_window`, `quickview_set_dirty`, `workspace_for_path`, `open_path_in_workspace`, `show_main_window`
- **Sessions** — `create_session`, `list_sessions`, `write_to_session`, `write_text_to_session`, `resize_session`, `kill_session`, `delete_session`
- **Tokens** — `get_token_report`, `record_token_event`, `get_budget_status`, `set_token_budget`
- **Templates** — `list_templates`, `save_template`, `delete_template`
- **Providers / Agents** — `list_providers`, `list_models`, `suggest_model`, `list_adapters`, `switch_agent`
- **Recap / Export** — `get_session_recap`, `export_session_json`, `export_session_csv`
- **Theme** — `get_theme` (nullable — `null` = no explicit choice), `set_theme`, `list_themes`
- **Projects** — `open_project`, `list_recent_projects`, `create_project`, `update_project_customization`, `set_project_pinned`, `set_project_order`, `close_project`, `list_closed_projects`, `reopen_project`, `delete_project`
- **Rail groups** — `list_groups`, `create_group`, `rename_group`, `set_group_tint`, `set_group_order`, `delete_group`, `set_item_group`, `set_items_group` (several items of one kind, all or none; called through `groupsStore` by the rail's groups UI)
- **Workspaces** — `create_workspace`, `list_workspaces`, `delete_workspace`, `archive_workspace`, `list_archived_workspaces`, `restore_workspace`, `update_workspace_customization`, `rename_workspace`, `update_workspace_link`, `update_project_jira_key`, `get_git_status`, `list_branches`, `workspaces_git_summary`, `get_git_diff`
- **Missions** — `create_mission`, `list_missions`, `get_mission`, `update_mission`, `archive_mission`, `logbook_summary` (per-mission free; project/global Pro)
- **Chat** — `send_chat_message`, `run_shell_command`, `stop_shell_command`, `list_chat_messages`, `get_chat_agent_log`, `list_subagent_types`, `cancel_chat`, `list_running_threads`, `list_chat_threads`, `create_chat_thread`, `rename_chat_thread`, `delete_chat_thread`, `list_skills`, `list_skipped_skills`, `read_attachment`, `list_mcp_tools`, `list_mcp_server_status`, `get_thread_mcp_disabled`, `set_thread_mcp_server`, `get_thread_permission_mode`, `set_thread_permission_mode`, `get_mcp_config`, `save_mcp_config`, `test_mcp_server`

## Appendix B — Data model (SQLite)

Database at `~/Library/Application Support/octopush/octopush.db`; all schema + migrations in `src-tauri/src/db.rs` (additive `add_column_if_missing`). Principal tables:

- **projects** — id, name, path (UNIQUE), created_at, last_opened, jira_project_key, closed_at, pinned, sort_order, tint, setup_script, group_id (nullable; a `project`-scope group; no FK, cleared by `delete_group`), issue_tracker (nullable: `jira` / `epiku` / `none`, NULL = the default, #1127), epiku_project (nullable: the Epiku project it reads, NULL = the one in Settings)
- **workspaces** — id, project_id (FK CASCADE), name, task, branch, worktree_path, setup_script, status, created_at, last_active, glyph, tint, test_command, linked_issue_key, issue_link_dismissed, from_branch, group_id (nullable; a `workspace`-scope group of the same project; no FK, cleared by `delete_group`; kept through archive and restore), after_workspace_id + after_condition (nullable; the mission of the same project this one waits on and `run_finished` | `pr_merged`; no FK, cleared when that mission is deleted or archived; no cycles), branch_from_prerequisite, auto_start (bools, default 0)
- **groups** — id, scope (`project` | `workspace`, CHECK), project_id (FK CASCADE; NOT NULL for a `workspace` group and NULL for a `project` group, CHECK), name, tint (one of the 7 monogram tints or NULL, validated in Rust), sort_order (position among the groups of the same scope and project), created_at; index `idx_groups_scope` on (scope, project_id, sort_order). Rail groups: the data layer only, the rail UI ships next (see section 2, Notable implementation details). A group has no member list of its own, and a row with no members is valid.
- **missions** — id, workspace_id (nullable — none for design/probe), project_id (FK CASCADE), intent (build/fix/review/probe/design/perf/ops/test; whether a mission ships nothing is derived from intent × git_isolation, never stored), title, status (active/done/archived), linked_issue_key, git_isolation (worktree/readonly/ephemeral/pr), exec_isolation (none/sandbox/container/cloud), payload (JSON), created_at, updated_at, archived_at. Partial UNIQUE index `idx_missions_writer` on active worktree/pr/ephemeral writers (never two active missions writing one checkout). Back-refs: `runs.mission_id`, `chat_threads.mission_id`, `terminals.mission_id` (all nullable). One-shot `app_meta`-gated backfill (`missions_backfill_v1`) re-parents existing workspaces.
- **work_spans** — id, mission_id (nullable), workspace_id (nullable), project_id (NOT NULL), surface (talk/direct/…), source, started_at, ended_at (+ indexes on mission_id, workspace_id, ended_at). Activity-time ledger for the Logbook, written by `record_activity` (coalesces within a 10-min idle window). Worked hours are the span-union, computed in `mission_spans_summary`/`logbook_summary`.
- **spend_events.mission_id** — nullable back-ref stamped from the active mission of the row's workspace at write time (TALK/DIRECT/REVIEW; RUN-legacy/adhoc unattributed); one-shot backfill `spend_events_mission_backfill_v1`; index `idx_spend_mission`. Powers per-mission cost/savings in the Logbook (`mission_spend`).
- **sessions** — id, name, color, icon, project_root, agent config, token_budget, tokens_used/input/output, status, context_files, tags, created_at, last_active
- **terminals** — id, workspace_id (FK), label, position, created_at
- **chat_threads** — id, workspace_id (FK CASCADE), mission_id (nullable back-ref, stamped at creation from the workspace's active mission — live-path, not just the one-shot backfill), title, created_at, updated_at, mcp_disabled (nullable JSON array of the MCP servers off in the conversation; NULL = all on; copied by a fork; a server renamed in Settings is renamed here too), permission_mode (nullable: `plan` or `edit`; NULL = Edit freely; copied by a fork; a value the build doesn't know reads as Plan only)
- **chat_messages** — id, workspace_id (FK CASCADE), thread_id, role, content, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, created_at
- **chat_agent_log** — id, thread_id (cascaded by `delete_chat_thread`), call_id (the `Agent` tool call), entry (LiveEntry JSON), created_at — a Talk sub-agent's persisted live journal
- **file_edits** — attribution of changed files to the chat message that produced them
- **pipelines** — id, name, description, is_builtin, created_at
- **pipeline_stages** — id, pipeline_id, position, role, agent_model, effort, escalate_model, escalate_effort, substrate, checkpoint, max_iterations, pos_x, pos_y, parents, tools, custom_name, instructions, loop_target_position, loop_max_iterations, loop_mode
- **runs** — id, workspace_id, pipeline_id, task, status, cost_usd, baseline_cost_usd, reference_model, retired_cost/tokens, budget_usd, linked_issue_key, timestamps; the Claude plan park `plan_window`, `plan_resets_at`, `plan_resume_at` (epoch s; NULL = the director resumes), `plan_resume_count`
- **run_stages** — private per-run copy of stages + status, tokens, cost, artifact, feedback, error, loop_iterations, diff_snapshot, session_id, resume_pending, baseline_commit, effort, escalate_model, escalate_effort, escalated
- **roles** — key, label, description, prompt_body, artifact_kind, environment, can_loop, default_tools, default_substrate, default_checkpoint, token estimates, is_builtin
- **stage_log** — persisted live-journal entries per run stage (incl. reset markers)
- **stage_iterations** — archived stage attempts (ordinal, role, model, status, artifact, error, cost, tokens, closing_feedback, diff_snapshot)
- **run_events** — append-only run audit log
- **token_events** — session_id (= workspace id), timestamp, input/output/cache_read/cache_creation tokens, model, cost_usd
- **budgets** — scope_type, scope_id, period, limit_usd, updated_at (UNIQUE on scope_type+scope_id+period)
- **app_meta `claude_plan:<kind>`** — the latest Claude plan window per kind (`PlanSnapshot` JSON: kind, utilization, resetsAt, status, overageStatus, usingOverage, seenAt), written by `PersistingSink` on `plan://updated`
