## Appendix C — Keyboard shortcuts

Global shortcuts are owned by a single `keydown` listener (`useGlobalShortcuts`, called from `src/App.tsx`) that walks the declarative `GLOBAL_SHORTCUTS` table in `src/hooks/useGlobalShortcuts.ts`: the first chord that matches claims the key, a Run-only entry does nothing outside Run (and doesn't `preventDefault`), and a key an inner handler already `preventDefault`ed is ignored. A test checks every table entry's key caps against this appendix. (The Settings → Shortcuts pane documents a curated subset.)

| Shortcut | Action |
|---|---|
| `⌘1` … `⌘9` | Switch to workspace N |
| `⌘⇧1` / `⌘⇧2` / `⌘⇧3` | Run / Talk / Review mode (the mode switcher's order) |
| `⌘⇧D` | Direct mode |
| `⌘⇧M` | Mission Control (the fleet cockpit) |
| `⌘⇧L` | Logbook Room (cross-mission rollup — Pro) |
| `⌘⇧P` | Open a pull request (the PR composer for the active workspace; needs it on a named branch, and leaves the key to a focused code editor or terminal) |
| `⌘N` | New workspace (current project) |
| `⌘⌥N` | New Talk conversation in the active workspace, shown in Talk (from any mode; not under a dialog; physical `N` key) |
| `⌘K` | Toggle command palette |
| `⌘P` | Workspace file finder |
| `⌘⇧F` | Workspace text search |
| `⌘\` | Toggle companion (layout refit). While Run shows two or more panes, or Talk's terminal seat is open, the Companion is folded; `⌘\` brings it back over the panes |
| `⌘,` | Open Settings (General) |
| `⌘⇧T` | Open Settings · Usage |
| `⌘⌥1` … `⌘⌥9` | **Run mode** — jump to the Nth terminal session (hold ⌥ to see the numbers on the session line) |
| `⌘⌥←` / `⌘⌥→` | **Run mode** — previous / next terminal session in the focused pane, wrapping; skips sessions shown in another pane |
| `⌘[` / `⌘]` | **Run mode**, two to four panes (an empty seat counts) — focus the previous / next pane in reading order (left to right, top to bottom; slot 0 is the large pane of three), wrapping (physical bracket keys; `⌘⌥[`/`⌘⌥]` stay the editor's fold keys) |
| `⌘⌥K` | One switcher that follows the mode; toggles. **Run mode** — session switcher (search, switch, close, open a new one); inside it, `⌥⏎` opens the selected session beside instead of switching. **Talk mode** — conversation switcher (filter by title, `⏎` switch, `⌘⏎` new conversation). Elsewhere it does nothing |
| `⌘D` | **Run mode** — Open beside: the pairing switcher (*Which session sits beside this one?*), or an empty seat when every session is on screen; a new pane is appended up to four (a 2×2 grid); with four and no empty seat, the pick replaces the focused pane's session. **Talk mode** — open or close the terminal seat beside the conversation (on its last session, else with the pairing switcher). Elsewhere it does nothing (physical `D` key; a focused editor keeps `⌘D` for next occurrence) |
| **Talk** | `↵` send · `⇧↵` newline · `↑`/`↓` prompt history · `Esc` stop the running turn (only with the focus in Talk, or on nothing while Talk shows; an open popover, menu or dialog, a focused approval card, editor or terminal keeps its own `Esc`; the Stop button's title says "Stop (Esc)") |
| `⌘⌥A` | **Talk mode** — focus the oldest approval card waiting in the conversation on screen (a card never takes the focus by itself; physical `A` key). Does nothing when none waits or under a dialog |
| **Approval card** | With the card focused (never by itself: a click, `Tab` or `⌘⌥A`): `⌘↵` its lead answer (Approve / Allow once; on a credentials or secret card, the safe answer, which plain `↵` also takes) · `Esc` deny. Plain `↵` never approves a flagged command |
| **Direct gate comments** | With the gate's document focused: `↓`/`↑` move over its passages · `⏎` comment on the marked passage or the selection · `Esc` put the cursor away. In the composer: `⌘⏎` / `Ctrl+⏎` add the comment (only with a note) · `Esc` cancel |
| **Editor** | `⌘S` save · `⌘F` find/replace · `⌘G`/`F3` next/prev · `⌘⇧L` select all occurrences · `⌘D` next occurrence · `⌘⌥G` go to line · `⌘`/`Ctrl`-click or `F12` go to definition · `⌃−`/`⌃⇧−` back/forward (`Ctrl+Alt+−`/`Ctrl+Shift+−` on Windows and Linux) · `⌥F7`/`⇧⌥F7` next/previous change (with `fn` on Apple keyboards, unless "Use F1, F2, etc. keys as standard function keys" is on) · `⌘⌥[`/`⌘⌥]` fold/unfold · `⌃⌥[`/`⌃⌥]` fold/unfold all · `⌘=`/`⌘−` font · `Alt-Z` wrap |
| **Scratchpad** | `⌘F` find/replace · `⌘G`/`F3` next/prev · `⌘D` next occurrence · `⌘⇧L` select all matching · `⌘⌥G` go to line · `Tab` indent |
| **Diff triage** | `j`/`k`/↓/↑ move hunk · `]`/`[` jump file · `Space` fold · `a` accept · `x` reject · `A` accept file · `v` viewed · `o` open in editor · `w` why · `m` ask for a change (working tree only; in its field `⌘⏎` adds the comment, `Esc` drops it, `⌥↑`/`⌥↓` pick a line and `⌥⇧↑`/`⌥⇧↓` extend the range) · `/` filter · `c` commit · `?` help |
| **Review** | `⌘⇧E` reveal the open file in the file tree |
| **File tree** | ↑/↓ move · →/← expand/collapse · Home/End · Enter/Space activate · ContextMenu/Shift+F10 menu |
| **Rail** | `⌘⌥G` move the focused mission row or project line to a group (rail-scoped: only with the focus on a row or line, so the editor's and scratchpad's `⌘⌥G` go to line is untouched; on a selected row it moves the selection) · `⇧F10`/ContextMenu the focused mission row's, project line's or group header's menu (in the slim rail, a mission group's chevron) · `F2` rename a focused group header · `←`/`→` fold/unfold a focused group header · `⌘`-click / `⇧`-click select missions of one project · `Esc` clear the selection |
| **Dialogs** | `Esc` close topmost · `Tab` trap within ModalShell |

## Appendix D — Processes & on-disk locations

- **Processes** — the Tauri app (`octopush`), the PTY daemon (`octopush-pty-server`, out-of-process, launchd-adopted), and on demand the MCP server (`octopush-mcp`, stdio, spawned by a CLI like Claude Code). Direct CLI stages spawn `claude -p …`; Run terminals spawn the user's login shell.
- **`~/.octopush/`** — `settings.json` (keys, base URLs, git credentials, issue-tracker config, editor command, last pricing refresh, the `historySyncEnabled`/`librarySyncEnabled` cloud-sync opt-ins + their `syncOwner` Clerk id, the `notifyElsewhereEnabled`/`notifyElsewhereUrl` webhook opt-in), `providers.json` (provider/model catalog incl. pricing), `theme.json`, `projects/` (default scaffold location), `pty-server.sock` / `pty-server.pid` / `pty-server.log`, `pty-state/<id>.log` (terminal scrollback), `history/<session>.hist`.
- **`~/Library/Application Support/octopush/`** — `octopush.db` (SQLite: projects, workspaces, sessions, terminals, chats, pipelines, runs, roles, journals, token events, budgets, …).
- **`~/.claude/`** — read for `mcp.json` (MCP servers) and `skills/*` (user skills); Claude Code's own config receives the `octopush` MCP registration.
- **Per-project** — `.octopus-worktrees/<branch>/` (workspace worktrees), `.claude/skills/*` and `.claude/mcp.json` (project-scoped skills/servers), and the migration from legacy `~/.octopus-sh` / `octopus-sh` dirs runs once on launch.
- **Privacy posture** — local-first, no analytics/telemetry. Outbound traffic: configured AI providers; Clerk/Dodo when the account is used; Octopush's sync API (`octopush-api.vercel.app`) **only when the user opts in** to history and/or library sync; integrations the user enables (Jira over HTTPS, GitHub via `gh`/REST, LiteLLM gateway, MCP servers) and git remotes; the updater endpoints; the LiteLLM pricing table on manual refresh; "A webhook URL you set in Notify me elsewhere, only if you turn it on or send a test — a fixed label, the project's name and the mission's title (the start of its task), never code, diffs, the crew's questions or agent output." Agent CLIs it launches (Claude Code, Codex) follow their own telemetry policies; an opt-in (Settings › Privacy, off by default) starts Claude Code for crew stages and Routines with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`, never Run terminals or Talk. Mirrored verbatim in Settings → Privacy.
